Walking over to her, polished brogues clicking on the wood, Lena sank down to a crouch beside the bed, her coat splayed out around her feet as she cocked her head to the side and observed Kara.

 

            “But I thought I knew you . I thought- … my world used to begin and end with you, so I thought - naïvely, albeit - that you would never think I was capable of something like that.”

 

            “You should’ve told me,” Kara rasped, the words scraping her throat. “All this time- you should’ve told me. ”

 

            “I didn’t want to,” Lena whispered, rubbing her fingertips over her brow as an ache blossomed there. “Not after … not after everything that happened. We tore right through each other and I couldn’t even look at you anymore. The truth wouldn’t have changed anything.”

 

            “It would’ve changed everything.”

 

            “How? Something between us broke beyond repair the moment you accused me of having his mark on my arm. That was mortifying for me, to have you see … well, you saw it. You guessed the truth behind it. But that wasn’t enough proof for you. Beneath it all, I was just another Slytherin to you.”

 

            Kara let out a choked sound of surprise. “That’s not the whole truth. The truth was … I was a little bit in love with you.”

 

            Shock was slow to bloom on Lena’s face as she visibly whitened. After a moment, she managed to make herself move, pushing herself to her feet, stiff and silent. Lena missed her friend, but the person sitting before her wasn’t really her Kara. This was a woman who’d lived her life without her for the last five years, looking at Lena as if she expected her to forget all of that, to react favourably to confession. Lena didn’t even know if she was telling the truth, 

 

            “Okay,” she said, and even she wanted to flinch at the dead sound of her voice. So dry, so brittle.

 

            Surprised by her own honesty, Kara rubbed the scarred bridge of her nose, her pale scars livid against the fierce red blush. It hit Lena hard to see her like that, exactly like the somewhat shy and bashful Hufflepuff who’d appeared in her secret room and lodged herself in the space behind Lena’s rib cage. 

 

            Lena adjusted her satchel and pressed her lips into a flat line as she stared down at the worn floor and lingered. When she peered back up through her lashes, she faltered at the sight of Kara and was soft as she spoke.

 

            “The love was there. It didn’t change anything, but it was there.”

Chapter 19

            Kara fell into a deeper depression than she’d been in for a while with the devastating blow of knowing that Lena had returned her feelings in some capacity. All that she was really sure or was Lena had cared for her deeply and had harboured so many lies in an effort to keep her safe - at the expense of her own well-being - and Kara had turned her back on her when she’d needed her most.

 

            Over the years, she’d spent a lot of time thinking about Lena, about the first person who’d made her feel like she had a friend at Hogwarts, who’d made her think they being a werewolf didn’t have to mean the end of her life. There had been a deep kindness to her that had been unmistakable to Kara, if hidden away by Lena’s aloof demeanour that most people couldn’t penetrate. It had felt like they were the only two people privy to their own secret world, in the way kids always seem to think that things are more special than they really are. But even now, Kara would be lying if she denied feeling like Lena was the one person who’d truly left a mark on her life.

 

            There had been moments when she’d considered what had happened and doubted her part in it, but she’d always circled back around to that Hogsmeade weekend. There had been that duel with Winn where Lena had cut his chest open, and Kara had admitted to her part in that, and there had been other instances where things had felt off - she’d almost kissed Lena, Lena had shut herself off, they’d argued, she’d forced Lena’s hand to reveal her scar, Lena had threatened to hex her. It had been messy and dramatic the way all things were to teenagers caught in the middle of so much strife and opposing sides. 

 

            But to find out the thing that has ultimately led to their undoing had been a lie out of necessity, out of Lena’s loyalty to the Order, was too much for Kara to handle. They’d been on the same side without her even knowing just how involved her friend had been, and because Lena had managed to keep her mouth shut - something some of the younger Order members struggled with in lieu of bravado and glory - she’d had to lose her.

 

            Once Lena had walked out of her room in The Leaky Cauldron, Kara had run the water in the bathroom and took a long shower, her hands braced against the tiled walls as she stood beneath the spray. She felt numb and exhausted, and only partially due to the full moon. Tom always gave her a couple of days to recover afterwards and Kara was grateful as she crawled beneath the blankets and sobbed into her pillow as confusing heartbreak she hadn’t felt the likes of since her last year of Hogwarts slammed into her.

 

            It wasn’t a regular occurrence for her to see Lena at the pub, but after two weeks without a glimpse of her, Kara came to the conclusion that she was avoiding her. She didn’t even have it in herself to feel any pity for herself or any blame toward Lena. Moving through the motions of work and life, oddly solemn and quiet at drinks with her friends and dinner with Eliza, both easily explained by a particularly rough full moon - it had been, but not for the reasons they imagined - Kara felt herself settle into a rut. 

 

            It wasn’t as bad as last time, far from rock bottom but so emotionally numbed that she couldn’t sound convincing when Alex interrogated her over ice cream at Florean Fortescue’s, but it was a different type of devastation. A job was one thing but a missed opportunity, a lie, an almost, was enough to keep her up at night.

 

            Three weeks after Lena had left her room, as June was coming to a close and the next full moon was approaching, Kara received a letter. It was addressed to her and delivered by a Hogwarts owl, the seal pressed with the school crest, which posed at least a dozen questions to the young woman. The letter inside was brief and vague, requesting a meeting with her the following day at eleven o’clock in the morning. The bottom of the letter was signed by Albus Dumbledore.

 

            Rising early the next morning and setting her cramped room straight, Kara spent an age trying to tame her flaxen mess of curls and settled on a deep blue shirt tucked into her flared jeans. Wand in her back pocket, battered watch on her wrist and her old glasses perched on her nose, she went downstairs to help with the breakfast rush as a distraction.

 

            Ten minutes to eleven, Tom told her Dumbledore had arrived and was waiting in a private parlour to speak with her. Untying the apron splattered with coffee and damp from dishwater, Kara assured the barkeeper she wouldn’t be long before making her way to the room he’d tucked her old headmaster away in.

 

            Pausing outside, Kara straightened and then knocked on the worn door. It swung inwards on groaning hinges a moment later and Kara was left lingering with uncertainty on the threshold of the room, taking in the sight of Dumbledore in silver robes on a sagging sofa. He smiled congenially as she blinked owlishly, wringing her hands in a nervous manner.

 

            “Professor Dumbledore,” she quietly greeted him, nodding politely.

 

            “Miss Danvers, come in, come in,” Dumbledore beckoned, rising from his seat and gesturing to an armchair. “I trust you’ve been well?”

 

            “Oh, um, yes, sir. And yourself?”

 

            “An old man can only lament about his lost youth, but I won’t bore you with it or we shall be here all afternoon. I have more important matters to discuss with you, in fact, an opportunity I hope you’ll favourably entertain.”

 

            Confused now, Kara swallowed dryly. “Sir?”

 

            Her voice lilted up at the end, anxiety winding through her, and he looked at her with piercing pale blue eyes, a small smile on his face. Trying not to fidget, Kara stared at him with wide, youthful eyes, waiting.

 

            “A spot of tea first, I think,” Dumbledore said, conjuring steam from the teapot already laid on a set tray. 

 

            He poured a stream of amber into two cups and asked after her taste for milk and sugar before holding up a shortbread biscuit and eyeing it. Smiling kindly, he nudged the piled plate towards Kara and bid her to help herself.

 

            Taking one, Kara held it gingerly, feeling a little flustered in the presence of her old headmaster. Despite being years out of Hogwarts, she felt young and vulnerable again, looking at him with innocent blue eyes as she tried to fight back the flustered flush of being in his company. There had been the rare occasion she’d found herself before him in the past, and his stare had always had an unsettling piercing quality that made Kara feel like he was reading her mind.

 

            Dumbledore took a bite of his own biscuit and washed it down with tea before dusting crumbs off his lap and settling in. He cradled his cup and saucer in his withered hands and watched Kara closely as she took a quick sip of tea to break the tension.

 

            “Tom tells me you’re a valued employee here. How are you liking the work?”

 

            “Oh, um, I’m very grateful to Tom,” Kara truthfully replied. “It’s- I enjoy the routine. And the customers are friendly - mostly.”

 

            He nodded as he sipped his tea and Kara felt as if she was enduring some sort of test, the anticipation of the meaning behind the sudden meeting eating her up. Shifting restlessly, she cleared her throat and resisted the urge to tug at her shirt collar, feeling clammy and flustered.

 

            “Then I’ll be sorry to upset Tom with my reason for visiting you today,” Dumbledore said with a twinkle of amusement in his pale blue eyes.

 

            Eyebrows rising a fraction, Kara jostled her tea as she perched on the edge of her chair. “Sir?”

 

            “There’s a vacant teaching position for the upcoming school year; Professor Babbling is retiring. I’d like you to come and teach Study of Ancient Runes, come September.”

 

            Whatever Kara had been expecting, that wasn’t it. A small sound of surprise escaped her and her expression crumpled as she floundered for a moment.

 

            “Sorry, Professor, I- I’m afraid I don’t quite … understand.”

 

            He smiled kindly, taking another biscuit. “You have a natural talent for the subject, if I remember correctly. And I’m in need of a good teacher. I was hoping you might be interested in filling the position.”

 

            Still somewhat blindsided by the offer, Kara didn’t know what to say. Setting her teacup and saucer down a little shakily, the fine china rattling, she wiped the shortbread crumbs off her lap and tried to process it. Her heart was beating a little quickly, her palms clammy as she ran them over the thighs of her pants, and she stared at Dumbledore with open confusion.

 

            “I … don’t think I’m qualified,” she haltingly replied.

 

            “I believe you would be. Teaching takes an extraordinary amount of patience and tolerance; I think you would manage that better than most, considering the arduous toll you take each month. I believe you’d be a valuable member of staff, and I’ll be frank with you, I did hear about the unfortunate business with the Department of Mysteries. I spoke at length with Professor Croaker about your aptitude, but he couldn’t be persuaded otherwise. But I think you would do well at Hogwarts.”

 

            Mouth opening and closing for a moment, Kara shifted on her seat and swallowed thickly. It sounded too good to be true, too surreal to have fallen in her lap that easily. Things like that, opportunities that great, didn’t fall in the lap of a werewolf. Kara was wary, not wanting to get her hopes up.

 

            “You would have accommodation at the castle, of course. All of your needs would be met by our House Elves. Then there’s the matter of your salary. As a new teacher, it wouldn’t be as high as the other Professor’s but it would be fair; for the week it would amount to twenty-five Galleons.”

 

            Kara’s stomach lurched at the offer. That was more money than she’d made as an Unspeakable, more money than she could’ve hoped for. Wiping down tables at The Leaky Cauldron for five Galleons a week and the Ministry allowance had been enough for Kara to get back on her feet, but twenty-five Galleons a week for an entire year would be life-changing for her. She wouldn’t have to worry about bills and rent and having enough to eat, she wouldn’t have to rely on her family to carry her through rough patches, she would be allowed the freedom of the Forbidden Forest on a full-moon night once more. It was an offer she couldn’t refuse.

 

            “That’s- I- it’s a really generous offer,” Kara replied, flustered and rosy-cheeked as she tried to formulate a coherent sentence. “Thank you, Professor.”

 

            “Does that mean you accept the position?”

 

            “Yes, I think- I think I’d like that very much.”

 

            He smiled and nodded, reaching for the pot of tea and waving his other hand over it as steam curled from the spout. “Good, good. Now, let me explain further.”

 

            Pouring more tea for them both, he went into detail about the job requirements, the curriculum and assignments she was expected to create, the hours of work with the roster of nighttime monitoring for students out of bed. Kara vividly remembered the kind of trouble her Housemates and friends had gotten up to at school and wryly resigned herself to her new role as the one to put a stop to it all. 

 

            She’d never envisioned herself as a teacher, but with the prospect set before her, the idea took root inside her mind. Kara found it growing on her, imagining days spent at the front of a classroom, teaching a curriculum she’d learnt herself only a few years ago, marking essays in her own office and doling out House Points and visiting her favourite spots around the castle. A wave of nostalgia for her Hogwarts days - the good periods - washed over her and a smile curled the corners of her mouth.

 

            Dumbledore left with a handshake and a promise to see her on September 1st for the start of the school year and Kara remained in the room for a few minutes more. Her tea had cooled and her heart was still racing as she limply sat on her armchair and tried to quell the nervous excitement that made her stomach feel like it was doing flips.

 

            Eventually, she gathered up the tray and whisked it back out to the kitchen to be cleaned and dried and used for the next customer. Heading upstairs to help with the housekeeping, Kara made her way through the recently vacated rooms as she stripped beds and remade them with clean sheets, set the broom to sweep and pushed the trolley along, gathering up rubbish and copies of The Daily Prophet and forgotten Knuts and other oddities. 

 

            Her mind was preoccupied with thoughts of Hogwarts and teaching for the remainder of her shift, and she felt a stab of guilt at the thought of telling Tom. His kindness and willingness to take a chance on a werewolf wouldn’t be forgotten, and Kara would’ve hated to leave on bad terms. There was the added relief of two more months of work to put in before the start of term, and she felt as if she’d been dragged out of the gloom that had enshrouded her as she met Alex there after her sister finished work.

 

            Alex was already at a rickety table and chair when Kara arrived downstairs, sipping a pint and visible through a haze of green as she smoked away. Kissing her sister’s cheek in greeting, Kara made her way over to the bar and ordered herself a glass of Berry Ocky Rot , celebrating with the strong fruit wine that she usually avoided on account of it being cheap and giving her a nasty headache. 

 

            “I’ve got a job,” she quietly exclaimed as she claimed a seat, leaning in close to Alex like it was a secret.

 

            Her cheeks were flushed with delight, her blue eyes instilled with some of the happiness that had long since evaded Kara, and she gave her sister’s arm an excited squeeze. Alex lowered her pint, her face furrowing as she swallowed, turning towards Kara.

 

            “Another one?” 

 

            “A good one,” Kara said with a prickle of pride, straightening slightly as she toyed with her fingers.

 

            There was something girlishly youthful about her, eyes wide with surprise and her pale hair curling at her temples and hairline, accentuating the frazzled air about her. She was almost palpably brimming with excitement, leaning back on her chair without a care in the world as Tom and the other bartender worked that night’s shift. Even across the room, Kara kept her voice low to make sure her boss didn’t overhear before she could tell him herself.

 

            “Doing what?”

 

            “You’re looking at the newest Hogwarts Professor of the Study of Ancient Runes.”

 

            Eyebrows rising towards her hairline, Alex was shocked for a moment before her face split with a smile. She wrapped her in a quick hug, congratulating her with evident relief, some of the worry she harboured for her sister vanishing in the wake of something stable and good that would put Kara’s mind to use. 

 

            While grateful for her job working the bar and providing housekeeping for the short-term guests, Kara would be lying if she said she didn’t miss the intellectual workout of Arithmancy and decoding Ancient Runes at the Department of Mysteries. Being an Unspeakable had called to the parts of her that wanted to uncover the secrets of magic and she missed doing something stimulating, even if bartending had offered her more stability and socialising than she’d had in a while. 

 

            “Well done,” Alex said with a grin, “you didn’t even tell me you applied.”

 

            “Oh, well, I didn’t,” Kara said as her face furrowed. “Dumbledore just sent me a letter yesterday asking to meet with him today and he just … sprung it on me, I suppose. I guess he hasn’t had much luck with the other applicants or whoever’s on his list but don’t look a smoking dragon in the mouth, right?”

 

            Nodding sagely, her sister finished off her beer and stated they were going to celebrate. Fetching two shots of Pinnock’s Gigglewater, an imported liquor from America that Alex had recently become obsessed with in her efforts to align herself with her home country, they clinked their glasses and knocked them back quickly. It burned and had them both pink-cheeked with laughter once the alcohol hit.

 

            Feeling lighter than she had in months, Kara quickly became inebriated as they celebrated her new job and her new funds. Dumbledore had casually mentioned the weekly pay for a Professor, even on school holidays, which she could expect to be deposited in her Gringotts vault by the end of the week to help her prepare her class curriculums and buy any necessary material. It was a larger sum than Kara had received in a while and she spent it wisely.

 

            After breaking the news to Tom the following day, slightly hungover and dishevelled as she apologetically handed in her notice with the intention of working up until the start of term, Kara wandered Diagon Alley and the offshoots of other markets and stalls. She’d already scraped together enough savings to browse the secondhand clothing store for a few new robes, settling on a frost blue one and another in a comforting tan, finding a slightly moth-eaten tweed suit and a battered briefcase as well to look the part of a Professor. 

 

            At only twenty-four, Kara’s face still held some of the roundness of youth, although lingering signs of being underfed gave her a leanness that would only be exacerbated as her bone structure settled. With the addition of numerous scars and the increasing amount of grey hairs, she could pass for older than she was and hoped that would provide an air of authority that her nervous demeanour lacked.

 

            Buying numerous books to add to her old textbooks, Kara spent every morning and evening jotting down notes and drafting essay and homework ideas for different years over cups of tea and coffee and plates of buttered toast and bowls of soup. It felt a lot like being at Hogwarts again, or a fresh Unspeakable, translating meanings and jotting down notes, all of it rudimentary to Kara now but still a welcome change from dirty dishes and pulling pints.

 

            Eliza was delighted when she told her the news the Sunday she went over for a roast dinner, sitting in the balmy evening air amidst the hydrangeas and dirigibles, crickets chorusing amidst the plants as they ate strawberries and cream while Alex stood in the front garden, all three of them pretending that they didn’t know she was smoking. Her family were more forgiving with Kara and easily pleased, knowing since the moment she’d joined them that it would never be easy for her. Just graduating from Hogwarts had been a cause to celebrate, and doubly so when she’d actually landed the job at the Ministry. Kara didn’t blame them for doubting; she’d never imagined it for herself either. But now, she could feel Eliza’s palpable relief and pride at the prospect of her daughter’s new career path.

 

            Dumbledore had mentioned she’d be able to visit home most weekends, unless she was otherwise occupied with work duties, and could leave the school grounds outside of school hours if need be. Of course, there would be the holidays as well, with most students going home, save for a handful, which meant Kara would be left with plenty of time to come and go home. Even if she couldn’t manage it every week, it wouldn’t be so long between seeing her sister again, and Alex and Eliza would be reassured she was eating enough and well looked after in the castle she’d spent six years traipsing around.

 

            September 1st arrived quickly and Kara lugged her trunk down the twisting stairs of The Leaky Cauldron with Bastet under her arm to leave. She shook Tom’s hand and promised to stop by before apparating to Hogsmeade. It was a damp day, early fall greeting her as a wave of nostalgia slammed into her, everything green and wet, the road on the outskirts of the village looking up to the castle ahead. She could smell the woodsmoke from the village which gave way to pine as she began the leisurely walk up the long road, enjoying every second of it as she took her time and reminisced.

 

            The gates were open in anticipation of other teachers and the students later on and Kara wearily allowed Filch to search her trunk before levitating it after her. Stepping inside the castle courtyard, she felt like she’d stepped back in time - only a few years, but to a different period altogether. She’d walked through this courtyard to catch carriages pulled by Thestrals or walk to the village on Hogsmeade weekends. And the Entrance Hall, where she’d lurk about, waiting for Lena so she could trail her up to their room, or Alex and her friends so they could throw a Quaffle around on the lawn outside.

 

            Standing in the Entrance Hall for a long minute, a faint smile on her lips as she felt a sense of coming home suffuse her, Kara was disturbed by Professor McGonagall. While she’d never been Kara’s Head of House, there had always been a resigned maternal air about the ageing Professor from her years spent teaching. Kara knew well enough she didn’t suffer idiots and suddenly felt like a fidgety schoolgirl again as she smiled crookedly.

 

            “Professor McGonagall.”

 

            “Miss Danvers. Although, I do think it more appropriate to call each other by our first names, considering we’ll be working alongside one another. Don’t you agree?”

 

            Mouth opening and closing, Kara was mildly startled at the prospect. “Oh, um, right, of course, Professor.”

 

            Arching an eyebrow as a smile twitched the corners of her narrow lips, McGonagall gestured to her as Kara flushed and laughed nervously.

 

            “Let your cat go and I’ll show you to your rooms so you can get settled in before the feast. Albus is at the Ministry on urgent business but sends his regards and hopes you’ll settle in comfortably. He’ll be at the feast tonight, of course. Severus is here already - did you hear about Horace Slughorn’s retirement? No? Well, Severus Snape took over the teaching position for Potions shortly after you graduated.”

 

            Professor McGonagall led Kara up through the castle, towards the North Tower where Classroom 6A was situated on the sixth floor. The Room of Runes, as it was commonly known, was much like any of the other Hogwarts classrooms. Sunlight streamed in through the row of windows, highlighting worn desks, a stocked bookshelf and a pristine chalkboard. The ceilings were vaulted and the warm stone radiated comfort in the morning sunlight as she breathed in the familiar odour of lingering parchment and dust and polish, taking note of the moving portraits that she’d spent hours watching as she tuned out the lessons.

 

            A curved staircase at the front of the classroom led up to her quarters; a private office furnished with a desk and shelves and an old sofa, leading through to a bedroom with an adjoining bathroom. There was plenty of space for Kara and her meagre belongings and Professor McGonagall left her to get settled in. 

 

            Hanging her clothes up in the heavy wooden wardrobe and lining her stack of worn books on the shelves in her office, Kara was filled with pride as she unpacked. She had pots of ink in a few shades and a variety of quills - some expensive and others cheap - framed photos she dotted around the place and bottles of perfume in the bathroom and potted plants from Eliza that she’d cared for over the years. Making it as homely as possible, while very much relying on the faded grandeur of the ancient castle, Kara was pleased with her lodgings by the time her empty steamer trunk was tucked under the bed.

 

            Heading downstairs, she reacquainted herself with the familiar hallways and rooms, visiting the kitchens to say hello to House Elves she remembered fondly, although they were rushed off their feet with preparations for the feast and she was almost overwhelmed with offers and food and drink as she tried to escape. Ending up back outside in the crisp air, Kara followed the path through the grounds, skirting the Greenhouses to stare at the Forbidden Forest. She hadn’t realised how much she’d missed it, the freedom to run, waking up covered in dirt without the phantom pain of fresh wounds that had already been healed to new silver scars.

 

            “Good to be back, eh, Danvers?”

 

            Turning as surprise flitted across her face, Kara’s face creased with a smile at the short witch covered in dirt as she held a newly potted Venomous Tentacula.

 

            “Professor Sprout!” Kara softly exclaimed with delight.

 

            “None of that business; call me Pomona, as long as the children aren’t around. Here, help me with this beauty. I remember you were good with plants in a pinch. How’s your mother doing?”

 

            Falling into easy conversation about Eliza’s work as she helped her old Head settle in the new plant, and then found herself armed with shears to prune Shrivelfig leaves for Potions stores. 

 

            The day passed quickly, and after eating her fill at the feast after standing for Dumbledore’s introduction of her to a sea of students, Kara was exhausted and slept soundly. She didn’t think she’d slept in such a comfortable bed since her old one in the Hufflepuff Common Room. 

 

            Rising early, she sent a letter to Alex with a school owl, enjoying the sunrise from the top of the Owlery, and braced herself for her first lesson. Surprisingly, Kara took to teaching like a natural.

 

 

            September quickly fell into October before she’d even managed to process it, and Kara felt like a completely different person. It was surprising how a month could transform someone, and she was no longer as quiet and solemn when she went home to visit her family, animated with stories about students and teachers gossip and other mishaps she’d heard about. 

 

            She spent hours at her cluttered desk marking homework and almost cried after the first full moon back when she’d traipsed back through the forest with nothing more than scratches and bruises. Filling out more as she added a healthy few pounds, Kara’s subdued cheerfulness resurfaced, the pinched look of worry vanished, and she fell in love with learning all over again as she perused the library and listened to her old Professors talk about their work and some bit of news, treating her like an equal, and not just a werewolf.

 

            Every morning, she did the crossword in The Daily Prophet, able to afford the luxury of a few wasted Knuts a week to pay for it, and watched the Quidditch teams practice from a distance as she walked around a portion of the Black Lake in the evenings. The bracing Scottish air in autumn agreed with her and Kara found her life fulfilled once more.

 

            Soon enough it was late November, snowstorms already blanketing the peaks of the mountains, and Kara braved the icy chill as the full moon arrived. Shivering as she stumbled through the dark forest, only humouring the idea that a transformation inside a dank cell wasn’t that bad, she went as deep as she could before she was left sweating profusely, panting for air as the change came upon her. No one heard her screams as she writhed on the floor, bones breaking and reforming and fur sprouting until a wolf was left in her place.

 

            Kara came to the next morning with a pounding pain in her skull. Blinking at the canopy overhead as it pitched and reeled, a patchwork of wintry grey sky visible between stark branches, she felt a sharp pain in her chest. Her mouth was filled with the taste of blood, her chin coated with it, and her lips thick and numb as she tried to draw in a breath. It was shallow and sharp, the wind gusting back out of her in a plume of white as the frigid temperature of the forest made her shiver. The rancid smell of vomit coated her and she breathed through her mouth as she tried to take stock of things; she’d never woken up after a transformation in such a state before.

 

            Eyes throbbing, Kara tried to sit up and found her shoulder nauseatingly dislocated. Managing to turn onto her knees, she cradled her arm to keep it from hanging limply and fought back the acidic taste of bile rising at the back of her throat. Crawling over to a sturdy trunk, Kara wedged her good shoulder against it and pushed herself up on shaky legs, finding it hard to breathe as she swayed, black spots dancing before her eyes. 

 

            Standing for a moment, she looked down and found herself staring at the oddly shaped mess of her rib cage. Bruised black and showing definite signs of broken ribs, the breath caught at the back of Kara’s throat and she doubled over, vomiting at her feet. Her frozen fingertips tingled as she wiped the sick off her chin, a hiss of pain escaping her as what must’ve been a broken jaw flared with white-hot pain at her touch.

 

            It took her a lot longer to traverse the usual distance to the edge of the Forbidden Forest, where her clothes had been left the night before, and Kara couldn’t do more than pull her robe on. Her whole body hurt and her vision furred at the edges from the pain as she bundled up the rest of her clothes, padding barefoot to the tunnel leading into the castle. 

 

            Kara had made that trip so many times before that it didn’t matter if she felt like she was about to pass out. Stiff and feverish, she staggered into the Hospital Wing an hour later than she should’ve, the late sunrise already shaving hours off her day and making it risky for her to wander in like a stray. Madam Pomfrey spotted her immediately, closing the door to her storeroom and clicking her tongue.

 

            “I was about to come and look for you,” she chided Kara as if she was still one of her students. “I thought you might’ve gotten lost. Sit, sit. Let me take a look at you. Dear me, you’re as pale as any of the ghosts.”

 

            “Poppy, I-“ Kara started, her voice shaky and faint. 

 

            She cut off as she spluttered up a mouthful of fresh blood, breathing raggedly as she pressed a hand to her chest through her cloak. Her vision dimmed and there was a ringing in her ears as the school Healer spoke, distant and incomprehensible.

 

            Her hands were warm as she guided Kara down onto the narrow bed and drew the curtains around them for privacy. Parting the robe, she blanched and her mouth thinned as she used her magic to assess the damage.

 

            “You ought to go to St. Mungo’s for this,” Madam Pomfrey concluded after a moment. “Bones I can fix, wounds I can heal, but it looks like you’ve been half-trampled to death and I’m not confident there’s no internal damage. Best leave it up to the experts, dear. I’ll call for a Mediwizard.”

 

            “There’s no need-” Kara choked, a stabbing pain in her chest as she fought for breath to continue. “I’ll Floo-“

 

            “In your state? I wouldn’t trust you to make it to the next grate in one piece. Stay put and let me get some help.”

 

            As embarrassing as it was to need assistance, Kara obeyed and waited patiently as Madam Pomfrey did what she could until a Mediwizard arrived, wheelchair in tow. She was made to sit in it, her wand and glasses in her pockets and her clothes and shoes in her lap, and Kara slurred a vague goodbye and thank you to Madam Pomfrey before she was escorted to St. Mungo’s, feeling grateful it wasn’t on a stretcher, which was the only way it could’ve been more humiliating. Only, she found out she was wrong as she was wheeled through the waiting room to the Admissions Department to be checked in.

 

            “Twenty-four-year-old werewolf,” her Mediwizard wearily recited from the clipboard he’d filled out in the Hospital Wing. “Looks like internal bleeding. It’s not spell-based but-“

 

            “Hey.”

 

            Kara visibly paled as she turned to find Lena hurriedly pushing past another Healer and patient, dressed in her scrubs and sea-green robes. Despite the curt sound of her voice, she seemed otherwise unbothered as her eyes raked over Kara, and stopped in front of the Mediwizard. Crouching in front of her, Lena frowned as she flicked the lit tip of her wand across Kara’s pupils, watching them constrict and dilate before she tucked it in her pocket and then held a hand out for the clipboard the Mediwizard was holding. She didn’t even look at him, her eyes piercing Kara as they stared at each other, weighted.

 

            “I’ll take this one.”

 

            “But she-“

 

            Now Lena raised her eyes to the man’s and gave him a cutting look of impatient irritation. “I’ve treated her before on the Dai Llewellyn ward. It was a full moon last night; she’s my patient.”

 

            At Lena’s sharp tone, he relinquished the clipboard and muttered under his breath, while Lena quickly towed away her patient. Making for the elevators, Lena snagged the arm of a passing nurse and rattled off a string of details and medical jargon to finish checking Kara in that she was too far gone to understand herself. A cough wracked her as they waited for the elevator and she spat blood all over the toes of her scuffed boots, feeling her strength sap as she wilted in the wheelchair.

 

            Eventually, the elevator clanged to a stop on the ground floor and Lena wheeled them inside, not waiting for anyone else as she jammed her finger into the button for the Fourth Floor. It was suddenly silent as the sounds of the hospital faded behind the metal grille, and Kara closed her eyes at the suffocating awkwardness blanketing them.

 

            “What happened?” Lena asked after a long minute, her voice curt.

 

            “Don’t … know,” Kara breathlessly rasped, her face crumpling as she tried to inhale. “Centaur, I think. Woke up … like this.”

 

            Wearily sighing, Lena gripped the handles of the wheelchair and towed Kara out of the elevator a moment later. They made their way down a long corridor to a ward for Charms-related care, where Lena started asking for assistance. Two nurses helped Kara onto the bed and one drew the curtain as Lena requested items, hooking a wheeled trolley with her foot and drawing it closer.

 

            Standing over Kara, who was grey-faced now and mottled with bruises, Lena took her pulse as she stared down at the watch on her left wrist, measuring the time. Then she unwound the stethoscope from around her neck and worked the cold disc underneath the neck of Kara’s robe, listening to the left and right sides of her chest. Mouth turning down at the corners, Lena cast a glance at one of the nurses.

 

            “Her pulse is weak. Get me a Restorative Draught. And two vials of Blood-Replenishing and one Sleeping. She has a pneumothorax too; fetch Healer Arias for me.”

 

            Turning her attention back to Kara, Lena’s eyes raked over her damp robe and the blood and vomit caked to Kara’s ashen skin. Her mouth turned down at the corners and she glanced at another nurse.

 

            “Fetch me a robe for her, please. Let’s clean you up so I can see what’s underneath.”

 

            She directed the last part at Kara, and the other nurse piped up with the offer to do it, as was usually the case for nurses. Lena put her back to the nurse, shoulders hunched and a stubborn flicker in her eyes as she defensively insisted on doing it herself.

 

            Waving her wand to vanish the worst, Lena conjured water into a metal basin on the trolley and heated it with a dismissive flick of her wand. Dunking a cloth into the water, she wrung it out and then hesitated before gingerly touching two fingertips to Kara’s chin to steady her as she wiped away the grime. It hurt like hell and Kara clenched her teeth, which was also a bad idea, pain knifing through her jaw.

 

            Exhaling sharply through her teeth, she screwed her eyes shut - not that she could make out much without her glasses - and let Lena get on with business. Her old friend tried her hardest to be gentle as she rinsed away blood and vomit until the water was pink and cool. The nurse was back a few minutes later with a clean hospital robe for her and everything seemed to blur after that.

 

            Stretched out on the bed, an IV drip started for the Restorative Draught with a pinch as Lena slid a needle beneath the skin, Kara coughed and gasped and struggled to breathe her way through the medical examination. Fingers gently probing along with the tip of her wand, Lena correctly identified the dislocated shoulder that had left Kara’s arm hanging uselessly, and then the broken collarbone that had shifted downwards and pierced the top of her left lung, along with the ribs smashed to pieces and the fractured sternum. 

 

            Given copious amounts of some bitter potion for pain, Kara was blissfully relaxed as she watched Lena work with a slack-jawed air of awe. A hawkish look of narrow-eyed suspicion due to her nearsightedness, Kara watched Lena as she ran her fingers over the bruised mess of her rib cage, the gown parted around her injuries, pointing her wand at the divot where her chest had almost been caved in.

 

            “Ossio Dispersimus,” Lena murmured and Kara felt a disorienting feeling of lightness in her chest as her broken bones were vanished.

 

            Gentle fingers pressed along her rib cage and then Lena’s wand coaxed the broken collarbone back together with a painful wrenching that left Kara biting back a scream of pain as her body tensed, tendons taut and teeth clenched. Then came the second wave of pain as Lena had a nurse brace Kara and then rotated her arm back into the shoulder socket. Vision going black for a second, Kara repaid the help by promptly vomiting down Lena’s front, drenched in sweat and shaking terribly from the ordeal of it all. And that was all by mid-morning.

 

            Sam arrived a short while later, as Lena was unstopping a bottle of Skele-Gro and measuring out a dose for Kara. Exhausted and harried, she greeted Lena with an apologetic grimace before offering Kara a kind smile.

 

            “Kara Danvers.”

 

            “Sam,” she rasped, her voice like gravel as she lay back against the thin pillows, bound in bandages and feeling awful.

 

            “Up to more trouble? What’ve we got?”

 

            “Pneumothorax. Broken collarbone from blunt force snapped it in half and it punctured the left lung. I’ve fixed the collarbone and patched the wound. No signs of internal bleeding. Multiple fractures to her ribs and sternum and a dislocated shoulder too. Displaced rib fractures have been vanished; I’ve bound her chest and have a dose of Skele-Gro here.”

 

            Nodding, Sam listened to Kara’s chest for breath sounds and her heart rate and then gently probed along the bruised jaw as Lena continued to rattle off the other injuries. They were mostly just bruises and a healing salve had already been applied to them, turning from black to violet as they spoke.

 

            “Restorative Draught seems to have done the trick,” Sam approvingly replied, giving Lena’s arm a quick squeeze. “Finish her chart and head off; you should’ve been gone already.”

 

            Nodding, Lena handed Kara the cup of Skele-Gro, and because of her unfortunate luck, it wasn’t Kara’s first time having to choke down the foul potion, followed by the sleeping draught. Even more unfortunate was the news that she’d have to spend the night in St. Mungo’s. Kara had had her fill of hospitals for a lifetime and had been looking forward to going back to her rooms above her classroom, drinking tea and reading books in bed before a feast in the Great Hall.

 

            “Don’t pout about it,” Lena murmured as she ran her finger down the piece of parchment attached to the clipboard, jotting down notes and checking the labels of the potions. “I’ll have the nurse bring you a cup of tea.”

 

            Kara’s lips twitched, “you trying being crushed by a Centaur and try not to pout about it.”

 

            With a quiet scoff of laughter, Lena’s eyebrows rose and fell quickly and she hummed as she jotted down something else. “I’ve endured worse.”

 

            Brow furrowing, Kara’s eyes dropped to the hazy outline of Lena’s left arm. Noticing where her attention was, Lena shook out her arm and flexed her fingers in a nervous tic from the time Lillian had crushed them beneath her book, clearing her throat as she pushed on.

 

            “You have a very interesting method of making amends,” Lena dryly commented, quill moving quickly. “This is the second time you’ve vomited on me out of our last two meetings.”

 

            “I’ll try not to make it a habit.”

 

            “Well, I wouldn’t want to spoil your fun.”

 

            Closing her eyes as she smiled wanly, Kara rubbed her forehead and then wrinkled her nose at the feeling in her chest. It felt like painful splinters beneath the skin and Kara shifted with discomfort. That was only the beginning of it.

 

            Finishing off her paperwork, Lena set the chart at the end of Kara’s bed and stood there for a moment, staring at her. Kara could just make out the hazy features of her gripping the end of the bed rail. Even though she couldn’t read Lena’s expression, Kara could envision the brooding look with perfect clarity as her chest twinged - this time she didn’t think it was from the Skele-Gro.

 

            “Well, I’m about an hour overdue to clock out so … get some rest,” Lena awkwardly said, glancing down at her watch. 

 

            “Thank you, Lena,” Kara mumbled.

 

            Hesitating, Lena nodded and then vanished behind the curtain with nothing more than the scuff of her shoes. Staring up at the drab ceiling as pale sunlight filtered through the window behind her, Kara tried to ignore the growing discomfort of regrowing the missing shards of her ribs.

 

            She ended up drifting in and out of sleep, bone-tired from her sleepless night cavorting around the forest, potentially dallying with Centaurs, and woke frequently to the growing pain in her chest. The intern Healer managing her case in Lena’s absence administered another potion to manage her pain after a lunch of bland chicken and boiled vegetables, and a nurse brought her a cup of tea which was pathetically weak and barely lukewarm. She was left to her own devices then until sleep claimed her again. 

 

            The ward was the deep blue of an early dusk when she woke again. It was boring, being bedbound in a hospital without her things, and after laying there for a while, Kara fumbled for her glasses and listened to the quiet murmurs of Healers and patients behind the curtain blocking her from sight. Her dinner was brought to her and she picked at it as night was ushered in, bringing darkness and a chill to the ward, and Kara thought about the treacle pudding and hot coffee she could be having at that very moment if her unconscious mind had known not to meddle with other creatures.

 

            Massaging the tender, bandage-wrapped mass of her chest as her tongue ran over her sore teeth, making sure they were all still there, Kara fought back a wave of nausea at the pain that suffused her. Regrowing bones was a nasty business and it left her covered in a sheen of sweat as her newly healed lungs dragged shallow breaths in and out. She was about due for another potion and wasn’t too proud to reject it as the Skele-Gro came into full effect.

 

            Jaw clamped shut and face pinched with pain as she lay tensed on the bed, her eyes flew wide open when the curtain was pulled back a minute later. Instead of a nurse, she found herself looking at Lena, back again, her sea-green Healer robes thrown over a cream turtleneck and a weary slump to her shoulders. It was almost ten o’clock, and definitely not time for her next shift yet.

 

            “Here,” Lena said, skipping the greeting to set down a steaming paper cup of tea. 

 

            It was a builder’s brew, deliciously strong with two sugars, the way Kara took it, the way Lena remembered she took it. Struggling to sit up, Kara blinked dumbfoundedly, her face grey and sweaty, her pale curls bedraggled around her narrow face.

 

            “Thank you. I thought you’d gone.”

 

            “I was on-call. Just my luck.”

 

            “Oh.”

 

            Lena had a coffee for herself, black and bitter, and she took a sip before perching on the edge of Kara’s bed. They stared at each other for a moment and Lena reached into her pocket, her fingers curling around something before she dropped it in Kara’s lap. It was a neatly packaged Chocolate Frog box.

 

            A small choked sound escaped Kara and she didn’t know whether she wanted to laugh or cry. Suddenly, she felt sixteen years old again, waking in the Hospital Wing after a full moon to Lena at her bedside. 

 

            Setting her cup of tea aside, Kara opened the box with shaky hands and trapped the hopping frog beneath her palm, killing the enchantment, before turning over the card. 

 

            “Who’d you get?”

 

            Turning the card between deft fingers, Kara’s lips twitched wryly as she quickly dashed her arm across her wet eyes. “Elizabeth Walsh. She created Fiendfyre-“

 

            “I know who she is,” Lena quickly interrupted, her voice low and curt.

 

            “Of course you do. I always used to think you knew the answer to everything.”

 

            Stiff and pale, Lena raised her cup to her lips, which barely moved as she spoke. “Not everything.”

 

            Watching her closely, Kara knew there was something off about her without Lena even having to say it. After years of seeing her friend suffer in silence over things she kept close to her chest, Kara could spot Lena’s tells from a mile off, see the tension in her slope or her shoulders, the twitching muscle in her jaw as she clenched her teeth, the oddly strained note in her voice. There were dark circles under her eyes from a long shift and not enough sleep and Lena rubbed them with her thumb.

 

            “Shouldn’t you be sleeping?”

 

            “Ideally,” Lena wearily replied, draining the rest of her coffee. “So should you.”

 

            Kara’s lips were a bloodless line and she had a sip of tea to fortify herself, sugar humming on her tongue as she swallowed. The heat warmed its way down her throat but couldn’t cut through the pain in her chest. Making a low sound of agreement at the back of her throat, Kara rubbed her chest, feeling clammy and lightheaded.

 

            “Once I’ve had my potion.”

 

            Lena glanced sideways at her then, blinking herself out of whatever reverie she’d been in. Her lips parted and she quickly climbed off the bed, so wrapped up in how easy it was to talk to Kara, the years falling away until it was just the two of them.

 

            Shaking her head slightly, Lena hesitated and then turned, vanishing through the curtain and returning five minutes later with a vial in hand. She handed it over to Kara and made a note on her chart, checking the time and then watching her drink it.

 

            “Get some rest.”

 

            “You too,” Kara murmured as the potion immediately cut through her, the grimace smoothing out into blissful weightlessness.

 

            She sank back against the pillows and Lena lingered a moment later before she left. Waiting for her mind to slow enough to let sleep creep back in, Kara turned over the Chocolate Frog card in her hand, running her thumb over the moving photo and letting her mind dwell on the layered conversation with Lena.

 

            As devastatingly embarrassing as it had been for her to admit the truth last time, only to have Lena confirm it and then leave, there was a sense of peace in seeing her again. It almost made Kara feel lighter, like she’d gotten through the hard part of seeing her old friend again. The truth was out, and while that had only made her feel worse, she was better off knowing the real reason than the assumptions she’d conjured up from her own ideas.

 

            Sighing, she grimaced and turned the card over as she glanced at it and her stomach quickly jolted. Sitting up quickly and reaching for her wand for better illumination, Kara held it over the image of a familiar-looking woman. Perhaps a decade older, yes, and with copper hair that wasn’t quite so stark against her pale skin, was a woman that was the spitting image of Lena. 

 

            Kara felt her stomach drop as she was shot through with understanding, a lump constricting her throat as her eyes rose to the spot where Lena had walked through the curtains. She’d never talked about her mother much, only Lillian and only on occasion, but Kara knew she was dead. The immediate change in Lena’s demeanour as soon as she’d said the name of the woman on the card sent a stab of pity through Kara as she imagined the pain of grieving for one mother while suffering the abuse of the only one she had left.

 

            Murmuring a quiet Nox, Kara set her wand down and removed her glasses before turning onto her side. Curling her fingers around the card of Lena’s mother, she was still thinking about her and how differently her daughter might have turned out when she drifted off to sleep.

 

            Waking early the next morning after a fitful sleep and a sharp chest pain, Kara felt well-rested and whole. Sitting up against the thin pillows, she waited for rounds so she could be discharged, wondering if she’d made her ten o’clock class, and was surprised when Lena walked in a short while later.

 

            “You’re still here?” she softly exclaimed.

 

            Fixing her with a piercing stare, the corner of her mouth twitching with faint amusement, Lena arched an eyebrow. “Long night. I’m heading out after I’m done here.”

 

            “Oh.”

 

            She was silent then as Lena ran through her quick examination, checking her pupillary response and her pulse and breath sounds. After gently probing all of the areas where Kara had suffered fractures, and applying more of the bruise-healing salve, Lena declared her fit to go home.

 

            Setting down the tin of the salve on the nightstand beside the bed, Lena’s movement stilled as her eyes snagged on the card. Kara had set it there this morning and the moving photo was on display for them to see. Cocking her head to the side, she looked up at Lena.

 

            “She was your mum?”

 

            “Mhm,” Lena tightly hummed.

 

            Picking up the card, Lena studied it for a moment and her throat bobbed with the effort it took for her to swallow. Turning it over, Lena set it face down on the nightstand again and drew in a shaky breath.

 

            “You never told me much about her. How old were you?”

 

            “Four.”

 

            “What happened?”

 

            Turning to look at her, a furrow between her eyebrows and a brooding look of melancholy and grief in her eyes, Lena didn’t respond. Kara thought she’d overstepped, pushing the boundary between them, asking the questions she’d never asked even when they’d been closer than ever at Hogwarts. But it was different now. They were adults, they’d already hurt each other and had too many secrets divulged to really hurt each other anymore. Things didn’t hold the same weight for them now; you couldn’t reject someone who wasn’t in your life.

 

            “She drowned.”

 

            Lena’s answer was so quiet that Kara barely heard her. She didn’t elaborate or offer any other words, just stared at the back of the Chocolate Frog card with the information about her mother’s contribution to magic. The discovery of a dangerous spell had spread through circles or Dark Wizards, courtesy of Lionel Luthor in his heyday, when Elizabeth had just been an ambitious potioneer trying to create a flame that wouldn’t extinguish while she brewed her potions, tweaking the spell for Gubrathian fire and stumbling upon something far more sinister. Kara wasn’t to know all of that though as Lena brooded over the information she’d dug up over the years from snide comments from Lillian and snippets from Lex. And Kara didn’t need to know her mother had spiralled down to an unthinkable low and tried to drown Lena too.

 

            “You’re free to go,” Lena eventually said.

 

            Nodding, not knowing what else to say or do, Kara climbed off the edge of the bed. She was already dressed in her rumpled clothes from a few days ago and dragged on her bloodstained robe, fiddling with the fastenings to prolong the moment. Struck with the sudden realisation she didn’t want to say goodbye, a lump caught in Kara’s throat and she fought to swallow it down, inhaling shakily as she summoned some courage.

 

            “Could I see you again?” Kara asked, halting and uncertain.

 

            Lena’s nimble fingers stilled as she looked up through her lashes, expression unreadable. Her mouth twitched slightly at the corners and she softly cleared her throat, somewhat haughty as she swallowed her old wounded pride.

 

            “If you’d like.”

 

            The tightness in Kara’s chest loosened and her shoulders dropped slightly. She hadn’t expected any eagerness or delight on Lena’s behalf and thought it was a magnanimous concession, if a little awkward as their eyes met and Kara watched Lena’s throat bob. 

 

            Neither of them knew how to break the silence and Lena coughed as she tried to clear her throat. After a moment of hesitation, Kara quickly bridged the short distance between them and wrapped Lena in a tight hug, catching them both by surprise.

 

            Lena didn’t know how long it had been since someone had hugged her like that. Someone who knew almost everything about her and chose to love her in spite of it all. Probably not since Kara had hugged her last. She found her eyes stinging, although she refused to cry, and didn’t know whether it was for herself or the woman in her arms. Eyes closed, savouring the moment like a drowning woman resurfacing for air, Kara held on a moment too long.

 

            “What was that for?” Lena warily asked when she stepped back.

 

            Chewing on the inside of her cheek for a moment, Kara settled on the simple truth, her voice small and shy. “I’ve just really missed you.”

Chapter 20

            Christmas arrived swiftly with snowy days at Hogwarts and distracted students who were eager to go home for the holidays and didn’t turn in their homework. Kara wearily doled out detentions and stripped House Points as easily as she gave them, although she wasn’t too harsh on any of them, given her own enjoyment at being at Hogwarts for Christmas again. While she’d hated it at school at first, she’d become incredibly fond of the place over the years, and the large decorated trees and enchanted snow in the Great Hall felt homely to her.

 

            Kara planned on going home for Christmas but lingered at Hogwarts a few days after the term had ended to catch up on her essays to mark and help out with the few students staying behind. On her last day, Kara held a friendly Quidditch match for those who wanted to join in, claiming her old position as a Beater and enjoying the freezing morning in the air, until she was as red-cheeked as the other students by the time they’d called it a day. 

 

            Damp and exhausted, she went back to her rooms to have a hot bath and change into dry clothes and then went to the kitchens for tea and mince pies. A book came with her, along with letter-writing materials that she didn’t touch as she breathed in the smell of Christmas ham and sizzling oil as the House Elves worked around her out of the way corner, the haze of steam warming her throat as she jotted down a few notes for a revised lesson plan and eyed the blank parchment and sealing wax.

 

            Eventually, after she’d exhausted all other pretences of work and her book wasn’t holding her interest, she pulled a blank sheet towards her. Dipping the quill in ink, Kara hesitated, anxiously chewing on her lip as she tried to think of what to write. It used to be easy to write letters to Lena when they were apart over the holidays, but now she didn’t know what to say. In the end, she cut straight to the point and steeled herself against potential rejection.

 

I’ll be home tomorrow for the rest of Christmas and New Year. I’d like to see you again if you’re free.

 

-K 

 

            Folding the parchment in on itself, Kara dribbled yellow wax over the folded edge and then gathered up her things. Saying goodbye to the House Elves as she passed back through, apologetically shaking off the insistences that she stay, Kara walked to the Owlery and borrowed one of the school owls to send her letter.

 

            Afterwards, she packed her bag with the essentials for home and then went to the staff room for coffee and biscuits with the few remaining Professors and Hogwarts staff. Hagrid had made a batch of his rock cakes as a Christmas treat and Kara politely nursed one after the initial fear that she’d broken a tooth with the first bite.

 

            They all went down to the Great Hall for dinner after that, the sky outside already dark despite the early hour, and Kara was worn out by the time she’d eaten her fill. Talking to a few of her students as she wandered up to her rooms, she left them with well wishes for the holidays and retired for the night, laying in bed with Bastet curled up on her lap and moonlight slanting in through a gap in the curtains. It wasn’t quite yet full.

 

            The next morning, Kara bundled up warmly against the weather and stopped by the staff room to say her goodbyes before leaving. Her satchel had been extended and she had it slung over one shoulder with Bastet cradled in her arms, the cat as content as a baby as Kara’s body heat provided a nice defence against the sleet as they left. 

 

            Making the walk down to the gates of the Hogwarts grounds so she could apparate, Kara amounted to nothing more than a worn-out old coat covered by a robe, fogged up glasses from her warm breath, and a long scarf in Hufflepuff colours from her school days. The landscape around her was austere and drab and she was quick as she walked, her lungs burning from the cold until she passed through the gates and turned on her heel.

 

            The milder climate of Cornwall greeted her a moment later and Kara grinned as she made her way across the field behind their cottage and climbed over the garden fence. Arriving home amidst Eliza’s Fanged Geraniums, Kara dodged a bite and set Bastet down to start on the mice that always snuck in, and the few gnomes as well. 

 

            Making her way to the back door, Kara jerked it open and stomped her feet on the mat as she breathed in the smell of simmering meat and fragrant herbs.

 

            “Hello? I’m home.”

 

            Movement sounded from the living room and Eliza ducked her head into the hallway before brightening up. Wrapping her cardigan tighter around herself, she came to hug her daughter.

 

            “Hello, sweetheart.”

 

            “Merlin, it’s warm in here. I practically had to brave a snowstorm to get past the castle wards,” Kara said, stamping her feet as she regained the feeling in them. 

 

            Shedding her layers and making herself at home, she brewed the tea while Eliza fixed some cold cuts of meat and asked about school. Despite Kara making it home at least a couple of times a month, Eliza was always anxious about how she was doing, if she was liking the work and had settled in okay. Kara soothed her concerns every time and didn’t know how to explain to Eliza that it was the most stable and reliable thing she’d had since she’d been at Hogwarts as a student. There was a familiar comfort to the routine of school and Kara welcomed it back with fonder feelings than her actual school days with bullies and secret friends.

 

            Alex came over with Kelly later on and the four of them had dinner before the couple left and Kara enjoyed a quiet night listening to the Wizarding Wireless Radio with her mum, breathing in the smell of pine from the decorated Christmas tree with gifts already piled underneath. Kara had managed to spend her last day away from Hogwarts shopping in Hogsmeade and Diagon Alley and had added her own to the pile as well, delighted at the prospect of spoiling her family this year. And for all her love of Hogwarts, there was something to be said for being home for Christmas when she fell asleep in her own bed. The only thing that could’ve made it better was if there wasn’t a full moon on the 27th.

 

            As it was, Kara woke on Christmas Day already feeling the effects of the approaching full moon. She was pale and a little shaky as she drank her coffee and opened her gifts, Alex and Kelly arriving early so they could be there and have breakfast with them before heading to the latter’s family for lunch. Kara received a new robe from Eliza, a wireless radio from Alex and a new quill from Kelly. In return, she’d bought her mother a brand new pair of dragonhide gloves for gardening, her sister a Mokeskin pouch for collecting evidence on the job, and a few skeins of never-tangle wool she’d splurged on at Spindlewarp’s Wool Shop for Kelly’s newfound hobby of crochet.

 

            With just her and Eliza for lunch, Kara helped her prep for dinner and they ate soft cheeses with crackers and got started on the spiked eggnog a little early before a letter arrived on the leg of a familiar black owl and Kara went upstairs to her room to read it. Feeling a little queasy, although that could’ve been from the impending transformation, Kara sat on the edge of her bed and opened the note, reading it quickly.

 

The 29th, if you’re feeling better.

 

-L

 

            The breath caught in Kara’s throat at the idea of Lena keeping track of the moon’s cycle for her sake and she swallowed thickly before memorising the address noted and hiding the letter in her bag. She felt nervous at the prospect of seeing Lena again but was relieved that she hadn’t been outright rejected, and was consumed by thoughts of seeing her old friend again for the rest of Christmas Day. 

 

            On Boxing Day, she went to Alex and Kelly’s flat for drinks with their friends, reuniting with all of the ones she hadn’t seen in a while and eagerly filling them in on her job. Mike was there and her awkwardness quickly turned into keen relief as she watched him kiss Imra, as if trying to hurt Kara’s feelings, but she was glad his attention had moved on and hoped Imra was happier than she’d been while sleeping with him. She played Exploding Snap with Nia and Querl at the coffee table while drinking wine and trying to put on a brave face in lieu of the full moon tomorrow, and the hollow fatigue that had settled into her bones. 

 

            Kara ended up in the cluttered spare room at her sister’s flat to sleep while the gathering went on behind the thin door. Listening to the sound of Alex’s vinyls and the low murmur of voices, Kara drifted off to sleep and didn’t wake until late the following morning. She made scrambled eggs and strong coffee for those that remained, James asleep on the sofa and Winn’s small frame curled up on an armchair.

 

            Hugging everyone goodbye and wearily placating Alex that she could come and visit tomorrow, Kara went home to Eliza’s to await her evening. Brooding about the place with an increasing feeling of nausea, she eventually gathered her things and kissed her mother goodbye before Flooing to St. Mungo’s and enduring the process of checking in and the medical examination and the trip down to the cells in her robe, before it was taken from her and she was left shivering in the dank cell. The smell of the place was stomach-turning and Kara hadn’t gotten used to the ascetic bleach and blood and sweat and fear over the years; she’d only added to it.

 

            Waking the next morning with a pang of grief that cut so deeply that her blurry vision became even more so as her eyes filled with tears, Kara was awkwardly comforted by the Healer assigned to her. In her exhausted state of pain, she’d woken with the keen sense of something missing and it didn’t take her long after regaining consciousness to realise that it had been disappointment at waking up alone again after the last time. And it wasn’t just waking up alone, because her family would’ve come if she’d let them or asked them to, but rather the surprise of having Lena at her bedside after healing her wounds and filling her with that comfort of their Hogwarts days, only to lose it again the next month. Emotions heightened and her body spent of all energy, it had blindsided Kara at her most vulnerable.

 

            Discharged a short while later, fresh bandages wrapping her waist from the new scars on her right obliques, Kara went home and quickly extracted herself from Eliza’s protective fluttering about. Showering and slipping straight into bed, Kara slept until noon and then sat cross-legged at the desk wedged into the room to write in her journal. 

 

            She was halfway through trying to untangle her jumbled thoughts when the door opened. Turning on the chair, Kara looked at her sister and hurriedly shut her journal before rubbing her eyes, ink dried on her fingers and a peaky pallor to her face. Despite how much she’d slept, she still had dark circles under her eyes and never quite felt rested after a full moon.

 

            “How’re you feeling?” Alex asked, collapsing onto her old bed.

 

            “Fine.”

 

            “What’re you doing?”

 

“Just … journaling.”

 

            Alex’s eyes landed on the closed diary and her lips twitched with amusement as she raised her eyebrows. “You’re still doing that? Mum sent me up to see if you’re hungry. There are still some leftovers in the fridge.”

 

            “Sure.”

 

            Quiet with apprehension for the rest of the day, assuring her family that she was fine and just tired, although they were far too perceptive to fully believe her, Kara read on the sofa and made pumpkin pie with Eliza, memories of home sweeping in with the American dessert. Alex offered a game of chess and Kara distractedly beat her and went to bed shortly after eating dinner and washing up.

 

            The next day, she woke feeling nervous and hovered around the place, sorting out the linen cupboard and scrubbing the floors clean as a distraction while Eliza tended to her garden. Around lunchtime, Kara ate her sandwich and glanced at her watch, clearing her throat and taking a sip of pumpkin juice as she aimed for nonchalance.

 

            “I might go to Diagon Alley for a bit. Pick up a few things, say hello to Tom.”

 

            “Make sure you wrap up; it’ll be cold in London.”

 

            Nodding and mumbling that she would, Kara finished off her lunch and went upstairs to get ready. She wore one of her nicer jumpers, not quite as worn as the others, and donned her new robe over her beloved coat, hid a bottle of Firewhisky amidst the folds and made her way downstairs. Ducking her head into the kitchen, she said goodbye to Eliza and stepped out onto the street before Apparating to the address Lena had given her.

 

            Finding herself on the landing of dark wood and antique crown moulding, Kara checked the door numbers and knocked on the one matching the letter. Her heart was fluttering nervously in her chest and she nudged her glasses up her nose, straightening from her anxious hunch as she waited. Soft footsteps approached the door and it was opened a moment later by Lena, looking tired but more put together than Kara.

 

            “Hi,” Kara murmured.

 

            “Hi,” Lena replied, leaning against the door a moment before stepping back to open it wider. “Come in.”

 

            “Thanks. I, uh, I didn’t know what time to come. I wasn’t sure if you had work last night so I thought I’d let you sleep a bit.”

 

            Lena’s lips twitched slightly and Kara’s stomach jolted at the light sage of her eyes, so scrutinising as they ran over her shabby form. Shutting the door, Lena let her into the flat and Kara felt a flicker of envy. It was beautiful in a timeless way, all dark wood and muted shades of green and greys, elegantly furnished in a way that gave Kara a glimpse of the life Lena had grown up with, just tailored a little to suit her better. Even now, she wore a fitted black turtleneck and wide leather pants that leached the colour from her and bordered between proper and just a little bit edgy.

 

            “I got home just after midnight.”

 

            Nodding, Kara looked around the place as the tension between them thickened. “Nice flat.”

 

            Lena nodded in return, arms folding across her chest as she watched her, a muscle twitching in her jaw. Meeting her gaze, Kara blinked and then scrambled into the folds of her robe, drawing the bottle from her coat pocket.

 

            “I brought this. Um … I guess it’s a Christmas present. I don’t know.”

 

            She let out a strained laugh as she thrust the bottle out and Lena’s lips twitched with another smile. Taking the bottle, she turned it in her hands, staring at the label for Old Ogden’s. A slightly bigger smile crossed Lena’s face as she raised an eyebrow.

 

            “Thanks. Fancy a glass?”

 

            “Sure.”

 

            Fetching two glasses, Lena cracked open the bottle and poured more than a standard drink into both before levitating them after her as she gripped the bottle. Kara snagged hers as it drifted past and followed Lena over to the sofa, taking a seat in the armchair instead as she put some space between them. 

 

            Setting down her glass, she shed her robe and cloak and neatly folded them over the arm before picking her glass back up. Lena took a sip of her drink as Kara restlessly shifted, feeling out of place in the obvious wealth of the place

 

            “So, how are you?” Lena curtly asked.

 

            “Good,” Kara murmured, rubbing her forehead as she frowned slightly. “I, uh, I don’t think I told you last time but I’ve been teaching at Hogwarts. The Study of Ancient Runes.”

 

            “I did hear,” Lena murmured. “How do you like it?”

 

            With a quiet huff of laughter, Kara gave her a wry smile. “A lot more than wiping tables.”

 

            “Good.”

 

            “And you? How’re things going?”

 

            Shrugging indifferently, Lena gave her a sharp smile that didn’t reach her eyes before taking another sip of Firewhisky. Kara mirrored her and eased herself back into the armchair.

 

            “As planned.”

 

            A faint furrow formed between Kara’s eyebrows at her response but she didn’t push for an elaboration on what Lena meant. Trying to keep the stilted conversation going, she cleared her throat and tried for a different angle.

 

            “So, what’s it like being a Healer?”

 

            “Everything my mother anticipated for me,” Lena wryly replied, her eyes flashing dangerously as she gestured with her glass and took a sip. “The hours are long, the patients usually intolerable, the work rewarding. I enjoy it.”

 

            Letting out a short laugh, Kara wrinkled her nose, twisting the hem of her jumper in her spare hand as she nursed her Firewhisky in the other.

 

            “I take it it was your mum who punished you with that stint on the Dai Llewelyn ward?”

 

            Blinking as she processed the question, briefly confused until she realised what Kara meant, Lena straightened and squared her shoulders. She momentarily considered lying and agreeing with Kara’s assumption, but something made her hesitate before she answered honestly.

 

            “No,” she murmured, “no, I volunteered. After my first full moon on the ward.”

 

            “Why?”

 

            Lena didn’t answer for a long minute, the tension unbearably thick as they stared at each other. Reaching for the bottle, she finished off her glass and refilled it before leaning across the coffee table to refill Kara’s barely-touched glass as well. 

 

            Setting her glass down, Lena screwed the bottle cap back on and then shifted so her leg was tucked up beneath her and her elbow was propped up on the arm of the sofa. Cheek cupped in her palm, she stared at Kara for another weighted moment.

 

            “I wanted to look after you. We made an oath, and no matter what happened … I always keep my oaths.”

 

            Mouth flattening as her eyebrows pinched together, Kara had no response. Continuing to stare at her, Lena let out a weary sigh and tapped her fingers on the sofa cushions before she continued, curiosity lacing her monotone drawl.

 

            “I’m not really sure what happened there. Things weren’t quite right for a while, were they?”

 

            “No, they weren’t. Even before … everything. I, uh, I think I just-“ Kara stammered, trying to push past the discomfort. “I started to … have feelings for you and it was- with everything … about me it was- I was struggling with how to manage it. I remember the first time I wanted to kiss you. I think that was the beginning of the end. I couldn’t- I couldn’t do it because I didn’t … you were you and I-“

 

            Still and watchful, her whole body tense as she patiently listened to Kara fumble her way through her explanation, Lena felt her chest constrict. 

 

            “You were what?” Lena softly asked.

 

            Wrinkling her nose, Kara rubbed her old scars and felt embarrassment flare up, reddening her cheeks. She sighed and gestured helplessly at her face, at her increasing number of grey hairs.

 

            “A werewolf.”

 

            “I was well aware.”

 

            “Exactly. So you knew there would never be a world where you and I … I mean, we kept everything a secret for a reason.”

 

            “We were kids; it was childish. School rivalries. Stupid stuff like that doesn’t matter in the real world.”

 

            “It does,” Kara rasped. “And it wasn’t just that. People don’t want to touch me, to- to be around me once they know the truth. Half of the Healers look repulsed -“

 

            “Who?” Lena softly demanded, fury in her eyes.

 

            Waving a hand, Kara shook her head. “No one. It doesn’t matter. I never cared what anyone else thought, I just- I wanted you to like me. And I couldn’t bear the thought that you wouldn’t.”

 

            Lena’s mouth opened and closed and she didn’t know how to respond to that, her expression clouding over with conflicting feelings. There was only so far logic and brains could get her with emotional intelligence, and, unfortunately for Lena, her mother hadn’t put nearly as much care into it to help her out. 

 

            After a moment of silence, Kara cleared her throat and hesitantly ventured a question. “Did you mean what you said?”

 

            “What did I say?” Lena countered, coy and a little firm in the face of Kara’s reservations.

 

            Blushing, Kara looked down at her lap, toying with her fingers in a nervous manner Lena recognised from their years of friendship. She’d almost forgotten just how self-conscious and shy Kara could be. It had been years since they’d ever been so vulnerable with each other to be so uncertain, but years since they’d closed each other out as well. It stung a little.

 

            Nudging her glasses up, Kara floundered for a few seconds, mouth opening and closing as she tried to form the words. There were any number of things she could’ve been alluding to and Lena wouldn’t be the one to make it easy for her now.

 

            “You said the love was there … did you- I mean …”

 

            One side of Lena’s mouth hitched up unevenly as she quietly scoffed. Draining her Firewhisky in one large mouthful, she set the glass down heavily and drew the back of her hand across her mouth.

 

            Her lips twisted bitterly and she met Kara’s shadowed stare. “Are you asking me if I loved you? I don’t know how to say how I felt. But … yes, I did love you. Even when I hated you.”

 

            Kara looked as if she’d been winded, her complexion pale and a fragile look of pain on her narrow face. Head ducked down, she rubbed the scarred bridge of her nose and swallowed thickly.
