            “I don’t understand how you-“ Kara started, closing her eyes and lurching to her feet. “You can’t mean that.”

 

            The armchair legs scraped along the floor at the abrupt motion, grating and loud, and she turned her back on Lena. Bracing her palms against her thighs, Lena pushed herself to her feet and crossed the gap between them, snagging Kara’s wrist. 

 

            She pulled her sharply towards her and Kara had no choice but to turn, finding their faces only inches apart. Lena was frowning, her face hard with annoyance as her pale green eyes flitted over Kara’s face.

 

            “Pour Veritaserum down my throat and you’ll see it’s the truth.”

 

            “How could you? After knowing what you knew about me,” Kara asked, her voice cracking as she gestured to her body and the hidden scars. “Someone like you could never have loved someone like me.”

 

            “I just saw you,” Lena hoarsely replied with a helpless shrug. “And that’s the one thing you failed to do for me. You decided you couldn’t love me after deciding what you knew about me, so …”

 

            “You’re wrong,” Kara hoarsely replied, shaking her head. “I never decided to stop loving you. Even now … even now, I-“

 

            Mouth flattening to a bloodless line, Lena looked at her with regret and accusations and old pain as she jerked Kara closer by her wrist. Her mouth turned down at the corners with disappointment and she frowned slightly.

 

            “You don’t know who I am anymore, Kara. You wouldn’t even know the first thing about the person I’ve become.”

 

            “You’re wrong,” Kara whispered, cocking her head to the side, her eyes appraising and perceptive as she smiled slightly, sweet and earnest. “I’ll always know exactly who you are. I could walk out of here right now and not speak to you for fifty years but I would still know you better than anyone else in the world. You’re Lena and I’m Kara and …that has always been enough.”

 

            Lena’s face crumpled with a bewildered look of anguish. How could they still have such an effect on each other after so many years? They’d barely spoken, and when they had it was stilted and aloof, filled with heartbreak and unease, but even now after so many years, there was still the sense that all of their unknowable parts were laid bare to each other. It went against everything Lena had spent her whole life trying to resist, her mother’s cruelty closing her off to this very thing. But she was Kara, and that had always been enough.

 

            Mouth dry and heart racing, Lena stared at Kara and Kara stared back, both of them so close that there was that awareness between them, the moment weighted with anticipation. They could both feel it and it was inevitable, really, ever since that moment they’d slow-danced without any music and Kara had backed out at the last moment. There was that same knowledge that Kara wanted to kiss her and Lena wanted her to, that slight lean in, the hesitation that had Lena gritting her teeth as she baulked at the idea of her dodging it again.

 

            “Don’t be a coward like last time,” Lena murmured through numb lips.

 

            Tensing as she considered Lena’s words, Kara ended up closing the space between them to roughly grab the side of Lena’s face in her free hand. Her lips were firm and unyielding as she kissed her hard enough to bruise, and everything in Lena responded to that touch. 

 

            It felt inevitable in some way and Lena pressed back against her, lips parting, teeth scraping over Kara’s bottom lip as she reached up to loosely wrap her fingers around Kara’s throat. She still had a tight grip on her wrist and Lena felt a flicker of satisfaction to have the upper hand in the moment.

 

            And then Kara started to draw back slightly, their foreheads touching, her breath warm against Lena’s mouth. She was slightly out of breath as she dropped her hand from Lena’s face, her nose gently bumping Lena’s.

 

            “We shouldn’t. Not like this.”

 

            “This is the only way,” Lena replied, similarly unbalanced by the turn of their afternoon. “We decided to keep each other a secret so this is how it is. It’ll never be more than this now.”

 

            She anticipated Kara pulling away and was surprised when she didn’t. Pulling her closer, Kara kissed her until Lena was struggling to breathe, clinging to her with a brimming sense of urgency, of resentment and a need that had been there for so long that it felt odd to finally be given the satisfaction of acknowledging it.

 

            Dropping her hands to the button of Kara’s jeans, Lena quickly undid it and found Kara’s fingers anxiously on top of hers, stilling her movements. Lena could feel the faint tremor in Kara’s body, the kiss breaking off, her pulse jumping at her throat as she squeezed her eyes shut behind the lenses of her askew glasses.

 

            “Don’t take them off,” Kara softly pleaded, her voice shaky with panic.

 

            Lena paused, taking in her bared teeth and pink cheeks, cringing at even having to say it. Gently nosing Kara’s cheek, she kissed her jaw with more tenderness than she wanted to feel. Such a big part of her was still mad, wanted to harden herself against Kara, but even beneath all of that, she just wanted her. 

 

            Dragging her pants down just a fraction, enough room for her hand, Lena kissed Kara as she let all of her pent-up emotions boil over. Cupping the back of her neck, she didn’t let up, driving Kara down onto her sofa, straddling her lap as Kara sighed into her mouth, entirely at her mercy. Lena wasn’t feeling very forgiving.

 

            Somewhere in the process, Lena’s leather pants were peeled off, although she firmly kept her turtleneck on, hot around the neck as Kara did unspeakable things to her in the living room. It was all so fast that they were both grateful they weren’t afforded any time to think past their base desire, to think of the consequences or the meaning. 

 

            Not until Lena was sprawled on the sofa with an arm thrown across her eyes, her chest rising and falling quickly and a hint of colour in her cheeks. Kara was kneeling on the floor, her cheek resting on her thigh, eyes closed with a look of reverent peace on her face.

 

            But then the moment passed and they sobered up enough for Lena to find her underwear and drag them on as Kara buttoned up her jeans. Neither of them spoke as Kara grabbed her coat and pulled it on, a tremor in her hands as she patted down her pockets for her wand and narrowly avoided stepping on her glasses. 

 

            The unbearable tension between them had dissipated but now it was just awkward as Lena raked a hand through her hair, pants in hand and her cool demeanour creeping back in. Clearing her throat, Kara fastened her cloak and looked at the floor before Lena’s feet.

 

            “I, uh- sorry.”

 

            Lena didn’t know how to ask her to stay so she just nodded and watched Kara walk towards the door and step outside. Tossing her leather pants aside, Lena flopped down onto the sofa and banged her head against the back of it as frustration built up in her chest. Running a weary hand over her face, she straightened up and reached for the bottle of Firewhisky, draining what was left in both of their glasses first before refilling it.

 

            Then she brewed a pot of tea and slipped into her office, dragging the chair out and sinking down onto it. Wiping her face on the sleeve of her jumper, she sniffed and cleared her throat as longing washed through her, a deep ache in her chest and the keen sense that she’d just failed somehow. She was unable to feel even an ounce of happiness, even now.

 

            The grey day was beginning to melt into a grey night, the light thin and miserable as Lena opened the drawer to the quill stolen from its hiding spot in her family home. Setting a fresh piece of parchment before her, Lena pressed her lips into a resolute line and started the familiar sentence that had been the pillar of her childhood.

 

            The pot of tea sat beside her on the desk until there was no steam, the contents long grown cold and the light outside the sepia glow of a Dublin lamppost. And just like they had so many other times since she’d left home, the old words on Lena’s left arm reopened as she sought absolution from the comforting punishment of her childhood.

Chapter 21

            Lena decided to put it all behind her as the new year arrived and she pushed her brooding moods behind her and told Andrea and Sam she was fine when they pressed her about it. It had been a one-time thing that Kara had clearly regretted the moment it was over, leaving without a single word, so Lena decided to treat it similarly.

 

            Until a letter arrived at her apartment a week later, courtesy of the nondescript Hogwarts barn owl. Lena didn’t have to question who it was from but she’d needed a drink to quell any potential nerves or the sting of rejection. Opening the letter, she found it sparse but confusing.

 

Hogsmeade weekend 25th January. Can I see you again? Meet me at the Hog’s Head at 9 o’clock if yes.

 

-K

 

            Lena neatly folded the letter away and didn’t offer a reply. She spent the next few weeks contemplating whether she should go or not, especially with the full moon the next day and Kara undoubtedly exhausted and irritable. Inevitably, she went anyway.

 

            Ordering a dusty bottle of Butterbeer at the bar, a nagging sense of familiarity with the barkeeper, Lena retreated to the table near a crackling fireplace and shed her robe. Kara wasn’t there yet and Lena glanced down at her watch, ten minutes early and restless as she wondered if she was going to be stood up. Especially when it hit five past and the only other patron was a hunched old wizard making his way through a pint of ale already.

 

            A few minutes later, the door opened and Kara stepped inside, casting a glance over her shoulder to make sure no students were following her. Her eyes found Lena and her shoulders slumped with relief. Lena couldn’t help but notice how pale she looked, her freckles stark and her bags prominent.

 

            Kara fetched a drink and walked over to the table, sitting down across from her. “Sorry I’m late.”

 

            Nodding, Lena took a sip of her drink. “It’s fine.”

 

            “I, uh, I thought maybe we could talk.”

 

            Lips curling wryly, Lena arched an eyebrow. “About what?”

 

            Wincing, Kara turned to look at the barkeeper, who was wiping down the length of wood in slow methodical motions. Looking down at her lap, she rubbed the bridge of her nose.

 

            “You know what,” she murmured, disgruntled and a little flustered.

 

            “I don’t really have anything to say,” Lena shrugged, “it happened, you clearly regretted it, it’s fine.”

 

            “I never said that.”

 

            Arching an eyebrow, Lena grinned crookedly as her eyes flashed dangerously. “Not everything needs to be said. Although, I am surprised you sent a letter to see me again. I wasn’t afforded the luxury of a goodbye last time.”

 

            “Stop it,” Kara stiffly warned her.

 

            A mild look of amusement crossed Lena’s face and she took a sip of her Butterbeer, wishing she’d gone for something that would sear its way down her throat. Instead, it just felt too sickly sweet to stomach as her insides knotted.

 

            “Is that it then?” she asked, glancing down at her watch. “I’ve just come from a thirty-hour shift so …”

 

            Kara looked down at her lap and pressed her lips into a flat line as she remained silent. Waiting for a response, Lena let out a quiet huff of disbelieving laughter as disappointment knifed through her. Snagging her bottle, she tipped it back, a rueful twist to her lips as she kept her eyes on Kara, and then firmly set it back down. Her chair scraped against the stone floor as she climbed to her feet.

 

            “For the drink,” Lena murmured, setting a few coins down on the scarred table. 

 

            Grabbing her robe, she pulled it on as she walked through the pub, ignoring the weary call from behind her. Sniffing, she hardened herself against the mournful yearning in her chest and shouldered open the door to the breathtaking January air as it assaulted her.

 

            “That’s it?” Kara called out as she barged out of the pub behind her, long legs quickly crossing the space separating her from Lena.

 

            Turning, Lena rubbed her temple as if Kara was giving her a headache. She hadn’t slept in twenty hours, and only then it had been fitful bursts in on-call rooms between patients, and Kara was as pale and exhausted as she was with the full moon so near as well. They didn’t need to be at each other’s throats right now. Advancing towards her, Lena’s mouth thinned grimly.

 

            “Don’t make a scene,” Lena murmured. “Your students are here.”

 

            Eyes darting around as she shrank in on herself, Kara tucked her hair behind her ears and gave Lena a pleading look. But Lena had already turned away from her, taking another step away as she closed her eyes and thought of home.

 

            As Lena turned to Apparate, she felt wiry fingers grip her arm and surprise shot through her as everything stretched and blurred and she found herself on the landing to her flat. And she’d brought Kara with her, both of them windswept and surprised as they stared at each other. 

 

            Mouth opening and closing, Kara looked at her with wide eyes and then rushed forward, pushing Lena back against the door as she kissed her desperately. Lena kissed her back for a second before tearing herself free, turning her head to the side as she closed her eyes and felt Kara’s warm breath on her cheek.

 

            Turning around, Lena opened the door and let herself in, stiff as her heart pounded in her chest. Whatever reaction she’d anticipated from Kara, it hadn’t been that, and Lena’s fingers itched towards her scar as she let herself entertain the prospect that she’d been wrong. Maybe Kara didn’t regret it as much as she’d thought.

 

            “What are you doing?” Lena hissed through her teeth as she whirled around on Kara, whose boots scuffed the floorboards as she hurriedly followed Lena inside before she could slam the door.

 

            “I … I don’t know.”

 

            “Kara. You can’t just- you can’t do what we did and then walk out without a single word, then ask to see me and follow me home and kiss me. You can’t mess with my head like that, it’s not fair. And I don’t have time for this.”

 

            “I know. I’m not- I’m not trying to mess with your head-“

 

            “Then what are you trying to do?”

 

            Digging the heels of her palms into her forehead, Kara squeezed her eyes shut, teeth clenched. “I don’t know! It was confusing for me. I’ve never done that before.”

 

            “Oh,” Lena scoffed, “it was confusing for you? You managed it just fine while you shagged your Housemate.”

 

            A flicker of pain crossed Kara’s face as she dropped her hands, cheeks turning pink as she hunched her shoulders. “Because I didn’t care about him. I- it wasn’t anything like that. He was just there and … he liked me.”

 

            They stared at each other for a long, weighted moment and then Kara sighed. She tipped her head back as her mouth thinned, and then lightly touched her fingers to her stomach.

 

            “I wouldn’t have kept it, you know,” she mumbled, brooding as she frowned, annoyance making her stiff and defensive.

 

            Lena stared at her blankly for a second and Kara eyed her warily, drawing in a shaky breath. “The baby. It would’ve been born by now, if it was possible for me, but … even if I’d had a say, I wouldn’t have kept it.”

 

            “What do you want me to say?” Lena rasped, spreading her hands helplessly. “That I’m glad you didn’t want a baby with him? That the thought of you being with someone else makes me sick with jealousy? That I want to be with you? I can’t say any of that.”

 

            “Why not?”

 

            A spasm of anguish crossed Lena’s face and she smiled unevenly, her eyes flitting around the place. Licking her lips, she shook her head.

 

            “It would be selfish.”

 

            “But true?”

 

            Lena didn’t reply but her mouth thinned and she slightly ducked her head, ashamed. Kara swallowed thickly and shed her robe, moving further into Lena’s flat without invitation and sinking down onto the sofa. Her robe was messily folded beside her and she ran a hand through her curls as Lena turned to study her.

 

            “Even if it was true, it wouldn’t change anything. What, do you want me to be your girlfriend? You- you kiss me one time, you- you fuck me on my sofa and you want me to forget-“

 

            “No,” Kara quickly interrupted, stiffening as she clenched her hands in her lap. “No, that’s not- I don’t want you to be my- my girlfriend.”

 

            She wasn’t lying either, it was just far too trivial a word for what she wanted. 

 

            “Then what do you want?” Lena softly demanded. “What do you want from me?”

 

            “I- I don’t know,” Kara exclaimed, her body tense and voice fraught with frustration and impatience. “I just- I miss you, I- we just- we just stopped talking and I hate that it was over something so … stupid. A misunderstanding. Why didn’t you just tell me?”

 

            The breath was forcefully expelled from Lena’s lungs as she blinked in surprise. “I shouldn’t have had to. I couldn’t tell you. I wanted to but not at the expense of so many people’s safety. I was frightened and you were the only person I had, and then you walked out and you didn’t come back. You didn’t say a word to me; no letters, nothing. ”

 

            “You didn’t send me any letters either,” Kara retorted, angrily swiping at her wet eyes. “I left you a crane. I don’t know if you got it but … I didn’t know what else to say. I was heartbroken to think that you - you of all people - could do something … horrible. I grieved for you more than anyone that died in the war. And I wasn’t even sure if you missed me.”

 

            “Missed you?” Lena choked out, blanched pale with disbelief. “You were the first good thing to happen to me. Maybe the only good thing that’s ever happened to me. You broke my heart.”

 

            “You threatened to hex me and told me to go.”

 

            A flicker of regret crossed Lena’s face and she ducked her head as her mouth thinned. Rubbing her forehead, she let out a weary sigh. “You should be resting.”

 

            “I’m not your patient.”

 

            Letting out a small laugh, Lena walked over to her and dropped down to a knee, her eyes drinking in the haggard sight of Kara with evident concern. She grabbed Kara’s thin wrist and measured her pulse, finding it a little quick but not unusual for a werewolf the day before a full moon. “A good thing too, or it might raise some questions about ethics,” Lena grumbled, although, if given the chance, she would have treated Kara every single time she so much as had a cold.

 

            “Well, I wouldn’t want to make you do anything unethical,” Kara wryly murmured, her eyelids shuttering, a faint sheen of sweat on her forehead.

 

            “Which begs the question, what do you want?”

 

            Her lips barely moved as she replied, her voice a resigned sigh. “You. Just you. I miss talking to you. I know you might not feel the same way, but-”

 

            “You idiot,” Lena cut her off with a sigh before reaching out and crushing her lips against Kara’s in a bruising kiss.

 

 

            From there started a months-long secret affair between the two of them, meeting up whenever they were both free from work, which wasn’t that often with their conflicting schedules. There was also the added difficulty of Kara’s family as well, sometimes feigning detentions to supervise, hallways to monitor and homework to mark so she could leave dinner early and catch Lena before her shift started at St. Mungo’s. 

 

            They didn’t tell a soul, sticking to their old promises to keep each other secret, and they preferred it that way. Despite the glaringly obvious pining, which they both remained blind towards, they refused to think of it as anything but present. There was only a little bit of talk about the past - usually what they’d gotten up to after graduating - and they didn’t dare talk about a future together, their feelings or hopes or anything that could break the fragile peace. They’d hurt each other enough already, in many ways, and they were content to co-exist in their little bubble of secrecy, just as they had at school. The only difference was now they’d succumbed to the tension that had been unbearable to them as teenagers.

 

            It wasn’t always easy though, the awkward moments creeping in at times as they found themselves at an impasse, neither of them capable of saying what they really felt, neither one of them wanting to start an argument over old wounds. There was a lot left unsaid - not just the murkiness between them but from their childhoods, their insecurities, their doubts. Not once had Kara removed a piece of clothing aside from her shoes, not even a little bit, and Lena kept her shirt on no matter what. Even when the weather warmed and she swapped her turtlenecks for linen shirts, Kara scattering a few buttons the first time as she’d torn open the front, Lena didn’t let her shirt slip further than the crook of her elbows where it pooled, still covering the scar on her left arm. 

 

            It was halfway through May before Lena was determined to change that. They kept so much a secret from the outside world, and always had, but the one thing they’d never done was not trust each other. Not until it all went to shit, but they were moving past that now - sort of. Lena wouldn’t say she trusted Kara again, but she trusted her as much as she trusted anyone, which was a marginal improvement from where they’d stood before. 

 

            Kara came over that Saturday, a day spent knocking House Points for duelling in the hallways and trying to decipher bad handwriting leaving her glad to be free of the castle for a while. Lena had finished work at ten the night before and slept through to the early sunrise of spring, awaiting Kara’s arrival that evening. The sky was pink when she knocked on the door, wearing a worn cotton shirt with a waistcoat over the top, looking every inch the Professor, right down to her brogues and wire-rimmed glasses.

 

            “Hi,” Lena greeted her, gesturing inside.

 

            They’d gotten used to this routine, no welcome or goodbye kisses, no unnecessary affection that could be mistaken for something else. It was almost therapeutic in a way, letting a stream of words free as they divulged what was bothering them, things at work that had left them weary and irate, without the constraints of a relationship, without the emotional labour of having to carry each other’s burdens as well as their own. Which wasn’t to say that a certain depth didn’t develop between them, something even more frighteningly encompassing than they’d had before. They were both afraid to acknowledge it, knowing to put a name to their feelings would be to kill it. 

 

            Going through the usual motions of enquiring about how they were and how work was as Kara took her shoes off, always preferring to walk around in her socks, even at school, always fondly reminding Lena of their first meeting as her lips twitched, they gravitated around each other through the apartment. Kara would set her coat or robe over the back of the armchair, Lena would list off drinks choices, and if they happened to be meeting around a mealtime, options for food. Kara always preferred the local Chinese run by Muggles and they always ordered in, never seen in public together.

 

            Already past dinner time now, Lena assumed Kara had eaten in the Great Hall and fetched the wine they’d settled on as Kara drifted towards her closed bedroom door. They didn’t always make it that far, depending on how much of a rush they were in or how long they talked, but Lena was content to follow Kara’s lead - for the most part.

 

            “Take your clothes off,” Lena quietly commanded her as she entered the room.

 

            Caught off guard by the departure from their usual routine, Kara paused at the foot of the bed. Setting the wine glasses down on the nightstand, Lena waved her hand at the cork and then poured the Shiraz into both before sinking onto the edge of the mattress.

 

            Taking a sip of wine, she gave Kara a nod to continue and set her glass down. Letting out a strained laugh, her mouth twitching at the corners, Kara flexed her fingers and licked her lips.

 

            “I, uh, I don’t-“

 

            “Kara,” Lena murmured, her voice softening with the familiarity of years between them. “I’ve seen you undressed at least a dozen times. I’ve seen a thousand naked people at work. I’ve seen you at your very worst and put you back together. And let you fuck me at least twenty times already; it’s okay.”

 

            Scars stark white against her reddening face, Kara rubbed the back of her neck as her glasses slid down her nose as a cold sweat beaded on her skin. Audibly swallowing, her voice was frayed as she spoke.

 

            “I have a lot of scars-“

 

            “I know you do.”

 

            Mouth open as she tried to make another excuse, Kara failed and her shoulders slumped. Exhaling sharply, she gestured helplessly and then jerked her chin at Lena, shifting the attention back to her.

 

            “You never take your shirt off either.”

 

            Bristling as if Kara had just pressed on a tender bruise, Lena’s lips twitched derisively. Taking another sip of her wine, she was slow to respond.

 

            “That’s different. You’ve still seen me undressed - mostly.”

 

            “So have you - fully.”

 

            Arching an eyebrow at Kara’s careful logic, Lena smiled faintly. “Is this an I will if you will situation?”

 

            Curiosity sparked in Kara’s eyes as she toyed with the frayed cuffs of her shirt. “Will you?”

 

            Lena’s thin amusement dimmed as she considered the question. Her right hand instinctively curled over her left forearm, right over the words that had been etched there for over half of her life. In the midst of her life falling apart, it had been clear in Lena’s words, her actions, her body language that this was one of her most painful secrets and deeper shame. Kara had known it, even as she’d forced Lena’s hand in divulging it.

 

            It felt like a test of trust and truth and Lena chewed her bottom lip for a moment before she unbuttoned her pants. Shimmying out of them, Lena fiddled with the buttons of her linen shirt before methodically undoing them, one by one. Kara had seen her mostly undressed before, yet it was a frighteningly vulnerable thing for Lena to expose her forearm, more so than any other part of her. She’d never once slept with someone without the security of long sleeves covering the mark that so easily could’ve been covered by a spell. But Lena’s scars ran deeper than the surface.

 

            Even as cocky as she’d appeared, shedding her pants and underwear and unbuttoning her shirt, letting the soft-worn linen slip down her shoulders, exposing her narrow shoulder blades as Kara took in her perfect posture, Lena hesitated. The shirt pooled in the crook of her elbows, leaving her almost entirely bare, late afternoon sunlight tinting her porcelain skin golden, and still it took her a moment to work up the courage to take it off. 

 

            Left hand worked at the buttoned cuff of the right sleeve and Lena pulled her arm free. Moving to her left arm, she toyed with the button but didn’t undo it. Sitting there for a minute, Lena didn’t move, and it wasn’t until Kara’s feet scuffed the floor that she inhaled deeply.

 

            Crouching before her, Kara looked up at Lena with gentle understanding that Lena couldn’t bear. Reaching for her glass of wine, she tipped back the rest of the contents and set it back down on the edge, her clumsiness leading it to topple off. Kara turned at the tinkling sound of breaking glass and made to clean it up, but Lena grabbed her arm and squeezed it tightly.

 

            Turning her attention back to Lena, Kara reached for the cuff of the shirt and carefully unbuttoned it. Eyes shut tight, her whole face crumpled with old pain and shame, Lena tipped her head back slightly and let Kara pull her shirt off her. 

 

            She could feel the heat rush into her cheeks and swallowed thickly. Then there was the featherlight touch of Kara’s fingertip pressing against the pale words, and Lena winced as a small sound of objection caught at the back of her throat, the memories of her skin rent open in her own hand too raw for her to mask the sudden surprise of being touched there. Her heart was pounding in her chest and she fought the urge to snatch her shirt back and shrug it on, the comfort of a long sleeve offering her some armour against what she’d been forced to do to herself, and what she’d chosen to do after the fact.

 

            And then Kara placed a gentle kiss over it and Lena’s eyes stung fiercely behind closed eyelids. Winding her fingers in Kara’s wild curls, Lena kissed her harshly, holding onto the feeling of wanting her to distract her from the pit in her stomach. Grounding herself, her hands ran over the pilled cotton of Kara’s shirt and she broke off the kiss, pulling back.

 

            “Your turn.”

 

            Removing her glasses and running a hand over her face, Kara climbed to her feet. She set her glasses on the nightstand, beside the bottle of wine and her full glass, picking up the latter and draining it in three gulps to take the edge off the discomfort. Setting it down with more care than Lena, she turned her stormy blue eyes to the other woman and reached for her buttons.

 

            “Turn around. Don’t look.”

 

            Resisting the urge to tell her she’d looked before, numerous times - albeit in a professional setting as Healer and patient - Lena turned, settling across the bed on her stomach and pillowing her head with her arms. Kara was behind her and she could hear the rustling of fabric, of shirt pants being shed and carefully folded into a neat pile.

 

            The mattress jostled as Kara climbed onto the bed, and Lena let out a breathless laugh at the trail of kisses pressed from behind her knees up to her shoulder. She tried to turn but Kara made a sound of protest, a low hum that made Lena still. Settling on one side of her, Kara eased Lena onto her side, her fingers gently grasping her throat as she kissed beneath her jaw.

 

            Lena’s eyes were closed as she felt every inch of Kara’s warm skin pressed up against her, and she had to resist the urge to squirm at the rough palm skimming over her outer thigh and waist. Nose pressed into the back of Lena’s neck, Kara’s voice was uneven and quiet as she spoke.

 

            “Satisfied?”

            

            “Not even close,” Lena raggedly managed to reply.

 

            But Kara kept Lena pulled against her chest, that part of her that couldn’t bear to look in the mirror most days, that hated her own body, too overwhelming to let her be vulnerable. It didn’t matter if she’d been naked and unconscious before Lena before, allowed her to patch her up and wipe away the blood and vomit, it didn’t matter that she’d let Mike see her scars that very first time, it didn’t matter than Lena would never have said anything. All that mattered to Kara was that she’d spent years plagued with self-doubt over her feelings for the very woman pressed up against her, and no matter if Lena let her fuck her on their days off or said she’d felt the same about Kara, her self-consciousness was too deeply rooted for her to be so exposed.

 

            Lena was all too willing to let Kara distract her for a while, all conversation forgotten until she’d instinctively turned in her embrace, pressed up flush against her, kissing her and cradling her face in her hands. When her hand slid down to Kara’s shoulder, she felt her stiffen and broke off their kiss, her eyelashes fluttering with surprise as she took in the pinched look of fear on Kara’s face. Before she could even voice her concern, Kara was kissing her again, rolling Lena onto her back as she grabbed her wrists and pinned them beside her head, a blatant do not touch.

 

            Falling back into Kara’s touch, Lena was quickly swept up in the feeling of her hot mouth and calloused palms, capable touch and soft skin. She would’ve liked to run her hands over the slight ridges of the bigger scars, the shiny surfaces of the thin shallow ones, but Kara held her firmly in place and Lena didn’t resist. 

 

            Not until her pounding heart had settled and her breaths had evened out again and she turned her attention to Kara. Pulling away, Lena sat up and looked at Kara, who blanched, hurriedly sitting up and shrinking into a ball on the rumpled sheets, covering as much of herself as possible. Her lanky legs were crisscrossed with old scars and she hunched her shoulders, arms crossed over her chest.

 

            “What’re you doing?” Kara hoarsely asked.

 

            Fixing the broken wine glass, Lena poured them both some more Shiraz from the bottle and knelt on the edge of the bed. She extended Kara’s glass to her and cocked her head to the side, her gaze analytical and soft.

 

            “I want to look at you,” she said, leaning forward even more as she motioned with Kara’s glass. “If that’s okay with you.”

 

            Licking her lips, Kara leaned forward to take the glass, her eyes clouded and anxious. “Why?”

 

            “Because I would. I’d like to take my time, seeing as this is a rare opportunity to see more than half of your arse.”

 

            Rolling her eyes as she flushed, Kara took a sip of her wine. “I don’t like people to see me.”

 

            “Okay, I won’t look,” Lena earnestly replied, clapping a hand over her eyes, “I’ll just touch.”

 

            Snorting, Kara leaned forward and pulled Lena’s hand away from her eyes, giving her a withering look. “That’s worse.”

 

            “Why?”

 

            Fidgeting restlessly, Kara shrugged. Her shoulders had broadened over the months spent at Hogwarts, the weight she’d added to her thin frame while at The Leaky Cauldron further aided by the meals in the Great Hall and the freedom to run around the Forbidden Forest on a full moon. The toll of transforming didn’t carve away at her like the cells at St. Mungo’s did and Lena was secretly relieved, having noticed the changes with each meeting.

 

            “It just- they’re not … it’s- I don’t like to be reminded of them. I mean … they’re not exactly nice, are they? If you touch them, that’s all I’ll think about.”

 

            “Well, if I touched you, it would only be to change your mind about them. I’d hope you’d think of other things instead.”

 

            Lena’s smile was slightly cocky and Kara scoffed, rubbing the back of her neck. Finishing her glass, Lena set it safely aside this time and shifted closer on the bed, still a few feet from Kara. Reaching out, she touched a pale hand to Kara’s furiously red cheek and hummed appreciatively.

 

            “I like it when you do that.”

 

            Turning her head aside, Kara grimaced. “I don’t. It’s embarrassing.”

 

            She reached up and touched the pale scar on her nose and the one on her chin and Lena reached out to snag her fingers, pulling them away. Then she eased Kara’s chin back so their eyes met and studied her face closely; the freckles, the scars, the grey hairs of premature ageing.

 

            “You have nothing to be embarrassed about.”

 

            “Easy to say when you’re not hideously scarred,” Kara said with a hollow laugh.

 

            Surprise jolted Lena and her own laugh was hoarse as her eyebrows shot up. “Oh?”

 

            “You know what I mean.”

 

            “I’ve seen them before; you have nothing to hide.”

 

            “Then why do you want to see them again?”

 

            “Well … this is a bit different to when you’re unconscious as my patient, don’t you think?”

 

            Lips twitching wryly, Kara ducked her head and rubbed her forehead. Softly sighing, Lena tucked her legs beneath her and studied Kara carefully before reaching out to touch the scar on her nose, her touch featherlight.

 

            At her touch, Kara reared her head and Lena’s fingertip glided over her lips, which parted slightly, the breath catching in her throat, and onto the scar on her chin. Slowly, with all the patience in the world and the care of someone who knew how fragile the moment was, Lena traced the silvery scars on Kara’s neck and down to her shoulders and collarbones.

 

            “Which was first?” she murmured, her eyes lifting from the scar she was fixated on to take in Kara’s reaction.

 

            She didn’t speak, just took a sip of wine and then brushed her fingers over the old parallel scars on her shoulder. Then the other shoulder, where Lena could decipher the marks of a bite, the wound that had turned her all those years ago. Ducking her head down, she pressed a kiss to the scar, following the crescents of it, and could hear the quickness of Kara’s heart.

 

            Pressing her palm flat over her chest, Lena softly shushed her, knocking back the rest of her wine and tossing the glass aside on the mattress. Flecks of red soaked into the sheets but her attention was already on Kara’s other scars, peppering kisses along the faded ridges of old silver lines and the puckers of newer ones.

 

            “Is this okay?” Lena asked, pausing at Kara’s ribs, her hands splayed over them.

 

            “Yes,” came the tense, slightly breathless response.

 

            Nudging her nose against Kara’s warm skin, Lena hummed and pressed a kiss to a little nick on her breastbone. “Tell me if it’s too much.”

 

            “It’s not. I just- no one has ever- no one’s touched them before. I’m not- I’m not used to it, so-“

 

            “Can I touch them all?” Lena asked, resting her chin on Kara’s stomach as she looked up at her, eyes wide and achingly soft.

 

            Nodding, Kara tipped her head back against the mattress, her face flushed and her wine glass abandoned on the floor in favour of knotting her fingers in the sheets. She was too tense for Lena’s liking and it was a painstaking age of kissing her way through every scar before she commanded her to roll over and continued the process all the way back up to the nape of her neck.

 

            Lena basked in the new feeling of bare skin against skin, of how warm Kara was and how she moved and sighed and dug her nails in, the moments where she stiffened as Lena’s hands skimmed a particularly insecure spot, the moment where she finally fully relaxed beneath her touch. She kissed her everywhere, taking her sweet time, consciously aware that this was an altogether new experience for Kara. Softening her old anger to gentle worship, Lena strung it out for as long as she could, until Kara was almost desperate for her touch. 

 

            Once she was done, Lena lay with her cheek pressed against Kara’s stomach, over the scars where the werewolf had torn herself open so many months ago. Sweat cooled on both of their skin and she cradled Kara’s thighs in her hands, eyelids shuttered and no desire to move as she lay sprawled between her legs.

 

            The sky was a deep purple outside and Lena was bone tired, her body loose-limbed and aching in a pleasant way. Kara was stretched out on her back, fingers tangled in Lena’s hair and her other arm folded beneath her head. It was the most intimate they’d ever been, a sense of normalcy and peace to their arrangement, and if Lena had stopped to think about it for a second, it would’ve unsettled her.

 

            So much of what they were doing was at odds with how she felt. She’d never denied her attraction to Kara, or how much she cared for her, but she’d also never hidden her wounded feelings and residual anger and bitterness for how it had all played out. The conflicted feelings of sleeping with her only friend who’d betrayed her in the worst way was something Lena tried not to dwell on, lest she overthink it too much. Besides, they weren’t friends anymore. Lena didn’t know how she would have described Kara if there had been anyone to explain her to.

 

            “Lena?” Kara whispered to the quiet room.

 

            Pushing herself up, Lena made a low sound of curiosity at the back of her throat. She shifted up the bed and lay down beside Kara, who rolled onto her side so they were face to face. Lena raised a hand to brush a curl back from Kara’s forehead. Her thumb lingered beside her temple, her fingers gentle as her heart got caught in her throat, making it painfully tight with how much she loved her and how scared she was that Kara would find out.

 

            A faint smile of serenity crossed Kara’s face as her eyelids shuttered and she ducked her head down into the crook of Lena’s neck and shoulder. Her lips were soft and warm as she kissed the hollow of her collarbone, while Lena’s hand lazily worked through her curls, gently untangling them as she waited for Kara to continue.

 

            “You’ve never been a failure,” Kara whispered against her throat. “Not even when I assumed the worst.”

 

            Stiffening as her hand stilled, Lena squeezed her eyes shut and inhaled sharply through her nose. It took her a moment to find her voice, small and panicked as her eyes smarted with tears. But Lena didn’t cry, had it brutalised out of her until she was numb to pain, but Kara’s words ripped open an old wound that would be unbearably painful if Lena didn’t patch it up quickly.

 

            “Don’t,” Lena warned her. “Don’t say that. Don’t or I’ll- just don’t. Please.”

 

            “Okay.”

 

            They fell silent after that and fell asleep shortly after, a warm breeze buffering the curtains and the sounds of the city beyond as they lay skin to skin, Kara’s cheek on Lena’s chest and Lena’s arms wrapped around her. Throughout the night, they both shifted and stretched out across the wide mattress, subconsciously making themselves comfortable while gravitating towards each other as if they’d slept beside each other on countless occasions. They hadn’t, of course, their arrangement having an unspoken rule about Kara staying over, especially considering her career.

 

            It was with wary surprise that they woke beside each other the next morning, Lena first and Kara shortly after as if woken by the movement of the former as she sat upright and dragged a cashmere blanket around herself. Sitting on the edge of the mattress, tense and thoughtful, the blanket wound around her body, saying nothing, Lena didn’t react to Kara’s weight shifting the mattress.

 

            Getting dressed around her, picking up her clothes and slowly piecing yesterday’s outfit back together, Kara finished buttoning up her waistcoat and Lena glanced up at her.

 

            “I should go.”

 

            Nodding distractedly, Lena frowned slightly as she tried to shake off the uneasiness of waking up beside Kara. Really, she was trying to shake off the aching desire to do that every morning, while Kara was similarly trying to make a swift exit before her mind could linger on any hopeful thoughts of it happening again.

 

            “I’ll see you next time,” Kara murmured.

Chapter 22

            It was June and a rare warm day in Dublin, Kara’s shirtsleeves rolled to her elbows and Lena’s still buttoned at the cuff as the sun started to set, the heat waning as the shadows lengthened. They had Chinese from the local takeout, the sounds of the city pouring in through the window, and they were both dishing up food, loose-limbed and dishevelled after a lazy afternoon in Lena’s bedroom.

 

            Dragging out a chair, Kara sank down onto it as Lena finished telling her some story about work from the day before. Her mother had been there when a patient had been admitted for emergency treatment, and Lena had been in the operating theatre with a Charms Attending, assisting as Lillian supervised as well, watching her daughter like a hawk for even the slightest mistake. Lena had never been allowed to fail though and had hunched her shoulders and stilled her trembling hands as she assisted the Healer with reconstructing the man’s chest cavity. Lillian had left an hour in without a word to her daughter about her performance.

 

            “How do you stand it? Seeing her every day?” Kara asked.

 

            Lena’s lips twisted in a humourless smile, her thumb grazing over the sleeve of her left arm. “I saw her every day from the age of four to eleven and every summer holiday in between. It’s not so bad because … well, I know she can’t hurt me in front of other people.”

 

            “But still … how can you be around her and not want to scream? My- my mom … she never mistreated me, she just gave me up, but I think … if I was ever in front of her, I would just be so angry.”

 

            “It’s … complicated.”

 

            Brow creasing with confusion, Kara unpacked the special fried rice and stared at Lena. “In what way?”

 

            Shrugging self-consciously, Lena’s mouth turned down at the corners. “It just- the things she did … they weren’t the worst things anyone’s ever done to me.”

 

            Kara looked aghast and Lena shook her head, sharply exhaling through her nose. “I’m not going to get into it; it’s personal and you already know more than I’d like. More than anyone else.”

 

            “I’d never tell anyone.”

 

            “It’s not that. I just don’t like to think about some things. Some things are private.”

 

            “Like you and I.”

 

            Lena’s lips twitched with a faint smile, “you and I … are secret. Just like we promised.”

 

            “That’s not entirely true. Alex knows about you, and my friends were there that day you brought me home. We- we never got to talk about that.”

 

            “There wasn’t much to say.”

 

            “You blew our cover.”

 

            “Well … you were always the one that cared more about keeping our friendship secret. I only cared about keeping you at all, however which way.”

 

            Cringing slightly as she revealed too much of her hand, Lena cleared her throat. “It doesn’t matter now, anyway. We’re not children anymore so we don’t have to keep secrets.”

 

            Snorting, Kara arched an eyebrow, “yeah, right. You’re saying if I asked you to come and have dinner with my family, you’d be on board?”

 

            Hesitating, Lena considered it for a moment, lips pursed. “No, I wouldn’t. That doesn’t mean you couldn’t talk about me though. If you wanted to. I couldn’t make you do anything, could I? Not if you didn’t want to.”

 

            “Are you saying I’m stubborn?”

 

            “Undoubtedly so. You’re almost incapable of letting people help you, no matter how much it inconveniences you.”

 

            “I let you help me. Back when you used to work on the Bite Ward.”

 

            “Very reluctantly. You always seemed mortified to even be in the same room as me. But you never accepted my money, so again … stubborn.”

 

            “It all worked out in the end though,” Kara said with a dismissive air of pride as Lena walked over to the kitchen to pick up the bottle of red wine she’d chosen. “I managed to turn things around without any help. Sometimes it pays to be self-sufficient and independent.”

 

            “If you say so.”

 

            “You know, I never thought about teaching as a career option. I think I just always thought that the Professors we had would always be there, and once we graduated we’d never get to go back. I like it though. I like being in the place that gave me freedom once a month, even if there were other moments where I felt alone.”

 

            “I thought you’d like it,” Lena said with a smile in her voice, pouring wine as her cheek dimpled shallowly. “When Dumbledore suggested the Defence Against the Dark Arts position, there was absolutely no way I would’ve let you take a cursed-“

 

            Lena trailed off, a sudden jerk of her hand making her slosh wine over the table. She set it down and grabbed a tea towel, mopping it up as she felt Kara’s confusion.

 

            “What? What are you talking about, a Defence Against the Dark Arts position? Dumbledore didn’t offer me that.”

 

            “Didn’t he?” Lena murmured evasively. “I guess I assumed he would’ve offered you that one too, seeing as it was open.”

 

            She turned and set the tea towel with its vivid red stain on the kitchen counter and cleared her throat, aware of the fact that Kara had risen from her seat. Turning back around, she picked up the bottle of wine and continued to pour their wine, her stomach twisting uncomfortably.

 

            “What?” Kara pressed.

 

            “What?” Lena cluelessly echoed, meeting her eyes and raising her eyebrows a fraction as she smiled faintly.

 

            “What aren’t you telling me?”

 

            Face crumpling with feigned confusion, Lena shook her head and let out a quiet huff of laughter. “What do you mean?”

 

            Kara moved in close, her fingers wrapping around Lena’s wrist as she held her still, blue eyes piercing and demanding.

 

            “Tell me.”

 

            “Let go of me,” Lena quietly ordered her, her voice firm.

 

            Kara scoffed but let go of her wrist, taking in the evasive look of sheepish guilt on Lena’s face, caught in the act of something unknown. Swallowing thickly, Kara stared at her and Lena made to pour the other glass of wine before she found the bottle yanked from her hand, held tightly in Kara’s grasp as their eyes met.

 

            “What did you do?”

 

            “Nothing,” Lena dismissively replied, rolling her eyes as she tossed her dark hair and took the bottle back from her. “I just- after I saw you at The Leaky Cauldron, when you said you worked there - lived there - I … well I spoke to Dumbledore.”

 

            Blinking as she processed Lena’s words, it took Kara a moment to respond. “I- you- why would you do that?”

 

            “Because you’re too intelligent to spend your life pouring pints. And he owed me after everything that happened, the things I had to do for him, so …”

 

            The thought came together slowly in Kara’s head as she visibly paled, her shoulders stiff and disbelief creeping into her features. “You … I got the job because of you?”

 

            Scrambling to reassure her, Lena spluttered for a moment, “well, I- no, that’s not entirely true. I called in a favour but … well, he wouldn’t have given you the job if he didn’t think you were up for it. And after he didn’t have any luck with your old boss-“

 

            “You asked him to talk to Croaker?” Kara exclaimed, her cheeks reddening now, her pale scars livid as anger bubbled up.

 

            Realising her mistake, Lena made a small sound of helplessness. “You- you didn’t deserve to be fired. I thought I could help-“

 

            “That wasn’t your decision to make.”

 

            Eyelashes fluttering as she endured Kara’s shouting, Lena swallowed as her pulse spiked, raised voices always leaving her feeling childishly small. Her palms were clammy and she cast her eyes downwards, chastened.

 

            “I understand that you- you might be upset but … you needed help, Kara. All I did was ask the question for you and ask him not to suggest a cursed position. Everyone knows any Defence Professor won’t last longer than a year. He mentioned Ancient Runes had an opening so I asked. I … called in a favour. Whatever you’d like to call it. But it doesn’t matter.”

 

            “It doesn’t matter?” Kara echoed, her voice rasping as she stared at Lena, mystified. “I- you don’t get to tell me what matters. I- I thought …”

 

            “You have a good job. A job you enjoy. Does it really matter how you got it?”

 

            “Yes. Yes, it does. It matters to me. I don’t want someone else’s pity. I have my own life, my own independence. I don’t need other people-“

 

            “It wasn’t pity.”

 

            “Yes, it was. You’ve pitied me for years, haven’t you? While you’ve lived in your nice home with your family’s money and the career you always imagined and everything you could ever want handed to you. And that’s how you think it works, don’t you?”

 

            “I have had nothing handed to me,” Lena snapped, which she knew wasn’t entirely true, with the large sum of her inheritance earning interest at Gringotts. “I had to work harder than anyone to get where I am; you could fail at everything and go home with your tail tucked between your legs and your family still worshipped the ground you walk on. I didn’t have that option. And you’re angry at me because I haven’t had to struggle financially for what I have but then you turn around and get angry because I tried to help you get … something because you have no ambition to make things better for yourself. If it wasn’t for me you would still be wiping tables at The Leaky Cauldron.”

 

            “I don’t want to be reliant on other people. This isn’t their life to work out. It’s no one’s business what- what job I have. But you made it your business and had this handed to me instead of letting me earn it the way I wanted to.”

 

            Shaking her head, Lena’s shoulders slumped as she scoffed contemptuously. “You are too fucking proud for your own good, do you know that?”

 

            The wine bottle shattered on the floorboards as Lena made a cutting motion with her arm, losing her grip on the glass and letting gravity do the rest. Red wine pooled amidst the shards of green glass and Kara was flushed with wounded embarrassment, her pride at bettering herself sullied by the idea that it had been Lena’s doing after all.

 

            “I was fine. I was managing and it wasn’t for you to insert yourself into my business,” she choked out. Closing her eyes, she ran a hand through her curls, grey and gold and dishevelled as she let out a breathless laugh. “Merlin, I’m an idiot. I should’ve known - I should’ve known you hadn’t changed. Not at all. You’re still exactly the same, lying to me, messing around in things that aren’t your business.”

 

            “Excuse me?” Lena choked out, shock slapping her as she jerked back.

 

            Glasses crooked as she pinched the bridge of her nose, Kara hunched over and shook her head. “I’m such a fucking idiot . How did I let myself get wrapped up in you again?”

 

            “You? How did you get wrapped up in me? You kissed me. You fucked me. You escalated this once again, and yet I still get the blame for it. And I was the idiot, not you, to let you get me in this position-”

 

            “Don’t pretend like you didn’t want-”

 

            “It’s not about wanting. You knew it was a mistake the first time but you still came after me when I was perfectly content to chalk it up to a bad decision.”

 

            Scoffing, Kara pressed a hand to her forehead. “A bad decision?”

 

            Taking a step forward, Lena’s face crumpled and she let out a strained laugh, reaching for her. “Kara-“

 

            “No. No, I won’t stand here and listen to you explain it any further. You lied to me. And for what? Why?”

 

            “Well, we were hardly on talking terms, were we? And I didn’t lie,” Lena haughtily scoffed, “I omitted a few facts.”

 

            “Omitted a few facts,” Kara chuckled, nodding as her eyes brightened with anger. “Right. You’re good at that, aren’t you? That’s- that’s what you do. You sneak around behind everyone’s back, so -“

 

            “That’s what this is about, is it?” Lena breathlessly asked, a pain in her chest as she felt everything unravel in her hands. “I’m a Slytherin. I can’t be trusted.”

 

            Lips twisting derisively, Kara shrugged, hugging her arms to herself. “You meddled in my life and let me believe it was all me; how am I supposed to trust anything you say?”

 

            “You know me-“

 

            “I did. We haven’t known each other in years-“

 

            “And whose fault is that?” Lena demanded.

 

            “Yours,” Kara snapped. “It was yours then too. You kept me in the dark, you did exactly the same thing, and then you told me to go. Only you were a kid then, and you’re not now, and this is about me. My life.”

 

            “I got you a job, Kara. It’s a fucking job,” Lena softly replied, helpless and small.

 

            Closing her eyes, Kara let out a frayed laugh, covering her face with her hands. “It’s not. It’s not just a job. It’s- it’s-“

 

            “Your pride?” Lena sneered. “You’d rather be poor and live in a hovel and fuck men who find you so repulsive that you can’t take your clothes off in front of them, instead of letting someone help you?”

 

            Kara flinched as if Lena had slapped her, her mouth falling open, tears stinging her eyes as she struggled to speak. Her throat felt tight and she protectively curled in on herself, as if she could make her lanky frame smaller, unnoticeable with its pale scars that Lena didn’t think were repulsive but had let the words come out all wrong in her anger.

 

            “Fuck you,” Kara whispered, devastation knifing through her as she ducked her head, cheeks red as she blinked back tears. 

 

            “Me? I’m the problem here because I was trying to help you? All I’ve ever done is fucking help you. Not because I stand to gain from this, or because I owe it to you but … because I care about you so much and that- that just fucking terrifies you, doesn’t it? That someone could ever like you, knowing what you are.”

 

            Wiping her eyes on her sleeve, Kara inhaled sharply to reply but was cut off as Lena continued. 

 

            “You know what? You think no one will ever want you because you’re a werewolf but that’s not true. No one will ever want you because you're insufferably self-pitying and too stubbornly proud to let anyone want you. And you’re a coward.”

 

            “You have no right-“

 

            “You’re a fucking coward,” Lena shouted at her, with all the drama of a twenty-three-year-old having her heart broken by the same girl for the second time.

 

            A flat laugh escaped Kara as her lips twitched ruefully, “and you haven’t changed at all.”

 

            “Get the fuck out of my flat.”

 

            Lena grabbed Kara’s robe and bundled it up into a ball before storming over to the door and yanking it open. She tossed the robe onto the landing and Kara made a sound of protest, following it out. Before she could say another word, Lena slammed the door shut behind her and then slammed her palms against it for good measure, cheeks rosy with burning anger and her eyes bright. Not with tears - she could never cry, not over something like this. It had been beaten out of her years ago.

 

            Instead, she kicked the door for relief and felt the sickening crunch of a few toes as they broke. It wasn’t her finest moment, not by a long shot, and as she let out a torrent of swearing and hobbled over to the sofa, Lena let out what sounded like a choked sob before she got to work healing her toes in between mouthfuls of a bottle of sherry she’d brought out for after dinner. As it was, dinner was dead in the water and she needed the burn of alcohol to mellow her anger before it ate away at her.

 

            The only thing it did was help her stamp it down until it was a small, burning hot spark in her chest, still there but just ignored, where it could smoulder away until it slowly consumed her. But then she was filled with the even worse sensation of being pleasantly numb and Lena couldn’t stand it. Sipping another mouthful of sherry from the bottle, she ignored the pool of wine, ignored their uneaten dinner and walked straight into her office.

 

            Taking a seat at her desk, she unbuttoned the cuff of her left sleeve and pushed it up, sniffing and swallowing thickly as the breath hitched in her throat. Pulling out a piece of parchment, she reached for the Blood Quill and then hesitated. Twirling it between her fingers, she stared down at the old scar and her mouth thinned at the corners with regret. 

 

            Sitting there for a moment, Lena stared at the pale skin of her arm, marred by words that she despised, and she was filled with a silent plea to not do it. The emptiness that replaced her anger, her heartbreak, couldn’t be managed by carving those letters into her skin again and again. She didn’t want to feed into what her mother had made her do, made her think. Lena didn’t want to be a failure but that seemed to be all she was capable of doing. She’d tried to help her friend and that had disintegrated any semblance of trust or a relationship between them as if Kara had been waiting for an excuse to bow out of this thing between them and had leapt at the first opportunity.

 

            Grinding her teeth together, Lena tossed the quill down and ran her hands over her face. All she’d done was call in a favour - well, less than a favour and more a demand, her old anger and betrayal at Dumbledore leaving her harsh and stubborn as she had the audacity to order him to give Kara a job. She was too young to see that he hadn’t so much as agreed to her request in a way that gave her all the power, but he’d seen his opportunity to strengthen the allegiance of a lost girl who needed an opportunity to get back on her feet. It would benefit him a lot more, in the long run, to have another loyal outcast dependent on him than to rebuff Lena’s demands and let her cause trouble for him. He bought silence and loyalty in one easy decision that made no difference to him at all, really.

 

            But Lena couldn’t see the large chess game the old man was playing, had only felt vindicated as she’d been assured he’d offer Kara a position. And now she was regretting her decision to get involved at all, Kara’s pride such a flimsy thing that she would see it as embarrassing to accept help from the one person who’d always been there to help her. Lena had helped her with her homework, with her bullies, with her grief and her friends, with her wand work and Lycanthropy, had healed her and dragged her out of fights to keep her safe in a war. There were countless ways she’d helped Kara but this had been the one that was too shameful for Kara to bear.

 

            Shoving herself back from her desk, she stalked through to her bedroom and fished out a cloak and her purse before apparating to Knockturn Alley. The sign for The White Wyvern appeared out of the gloom of the tall buildings blotting out any sunshine making it into the narrow street, and she stepped inside the dingy pub, craving the presence of other people until she could make sense of her feelings. Veronica was at the bar and she gave Lena a quick grin, setting down a measure of Firewhisky for her before turning to another customer.

 

            Taking the glass, Lena knocked it back in one mouthful, relishing the taste of it as she slammed the glass back down. A minute later, Veronica was in front of her again with the bottle, raising her eyebrows.

 

            “You look rough.”

 

            “Bad day,” Lena curtly replied, fishing out a few coins and letting them clatter to the bar top as her friend refilled her drink. “Anyone else here?”

 

            Jerking her chin towards the far corner, Veronica poured her a double. “Andrea’s here with Russell and his mate. That Daily Prophet bloke. Gayle’s back as well; just got in from Russia this morning.”

 

            Nodding, Lena picked up her drink and thanked her before winding through the pub, seeking out her friends. She quietly greeted them and took a seat beside Andrea, the only one she considered a friend really, and sipped her drink as she remained on the outskirts of the conversation, Gayle telling them about her trip and where she was off to next.

 

            Lena drank until she could barely stand, the threat of splinching herself leaving her bundled onto the Knight Bus to get home alone. It became a routine after that, the hours she’d spent with Kara in her free time replaced with her friends as she became a more frequent fixture at drinks. They had always gone almost every day after work, and with Lena’s hours she’d never been able to go that often, but nursing her secret bruised feelings, she made more of an effort these days, seeking a balm to her loneliness.

 

            At work, Sam could tell there was something wrong but Lena brushed her concern aside and threw herself into her work, grateful for the long hours and any overtime she could grab. There were many times she slept at St. Mungo’s in an on-call room, a change of scrubs and a shower in the changing room and a week straight of sandwiches and pumpkin pasties in the tearoom upstairs to sustain her.

 

            She didn’t hear from Kara, as expected, but she saw her a few weeks later in Diagon Alley, the school year over and summer holidays ushered in with an influx of teenagers in casual clothes filling the shops and markets. Lena had been there to pick up a new healing book from Flourish & Blotts and caught sight of Kara angling towards The Junk Shop wearing a yellow knitted vest over a pale blue shirt and flared jeans. Stopping in her tracks, her new book tucked under her arm, Lena’s eyes tracked her through the crowd, feeling as if she was watching her life walk away from her. Tall and golden, her curls carelessly tied up and her wand stuck through it, Kara chatted to her sister and held open the door to the shop.

 

            Lena saw the moment she was spotted, Kara’s mouth stilling, their eyes locked, a shock of intimacy in the act. It would’ve been easy then to walk over to her, to apologise and put it all behind them, but if Kara was proud then Lena was doubly so, and it was only the luck of her circumstances that meant she’d never have to rely on other people the way Kara did. Still, she considered it for a moment, until she watched Kara’s face stiffen and she turned away, stepping inside as if Lena was no one at all, as if she hadn’t even seen her.

 

 

            Kara left Lena’s flat and spent the next few hours walking around Dublin in her robes, attracting strange looks as she bristled with anger, her face like thunder and her cheeks still holding a touch of pink as her mind replayed the moment over and over again. The night cooled and her feet grew sore and Kara wound up in The Leaky Cauldron when she found herself reluctant to return to Hogwarts just yet.

 

            Alex was there, as well as Kelly, Querl and Nia, and they were all surprised to see her unannounced but made room at their rickety table. Drinking pint after pint, Kara was sullen and flushed but refused to tell them what was bothering her as she let the alcohol do its work, not knowing that a few streets away in another pub Lena was doing exactly the same to forget her too.

 

            When Alex went out to the back courtyard to smoke, Kara went with her and ended up bursting into tears as she leaned back against the brick walls. Digging the heels of her palms into her eyes, she hunched her shoulders and sobbed and drunkenly apologised as she slid down the wall as Alex tried to haul her back up. She couldn’t say what was wrong, couldn’t bring herself to say the words, to explain what had gone on, Lena’s bluff was called because Kara knew she still could never bring herself to divulge their secret thing to everyone else. It took her a while to calm down, Kelly fetching her a pint of water and Alex giving her a cigarette, reneging on her usual insistence that her sister not smoke, the acrid taste of tobacco and the purple cloud of smoke making her cough as she hiccuped her way to silence.

 

            Returning to Hogwarts after midnight, unsteady on her feet as she walked the path up to the castle, boots scuffing the ground, Kara greeted Filch when the old caretaker scowled at her. He’d never made his dislike for her a secret, muttering things about blood impurities and creatures whenever he was in her company but she just gave him a thin smile and shuffled all the way up to her quarters in her tower, red-eyed and tired and reeking of smoke.

 

            Sleeping off the alcohol, she woke later than usual and had to quickly shower to wash off the sour odour of alcohol that made her smell like a distillery. Knocking back a potion to help with her hangover, Kara rushed downstairs for a late breakfast, hastily stacking up slices of toast with butter and jam and draining three cups of coffee in succession, much to the curious, piercing stare of Professor Flitwick on her left.

 

            Retreating upstairs to prepare for her class of Fourth-Years, Kara arrived only minutes before them and was scrawling runes on the chalkboard as the seats filled. It was a long hour and then again afterwards for one of her Fifth-Year classes, prepping them for their O.W.L.s which were only days away now. There was another Fifth-Year class after them and then a Sixth and Seventh back-to-back after lunch, and Kara’s free periods were spent empathetically helping her O.W.L. and N.E.W.T. students through their frazzled panicking over their coursework.

 

            She did some marking before heading down to dinner, picking at her steak and kidney pie and feeling less than enthusiastic at the apple crumble before retiring to her office. In the long hours of the afternoon, as the sunset slowly crept up on them, she drafted several letters at her desk, her frustration growing with each one as she vented the emotions she’d bottled up all day.

 

            Once she was done she sealed it and climbed to her feet, wandering through the castle to the Gargoyle Corridor and the statue hiding the entrance to the Headmaster’s Tower. Speaking the password given to her at the start of the year, she watched the gargoyle step aside and rode the staircase up to the door, raising her fist to knock.

 

            “Enter.”

 

            Opening the door, Kara stepped inside, that feeling of being in trouble and being called to Dumbledore's office creeping up on her as it did every time she found herself in his presence. In her shabby robes before him, she felt inadequate as a teacher, and her revelation from the day before only added to that fraudulent feeling.

 

            “Kara, you’re just in time for a bit of tea. To what do I owe the pleasure?”

 

            Somewhat flustered as she tried to compose herself, firm and professional, she held out the sealed letter and cringed at her ink-stained fingertips from her laborious process of getting the words down right.

 

            “I just wanted to give you this in person, sir.”

 

            He took the letter and broke the wax, his pale eyes scanning the words as Kara stood stiffly before his desk, a muscle twitching in her jaw as she tried to contain her anger. Head bowed, she waited until he’d finished, the letter set down on the desk and his wingback chair creaking as he leaned back.

 

            “May I ask why?”

 

            “I- why did you offer me the job?” she blurted out, countering his question with her own, testing him.

 

            “I thought you’d be a suitable candidate.”

 

            “But why? How did you know I needed a job? A better one.”

 

            “I knew you’d been fired from the Ministry-”

 

            “How?”

 

            Dumbledore didn’t reply for a moment, just studied her with that infuriating air of serenity that was never ruffled. Kara had never heard him raise his voice above the soft tones of an old man and she felt off-balance as she felt her own emotions rising within her, slipping out of her control.

 

            “Something tells me you already know the answer.”

 

            “Did Lena ask you?”

 

            “Yes, Miss Luthor came to me to put your name forward for the position.”

 

            It took Kara a moment to reply, eyelids fluttered as her mouth opened and closed, hands curling into fists and then flexing as she felt her cheeks redden. She was embarrassed, and maybe that said a lot about her pride, just like Lena had said, but Kara didn’t like to be pitied and didn’t want any handouts. 

 

            “Put my name forward? She- I know what she was doing for you during the war. This wasn’t her simply putting my name forward; you did it to placate her, because of what she knew and the people you didn’t protect.”

 

            “You’re angry.”

 

            Letting out a frayed laugh, spluttering at his observation, Kara nudged her glasses up and pressed the heels of her palms into her eyes. The sound of Fawkes ruffling his feathers and the odd whirring and clicking of Dumbledore’s machines filled the silence of his office as she stood there for a moment.

 

            “There’s no shame in accepting help from those who offer it,” Dumbledore gently assured her.

 

            “It wasn’t offered. It was presented as an opportunity I’d earned on my own merit when that’s not the truth at all.”

 

            “That doesn’t mean you have to resign. Your work has been exemplary. Your students’ grades reflect well on your ability to teach and I’ve heard nothing but good things from your colleagues.”

 

            “I don’t appreciate being lied to, sir.”

 

            He hummed and picked up her resignation letter before folding it up and letting out a regretful sigh. “Well, if it’s what you think is best for yourself, I suppose I have no other choice but to accept your resignation. I’m regretful that I can’t convince you otherwise and I offer you my sincerest apologies for my ambiguity in the matter. ”

 

            “I’ll work the rest of the school year,” Kara murmured.

 

            “That would be appreciated. If you should change your mind, please do come and see me.”

 

            Nodding curtly, trying to stamp down her anger as her hands shook, Kara turned on her heel and made for the door. Her hand rested on the doorknob and she started to turn it when the Headmaster’s frail voice called after her.

 

            “If I may be so bold, I don’t pretend to know the nature of your relationship with Miss Luthor, only the loyalty she has shown you over the years. If I’m not mistaken, she’s been honest with how she aided the Order during the war but I think even you do not know the extent of the risks she took to ensure your safety. Yours particularly. It is rare for someone to do so much good without seeking reward. Do not judge her badly, Kara, for having her heart in the right place.”

 

            “Goodnight, sir,” Kara stiffly replied.

 

            She stepped onto the staircase and rode it back down before returning to her rooms, thinking over his words and cursing him as well as Lena for all the secrets they kept. Even then, she doubted herself, but Kara was too upset, too wrapped up in her wounded pride to change her mind, to admit that she was making a rash decision, one that she might later regret. Having an early night, she lay in bed in her pyjamas with Bastet curled up on her chest, a black shadow in the faint moonlight slipping through the windows, and thought everything over, again and again, doubting herself.

 

            As the remainder of the school year slipped by with astonishing speed, disconcerting and bittersweet for Kara, she didn’t waver in her decision and that just made her doubt even more. It was a good job, one she enjoyed almost as much as being an Unspeakable, one she could have seen herself staying in long-term, if she hadn’t let her stubborn pride take over. She hadn’t told anyone else either, the staff obviously aware but her family oblivious to her resignation, knowing that she wouldn’t have the words to explain why and that, most likely, even if she had they still would have thought it was an overreaction. But then they’d always tried to help her too, no matter how much she insisted that she do things by herself, shoulder her problems alone.

 

            Her last few days at Hogwarts, Kara took to wandering the hallways in her socks, a comforting, familiar routine from her childhood, the cold stone seeping through the darned cotton, the musty smell of age and wood and chalk and damp making her feel nostalgic and heartsick. And try as she might, she couldn’t stop thinking about Lena. All the time they used to spend together was now spent thinking about her, a hole in her schedule as she found herself lonely and bored, Lena’s absence lingering and filling her with a sharp ache that left Kara feeling like she’d spend the rest of her life pining after her.

 

            The last day came and there was a feast in the Great Hall, the excitement for the summer holidays palpable, while the Seventh Years animatedly chatted about the jobs they’d apply for and what marks they’d get. It filled Kara with a pang of longing for those younger days when she hadn’t had to worry about a job, beyond casual work on the school holidays, and when she hadn’t had to untangle the confusing web of feelings for her best friend, had been able to keep things simple and secret as they walked the hallways in their uniforms, pretending not to know each other, and drank tea and brushed biscuit crumbs from their homework as they tucked themselves away together, two lonely girls together.

 

            Her eyes stung fiercely the next morning when she carried her bags downstairs, the sky a clear blue, the castle grounds green and the mountains tall and free from snow. The lake sparkled in the early morning sunlight and she cast a longing look at the Forbidden Forest and the reprieve it had offered her from the cells of St. Mungo’s, wishing she could slip away into the cover of them and abandon all responsibilities. Even as she thought it, the idea seemed so preposterous that it gave Kara pause, the sudden impulsive urge to do so gripping her so tightly that she imagined maybe that was what she did need. Not in the sense that she wanted to disappear without a word, but that it might be good for her to leave for a while, do some travelling, gain some life experience and make the most of the savings she’d accumulated over the school year.

 

            The idea grew from a yearning whim to something solid as she watched the tail-end of the students vanish down the long pathway to the school gates and heard footsteps come up behind her. Turning, she found herself looking at Dumbledore in his silvery embroidered robes, his blue eyes piercing and knowing as he clasped his hands behind his back and smiled kindly at her.
