            She sought out creatures in areas where there had been sightings, finding the Swedish Short-Snout and Hungarian Horntail at the Romanian Dragon Sanctuary, blue flames lighting up the austere landscape, Thestrals in the forests at the northern point of France, a keen ache in her chest for her father and the herd in the Forbidden Forest she’d used to feed with Lena, a Sea Serpent off the coast of Spain as she went on a catamaran with the Muggles, who didn’t even recognise it for what it was as they snorkelled along the reefs. Kara went flying across the tundra in Russia, for the sake of all that open space and raw wilderness, holing herself away on one of the full moons as she transformed so far from civilisation that her only company had been normal wolves howling as the change crept up on her. In Norway she spent some time with an Ancient Runes Professor, studying under the old woman as she learnt some of the customs that still existed in the pockets of the old ways there. 

 

            Growing accustomed to her new way of life, Kara became more confident in her anonymity there, no one knowing her from school or work, no one familiar until she came to know the locals. There was the kind bookseller who she spent chunks of her pay buying from, the witch at the café who knew her order by heart, the group at the pub who regularly invited her to their games of Wizard’s chess after a quiet night when the old man had been alone with no opponent and Kara had thrashed him two games in a row. Then there was Paris beyond the market, learning about Muggle history and combing the archives at work to see how her own world fit into that, visiting ornate buildings and parks and encountering a dark-haired Muggle Frenchwoman or two who took her home when she’d had too much to drink, their elegance painfully reminiscent of Lena and leaving Kara hurting her own feelings as she ghosted them the next morning, Apparating out of their apartments before the sun was up. 

 

            She turned twenty-six in September and celebrated with a slice of chocolate gateau alone in her room, listening to her trusty radio and opening the gifts from Alex and Eliza. Her sister had wanted to come and visit but Kara had told her not to waste her leave on it, her promise to come home for Christmas still in the cards, but she had to admit as she read their cards and opened the new sweater for the approaching cold weather, the knitted socks and silk scarf and the photo album for all of her Polaroids, she missed them. For all her enjoyment in her little life in Paris, there was a loneliness that Kara hadn’t anticipated. She didn’t have friends, as per se, and her mediocre French ostracised her more, but she was too stubborn to give in just yet. 

 

            The end of November was bitter and Kara had to keep a conjured fire going in her room all night and into the morning to take the edge off, the thin walls and old bones of the hotel not affording great insulation. The Records Room was arguably worse, cavernous and underground, the cold seeming to seep in through the walls, and Kara spent hours every day checking for mould or rot or dampness that could damage the fragile books or parchment scrolls stored there.

 

            Reshelving a trolley full of artefacts on the last day of the month, Kara hauled herself up a ladder and set the birth registry back in its spot, between the Beauxbatons student list and a comprehensive beasts index. It was a slow day, quiet, the kind of day that gave Kara a lot of time to read in between helping restock and care for their information. 

 

            She shelved another book in the correct section and heard the sharp click of heels echoing in the spacious room. High up and with one arm occupied by books, Kara couldn’t crane her neck enough to see who the new visitor was but started to descend as a feminine voice called up to her, a velvety burr.

 

            “Salut.”

 

            “Bonjour mademoiselle,” Kara lightly replied, slowly making her way down the ladder. “Un moment, s'il vous plaît.”

 

            “Oui.”

 

            Climbing down the last few rungs, Kara’s brogues struck the stone floor of the library and she dusted her palm on the thigh of her flared periwinkle pants, the remaining books cradled in the crook of her other arm as she turned and froze, the words dying on her lips. 

 

            “Comment allez- oh.”

 

            “Ça va,” Lena wryly replied, folding her arms over her chest.

 

            She was wearing maroon robes over a matching leather trench coat beneath, belted tightly at the waist. Fitted cream leather gloves encased her hands and she gently plucked at the fingertips, removing one and then the other as they stared at each other. The air was thick with tension, Lena’s green stare piercing and steady as Kara felt a hot flush start in the toes of her worn brogues and travel upwards to the roots of her hair, staining her cheeks red. 

 

            At twenty-five now, Lena held herself with more surety, years out from beneath her mother’s thumb and spent learning how to be her own person agreeing with her. She looked stunning and that was somehow worse.

 

            Clearing her throat as she shifted the armful of old books, holding them tightly against the houndstooth print sweater vest she was wearing over her shirt. Kara didn’t want to look at her, eyes flitting around the cavernous space, from shelf to shelf, row to row, as she straightened, her shoulders squaring.

 

            “You speak French?” she asked after a moment.

 

            “Oui.”

 

            One side of her mouth hitched into a faintly smug smile. Of course Lena spoke French. She was exactly the kind of person that would speak it, her mother forcing her to practise genders, adverbs and tenses over breakfast. 

 

            “What’re you doing here?” Kara tried again.

 

            “I’ve come to check out a book,” Lena said with a quick grin, sharp and humourless. Kara didn’t play to her charms and stared down at the floor, a serious look on her face as a muscle twitched in her jaw. “Obviously I’m here to see you.”

 

            “Who’s it obvious to? Last time we saw each other you threw me out.”

 

            “Last time we saw each other you blanked me dead,” Lena countered.

 

            Scoffing, Kara raised her eyes to the high ceiling, head tipped back and throat bobbing as she swallowed thickly. “Can you blame me?”

 

            “Yes.”

 

            Dropping her head to look at Lena with shock at the venom held in a singular word, Kara’s lips parted as she drew in a shallow breath. A hoarse bark of laughter escaped her, echoing off the high ceilings as it broke the hushed quiet.

 

            “What do you want? How did you find me?”

 

            “Don’t worry, I’m here for work purposes,” Lena haughtily informed her, her hard stare inscrutable. “I’ve been assisting a Potions Master for the last year with his research for a potion he started working on a couple of years ago. It’s finally made it to trials and you’d be a good candidate for it.”

 

            Kara’s mouth thinned and she scoffed, her mouth twisting derisively as her eyes shifted away from Lena. Her palms were getting clammy on the worn leather of the book covers and she could feel her heartbeat growing quicker, a cold sweat on her lower back and the urge to get away, to escape the situation before she upset herself. 

 

            “Not interested.”

 

            “You already know I’m banned from the Bite Ward so I won’t be affiliated with treating you in any way, aside from a brief mention in Belby’s paper perhaps. Hopefully, after today we’ll never have to see each other again, so it shouldn’t be a problem.” 

 

            Distracted by the sight of a man trying to float himself up to a shelf, Kara bit back a curse and ignored Lena’s response as she rushed off with her armful of books, a little frazzled and irate.

 

            “Ah, monsieur? Monsieur! Bonjour, puis-je vous aider?”

 

            Fetching the register he was trying to reach, Kara fumbled through broken French as she tried to explain how he had to use a ladder or the record’s recall system to remove anything from the shelves. He seemed unfazed and retired to a dim corner to peruse the list of Ministry officials from the last century while Kara continued onwards, scrambling to remember where she was up to in her reshelving as she tried to forget that Lena was there.

 

            She hadn’t heard her voice in years but she had silent conversations with her and hearing her voice now pitched Kara off balance. Throat dry, she shakily shelved a book in the correct section and listened to the slow click of heels on the floor. Irate, Kara turned around as Lena approached, flustered and embarrassed.

 

            “What do you want?” she wearily asked.

 

            Lena stood before her for a moment, her expression unreadable and her silence too weighted with tension as if she was considering her words carefully, choosing how much of herself to reveal. Or perhaps that was Kara’s wishful thinking as she ached for the opportunity to undo all of the damage between them, to go back to easier days when they were teenagers tucked away at Hogwarts, or even those brief few weeks of bliss, where they’d lingered in some space separate to their real lives, ignoring everything else and anticipating the fallout. Eventually, she gave Kara a thin smile, tight and almost a sneer, her green eyes bright but inscrutable, and she shrugged dismissively.

 

            “If you change your mind, give my name at St. Mungo’s and tell them you’re there for the Wolfsbane trial.”

Chapter 25

            Lena glanced at her Interns and dished out orders in her rapid style as she strode through the hallways of St Mungo’s with purpose. She held a stack of patient files in her arms and had just finished up her rounds for the day, exhaustion weighing heavily in the slump of her shoulders as she left her patients in the hands of the Interns that she swore were thicker than she’d ever been. With a few years tucked under her belt and her new status as an Attending giving her more authority now, and new robes, Lena felt comfortable in her job, having earned her stripes and proven that she hadn’t gotten by riding on the hem of her mother’s robes. In fact, it had been a hindrance more often than not to be related to Lillian, any punishments falling twice as hard on Lena for minuscule mistakes that her fellow Healers received a slap on the wrist for.

 

            Handing in the files at the nurse’s station, Lena glanced down at her wristwatch and sighed, giving her Interns a cursory look of dismissal. “Only page me if it’s an emergency. And by that I mean their organs had better be outside of their body.”

 

            At the mumbled agreements, she turned and stalked off through the hospital, ducking into the staff changing room and shedding her robes. Pulling on a long coat over her scrubs, Lena packed away her things and hauled her satchel onto her shoulder before sweeping out of the room. She caught Sam on the way to the waiting room and they walked side by side to the lift.

 

            “Plans for tonight?” Sam asked, a soft but weary smile on her face.

 

            “Dinner.”

 

            “When are you in next?”

 

            Pinching the bridge of her nose, Lena’s mouth thinned. “Tomorrow afternoon. You?”

 

            “Thursday.”

 

            Lena arched an eyebrow and gave her friend a crooked smile, “aren’t you the lucky one. What have you got planned?”

 

            “We’ve got snow for the next two days near me so probably some housework and occupying an unruly six-year-old.”

 

            “Oh, the joys of motherhood. Well, if you want to get a break from the snow, my shift doesn’t start until five tomorrow.”

 

            “Diagon Alley?” Sam suggested.

 

            “Ten o’clock?”

 

            “See you then.”

 

            Sam gave her arm a squeeze as they bypassed the rows of chairs in the waiting room, a man with tentacles waving around his head, a woman with a blinking third eye in the middle of her head dozing in her chair, a man talking in riddles pacing back and forth sticking out. Lena said goodbye to her friend and watched Sam Floo out before she grabbed a pinch of the powder herself and stepped into the emerald flames. Whisked away to Ireland, Lena was spat out in her living room and dusted her coat off before removing it and folding it over the back of a chair.

 

            Kicking off her shoes, Lena raked a hand through her hair and considered a shower before deciding to collapse into bed and deal with the antiseptic smell clinging to her before she went out for dinner. It was eight-thirty when she got home and she slept until three in the afternoon, waking to a steel grey sky and lashing rain against the windows. 

 

            Showering and dressing in warm pyjamas, Lena shuffled around the kitchen in her slippers as she put together a late lunch, shoving ham and cheese into a croissant and wolfing it down with strong coffee and an invigorating potion to perk her up. Going through the motions of setting her life in order, Lena charmed the dishes to wash themselves, cleaned the bedding and put the sheets back on, made the broom sweep across the floor and opened the windows to let in the fresh air, smelling of rain and pollution and greenery as the city spilt inside.

 

            A copy of The Daily Prophet had been delivered that morning and Lena read the front page and a few of the sections that interested her before idly filling out the crossword before she turned her attention to the Healing journal that she’d subscribed to. Her paper with Belby would be published in it before the end of the year after they’d finalised it with a few more months of research and data, and Lena felt a spark of excitement at the prospect. Her mother had already expressed how much of a waste of time she thought it was, verging on blatant disregard for her instruction that Lena was banned from the Bite Ward, although argued Lena hadn’t stepped foot in the ward, but she would never know the reason for Lena’s fixation of Lycanthropy. 

 

            Reading through new research and newly available potions for treatments, new spells that had been created to help various Healing techniques, Lena wasted the afternoon until it was time for her to start getting ready for dinner. Fixing her hair into sleek, dark waves, she carefully applied her foundation and eyeshadow, mascara and delicate dabs of blush and heard the sound of the front door open, the deep familiar voice drifting through the place.

 

            “Only me.”

 

            “I’m just finishing off,” she softly called back, lining her lips.

 

            Clipped footsteps approached and Jack knocked on the bathroom door before stepping inside, the picture of handsomely put together, neatly groomed with the sharp smell of his aftershave bordering on overwhelmingly masculine as it filled the bathroom. He crossed over to her, one large hand cradling her waist as he dropped a kiss on the top of her head. Letting out a low wolf whistle, he grinned as Lena scoffed, rolling her eyes and elbowing him in the stomach.

 

            “You look nice.”

 

            “Mm, thanks,” she mumbled, rooting around in her makeup bag for lipstick.

 

            Stepping aside, Jack leaned against the long vanity and watched her for a minute before he turned, preening as he eyed his appearance in the mirror.

 

            “Who’s going again?” Lena asked, applying maroon lipstick in the bathroom mirror.

 

            Fixing his hair in the mirror and then adjusting the collar of his black turtleneck, Jack hummed. “Just Andrea, Russell, William and his new girlfriend. You’d probably know her from school but I can’t remember her name for the life of me. Anyway, she works at The Daily Prophet with him and Andrea; one of the new journalists.”

 

            “Are we doomed to spend dinner talking about whatever drivel the news has contrived today?” Lena drawled and then sighed.

 

            “We can always rely on you to regale us with gory stories of whatever operation you had to perform today instead.”

 

            Rolling her eyes, Lena blotted her lips and sprayed perfume at her throat and wrists before she stalked out of the bathroom to get dressed. Along with the black turtleneck plucked from the cupboard, she pulled on a dragonhide skirt in deep forest green, paired with tights and her heeled boots. Despite a year of dating, Lena didn’t let Jack into the bedroom as she changed, her left arm firmly covered at all times in his presence - even with the lights off - and she emerged with a burgundy robe draped over her arm and a small handbag in hand.

 

            Pulling on her robe, Lena fetched her keys and wand and gave Jack a quick smile. “Ready?”

 

            “Mhm,” he murmured, pulling her closer and giving her a chaste kiss.

 

            Clearing her throat, Lena pressed her lips into a flat line, “we’re going to be late.”

 

            “We’re early but … I suppose.”

 

            They Apparated to Carkitt Market together and stepped into the comfortable interior of The Hopping Pot , Lena’s eyes searching the space for their friends. They were the first ones there and claimed a table for six at the row of booths, sinking onto the padded benches. Lena removed her robes while Jack went to order their first round of drinks.

 

            “Darling!” Andrea exclaimed as she swept through the pub, ducking down as Lena rose, kissing cheeks.

 

            Russell was behind her and cupped Lena’s arm as he kissed her cheek before disappearing to order drinks with Jack. They returned with the drinks and the girls shuffled further into the booth as they made space, Lena taking her glass of elderflower wine and taking a quick sip. They were swept into conversation while waiting for William and his girlfriend to arrive and it was only a few minutes later that his tall form cast a shadow across the table and the slender, relatively tall figure of his girlfriend hung behind him. Blonde curls salted grey with a new fringe cut in, scarred chin and nose and cheeks, worn, ill-fitting clothes and wide spectral blue eyes behind wire-rimmed glasses. Lena’s stomach dropped as she forced down her mouthful of wine.

 

            Setting her glass down heavily, she pressed her fingertips to her lips as her brow furrowed, her eyes trained on Kara. William was making introductions but Lena’s ears felt like they were ringing, his words a distant buzz, and Kara was staring straight back at her with the wooden expression of a stranger. Forced to shuffle along as Jack pressed up against her to make more room, Lena was broken out of her stupor.

 

            “Lena, you remember Kara, don’t you?” Andrea asked with a sharp edge to her stare, even though she smiled. “She tried to hex me once but caught you in the face instead.”

 

            Visibly pale, Lena found it hard to make her lips move to formulate a response. It felt like an eternity before she swallowed past the tightness in her throat. “Right, of course.”

 

            Kara flushed red, her scars stark, and she looked like she wanted to Apparate right out of the pub as she shifted uncomfortably beside Russell while William went to order drinks. 

 

            “So … she works for you?” Lena asked Andrea, flat-out ignoring Kara.

 

            “Yes, a junior journalist. The fluff pieces.”

 

            “Right,” Lena curtly replied.

 

            Her grip on her wine glass was tight and she knocked back the rest of it before setting it down. Jack laughed as he slung an arm around her shoulders, eyebrows rising in mild surprise.

 

            “Merlin, you knocked that back fast.”

 

            Shifting uncomfortably beside Russell, Kara opened and closed her mouth before speaking. “So, you two- you two are … going out?”

 

            “Just over a year this time,” Jack said with a pleased smile. “Lucky bastard, aren’t I?”

 

            Lena was stiff beside him and they were all spared any further talk of her personal life as William returned with two pints. Kara took a meek sip of hers and Jack snapped his fingers before slapping the table.

 

            “I do remember you!” he exclaimed. “You were in the Duelling Club.”

 

            Blinking, Kara stammered for a moment. “Y-yes. Yes, I was.”

 

            “Hufflepuff?” he asked, narrowing his eyes a fraction. 

 

            “Yes,” William grinned as he reached across the table to cover Kara’s hand with his own. “Go easy on her, you lot. She’s probably not used to spending as much time with Slytherins as Russell and I are.”

 

            Lena wrinkled her nose and tapped the side of her empty glass, watching as Kara slid her hand out from beneath William’s to take a sip of Dragon Scale. Clearing her throat, Lena abruptly half-rose from her feet, backed into the corner.

 

            “I think I might get another drink.”

 

            Jack rose to his feet. “I’ll get it.”

 

            Shaking her head, Lena curled her hands into fists. “No, no, I’ll get it.”

 

            The two men shuffled out of the booth to free her and Lena walked towards the bar, raking a hand through her hair. The pub had started to fill with the after-work trickle of customers and she stood at the bar as she waited to be served. Ordering a Firewhisky for herself, along with another glass of elderflower wine, Lena knocked the searing shot back and closed her eyes, feeling the warmth scorch her insides and fortify her. 

 

            “I didn’t know you’d be here.”

 

            Her eyes snapped open at the soft sound of a hesitant voice just behind her right shoulder. Intense heat rushed through Lena and she gripped the edge of the bar as she swallowed.

 

            “Neither did I.”

 

            “I can go-“

 

            Mouth twitching with a wry smile, Lena let out a quiet huff of laughter. “That would require an explanation.”

 

            “I take it none of them knows about me.”

 

            “Why would they?” Lena bluntly asked.

 

            Stepping up to the bar, Kara ordered herself another drink as well and Lena wondered if she’d knocked hers back just as fast to take the edge off the discomfort of being around each other. Setting down a few Knuts, Kara tapped the bar as they studiously ignored each other. It was torturous and Lena could feel the palpable tension as keenly as if they were pressed up against each other. 

 

            That was a problem in itself, the vivid memory of how that had felt, the warmth of Kara’s skin as they were vulnerable with the only person they could be. But who knew? Maybe it had changed for Kara now. She was dating William and who knew what their relationship was like, how much she revealed to him and whether she let him kiss her scars the way Lena had.

 

            A glass was set down in front of Lena and she swallowed thickly and thanked the barman. Picking it up, she hesitated. “I take it William doesn’t know either? About any of it?”

 

            “No,” Kara admitted.

 

            Nodding, Lena didn’t meet her eyes. “Then we’ll keep it that way.”

 

            Even all these years later they were still each other’s secret, and a part of Lena was glad that they had their own little world to themselves but it was also bittersweet to know that they’d never escape the awful cycle of secrecy and heartache they inflicted upon each other.

 

            Turning to leave, she was brought up short by the sight of William standing behind them, backing up to put some space between them and almost bumping into someone else. A hand grabbed her left arm, right over the place where her scar lay, and Lena dropped the glass of wine in shock. Finally looking at Kara, her face was deathly pale and rigid and her lips barely moved as she spoke, feeling her fingers like a branding iron through the wool of her jumper.

 

            “Let go.”

 

            Kara’s fingers relinquished their hold and William raised his eyebrows slightly, smiling as he reached out as if to steady Lena.

 

            “Woah, steady on. Call the Knight Bus, someone’s had enough,” he joked.

 

            Lena’s expression was flat and Kara let out a strained laugh. Turning back to the bar as she repaired the glass and cleaned up the spilt wine, drying off her boots, Lena ordered herself another one.

 

            “Let me.”

 

            She glanced sharply at Kara and quietly scoffed. “No, thank you. I can buy my own drinks.”

 

            “It’s my fault you dropped it.”

 

            “I don’t need your money. I’m fine,” Lena firmly muttered, rebuffing the few Knuts Kara tried to hand over, knowing that Kara probably couldn’t afford it anyway.

 

            Giving her the cold shoulder, Lena got a fresh glass and Kara waited with William as he ordered a round for the table. Reclaiming her seat, Lena was stony-faced as she listened to the men talk about the latest Quidditch game.

 

            Andrea leaned forward and raised her eyebrows, jerking her head off to the bar. “What do you make of her?”

 

            “It’s not my concern, is it?” Lena evasively replied.

 

            With a sharp laugh, Andrea arched an eyebrow, baby blue eyes shining with amusement. “Are you still holding a grudge over that hex?”

 

            “No,” Lena honestly replied. “No, I’m not holding a grudge over that. She’s just- she’s not my girlfriend, is she? What does it matter what I think?”

 

            “Mm. Bit meek though, isn’t she? Like a dormouse. Pretty, if it wasn’t for the scars. She didn’t have that many at school, did she? Honestly, I don’t remember her much, beyond that little tiff you had with her.”

 

            Lena bristled defensively and forced herself to take a sip of her drink before replying, her voice a little uneven. “Don’t be so shallow.”

 

            “Shallow?” Andrea scoffed, rolling her eyes. “It’s just an observation. I said she was pretty.”

 

            Russell cupped the back of Andrea’s hand and pressed a kiss to her cheek, grinning. “Not as pretty as you.”

 

            Rolling her eyes, Lena’s eyes strayed back over to Kara, who was approaching with William. Stomach turning, a sour look on her face, Lena planted her chin on her hand as she let her eyes wander up to the tiled alcove, aloof but her whole body strung with awareness. Lena was just grateful she was as far from Kara as she could get, pressed up against the panelling of the wall, thinking about how much worse it would be if she was pressed up beside her, or across from her as their eyes constantly snagged and feet bumped beneath the table. 

 

            They ordered food and Lena picked at her steak and Guinness pie with little relish, adding little to the conversation as Kara was likewise quiet diagonally from her. Plied with drinks as round after round was ordered, Lena switched from wine to Wizard’s Brew, knowing that too much of the stronger stuff would blur the edges of her resolve. Lena didn’t know whether it would make her angrier or sadder and thought beer was the safer option, already pleasantly numbed by the Firewhisky she’d had.

 

            “Right, I was thinking,” Russell said, leaning forward, elbows on the table and a childish grin on his face. “What about a weekend away in the Lake District? Drinking, Quidditch, swimming if anyone’s daring enough, and good food. My aunt has an old cottage there we could use.”

 

            “We’ll have to invite Veronica and Gayle as well,” Andrea insisted.

 

            “Plenty of room for them too. Now, is everyone on board? Will? Kara? Jack? Good, good. Lena?”

 

            Rolling her eyes, she reached for her pint and took a sip, “I’ll have to see what my work schedule is like.”

 

            There was a collective groan and Andrea gave her an exasperated look. “You’re coming. You can’t leave me with this lot.”

 

            Smiling thinly, Lena nodded, “I’ll try my best.”

 

            “Jack,” Andrea sighed, “make sure she does. I’m entrusting her attendance to you and I’ll be cross with you both if she doesn’t get time off.”

 

            “I’ll swear an Unbreakable Vow if it appeases you,” he replied with a wink, stealing some of Lena’s chips until she slid the plate over to him to finish off the rest of her food.

 

            Once their plates had been whisked away and William and Jack went to order another round of drinks, Lena slipped out of the booth, murmuring that she needed to go to the bathroom, even though she really needed some air. Winding through the throngs of customers, she pushed through the door to the toilets and sighed as she stood in front of the mirror and washed her hands for something to do, the porcelain sink speckled with remnants of pink powder and tobacco fibres, the smell of smoke lingering in the air. 

 

            Drying her hands off, Lena shook out her hair and fixed it before adjusting her skirt and pulling down the cuffs of her turtleneck sleeves. She could still feel the ghost of Kara’s touch and it made her uneasy, restless at the memory of it, of the memory of a lot of pain associated with the scar. It had been a few months since she’d found herself in a low enough place to use the quill, the bite of it not quite the blinding pain of her childhood after so many years of feeling her skin split open, but the scar itched as if she’d freshly opened it, leaving her craving the soothing numbness of Murtlap Essence. 

 

            Eyes closed, thumb pressed hard against the wool of her sweater over her forearm, Lena breathed slowly, trying to erase the sensation of Kara’s tight grasp, only to be assaulted with the memory of her lips brushing over it instead. Anger knifed through her, anger at herself and her stupidity and the unbalanced jitteriness of finding herself trapped there, pretending she didn’t know Kara so intimately. And then the door creaked open and Lena snapped herself out of her thoughts and pretended to rummage through her purse until she caught sight of who the newcomer was in the mirror.

 

            “Why do you keep following me?” Lena murmured, a frown between her eyebrows as she fished out her lipstick.

 

            “Pot, kettle, black.” Tongue-tied for a moment, Kara looked down at the floor, nervously wringing her hands before her. “I just wanted to apologise.”

 

            A sharp laugh escaped Lena as she started dabbing maroon onto her lips, her eyes meeting Kara’s in the spotted mirror. “Well, that doesn’t sound like you.”

 

            A ripple of guilt and pain and shame ran across Kara’s face as she ducked her head down. “I haven’t been fair to you, I- I know that. I just-” Kara squeezed her eyes shut, rubbing her forehead as a pink blush crept into her cheeks. “It’s always been easier to- to blame you for things so I didn’t have to- it doesn’t matter, I just … I wanted to say I’m sorry. I did a lot of thinking while I was away … I regret a lot of what happened and … I should’ve apologised last time I saw you but you caught me off guard and- well, I really am sorry. And thank you. I’ve been participating in the trial. I realised it would’ve been very stupid to reject the opportunity because of what … happened between us.”

 

            Shoving her lipstick back into her purse, Lena rounded on her and folded her arms over her chest, her expression impassive as she tried to stifle her feelings. She hated that after so many years they were still that strong, they still overshadowed how she felt about anyone else, and perhaps it wasn’t fair to Jack but Lena had no plans to have her heart broken by Kara again.

 

            “Right, well, I’m glad you haven’t lost all sense then.”

 

            Kara’s expression clouded, bewildered and searching, and Lena felt as if all of her secrets were laid bare beneath those knowing blue eyes. Hesitating, Kara licked her lips and opened her mouth, but no sound came out. Closing it again, she let out a resigned sigh, her shoulders deflating with the motion, and tried again.

 

            “I think … I’ve always known that you’ve always tried to help me, and I know I’ve been stubborn and arrogant and an arse about it - too proud for my own good - but … you’re a good person, Lena. I’m sorry if I ever made you feel like you weren’t.”

 

            Eyes bright with old pain, Lena gave her a wry smile, bitter and humourless. “If you ever did? You threw everything back in my face. Over a job. Every single doubt and criticism you knew would hurt.”

 

            “I’m sorry,” Kara hoarsely replied. “I just- you’ve always kept so much to yourself. Sometimes I felt like I didn’t even know you anymore. You … it frightened me, how easily you could keep secrets, how easily you could mess around with my life, while I could barely get it together enough to scrape by. Um … I think I just- I was embarrassed and I felt like you- you pitied me and I couldn’t bear it. I never meant to make you feel bad for that. It was all in the moment.”

 

            Lena faltered for a moment, a prickle of shame washing over her as well and she cleared her throat as she looked down at her feet. “I think … I said some things I didn’t mean as well. In the moment.”

 

            Kara let out a strangled hum of laughter, pain brightening her eyes. “Well, I think that’s one thing I’ve been better at than you.”

 

            “Mm.”

 

            “Anyway … thank you. For coming to Paris. I didn’t deserve your kindness.”

 

            “No, you didn’t,” Lena agreed.

 

            They lapsed into an awkward silence for a moment and Lena could feel the rapid patter of her heart as she drew shallow breaths, the tension too unbearable for her to stand it any longer. Before she could make an escape, put the buffer of four other people between them again until the infernal dinner ended, Kara spoke.

 

            “Can I ask you a question?”

 

            Raising an eyebrow, Lena shrugged evasively and Kara took it as a sign to forge onwards, the question halting and uncertain as she fiddled with the moonstone necklace Lena had bought her years ago.

 

            “Why did you never let people see the good in you? The things you did … you didn’t have to keep it all a secret.”

 

            Lena’s lips twitched slightly, a faint hint of bitterness to it. Her voice was soft and weary when she answered after a moment of consideration, wondering if she even owed Kara her honesty. “Because then they’d expect me to be like that all the time, and I’m tired of living up to other people’s expectations.”

 

            “How can you be okay with people having the wrong impression of you?”

 

            “You were the only person I cared about having the right impression of me. No one else ever mattered that much.”

 

            “Oh.”

 

            They lapsed into silence again, Lena hugging her arms to herself, Kara shifting restlessly, the noise of the pub drifting through the heavy wooden door. Waiting a moment longer, Lena arched an eyebrow in a cool look of haughtiness.

 

            “Was there something else?”

 

            “I won’t go,” Kara blurted out. “On the trip. Not if you don’t want me to; I know you said you didn’t want to see me again.”

 

            “Do whatever you want,” Lena choked out, a laugh getting stuck in her throat as she waved a hand dismissively. “It doesn’t matter to me at all. Not in the slightest.”

 

            The lie was caustic and hard to get out, and Lena thought it must have been written on her face how much it pained her, how it was a personal torment to be around Kara in such a way, after everything. It would have been easier to be her Healer, to see her around Diagon Alley from a distance, some layer of separation between them that they couldn’t bypass. Instead, Lena was forced to sit with her and eat dinner while their boyfriends spoke about Quidditch and the news and work at the Ministry.

 

            “Okay. I’ll go then."

 

            “Like I said, it doesn’t matter to me at all.”

 

            Checking her reflection and fixing a strand of hair in the mirror, Lena turned and made to leave but paused as she was seized by the mortifying urge to reach out and gently brush aside the messy curls of Kara’s fringe. Her fingertip grazed her temple and Kara blinked in surprise, her eyes flitting sideways to Lena’s impassive face as her lips parted.

 

            “I like the fringe.”

Chapter 26

            After Lena had left the Records Room, Kara had thought long and hard about the offer and her pride and how the faintest sliver of a chance to improve her life shouldn’t be squandered over her wounded feelings, and with that, she packed up her things, quit another job and got a Portkey across the channel to just outside of Bristol before she Apparated back to Cornwall. She hadn’t felt homesick while she was away but now, as she walked the familiar streets of Falmouth, it flooded in, belatedly.

 

            There was the old Muggle man watering his garden, there was the local corner shop where Kara had used to buy milk for Eliza with the odd Muggle coins when they ran out, and the field behind the cottage where children played with a round ball on the grass in the summer. Feeling buoyed by her decision with each step, Kara was practically floating with relief and delight as she walked down their street and spotted their cottage.

 

            Walking up the garden path, she knocked on the door and waited for Eliza to answer it. Her mother let out a cry of surprise and engulfed her in her embrace before Kara could even get out a hello. Laughing, Kara dropped her briefcase and Bastet twisted out of her arms and she hugged Eliza back tightly, burying her face in her mother’s shoulder. And somewhere in the process her laughter dissolved into hitching sobs and her smile was wavering as Eliza pulled back and cupped her damp cheeks in her hands.

 

            “Oh, sweetheart, it’s alright. You’re home now.”

 

            “I missed you,” Kara thickly replied, wiping her cheeks on the hem of her coat.

 

            “Come on, put your things upstairs and I’ll make us some coffee. I was just finishing up an order.”

 

            Stooping to pick up her case, Kara stepped into the narrow hallway and plodded upstairs. The bedroom that she would always view as hers and Alex’s, no matter how long her sister had been in her own place, was largely unchanged and Kara set her case down and removed her coat. Bastet jumped up onto the bed and curled up on her pillow and Kara scratched her behind her ears as she smiled fondly, both of them pleased to be home.

 

            Downstairs, she regaled Eliza with stories of her travels, showing her photos and plying her with gifts she’d pulled from her suitcase. The enchanted scarf that changed colours depending on the weather from a market in Marrakesh, colourful hand-painted plant pots from Peru and garden shears crafted by Goblins she’d bought for a Bezant at a Parisian jumble sale. 

 

            Alex and Kelly came over that night and Kara slipped back into her old life, interviewing for jobs and getting shut down when she revealed she was a werewolf, until she decided not to mention it and let the companies do their own checks. That’s how she ended up interviewing at The Daily Prophet for a junior journalist position, flushing at the sight of Andrea Rojas, the new owner’s daughter who’d come in to steal the Editor-In-Chief role, as she remembered attempting to hex her one time before catching Lena in the face. There was Cat Grant, the CEO, and a senior journalist with light brown skin and a classically handsome face there as well, the three of them interviewing Kara before she ultimately landed the position, much to her surprise. 

 

            It was clear to Kara that Andrea remembered her, and she had to wonder why she hadn’t blocked the decision to hire her, considering for a brief moment that maybe she’d told Lena, remembering they were friends, and Lena had told her to give her the job before she considered the fact that things were less than amicable between her and Lena and she didn’t think she’d be looking out for her this time around. She started the following Monday, showing up early in her men’s suit trousers, held up by suspenders with a wide brown tie around her neck and her favourite blue robes over the top.

 

            In the office tucked away in Diagon Alley, Kara looked through the front door of the editorial floor and breathed in the smell of freshly printed paper, the ink on the fingertips of the journalists and editors, cigarette smoke creating a haze over the floor as people called back and forth or gathered around desks. She felt nervous excitement kindle in her stomach and was a little out of her depth, until the senior journalist who’d interviewed her swept past and cast her a second glance, motioning for her to follow after him.

 

            His name was William, a Hufflepuff who’d been years ahead of her and only vaguely familiar. He showed her to an empty desk and gave her a stack of advice column drafts to edit for spelling and punctuation. A month later, he asked her out to dinner and two months after that Kara found herself inside The Hopping Pot, staring at Lena with a jolt of panic making her feel slightly nauseous. 

 

            At the end of February, Kara found herself packing a bag after work with clothes for a couple of days, the dreaded weekend holed away somewhere in the Lake District upon her, and Kara was regretting her decision to call Lena’s bluff. She knew that neither of them really wanted to be there together, in such close proximity for a few days, living and eating together in the miasma of tension that prevailed between them. 

 

            It would be unbearable and Kara had considered cancelling at least three times already that morning, but couldn’t come up with an excuse that would be believable to William as well as Alex. Reluctantly folding clothes into her worn leather backpack from her school days, Kara was ready just in time for William to Apparate onto the landing and knock on the door. She could hear the forced politeness in Alex’s voice as she answered the door to him, ushering him inside the apartment, and Kara quickly donned her robe and went to spare them both the farce.

 

            “I’ll see you Sunday,” Kara said, kissing her sister’s cheek in passing.

 

            “Have fun. Don’t fall in a lake; Vasquez said they’re infested with Grindylows.”

 

            Grabbing William’s arm, Kara rolled her eyes at Alex, who was holding a piece of buttered toast and looking dishevelled from just waking up before her night shift. Saying goodbye, she led her boyfriend outside and then let him Apparate them to the cottage Russell had given William the address for.

 

            It was more of an old manor house, not massive but certainly bigger than the cottage Kara had grown up in with Eliza. Made from warm yellow stone, wisteria crept up the walls and shaded the violet-painted door and Kara looked around, shading her eyes as she took in the green countryside and the shimmering glimmer of water in the folds of the rolling hills. It was four-thirty but the late February weather painted grey skies overhead as the sunlight failed. The door opened and Russell stepped outside, clapping his hands together as he grinned, the sleeves of his sweater pushed up to his elbows.

 

            “Glad you could make it,” he said, clapping William on the back and giving Kara a polite hug. “Come in, come in. Andrea’s just making tea.”

 

            They followed him inside and poked their heads into the kitchen to say hello to Andrea before Russell led them upstairs to their designated room. He informed them that Veronica was there and Gayle would be late, coming in from Iceland later from a work trip. Kara refrained from asking if Lena was there yet and bit her tongue on the way back downstairs.

 

            Settled in one of the sitting rooms, a cup of tea resting on its saucer on the coffee table, she plucked at the front of her sweater as a roaring fire made the air feel oppressively warm. They all gossiped and chattered as only old friends could and Kara was sort of just there , sipping her tea as she sat at the end of the sofa, unnoticed unless spoken directly to.

 

            It was just before seven when Lena and Jack arrived, windswept and tense, the latter’s usual cheer somewhat forced as he ducked in first, carrying their bags. Lena was removing a pair of emerald dragonhide gloves, her expression grave and eyes piercing as she tucked them safely in the pocket of her robes.

 

            “Look who finally showed up,” Veronica remarked, taking a sip of her brandy.

 

            Everyone greeted each other and Kara and Lena exchanged shallow nods of acknowledgement. Lena was wearing a pair of plum-coloured pants that flared out at the knee, a grey cashmere sweater tucked in and a robe of the same colour over the top, put together perfectly with her deep purple lipstick that made her lips look bruised. There were lavender shadows beneath her eyes and a rigid set to her pale face as her eyes restlessly roamed the room.

 

            “Sorry, someone was late getting home from work,” Jack said with a smile, shaking hands and kissing cheeks.

 

            “Next time I’ll let my patient die, shall I?” Lena haughtily replied, shedding her robe. “Which room is ours?”

 

            Her eyes landed on Russell, eyebrows slightly raised expectedly. He climbed to his feet to show her and Jack wrinkled his nose, sheepishly smiling as he lowered his voice to a whisper, letting Russell take their bags as he moved out of the doorway.

 

            “She’s in a shit mood.”

 

            “Ah, she’ll be fine once she sleeps it off,” Andrea dismissively replied. “Do you want some tea? Veronica’s opened the brandy already.”

 

            “Oh, go on then. I’ll have a drop of it in my tea.”

 

            He removed his long leather coat and hung it up on the stand in the entryway before making himself comfortable on the sofa. Lena returned five minutes later and accepted a cup of tea from Andrea, exhaustion slumping her shoulders. Kara watched her warily, knowing a tired Lena was one who was sharper, more irate and vulnerable to brooding. 

 

            “Long shift?”

 

            “Forty-eight hours,” Lena hummed. “I have to be on-call all weekend while I’m here too.”

 

            Jack’s mouth turned down at the corners and he sipped his tea, annoyance in the tightness at the corners of his eyes. Knocking back her own tea, Lena set her cup back down and cleared her throat.

 

            “What’s the plan for dinner?” William asked, an arm around Kara’s shoulders.

 

            “I took the liberty of visiting the Muggle shop in town,” Andrea said with a prickle of pride in her voice. “I bought a shoulder of lamb.”

 

            “A shoulder of lamb?” Lena echoed with sceptical amusement. “Did you bring a House Elf to cook that for you?”

 

            “Well, no, but I’m sure we can figure it out. How hard can it be to cook? I was excellent at Potions.”

 

            “And they’re so similar,” Veronica snorted. “What about you, Russell, William, Danvers? Your lot love their food, don’t they? Wasn’t your Common Room right near the kitchens? Lucky gits.”

 

            A faint smile crossed Kara’s face as she hunched forward, conscious of everyone looking at her. “Yes, I can cook.”

 

            “There we go. Sorted. Get the Hufflepuffs on it. They like hard work anyway.”

 

            Russell shifted forward, narrowing his eyes slightly as he stared at Kara, not unkindly, just curiously. “Where are you from originally?”

 

            “America,” Lena answered without thought. They all looked at her and she rolled her eyes, gesturing off-handedly to Kara. “She clearly has the accent.”

 

            Scoffing, Jack gently ribbed her, “she sounds more English than you.”

 

            “You flatter me,” Lena snorted.

 

            “So, how’d you end up at Hogwarts?” Russell pressed.

 

            Flushing, Kara self-consciously rubbed at her nose and her eyes flitted over to Lena’s, whose expression was soft for the briefest moment until she looked away. “My dad died so we moved.”

 

            It was the lie she’d given everyone ever since the beginning but Lena knew the truth and Kara braced herself for betrayal, for the scoff of amusement, the truth to spill out of her. But she was being unfair with that assessment, as she so often was where Lena was concerned, her own doubts about her secrets projected onto the one person she’d carelessly shared them with, thinking there would never be a time when they wouldn’t have been best friends. 

 

            An awkwardness filled the sitting room and Jack cleared his throat, climbing to his feet. “Right, well, shall we cook? I’ll help, Kara. I’m a fantastic cook, as Lena can attest to.”

 

            Lena’s face was inscrutable as she folded her legs beneath herself and stared down at her lap, picking at a stray thread in the seams of her pants. Climbing to her feet, she followed Jack to the kitchen with William and Russell in tow and set the men to peel all of the vegetables while she marinated the lamb with a variety of herbs she found dried in the pantry.

 

            They didn’t eat until almost nine, and that was with magic helping speed up the process. Crowding around the dining table, they drank wine and ate their lamb and roasted vegetables as they chatted, music playing in the background on the old gramophone that Russell had put on in one of the sitting rooms.

 

            Afterwards, those that hadn’t cooked set the dishes to wash and Lena curtly announced she was going to bed as soon as everything had been tidied up. No one tried to convince her otherwise, sharing raised eyebrows and grimaces as they shared around little glasses of port and brandy and Firewhisky. Gayle showed up close to midnight and they all went up to bed shortly afterwards, Kara changing in the bathroom down the hall before slipping into bed beside William. He was already out, snoring softly, and Kara found her mind restless as she kept thinking of Lena, who was just a few doors down.

 

            Rising early the next morning, Kara pulled on thick socks and a fleece, zipping it up to her chin. Pulling on a pair of Chelsea boots, she quietly trod downstairs, one of the steps groaning loudly in the quiet of the house. Still, it was the shadowed grey of pre-dawn and she wrongly assumed she was the only one up, easing the back door open and stepping outside.

 

            Her eyes watered from the cold as her breath exhaled before her in a plume of white and Kara startled at the scuff of shoes against stone. Whirling around, heart pounding, she blinked owlishly as she made out the sight of Lena leaning against the damp stone of the house, coffee steaming in an enamel mug as she stared back at Kara, her face a pale smudge in the dimness of the morning.

 

            “Oh. Sorry, I thought I was the only one up.”

 

            Giving her a thin smile, empty and cool, Lena let out a quiet bark of laughter, a check blanket drawn around her shoulders like a shawl. “I keep odd hours these days.”

 

            “Oh. Right. I suppose with work.”

 

            Draining her coffee, Lena pushed off the wall and made for the door, bypassing Kara, who was seized by the urge to say something. The tension between them was maddening and perhaps she’d been naïve to think that a few meetings with friends as a buffer would help, but it was torturous and Kara felt balefully helpless.

 

            “Lena-“

 

            “We don’t have to do this. We’re not friends so we don’t have to talk. If you’re going to be hanging around all the time, fine , but there’s no reason for us to talk, so just … don’t.”

 

            Mouth opening and closing as she was left stammering wordlessly, Kara watched Lena retreat back into the house with her empty coffee mug. The door hinges creaked and the door shut and Kara was left outside to watch the foggy sunrise and listen to the call of birds filling the quiet countryside as a bitter wind howled through and the rising sun glittered on top of the nearest lake. It was peaceful but there was a disquietness inside Kara as she restlessly paced back and forth, until her hands were cold and her cheeks were stinging.

 

            Taking a hot shower, she dressed quickly and made her way downstairs, leaving William to sleep off the alcohol he’d consumed the night before, and was confronted with a bleary-eyed Andrea perched on the kitchen unit near the open window as she smoked. 

 

            “Morning,” Kara murmured.

 

            “Alright?”

 

            “Mm. Was there anything for breakfast?”

 

            “Russell bought everything for a fry-up.”

 

            Nodding, Kara raided cupboards and the pantry and fridge, setting pans down to heat while she quartered button mushrooms and large tomatoes and set everything on to cook. Heating up some water in the large tin kettle, she made a pot of tea in the china and poured a cup for herself and Andrea, sitting in the cool dimness as the old house creaked and shifted around them.

 

            “How’s the job?” Andrea asked.

 

            “Good. Thank you for the opportunity.”

 

            “Mm, well, Cat really pushed for you.”

 

            Nodding as she turned the sausages and bacon in the pan, Kara cleared her throat. “Do you want fried or scrambled eggs?”

 

            Tossing her cigarette butt outside, Andrea hopped down from the counter and deliberated for a moment before leaving the choice up to Kara as she went to rouse everyone. Remembering that soft-fried eggs were Lena’s favourite, Kara settled on them and started cracking them in a pan. The kitchen soon filled, everyone serving themselves, and Lena brewed coffee and a fresh pot of tea, handing out cups as they filed into the dining room. 

 

            “Alright, who’s ready for a game of Quidditch after breakfast?” Russell asked once he’d cleared his plate.

 

            There was a groan from Andrea but Kara quietly agreed to a game, the only one there who’d actually played for her Hogwarts House Team, and Gayle agreed to play as well, while William abstained, no good on a broom but saying he had a sore shoulder. They played two against two, girls against the guys, and Kara enjoyed the bracing air as they recklessly played above the nearest lake, laughing when Jack got soaked up to his knees when he fumbled the Quaffle.

 

            Tired and damp as they played through a light rain, they all returned to the house and took turns to have a hot shower. Gathering in one of the sitting rooms afterwards, they drank tea with a touch of Firewhisky in it, making Kara’s fingertips and nose tingle, and played Exploding Snap as they chatted and laughed. 

 

            A few of them decided to go for a walk before lunch so Kara bundled up along with them and stared at Lena’s back the whole time. Anyone who’d looked at her might’ve thought she was trying to silently curse Lena, her stare so intense, but Kara was wrestling with the tangled knot of her conflicting emotions as she tried to handle being within Lena’s vicinity. 

 

            They skirted partway around the lake, hugging the foot of a rugged mountain, and Kara breathed in the sharp, cold air, her right hand encased in William’s as she let him gallantly help her over puddles and rocks and around brambles. Someone had had the sense to pack a picnic blanket and the bottle of Firewhisky and they rested in the pale sunshine, clouds on the horizon, and skipped pebbles across the surface of the lake until they disturbed a Kelpie and all legged it back the way they’d come, the picnic blanket streaming out behind Jack as he snatched it up, Andrea thrown over Russell’s shoulder, their laughter leaving them breathless.

 

            Pink-cheeked and caught in the beginning of the latest bout of rain, they made it back to the house, where Gayle and Veronica were muttering over a pot of soup they’d made for lunch. Sighing, Lena took over and made it edible, making a comment about how she didn’t know how they’d managed to feed themselves after she’d moved out, and Kara hung back, watching the oddly domestic scene of the intimate friend group she existed on the fringes of.

 

            The rest of the afternoon sort of drifted by, everyone wrapped up in blankets, sharing chocolates and sweets and listening to the radio. It seemed peaceful and unremarkable until Lena appeared in the doorway with the book she’d been reading closed over a finger to mark her spot. There was a crease between her eyebrows that Kara wanted to smooth away.

 

            “Has anyone seen my pager?”

 

            They all shared looks of mild indifference, shrugging and returning to their conversation. Kara was still watching Lena from the corner of her eye though, and could see the jut of her jaw, put out and impatient.

 

            “Seriously, has anyone seen it? I’m on-call today-“

 

            “It’ll be fine if you don’t have it on you for one day,” Jack rolled his eyes.

 

            Clicking her tongue with annoyance, Lena’s mouth thinned. “I have patients.”

 

            “Someone else will take care of them, darling. Come and sit down.”

 

            Standing there, her lips parted and her frown deepened. “Are you seriously not going to help me look for it?”

 

            Kara was already climbing to her feet to her, Lena’s eyes flickering to her momentarily, before Jack pushed himself to his feet with a sigh and walked over to her. Sinking back down onto her seat, Kara looked away as he cradled her shoulders in his hands and gave her an easy smile. “It’s fine, it’s in your bag upstairs. I put it there for safekeeping.”

 

            A laugh of disbelief got caught in Lena’s throat, “did you take it from me?”

 

            Looking sheepish, Jack’s smile wavered, “well, I- oh, come on, Lena.”

 

            She’d started to walk out of the room, bristling with annoyance, and Jack followed after, beseechingly. They could all hear him clearly as Lena’s feet hit the first step.

 

            “I only took it to make sure you didn’t go anywhere for a few hours. I was going to give it back afterwards. Honestly.”

 

            “After what?” she hotly asked.

 

            “After I asked you to marry me.”

 

            Everyone in the sitting room froze and then Andrea shed her blanket and climbed over the back of the sofa, rushing to the door. She let out a squeal of surprise and everyone else shared a look before Lena’s other friends rose to their feet to crowd behind Andrea and watch.

 

            Kara remained firmly seated, the blood draining from her face, her heart pounding and her palms clammy as the world felt like it was ending. It shouldn’t have felt like that. She should’ve felt relieved, this awkward thing between them put to bed once and for all, she should’ve been happy that Lena had found someone, just like Kara had. But she didn’t feel any of that, she just felt hollow sickness as she stayed seated and missed whatever happened next. No resounding yes came from Lena but congratulations were passed around by the people who were genuinely happy for the couple.  

 

            Everyone filtered back into the room and Lena was last, with a large rectangular cut diamond on her left hand and a dazed look on her pale face. Her eyes locked with Kara’s across the room and she seemed to turn impossibly whiter, her lips parting, shocking her back to the present. Kara swallowed the ashen taste in her mouth, swallowed the realisation that she only loved one person in that room and it wasn’t her boyfriend, trying to make her lips twitch with even a ghost of a smile with no success.

 

            “Congratulations,” she managed to choke out, hoarse and broken.

 

            “We need to celebrate,” Andrea insisted, sparing any further need for Kara to try and fake enthusiasm or excitement for the newly engaged couple.

 

            It all seemed to blur together after that, a bottle of champagne popped open, and whatever glasses were scrounged up filled to the brim and shared around. There was a toast as they clinked or raised glasses, depending on their proximity to someone else, and sipped the sweet champagne Jack brought as everyone pestered Lena with ideas.

 

            Lena seemed to shrink in on herself, a blank look on her face as she barely got out a few words, and once Kara had finished her glass she excused herself, mumbling to William that she had to use the toilet. She did lock herself in the downstairs toilet, splashing cold water on her face and drying it off with a towel before she stepped back into the hallways and faltered. Kara couldn’t go back into that room. It would kill her to do that.

 

            Instead, she went into the empty drawing room, filled with bookshelves and a sofa and stuffed armchair, moving portraits on the free spots of wallpapered walls and a window overlooking the front of the house. She paced slowly on the carpeted floor, her footsteps muffled by it and felt her resolve breaking as her heart ached painfully in her chest. Kara didn’t know what to do 

 

            The door opened five minutes later and she whirled around, blanching, only to find Lena standing there, which was the worst possible scenario for anyone there it could have been. But then who else would it have been? Kara doubted if William had realised how long she’d been gone, and no one else would have cared enough about her to see where she was.

 

            Sniffing, Kara cleared her throat. “Come to gloat?”

 

            “Gloat?” 

 

            “About how perfect your life is turning out.”

 

            Lena let out a quiet huff, shaking her head as she smiled tight-lipped. “You clearly think otherwise.”

 

            “Do I?”

 

            “Out with it then,” Lena ordered her.

 

            The corner of Kara’s mouth twitched with annoyance and she tapped her fingers against her thumb in an anxious rhythm. A quiet huff escaped her and she looked down, her jaw working as frustration settled in the lines of her shoulders, that old feeling of inadequacy holding her back from revealing the truth of her heart. Even if she had felt worthy of someone like Lena, Kara didn't think she had the right to say it. Not after everything that had happened.

 

            “You already know what I would say. You don’t need me to state the obvious.”

 

            Lena licked her lips, faltering for a moment. “Say it anyway.”

 

            Tipping her head back, Kara scrubbed the palms of her hands over her face, throat bobbing as she swallowed thickly, past the regret, anger and jealousy. Jealousy for Jack , not Lena. She pulled off her glasses and pinched the bridge of her nose as she hung her head for a moment.

 

            “He’s nice,” she haltingly started, “but ... he will bore you.”

 

            Cocking her head to the side, Lena let out a confused laugh, her eyes creasing as the faltering smile refused to reach them. “Bore me?”

 

            “You can’t marry him,” Kara quickly blurted out, squeezing her eyes shut as she hunched her shoulders against the fallout of her actions.

 

            “Well … I can’t leave him,” Lena murmured, her thumb working beneath the cuff of her left sleeve, scratching at the soft skin there, an anxious creeping gesture as she worked towards the scar. “I don’t think anyone else is ever going to love me, so … if I don’t have him-“

 

            She faltered, trailing off into silence and then letting out a strained laugh as Kara looked at her, wide-eyed with mournful disbelief. Rolling her eyes and gesturing off-handedly, Lena’s lips twisted ruefully and she sighed.

 

            “I know what you must be thinking but I’m not a narcissist; when you’re not given enough love growing up, you learn to take it however you can. Even if it’s not good.” 

 

            “You don’t have to take it from him ,” Kara rasped.

 

            Lena’s laugh was caustic, catching in her throat. “Then who? Who’s going to love me better than he does?”

 

            Me, Kara wanted to shout back, splitting the quiet tension filling the drawing room. They were tucked away in there together and she felt hot all over, dread sitting heavily in her stomach like a stone as she watched Lena slip further out of reach. It was selfish of her and she wouldn’t have pretended otherwise but she also couldn’t force the word out, and that felt like a saving grace as she refused to cave to what she really wanted to put Lena first, even if it didn’t look that way. It wasn’t particularly selflessness that stayed her, although she really didn’t want to fuck up Lena’s life more than she had in the past, but mostly cowardice. The thought of rejection made Kara’s stomach sink and she knew that she would have to bite her tongue and be happy for Lena; it was the least she could do after so much pain. 

 

            They stared at each other, the moment weighted, and Kara watched Lena dig her nail into her forearm. She might not have known everything, might not have known her friend even half as well as she’d always thought, but that age-old anxious habit from their childhood made Kara’s insides lurch with concern. Wincing, she lurched forward, stumbling over her own feet as she reached out, grabbing Lena’s arm to stop her.

 

            “Stop that,” she whispered, her other hand going to Lena’s forearm, where she gently smoothed a thumb over the cotton covering the aggravated scar, as if she could take away the itching desire to reopen the old words.

 

            Standing so close to the bookshelves lining the back wall, Lena was almost backed up against them now. Kara could see her pulse fluttering at her throat, smell the maddening perfume that she’d dreamt of, and feel the sinful urge to make a horrible decision and tear up the lives of four people for nothing. And Lena stood there, stiff and smouldering with indignation and unmistakable desire, her expression almost daring, catching Kara off-guard.

 

            Their lips were so close, one careless move and Kara’s mouth would brush Lena’s. She lowered her chin slowly, aware she was making a treacherous mistake as she crushed her lips against Lena’s in a hard kiss, expected but also surprising, as if neither of them believed she’d have the nerve to waltz back in and kiss her after so long, after everything. 

 

            For a brief moment, Lena melted into it as she kissed her back, her lips parting, tongue ever so slightly grazing Kara’s, before she came back to herself and wrenched her head aside, lipstick skating across Kara’s cheek in a maroon smudge, and pushed her away hard. Stumbling back, Kara’s hand went to her cheek, fingers worrying at the dark red, and she was faced with Lena, fuming and contemptuous. 

 

            “What the fuck is wrong with you?” Lena hissed, her voice fraught with astonished panic. 

 

            “I-“

 

            “How dare you. How dare you kiss me when my- when Jack is in the next room- when William is in the next room. Do you have no shame?”

 

            Mouth opening and closing, Kara was pink-cheeked and speechless. Forging forwards in her tirade as she fought to keep her voice down, Lena hunched her shoulders and pointed a finger at Kara, advancing.

 

            “You want to talk about how bored I’ll be while you settle for someone who is so dull that kissing me is the only way you can get a cheap thrill in life. Are you really so self-centred that you would try and take away my happiness out of spite?”

 

            “Spite?” Kara spluttered. “You think I would do it to spite you? After everything that’s happened between us, you think that would be the only reason I would kiss you?”

 

            “What else am I supposed to believe? You show up every few years like a bad penny to take advantage of me again, and I’m the one who’s left alone to deal with it.”

 

            “Take ad- is that what you tell yourself happened? That I was using you? Do you really make it into something so … ugly? Instead of admitting the truth.”

 

            A muscle twitched in Lena’s jaw and she scoffed, rolling her eyes. “The truth. What truth? I might’ve told you a few trivial secrets but that doesn’t mean you know me any better than anyone else I’ve shagged along the way.”

 

            Flushing at the dismissive way Lena brushed over everything that lay between them, Kara felt anger rise in her chest.

 

            “The truth is that you’re the coward - not me. You want to be with me and it terrifies you, doesn’t it? And you’re ashamed,” Kara said through her teeth as her voice wobbled, eyes bright with a film of tears. All of that hatred for what she was, that self-loathing for the way she looked, knowing that she would never be good enough because of what she was, rising to the surface as she gave voice to the secret fears she’d harboured inside. “Ashamed you could ever want someone like me. Aren’t you? I was never going to be anything more than a secret.”

 

            Standing her ground, Lena let out a blustering sound of indignation, drawing herself up tall as she faced Kara with her best imitation of her mother, frighteningly cold and haughty. “The only thing I’m ashamed of is my own stupidity-”

 

            “Oh, come on.”

 

            “I’ve always been too smart to fall for … whatever it is that made me think that you and I could ever-”

 

            “Alright.”

 

            “You’ve proven over and over again that you don’t give a shit about me. You’re selfish and self-pitying and too spineless to even admit the truth. And you have the nerve to say I can’t admit the truth? The truth is you’re too broken to even know what you fucking want. You’re a destructive person; nothing good has ever come from knowing you. And you know what, I think you’re just jealous of everything I have and everything you never will. You’ll never know what it’s like to be loved because you won’t let anyone. Because if you wanted me, you wouldn’t have treated me like shit for being the only person who actually did anything to fix your pathetic life for you, because your sister did fuck all, and so did your mum and your friends, because they’re too concerned with coddling you instead of telling you to grow the fuck up and take some responsibility for yourself. You are going to go through life being miserable because you’re too worried about what other people think about you when you had the opportunity to be wanted and you threw it back in my face because you are so self-conscious that you won’t let yourself believe that someone could genuinely care about you, despite what you are.” 

 

            “And that’s so easy for you to say because you’ve never had to live a day in my life, seeing the way people treat me when they know. If it was really that fucking unimportant ask yourself why I have to be on a Ministry register, why there are Ministry benefits exclusively for werewolves because no one wants to hire us. Why I’ve lost jobs and homes and family over it. Don’t stand there and tell me I’m self-pitying because of what I am when you’ve never been anything other than perfectly beautiful to the entire fucking world. You’re mad at me? Fine. I deserve it, I won’t say that I don’t, but don’t you dare gloss over the fact that my mother abandoned me when I was a kid because of what I am. You don’t know what it’s like to grow up hating yourself. You don’t know a fucking thing about how I feel.”

 

            “But you wouldn’t even admit it if I did, would you? You hate the idea that maybe I know what it’s like to be treated badly because what excuse do you have for yourself then? Hm? If you cared about me in the slightest , you would have left me the fuck alone instead of trying to spoil everything again.”

 

            “Okay, okay,” Kara interrupted, her voice rising as her cheeks flamed at the barbs that struck home. “You’ve made your feelings about me perfectly clear.”

 

            The door opened then, and Jack stepped inside with a confused look on his face, wariness in his dark eyes as he took in the two women bristling with anger and hurt. “Is everything alright in here?”

 

            “Fine,” Lena churlishly replied, raking a hand through her hair. 

 

            Kara glanced sidelong at the door, catching a glimpse at the rest of Lena’s friends scattered throughout the hallway - Veronica lingering in the kitchen doorway, Gayle seated at the table, Andrea behind Jack’s shoulder and Russell hovering in the middle of the entryway. 

 

            Hastily wiping away a tear, Kara cleared her throat, trying to get rid of the lump that was lodged there. Closing her eyes as her shoulder slumped, pinching the bridge of her nose, Lena gestured to the door with her free hand.

 

            “Give me a minute. I’ll be out now.”

 

            Lingering as if he wanted to say something else, confused by the strange tense atmosphere in the drawing room between two women who supposedly barely knew each other, Jack opened his mouth and then thought better of it. Quickly backing out, he left the door open a few inches and they listened to the scuff of shoes in the hallway.

 

            “I think you coming was a mistake,” Lena forced out after a moment.

 

            Kara let out a choked laugh, the tears brimming up with surprising fervour now, spilling over and constricting her throat. “The whole thing has been a mistake.”

 

            “I’m sorry if I gave you the wrong impression-”

 

            A loud scoff cut her off, Kara’s expression bittersweet and devastated as she shoved her glasses back on and ran her sleeve over her cheeks.

 

            “Go away, Lena,” Kara breathlessly mumbled, the words strangled. “Plan your wedding, spend time with your fiancé. I won’t bother you anymore. I hope he makes you happy and I hope you never have to think about anything as much as I think about you.”

 

            Without another word, Kara rushed out of the room, almost barrelling straight into Jack before she contorted herself to slip past, feet thundering upstairs. She shut the bedroom door behind herself and let out a pent-up sob, shuddering and pitiful, and started grabbing her scattered clothes and personal items, shoving them into her backpack.

 

 

            Lena listened to the raised voices seeping downstairs as Jack and her friends filed back into the drawing room, looking surprised and confused as a muscle twitched in Lena’s jaw and they whispered questions to her. Flopping down onto a stuffed armchair, Lena tipped her head back, and a moment later she heard footsteps thunder back down the stairs and the front door flew open. 

 

            Through the window, she straightened up and watched as Kara stalked out into the blue of falling rain, shoulders hunched and head ducked down, and then Apparated away from there, leaving Lena feeling hollow and unbalanced as guilt nettled at her. 

 

            “What the bloody hell is going on?” Jack asked, blinking as he gave Lena a mystified look.

 

            Her fluttering pulse began to settle and Lena toyed with the new engagement ring, a touch too big and the weight of it unfamiliar and uncomfortable as she twisted it around her fingers. Mouth thinning, she met Jack’s gaze and then everyone else’s, a crease forming between her eyebrows.

 

            “What?” she wearily drawled.

 

            “What did you say to her?” Veronica laughed, lounging against the wall. “Typical sensitive Hufflepuffs. This is why I hate to socialise with anyone outside our House - or tax bracket.”

 

            Scoffing, Lena sank into the armchair and rolled her eyes, opening her mouth to reply when William walked in, a pinched look of confusion on his face as he held a small brown book in one of his hands. 

 

            “Well … she’s dumped me,” he announced, rather pointlessly and they’d already surmised as much from the muffled shouting and Kara’s abrupt exit. “Turns out she’s a werewolf as well.”

 

            There was a round of expletives and shocked murmurs and Lena was silent as she gripped the arms of her chair, her eyes fixated on the book, a nagging suspicion in her mind as she bit her lip. 

 

            “Not surprising to you, eh?” William snidely said as he turned his attention to her.

 

            Rolling her eyes, Lena’s lips twitched, “I was her Healer, of course it’s not.”

 

            “Healer is it? That’s not what she’s written here. L is going to be there this weekend. She’s worried that being around you will be too hard after everything that’s happened. Let’s think; how many people here have names beginning with L, Lena? You’re smart, aren’t you?”

 

            Launching herself out of the armchair, Lena’s eyes were dangerously sharp as she stalked over to William, tearing the book from his hand as she realised the familiarity of it now - the same style as the little diaries Kara had toted around at Hogwarts. Livid, Lena’s lip curled as she stared up at him, his tall stature imposing and solid but nothing Lena could ever have been frightened of. Whatever he could do, she’d had worse.

 

            “You read her diary, you prick?” she hissed.

 

            “You’re awfully protective-”

 

            Whipping out her wand, she cast a silent hex that made his tongue shrivel in his mouth, cutting off his presumptuous comment. Anger flashed across his face and Lena tightened her grasp on her wand, rigid and white-knuckled, her face pinched with panic as she feared the truth coming out in front of all of her friends.

 

            Reaching for her, William scowled and was cut off by Jack, his hand clamping down hard on his friend’s shoulder as he gave him a grave look of warning. “Oi, dial it back a bit, mate. Why don’t you walk it off? Russell?”

 

            Russell coaxed his best friend from the drawing room and everyone else hovered uncomfortably, casting curious glances at Lena. Knowing now was her chance to defend herself, she chewed on the words for a moment, seething as she held Kara’s diary protectively in her grasp.

 

            “We were friends at Hogwarts,” Lena finally ground out, not a lie but not the whole truth. “We fell out at the start of my Sixth Year, so … there you have it.”

 

            “Oh,” Jack murmured, relief washing through him.

 

            Fixing Andrea with a hard look, Lena clenched her teeth and swallowed. “You better not fire her over this.”

 

            “She’s a fucking werewolf-”

 

            “You better not fire her,” Lena cut her off, “I mean it, Andrea. You get rid of her and I’ll-”

 

            With a confused laugh, Andrea frowned, blue eyes blinking in surprise. “Merlin, what’s gotten into you?”

 

            A headache was starting to blossom behind Lena’s eyes and she rubbed her forehead, letting out a forceful sigh as she closed her eyes. “I need to lay down for a bit.”

 

            “I thought we were celebrating,” Veronica pouted.
