            Swallowing, Lena licked her lips, the ghost of Kara’s mouth on hers making her stomach lurch. “I’ll be down for dinner.”

 

            Squeezing past everyone, she grabbed the bannister and hauled herself up the stairs, shutting herself into the bedroom she shared with Jack and resting her forehead against the wood. Letting out a shaky breath, she turned away and walked over to the bed, the mattress sinking beneath her as she sat on the edge and rummaged through her bag for her pager. The loose ring on her finger amplified her frustration and she wrenched it off, setting it down on the nightstand before laying down, a clouded look on her face as she stared at it, Kara’s diary cradled against her stomach. She wouldn’t read it, would never dare violate something sacred, but she would keep it safe until she could get it back to Kara.

 

            The door opened five minutes later and she closed her eyes, listening to Jack’s lumbering footsteps before he jostled the mattress as he sat by her feet. “Want to talk about what went on down there?”

 

            Pushing herself up onto her side, Lena sucked her teeth as an intense look of dislike crept into her features. “William’s a complete twat and I don’t want to even begin with his girlfriend - ex- girlfriend. Let’s leave it at that.”

 

            “No, I don’t think we should,” Jack murmured. “There’s clearly more to it. I think I’m at least owed the truth.”

 

            “I told you the truth. We were friends and then we had a falling out. I haven’t forgiven her for it, and I don’t think she’s forgiven me either, so all’s fair and perfectly fine with me, but I should have told her not to come on this trip. I thought it was all behind us but … I guess not.”

 

            He let out a long breath, reaching out to place a warm hand on Lena’s leg, “but we’re okay? There’s nothing I should be worried about?”

 

            “No. Nothing at all.”

 

            Lena’s pacer turned hot in her other palm and she sat up, staring down at it and deciphering the letters and symbols. Mouth turning down at the corners, she climbed to her feet.

 

            “I have to go. Work.”

Chapter 27

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

            On Monday, Kara was faced with the horrible prospect of work, her face flushing the moment she walked into the office, not quite cowardly enough to claim to be sick, as William and Andrea’s eyes landed on her. They were standing close together, Andrea sitting on his desk while he arranged his quills, their heads ducked together, and Kara paused before continuing to her desk.

 

            She’d just gotten settled in, a stack of paperwork on her desk with leads to chase up, when Andrea approached. Her pale blue eyes were frosty and her imperious bearing made Kara feel shabby and meek, expecting the worst. 

 

            “Cat would like to see you in her office.”

 

            Nodding, Kara rose from her chair and curled her hands into fists to stifle their trembling as frustration welled up inside her. It seemed an unfair punishment to suffer unemployment over offending two of Andrea’s friends but she supposed she couldn’t fault the loyalty of her boss. Andrea walked on ahead, heels clicking forebodingly, and held the door to Cat’s office open for her before following her inside and firmly shutting it behind. 

 

            “Kiera, take a seat.”

 

            Kara had long since stopped trying to correct Cat, the whip-sharp blonde woman too forceful and dismissive to remember her name, and she obediently sat across from her. Leaning back in her chair, Cat removed her glasses and set them down with a sigh.

 

            “Andrea’s brought some troubling news to me.”

 

            “Ma’am?”

 

            Pointing at her face, motioning her finger in a circle, Cat narrowed her eyes dubiously. “Regarding that.”

 

            Kara’s stomach dropped, the sickening feeling of dread filling her as she turned shockingly pale. She found it hard to breathe for a moment, her vision dimming as the resounding thought that Lena had told them swept through her mind. Whatever she’d expected the reason for her sacking to be, it hadn’t been that, her unwavering belief that this was the one thing Lena would take to her grave for Kara, if nothing else. But who else there knew? Kara hadn’t even considered telling William. 

 

            Eyes darting to Andrea’s impassive expression, Kara’s lips moved wordlessly as she tried to ask, to confirm the devastating suspicion that the person who’d kept all of her secrets had let the biggest one loose out of spite.

 

            “I had my doubts when we hired you, but I thought a fellow American might bring something fresh to the dull reporting of the British. Especially in tandem with Mr Rojas becoming the new owner of the paper. Unfortunately, I’ve found you … disappointingly British - you attended Hogwarts, correct?”

 

            “Yes, ma’am. Second year onwards,” Kara managed to rasp.

 

            “Well, I’m still hoping my initial thought was correct but we do have to do something about your little problem. We can’t let the office know we have a werewolf running around.”

 

            Swallowing thickly, Kara felt a prickle of hope swell in her chest. “You- you’re not … firing me?”

 

            Sighing, Cat rolled her eyes. “It would be an easier solution but not yet. It hasn’t proven to be a problem so far so why be hasty? I’ll admit, it’s not for any sentimental reasons; we’re short-staffed, as you know, and to put it bluntly, it’s hard to find people willing to work for as little as we’ve offered you.”

 

            A strangled laugh got stuck in Kara’s throat and she nodded, feeling weak with relief. “I’m very grateful, ma’am.”

 

            “I’m sure you are,” Cat replied, bewildered. “There’s also the matter of Mr Dey. He’s reluctantly signed a confidentiality agreement to keep this information to himself, so word shouldn’t spread through the office. I did take the liberty of checking the registry and see you’re on there which means I can’t control whether any other employees seek that out themselves but we shall cross that bridge if we come to it. Now, back to work with you.”

 

            “Thank you, ma’am.”

 

            Quickly climbing to her feet and stepping out of the office before Cat could change her mind, Kara was on her way to her desk, head down and shoulders hunched, when she heard Andrea call her name. Slowing, she turned and backtracked, shifting restlessly as she avoided glancing at Lena’s friend, her stomach twisting nauseously.

 

            “Why didn’t you use what you found out to get me fired?” Kara hesitantly asked.

 

            Andrea paused, narrowing her eyes in confusion. “Business and personal feelings are two separate things. I’m not prone to listening to other people if it’s against my own ambitions.”

 

            “Then why?”

 

            “Because your meek little Hufflepuff act might fool other people but I’ve seen your ruthless streak and I think that you’ll be a good journalist - once you figure out how to make your writing sound less like an essay.”

 

            “My experience lies in academia.”

 

            “Mm, Professor and an Unspeakable. And now you’re the grunt at a newspaper not exactly known for its journalistic integrity. I plan on changing that, so if you want to stick around for it, you need to learn to do the job you were hired for.”

 

            Brow pinched with confusion, Kara opened and closed her mouth. “I’m sorry I tried to hex you.”

 

            A laugh of surprise escaped Andrea, who arched an eyebrow. Kara’s cheeks reddened and she gave her a crooked smile.

 

            “That’s not what I meant to say. I mean, I am sorry, it was just- it was-“

 

            “Don’t worry, I don’t hold grudges as long as Lena.”

 

            “She doesn’t hold grudges; she gives any number of chances, no matter how many times she’s been hurt. She’s the best person I know,” Kara found herself saying, betraying too much of her feelings.

 

            Cocking her head to the side, Andrea gave her a look of mild curiosity. “What happened between you two?”

 

            Wincing, Kara looked down and pushed her glasses up her nose. “We were friends at Hogwarts. Until the start of my Seventh-Year. A misunderstanding we haven’t been able to move past since.”

 

            “No, that’s not it. Tell me the truth.”

 

            Blinking in surprise, she looked up and met her editor’s eyes, mouth opening and closing. Kara couldn’t tell her the truth, couldn’t divulge that secret she’d held close for so long, that old promise kept for Lena. No matter if Lena didn’t keep hers.

 

            “It’s the truth,” Kara quietly insisted. “I wasn’t a good friend.”

 

            Andrea stared at her for a moment longer before accepting the vaguely truthful explanation, and Kara’s shoulders slumped slightly with relief as her boss left her to get back to her work. There was a clear divide in the office after that, any friendship Kara had earned in relation to William was immediately snuffed out. He ignored her completely and Kara didn’t know what Lena had said once she’d Apparated home but Andrea was strictly professional, and perhaps a little bit harsher than she’d previously been.

 

            Weeks passed by and she found the job not quite as satisfying as she’d hoped, although it covered her portion of the rent and bills that she paid to Eliza after moving back in when she’d started to feel unfairly resentful seeing her sister with Kelly every day. After work, she’d help Eliza parcel up dried herbs from the garden for delivery to various apothecaries and cook dinner, a certain peace settling between them as Kara sought out some semblance of routine, of normalcy. Her life seemed very tumultuous, nothing grounding her since she’d graduated from Hogwarts, and Kara was restless and flighty. 

 

            She seemed to have no outlet for her bottled-up emotions, short of crying all the time, which she didn’t do. Coupled with the monthly experimental doses of the Wolfsbane potion she was taking, it made her irritable, aching and a little bit bitter. Work was her only distraction and even that couldn’t have been called satisfying, and she had to hold back from quitting yet another job, knowing she was burning through her options quickly. Of course, there was always Hogwarts to go back to, if there was a position, but Kara was hesitant to reach out to Dumbledore, wondering what the cost would be this time.

 

            It was August before she knew it, only a few months left in the year and she spent another night at St. Mungo’s, kissing Eliza’s cheek goodbye and Flooing into the waiting room. She had to get there earlier these days, answering questions, allowing them to take blood samples and do a more in-depth examination before giving her the latest dosage with some sort of tweaked measurement of some ingredient to find what would work. They were all much the same, leaving Kara more aware of herself while the transformation happened, although two months ago there had been less violence and she’d mostly just slept.

 

            The last dose of the potion was foul as she knocked it back in the confines of a cell, the scent of blood, bleach and fear pouring from the stones as dreadful as that first time. It never failed to make Kara’s stomach twist nauseously and even more so these days when she didn’t know what to expect. For half of her life now, she’d gone through the agonising transformation, but for nine months she’d lost all familiarity with it. Sometimes it was worse than usual, others not as bad, but the not knowing made her anxious as she waited.

 

            This time was perhaps the worst, an excruciating series of bones snapping and stretching and reforming, her body on fire as Kara saw red. Fury spilt out of her, teeth bared and a ragged sound at the back of her throat, and Kara thrashed on the cold stone floor as her body twisted into something else. Hair sprouted, her face lengthened into a snout as her jaw was wrenched forward, her arms and legs snapping at the joints as they were reformed backwards. 

 

            By the time a werewolf stood in her place, Kara was frantic and heaving, muzzle pulled back, a wild look in her eyes. She threw herself at the door over and over again, and then clawed at the walls, pulling out her nails from the effort. Wilder than usual, so much rage exacerbated by the latest dose leaving her horribly aware inside but lacking any self-control, Kara let out hair-raising howls and bruised her body with her attempts to break out of the cell. Until that wasn’t a good enough outlet for her anger and she started clawing at herself, the few nails that hadn’t been ripped out cleaving through fur and muscle, staining the floor with fresh blood.

 

            Kara woke in the cell before they managed to open the door and get her, a negative side-effect of being more conscious during the process, and she let out a mewling cry, bloody face pressed to the stone floor as she shivered in a pool of her own blood. Her whole body hurt and the overwhelming coppery tang made her convulse as she vomited, unable to even move as she blinked in a daze, stunned by pain. A Healer was next to her then, checking her airways and bandaging her up before she was on a stretcher and watching the vaulted ceiling of the hallway pass by overhead.

 

            Up on the Dai Llewelyn ward, Kara was settled into bed on her stomach, starched sheets pulled over her naked body and the bandages pulled back in increments. It was slow work by the Healer and Kara blinked back tears when the pain became too much, wishing she could sink into the grateful arms of unconsciousness like she usually did. The sting of Dittany and silver almost did it for her, her vision turning black for a moment before she resurfaced, feeling bitter about the new scars that would mark her shoulders, ribs and lower back. Each month, she didn’t think she could hate her body more; each month, she proved herself wrong.

 

            Even then she couldn’t sleep and was kept awake with a potion for the pain as she lay against the pillows, feeling hot and itchy and weak, her responses to their endless questions irritable and impatient. Rubbing at her prickling eyes as she chafed against the sheets, Kara was curt and restless, sighing and wincing as an hour stretched into two. She was forced to recount everything she remembered, rate her pain, and allow them to examine her again while she lay there, exhausted and growing increasingly upset. 

 

            Eventually, she was allowed to leave, her body weak and aching as she dressed herself and gathered her things. Her lips were thin bloodless lines and her eyes were ringed by dark bruises, hollowed out with exhaustion as she practically staggered through the hallways to the lift and rode it down to the waiting room. Flooing home, Kara’s knees buckled as she stepped onto the floor of the living room at home but Eliza was there to catch her.

 

            Assuring her mother she was fine as she was led to the staircase, Kara couldn’t make it past the second step, so tired and weak that she swayed unsteadily. In the end, Eliza made her a bed up on the sofa, lighting a fire and making Kara drink a cup of tea and a sleeping potion before she passed out beneath a blanket and slept until the afternoon.

 

            It was already grey outside when she woke to the sound of rain and Kara rubbed at her eyes and listened to it for a moment. Eliza heard her shifting movements a minute later when she tried to sit and brought her another cup of tea and a bowl of porridge to fill her up. Dutifully eating it all, Kara sank back against the pillows and didn’t move any further as she turned the radio on and listened as her body went slack against the pillows.

 

            It was approaching dinner time and Kara was feeling marginally better as the sky deepened outside and the cottage became cosy and warm. She’d picked up a book shortly before and was slowly making her way through it with little enthusiasm when there was a knock on the door.

 

            Kara set her book aside, sitting up on the sofa as her eyes glanced through the archway in the hall beyond. Pushing herself to her feet, feeling weak and weighed down by exhaustion, her whole body aching, Kara shuffled out of the living room, calling down the hallway to the kitchen as she heard the scrape of a chair, Eliza climbing to her feet.

 

            “I’ll get it.”

 

            Opening the door, Kara’s expectant look quickly turned to surprise as her lips parted. Lena stood on the doorstep, shivering, and pulled her robes tighter around her. The rain was still coming down and she had drops glistening in her dark hair, her face pale and drawn and looking less put together than Kara had ever seen her.

 

            “I- what are you doing here? How did you know I was back here?” 

 

            “I looked at your patient file.”

 

            “Isn’t that illegal?”

 

            “No, I’m a Healer. It’s illegal to use it to come to your house for personal reasons though.”

 

            Kara let out a small laugh, looking down as she gripped the doorframe, scuffing her socked foot along the stone floor. “Well, my mum’s home.”

 

            “Oh,” Lena mumbled. “Oh, sorry, I-“

 

            Hesitating, Kara opened her mouth to reply but was interrupted by her mother when no guest was invited inside. “Who is it?” Eliza called from the kitchen.

 

            Wincing, Kara scrambled for an excuse. “It’s- I, uh, it’s- it’s one of the Healers from the trial.”

 

            “Oh. Is everything alright?”

 

            “Just a random checkup,” Kara called back. 

 

            “Well bring them in, Kara,” she chided. “It’s pouring down outside. I’ve got the kettle on; do they want tea?”

 

            Turning back to Lena, who looked uncertain as she hovered on the threshold, Kara paused before she sighed and opened the door wider. With a grim set to her mouth, she stepped aside and gestured Lena in.

 

            “You’d better come in.”

 

            Wariness flicking in her green eyes, Lena stepped over the lip of the door and Kara shut the rain out. Hesitating, they were forced into close proximity of the narrow hallway and Kara wasn’t sure if she should offer to take Lena’s robe or if she should curse her for being there.

 

            “Wait here,” she eventually murmured.

 

            Turning, shoulders hunched, Kara slipped down the short hallway and into the kitchen. Eliza looked up expectantly and then frowned when no one followed after Kara. Three cups were set out and her mother was stirring two sugars into the one for Kara.

 

            “We’re going to go upstairs. It’s more private that way, for the, um, the trial stuff.”

 

            “Alright, sweetheart. Ask if they want any sugar.”

 

            “She doesn’t take sugar,” Kara murmured.

 

            Eliza slowed, giving her a curious look before handing over two mugs. Quietly thanking her, Kara carefully carried the tea back down the hallway, jerking her head to Lena and walking upstairs. She shouldered open her bedroom door and set the mugs down on the desk separating the two beds, sinking down onto hers as Lena shut the door.

 

            The room was dark and silent and Kara grabbed her wand, flicking it at the light as the room was bathed in a warm amber glow. Lena looked at Kara, the sky through the window behind her a deep blue-black as the rain continued and they were holed inside the warmth of Kara’s cramped bedroom.

 

            Remaining standing, Lena looked around, taking in the Quidditch posters and moving photos on the walls, the knick-knacks from her travels and her old blanket from Eliza. Noticing Bastet curled up on the bed, Lena quietly greeted her, reaching down to smooth her dark fur. Eventually, Lena sat down across from her, robes pooling around her, and looked at Kara. She looked sorely out of place in the cramped bedroom of secondhand furniture and the clutter of Kara’s life and the werewolf flushed slightly with embarrassment.

 

            “Why’d you tell them?” Kara finally asked.

 

            Lena stared back at her with blank confusion, her eyebrows raised a fraction. “What?”

 

            “Your friends. About me.”

 

            “I had to tell them something .”

 

            A pained huff of laughter worked its way up Kara’s throat as her expression softened with wounded dismay. “Did it have to be that I’m a werewolf?”

 

            Lena bristled, anger sharpening her features. “It was William who shared that little snippet. He stole your diary.”

 

            Blinking, Kara’s lips parted and she watched as Lena withdrew a small book and tossed it across the gap separating them. It bounced on the mattress beside Kara, who looked down, fingers skimming over the cover. She hadn’t known where she’d lost it, only that when she’d gone to write something in it, it hadn’t been where she’d thought it was. 

 

            “Don’t worry, I didn’t read it. I kept it for safekeeping.”

 

            “You- I- I thought-“

 

            “The only thing I told them about you and me is that we were friends at school - for a while.”

 

            “I’m sorry. I just- I know that … you were mad at me. Rightfully. I thought you were the only one that knew so …”

 

            “Of course.”

 

            “I- I wouldn’t have blamed you if you’d told them all.”

 

            “I would never . I promised you.”

 

            Nodding, a lump in her throat now, Kara protectively traced the spine of the diary. Reaching for her cup, she took a sip of tea and then cradled it between her hands. They trembled slightly, weakened from the transformation the night before, and she wanted to sleep but didn’t know how to end the uncomfortable, dragged-out meeting.

 

            “So, you just wanted to bring my diary back?”

 

            “Yes. Sorry it took me so long. I didn’t know how to see you without feeling horribly angry with you. And at myself too, I think.”

 

            “You shouldn’t be angry at yourself. I’ve been the creator of my own misfortune once again. You were right; he was boring and I guess he wasn’t even as nice as I’d originally thought. You, uh, you’d been bottling that up for a while though, huh?”

 

            “I think … we’ve both- we’ve been horrible to each other at times. I didn’t- I didn’t mean all of what I said. I think … maybe I meant some of it but I was unfair about other things; you’re right, I don’t know what it’s like for you. I just- I always wanted to make it easier for you, so you didn’t have to feel that way about yourself. I shouldn’t have said it though. I don’t know why the worst of me comes out so easily around you, or your worst either, except that … we’re too similar in some ways. You’re stubborn but … so am I. We’re both sad, lonely, traumatised. Maybe a little ashamed about it beneath it all.”

 

            Her tirade turned slightly breathless as she spoke to the carpet between the beds, rubbing her forehead as she brooded over their faults. Kara couldn’t argue against any of them. They were achingly similar, the hidden parts of them calling to each other, the familiarity of it peeling back the armour, allowing them to be vulnerably ugly in ways they couldn’t with other people. The curse of loving other people was to hurt them in ways you couldn’t hurt friends held at arm’s length, or strangers who didn’t know the secret parts of them. They were so good at hurting each other because they knew exactly which wounds to press on.

 

            Tears smarted Kara’s eyes and she wasn’t sure if it was because she was particularly exhausted and wrung out by the full moon or whether it was all that pent-up longing and sadness for Lena. The breath gusted out of her and she nudged her glasses up to rub at her eyes. After so many years of tying herself into knots over her condition, that fear of rejection, of loneliness and unworthiness, expressed as anger that should never have been directed at Lena, all she felt now was defeated regret at how badly it had all gone.

 

            “I don’t like feeling that way. I don’t know what’s wrong with me, why I can’t- why I have to ruin everything. I just … I wish I didn’t get so angry at you all the time, feel so hurt by you.”

 

            “It’s okay,” Lena softly murmured. “I’m the same. You and I are two sides of the same Sickle.”

 

            Letting out a choked laugh, Kara nodded. She hesitated, wrinkling her nose as she smiled tightly. “I wish we weren’t. Maybe if we were less alike we’d still be best friends. I was too scared to do it myself but … I always wished you would’ve changed your mind.”

 

            Straightening, Lena blew the air out of her lungs. “Kara, I-“

 

            “It’s alright. You don’t have to say anything. I know it’s too late for you and me, I know that you’re with Jack now, and I really do want you to be happy. That’s all I want for you. I was wrong to kiss you-“

 

            “I haven’t been with him for months,” Lena confessed, her voice a whisper. “I shouldn’t have been with him in the first place. I dated him before and I knew how he felt and … I took advantage of that so I could feel less alone. It was a shit thing to do. You were right though; I knew I couldn’t marry him. I guess I technically didn’t even say yes. But … I guess I just- there were a lot of reasons to end it but I didn’t care about any of those reasons until you kissed me.”

 

            “Why?”

 

            “Why?”

 

            “Yes, why. I mean … I thought- you never … wanted me. I’m- I’m repulsive to you-“

 

            “Why would you think that?” Lena asked, her voice hard but confused as her eyebrows drew together in a deep furrow.

 

            Closing her eyes, Kara curled her hands into fists in her lap and made a low sound of pain at the back of her throat. “You- you said- when you said that no one would want me-“

 

            “ No. That’s what you think about yourself; I never said I felt that way about you. Do you think I would’ve come if I did?”

 

            “Why did you come?”

 

            Drawing in a shaky breath, Lena gave her an aching look of sadness. “I came because … I told you to leave me alone and I- I think it would’ve been permanent this time so now I’m afraid that … I’m going to love you forever and we’ll never be in the same room again if I don’t do something about it.”

 

            Straightening, caught off guard by her candour, Kara blinked a few times as she processed what she’d heard. “What?”

 

            “You told me you were a little in love with me when we were at Hogwarts. That day at The Leaky Cauldron. Do you remember?”

 

            “How could I forget?” Kara replied, vaguely embarrassed as she rubbed her scarred cheek. 

 

            Lips twitching ruefully as she kept her eyes cast down on her robes, fiddling with the fabric, Lena was slow to continue. “Well, that’s not enough to describe how I felt about you. Still feel about you. I think … you know that already.”

 

            Mouth pressed into a flat line, a pinched furrow between her eyebrows and a clouded look in her blue eyes, it took Kara a moment to speak. She’d harboured the pain of feeling so unwanted by the one person she so desperately wanted, so much of her self-worth tied to what she was instead of who , never believing anyone would look beyond that for long enough, that it had brought out the worst of her insecurities. And Lena was stating the thing Kara had always wished to hear from her as if she should have known it all along. 

 

            “No,” she choked out. “No, I didn’t know that. You never said, I- you told me to- to go . You never-“

 

            She didn’t get out much more than a small sound of surprise, cutting herself off before Lena continued, talking quickly as her voice trembled now and she rubbed the spot where her scar was hidden.

 

            “I did. I said as much as I could, in the only way I knew how. My- my mum has always been so quick to point out everything that isn’t mine. All of it was things she paid for - not mine . I was merely permitted to live with her, eat her food, wear the clothes she bought for me, and … the damage that has done to me, that I was- I was indebted to her for everything, for just existing, that nothing was private or truly belonged to me, has been irreparable. I was a child and I was made to feel like I didn’t exist as a person, that I was hers to control because of what she gave me. Even now, she points out how my job was given to me, as if I didn’t work hard for it, and suffer for it. But you … you were the first thing that was mine . You were mine, my private thing that belonged just to me. I loved you almost immediately.”

 

            She let out an awkward laugh and Kara could see how difficult it was for her to bare so much of herself. Even when they’d been sleeping together there had never been any talk of feelings, of what they’d meant to each other, and she knew that it would’ve been easier for Lena to be physically vulnerable than to say the words spilling out of her now.

 

            “We spoke to each other almost every single day for six years, how could I not have fallen in love with you? And then it all went wrong and I had no idea what was going on in your life and I didn’t hear your voice for years outside of my dreams. But you were out there living your life and knowing my darkest secrets and I didn’t think we’d ever speak again and then … I got you back and I knew that whatever I’d imagined existed between us was- was still there so maybe I wasn’t making it all up because you said- you said how you felt. You can’t begin to know what it felt like for me, to fill up that loneliness with you again, to feel like I existed to someone else, was loved by someone I also loved, even if we could never admit that. And then you were gone again and it broke my fucking heart and I thought … I thought that being with someone else who loved me would numb the pain a bit but I was just being selfish because I knew I didn’t love him back and … every time I looked at him, I thought of you.”

 

            Her green eyes were bright now, and if Kara didn’t know better she might’ve thought Lena was on the verge of tears. But Lena didn’t cry, Lena never cried, and it was anger and bitterness and old grief there instead of tears, while Kara’s vision blurred through her own tears.

 

            “You’re still the last thought on my mind every night, and I think you always will be,” Lena told her, her voice uneven and thick and only slightly bitter. “I don’t want to be too proud to admit the truth, and I knew you wouldn’t come back this time when I’d pushed you away so harshly. I never wanted you to go, I just- I was scared and ... I didn't know how to tell you the truth … so I’m here. I’m here and I just- I miss you and I don’t want to anymore so I’ll swallow my pride and ask you … is there- is there a chance?”

 

            Kara couldn’t breathe, her chest constricting so painfully tight as tears slid down her cheeks that she couldn’t speak at all. All she could manage was a quick nod, feeling as if her heart was breaking all over again, even though she didn’t know why. Lena had done what she’d been too afraid to do, and yes, too proud to do, and Kara’s chest hurt and her throat was too tight and she couldn’t even begin to tell her how she was the only person she’d ever loved and that frightened her more than anything else in the world. If a Boggart had been present in the room, it surely would have been the spitting image of the woman sitting across from her.

 

            But Kara couldn’t say any of that and just nodded, drawing in a shuddering breath that was half a sob. Wiping her pallid cheeks on the cuff of her plaid shirt she sniffed and then slowly held her hands out. Reaching across the space between them, Lena slid her cold hands into Kara’s, slender fingers grasped by the scarred, rough hands as the quiet intimacy of something so simple sealed the moment for them.

 

            “Are you sure?” Kara eventually managed to force past the lump in her throat. “I’m only going to get greyer and more scarred. I’m going to spend days every month feeling tired and irritable and it’s- it’s not nice. ”

 

            Lena choked on a laugh, reaching across the space to cup Kara’s scarred cheek in her hand as Kara slid off the bed to kneel in front of her. “You have always been beautiful to me.”

 

            A sob worked its way up Kara’s throat as her expression crumpled, heartbreaking agony written there as her eyes immediately filled with new tears. All those years of hating herself, of avoiding the hideously scarred reflection in the mirror, of feeling so utterly worthless - especially in comparison to her friend, who had always been so impossibly beautiful - made Kara so confused. How could Lena feel that way about her, knowing what she was? It was what had always made it so easy for Kara to shut down at the first sign of trouble, quick to throw accusations to save herself from the inevitable truth that she was so unlovable and monstrous beneath the veneer of their friendship. 

 

            Lena’s hand trembled as she traced a finger across the scar on the bridge of Kara’s nose. Closing her eyes to hide her tears, Kara let out a shuddering breath, her heart racing in her chest, and she leaned into her touch, shy and self-conscious but trusting Lena to mean what she had said. She was the only person to see all of Kara, every scar - save for the new ones - in an intimate way and so she didn’t find it too hard to open herself back up to her. It was all too familiar already.

 

            Skimming her fingertips across Kara’s cheek, Lena let out a resigned sigh, her face soft with sadness and her green eyes alight with doubt. Cradling the underside of Kara’s jaw, she gave her a worried look, hesitant and nervous.

 

            “Kara? I don’t know if I can trust you again yet.”

 

            Wincing with guilt, Kara looked down, “I guess I deserve that.”

 

            “I’m asking you to give me time to work things out. I- it’ll be the same for you. When you’ve only ever been a secret, it can mess with your sense of self-worth, and with everything else that’s happened … I’m confused. I know what I want - that I want you - but I need some time to figure out how I can reconcile the things that happened with how I feel.”

 

            “Of course,” Kara murmured, shifting back on her haunches. “Right. Yes, space, good. You should take all the time you need.”

 

            “No, not space ,” Lena haltingly reassured her. “Just a bit of grace. I just don’t really know how to process things properly and with how we get around each other, I don’t want to be bitter and resentful if it’s not what I expected.”

 

            “No, I know. I- I understand. Can we- I mean …” Opening and closing her mouth, Kara looked up, giving Lena a cautiously hopeful look. “Do you think … we need to be a secret this time? I mean … I feel like maybe … so much of what went wrong revolved around that. About what people would say or think. I don’t want to make the same mistake again.”

 

            Taken aback by the idea, Lena blinked. “I- no, we don’t but you wouldn’t want people to know. Your family- your sister-“

 

            “You want to be with a werewolf and you’re worried about what my sister would think of you?”

 

            “What would they say?”

 

            Cocking her head to the side, Kara smiled crookedly, dark circles beneath her eyes and a tiredness to the slump of her shoulders. Still, she climbed to her feet and held a hand out to Lena, her spur-of-the-moment decision to rectify past problems filling her with a trembling confidence that was unlike her. “We could always find out.”

 

            Eyes widening a fraction in panic, Lena licked her lips. “Now?”

 

            “My mum is downstairs. You can thank her for the tea.”

 

            Lena’s eyes strayed to the lukewarm cup and she let out a hoarse laugh. Tapping it with her wand, she watched steam curl from the surface and took a sip. Then she glanced up at Kara, wariness flickering in her eyes.

 

            “You can’t undo it once they know. Well … unless you get a Time-Turner. You didn’t happen to steal one when you were an Unspeakable, did you?”

 

            Kara laughed, raking a hand through her curls. “If I had I would’ve tried my hardest to undo the rest of it. Come on. It’ll be okay.”

 

            “Are you sure?”

 

            “Do you not want people to know? I know that I- well … I wouldn’t be what they expected for you.”

 

            “No, it’s just- it’s hard to reveal secrets when you’ve kept them for so long.”

 

            A small smile twitched Kara’s lips and she wiggled the fingers of her outstretched hand. “This one won’t be so hard. You’re the best secret I’ve ever had.”

 

            Sliding her hand into Kara’s, Lena let her pull her to her feet. They were standing close now, in the space between the beds, the memory of their last kiss months ago weighing in both of their minds, the tension thickening. With a quiet laugh, Kara squeezed Lena’s arm.

 

            “Come on.”

 

            Snagging her tea, Lena drained it all and followed Kara out of the room. Kara had to pause at the top of the staircase, gripping the bannister tightly as her vision dimmed momentarily, a cold sweat breaking out on her forehead. The different doses and variants of the Wolfsbane Potion she was receiving each month as part of the trial had varying aftereffects and Kara was feeling particularly nauseous that evening but she steadied herself for a moment, shoulders tense beneath her shirt.

 

            “Hey.”

 

            Kara flinched at the feeling of Lena’s hand on her back, the ridges of her spine prominent and sensitive from being ripped apart and reformed twice in less than a day. Rolling her shoulders against her prickling skin, crisscrossed with old scars, Kara let out a shaky breath.

 

            “I’m fine.”

 

            Taking the stairs slowly, Kara was flushed and hollow-eyed, damp curls sticking to her forehead and the nape of her neck. Once she reached the bottom, she took Lena’s cloak this time and hung it up beside her own before stiffly walking into the kitchen.

 

            “Mum.”

 

            Turning from the pot simmering on the stove, Eliza raised her eyebrows inquisitively. “All done?”

 

            Stepping aside, Kara beckoned Lena in from the dim hallway. “This is Lena.”

 

            “Oh, Kara’s Healer,” Eliza said, stepping forward and extending a hand. “It’s nice to meet you. Thank you for the opportunity. You can’t begin to imagine how much hope the potion has brought us.”

 

            Lena’s mouth opened as she found her hand being shaken by Eliza’s and her eyes slid across to Kara. Pink-cheeked and flustered, Kara cleared her throat.

 

            “I- mum, um, well, Lena is a Healer, and has been my Healer, and- and yes, she did help me get onto the trial but she’s not- she’s not my Healer. She’s, um … she’s a friend from school.”

 

            “Oh,” Eliza murmured, blinking in surprise as she released Lena’s hand. Looking at her intently for a moment, she frowned slightly. “Have we met before?”

 

            “No, ma’am,” Lena politely replied. 

 

            “Are you sure? You look awfully familiar.”

 

            Flushing, Lena shifted uncomfortably. “Not officially. I think last time I was here I barely made it past the hallway.”

 

            Kara swallowed a groan, rubbing her forehead, fingers coming away damp. The kitchen was warm and she gripped the back of a chair to steady herself. 

 

            “Last time she was here was during the war,” Kara filled her mother in. “She brought me home that time I went missing overnight.”

 

            “Oh. Oh, yes, well … dear me, your sister wasn’t very kind last time.”

 

            Lena just laughed and Kara cleared her throat. “Mum, um … Lena’s- she’s a, uh, a close friend.”

 

            “Then it’s very nice to meet you,” Eliza smiled, a faint look of relief flashing across her face as her shoulders dropped imperceptibly, quickly drawing her own assumptions.

 

            There was an odd tension to Lena as she smiled faintly, like a caged Owl as she was introduced to Kara’s mother, anticipating the worst. “You too, Mrs Danvers.”

 

            “I’ve made lamb stew if you’d like to stay for dinner,” Eliza offered, her eyes turning to Kara before her smile slipped. Eyes widening, she reached for Kara. “Sweetheart, you look all funny. Sit down and rest a bit.”

 

            Dragging out a chair, Kara sat heavily and wiped at her sweating face, clearing her throat as she grabbed her greying curls and twisted her hair in her hands, sticking her wand through it to hold it in place. Rolling the sleeves of her shirt up to her elbows, exposing pale scarred forearms, she gave her mother a tired smile.

 

            “I’m fine, don’t fuss.”

 

            “Let me look,” Lena murmured, sinking down beside Kara, her long green skirt pooling around her.

 

            She cupped Kara’s chin in a delicate hand and flicked her wand across Kara’s eyes, watching her pupils. Smiling thinly as she was momentarily blinded, Kara hummed with amusement.

 

            “You shouldn’t fuss either.”

 

            “I’m not fussing; it’s my job.”

 

            “You’re not my Healer.”

 

            Arching an eyebrow as she glanced at her watch and kept time, her fingers at Kara’s wrist, Lena scoffed. “Is a Healer’s duty not to all?”

 

            “Not when you’ve been banned from the Bite Ward.”

 

            Giving her a withering look, Lena shook her head and Kara gestured at the back door, opening it to let in a rush of cool air. It was immediately soothing, drying the sweat on her skin and slapping some clarity back into her.

 

            “You should sleep.”

 

            “I will. Soon.”

 

            “How was the transformation last night?”

 

            “Are you really not affiliated with the trial?”

 

            “No, only the fine-tuning of the potion as part of my brewing hours. No one was really begging to be involved in it so I volunteered but I’m still banned from the ward, which means no involvement there.”

 

            “Why’d you volunteer?”

 

            Lena just fixed her with an exasperated look, conscious of Eliza’s presence behind them as she dished up dinner. 

 

            “You didn’t answer my question,” Lena countered.

 

            Mouth thinning, Kara’s eyes darted up from Lena’s to stare at her mother’s back and then back down at Lena. Nodding in understanding, Lena climbed to her feet.

 

            “It was fine. It’s getting better,” Kara lied.

 

            “Good,” Lena gravelly replied. “You just need to get some rest. And I’d recommend an Invigoration Draught in the morning if you have any. If not, I can send Morrigan with some for you. Or I could- I could bring it myself.”

 

            “Thank you.”

 

            They ate after that, the three of them at the kitchen table with a fresh loaf of bread, bottles of Butterbeer and their bowls of stew. Lena said little, her familiar quieter side coming out, but she answered all of Eliza’s questions when they were posed to her and Kara felt nervous delight in her chest at the act of the three of them eating dinner together. She had never anticipated this moment, even though it had been an entirely impromptu decision, but it was something more important to Kara than she could put into words.

 

            After they’d finished, Lena tried to clean up but Eliza ushered the two young women out of the kitchen and they took up seats at opposite ends of the sofa. Lena watched her for a moment and Kara pretended not to realise until Lena leaned in, lowering her voice.

 

            “How was it really?”

 

            Running a hand through her hair, Kara let out a heavy sigh. “A bad one. I just- I remember it the next day and I felt more … feral than usual. Cut my back up nicely. Tore my nails out clawing at the walls.”

 

            She flexed her fingers with the newly grown neat nails, letting out a small laugh. Lena looked ashen and worried when Kara met her eyes with a grim smile on her face.

 

            “It’s alright. Some of them haven’t been bad. There was one two months ago where I kept my mind the whole time. I couldn’t stop myself though; I wasn’t … in control. Hurt worse than it ever has and they said it took ten minutes longer than usual transforming both ways.”

 

            Lena hummed dubiously, rubbing a finger over her lip in a rather distracting manner. Kara caught sight of a bracelet slipping from beneath the cuff of Lena’s shirt, surprisingly familiar, and she reached out across the gap between them and touched it.

 

            “You still wear it.”

 

            “Yes. And you still wear your necklace.”

 

            She jerked her chin towards Kara, who touched the moonstone and let out a soft laugh. “I only take it off for the full moon.”

 

            A small smile twitched Lena’s lips and she looked down at her lap, fiddling with her fingers and the Slytherin ring on it. Hesitating, she swallowed and tried again.

 

            “Kara, do you think- do you think you and I- do you think we’ll ever get past it? Do you think there’s any hope?”

 

            Swallowing thickly, Kara gave her an uneven smile. “I wouldn’t be myself if I didn’t think that. I’ll win your trust back, I promise you that. There - a new promise for us.”

 

            Lena let out a huff of laughter as Kara held out her hand. She took it and met her eyes. “We still have our oath, you know.”

 

            “I think we’ve broken that a few times already.”

 

            “I don’t know,” Lena murmured, “we kept coming back. Maybe it was that oath holding us to our words.”

 

            “Is that what we are now? Friends?”

 

            Rolling her eyes, Lena’s cheeks dimpled as she grimaced. “I don’t think you and I will be friends again. I don’t think we have been since school.”

 

            “Oh, no, we were friends of a sort,” Kara grinned.

 

            “Of a sort. Right. And what are we now? Girlfriends, of a sort?”

            

            “Something like that.”

 

            “Something like that,” Lena echoed, her voice a low mumble of amusement. “I guess we’ll see.”

 

            “Mm. Just … don’t go kicking me out again. I’d rather you just hex me for being a complete and utter idiot.”

 

            “A bold choice from someone who knows how bad my hexes can be.”

 

            Wrinkling her nose, Kara smiled. “It would still be preferable.”

 

            Sighing, Lena shook her head and then gazed at Kara for a long moment. “I should leave you to rest.”

 

            “You shouldn’t but I know you will.”

 

            “I’ll bring you that potion in the morning.”

 

            “Thank you. And for the diary. And for being the bigger person. I know it should’ve been me, and … maybe it would’ve been if I’d known I had a shot in the dark, but … I probably wouldn’t-“

 

            Snorting, Lena climbed to her feet. “Not a chance you would’ve.”

 

            “A small chance,” Kara defensively replied. “Once I got over being rejected. If I- if I thought that … maybe you did feel the same way.”

 

            Lena’s lips twitched with an ambiguous smile, revealing nothing about whether she agreed or disagreed with Kara. Stepping out into the hallway, she turned to the kitchen and Kara hovered as she listened to Lena thank Eliza, and then thank her again when she was invited back any time. 

 

            When she rejoined Kara in the hallway, she donned her damp cloak and Kara opened the door, stepping outside with her. The rain had recently let up and Falmouth was wet and glistening, the smell of fields and trees and salt in the air and the warm nebulous glow of lamp posts cast them in a dim light on the doorstep of the cottage.

 

            Staring at each other for a moment, not knowing what to say or do, they both opened their mouths to speak and then dissolved into shuddering laughs. Sharing a sheepish smile, they waited for the other. 

 

            “Thank you,” Kara eventually said, breaking the silence.

 

            Nodding, Lena’s expression clouded and she chewed her lip before slowly speaking. “This might sound awful but … please don’t break my heart again. I don’t think I have it in me to give you any more chances than this. I’m sorry, that might not sound fair to you-“

 

            “Lena Luthor,” Kara interrupted her. “I will not break your heart again. I promise.”

 

            A strained laugh escaped Lena and she ran a hand through her hair, averting her gaze. “Sorry, I just- you have so much power over me that it frightens me. You frighten me.”

 

            “Come here,” Kara whispered.

 

            Lena stepped forward and found herself engulfed in Kara’s embrace. Chin propped up on Lena’s shoulder, Kara closed her eyes and exhaled, feeling something come loose in her chest as she held Lena in her arms. They had so rarely hugged that it felt so much more intimate than a hug should’ve, and Kara had thought about it so often during their time apart, craving Lena’s touch, her warmth, the smell of her perfume, that she felt weak at the knees. It made her hold her tighter for a moment longer.

 

            Eventually, they came apart and she touched Lena’s cheek. “The only time you need to be afraid of me is on a full moon. I’ll try not to be too much of a monster the rest of the time.”

 

            “Oh, Kara , I never thought you were a monster,” Lena sighed with a tender look in her eyes. “Not even on a full moon.”

 

            She backed away then, a pale smudge in the dark, a crooked smile on her face as she raised a hand in a slight wave. Kara hovered just outside the doorway, backlit by the warm yellow glow inside, and watched as Lena Apparated away before she slipped back inside.

Chapter 28

            A knock on her bedroom door roused Kara the next morning, her body stiff and protesting as she pushed herself up, shifting the blankets and the cat and rubbing at her bleary eyes. Her face was flushed pink and creased with sleep, the imprint of her pillow on her cheek, and she made a low sound at the back of her throat.

 

            Eliza cracked the door open and poked her head inside. “Morning sweetheart. Sorry to wake you but Lena’s here.”

 

            Any trace of sleep vanishing, Kara bolted upright, eyes wide and her hair frazzled. Fumbling for her glasses, Kara shoved them on her face, cursing as her body ached at the speed she was trying to move. Feet going into slippers and attempting to flatten her awry curls and messy fringe, Kara crossed over to the door as Eliza opened it and stepped into the hallway to give her space. 

 

            Pausing at the top of the staircase, Kara’s heart twinged in her chest at the sight of Lena hovering just inside the door, wrapped up in a burgundy cloak with her dark hair braided down her back. She looked sleek and polished, a serious look on her face as she glanced around at the interior of the small cottage, moving photos on the walls, a sagging sofa covered with cushions and blankets, the radio going in the kitchen and plants crowding the space. Kara’s appearance snagged her attention and she blinked as she looked up at her, a faint softening of her face.

 

            “Morning,” Kara gravelly greeted her, voice still thick with sleep.

 

            Slowly plodding downstairs, Kara wished she wasn’t wearing her worn pyjamas, blue flannel bottoms and a t-shirt she’d picked up at a dragon sanctuary on her travels with a Swedish Short-Snout on the front, and felt a slow flush creeping into her cheeks. Eliza made a comment about needing to find her gardening gloves in her room, the cottage too small for any privacy that wasn’t behind a closed door, and Kara descended the rest of the way.

 

            “I, uh, I can’t stay. I just wanted to bring you this.” Reaching into her pocket, Lena pulled out a small vial and held it up, a smile toying at the corners of her mouth. “As promised.”

 

            “Thanks,” Kara murmured, taking it and running a hand through her hair, shifting from foot to foot.

 

            “How’re you feeling today?”

 

            Shrugging, Kara gave her a weak smile. “Tired. I’ll sleep it off today though. I’m fine.”

 

            “Okay, well make sure you eat something.”

 

            “I will.”

 

            “Um … I can’t tonight - my shift’s twenty hours - but maybe when I’m off … we could have dinner together? You could come to mine. If you want to.”

 

            Ducking her head, Kara thumbed the stopper of the vial and bit her lip. “Have you moved?”

 

            “No. Still at the Dublin flat.”

 

            “Is that Chinese place still open?”

 

            A quiet laugh escaped Lena and she nodded. Nodding back at her, Kara’s eyes creased at the corners. “Okay. So … you’ll send me a letter when you’re free?”

 

            “Alright.”

 

            “Okay.”

 

            Looking down at her watch, Lena sighed, her mouth thinning. “I have to go.”

 

            “Want to Floo?”

 

            Glancing into the living room and its mound of cold ashes, Lena hesitated and then nodded. Kara gestured her ahead and fished the plant pot filled with the gritty powder from the mantel and held it out. 

 

            Standing in front of the empty grate, they looked at each other for a moment and then Lena grasped a handful of Floo powder. Clearing her throat, she pressed her lips into a flat line, a shallow crease between her eyebrows.

 

            “Bye,” she blurted out.

 

            A shuddering laugh of surprise escaped Kara. “Have a good day.”

 

            Mouth hitching into a crooked smile, Lena dashed her handful into the fireplace and ducked inside before naming the hospital and being whisked out of sight. Lingering for a moment, Kara uncorked the vial and knocked back the potion, shuddering at the taste, and then turned, taking a step forward and pausing at the sight of Eliza on the stairs, her gardening gloves nowhere to be found.

 

            “Sweetheart, I’m not sure you’re very good at this flirting thing. You should have kissed her.”

 

            “Mum,” Kara ground out, her cheeks heating. 

 

            “What? A friend from school? Don’t take me for a fool, Kara Danvers.”

 

            Getting slightly defensive, Kara’s expression turned sulky as she met Eliza in the hallway. “She is a friend from school. I- well … we haven’t been friends since school. I wasn’t very nice to her. She, um-”

 

            Kara cut off, clearing her throat as she got tongue-tied around her explanation. Slipping through to the kitchen, she pulled out a chair and curled up on it, hugging her knees to her chest. 

 

            “She was in a different House - a Slytherin - so Alex never really liked her. I didn’t tell her we were friends until after. I guess … I was scared of what people would say. Her brother went to Azkaban after the war.”

 

            Softly sighing, Eliza ran a hand through Kara’s hair, giving her a solemn look. “Sweet girl, don’t let your sister’s quick judgement cloud your own. If you like her then you shouldn’t hide it - especially not from the people you love.”

 

            Looking down, Kara’s mouth twitched down at the corners. “I just- I really like her and I’m scared I’ll ruin it all again. I haven’t been very nice to her since school either.”

 

            Kissing her head, Eliza rubbed her back. “Tell your sister.”

 

            Nodding as she swallowed, Kara rubbed her tired eyes and let out a small sigh. The potion had taken the edge off and she ended up frying bacon in a pan, yawning and leaning against the counters with a cup of coffee in hand while Eliza got a headstart on her work. They ate breakfast together and then Kara helped her, packaging up quantities of petals and thorns, stems and flower buds and roots into little parchment envelopes or drawstring bags and vials. It was a cool day, rain threatening to fall, and Kara enjoyed the monotonous work at the kitchen table as she took a break from her own job.

 

            Passing the day by slowly, Kara thought a lot about Lena and the new development in their relationship, this fragile and surprising thing. She was afraid to even speak to her, so much clouding the air between them that one wrong thing could shatter their latest attempt to act on their desires. It had always been different for them; the desire for a friend turning into a budding crush and then the burning feelings and attraction and the unbearable tension. Now it was something gentler but no less desirable, the need for truth and trust and a chance to have the things they’d denied themselves over petty high school prejudices.

 

            She went to work the next morning, still a little tired, ignoring the glances from her various bosses and supervisors that had become the norm after a full moon, and went about her job drafting puff pieces and editing whatever came past her desk. It was grunt work for the most part, red ink slashing out words and making edits, correcting spelling and reformatting for the journalists who got to add their name to their stories and see it printed in black and white. Kara would get her opportunity if she proved herself but she just liked the routine of an office job, the smell of parchment and the ammonia of the ink, the whirring and hissing of clunky machines and the scratch of quills and copious amounts of tea wheeled past on trolleys by interns that were only just below Kara in the pecking order.

 

            Andrea was still intensely watchful but Cat liked her in a rather dismissive manner so Kara was content to continue with what she was doing and hope her hard work paid off. Not that it was that demanding, coming home every day with dry eyes and ink-stained fingers being the worst of her job, while Alex was usually nursing some sort of injury or lingering effect of a hex or charm she’d encountered while arresting criminals or following up suspects and charges. It was almost a relief that her sister was usually too tired to make frequent visits to the cottage and she slipped away to Lena’s house two nights later, curled up on her sofa as they shared a special fried rice with curry sauce and dumplings, a bottle of wine on the coffee table and music on Lena’s gramophone. 

 

            Kara didn’t stay for very long, wanting to so badly but not trusting herself to not mess it up and seeing the exhaustion written into the lines on Lena’s face. She helped tidy up after dinner and then murmured she had to go, giving Lena a shy smile as she hugged her robe to her chest and hesitantly broached the topic of Kelly’s birthday party the following Saturday night. It was just a house party at their apartment and Kara hadn’t told Alex about Lena yet but had decided that a party would be the best place to break the ice without causing too much of a scene.

 

            Warily accepting the invite, Lena smiled unconvincingly and Kara laughed, reaching out to give her hand a squeeze before she lost her nerve to act on her greater urges and ducked her head down. Rubbing the back of her neck, she cleared her throat and hurriedly said goodnight before leaving, Apparting to Cornwall and leaning her forehead against the locked front door as she cursed herself and walked inside. It seemed stupid that she was so hesitant to kiss Lena, having done all manner of things to her in the past but this time had the added severity of their feelings laid bare in the open and so Kara intended to take it slow, to build their trust back up.

 

            Biding her time until Kelly’s birthday, Kara’s anxiety built until it was twisting her stomach as she picked out a present for her and carefully wrapped it, selecting a pair of cerulean velvet flared pants and a matching vest over a ruffled shirt for the party, forking out a few Sickles for a bottle of Old Ogden’s Firewhisky to take with her and then leaving early to help set up. Music was already wailing out of the flat and Kara let herself in, the first one there as she called out, summoning Kelly from the cramped bathroom. 

 

            Kissing her cheek, Kara gave her a brief squeeze and handed off her gift and offered up the Firewhisky. Making herself useful, she opened packets of crisps and bags of nuts and plated up mini quiches and sausage rolls out of the oven while Alex finished getting ready and Kelly turned water into ice for the drinks. 

 

            Fidgety as her eyes kept glancing to the door, she started trailing Alex around. Her sister was wearing fitted leather pants and had a rolled cigarette behind her ear and kept glancing at Kara funnily as she set up a barrel of mead and strategically placed fat candles and lit them to create a comfortable glow before checking on the scotch eggs and cocktail sausages, plucking a pineapple and cheese stick from a plate and sighing as she rounded on Kara.

 

            “Merlin, what is it? You’re bouncing around like a Cornish Pixie.”

 

            Humming with nervous tension, Kara gave her sister a strained smile, holding her bottle of beer by the neck as she leaned back against the kitchen counters and picked up an egg and cress finger sandwich. Setting her bottle down as she took a bite, nervously fixing her fringe as she built up the courage, Kara cleared her throat and inhaled deeply, steeling herself.

 

            “I’m going out with someone.”

 

            Alex's interest was immediately piqued, her eyebrows rising and brown eyes bright with delight. “Really? Who? Do I know them?”

 

            Cringing, Kara let out a nervous laugh. “Yes, you do. We went to school with her. I just- can you have an open mind, please?”

 

            Suspicion darkened Alex’s face as she finished upending another packet of crisps into a bowl. “Who?”

 

            Wolfing down the rest of her sandwich, Kara mumbled around a mouthful as her cheeks reddened. Swallowing, she quickly picked up her beer and drained half of the bottle to buy herself a moment longer as Alex stared at her expectedly.

 

            “Lena Luthor.”

 

            Falling silent as the Weird Sisters album wailed in the background, Kara’s teeth worried at her bottom lip as she warily watched Alex absorb the information. Then her sister let out a small scoff of laughter and then a louder one before she was full-blown laughing, shaking her head as she picked up a cocktail sausage and gathered up two plates.

 

            “Figures.”

 

            “What’s that supposed to mean?” Kara asked, bewildered by Alex’s reaction.

 

            Glancing sideways at her, Alex arched an eyebrow. “Do you remember crying your eyes out when you told me you’d been secretly friends with her for years? Well, I didn’t buy it. You were fucking heartbroken.”

 

            “Um … okay. You don’t seem … mad.”

 

            Alex snorted, snagging two beer bottles and gesturing for the caps to remove themselves before handing one to Kara. They clinked bottles and her sister grinned.

 

            “Were you scared to tell me?”

 

            “Yes,” Kara spluttered, a nervous laugh slipping out.

 

            “I know I wasn’t very subtle about my hatred for her a few years back. I still dislike she was a Slytherin and wish you had more sense than that but … well, she’s not all bad. She doesn’t have a Dark Mark.”

 

            “And how would you know?”

 

            Blinking, Alex’s brow creased. “I raided her family’s house after the war.”

 

            Kara paused at the mention of that, knowing in some regard that Lena’s house had been raided when her brother had been arrested, but she hadn’t really put it together that Alex had been there, that they would have made Lena prove she wasn’t complicit. Her stomach dropped and she raised her bottle to her lips, taking a swig.

 

            “Well … anyway, I’ve invited her tonight. I wanted the two of you to get to know each other properly.”

 

            “Here? She’s coming here? Now? Bloody hell, Kara, a bit of warning would be nice. Winn is going to be here.”

 

            “I- well … he started it.”

 

            “She carved him to bits!”

 

            “You weren’t even there.”

 

            “What’re you two arguing about?” Kelly asked with amusement, emerging from the bedroom in the middle of putting hoop earrings in. Alex whirled around and pointed an accusing finger at Kara.

 

            “She’s going out with Lena Luthor , and she invited her to the party.”

 

            “Oh,” Kelly said with mild surprise. “She’s the one with the brother … I remember his trial.”

 

            “Right, well, just … keep her out of the way,” Alex said, pinching the bridge of her nose. “I’m off-duty tonight and I don’t feel like breaking up duels over school grudges.”

 

            Frowning, Kara’s mouth turned down at the corners. “She’s nice, you know.”

 

            “Mm, charming, I’m sure.”

 

            Rolling her eyes, Kara finished her second beer and set the empty bottle down before running a hand through her hair. Checking the time, she wondered whether Lena was the type of person to be early or late to parties, and as the flat started to fill, friends and other familiar faces trickling in, Kara grew more nervous at Lena’s arrival.

 

            It was almost an hour later when she caught sight of a wary figure in a long-sleeved velvet green dress and knee-high black boots. Relief cut through Kara and she realised she’d been worried Lena wouldn’t show up. They’d never spent any time together in public and this was something big that they couldn’t take back, but she was there, a little black gift bag in hand and a guarded look on her face as her eyes glanced around. They landed on Kara and she saw some of the tension bleed from Lena as she straightened, the corners of her mouth twitching.

 

            Making a beeline for her, Kara wrapped her in a gentle hug, eyelids fluttering as she smiled, breathing in the smell of Lena’s perfume. Pulling back, her smile grew a fraction wider.

 

            “You came.”

 

            “Of course,” Lena murmured, eyes darting around restlessly.

 

            “Let me get you a drink. I brought Firewhisky but there’s beer and mead and wine as well.”

 

            “Oh, hm, just wine please.”

 

            Nodding, Kara grabbed her hand and pulled her through the throngs of people standing around chatting. Finding a clean glass, she filled it with the first wine she found and handed it to Lena, feeling a little more relaxed now, but that quickly changed to panic as she caught sight of Alex honing in on the couple.

 

            “Shit,” Kara muttered, turning around and hunching her shoulders.

 

            “What?”

 

            “Alex.”

 

            Lena glanced over Kara’s shoulders and her lips twitched slightly, amusement or a nervous gesture Kara couldn’t tell. She turned and found herself close to her sister, shrinking back against Lena in a defensive manner.

 

            “Hi,” Kara said. 

 

            “Hi,” Alex slowly replied, arching an eyebrow.

 

            Clearing her throat, Kara stepped aside and gestured to Lena. “You remember Lena.”

 

            “Healer Luthor.”

 

            “Auror Danvers. How’s the shoulder?”

 

            Blinking, Kara’s face furrowed and she looked between them. “Um …”

 

            “Your sister ends up on my ward quite often,” Lena quietly confessed. 

 

            Letting out a surprised laugh, Kara raised her eyebrows at Alex. “Oh, really? Alex forgot to mention that.”

 

            “Last I heard you had a falling out so it didn’t seem relevant. And, well, seeing as I found out she was your girlfriend about an hour ago, you can’t hold it against me.”

 

            Lena looked sheepish and took a quick sip of her wine, avoiding Kara’s eye. Swallowing, she cleared her throat and raised her gift bag, attempting to change the topic. “I brought a present for Kelly.”

 

            Bemused, Alex reached for it with two fingers, gingerly hooking the handles. “It’s not a cursed necklace, is it? Merlin, lighten up Kara, it’s a joke. Come and say hi, Lena.”

 

            Glancing at Kara, Lena hesitated for a moment before following Alex. Lingering behind a moment longer, Kara let out a low groan and followed after them. As introductions were made, Kara nervously hovered behind Lena’s left shoulder like a shadow, all of her friends greeting her politely, although there was a faint undercurrent of tension between the ones who remembered her from Hogwarts, duelling in the hallways.

 

            Kelly was gracious and welcoming though, opening the gift to reveal a little bottle of perfume and looping Lena’s arm through hers to go and get them fresh drinks once they’d finished theirs. Feeling a little hot from her lingering anxiety, Kara plucked at the collar of her shirt and shifted beneath the mildly accusing stares of James, Winn and Imra. Pretending to ignore them, Kara cleared her throat and sipped her beer.

 

            “How long’s this been going on then?” James asked, looking confused by the whole thing.

 

            “Um … we were friends at school,” Kara admitted. “We kind of fell out for a bit but then we, uh, we sort of became … friends again a few years back. Then we sort of … fell out again. It’s a long story.”

 

            “Hang on a minute,” Alex said, rounding on her with suspicion in her eyes. “You cheeky cow, you were sleeping with her before and you didn’t tell me?”

 

            “Alright, don’t get your wand in a knot,” Kara grumbled, frowning. “Obviously it didn’t go well.”

 

            Snorting, Alex slung an arm around Kara’s shoulder and jostled her good-naturedly. Everyone else looked a little disgruntled and Winn was frowning, rubbing his chest as he remembered the old ghost of pain from their duel. Feeling flustered and sheepish, Kara cleared her throat.

 

            “I know it- it doesn’t make sense to you all … but if you could just give her a chance. I- I know she was a Slytherin but … she was my friend before any of you were. And we were all arses to them as well so I don’t think it’s fair-”

 

            “Fair?” Winn echoed.

 

            “Don’t try to claim the moral high ground. I know you got hurt but it was an accident and you hexed her first,” Kara ground out. “You just assumed she was harassing me because why else would a Slytherin want to be around me, right?”

 

            Arms folded over his chest, James raised his eyebrows. “You never mentioned her, not once, so clearly you had a reason for that too.”

 

            “Yes, this sort of reaction was the reason. I was embarrassed about what people would think and … I regret that. But the fact is she’s been better to me than I have to her, so if you think she’s so awful then you should have an even lower opinion of me. She’s the best person I know.”

 

            Kara was pink-cheeked and getting louder from the alcohol, her shoulders squared and jaw set. Squeezing her shoulder, Alex gave her a pointed look. “How about you do a lap?”

 

            Bristling with frustration, Kara curtly nodded, her jaw clenched as she ducked her head down and forged through the partygoers. Snagging a cheese and pineapple stick, Kara dragged the cubes off and chewed quickly, her eyes darting around as she tried to spot Lena. She found her tucked away near the fridge with Kelly in conversation, another glass of wine in hand, and she felt the knot in her stomach loosen.

 

            Slinking closer, she drained her own drink and fetched another one before sidling over to the duo and giving them a weak smile. “Alright?”

 

            “Lena was just telling me about her work on the Wolfsbane Potion. I didn’t know she was the reason behind the trial you’re on.”

 

            Rubbing the back of her neck, Kara smiled wanly, “oh, yes. Well, she’s really clever.”

 

            A small smile twitched Lena’s lips and she gave Kelly a wry look. “Kara’s always had a rather inflated opinion of my intelligence.”

 

            “Don’t be daft, it’s not inflated at all. I used to think you were so smart that if anyone could find a cure for me, it would be you. Childish naïvety I guess but then I never expected to even have a potion that even semi- works so maybe one day.”

 

            Lena blinked, staring at her with an inscrutable expression on her face as she took a measured sip of her wine. Kara was feeling jittery and annoyed and she dominated the conversation with Kelly until her sister-in-law went to circulate the room and mingle with some of her work colleagues and other friends.

 

            Left alone with Lena, Kara felt a little hot beneath the prickling stare of the other guests, sure that they were attracting looks from anyone that knew Lena, no doubt by sight only, with her old Hogwarts House branding her even years after graduation. Then there was the added gossip of Lena’s brother and Kara’s scarred face that had always drawn looks of surprise at best and revulsion at worst. Feeling self-conscious, Kara fetched beers for them both, pressing one into Lena’s hand and leaning in close.

 

            “Come here,” Kara whispered, grabbing Lena’s hand and towing her into the spare room as the music and pressing bodies and dim lighting covered them.

 

            It hadn’t quite returned to its former cluttered self since Kara’s brief stay but she shuffled past a few boxes and Alex’s old battered school trunk and turned to face Lena. Giving her a relieved look as the door muffled the majority of the music and the lack of bodies left the room mercifully cool, Kara leaned against the crowded desk.

 

            “I was staying here for a bit but … you know, it’s hard being around people in love when you’re just … bitter and lonely.”

 

            Lena let out a huff of laughter, “is the sentiment the same or are you moving back in soon?”

 

            Coy, Kara ducked her head down, adjusting her glasses as she lightly replied. “No, it’s not the same. I think I’ll stay with my mum for a bit though. It’s more spacious.”

 

            Humming, Lena pressed her sweating bottle against her cheek and eyed Kara. Her eyelids were heavy and there was a slightly dishevelled air about her, pale cheeks holding a touch of colour, lips parted and rosy from the wine she’d been drinking earlier.

 

            “Sorry. It was getting a bit much out there,” Kara said after a moment.

 

            “What’s wrong?” Lena softly asked, her expression tender.

 

            Rubbing the bridge of her nose, Kara shrugged. “Too many people, too many opinions.”

 

            “Ah,” Lena hummed, stepping in closer. “You’ve realised that maybe it’s not a good idea to invite your hated girlfriend to a birthday party to reintroduce her to your friends who had it out for her at school? Shocking.”

 

            “They don’t hate you.” Lena arched an eyebrow in disbelief and Kara wrinkled her nose, cringing slightly. “They don’t particularly like you but they’re blinded by school and the war and your brother.”

 

            Nodding, seemingly unaffected by their opinions, Lena took a sip of her beer. Lowering the bottle, she let out a quick laugh. “Well don’t worry. I didn’t expect them to like me or be very happy that you invited me. It’s not surprising; it’s the reason why we’ve always been a secret.”

 

            Biting her lip, Kara’s eyes roamed the room before finding their way back to Lena’s face. “You shouldn’t have been. It felt like it mattered so much back then but I wish … I wish it had turned out differently. Maybe you and I … well, maybe we could’ve been honest from the start. I might not have been afraid to kiss you if I hadn’t cared so much about what people think.”

 

            “I think you would’ve been,” Lena murmured and let out an awkward laugh. “I think you’re still afraid to kiss me now, and they all know.”

 

            A frayed laugh escaped Kara as she closed her eyes, pushing off the desk and taking a few steps away from Lena, clutching her beer bottle tightly. She tipped back half of it and then turned around.

 

            “The last time I kissed you it didn’t go so well.”

 

            A smile twitched Lena’s lips, her heavy-lidded gaze shuttering as she heaved a sigh. “I was frightened that time. Proposed to half an hour before that, there I was, kissing you back for a second, and I knew that if I didn’t stop … I would’ve done something horrible to someone who didn’t deserve it. I would never want to be the other woman. I was mad at you for exposing that weakness in me, that part of me that’s always wanted you, no matter how many years and miles. I think I’ve always hated how easily I come undone around you, all of my hard work to seem so unaffected and disciplined right out the window the second I’m alone with you.”

 

            She let out another small laugh, shaking her head. Kara felt her heart in her throat, a tremor in her hands as she fiddled with the bottle, taking in the faint look of amusement on Lena’s face. “I’m sorry.”

 

            “Don’t apologise. You did me a favour in the end. I think … I would’ve been so heartbroken I might’ve actually gone through with marrying Jack. It would’ve been miserable for all parties involved.”

 

            “How did he take it?”

 

            “Not well.”

 

            Nodding, Kara’s lips twisted ruefully and she meekly looked up, meeting Lena’s eyes again. “I’m sor-”

 

            “Don’t say it,” Lena laughed. “Even if you’d rejected me the other week, said you were sick of me and- and could never in a million years go out with me, I would’ve still dumped him months before that without any input from you. And I wouldn’t have gone back to him either so it’s not your fault. I just- I’m telling you this because I want you to know what I wanted and what I didn’t.”

 

            “What do you want?”

 

            A sharp smile crossed Lena’s face as she leaned against the desk and set her bottle down, crossing her arms over her chest. “I want you to kiss me.”

 

            A quick laugh escaped Kara and she moved closer, setting her beer down beside Lena’s, bottles clinking, and then nudged her knees apart as she stood between Lena’s legs. Almost nose to nose, Kara reached up to move a strand of hair out of Lena’s face and trace her fingertip down her temple and cheek and jaw. Hesitating, she leaned in slowly and pressed her lips to Lena’s.

 

            Lips parting beneath hers, Kara could taste the beer and wine and mint toothpaste, reaching out to thread her fingers through Lena’s dark hair while her other hand cupped the side of her neck, thumb ghosting down the middle of her throat. Lena’s fingers pressed into Kara’s back as she closed her eyes.

 

            “You look really nice tonight,” Kara murmured against Lena’s lips.

 

            “I hope so; I picked this dress out just for you.”

 

            “Trying to tease me?”
