            “A little. It’s only fair.”

 

            Kara hummed as she kissed Lena again, one hand going to the pale expanse of skin between her knee-high boots and the hem of her ruched dress, which had ridden up slightly as Kara pressed Lena against the desk. Breaking off again, Kara glanced over at the door, which had been shut but not locked, and hesitated, glancing back at Lena.

 

            “Come over tomorrow,” Lena murmured as she kissed Kara’s jaw. “I’m not working. I’ll cook for you.”

 

            Heart beating quickly, Kara struggled to swallow, the breath catching in her throat. “Okay.”

 

            “Okay,” Lena whispered before drawing back. “We should rejoin the party.”

 

            A small smile tugged at Kara’s lips and she nodded, hesitating before reaching out to fix Lena’s lipstick. Letting out a quiet huff of laughter, Lena pressed her lips together, trying to fill in the gaps of her smudged lipstick before she reached out to fix Kara’s hair for her.

 

            “I really do like the fringe, by the way.”

 

            Picking her hand up, Kara kissed her knuckles, blue eyes bright and warm, and then snagged her drink. Lena grabbed hers and they slipped back out into the party, smoke lingering in a haze above the heads of the gathered people, a new record on and Kara’s friends measuring out shots of Firewhisky as she towed Lena towards them.

 

            She fetched two more glasses and Nia poured for her before she handed one off to Lena and clinked their glasses. It seared its way down her throat and Kara felt lighter than she had in months, maybe even years, a wide smile on her face as she found it within herself to relax. Slowly, some of the others drew Lena into conversation, a barrage of suspicious questions answered smoothly or evasively until they stopped expecting to start a duel in the living room. 

 

            They drank all night, someone bringing out a deck of Exploding Snap and trying to create a house of cards, which blew up in their faces at random intervals, sending the cards scattering. People trickled in and out until the flat started to empty past midnight and it was just Kelly’s closest friends, Kara sprawled on the floor, leaning back against the armchair Lena was curled up on, nursing their drinks as Alex and Imra smoked and they ate slices of the birthday cake James had baked for his sister.

 

            Kara had already laid claim to the spare bed before the night had even started, and when they all started passing out on the sofa, on the rug with blankets and couch pillows, she climbed unsteadily to her feet and helped Lena up. Nose to nose, she smiled, slow and eyes creasing, pleasantly drunk.

 

            “Do you want to stay?”

 

            They’d never gotten drunk together before, never been at the same parties or same pubs with friends, and she was amused by the quiet watchfulness of Lena’s drunkenness, blinking owlishly as she sat silently for the most part. She didn’t like to dance and she hadn’t sung along when they’d put on one of Kelly’s Celestina Warbeck records and she didn’t quite fit in with the dishevelled group of friends, but Kara had the sense she’d enjoyed being there nonetheless.

 

            “Um …”

 

            “It’ll be a squeeze but you can sleep with me.”

 

            “Alright.”

 

            They were the last ones awake and Kara stepped over Querl’s sleeping form, ushering Lena to the spare room and gently easing the door shut behind them. Hesitating, Kara opened her mouth and then shut it again, her eyes turning slightly panicked as she pressed the back of her hand to her forehead, fringe ruffled and throat tight.

 

            “I didn’t- I didn’t bring any pyjamas,” she hoarsely stated.

 

            Closing the gap between them, Lena cupped Kara’s chin in her hand and smiled slightly before pushing past her in the narrow space between bed and desk.

 

            “Undress for me,” Lena instructed her, sitting on the edge of her bed.

 

            Kara let out a strained laugh, hesitating a moment before kicking off her shoes and undoing the buttons of her waistcoat. Hating the look of herself with her many scars but knowing it was nothing new to Lena, that they’d been here before on numerous occasions, albeit getting there with some difficulty, Kara slowly undressed. She removed it and turned then, shedding her shirt to reveal scarred shoulders and then more of her back, a silvery crosshatch of old wounds. 

 

            Climbing back to her feet as Kara started to fold her clothes on top of the desk, Lena stood close behind her, eyes trained on Kara’s back, and reached out to lightly trace a new one. She felt her stiffen under her touch and heard the breath get stuck in Kara’s throat as her own closed up.

 

            “This one wasn’t here before,” she murmured before her finger slid along another one. “Or this one.”

 

            Making a frayed humming sound at the back of her throat, Kara tipped her head back slightly. Lena could see her eyes squeezed tightly shut, the tense set to her shoulders. Slowly, she wrapped her arms around Kara and kissed the side of her neck.

 

            “How do you remember?” Kara whispered.

 

            Pressing her nose into the soft spot behind Kara’s ear, Lena hummed a laugh. “I’ve memorised every inch of you I could lay my eyes on. I would notice if you cut your hair even an inch or got a new freckle or a slight tan. You’ve always had such a low opinion of yourself but the truth is I can’t help but notice you; I’ve never been able to stop.”

 

            Making a low sound of amusement at the back of her throat, Kara slowly undid her pants and folded them as well and Lena sank back down onto the edge of the narrow bed, unzipping her boots and removing them. She made quick work of the row of buttons on the front of her dress and Kara half-turned, giving her a cursory glance of surprise as Lena removed it, her hand instinctively going to her scar. 

 

            Turning the rest of the way, Kara reached for her arm and gently peeled Lena’s fingers off the scar, reading the faint writing in the wan glow of the lightbulb overhead. I am a failure. Bending her head, she kissed it gently and then kissed Lena. 

 

            “You have never been a failure,” Kara whispered. “Do you hear me?”

 

            The breath caught in Lena’s throat and Kara could see the rapid rising and falling of her chest, the difficulty it took to reply. “Everyone fails at some point.”

 

            “You’ve never failed me . Not once .”

 

            “People are dead because of me.”

 

            Jerking back slightly, realising the burden of guilt that Lena still carried after all these years, Kara was speechless for a moment. “Not because of you. I’m sorry I ever made you think you were responsible for it, that I thought the worst.”

 

            “It’s alright.”

 

            Wanting to fall at her feet and apologise for it all, for everything that still lay between them, unforgivable and unforgotten still, eyes smarting with tears, Kara caught her hand and gave it a tight squeeze, forging onwards as she babbled drunkenly, her words slurring together.

 

            “It’s not your fault. You did your best with the knowledge that you had but you were just a kid.”

 

            Swallowing thickly, Lena turned away sightly her voice pitching low but gentle as she replied. “Leave it alone, Kara. Let’s go to bed.”

 

            Lena wasn’t looking at her but Kara nodded, slipping her glasses off and pulling back the blankets. It was a single bed, a squeeze for both of them but Kara turned on her side, her chest against Lena’s back as she pulled the quilt up over them and kissed her shoulder before wrapping an arm around her waist. Pressed against each other, alcohol humming in the system, they both fell asleep quickly and Kara could’ve sworn she’d never slept so soundly in her life.

Chapter 29

            When Kara woke the next morning it was to an empty bed. Blinking slowly as her mind caught up with herself, she looked around, pressing the quilt to her chest as she sat up and fumbled for her glasses on the desk. She knocked something light off the desk and once she’d gotten her glasses on, Kara’s eyes snagged on a little folded butterfly on the floor.

 

            Reaching down, she carefully unfolded it and read the brief message scrawled in Lena’s neat script, feeling a dull ache in her chest at how she could’ve missed something so simple.

 

Kara,

 

Sorry I had to leave without saying goodbye. I was paged into work. Hangover cures are in the kitchen.

 

I shouldn’t be long. Dinner at five?

 

Lena x

 

            Running her finger over their names, written boldly for the first time since they’d met all those years ago, she smiled at the kiss at the end. A small thing but so impactful, no fear about someone reading their notes and letters and finding out about them. Kara folded the paper back into a butterfly and got out of bed, feeling the roiling effects of a hangover making itself known.

 

            Dragging on last night’s trousers and shirt, she tucked the note safely in her pocket and slipped out into the cramped kitchen. Lena had left a few vials behind and Kara snagged one, immediate relief washing over her as it slid down her throat, and she looked around at the tidied flat. All bottles had been cleared away and the dishes were drying on the draining board. Everyone else was still fast asleep and Kara had the sneaking suspicion that Lena had been busy in the early hours of the morning or her sister had acquired a House Elf she hadn’t mentioned.

 

            Her friends started to rouse shortly afterwards and Kara doled out the hangover cures with a slightly smug air about her as she informed them Lena had left them for them. None of them made any comments but James rolled his eyes as he knocked his potion back and left shortly afterwards with Nia and Querl.

 

            “You’ve been busy,” Alex mumbled when she stumbled out of her room at eleven, eyeliner smudged around her eyes and her hair unkempt. 

 

            “Oh, no, that was Lena.”

 

            “Where’d she go?” Alex asked, looking around.

 

            “Work.”

 

            “Work? Bloody hell, she was half-bollocksed, last I remember.”

 

            “Potion,” Kara said by way of an explanation and an offering. “At least one of us was prepared.”

 

            Grunting in agreement, Alex drank hers and visibly straightened, the waxy sheen on her face vanishing as her slumped shoulders squared. Moving over to a window, she opened it and lit a cigarette, smoking as a light pattering of rain ushered in the smell of damp pavement and trees.

 

            “Breakfast? Or lunch, I guess,” Alex suggested to the remaining few. “I could murder something greasy.”

 

            Imra glanced down at her watch, “I can’t. I’ve got Mike’s Quidditch game in an hour.”

 

            “More fool you.”

 

            Rolling her eyes, Imra gathered up her things and dished out kisses on cheeks before leaving. Winn was still yawning and rubbing his eyes on the sofa and he said he was going home to sleep for the rest of the day.

 

            “Come on then, go wake the birthday girl up and let’s get something to eat. You’ll have to pay though,” Kara yawned. “I’m skint.”

 

            Exhaling a lungful of smoke out the window, Alex stubbed out the cigarette butt in the ashtray and went to wake her fiancée. Kara waited while they both dressed in the first clothes they could find, all of them looking hungover if not feeling it, with smudged makeup and tangled hair and the odour of liquor that cling to them as they Apparated to the courtyard behind The Leaky Cauldron and filed inside.

 

            Tom greeted them warmly and Kara spent some time in the kitchen, perched on a counter as she talked to the familiar staff and watched them cook up lunch for the customers. Slipping back out with a tray holding her order of tea and coffee Tom saddled her with, Kara claimed a seat and started stirring sugar and milk into her tea.

 

            It was fortifying and she poured another cup from the pot and refilled Kelly’s, the three of them reading gossip from last night as they stifled yawns and blinked gritty eyes, still not entirely ready to be awake yet. The three of them ordered English breakfasts and Kara wolfed hers down, the grease making her feel better as she finished first and sat with another cup of tea cupped between her palms.

 

            “Go on then,” Alex said as soon as she’d finished, fishing out a cigarette and lighting it with a finger.

 

            “What?”

 

            “What’s the full story? Out with it.”

 

            Rolling her eyes, Kara transferred her cup to one hand and rubbed the scar on her cheek. Shrugging, she sighed softly. “You already guessed it last night.”

 

            “Well, I want to hear it from you.”

 

            Kelly was finishing off her bacon and her dark eyes darted between them as she ate quietly, listening closely.

 

            Shrugging again, Kara looked a little ashamed as she slunk down in her chair. “I told you everything about school. How we used to meet in a secret room in the Astronomy Tower. We used to meet in Hogsmeade as well; she brewed a Polyjuice Potion once and would show up in disguise. Even went as you one time.”

 

            “Me?”

 

            Kara gave her a quick grin. “I think … well I started to fancy her, I guess, and that’s where it all sort of … went wrong. Obviously with what I am … anyway, then the whole thing happened with Winn and that just made things harder but it wasn’t until … there was stuff going on with the war. I blamed her for a lot of it and I was so wrong but the damage was done. I accused her of having a Dark Mark and it- it ended badly. We didn’t speak at all after that, not for years, until I ended up on the Bite Ward at St. Mungo’s while she was working the full moon shift. It was … horrible.”

 

            She let out a nervous laugh, raking a hand through her hair and taking a sip of tea to steady her. 

 

            “Well, it took a while but she- I guess she’s always looked out for me. Like with that night at the McKinnon’s. She’d find me outside St. Mungo’s, leaving after a full moon, and she’d take me home and make sure I was okay but we just- we’d argue every time. I didn’t know the half of it for a long time but … I blamed her for all the wrong stuff. I was a right idiot. I told her how I’d felt and she sort of admitted she’d felt the same and I- it took a while before we could get past it enough to … I don’t know what we were doing. We started sleeping together, of course we did, while I was working at Hogwarts. I, uh, I actually had a lot more free time than you thought, I just used to go and see Lena.”

 

            Alex had smoked her cigarette down to the filter and lit another one, draining her second cup of coffee as Kelly set her knife and fork down. Neither of them interrupted as Kara let the words spill out of her, kept inside for so long that it was a relief to get them out.

 

            “Well … it turned out she was partially responsible for me getting a job at Hogwarts. Called in a favour with Dumbledore - I’m not sure if I can tell you what went on there - and, um, well … I can be a bit proud sometimes-“

 

            “Oh, you fucking idiot,” Alex groaned, cigarette clamped between middle and forefinger as she rested her fingertips against her temple, already knowing what came next.

 

            “I found out and … I reacted badly. Again. Um … sort of a theme there, I suppose. It all sort of blew up and she kicked me out and I quit my job.”

 

            “See, I knew there was something going on.”

 

            “I didn’t lie,” Kara meekly replied, blue eyes vulnerable and wide. “I was pregnant. I- I did-“

 

            “You what?” Kelly softly exclaimed.

 

            Cringing, Kara’s cheeks flushed red. “It was years ago. An accident. It’s fine, it’s for the best. Um … but yeah, I went travelling, as you know, and then she showed up in Paris somehow-“

 

            “Merlin, Kara, are you that dense?” Alex sighed, giving her an aching look. “She didn’t show up somehow; she asked me where you were and told me about this great trial she’d helped develop for werewolves. She told me she’d treated you so she knew you were a werewolf and if I knew where you were, she’d pay you a visit and explain it all to you. I told her where to find you.”

 

            Blanching, caught off guard by the truth, Kara’s mouth opened and closed for a moment. “Oh. You- neither of you said.”

 

            “As mentioned, you’re a stubborn arse half of the time and I knew you’d be too proud to accept help if it came from someone who loves you so I let you think she found you alone. Obviously, I didn’t know the truth behind all of this.”

 

            “Oh. Right. Well … I came home. Didn’t see her for a few months after that, until I was seeing William.”

 

            “Bloody hell, remember him?” Alex laughed, nudging Kelly. “Professor Binns had more personality. One thing I’ll say is you have better taste in women than men.”

 

            “You told me to go out with Mike,” Kara spluttered.

 

            “At school. You know, going to Madam Puddifoot’s and for your first kiss. I didn’t think you’d date him. And William was almost as bad and I had absolutely no input in that, thank you very much.”

 

            Giving her sister a withering look, Kara shook her head, mouth thinning. “Dating options happen to be rather slim when you’re a werewolf. I mean, I didn’t tell William anyway - two months seemed rather soon - but it turns out his friends were Lena’s friends and I ended up on that weekend trip with them to the Lake District, remember? Um, so Lena was seeing one of them. I’m not sure if you remember him - Jack Spheer? Well … he proposed while we were there.”

 

            “I don’t like where this is going,” Kelly winced. 

 

            Kara made a low sound of strained amusement at the back of her throat. “We had another argument and then I- I kissed her.”

 

            “Kara Danvers,” Alex said, scandalised and enjoying herself far too much.

 

            “I, uh, I left. Again. Um … and then she showed up about a week ago.”

 

            “Showed up? Showed up at home? Was mum there?”

 

            “Yes. I told her she was my Healer. Anyway, we had this long talk and, uh, she wasn’t engaged anymore. I introduced her to mum then and … well, it’s still all a bit new and a bit, um, well … obviously there’s a lot of history there. I know- I know you don’t like Slytherins and … the whole thing with Winn … I just- I like her. A lot. If you could try for my sake-“

 

            Reaching across the table, Kelly touched the back of Kara’s hand. “School’s hard for everyone, especially in a war with a family like hers. She seemed lovely last night.”

 

            Giving her a grateful smile, Kara’s eyes slid to Alex’s face and she swallowed thickly. Her eyebrows rose a fraction and her sister sighed, green smoke escaping past her lips.

 

            “If you’re happy, I’m happy,” Alex slowly replied.

 

            Sceptical, Kara let out a hoarse bark of laughter. “Pardon?”

 

            Rolling her eyes, Alex shook her head and then stubbed out her cigarette. “You heard me. I don’t know her but I trust you, and I’ve watched you skulk about miserably too often for my liking so if she’s the reason for this sudden improvement, I’m not going to protest.”

 

            “It’s also none of our business,” Kelly diplomatically added.

 

            “Right. That too,” Alex nodded.

 

            A laugh escaped Kara, confusion crumpling her face as her mouth curved up at the corners. And then she laughed again, and again until her shoulders were shaking. Her eyes smarted with surprising tears and she hunched over, elbows on the table, the heels of her palms nudging her glasses up as she covered her face. Laughter turning to sobs, Kara dissolved into tears as the two women across from her were left speechless by her sudden breakdown.

 

            Swearing under her breath, Alex climbed to her feet, rounding the table to jerk the chair out beside Kara. Sitting, she wrapped an arm around her and urged Kara’s head onto her shoulder while Kelly pressed tissues into her hand.

 

            “Sorry,” Kara croaked, the breath hitching in her throat as she blotted her cheeks. 

 

            “What’s the matter?” Alex gently asked, her usually firm demeanour softening as concern eclipsed everything else.

 

            “Nothing,” Kara sniffed, seeming as surprised as the other two women. “I just- I made up this whole thing in my head. Ever since school. How … we could never even be friends because of what people would think, and then we were sleeping together knowing it would never be anything but a secret because of what I am and how you’d all hate her for her family … and this whole fucking time it wouldn’t have even mattered. I tell you and … it’s none of your business.”

 

            Mouth opening and closing, Alex looked at Kelly and then gave Kara’s shoulders a reassuring squeeze. Wiping her nose, Kara exhaled forcefully, her throat tight and embarrassment welling up.

 

            “Oh, well … if it’s any consolation, I probably would’ve been pissed if you’d dropped all of this on me a few years ago. It definitely mattered to me then. Honestly, if I didn’t have her patching me up every month, I would probably still be a right cow to her but you don’t really have much dignity when you’re stark naked, bleeding in a hospital bed while she patches you up.”

 

            “I’ll say,” Kara rasped, a shaky laugh escaping her. 

 

            She swallowed thickly, sniffing and then laughing again. Her eyes were slightly red and her cheeks were pale and splotchy, cut through with the silver lines of her old scars.

 

            “I’m just being silly.”

 

            “You’re not,” Alex murmured, a curious look of understanding in her eyes. “You love her, don’t you?”

 

            Wrinkling her nose, Kara smiled tightly. “Yes.”

 

            “Does she know that?”

 

            “Sort of.”

 

            “Do yourself a favour, love,” Kelly said with a wry smile. “Make sure she knows. It’s the worst thing in the world to be left wondering whether someone feels the same way about you.”

 

            She shared a look with Alex, whose mouth thinned as she ran a hand through her hair. “I got there in the end.”

 

            “How’s the wedding planning?” Kara asked, attempting to change the topic.

 

            Even now, it felt strange to be talking about Lena, to confess all of the things that had transpired, the ways she’d held Kara’s heart for so long. She could’ve spent hours divulging every facet of information stored away inside, every bit of Lena that was hidden from the rest of the world. Given the opportunity, Kara would never shut up about her. But it was new and she was frightened and her family were gracious enough to put her complex relationship to bed for the time being. It was already nearing the middle of the afternoon when they left the pub, the three of them tired and wilting despite the hangover cures, and Kara went straight back home to nap before her alarm clock started clanging an hour before she was to meet Lena.

 

            Showering and changing, she briefly saw Eliza and told her she’d be out for dinner, kissing her cheek and stalling when she told Kara to invite Lena over for dinner, before Apparating from the front doorstep to the landing outside Lena’s flat. Taking a second to fix her overcoat and wayward fringe, Kara raised a hand and knocked. It was opened a moment later by Lena, dressed in a deep plum jumper and high-waisted black jeans, black velvet slippers on her feet and her dark hair damp and clinging to her temples from a recent shower. The familiar scent of her perfume cut through the antiseptic smell of the hospital that seemed to cling to her stuff brought home from work.

 

            “Hi,” Kara said with a nervous smile.

 

            “You came,” Lena said with well-masked delight, a flicker of warmth in her green eyes as she jerked the door open wider. “Come in.”

 

            “You look knackered,” Kara noted as she stepped over the threshold, unwinding her scarf and touching Lena’s cheek. 

 

            “I’m shattered. Some antique dealer thought it would be a good idea to use a Box Blasting charm on a locked truck with an Erumpent horn inside it. Just about blew up his entire shop in Diagon Alley. All hands on deck for that one. Idiot.”

 

            “Are you sure you want to do dinner tonight? If you want to sleep-“

 

            Lena let out a small laugh, rubbing the bags beneath her eyes. “Yes. I feel like … we haven’t really gotten to spend much time together yet. Let me cook for you.”

 

            “I should be cooking for you. What’s on the menu?”

 

            “Steak.”

 

            “I can manage that,” Kara murmured with a firm nod.

 

            “You don’t have to. I invited you over; you’re a guest.”

 

            Letting out a nervous laugh, Kara raised her eyebrows slightly. She gingerly smiled, fiddling with her fingers. “How about you let me cook and then you do me a favour?”

 

            “Ah,” Lena hummed, a shrewd look clouding her face. “Why does this feel like a trap?”

 

            “My mum would like me to invite you over for dinner at some point. You know, for a family Sunday roast. Of course, you can say no; I know your work schedule is mad anyway so I'll just tell her-“

 

            “Oh. Well … that’s a generous offer. I get off early next Sunday morning so I can make it for dinner.”

 

            Blinking, mildly surprised by Lena’s willingness, it took Kara a moment to respond. “Oh. Um … okay, good. Great. Um … how do you like your steak?”

 

            Lena laughed, her brow creasing slightly with amusement. “Medium-rare.”

 

            “Right.”

 

            Showing her where everything was in the kitchen, Lena was made to sit with a glass of wine as Kara set a pot of water on to immediately boil and made the peeler take care of the potatoes. It all felt terribly domestic and only slightly different to the times she’d come over for takeout and sex after work, the added weight of a relationship making the moment seem more meaningful this time.

 

            Dinner was ready in short order and Lena refilled their glasses as Kara carried the plates to the table. They sat together at the end of the table, at adjacent seats. A little sheepish as she picked up her cutlery, her cheeks turned pink as she hesitated.

 

            “Sorry, I, uh, I have my steaks rare now. Is it- will it bother you? The plate gets a little … red.”

 

            “I’m a Healer,” Lena said with faint amusement. “I’m not squeamish.”

 

            “Okay, I just- I wanted to check-“

 

            “It’s a common side effect of Lycanthropy. Or even those who are attacked by a werewolf, not on a full moon. Um … I just mean, I know that some things will be different for you but I want you to know it’s okay, it doesn’t bother me.”

 

            “Of course you’d know that,” Kara murmured, quietly scoffing as she cut into her steak, a glimmer in her blue eyes.

 

            A quick smile crossed Lena’s face and she took a sip of wine, her green eyes light with amusement and softening as she looked at Kara. “I’ve read just about every book on the condition I can find. You said last night that if anyone could find a cure, you thought it would be me. Well, I’ve looked, I’ve tried. Even when she banned me from the ward, I still read as much as I could in my free time.”

 

            Chewing slowly, the meat tender and soft, Kara swallowed and cleared her throat. “Thank you. I don’t think I deserved that.”

 

            “Even at our worst, if I could’ve spared you a single full moon, I would’ve. I’m still searching, even now.”

 

            “I don’t think there is a cure,” Kara mumbled.

 

            “Not yet. Everything is incurable until someone finds the magic for it. I can’t pretend to understand the agony and … I’m not sure how much it’s worth, but it would never change how I feel about you. You will always be my Kara, regardless of the phase of the moon.”

 

            Setting her knife and fork down, Kara didn’t respond as she stared at Lena for a long moment, her stomach clenched and her pulse spiking. She was out of her seat without thinking, looking down at Lena for a brief moment before she kissed her, tasting wine.

 

            Caught off guard, it took Lena a moment to set her cutlery down and fumble for the edge of the table to push herself up. Kara knotted her fingers in her hair and pressed her close, so much pent-up tension spilling forth. She’d thought about this for days, weeks, months. Every time she’d seen her, the memory of the last time was branded in her mind, reminding her of everything she’d had and lost.

 

            And now she was holding her in her arms and Kara couldn’t breathe right as she kissed her, feeling Lena’s hands beneath the hem of her shirt. The muscles of her stomach went taut beneath the cold fingers grazing over scars and Kara made a small sound of objection into Lena’s mouth, making them both freeze.

 

            “Is it alright-“

 

            “Yes,” Kara whispered, touching their foreheads together. “Yes, I trust you.”

 

            It was easy for Kara to say after all the times she hadn’t trusted her, but she meant it, knowing what it felt like to be fully seen by someone, loved by someone, scars and all.

 

            “Come here,” she whispered, drawing Lena into a tight hug and holding her closely for a moment. “Hello.”

 

            A quiet, choked laugh escaped Lena and she pressed their cheeks together, her chin on Kara’s shoulder. “Hi.”

 

            “Do you want to finish your dinner?”

 

            “No.”

 

            Kara pulled back and looked at the half-eaten remains of their dinner before her eyes moved back to Lena’s face. Fingers sliding down the soft cashmere of Lena’s sleeve, Kara cradled her hand and then turned it, running a thumb over her palm. She brought it to her mouth, gently kissing the web of lines and then curling Lena’s fingers back over it, leaving her clutching the ghost of her kiss in her hand.

 

            Kissing her again, Kara pressed her against the table, cutlery and china rattling, and Lena’s mouth parted beneath hers. Thumbs stroking over Kara’s scars, Lena traced the lattice of silvery lines, her eyes closed, touch guiding her, and Kara wrapped her arms tightly around her waist.

 

            “Come to bed,” Lena whispered, chastely kissing the corner of her mouth.

 

            She tugged on Kara’s shirtsleeve as her mouth curved with a smile, green eyes wary but bright. Kara practically stumbled over her own feet, in a trance as she was led to Lena’s room, still the same as it had been before, all of this familiar, even the restless embarrassment as she unbuttoned her shirt, a lump caught in her throat at the thought of baring her scars. It was nothing new - Lena had even seen them last night, or early that morning rather - but that had been innocent, that had been to sleep, her scarred chest and stomach pressed against Lena’s smooth back after enough drinks to numb the self-consciousness. 

 

            This was something else entirely, her scars itching at the thought of being touched so purposefully, her skin crawling at the mere idea of Lena looking at her. Now she regretted her haste, thinking she should have finished dinner and had more wine to dull her nerves. Sensing her unease though, Lena drew in closer, her hands going to Kara’s buttons for her, undoing them slowly as she kissed the underside of her jaw. 

 

            Peeling it off her shoulders and dragging it down her arms, Lena kissed along her collarbones, lips warm and featherlight over the first scar Kara had ever received, the one she’d pointed out to Lena the first time she’d had the guts to willingly let her look. Her heart was a quick patter in her chest and her breath caught in her throat as she closed her eyes, her face hot and her hands balled into fists, gently resting on Lena’s hips.

 

            “Can I touch?” Lena asked, a little belated as she raised her mouth from Kara’s shoulder.

 

            Making a low, permissive hum, Kara let Lena push her down onto the bed, let her drag off her flared jeans and let her palms drag over her thighs. Baring her teeth in an agonised look of panic, Kara tipped her head back, tendons taut as she tensed.

 

            “Look at me,” Lena softly ordered.

 

            Eyelashes fluttering as she obeyed, surprised, Kara watched her undress, green eyes vulnerable and full of doubt, and it made it easier for Kara to relax, to get out of her mind. Climbing onto her lap, Lena kissed her then, hands raking through Kara’s greying curls, and they got too wrapped up in each other to even think of themselves. It was more tender than it had been in the past, more indulgent and drawn out, fraught with the building tension until Kara grew tired of Lena’s games. 

 

            It was raining heavily beyond the fogged glass of the closed window, the sky the deep grey of dusk and the city shut outside as they lay wrapped up in their own world. Warm skin and gentle kisses and the amber glow of the lamp Lena had lit made Kara not want to leave the comfort of the bed, not even once she’d exhausted herself so much that she couldn’t move, stretched out on top of the rumpled sheets, eyes heavy-lidded and damp curls sticking to her cheeks and temples.

 

            Lena lay beside her, watching her with awe in the soft part of her mouth, her wide eyes, and she couldn’t look away. She took in the high colour of Kara’s skin and the sprinkle of freckles, faded with the passing summer spent shut away inside The Daily Prophet’s office.

 

            “I shouldn’t like this so much,” Lena said with a breathless laugh, pressing the back of her fingers to Kara’s pink cheeks.

 

            It made Kara flush a shade darker and Lena took the opportunity to map the pale lines of her scars with her fingertip. After a moment, Kara rolled onto her back and blinked up at the ceiling, swallowing thickly, audibly. Her chest rose and fell as her breaths turned shallow and Lena watched as her eyes suddenly filled with tears and Kara clapped a hand over her face.

 

            Scrambling up, Lena looked down at her with alarm, her lips parting, a small sound escaping her. “Are you okay?”

 

            “Yes,” Kara earnestly replied, her voice cracking. She wiped the pad of her thumb over her eyes and drew in a shaky breath. “Sorry, it’s been a teary day, I guess.”

 

            “What’s wrong?” Lena softly asked, her expression falling.

 

            “Nothing. Absolutely nothing.”

 

            “I- wha- has something upset you?”

 

            Choking on a laugh, Kara sat up and ran a hand through her curls. She squinted at Lena, a narrow-eyed look of suspicion as she tried to make out more than the smudge of her face with her poor vision. Blinking owlishly, Kara looked around for her glasses until Lena gently pressed them into her hand. Sliding them onto her face, slightly crooked as everything came into focus, Kara’s shoulders dropped and she smiled sheepishly. Sniffing, she cleared her throat and gestured matter-of-factly while the words escaped her for a moment.

 

            “I just- I went for food with Alex and Kelly earlier. Obviously, my sister wanted to know the whole story, what had really gone on - she clued into there being more to it last night - so I- I told them. Everything. Even the bits I’m ashamed of. And then I got to the end and I expected … I don’t know, anger? Accusations? Annoyance? Instead, she said … as long as I was happy it didn’t matter and Kelly said it was none of their business.”

 

            Cutting off, Kara looked down at the sheets and ran her fingers over the soft linen as she brooded. “I don’t know why, I burst into tears. I think … since we were kids, I’ve carried the stress of people finding out. What they would think … about me, about us. Even when Alex found out, she didn’t- didn’t know. Although, apparently she did. But I just- it upset me to think about what we put ourselves through for something that doesn’t matter. It felt like such a big deal before and my sister didn’t bat an eye. And now I just- I can’t help but think about how much easier it could’ve been.”

 

            Reaching out, Lena brushed Kara’s hair off her shoulder and briefly cupped her chin. Head cocked to the side, she raised her eyebrows slightly, concern still clouding her face. “And now?”

 

            “Now?” Kara echoed, her voice rasping. She let out a quick laugh, blue eyes softening as she looked at Lena. “I’d just forgotten what it feels like.”

 

            “Has it been that bad with everyone else?” Lena cockily asked, a smug look on her face.

 

            Exasperatedly sighing, Kara’s expression softened ever so slightly. “Not the sex; to love you up close.”

 

            Stilling at her words, Lena looked down, dark hair curtaining her face. She swallowed, a muscle twitching in her jaw, and Kara was quiet as she waited for a response “Yes, I’d forgotten that too,” Lena admitted.

 

            “Come here,” Kara whispered, holding her hands out for Lena to nestle her face in her palms. 

 

            Eyelids shuttering, Lena smiled as she inhaled deeply and exhaled softly. “I didn’t say it,” Kara murmured.

 

            “You did in your own way. It’ll never be easy for people like us.”

 

            “It is easy. It’s always been easy with you, even when it was impossibly difficult . It’s half of the reason I’ve always tried so hard to keep my feelings to myself.”

 

            “What was the other reason?”

 

            Kara hummed, her lips twitching at the corners. “The other reason was I never believed someone like you could ever love someone like me.”

 

            “If not you, who else?” Lena wryly smiled.

 

            “Maybe someone who could love you back nicely.”

 

            “I tried that; he was boring.”

 

            Kara’s laugh was loud, filling the room, and then she leaned in and kissed Lena. “I’ll try not to bore you too much.”

 

            “Considering we’re always on the verge of shagging or fighting, I’m sure you’ll keep me on my toes. How thrilling.”

 

            Groaning, she touched her forehead to Lena’s and then kissed the underside of her jaw. Sobering up, realising she still hadn’t gotten the words out, the words she’d last confessed heartbroken a few years back, Kara softly sighed against the side of Lena’s neck. “I really do love you, you know.”

 

            “I know.”

Chapter 30

            “Your mother’s looking for you.”

 

            Lena’s head jerked up from her patient file at the nurse’s station as she looked at Sam, taking in the grim look as she’d kept her voice low. Setting her quill down, Lena swallowed thickly, a crease forming between her eyebrows. She was already changed out of her scrubs, dressed to go home after a long shift, tired down to her bones as she thought longingly of her bed.

 

            Sighing, she ran a hand over her face. “Of course she’d pick now, right when I’m about to clock out.”

 

            “Here, let me finish your chart,” Sam offered, dragging it towards her and plucking her own quill from the pocket of her white coat. “What treatment did you use?”

 

            “Just finishing off rounds. Patient is stable but the hiccups won’t let up; I gave him a unit of a Sleeping Draught to help him rest. My intern’s been told to check on him in an hour and page me.”

 

            “Alright, you head off.”

 

            Squeezing her friend’s arm, Lena felt a rush of gratitude flood her. “Thank you.”

 

            “You can buy the coffee tomorrow.”

 

            “You’ll still be here?”

 

            “We’re always here, love.”

 

            “Have a good day.”

 

            She rushed off, bypassing patients being wheeled on gurneys or wheelchairs, Healers all but running down the hallways, vials of potions clutched to their chests, harried Interns carrying bags of drawn blood samples and confused visitors trying to puzzle out the layout of the wards. Following the familiar route to her mother’s office, which she tried her hardest to stay out of, Lena paused outside, smoothing down her hair and her robes before knocking.

 

            “Come in.”

 

            Opening the door, she warily stepped over the threshold and eased the door shut. Standing in front of Lillian’s desk, she clutched the straps of her satchel in a tight grip and briefly met her mother’s eyes before Lillian slowly penned something on the page before her.

 

            “You wanted to see me?” Lena murmured.

 

            “Speak up and look at me when you’re talking,” Lillian curtly responded, setting her quill in the ink pot with a quiet clatter.

 

            A muscle twitching in her jaw, Lena gave her mother a level stare, her voice frosty as she repeated herself. Lillian’s lips twitched with amusement, the satisfaction of her ongoing control evident on her face. She let out a quiet huff of laughter.

 

            “You’ll join me for dinner tonight.”

 

            It wasn’t a question but a demand and Lena took a moment to formulate a response. “I already have dinner plans tonight.”

 

            “Then you’ll stop by beforehand. There’s something I’d like to discuss.”

 

            “Can’t we discuss it now?”

 

            “If I wanted to discuss it now, I wouldn’t have suggested dinner.”

 

            Feeling prickling resentment well up, Lena swallowed a rough sigh. Her gaze was steely though and her mouth tightened at the corners.

 

            “Fine. I’ll be there at half past four.”

 

            Lillian made a show of glancing at her watch before giving her daughter a dismissive look. “Go on then. Don’t be late.”

 

            “Yes, ma’am.”

 

            Turning on her heel, Lena pulled the door open with a little more force than necessary and resisted the urge to slam it behind her. Two Healers hurried past and she made an effort to wipe her face blank of any emotion, continuing on to the waiting room and stepping onto the street. Lena needed to stop by Diagon Alley before heading home and realised she could use the walk, cold air scouring her lungs as she rounded puddles and squeezed past Muggles, drawing a few looks in her billowing cloak, until she reached the pub front of The Leaky Cauldron.

            

            The air was humid inside, a roaring fire filling the pub with the sweet smell of apple wood, and Lena nodded at Tom as she bypassed occupied tables for the back alley. She was quick at the market, selecting a bouquet of flowers and then returning to the pub to buy a bottle of wine. 

 

            Afterwards, she Apparated home and set the flowers in water before collapsing into bed with the aid of a Sleeping Draught. An alarm was set for three and she didn’t stir until then, her eyes gritty as she was dragged from sleep, desperate for more. A potion to perk her up did the trick and she quickly showered, rinsing the smell of St. Mungo’s from her hair and skin before she went through the careful process of dressing.

 

            It was casual, a family Sunday roast, so Lena opted for a knitted black long-sleeved top with a jacquard patterned skirt in white and maroon, tights covering her legs and small heeled boots on her feet. Her dark hair hung sleek and straight and she did her makeup as she did for work, keeping it neutral as she tried to present herself as somewhat softer than usual, with no dark lipstick or sharp eyeliner.

 

            Fetching a robe to go over the top, she safely stowed her gifts in an extended handbag and spent a few more minutes fussing over her appearance, fiddling with her rings and the slender bracelet Kara had bought her years ago, over whether she’d applied too much perfume and whether she should have chosen pants instead of a pencil skirt. She delayed leaving for her mother’s for as long as possible until she was verging on being dead on time - not late.

 

            With a resigned sigh, Lena grabbed a fistful of Floo powder and stepped into the grate, watching others spin past in disorienting succession. She came to an abrupt halt, the smell of old wood, damp stone and something sweet, like old leather-bound books or decaying flowers, slamming into her with gut-wrenching familiarity. It was the smell of her childhood, dragging Lena back down into memories she would rather have forgotten.

 

            Stepping out of the large fireplace, she found Lillian already seated on the sofa, a tray of tea laid on the coffee table, steam curling from the spout of the pot. Wariness crept over her, shoulders tense as she clutched her bag in hand, eyes darting around the familiar room as the blood drained from her face.

 

            “You’re late.”

 

            Glancing down at her watch, Lena was a minute early. “No, I’m on time.”

 

            “Sit. Have some tea.”

 

            Lillian was watching her intently and Lena chafed uncomfortably at the attention, her cordial tone only meaning that worse was to come. Her mother had almost been preferable in a bad mood because at least Lena had known to stay out of her way. These contrary moods were more dangerous, never revealing what was going to happen next. 

 

            Taking a seat on the armchair on the other side of the coffee table, setting the tray of tea between them, Lena put her bag down on the floor. Reaching out, she raised the pot and poured for herself and then refilled her mother’s cup before adding a dash of milk to each.

 

            “I can’t stay long.”

 

            “Then I’ll be brief. It’s been brought to my attention that you’re no longer engaged to that Spheer boy.”

 

            Freezing, unease creeping up Lena’s spine, she cleared her throat, setting her tea and saucer down. Running her palms over her thighs, she sat back, ramrod straight and stiff.

 

            “No, not for a few months now.”

 

            “Why?”

 

            “That’s personal,” Lena coolly replied. “I don’t remember you showing much interest in my dating life before. You never even met the man; I’m surprised you even knew we were engaged.”

 

            With a lazy shrug, Lillian sipped her scalding tea. Her eyes were dangerously piercing though and Lena knew she was on the wrong foot there somehow.

 

            “He’s a Pureblood Slytherin from a wealthy family. There wasn’t much need for me to intercede, and we both know you’ve made your opinion of me clear and I find you as equally intolerable. Why bother with the farce?”

 

            Lena’s lips twitched with amusement at her mother’s blunt honesty. At least she could always rely on that, never letting herself be deluded into thinking Lillian cared about her. Sure, she might love her, the same way Lena loved her in return, but it was a hard kind of love, lacking any warmth. There was something unbreakable between them that had been forged by the cruelty inflicted on Lena as a child and she hated that she could never quite escape. 

 

            “I would like to know why, ” Lillian pressed.

 

            “I-” Lena faltered before inhaling sharply. “I didn’t love him.”

 

            Scoffing, Lillian shook her head. “You’ve always been so wrapped up in this notion of love. As if that matters. You aren’t built for that; I made you better than that.” 

 

            “I’m exactly what you made me so maybe you should’ve tried harder if that was the desired outcome,” Lena bitterly replied, her lips twitching derisively.

 

            “You think you love that girl?”

 

            Stiffening at the mention of Kara, Lena’s mask dropped for a moment, a grey look of surprise making her face go slack as nausea bloomed in her stomach. She could feel her heart in her throat and it was an effort to swallow down the lump, a cold sweat prickling her skin as she tried to regain her composure.

 

            Smug and contemptuous, Lillian arched an eyebrow in a lazy manner. “Did you think I didn’t know?”

 

            “Clearly you’ve just found out,” Lena gently snorted. “Or we would’ve had this conversation a lot sooner.”

 

            “Or perhaps I gave you the benefit of the doubt because I didn’t think the daughter that I raised would be stupid enough to parade around Diagon Alley with a werewolf.”

 

            Her mother’s voice rose as she spoke, her lazy demeanour turning taut as anger and steel crept into her face and tone. Lena blinked, her mouth opening and closing as she tried to figure out how she knew. How could her mother have figured out so much?

 

            Reaching for a manila file beside her, Lillian slapped it down on the coffee table, a few slips of paper escaping. Kara’s name was written on the tab and Lena’s stomach dropped. Swallowing, Lena fixed Lillian with a level stare.

 

            “What would you like me to say? That you’re wrong? You’re not.”

 

            “You’re a disgrace . Everything I have done to get you where you are today and you throw it back in my face. That’s the thanks I get for my hard work?”

 

            “Your hard work?” Lena snapped. “It wasn’t you who spent hours every day, studying and practising, losing sleep over it all. I learnt every spell, every potion, every herb and creature to please you and none of it was good enough. All you did was try to break me over silly mistakes for your own revenge because my father stepped out and you got stuck with the daughter you never wanted. Don’t tell me how hard you worked for my career.”

 

            “Blood will always out; I suppose that’s true enough. Running around with half-breeds for company, what would your father say about you? You demean the Luthor name.”

 

            “Who cares what he would say? He’s dead . He’s dead and he’s the one who went around with a Muggleborn witch behind your back. How embarrassing it must have been for you, a Pureblood and you still weren’t good enough. And then to end up with a Half-Blood daughter. How ironic . I never stood a chance. You hated me from the moment he brought me home but I will not let you dictate my life anymore. I will not let you make me feel ashamed for who I love.”

 

            Her mother swiped the tea tray from the table, her face stony with anger. Crockery and metal tinkled into a heap, the smell of bergamot and a rich earthy note filling the air as spilt tea seeped into the rug. Lena shot to her feet, bristling with anger, her face pale and hard as she clenched her hands into fists. 

 

            “We’re done here.”

 

            Lillian rose too, intimidatingly tall and making Lena feel so small, so young. She thought they’d outgrown this, that she was too old to regress back into that little girl who’d never been able to fight back. In her foolish belief that she was an adult now and that made them equals, she underestimated her mother. She slapped Lena so hard that her vision went black for a split second. 

 

            Blinking, unable to even make a sound, Lena’s mouth parted and the air was forced from her lungs. Stepping in closer, Lillian grasped her chin tightly in her fingers, nails leaving deep gouges in her skin, and forced Lena to look up at her. Stunned, Lena wasn’t afraid, only angry. No one had dared lay a hand on her in years.

 

            They stared at each other for a weighted moment before Lillian scoffed contemptuously and shoved Lena away, releasing her face. Stumbling backwards, more from the shock than the force, Lena’s throat felt tight. Her face registered no pain, only an intense sting, but she was sure an angry red welt was already forming on her cheek and she could feel the hot thickness in her lip from her mother’s ring.

 

            Whipping out her wand, Lena had it pointed at her mother’s chest, an arrogant tilt to her chin as she stared up at her. There was the faintest tremor of doubt in her hand as she swallowed thickly. Licking her lips, she tasted blood, shifting unsteadily.

 

            “Don’t you touch me again,” Lena hoarsely warned her.

 

            Sneering, Lillian huffed with laughter. “Or what? You’ll hex me? Foolish girl, I could have the skin flayed from your body before you could so much as utter a word. You couldn’t stomach it anyway. You’ve always been pathetically soft.”

 

            “You see that as a weakness, but it’s a strength to have suffered as much as I have without perpetuating it. I won’t let you make me cruel; I refuse to be like you.”

 

            “There are worse monsters than me in the world. You should know; you’ve seen her on the Bite Ward. Yes, I put the pieces together you silly girl. You’re not as clever as you think.”

 

            Cheek an angry red, further reddened by the anger that threatened to overwhelm her, Lena’s knuckles turned white around her wand. “She’s not a monster, not even on the full moon. You’re worse than she’ll ever be and she has more reason too. ”

 

            “Why must you fail me so often?” Lillian seethed.

 

            Raising her chin, mustering all the courage she had, Lena’s voice was gravelly and shaking as she replied. “I have never been a failure. Not to you or anyone else. You were wrong.”

 

            Lillian laughed, cold and sharp. “Look at you. Twenty-five years and you’ve finally grown a spine. How sweet.”

 

            “Fuck you.”

 

            “Watch your tone,” Lillian harshly replied, her amusement vanishing as her face hardened. “I will not have you speak to me like that in my own home.”

 

            Fingertips tugging down the cuff of her left sleeve as her right hand kept her wand trained on her mother, a little shaky as her stomach knotted itself, Lena let out a hitching breath. “I was leaving anyway.”

 

            She stooped for her bag and all but ran out of the room, her steps long as she crossed the foyer, shoulders hunched as she expected a curse to strike her in the back. Slamming the front door behind her, Lena crunched gravel beneath her shoes as she stalked down the driveway, her breaths coming quick and sharp. Glancing down at her watch, she saw that she was already late, no time to go home, no time to fix her appearance. 

 

            “Fuck, fuck, fuck,” she hissed, pacing as she passed the boundary of the estate, not wanting to show up as she was but not wanting to keep Kara waiting. 

 

            Kara, who was good and kind and warm. Kara, who was so gentle, except for her hands, which were rough from working in her mother’s garden. She wore cosy clothes from secondhand shops and loved Quidditch, never raised her voice unless Lena had goaded her too far, who would never lay a finger on her.

 

            Beyond the gate, she Apparated to Kara’s street and came out on the doorstep. Drawing in a deep breath to steady herself, she raised a hand to knock. Listening to the voices through the wooden door, Lena could feel herself unravelling and desperately tried to rein herself back in as her heart pounded with residual adrenaline. She’d never stood up to Lillian like that and she doubted she’d be allowed to repeat it again unscathed.

 

            The door opened a moment later and Lena blinked at the warm light spilling out, the smell of roast lamb and rosemary and garlic wafting outside. It was a grey day and Lena felt as dismal as the weather as she huddled on the doorstep, trying to stop her hands from shaking as she took in Kara’s delighted smile and felt her chest cave a little.

 

            “Hi,” Kara brightly greeted her, her momentum propelling her forward to kiss Lena’s cheek.

 

            Flinching back, Lena turned her head aside. Guilt immediately knifed through her and she saw the smile die on Kara’s lips, doubt sown in her blue eyes and quickly hardening to anger as she took in Lena’s face. Lena hadn’t flinched in years .

 

            “What-“

 

            “Sorry, can I use your bathroom?” Lena hoarsely asked. “I didn’t have time to go home before coming.”

 

            “I- of course. It’s upstairs.”

 

            Nodding, Lena pushed past her and hurried upstairs. Kara hauled herself up two steps at a time, shouting they’d be down soon. Finding the bathroom by herself - it was a tiny cottage - Lena didn’t manage to get the door shut behind her before Kara grabbed the edge and pushed it open. Tugging on the light cord, Kara shut the door and faced Lena.

 

            “Let me see,” she murmured, reaching out to tenderly cradle Lena’s jaw.

 

            “It’s fine,” Lena muttered, jerking herself free, embarrassment welling up. 

 

            “Did your-“

 

            “My mum, yes.”

 

            A short laugh escaped her as she looked at her pallid reflection in the mirror, her cheek still an angry red. Half-moons gouged her cheeks where Lillian had grabbed her and her lip split from her mother’s ring. 

 

            Working a quick Episkey spell, Lena licked her healed lips, tasting the faint tang of blood, and then turned her attention to the cheek. Muttering beneath her breath, Lena leached the redness and the deep crescents from her skin. In a minute, she’d undone the damage but she could still feel the ghost of the slap.

 

            “Lena,” Kara whispered, barely contained anger making her voice tremble on the two syllables.

 

            “This is nothing. You think a slap hurts when she’s responsible for- for everything else? Leave it.”

 

            “I’ll-“

 

            “What?” Lena rounded on her, tense and irate, her voice not unkind but short. “What will you do?”

 

            Tears filled Kara’s eyes and she swallowed thickly. “I’ll never lay a hand on you like that.”

 

            Expression softening, Lena reached up to brush away a few tears. “You don’t need to tell me that; I already know. It’s alright. It’ll be alright. It’s just a slap.”

 

            Letting out a choked sob, Kara’s face crumpled with agony. “Don’t say that.”

 

            “Shh, come on, we need to go downstairs. Don’t cry. I’m alright, I promise.”

 

            Blowing the air out of her cheeks as she tried to compose herself, Kara blinked rapidly. Softly cursing, Lena rummaged around in her handbag and came up with a little bottle of eyedrops she used for work when she’d been awake for thirty hours and her eyes were bloodshot and dry. 

 

            “Here,” she whispered, slipping Kara’s glasses off her face. “Tip your head back.”

 

            Kara’s breaths hitched quietly as she let Lena put the eyedrops in, rubbing at her cheeks before she put her glasses back on. Her nose was a little pink and Lena’s expression softened as she reached out to cup her chin. Giving her a quick kiss, she smiled.

 

            “Hi.”

 

            Mouth turning down at the corners, Kara was doe-eyed and solemn. Sighing, Lena reached into her bag and brought out the bouquet of singing daffodils, which trumpeted in chorus, and Kara let out a surprised laugh.

 

            “Much better,” Lena murmured, satisfied.

 

            “Thank you.”

 

            “Let’s go down,” she insisted.

 

            Holding her hand, Kara fiddled with Lena’s fingers, chewing on her words as she struggled to speak. “Are you alright?”

 

            Sighing heavily, Lena gave her a weak smile, the corners of her eyes tight, and she kissed Kara’s knuckles. “Better now that I’m with you. Come on.”

 

            Kara hesitated and then dropped Lena’s hand, opening the bathroom door. She kept a tight fist around the stems of her bouquet and plodded downstairs with a resigned slump to her shoulders. Lena followed after her and Kara paused in the narrow hallway to take her cloak and her handbag once Lena had fetched her bottle of wine.

 

            Stepping into the kitchen, Kara cleared her throat, “Lena’s here.”

 

            Eliza turned from the stove, a smile lighting her face as she moved towards Lena. “Hi, sweetheart.”

 

            Unprepared for the welcoming hug, Lena managed to not flinch, somewhat enduring it as she felt shy and uncertain. She’d never been very loud or sociable, something she’d always had in common with Kara, but now she was very much aware that she was the outsider here in the space where Kara was at ease.

 

            Kelly also gave Lena a hug and then she nodded at Alex, who leaned against the kitchen counters, her brown eyes appraising but not unfriendly. Lena handed off the bottle of wine, her hands still shaking a little as fresh adrenaline washed through her, and she watched as Kara fetched a vase for the daffodils.

 

            “Sit, sit,” Eliza urged her, a hand on Lena’s shoulder as she startled slightly and then flushed, the tension bleeding out of her as Eliza gently squeezed reassuringly.

 

            Sitting heavily on a chair, Lena fidgeted with her hands in her lap, chewing on the inside of her lip as she still felt the dull ache of it splitting, her fingers worrying over her hidden scar. As Kara rounded the table, her fingers glided across Lena’s back, leaching some more of the tension out of her.

 

            “Drink?”

 

            “I’ll have the same as you,” Lena murmured, looking up and giving her a small smile.

 

            Nodding, Kara fetched drinks for everyone, setting a glass of Tongue-Tying Lemon Squash in front of Lena and dragging out the chair beside her. She took a sip and squeezed Lena’s knee beneath the table, a tense set to her jaw. 

 

            Kelly and Eliza peppered her with questions about work, with a few posed by Alex, who made them sound like interrogations. It made Lena feel like she was back in the dining room at her family home, a bunch of Aurors standing around asking her questions about her brother as she tried her best to cooperate without implicating herself. Feeling particularly vulnerable at that moment, Lena’s answers were short and a little curt.

 

            “Why’d you want to be a Healer anyway?” Alex asked, arms folded over her chest.

 

            Lena snorted, giving her a thin grin. “I, ah, have the insatiable desire to help people.”

 

            Humming dubiously, as if she didn’t believe that reason, Alex picked up her drink and took a sip. Eliza slipped outside to fetch some more fresh herbs as she finished off the vegetables in the oven.

 

            “It must pay well at least. Not that you’d need to worry about that. Families like yours always seem to have vaults full of money at Gringotts.”

 

            “Oh, come on, Alex,” Kara sighed. 

 

            “Yes,” Lena lightly agreed, her lips curving wryly. “But don’t worry, my trust isn’t nearly as big as my inheritance will be. Lucky me to be the sole heir.”

 

            Scoffing, Alex laughed. “Oh, is that the reason why you turned your brother in? Takes a lot of guts,” she said with grudging respect.

 

            “What are you talking about?” Kara said, her face crumpling with confusion.

 

            Lena went still, her hand slowing as she set her own cup down, eyes cutting across to Alex. A flicker of annoyance welled up inside before she stamped it back down, clearing her throat as she shifted uncomfortably. 

 

            “Sorry, I thought-” Alex started, a sheepish look of panic on her face as she realised she’d put her foot in it.

 

            “It’s fine,” Lena cut her off, a flush creeping up her neck. “I don’t talk about it, for obvious reasons.”

 

            “I’m sorry,” Kara slowly said, turning to look at Lena. “What?”

 

            Clearing her throat, Lena reached for her glass, shifting restlessly. “I turned my brother in. I’m the reason he’s in Azkaban.”

 

            Gaping at her, Kara’s eyes were wide with shock as she stammered, unable to find the words to clarify what Lena confessed. No one knew, no one outside of Dumbledore and the few Aurors who’d seen the letter that Lena had written to him, passed on by her old Headmaster. Lena knew that no one else knew because she was still breathing, and if her mother had found out, she knew Lillian would have made her wish for the days a little light torture had been her punishment. 

 

            “You’re right,” Lena murmured with a thin smile, slightly bitter and mocking. “It was for the sole inheritance. Why else would a Slytherin do something good?”

 

            Eliza walked back in and they fell silent, her eyes glancing around the four of them and noting the tension. Kara looked peeved and Lena gave her knee a quick squeeze before taking a sip of her squash, tart lemon hard to swallow.

 

            “Alex, Kara tells me you’re a big Quidditch fan too,” Lena smoothly continued. 

 

            “Used to be for the Fitchburg Finches, now it’s the Falmouth Falcons. And you?”

            “Lena’s more academically inclined,” Kara said with a hoarse laugh. 

 

            “Kelly? Please tell me I have one ally here.”

 

            Wrinkling her nose as she sheepishly smiled, Kelly shrugged. “Caerphilly Catapults season membership holder, I’m afraid.”

 

            Groaning, Lena shook her head. The ensuing conversation about manoeuvres with names Lena couldn’t begin to comprehend the meaning of - Dionysus Dives and Porskoff Ploys - or a player Haversacking at a game they’d all gone to recently all went over Lena’s head but she was content to sit and listen. After a few minutes, she quietly asked Eliza if she’d like a hand and was waved away and continued to listen with polite interest to the conversation. 

 

            Dinner was ready a short while later and Lena helped Kara set the table with the cutlery while Alex opened the bottle of wine Lena had brought and Kelly quickly polished a few glasses. Lena was quiet throughout dinner, eating small bites as she felt out of sorts by the casual ease of a family eating dinner together as they talked about their days and work or a conversation they’d had with one of their other friends. Her own family dinners on the summer holidays had always been silent affairs, preceded by the horrible torment of increasingly difficult questions and the bite of a quill. It felt uncomfortable to be surrounded by so much open love and she muddled through dinner with a stone in her stomach as she thought about a life that had never existed for her but could have been under different circumstances.

 

            After they’d finished eating, Lena helped stack plates while Kara filled the sink with soapy water, rolling her sleeves up to her elbows with an ease that was usually absent as she bared her scars to the four women in the kitchen. Draining her glass of wine, Alex set it down on the counter and cleared her throat. 

 

            “Why don’t I show Lena the garden?” Alex suggested.

 

            She was already opening the back door, giving Lena a pointed look. Hesitating a moment, Lena climbed to her feet, nodding as she moved towards the door. It was cold outside and she hugged her arms to herself, taking in the overflowing garden in the waning light of an early dusk.

 

            “Sorry, had to use you for cover. Mum doesn’t know I smoke,” Alex murmured, knocking a cigarette out of a packet and offering it to Lena. “Want one?”

 

            Holding a hand up in rejection, Lena let out a huff of laughter. “No thanks.”

 

            “Um, sorry about that. Earlier, I mean. I didn’t know that she didn’t know.”

 

            Waving a hand dismissively, Lena smiled thinly. “It’s fine, it doesn’t matter. I would’ve told her if it had come up.”

 

            Nodding, Alex tipped her head back and blew a pink smoke ring before a cloud followed. She paced slowly, the damp grass muffling her footsteps and Lena shifted restlessly, uneasy around the Auror.

 

            “I don’t hate you, you know.”

            

            “It wouldn’t matter to me if you did,” Lena earnestly replied. “But it matters to Kara.”

 

            “Mm. Even if it didn’t, I guess it helps to keep the peace. And I don’t think you’re all bad, anyway. I meant it, it takes a lot of guts to turn in family.”

 

            Rubbing her lip, Lena laughed. “Not as much as you would think when you don’t get on.”

 

            “Right. I’ve seen your mum at the hospital; she seems … terrifying.”

 

            “An understatement.”

 

            Alex laughed and sucked down another lungful of smoke before letting it out as she slowly exhaled. Looking around the garden, catching a glimpse of a pair of cat eyes glowing in the dark and hearing the patter of garden gnomes running through the bushes, Lena found it charming and peaceful. It was a stark contrast to the neat, austere gardens of her childhood home, with its topiaries and clipped hedgerows.

 

            “Lena?”

            

            She turned to Alex, eyebrows rising. “Yes?”

 

            “Why her?”

 

            Blinking, Lena looked taken aback by the question. A lopsided smile crossed her face as a furrow formed between her eyebrows.

 

            “You’re beautiful, there’s no denying it,” Alex reluctantly told her, snorting. “Rich, from an old family and apparently the most intelligent witch to ever grace Hogwarts. I’ve read your file.”

 

            It was news to Lena that she even had a file but she supposed you couldn’t be related to a Pureblood Slytherin family during a blood war and not be suspect. There would have been nothing for them to dig up on her anyway, save for a few detentions and perfect marks. 

 

            “I think she’s beautiful too.”

 

            “Of course she is, I’m just saying … people like you don’t look beneath the scars to see that. And they certainly wouldn’t stick around after finding out.”

 

            There was a truth to Alex’s words and it wasn’t meant maliciously. It didn’t matter whether Kara had been as rich as Lena, as intelligent as her or from a family like hers; as soon as she’d been bitten, it all ceased to matter.

 

            Hesitating, Lena wasn’t quite sure what to say. “I suppose …she was just the first person to show me something I’d never experienced before.”

 

            “What’s that?”

 

            “A little kindness.”

 

            Looking perturbed by Lena’s answer, Alex made a low sound at the back of her throat and pinched the end of her cigarette, carefully stowing the butt in the pocket of her jeans.

 

            “Well, from what she told me, she was also a bit of an arse.”

 

            “She was,” Lena laughed. “I’ve seen all of the ugly parts of her; she’s proud, she blamed me for a lot of shit I didn’t do, she can be arrogant, selfish and insecure. So can I. But is it really so hard to believe that she’s the only person who’s ever made me feel happy?”

 

            “No, it’s not hard to believe at all. I just … I didn’t expect you. Now, I don’t know you well at all , but I misjudged you a bit. A lot. I don’t know, I probably would’ve thought she’d lost the plot if she brought you home a couple of years ago, but … now I think I’m glad.”

 

            Suspicion clouded Lena’s face. “Really?”

 

            “I love my sister. I’m sure she’s told you all about how we didn’t get on-”

 

            “You were the topic of many conversations in the early days of our friendship.”

 

            Alex let out a huff of laughter, burying her hands in her pockets. “Well, there you have it. You probably loved her before I even did. I guess I just wanted to say thanks for looking out for her. From what I know, it’s been rocky and maybe she didn’t deserve you being the bigger person or so many chances, but thanks.”

 

            “I do love her,” Lena hoarsely confessed.

 

            Sighing as her face softened, a faint crease of worry on her face, Alex nodded, her mouth thinning slightly. “I know. I could kiss you for that.”

 

            “Warming up to me already?” Lena murmured, arching an eyebrow.

 

            “Well … I’ll give you the benefit of the doubt, anyway.”

 

            Nodding, Lena’s lips twitched slightly. “I guess I’ll try not to hold you being a Gryffindor against you too much as well.”

 

            Snorting, Alex shook her head before exhaling and gesturing to the back door. “We’d better get back in. It’s not a big garden.”

 

            “I don’t think anyone thinks we’re looking at the garden.”

 

            “Probably not. I’m surprised Kara’s not pressed up against the window, making sure we’re not duelling. Maybe we should tease her a bit.”

 

            Cracking a smile, Lena hugged her arms to herself. “Next time. She already looks stressed enough to pass out.”

 

            They slowly started making their way back to the door, the light faltering now as dark clouds crept in off the coast, a faint tang of salt on the wind. It was bracing and different to the damp green of the Irish countryside she’d grown up in. She wondered what it would be like to be so near the sea, the thought of so much water making her skin prickle with unease. 

 

            “Hey,” Alex stopped her, breaking Lena out of her thoughts with an odd smile on her face. “Thanks for doing all of my homework, by the way.”

 

            A surprised laugh escaped Lena and she gave her a genuine smile. “You’re welcome.”

 

            They stepped back into the warmth of the kitchen to find the washing up done, the kitchen tidy and Kara leaning against the counters with an agitated set to her gangly frame. She perked up at the sight of the two of them and smiled.

 

            “I made tea,” she announced, quickly picking up two mugs.

 

            Handing one off to Lena and the other to Alex, Kara scooped up her own and held it between her rough palms. Her expression was soft, eyebrows slightly raised, the corners of her mouth curving up, blue eyes questioning as if she expected them to clue her in on their conversation outside.

 

            “Keep your nose out, Kara,” Alex said, giving her cheek a fond pat before following the sound of voices to the living room.

 

            Rolling her eyes, Kara quietly scoffed and rubbed the back of her neck as Lena leaned against the edge of the table, a few inches between their knees as they faced each other. She took a sip of tea, the warm comfort of it sliding down her throat as she felt some of the roiling tension gone after a distracting evening. Her encounter with Lillian had dulled somewhat, blurring into something inconsequential that couldn’t touch her in the warm kitchen of Kara’s home. 

 

            “Are you alright?” Kara haltingly asked. “If you don’t want to stay any longer, that’s okay. They all know you didn’t get off work until this morning so I can just say you’re tired. You probably are tired.”

 

            “That’s pretty much a guarantee these days,” Lena said with a thin smile. “But I’d like to stay a bit longer if that’s okay.”

 

            “Of course it is,” Kara murmured, reaching out to tuck a strand of dark hair behind Lena’s ear. “Stay as long as you’d like.”

 

            She ended up staying another hour, sitting by the fire, another cup of tea in hand as she sank into the sofa, worn soft from years of use, Kara’s knee pressed against hers. Kara was anxiously making her way through a tin of homemade biscuits, dunking them in her tea and frequently offering them around. It was close to the next full moon and she looked peaky, her cheeks pale and a hollowed-out look to her eyes.

 

            The sky was pitch black outside and her shoulders were slumped, eyes prickling with exhaustion when Eliza took her empty cup from her and laughed. “You look tired, sweetheart.”

 

            “Mm. Sorry, it was a long shift.”

 

            Hiding a yawn as her eyes squeezed shut, Lena blinked rapidly and smiled sheepishly as she brushed her hair out of her face. “You should go home and sleep,” Kara murmured.

 

            “Probably.”

 

            “Come on, I’ll walk you out.”

 

            They climbed to their feet together and Lena said goodbye to Alex and Kelly and then slipped out of the living room to say goodbye to Eliza, thanking her for dinner and feeling only a little bit out of sorts with the hug she was wrapped in. Her throat felt tight and her smile wavered as she nodded slightly at Eliza’s insistence that she come again.

 

            Walking her to the front door, Kara hovered as Lena pulled on her cloak and picked up her handbag, calling another hesitant goodbye before opening the door and stepping out into the cool evening. Fidgeting with her fingers, Kara gave Lena a concerned look as she followed her outside, easing the door shut a fraction.

 

            “Will you be okay by yourself? I mean … if you didn’t want to be alone after … everything, I can come over.”

 

            Lena gave her hand a quick squeeze. “Thanks but I’ll be fine. You should sleep too; full moon’s in two nights.”

            

            Looking up, they tried to spot the moon through the cloud cover, ominously evasive as Kara rolled her shoulders restlessly. Their eyes met again and Lena gave her a crooked smile, leaning in to kiss her quickly.

 

            “Thank you.”

 

            “I hope Alex wasn’t too awful.”

 

            “She was nice. They all are. You’re very lucky.”

 

            “I know,” Kara murmured, her voice serious and tender. “You’ll fit right in.”

 

            “Kara, I- you know that I love you.”

 

            Lena spoke quickly, almost tripping over her words, and Kara let out a bewildered laugh of surprise. “Yes.”

 

            “Do you know why?”

 

            “Not really. I’m still trying to figure it out.”

 

            Lips twitching slightly, her cheek shallowly dimpling, Lena swallowed and briefly cupped Kara’s chin. “Remind me to tell you in detail at some point.”

Chapter 31

            The first full moon since they’d started seeing each other came around and Lena wasn’t rostered on to work so an hour before the full moon, she found herself behind the curtain of Kara’s bed as her girlfriend subjected herself to the brief examination and drawing her blood. Lena was there as a visitor of course, abiding by her mother’s edict but finding a loophole, and she watched and listened in silence.

 

            When it was time for Kara to go downstairs, Lena went with her, rising to her feet, defiantly meeting the pointed look of the Healer assigned to Kara, and taking her girlfriend’s hand. She squeezed tightly, running her thumb over the small scars nicking the backs of Kara’s fingers as she went with her.

 

            “It’s okay, you don’t-” Kara started to whisper, leaning in close.

 

            The hairs on her arms were on end from the cold and Lena felt a lump in her throat as she gave Kara a wan smile. “I want to.”

 

            Nodding as she resolved not to push Lena on the matter, Kara continued after the Healer, in the stream of other werewolves making their way downstairs. None of them looked alike, yet they all bore the same greying hair - in varying stages of total grey - all had scars, all had the peaky look of a person about to vomit as the full moon crept up on them.
