Lena felt so much pity well up inside her that it hurt to breathe.

 

            She accompanied Kara right down to that dank hallway of cells, to the very door of the one she was set to be locked inside. Stroking her hair and cupping the back of her head, Lena kissed her firmly and then stepped away at the clearing of the throat of the Healer waiting with Kara’s dose of the latest Wolfsbane Potion they were testing out. Lena’s stare was unwavering as she watched Kara knock it back with a grimace of disgust, her eyelids shuttering, looking unlike herself without her glasses, barefoot in the thin robe, white as a ghost with the hollowed look of a sick person. 

 

            “I’ll be right here,” Lena softly told her.

 

            Kara nodded and then hesitated, a look of intense embarrassment leaving her staring at the floor. “Don’t look.”

 

            Lena wanted to tell her it didn’t matter what she saw, that she would love her all the same, that she had never stopped loving her through those long years apart - even when she’d hated her - not even on the months she’d pulled her out of pools of vomit and blood and put her back together with the tenderness only a person who loved her could have given. She knew what she’d see if she looked, had seen it before with other werewolves as an Intern, and she would have felt her heart split in half at the agony her girlfriend would have felt, her body breaking and reforming, but the love would have stayed. The love wouldn’t change no matter what they went through, that much Lena knew for a fact.

 

            Still, she respected Kara’s privacy enough to let her transform unobserved, as she always had, but she didn’t leave. Not once the heavy door was bolted and charmed for safe measure, not once the hoarse shouts of a dozen werewolves started, or when it turned into a hair-raising howl, keening up and down the length of the hallway from behind closed doors. She didn’t even look when they all fell silent, one by one, exchanging glances with the Healer left downstairs to supervise, the sudden fear that the Wolfsbane Potion had poisoned them all knifing through her with breathless panic.

 

            “Homenum Revelio,” Lena whispered, her thin voice wavering as her throat felt tight, resorting to spells to check if Kara was okay behind the closed door.

 

            There was no light from her wand but there was an odd swooping sensation that alerted her to the presence of the six werewolves locked in their cells. Including Kara. The breath was expelled from her in a sharp, slightly frayed whimper. Closing her eyes, Lena stumbled backwards until her shoulder blades hit the frigid stone wall and she sank down to her haunches. Wand held limply in her fingers, she raked a hand through her hair and settled in for the long night.

 

            Lena was accustomed to hours spent working her long shifts and then reporting back for on-call summons to help out in emergencies or if her patients took a funny turn, so it wasn’t a particularly arduous task for her to stay awake. It was cold though and her book wasn’t interesting enough to distract her from thoughts of Kara, who was eerily quiet, as were the rest of them. Under different circumstances, Lena’s curiosity would have gotten the better of her but some delicacy and dignity should be afforded to the werewolves on a full moon so she was left to wonder until the awful wolfish sounds started back up as the sun started to rise and they turned back into humans.

 

            Healers arrived shortly after that, stretchers floating along with Mediwizards on hand to ferry the patients back upstairs. Lena stiffly rose to her feet and blinked the gritty feeling in her eyes away as she watched them unlock Kara’s cell door, trying to catch a glimpse of her inside. She couldn’t see much past the bulk of the Healer kneeling at her side and it took everything in Lena not to interfere, not to rush in and take over, fiercely claiming Kara as her own patient. If pissing off her mother at the detriment of her own career hadn’t been a definite consequence, she would have.

 

            Watching as they got her on a stretcher and covered her with a blanket for modesty’s sake, Lena anxiously wrung her hands, her green eyes wide and doleful. She had been such a common sight on the Bite Ward for a while that it took Healer Smethwyck a while to realise she was there, although it had been years since she’d been banned. His brow furrowed as he turned from one of the other patients, moving on to Kara and giving her a cursory once over before instructing them to get her upstairs to the ward.

 

            “Luthor, you’re not allowed to be here,” Smethwyck warned her in a low voice, although his expression implied he wouldn’t report her to her mother.

 

            Still, Lena shrank back, allowing the Healers to whisk away the werewolves, more of them than ordinarily thanks to the trial, and then made her way upstairs at a slower pace. It would be a while before Kara woke up but Lena was eager to know the findings of the research, the extent of Kara’s injuries, which new scars she would kiss so softly as to impart some of her love into them so Kara would hate herself a little bit less. 

 

            Lingering outside the ward as she knew better than to get in the way of the mania of treating patients who were bleeding profusely from deep gashes, she waited impatiently, grey with worry and residual exhaustion from yesterday’s shift that she hadn’t slept enough to recover from. Rightfully, she should have gone into one of the on-call rooms and slept in the long hours between transformations but Lena’s loyalty was that to rival a Gryffindor’s and she knew she would have rather cut her own leg off than walk away from Kara at her most vulnerable. 

 

            Eventually, Smethwyck caught sight of her hovering in the hallways and grimaced before waving her inside. He made a shooing gesture towards Kara’s bed and Lena slipped behind the curtain, finding the Healer just finishing up with a look of consternation on his face.

 

            “How is she?” Lena meekly asked.

 

            “Fine.”

 

            “What injuries did she sustain?” Lena asked again, trying not to be too brusque in light of his unhelpful response.

 

            He gave her a funny look, a faint smile tugging at the corners of his mouth. “None. There aren’t any injuries. On any of them. No prolonged transformation time either.”

 

            Blinking, Lena’s mouth opened and closed and then she frowned, her eyes clouding with confusion. A small sound of perturbation escaped her and she lowered herself down onto the chair set off to the side of the cordoned-off bed. Gripping the arms of it, she took in the smooth lines of Kara’s face in peaceful rest and thought she did look rather untroubled this time. She looked like all the times Lena had sat beside her bed at Hogwarts, with no new scars or injuries beyond superficial scrapes and bruises gathered from running through the Forbidden Forest all night. This time, she didn’t even have those.

 

            Brooding over the revelation, Lena rubbed absentmindedly at her forehead as she tried to parse through the impact of what Belby’s discovery could mean. It was far from a cure, and they wouldn’t have the full extent of what had transpired within the cells until the werewolves came around and could recount what they’d experienced, but no new injuries were a stark improvement when they had to be locked up all night with only themselves for company. 

 

            When Kara came around, groggy and limp, her eyes landed on Lena. Still as she watched her closely, waiting for her to come to her senses before bombarding her with questions, Lena swallowed thickly. The breath gusted out of Kara’s lungs and she closed her eyes again before laughing shakily. It was a stuttering, weak thing and it quickly dissolved into breathless sobs as she swiped her thumb across her eyelids, fighting for composure.

 

            “Are you okay?” Lena asked the most pressing question.

 

            Nodding, Kara made a pitifully small sound at the back of her throat. Sniffing, she drew in a shuddering breath and Lena climbed to her feet. Helping set her glasses on her face, she then helped Kara into a sitting position, fluffing up the pillows behind her and then perching on the edge of the bed.

 

            “It worked,” Kara hoarsely told her.

 

            “You- you didn’t- I thought you still transformed. I- I thought I heard you all.”

 

            “I did. I did but … I was myself. I … I didn’t hurt myself. I remembered. I just- I curled up and went to sleep. I didn’t have to … do that to myself.”

 

            Lips parting in shocked surprise, Lena felt elation in her chest, expanding like a balloon. Relief made her shoulders slump and a hoarse laugh escaped her as her eyes creased at the corners. 

 

            “Really?”

 

            “Yes.”

 

            “I- Merlin, this changes everything. ”

 

            A smile slowly stretched across Kara’s face and her blue eyes were swimming with tears as she laughed. The two of them sat there for a minute, laughing quietly together, disbelieving and giddy with the prospects the Wolfsbane Potion could bring. Of course, it didn’t lessen Lena’s ambition to one day cure Lycanthropy but it was a step in the right direction to improve the quality of life for all werewolves.

 

            They were still thrilled by the information when the curtain was torn back ten minutes later, both women looking over before stiffening. Lena’s laughter died in her throat and she couldn’t speak for a moment as she took in the sight of Lillian in her Healer robes, looking polished and quietly fuming, just having shown up to her shift to hear her daughter was upstairs.

 

            “What are you doing here?” Lena sullenly asked.

 

            “I might ask you the same question.”

 

            Eyes darting to Kara, her ice blue eyes were flat with contempt and Lena had the urge to shield Kara from sight with her body. Lillian’s gaze returned to her daughter with a sneer of disgust as she cocked her head to the side, awaiting an explanation.

 

            “I’m visiting,” Lena stated with an edge of sarcasm.

 

            “I expressly forbade you from stepping foot in this ward again,” Lillian said, her tone brittle and her intimidating height making Lena wilt for a second before she stubbornly jutted her chin forward.

 

            “You forbade me from working on this ward again. I’m not working.”

 

            “I made no such distinction.”

 

            “I’m here as a visitor.”

 

            Lillian arched an eyebrow, the expression so intimately familiar that Lena could feel the phantom sting of the quill. “Is this the hill you want to die on?”

 

            Chewing on the inside of her bottom lip for a moment, Lena jerked her chin up, remaining firmly seated. “I may as well be hanged for a dragon as an egg.”

 

            “So be it.”

 

            Her eyes cut across to Kara again and her lip curled derisively before she let out a cold huff of laughter and then retreated. Mouth thinning with regret, her blue eyes burning with venomous hatred, Kara was stiff as Lena met her eyes. 

 

            “You should’ve gone.”

 

            “I’m not leaving you.”

 

            “I come here every month by myself-”

 

            “I don’t care,” Lena softly exclaimed. “I don’t care if you normally choose to come alone; I won’t let you. And I certainly won’t let her dictate what I can and cannot do in my free time. She has no power over me when I’m off the clock. She hasn’t since I graduated.”

 

            Opening her mouth to argue further, Kara was silenced as Lena let out a quick laugh, a ripple of worry smoothing out into tender softness as she covered Kara’s hand with her own. “It’s fine. Don’t worry about it, really.”

 

            But Kara did worry. The things she knew about Lillian could barely scratch the surface on the abuse Lena had suffered at her hands but it was still enough for her stomach to knot with unease but she kept her thoughts to herself. It wasn’t for her to tell Lena how to stand up to her mother and Lena was still riding the high of the breakthrough in the potion, a big step in the right direction for treating Lycanthropy.

 

            For all the times she’d tried to convince Kara to stay at St. Mungo’s and grimly had to discharge her against medical advice, Lena was quick to suggest they go back to her apartment so she could cook Kara a proper breakfast. The food at the hospital was mediocre at best and she knew a good fry-up would be a better way of filling Kara up after the ordeal of her night. Even if she’d been able to curl up and sleep instead of staying awake the whole night as she usually did, it was still an exhausting process to transform and Lena wanted to make sure she was well looked after. 

 

            No injuries meant that she was discharged almost instantly and Lena helped her dress as Kara’s body ached in protest, her joints stiff, her muscles sore, as if she was an arthritic elderly person instead of on the cusp of twenty-seven. Dressed warmly against the chill of September, Kara was bundled out of the hospital and to the flat in Dublin, lavish and comfortable and quiet after the sterile bustle of St. Mungo’s.

 

            Lena made her a bed up on the sofa with soft blankets and had breakfast frying in a pan by the time the kettle whistled and she made them both strong cups of tea. Tired, she all but slumped at the end of the sofa, shifting Kara’s feet into her lap as she made herself comfortable, listening to the sausages, bacon and tomatoes sizzle. Sipping her tea, Lena would have been happy to stay there all day, the peace of it welcome, but she climbed to her feet again five minutes later to crack the eggs in another pan and toast some bread.

 

            They ate at the table and then as the dishes washed themselves they napped on the sofa, at opposite ends with the blanket draped over their intertwined legs. The days had started getting shorter as autumn dragged towards winter so when Lena woke earlier than she would have liked, although she hadn’t meant to fall asleep at all, it was to lengthening shadows splayed across the floorboards.

 

            When she shifted, she woke Kara as well and her girlfriend blearily looked around as she stretched and yawned. Blinking owlishly, Kara glanced down at her watch and straightened up.

 

            “Merlin, is that the time already? Mum will have the Aurors Office out looking for me soon,” Kara said with a laugh, raking a hand through her hair.

 

            Lena hummed, rubbing her eyes and stifling a yawn of her own. “The big, bad Slytherin will get arrested for abduction. That won’t do at all. ”

 

            “It’s fine, I know people.”

 

            “Oh, you know people, do you?” Lena laughed, giving her a quick smile.

 

            “Mhm. Although, I wouldn’t trust my sister as far as I could throw a Garden Gnome when it comes to arresting Slytherins.”

 

            “She might still be holding a grudge at me getting off easy last time she burst into my home.”

 

            Kara wrinkled her nose, a sheepish look of guilt on her face, as if she’d been complicit in the raid on the Luthor manor. Sobering up, Lena raised her eyebrows a fraction and climbed to her feet, the blanket pooling on the sofa where she’d been sitting. Leaning down, she trailed her fingertips along the length of Kara’s jaw.

 

            “Would you like to stay tonight?”

 

            “Okay,” Kara murmured, her lips ghosting over Lena’s as she smiled. “But I should send my mum a letter; she thinks I’m coming home and she’ll worry.”

 

            Nodding, Lena moved over to the window with the stand for her owl, Morrigan opening an eye to stare at her before she turned her head around. Letting out a quiet laugh, Lena stroked her fingers over the bird’s feathers.

 

            “Don’t be like that,” she clicked her tongue. “You can hunt after you send it. Maybe there are more mice in Cornwall.”

 

            Kara laughed as the owl ruffled her feathers and raised her eyebrows in question, “do you have a spare quill and some parchment?”

 

            “In my office.”

 

            Gesturing towards the closed door, Lena moved over to the stove to take the whistling tea kettle off the stove as Kara walked into the office, leaving the door open. Filling two cups, she listened to Kara drag the chair out and the faint rustling of parchment, a drawer sliding open. 

 

            “Do you have any ink in here?”

 

            Shaking her head, Lena let the tea steep and padded into the office, her footsteps quiet on the wooden floorboards as she took in the profile of her girlfriend sitting at her desk, hunched over. 

 

            “It’s in the third dr-”

 

            She paused at Kara’s side, blinking as her lips parted in surprise. Kara looked up at her, a quill held tightly in her right hand as her left hand reached for the top left drawer. Suddenly, Lena reached out to grasp Kara’s wrist in an iron grip, her face bone white, her green eyes panicked as she breathed quickly, like a cornered rabbit. 

 

            “Hey. Wha-” Kara complained, her face crumpling.

 

            “Not that one,” Lena roughly choked out, yanking the quill from Kara’s fingers, which had instinctively curled tightly around the quill, flattening the fluffy wisps of the black feather.

 

            Spluttering in protest as she was forced to relinquish her hold on the quill, Kara pushed the chair back with the scrape of wood and climbed to her feet. Turning away from her, Lena closed her eyes, feeling the pounding of her heart, the shakiness of adrenaline as she raked a trembling hand through her dark hair, chin wobbling as she paced away.

 

            “What’s going on?” Kara softly asked.

 

            Lena’s response was terse and rough, regretting her tone immediately. “Nothing.”

 

            “It looks like something to me.”

 

            “Just … write your letter.”

 

            “Should I? I mean … do you want me to go?”

 

            “No.”

 

            Lena’s hurried response hung heavily between them as she turned around, ashen-faced and tired, bags beneath her eyes and a hard set to her jaw as she clenched her teeth. Her expression turned almost surly, petulant in a childish manner as she crossed her arms over her chest, thumb worrying up and down the length of the quill that had sapped so much of her blood to leave the words carved into her arm.

 

            Mystified by her erratic behaviour, Kara’s mouth opened and closed and Lena hung her head, the tense set of her shoulders holding for a moment before they sagged. Rubbing her forehead, she let out a weary sigh.

 

            “I want you to stay,” Lena softly whispered.

 

            “Okay,” Kara replied after a second, her blue eyes clouded, a pinched look of concern on her face. “Well … can you find me a quill I can use so I can finish my letter?”

 

            Straightening out the blood quill almost tenderly, Lena safely stowed it away in another drawer and ferreted out a normal quill and a pot of ink, setting them down clumsily on the desk and then backing away. She made a hasty exit from the office and returned to their tea, steeped a touch too dark as she splashed milk into them both with a jittery hand. 

 

            Wrapping her cold fingers around her own cup, Lena’s throat was dry as she tried to stifle that queasy feeling at the image of Kara’s skin rent open in her own hand. She was still standing in the kitchen with her cup of tea when Kara walked out with a neatly folded scrap of parchment in her hand. Making her way over to Morrigan, she tied the letter to her leg, the owl familiar with Kara and reluctantly standing still as the note was attached before she was led to the window and sent out into the waning evening.

 

            Turning, Kara looked wary as she crossed over to the kitchen and took her cup of tea with a murmured thank you, shoulders hunched as she cradled the cup in her palms. Clearing her throat, Lena spoke to her shoulder as she felt the faint prickle of heat in her cheeks, unable to meet her eyes.

 

            “Were you still hungry? I have shortbread in the cupboard.”

            

            “Sure.”

 

            She fetched the biscuits and set them down on the counter, taking a sip of her tea as she stared at the marbled top, listening to Kara take out a shortbread and take a bite. After a moment, Lena sighed and glanced at Kara quickly, her gaze vulnerable and apprehensive. It was all so new to her, trying to strike a balance between the doubts that things between them could overcome the hurt they’d inflicted on each other in the past, trying to recover that trust - and she did trust Kara, just not with herself - knowing there were so many secrets Lena kept locked away inside, ones she’d never divulged to anyone, that made her irate, angry, panicked, cold. She didn’t want to lash out at Kara over misunderstandings but it put Lena on edge, a cold sweat at her lower back, her palms clammy around her cup.

 

            “What would you like for dinner?” she softly asked.

 

            “I don’t mind.”

 

            “Chicken soup? Soup’s good for you when you’re unwell.”

 

            “I’m not sick.”

 

            “I know but it’s comfort food. You go and sit down; I’ll make it.”

 

            Without giving Kara much choice, considering she’d asked in the first place, Lena raided the fridge for the necessary ingredients and pulled out a large pot. Kara found herself a book to occupy the time with and read quietly on the sofa as Lena roughly chopped carrots and potatoes and measured out herbs as she consulted a cookbook on the countertop. The smell of the simmering broth half an hour later permeated the flat as she made them some more tea and curled herself up Kara’s feet again.

 

            They didn’t mention the quill and Lena was thoughtfully quiet for the remainder of the afternoon until she cut thick slices of bread and dished up their chicken soup and they sat at the kitchen table together. 

 

            “When are you working next?” Kara asked.

 

            “Tomorrow night. Long shift; the new round of Interns are starting their placements.”

 

            “Oh, does that mean you’re going to be bossing them around?”

 

            Giving her a crooked smile, Lena arched an eyebrow, “that’s my prerogative as an Attending.”

 

            “How are the new scrubs treating you?”

 

            “It feels good to be in green.”

 

            Kara let out a quick laugh, her eyes creasing with amusement. “It’s a good thing it’s your colour; you’ll be spending a lot of time in them.”

 

            “I was thinking, as an Attending … I should be able to wrangle a few days off. I’ll still be working like a House Elf most of the time, obviously, that’s just part of the job but … if I can get a weekend off, maybe we could go somewhere for your birthday.”

 

            “What did you have in mind?”

 

            Lena shrugged, “you’re the one who’s been everywhere and it’s your birthday; where do you want to go? Where haven’t you been?”

 

            “I’ve been everywhere so you should pick. How many places have you been to, actually? France, obviously.”

 

            “Obviously,” Lena agreed with a thin smile, thinking back on the summers spent in Paris, Lyon and Marseille, harangued by her mother about learning French before they’d wind up in Italy, drilling her in Latin lessons in between days in Tuscany, Como, Amalfi. “My parents used to take a few weeks off in the summer when my brother was at Hogwarts. We’d go to Italy, Germany, Switzerland, Monaco, Spain. I’ve been to most places in Europe and New York as well. Wherever my brother wanted to go in the summer holidays. We stopped going once he graduated.”

 

            “Okay, well, where would you like to go?”

 

            “I don’t know,” Lena murmured, her lips twitching wryly. “The only place I ever wanted to go was away from my family. To where you were.”

 

            Cocking her head to the side, Kara considered their options for a moment. She’d been able to amass a small amount in savings since working at The Daily Prophet and staying with Eliza but even then she couldn’t afford anything too luxurious without eating through a large chunk of it. And Lena didn’t seem that bothered by it, had probably spent her summers in the best hotels or holiday homes her family owned. Kara knew the type of Purebloods Lena’s family belonged to and she knew nothing she could offer her girlfriend could compare - except perhaps in love.

 

            “We could go camping,” Kara suggested. “If you just want a weekend with the two of us, what’s more perfect than the two of us in the middle of nowhere?”

 

            “Camping?” Lena sceptically echoed. “In a tent?”

 

            “I have one from my travels. And the rest of it. We’d just need to pick a place.”

 

            Considering it for a second, Lena hummed dubiously and then smiled. “Okay, fine. Camping it is. And as for the place, take me to the best spot you camped at that we can Apparate to.”

 

            “Deal.”

 

            They fell back into the ease of things between them over dinner, some of the lingering discomfort at the odd altercation earlier dissipating, although Lena was still aware of Kara’s curiosity over it. She resolved to tell her if she asked again, knowing Kara likely would and knowing there were answers to things Lena should have told her long ago, that might have made things end differently if it had all been laid bare. She was difficult to understand, she knew that, but it was by design that she held the keys too close to let anyone truly know the extent of her suffering. But she would tell her and she would break Kara’s heart just a little, knowing her girlfriend was too softhearted to not take it personally. 

 

            Kara cleared the table once they’d finished and set the dishes to clean themselves before tidying up, while Lena was left to watch her. She was starting to slump as her sleepless night and brief nap left her feeling drained but comforted by the presence of Kara and the knowledge that she’d been a part of something that could change her girlfriend’s life for the better. 

 

            Once she was finished, Kara crossed over to Lena and gave her a small smile, her own eyelids looking a little heavy too. “Come on, let’s go to bed. You need to rest before work tomorrow.”

 

            “I’ll sleep all day tomorrow. I want to spend time with you.”

 

            “I’ll be here in the morning.”

 

            Relenting due to the fact that she really was tired, Lena took Kara’s extended hand and let her pull her from the sofa. Making her way into her room, Lena stretched her limp muscles and fetched a pair of pyjamas before she crawled onto the bed, fishing her wand out of her pocket and flicking it to light the lamps. Shimmying out of her pants, Kara opted to sleep in her shirt as she sank onto the opposite side of the bed, gravitating towards Lena.

 

            Pressed up close to her side, feeling the warmth radiating from her, Lena was able to relax, exhaling softly as Kara toyed with her fingers, a soothing sensation that overrode the old instinct to flex them in memory of when Lillian had crushed them. There was barely a bone in her that wouldn’t be associated with pain if she was left to think about it too much whenever Kara touched her.

 

            “Are you okay?” Lena asked after a few minutes.

 

            “Mm, are you?”

 

            “Me? Why wouldn’t I be?”

 

            Kara offered no response and Lena let the silence lull her back into the comfort of her girlfriend’s arms, too awake to sleep just yet but enjoying the soft mattress as she lay limply with Kara. Fingers gently stroked her hair and Lena breathed in the smell of her soap at Kara’s throat from the bath she’d taken earlier to wash away the smell of St. Mungo’s. She pressed a delicate kiss to the pulse beating steadily at her jugular vein.

 

            “Tell me about the quill,” Kara eventually whispered.

 

            “You tell me a secret first,” Lena evasively replied as her stomach twisted uncomfortably. 

 

            “You already know all of mine.”

 

            “Do I?”

 

            “All of the big ones.”

 

            Lips twitching, Lena closed her eyes and was quiet for a second. “Tell me a little one then.”

 

            Kara considered the demand, her eyes on the ceiling as she chewed thoughtfully on her bottom lip. “You were the first person I wanted to kiss.”

 

            “Really? Who was first?”

 

            “That’s … a secret.”

 

            Lena let out a quick laugh, some of the coiled tension bleeding out of her as she propped herself up on her elbow. “Tell me.”

 

            Wincing, running a hand over her scarred face, which was steadily turning pink, Kara’s eyelids shuttered. “Mike Matthews.”

 

            “Ah,” Lena muttered. “And was he your first?”

 

            Shrugging nonchalantly, Kara’s mouth twisted derisively. “Yes. Who was yours?”

 

            “Andrea.”

 

            “Oh.”

 

            “Tell me another one.”

 

            “It’s- it’s not a secret - Alex knows - but … I went to see Alura - my- my mom - when I travelled back home. Um … it didn’t go well.”

 

            Sitting up, Lena stared down at her with a solemn look on her face, aching and pitying, wishing things could have been different for Kara than they’d been for her. But they’d both been treated badly by their mothers - the only difference was Kara had been treated well by one at least, had known love and safety. 

 

            “I’m afraid of the dark,” Lena confessed to her lap, a pink flush creeping up her neck. 

 

            “That’s why you sleep with the lamp on?” Kara asked.

 

            She didn’t ask why, and for that Lena was grateful, the knot in her chest loosening a fraction. Nodding, she looked at her and gave her a sheepish smile. Kara just nodded in response, reaching out to touch her knee as she pursed her lips, thinking hard.

 

            “I let my mum believe the trial is going well because she worries about me too much. I wish she wouldn’t; the secret is I still feel like I’m a burden to her. And Alex too. That I ruined their lives the day I got bit. They- they don’t make me feel like that but I- I just … I still feel bad.”

 

            “I came to your graduation.”

 

            “Really?”

 

            “Mhm. I was so mad at you,” Lena laughed weakly.

 

            Reaching out, Kara stroked her dark hair with tender fingers, a solemn look on her face as Lena looked up at her, face softening with amusement. Kara let out a breathless laugh, ducking down to kiss her gently, her fingers sliding over Lena’s cheek with aching tenderness. 

 

            “I regretted it instantly, you know.”

 

            Lena let out a quiet huff, smiling slightly as she arched an eyebrow. “Is that another secret?”

 

            “I’m not sure. I think everyone knew something was going on; you were the secret though.”

 

            “Ah, well, you were just honouring our old oaths.”

 

            She said it with a resigned sigh, as if she regretted their promises to keep each other secret and all the rest of it that came after that promise - the broken promise to always be friends, to look after one another. Lena had tried her best to honour her part of it but then she’d always been the one who was more dependent on Kara than she had been on Lena, the one who’d been willing to go to more extreme lengths to help her, to keep her safe. Not that she’d even felt it wasn’t equal while they’d been friends, only that Lena had so little to herself that she’d clung to Kara with the desperation only one so lonely could feel.

 

            “I’m an Animagus,” Lena murmured after a moment.

 

            Eyebrows shooting up, Kara pushed herself up. “You’re kidding.”

 

            “Honest.”

 

            “When?”

 

            “In school. We were still friends at the time.”

 

            Eyes wide with disbelief, and a faint spark of disgruntlement if Lena wasn’t mistaken, Kara’s mouth opened and closed. “Really? Well, what are you?”

 

            Lips twitching, Lena shrugged nonchalantly. “A raven.”

 

            “Will you show me?”

 

            “Not now. We’re telling secrets.”

 

            “I- what’s it like? Can you fly?”

 

            “Yes. That part is a bit terrifying. I, uh, I don’t like transforming; I’m afraid of-“

 

            “Of heights. And water,” Kara remembered, that old thrum of delight at being known by someone flooding Lena’s chest.

 

            She hummed in agreement and then gave Kara an expectant look. “Your turn.”

 

            “I wish I’d never quit my job at Hogwarts,” Kara admitted, meek and nervously fiddling as she looked at Lena with guarded blue eyes. “Mostly because I don’t think I’ll ever make that much money again, or feel so useful. And the full moons too; I wouldn’t hurt myself in the forest. Um … anyway, so we both know that I was very insecure and … I think more than that, I regret what happened between us. I don’t think I … I apologised very well the second time around.”

 

            “You’re the only person who’s ever apologised at all,” Lena choked out, a keen ache cutting through her. “I-“

 

            Lena was sitting cross-legged and her shoulders involuntarily hunched. Mouth pressed into a hard line, she swallowed thickly and then let out a forceful exhale. Straightening, she drew in a shaky breath and then laughed, her face creasing with strained amusement, bitter and aching as she rubbed the back of her hand over her eyes, as if the sting in them was from tiredness and nothing else.

 

            The smile on her face was uneven and weak and she couldn’t look at Kara as she struggled to find the words. “The quill …”

 

            She trailed off and looked at her hands in her lap, her fingers inching towards her left forearm, covering the words hidden beneath the cotton of the loose shirt she was wearing. Closing her eyes, Lena shifted, laying back down and swallowing audibly as she tried to stifle the tremor in her chest. Kara didn’t say a word, not in reassurance or encouragement, and Lena was grateful. It took her another minute, bitterly amassing the words in her throat to explain it before she tried again. This time with more success, her voice acerbic and agonised.

 

            “The quill is how she used to punish me. It’s …dark magic. It uses- it uses your blood for the ink and it- it leaves a mark. She …” Lena faltered, her throat closing up mid-sentence before she forged onwards. “She used to make me write that line if I got a question wrong, if I- if I answered back. Over and over. It would- it would cut in and then heal over each time I would write a line but the scar …”

 

            She kept her eyes squeezed tightly shut, her right hand a tight grip over the scar, purposely avoiding Kara’s expression as she came to understand how the words became etched into Lena’s skin. Lena didn’t want to see the grey look of horror on her girlfriend’s face but she was forced to listen to the ragged, shallow sob that caught in Kara’s chest.

 

            “Lena-“

 

            “It got worse,” Lena murmured through bloodless lips, interrupting while she was oversharing. “I got used to the pain of the quill - it just used to sting by that point - so she’d … break things. My fingers, my nose, my wrist. Only when she was really mad. I’m- I’m scared of the dark because … we had a dungeon on the estate. It’s pitch black and if you’re locked inside there’s no way out. She’d leave me down there as punishment, no food, no light. Sometimes for days. This is before I went to Hogwarts. After I started school, when the quill wasn’t enough … she’d lock me in there with my brother and he- he’d … practise. Unforgivable Curses. I never wanted to go home on the holidays. I never wanted to.”

 

            Lena’s words were a raw gasp of pain now, the pressure building behind her eyes, but she still wouldn’t cry. She hadn’t cried since she was a teenager, since that day Lillian had crushed her fingers beneath her book and told her never again. She spoke about her pain now as if it was old, in the past, but Lena was still tormented by it and she felt embarrassed as she confessed it to the quiet room, feeling Kara’s eyes trained on her face.

 

            “Why didn’t you tell anyone?” Kara softly exclaimed, her voice breaking.

 

            “Who? Dumbledore? He wouldn’t have done anything.”

 

            “Me. Why didn’t you tell me?” Kara cried, her ashen cheeks wet with tears. “You could’ve stayed with me. My mum would’ve loved you.”

 

            Choking on a laugh, Lena dug the heels of her palms into her eyes. Her voice was hollow and weary and she didn’t have the energy to explain how trapped she had been there, how inescapable it had been. No one could have taken her away from her home; her mother resented her but had her claim to her until Lena had graduated from Hogwarts and walked out without a second thought.

 

            “I’ve never been loved by a mother; I thought that was normal. The reason I’m afraid of water is- it’s because … she filled her pockets with stones and- and took us out into the lake, held my head under until I was choking on it. I couldn’t breathe at all. A Kelpie got her and I … I survived somehow. That’s how I ended up with my dad, with my mum. She’s hated me ever since then. She tried to … to kill me. Not Lillian - Elizabeth. I was- I was four . I … I don’t think she was well. I was too young to understand it at the time but … I think maybe everything got to be a little bit too much for her; I don’t know whether she hated me or was saving me. I used to- I used to wish I’d just drowned. It would’ve been easier.”

 

            Flat on her back on the bed in her bedroom, lit by the glow of the lamps, Lena kept her eyes shut as memories assaulted her. The ones of her suffering at Lillian’s hands were sharp from their recency and painstakingly detailed but the only memories of that night with Elizabeth were the murky unease of cold water, of a sharp pain in her chest, the panic of a firm hand pressing down on her, of a sudden, bewildering loss. It left her restless and brooding, her skin itching with the phantom pain of a hundred instances of failure, her left arm tingling in particular as Lena smoothed a thumb over the scar.

 

            And then Kara was crying, the sharp, uneven breaths making themselves known as breathless sobs after a few seconds, and Lena opened her eyes, slowly pushing herself up onto her elbows. Shoulders hunched over, the heels of her palms pressed into her eyes, nudging up her old wire-rimmed glasses, Kara cried quietly as if trying to remain unobtrusive as if she didn’t have the right and didn’t want to alert Lena to her empathy. 

 

            Laying there for a second with that old familiar emptiness in her chest that left her feeling oddly vacant and numb to be recounting everything that had been done to her, as if it had happened to someone else’s body, as if she hadn’t been inside herself when it had happened, she looked at Kara. Her blonde hair fell around her bowed head, faded silvery scars tracing her bare forearms and legs, and Lena’s eyes were unreadable as she watched her.

 

            It took her a minute to respond, sitting up fully, reaching out to encircle Kara’s wrists as she tried to pull her hands away from her face. Lena didn’t like it when people cried, didn’t like that display of weakness that had never been afforded to her, and she liked it even less when it was Kara - not for the perceived weakness but for the pain, the sadness. She couldn’t find a single ounce of desire to cry for herself, so hollow, so empty , but she didn’t want Kara to cry.

 

            “It’s okay.”

 

            “I left you all alone,” Kara said as her voice cracked, burying her face in Lena’s lap as she gripped fistfuls of her shirt in a white-knuckled grasp. “I’m sorry. I’m so sorry.”

 

            “I’m fine. It hasn’t happened in years. ”

 

            But it wasn’t fine and Lena had recently been slapped so hard she’d seen black for a second, and that wasn’t lost on Kara as she made a choked sound at the back of her throat. Biting back a soft sigh of weariness at something that Lena had buried in the past, stamped down unless it was dredged back up in the occasional nightmare, in the skin-prickling unease of walking down to the cells in St. Mungo’s or walking down the narrow paths of Knockturn Alley on a particularly dark night. 

 

            “Don’t cry,” Lena mumbled, “you haven’t even reminded me to tell you why I love you yet.”

 

            “How can you? I was supposed to get you away from them.”

 

            “I was always going to get myself away from them. I never needed you to save me; I just wanted you to love me enough to come with me.”

 

            “You should’ve told me,” Kara tearfully whispered, her head rising enough to rest on Lena’s shoulder. “I would never have let you go back there. If- if you’d stayed with me … none of it would’ve happened.”

 

            Letting out a soft sigh, Lena’s eyelids shuttered as she smoothed a hand over Kara’s wayward curls, thinking about it. She could envision it, summers spent sleeping on the floor between the two narrow beds, a nest of blankets and pillows with Kara insisting they take it in turns and Alex disgruntled at the Slytherin monopolising the limited space in the cramped room. Christmases at the little cottage with a tree and a warm fire in the small living room, hot chocolate and games of Wizards Chess, and music playing on the gramophone. Days spent at the beach and gardening, walking through the Muggle towns and being a kid. 

 

            But Lena’s childhood was stolen from her and it didn’t matter how badly she’d wanted that, it had never been an option. She’d had the cavernous manor house with the hushed silence of a graveyard. No music, an unwelcoming fire in a too-big hearth, the dismal walls and neat grounds she was always eager to escape. The malingering presence of her mother and brother and even the ghost of her father. 

 

            Maybe if she’d had the former, she would have turned out better, wouldn’t have fucked things up so much, would’ve never been put in the situation where she’d had to lie for the sake of dozens of other people’s lives and lost the one thing that had kept Lena soft with love. 

 

            “It had to happen,” Lena murmured. “If it didn’t, if we’d changed things … more people would be dead.”

 

            “You think it was worth it?” Kara asked, her voice hoarse and disbelieving as she pulled back.

 

            Her cheeks were blotchy and her eyes were still damp, a mournful look of worry on her face as she stared at Lena. A wavering smile crossed Lena’s face and she reached out to wipe away Kara’s tears, her fingers shaking slightly.

 

            “It has to be because that’s how it was. But it started long before I ever got involved with Dumbledore, so at least I can tell myself enduring it was worth it to make myself useful. ”

 

            “I won’t let anyone hurt you again.”

 

            “Don’t make promises you can’t keep. We’ve made enough of them.”

 

            “I mean it. I-”

 

            She cupped Kara’s hands in her own and swallowed thickly, fingers brushing over knuckles. “Please don’t. I can’t make you the same promise and I don’t want to watch you get hurt each month, knowing there’s nothing I can do about it. It’s already enough for me that I got away. I’ll be okay now.”

 

            “I’m sorry. I love you. I love you. I’ll keep you safe now.”

 

            But the only thing Kara had ever been able to keep Lena was a secret, and that was all Lena expected from her. There were forces outside of their control that she wouldn’t hold Kara accountable for when they caught up to her. Lena had been lucky to remain in the background of so much of what had gone on during the war, spying for Dumbledore, putting her brother away, quietly betraying friends and family. She just hoped it would remain buried, that the sceptics and fanatics who thought the Dark Lord would come back, that the Potter’s child hadn’t defeated him forever, were wrong.

 

            She didn’t bother relaying any of this to Kara, the unease that filled her with anxiety over things outside of her control, that she harboured in the recesses of her mind when she couldn’t stop thinking. Lena just let her girlfriend believe that all would be well. They had each other now and this was as much peace as Lena had known since her Hogwarts days, and that was enough for her. 

 

            In between the quiet hitching of Kara’s sobs as the conversation petered out and the passing of time towards midnight, Lena fell asleep. She’d been comforting Kara, mumbling vague nothings and the next thing she knew she was waking to an empty bed, a sunbeam striping her face from a gap in the curtains and a leaden feeling in her body from catching up on some well-needed rest. Her hand reached out for the cold side of the bed with the rumpled sheets and she lay there for a moment, thinking about Kara.

 

            And then she could hear her, the muffled sound of her singing along with the gramophone she’d turned on, the faint whistle of the kettle cutting through the noise. Waking slowly, curiously bewildered, Lena shoved her feet into slippers and crossed over to the door, opening it quietly. She stood in the doorway for a moment, watching the shafts of sunlight stripe the floorboards as the day broke, the smell of cooking bacon in the air and Kara moving about the kitchen with the ease of someone who was familiar with the place.

            

            Enjoying the brief reprieve from life, Lena lingered in the doorway and watched her for a minute longer, taking in the scarred thighs, the worn baggy shirt with the sleeves rolled back, the way Kara’s messily tied up hair was golden in the morning sunlight as she clattered about, lifting the heavy kettle from the stove, hissing softly as she burnt her palm on the hot handle as she poured water into two waiting cups. It was so peaceful, so mundane, that Lena never wanted to move on from that moment.

 

            But she shifted at the hiss of pain, quickly crossing the apartment to come up behind Kara, a note of amusement in her voice. “Be careful.”

 

            Kara jumped slightly, glancing over her shoulder, blue eyes heavy with sleep as stray curls escaped her bun, and she smiled sheepishly, uncurling the fingers of her right hand to show the red welt across the palm. Clicking her tongue, Lena twirled her wand in her fingers and then pointed the tip at the mild burn. Kara wrinkled her nose at the itching sensation and once she was done, Lena pressed a kiss to the healed skin.

 

            “Thanks.”

 

            “Good morning.”

 

            “Morning,” Kara murmured, kissing her softly. “I was trying to surprise you with breakfast in bed. I guess the kitchen table will do.”

 

            Lena’s eyes slid past her to the pan of bacon and she smiled slightly. “Thank you.”

 

            “Here.”

 

            She splashed some milk into the cup and fished out the tea bag before handing it off to Lena, who cupped it between her cool palms and blew on the steaming surface, her eyes particularly intense as she stared at her girlfriend. Not that she hadn’t been treated well with Jack, or by her friends, but there was a palpable difference in the act of Kara cooking breakfast for her, as if it meant more purely from the fact it was made with her hands. Her hands, which had fine little scars crisscrossing the fingers and knuckles and thin wrists, which could hold Lena with such tenderness yet once a month could be so dangerous that she opened up her own flesh. But not anymore; Lena had been part of something that would put an end to it.

 

            Finishing off breakfast, Kara set the plates down on the table and they bit into their food as Morrigan ruffled her feathers irritably at the noise they were making and the music filling the apartment when she was trying to sleep. Lena smiled slightly at the bird’s disgruntlement and then looked at Kara, who was eyeing her with the intensity of someone with something on their mind they wanted to say but didn’t know how.

 

            “What?”

 

            “You kept the quill,” Kara haltingly posed, a statement but one that expected an explanation.

 

            Bacon sandwich lowering back to the plate, Lena’s mouth thinned. “I stole it.”

 

            “But you kept it. Why?”

 

            “A memento of my childhood,” Lena said with a thin smile.

 

            “But you- you would never use it, would you?”

 

            Kara’s voice was small, her blue eyes wide and doleful as she feared the answer. Reaching across, Lena cupped her chin gently and wrinkled her nose briefly as she smiled, an artificial look of ease that came from years of pretence, which Kara wasn’t used to. 

 

            “It’s just a memento.”

 

            Reassured, Kara’s shoulders went slack and she let out a strained laugh, eyes creasing at the corners as she looked a little sheepish. “Okay. Good. I just- I thought for a second that maybe- but she’s not here so it’s okay.”

 

            “It’s okay,” Lena agreed, a prickle of guilt needling at her.

 

            But Kara didn’t need to know what Lena did every once in a while when the agony of failing herself, her patients, and people around her, caught up to her. It happened so rarely that Lena didn’t even think it was worth mentioning, just a small secret that had been swept under the rug in light of the bigger ones she’d divulged last night. That was how she justified it anyway and she took another bite of her sandwich to stave off anything else. Once she finished her mouthful, she tactfully changed the topic without Kara getting suspicious.

 

            “Kara … I think you should apply for another position at Hogwarts. I won’t get involved this time and I think I’m all out of strings to pull anyway but if you miss it, you should apply again.”

 

            “No,” Kara slowly replied, setting down her tea. “I don’t think I want to do that.”

 

            “But you said-”

 

            “I know but … I couldn’t do it. I- I do miss it but … last time, after what you told me, I- I was desperate and we weren’t friends. It was easy to overlook the things you said about Dumbledore because … it wasn’t real to me. But after - after I found out why he hired me - he confirmed everything you told me when I confronted him and … I think he’s … he’s not really a- a good person. I think he’s a great wizard but he- I don’t feel comfortable working for someone who could- who could manipulate people like that. Not just you but anyone . And I know it was- it was war, things were … awful. People were dying. But I just- I think … there has to be something very unscrupulous about someone to use kids as means to an end.”

 

            Lena’s mouth had thinned as Kara talked and the corners twitched now. Leaning back in her chair, a weary slump to her shoulders, Lena narrowed her eyes slightly as she gestured with one hand as she formulated a response.

 

            “Looking back at it all now … I can see how easy it was for me to fall for it. I was so alone and I think he’s a very cunning person who can see the ways a vulnerable person needs to be steered to get his desired outcome while making them feel special. I just- I was afraid, I was so scared I’d become like my family that of course I said yes when he asked me to help. The unsung hero of the war. Now all I feel is resentment that he could use me like that, make me believe that I was important, so vital to the Order’s cause, while people were dying or missing and things were getting worse. I know that … the information I fed him was useful but it didn’t make it sting any less to suffer the consequences regardless. I suppose I should just be lucky I wasn’t caught by either side, really. I could be sitting in a cell beside my brother if people had gotten the wrong idea of my spying, or dead if the Death Eaters caught wind of what I was doing. I should be grateful.”

 

            Lena’s scoff and sarcastic arch of her eyebrow said she felt anything but, and Kara wasn’t going to argue with her on it, simmering in her own resentment over how things had played out between them as a result of the secrets. She still couldn’t quell the years-old guilt of assuming the worst of Lena when she’d known her character, had known her so completely that it had knocked her entire world off balance to suspect her best friend. Kara was still resentful of that too.

 

            “But,” Lena forged onwards, “I don’t want you to make decisions about your future with me in mind-”

 

            “Isn’t that exactly what I should be doing? We’re going out and … okay, it’s new but I take it seriously so I do need to consider you.”

 

            “Yes, but that’s not the point I’m making. Don’t let my own messy past with Dumbledore stop you from working a job you enjoyed. I know you can’t enjoy working at The Daily Prophet. Andrea only enjoys it because her dad has a stake in the company and she’s set to inherit it one day. If you enjoy teaching, you should teach.”

 

            Mouth twisting, Kara shrugged, picking at the crust of her sandwich. “I don’t know. I did enjoy it but … I think more than anything, I just liked the nostalgia. I miss being in school. Everything felt so simple . Last time, when I took the job, I was desperate for some way to live comfortably, have a good job, save good money and eat three meals a day. I liked the stability of it but … I’d be lying if I said it was my first option.”

 

            “Well, what would be?”

 

            Old bitterness crossed Kara’s face briefly and she quietly scoffed, cramming the rest of the sandwich half in her mouth as she scowled. Lena smiled slightly and sipped her tea as she waited for a response. Cheeks faintly pink, Kara eventually swallowed her mouthful and sighed as she stared down at the second half.

 

            “I’d give anything to go back to the Department of Mysteries. That was a fulfilling job. Using my mind, learning new things. Teaching was great but … I wasn’t learning , they were, which is the point in teaching but I just- I miss the thrill of testing out theories, the secret of all the work we did down there. I want to know things, I want to be creative with magic and- and understand why . You’re a logical person, factual and brilliant and you have your healing with your processes and your brewing. What would you do if that was taken away from you?”

 

            “I would be nothing,” Lena murmured.

 

            “Okay, well, that’s not true,” Kara protested.

 

            Laughing, Lena rolled her eyes, “I know, I know what you’re trying to say. I understand. You found the thing that you wanted to do, that you thought was your calling, and now it’s been taken from you.”

 

            “Exactly.”

 

            “So get it back.”

 

            Scoffing, Kara raked a hand through her hair and then gestured at her scarred face. “This tends to frighten people off. Like last time.”

 

            “Perhaps they’ve missed you.”

 

            “I wasn’t there long; they’ve probably forgotten me.”

 

            “All the better. Apply again. What’s the worst that can happen? They already fired you once and you still have a job.”

 

            Chewing anxiously on her bottom lip, Kara’s eyebrows drew together. “I suppose.”

 

            “Don’t worry, it’ll work out.”

 

            “You’re not- you’re not going to do anything, are you?”

 

            Finishing off her sandwich, Lena dusted crumbs off her lap and laughed. “What, like pull some strings? No. My contacts in the Department of Mysteries are slim to none, I’m afraid. And I think your reaction last time has driven home the desire for me to keep my nose out of your business.”

 

            Wrinkling her nose, sheepish embarrassment creeping over her, Kara rubbed the back of her neck. “Okay, well … I could have handled it better, I’ll admit.”

 

            “Yes. So could have I.”

 

            A tap on the window caught their attention then, interrupting as Lena raised her cup to her lips. Sighing, she set it down and climbed to her feet, crossing over to let the unfamiliar owl inside. It had a letter tied to its leg and she quickly undid it before shutting the window behind the bird. Glancing down, she saw the crest for St. Mungo’s in the corner and was surprised to find it bearing Kara’s name, not hers.

 

            “Um, it’s for you,” Lena said as she walked back over to the table, handing Kara the letter and then reclaiming her seat.

 

            Taking a slow sip of tea, Lena was suspicious as she watched Kara break the seal and pull out a letter. As she read it, she visibly whitened, her shoulders going taut, and once she was done she folded the letter back in half and slipped it back into the envelope.

 

            “What is it?” Lena quietly demanded.

 

            “Nothing.”

 

            Kara’s reply was quick and light, setting the envelope down. Pausing, her mouth thinning, Lena reached across the table but Kara was too fast for her, jerking the letter away and arching an eyebrow in a wry warning.

 

            “Really?”

 

            Muscle twitching in her jaw, Lena sat heavily on her chair again, annoyance flickering in her eyes. “What has she done?”

 

            “How do you know she’s done anything?”

 

            “She’s my mother. You think I don’t know her, what she’s capable of? Better than anyone. And do you think I’m so thick as to not be suspicious when a letter comes addressed to you the day after she sees us together?”

 

            “You said she already knew about us anyway.”

            

            “Kara.”

 

            After a brooding moment of deliberation, Kara relented, mostly due to Lena’s exasperated desperation as she all but slumped on the table, a pleading look on her face. Handing over the letter, Kara leaned back and crossed her arms over her chest, a rueful smile on her lips as Lena slid the letter out and unfolded it, her eyes darting back and forth as she quickly read through the short letter.

 

            “I’m out of the trial,” Kara softly surmised as dawning anger started on Lena’s face.

 

            Without a word, Lena slipped the letter back into the envelope with shaky fingers and set it down precisely on the table. Pushing her chair back, she climbed to her feet, not even looking at Kara as she made for her bedroom. Changing into the first things her hands landed on, Lena reemerged to find Kara cleaning up in the kitchen.

 

            “Where are you going?” Kara suddenly asked, blinking in surprise at the sight of Lena, dressed and reaching for a cloak hanging on the rack near the door.

 

            Swinging it around her shoulders, Lena was positively haughty as her sharp eyes cut across to her girlfriend. “Going to have a word with my mother.”

 

            “Leave it alone, Lena,” Kara gravelly replied, her voice a low warning.

 

            “No. No, I will not leave it alone. I will not let her punish you for her perceived insult because you’re a fucking werewolf and she doesn’t like it. Well, I don’t like her. I- I hate her. I hate her and I am sick and tired of her thinking she can do what she likes to me. To my life. No. She’s gone too far this time.”

 

            Kara choked on a painful breath, her face softening with a pleading look, blue eyes wide and worried. “She went too far the first time she laid hands on you. Now, I’m afraid she doesn’t know where it stops.”

 

            “It stops when she brings you into it. I won’t be long; don’t go anywhere.”

 

            “Lena-” Kara tried to reason with her again before her girlfriend was tossing a handful of Floo powder into the fireplace and gone in a swirl of emerald flames before she could stop her.

 

            The grate for St. Mungo’s arrived after a dizzying torrent of fireplaces and then Lena was striding through the hospital to her mother’s office, where she didn’t even pause to knock before she wrenched the doorknob open and found the office occupied. Looking up from her work, Lillian raised her eyebrows coolly.

 

            “This is an unwelcome surprise.”

 

            “Put her back on the trial.”

 

            “I don’t know what you’re talking about.”

 

            “Put her back on the trial.”

 

            “Lower your voice. Healer Smethwyck is in charge of the trial - and that Potion Master, Belby. I assume that is the trial you’re referring to,” Lillian drawled, a faint sneer on her face as her lips twitched at the corners.

 

            “And I’m sure one little whisper from your forked tongue and they were all too quick to kick her out of it. What did you threaten them with, cancelling the trial full stop? That’s healing malpractice, not to mention outright negligence of patient care. You swore an oath. ”

 

            Clicking her tongue, Lillian sighed heavily. “Oh, Lena, get off your high Hippogriff. You don’t care about the trial beyond this silly infatuation with that werewolf and it’s amusing that you pretend otherwise. You want to talk about malpractice? Well, how is a romantic relationship with a patient supposed to look?”

 

            “I’m not her Healer,” Lena stiffly replied. “You made sure of that when you banned me from the ward.”

 

            “Girls like her are ten a Knut; find someone better. Find someone better and I’ll ask Smethwyck to put her back on the trial. Merlin knows why you care so much about it though, the most it’ll do is give her one less hideous scar or two. It’s not going to change anything. She’ll likely be dead by forty at her own hands.”

 

            “Blackmail, is it?” Lena scoffed, disbelief crossing her face before she smiled. “Are you sure that’s the road you would like to take? I have a lot of memories I think the Auror Department would be interested in seeing, a lot of evidence that would see you sharing the same cell as Lex.”

 

            Laughing, Lillian lounged in her chair with an arched eyebrow, amusement written in the lines of her hard face. “Do it, girl. I dare you. You didn’t have the nerve to do it when you were younger and you don’t have the nerve to do it now. You and I both know you’re bluffing, so do us both a favour and tuck that tail between your legs and go.”

 

            “I could do it, you know,” Lena hoarsely warned her, her pulse racing as she licked her lips. “I could tell them all what you did to me.”

            

            “And will that help your precious girlfriend? Will that get her back on the trial? Do you think I don’t have enough friends in high places to brush this- this silly obsession with painting me as this awful mother under the rug? Go on, tell them everything and see how far it gets you. You’re too short-sighted, once again, you idiotic girl. You never did learn how to play the long game, never did know how to gain the upper hand without revealing all of your cards. I’m ashamed to call you my daughter. I’m embarrassed to even look at you. Get out of my sight.”

 

            Wanting to fight her on it, wanting to slap her mother, to hex her until she was hospitalised in the Janus Thickey Ward, unable to walk or talk or cause her daughter any further problems. But Lena wasn’t so cold-hearted as she wished she was, and Lillian was right. No matter how badly she hated her mother, she couldn’t go to the Auror Department, couldn’t let people take those memories from her and see for themselves the crimes the Healer had inflicted on her own daughter in the hours she wasn’t running the hospital, a place for healing and empathy. Lena couldn’t expose the raw wounds of her childhood like that.

 

            Instead, she turned on her heel and slammed the door shut behind her before walking through St. Mungo’s to the cavernous rooms in the dungeons where dozens of cauldrons were brewing various healing potions over flames. And there, in the back corner, the cauldron with the latest batch of the Wolfsbane Potion and the stack of parchment detailing the ingredients and instructions for every batch since the beginning of the trial, with all of the notes and annotations, findings and theories. Making sure the room was empty, Lena stole it all.

Chapter 32

            The next few days, Lena was tense and distracted as she tried to go about her days as usual, so busy as an Attending that she was almost grateful for work and her hectic roster so she could avoid worrying about the theft. She was surprised it hadn’t been brought to her attention yet and presumed that meant no one had noticed. 

 

            How they hadn’t noticed the disappearance of an entire study’s worth of notes and experimental methods for creating the potion Lena didn’t know. Then again, aside from Belby and Smethwyck, the former interested in a cure for Lycanthropy and the latter the primary Healer of them, Lena was really the only other person involved that cared in the slightest about the trial. And it wasn’t for selfless reasons that she had painstakingly spent her spare hours helping tweak the potion through a dozen forms, her innate aptitude for potion making leading her to find that three stirs there, a bigger dose of aconite and drinking the potion every day for a week prior to the full moon were the correct processes for the most recent batch of the Wolfsbane Potion to work. No one else except for Belby cared about how much to tweak the ingredient measurements by, how sugar rendered it useless, and how they had managed to treat the psychological aspect of the transformation, if not the physical.

 

            It was almost a week before the matter was brought to her attention and Lena was removed from a procedure she was performing. Frowning as she bid a third-year Resident to finish cleaning out the nasty claw marks of a Hippogriff attack that had perforated the intestines of the man, which Lena had already repaired, and close them up, she left the theatre at the wary Intern who had delivered the message that her mother requested her presence.

 

            Removing the scrub cap and mask, Lena pulled off her dragonhide gloves and washed her hands before exiting the room. The Intern was waiting for her and Lena had to resist the urge to roll her eyes.

 

            “I can find the Chief’s office just fine,” Lena curtly told the meek girl.

 

            “Oh, um, they’re not in her office.”

 

            “They?”

 

            “She told me to bring you to one of the boardrooms. Um … do you need me to-?”

 

            “Which one?”

 

            “Three.”

 

            Nodding, Lena continued walking towards the elevator and spared a glance for the Intern that trailed alongside her. “Don’t you have rounds to do?”

 

            “Not yet.”

 

            “Well go and find someone in need of a bruise salve. It’s a hospital, for Merlin’s sake, it’s busy.”

 

            Floundering for a moment, the girl nodded, wide-eyed like a stag in wand light. “Yes, Healer Luthor.”

 

            Rolling her eyes this time, Lena dragged the grille across the elevator door and pushed a button, descending through the hospital and trying to be patient as it stopped at two other floors. Finally making it down to the floor with the boardrooms, Lena took a moment to compose herself, trying not to worry too much about why she might have been summoned, although she knew why. Her spiking heart rate and her clammy palms as she buried them in the pockets of her robes were proof that her mind had already latched onto the reason.

 

            Stopping outside the closed wooden door with a placard denoting Boardroom 3, Lena composed herself and cleared her throat before knocking. A moment later the door opened itself at the command of her mother, who was standing behind the chair at the head of the table. Lena quickly took in the sight of Belby, Smethwyck, a short man she knew to be the head of the Alchemy Room where they did their brewing and two other witches and a wizard she didn’t know.

 

            “You wanted to see me?” Lena asked.

 

            “Come in,” Lillian stiffly ordered her, jerking out her chair and sitting down.

 

            She flicked her hand towards the chair opposite her, at the other end of the table, and it scooted itself out. Shutting the door, Lena sank down onto the chair and arched an eyebrow in a cool manner.

 

            “May I ask what is so important that I’ve been pulled out of a procedure?”

 

            “You’ve been assisting Mr Belby in his manufacturing of this Wolfsbane Potion,” Lillian said, trying not to sound too contemptuous at the nature of the man’s work. Clearing her throat, she shifted in her seat, her pale stare pinning Lena to her own chair. “Have you not?”

 

            “Yes.”

 

            “So, you have access to the research papers for the trial?”

 

            “They’re publicly kept in the Alchemy Room; any hospital staff can access them.”

 

            “So, you have access to them?” her mother repeated.

 

            “Yes.”

 

            “And are you aware of the enchantment on the Alchemy Room where only those with a certain clearance can remove confidential hospital property from the room?”

 

            Irate, Lena ground her teeth together. “Yes.”

 

            “So, as a Healer here you would be able to, if you wished,” Lillian surmised.

 

            Mouth thinning, trying to keep her expression blank as she sat stiffly in her chair, posture perfect and her eyes drilling into her mother’s. “What’s this about?”

 

            “My research has been stolen,” Belby ground out, his face reddening with anger.

 

            “Stolen?” Lena echoed, blinking.

 

            She looked at the other witches and wizards and frowned, shifting uneasily before she sat forward, clearing her throat.

 

            “Surely you’re not accusing me of stealing it?” she asked, a small scoff of laughter escaping her.

 

            “You’ve devoted almost all of your brewing hours to this potion, you’ve been invested in it from the beginning of the trial and you’re involved in a more personal manner as well. One might believe you have more incentive than most to steal it.”

 

            “I don’t see how my personal life has any correlation to my interest in healing research,” Lena evasively replied, running her fingers over the wooden arm of the chair as she pursed her lips and lowered her eyes to the edge of the table.

 

            “Your partner is a patient of ours, is she not? One of our, ah, afflicted patients. She was, until very recently, one of our Wolfsbane trial patients. Some might describe that as a conflict of interest.”

 

            “I’m not her Healer. I’m only affiliated with the trial as a brewer.”

 

            “But you were her Healer and you are aware of her removal from the trial.”

 

            Staring blankly, Lena’s eyes were bright with anger as a muscle twitched in her jaw. Arching an eyebrow, Lillian’s lips twitched slightly.

 

            “You confronted me on that matter directly, did you not?”

 

            “Yes.”

 

            “And you left my office quite angry.”

 

            “On several occasions but I’ve never been accused of theft any of those times,” Lena curtly responded, folding her arms over her chest.

 

            Lillian was quiet for a moment, her stare calculating, weighing her daughter’s commitment to her act, which they both knew she had done, wondering if Lena would follow through on her promise to bring to light Lillian’s actions if it came to it. Her mother doubted her ability to do so but for Kara, Lena would do just about anything. She hated to think it but Lena wasn’t quite sure if murder would be completely off the table when it came to her girlfriend. 

 

            “Nevertheless, that is the accusation presented today,” Lillian eventually sighed. “Unless you have any evidence to refute the claim.”

 

            “What evidence would I have? Would you like me to take some Veritaserum? Go ahead.”

 

            “That would be unwise,” one of the witches informed Lillian, almost too quiet for Lena to hear. “It’s an unethical solution that could have negative legal ramifications if Miss Luthor-”

 

            “Healer Luthor,” Lena cut in with a thin smile as the woman glanced at her.

 

            “Should decide to pursue this further.”

 

            Lillian scoffed, a cold sound of amusement. “We’re joined today by a legal representative for St. Mungo’s and two board members. They may not know you personally but they will ensure we thoroughly investigate your involvement in the matter, so I suggest you cooperate. The consequences will be far more severe if you don’t.”

 

            “And how, exactly, do you intend to investigate this?” Lena laughed. “Are you going to search my locker? Raid my home?”

 

            “We have a witness,” the lawyer informed her. “We’ll need to discuss the matter again with you in the future once they’ve been properly questioned. There’s also the matter of questioning other employees before we can get to the bottom of this.”

 

            “Is that it then? Can I go?”

 

            Lena’s brusque attitude wasn’t helping matters and she knew that but she hated to be in Lillian’s presence for longer than strictly necessary and it was clear her mother was willing to pin this on her daughter. Of course, she had every reason to do so and Lena would let them sack her for it, so long as she finished using a Doubling charm on every single document Belby, Smethwyck, herself and a few other Healers had amassed. Lena had made a spur-of-the-moment decision to steal the documents and she hadn’t thought about how she’d get it back, nor if she even intended to do that. Right now, all she could do was go about her job as usual and wait to see how it played out.

 

            “Just one more thing.”

 

            Lillian conferred with the two board members, who nodded in agreement to whatever pre-planned discussion they’d had, solemn expressions on their faces, and Lena’s mother pushed her chair back. Climbing to her feet and shuffling the pages on the table, Lillian dragged the moment out and Lena wasn’t sure whether she was enjoying it or fuming behind her cool mask at her daughter’s attempt to besmirch the family legacy at St. Mungo’s.

 

            “You’re being stood down until the matter has been fully investigated.”

 

            Spluttering, her face going white as she shot to her feet, scowling as she braced her palms against the table, Lena felt a hot flush work its way up her neck. Her anger was quick to arrive and she felt that closely-nursed hatred for her mother grow a fraction bigger. 

 

            “Stood down? You can’t-”

 

            “I can. I have. Actions must have consequences, Lena,” Lillian said, her voice softening with feigned disappointment. “Ethical misconduct is no small thing. If this investigation implicates you … it’ll be much worse than being stood down for a few days.”

 

            Mouth parting as a look of panic quickly crossed her features, Lena straightened up. Her green eyes blazed with anger and she clamped her jaw shut, teeth clicking, fixing her mother with a defiant look that said she would not lose this time. Lena had been raised around pain and abuse and had never known anything else until she’d met Kara, and that was where she drew the line. Kara, who was sweet but could hurt like hell, who was proud but so broken deep down from the trauma of being bitten and abandoned, who had been too frightened to let Lena love her but too in love to ever stop herself from loving her back. Lena wouldn’t let her mother take away the only thing that had ever brought Lena any happiness; she’d already taken away too much as it was.

 

            “You’re not to set foot on hospital grounds until you receive an official communication stating otherwise. And Lena, if you decide you’d like to cooperate further, do send an owl.”

 

            Swallowing back the sharp retort on the tip of her tongue, Lena hesitated before whirling around and yanking open the door. Her heart was pounding, her anger narrowing her vision to what was directly in front of her as she stormed through the hallways, riding the lift up to the floor where her locker was located. She packed her things into her satchel and then slammed the locker door shut, banging her hand against it for good measure, the loud bang rousing the attention of a Mediwizard passing by, sticking their head in and then quickly retreating. 

 

            Making her way to the waiting room, her face thunderous as she cut her shift short, Lena exited the hospital and Apparated home, unlocking the front door and dropping her bag on the floor. Quickly crossing the flat, she jerked open the door to her office and descended on her desk, rummaging through the stack of papers where she’d hidden the stolen work. Half of it had already been duplicated and she spread out the rest of it, holding her wand over the pages as she cleared her throat.

 

            “Geminio.”

 

            Duplicating page after page, Lena was tense and shaky as she swiftly made her way through the rest of the research. Once she was done, she neatly stacked the duplicated copies back in her desk drawer, on top of the stack of papers she’d saved for years, slowly adding to it over the course of two decades - less frequently now - bearing the same sentence over and over again. Closing the drawer, Lena shuffled the stolen documents into a pile and chewed on her lip as she tried to consider a way to return them without stepping foot inside St. Mungo’s. Ultimately, Lena decided she’d have to go back in the middle of the night, when the hospital was quieter, slipping through the hallways with her invisibility cloak.

 

            Deciding to worry about that later, anticipating Kara over that evening for dinner, Lena, who was still wearing her cloak, left for Diagon Alley and spent a couple of hours grocery shopping as she wandered through the adjoining markets and alleys before stopping at The White Wyvern to see Veronica for a quick drink to quell her anxiety and then returning home with an armful of bags. Putting everything away, Lena went to wash off the clinging odour of work on the scrubs and dressed warmly before she made for her office and hauled a spare cauldron out. She brewed her own potions at home, half a dozen set up along the long bench in her office, amidst ingredients, books, scrolls, weights and paring knives, vials and tweezers, gloves and jars. 

 

            With the new one, Lena dragged out the latest process for the Wolfsbane Potion, the only one they’d had any semblance of luck with so far, and read through the method three times before even beginning.
