Lighting a small flame, she set water to simmer and started weighing powdered silver and stripping the frilly heads of aconite from the stems. Despite leaving work early, Lena was exhausted, feeling the absence of the potions she would have taken to get her through her shift, but she worked tirelessly through the rest of the morning and afternoon until she could do no more. It had to boil for nineteen hours before being stirred thrice clockwise and the armadillo bile added. 

 

            She spent the rest of her time prepping the other necessary ingredients for the ensuing days of brewing. It wasn’t a cheap potion to make and as Lena eyed the list of ingredients Belby had cobbled together, tweaking along the way, her mouth thinned. She already had everything stored neatly on her well-stocked shelves but it wasn’t lost on her that Kara at her lowest and most vulnerable, unemployed on Ministry benefits, would never have been able to afford to brew it herself. Boom berry, boomslang skin, dittany, wiggentree bark, honey, moondew, unicorn horn, syrup of hellebore and powdered moonstone. It was a small fortune in ingredients.

 

            Finishing up, Lena made her way through to her bathroom to wash her hands and then flicked her wand in a sweeping motion to light the flat. Lighting a fire in the hearth for good measure, a flood of heat chasing away the chill of the wooden floors and high ceilings, Lena fed Morrigan a few owl treats and then checked the time and walked to the local Chinese takeaway to place an order, carrying the steaming paper bag back to her flat and waiting for Kara to arrive. She showed up not even five minutes after Lena got home, her cheeks faintly pink and a windswept look to her blonde curls as Lena opened the door at her knock.

 

            “Hey. Just in time,” Lena smiled slightly, brimming with nervous energy as she steeled herself to tell Kara what she’d done and why. “I just picked up some Chinese for dinner.”

 

            Leaning in to kiss her softly, her lips chapped and cold against Lena’s, Kara gave her a grateful look. “You sure know how to treat a lady.”

 

            With a quiet snort of laughter, Lena ran her thumb over the hidden scar in an anxious manner as she hovered near the door and waited for Kara to get settled in first. Kara beat her to the punch though, glancing at Lena, eyebrows slightly raised beneath her ruffled fringe. 

 

            “You look tired. How was work?” Kara asked as she unwound the scarf from her neck and stepped on the heels of her boots to take them off.

 

            “Oh, um … there’s actually- well, we need to talk … about work.”

 

            Blue eyes widening a fraction with soft curiosity, Kara hummed at the back of her throat as she shed her robe and hung it on a hook inside the door before shedding the tweed jacket she was wearing underneath. Lena gave her a wavering smile and picked up her hand, drawing her closer and kissing her again. Kara smelled of ink and paper and Lena felt her heart stumble in her chest, the overpowering need to protect her rising in her chest, even from herself, the entire reason she’d dedicated hours to the trial, to her independent research. 

 

            “Let’s have some tea first,” Lena murmured, squeezing her hand. 

 

            The kettle boiled almost instantly at the flick of her wand and she was tense as she filled two mugs, poured over milk and stirred sugar into Kara’s. Leading them to the sofa, her anger was still smouldering and Lena was brooding and churlish as she tried to form the story into a concise explanation.

 

            “So?” Kara softly asked.

 

            “I’ve been stood down, pending an investigation into ethical misconduct,” Lena bitterly explained, her expression crumpling with contempt as she crossed her arms over her chest, sinking back on the sofa.

            

            “What? Why?” Kara asked, bewildered.

 

            “I- look, I need you to trust me. I know I said I wouldn’t meddle in your life but this is- this is different. It’s my fault that you were kicked off the trial in the first place so-”

 

            Shoulders slumping, Kara gave her an anguished look. “What did you do?”

 

            Mouth opening and closing, Lena raked a hand through her hair, her green eyes flinty as she swallowed thickly. “I stole the research-”

 

            “You stole the research?”

 

            “Only to duplicate it!” Lena reasoned. “If- if she won’t let you take part in the trial, well … I’ll brew it for you myself . I help brew it anyway, so it’s not like I don’t know what I’m doing, I just- no one is even interested in the trial, except for Belby and a few others, so I thought- well, it’s not even been a week since the last full moon so I thought I’d have enough time to copy and replace it before anyone noticed but I’ve just- I’ve been so busy with work and spending time with you that I hadn’t gotten through it all yet and they just … well, they noticed.”

 

            “Lena,” Kara heavily sighed.

 

            “It’s fine. It’s okay. They’re just grasping at straws-”

 

            “You did steal it! That’s not grasping.”

 

            Rolling her eyes as she let out a breathless laugh, trying to act more nonchalant than she felt as she flexed the fingers of her right hand and felt the nervous flutter of her pulse at her throat. “You don’t have to worry, really.”

 

            “Well, I am worried! You can’t ruin your career for me. You can’t- you can’t break the law because you’re mad at your mum.”

 

            “I’m not,” Lena softly replied, reaching out to cover Kara’s hand with her own. “I’m not ruining it; nothing will come of it, I promise . You won’t get into trouble-”

 

            “Oh, will you just think of yourself for once? Please,” Kara exclaimed, her cheeks colouring, blue eyes glassy. “You think I give a shit if I get in trouble? You think I can’t bear the transformation every month without a potion that has worked once? I’m not holding out hope for a cure, Lena. The only thing I’m holding out hope for is that this time I won’t fuck up this thing between us like I have every other time, so don’t worry about me.”

 

            “Well, I do! I do worry,” Lena admitted, her voice cracking slightly. “I worry about how it affects you every month, how you were bitten so- so young and maybe that means- you think I care about my job more than I care about you?”

 

            Mouth thinning as Kara stared down at her lap, avoiding Lena’s glittering stare and the derisive twist of her lips. “No, I don’t think that.”

 

            Blowing the air out of her lungs, Lena’s incensed anger died back down and she shifted back, the apartment suddenly awkwardly quiet after Kara’s murmured response. Swallowing, Lena nodded, her soft voice breaking just a little.

 

            “Well … good.”

 

            Kara nudged her glasses up and pinched the bridge of her nose as they were silent for a moment, cups of tea steaming on the coffee table, untouched. After a moment, she sighed and looked at Lena with tender understanding.

 

            “Thank you but … put it back.”

 

            Lips twitching slightly, Lena stared at her through her lashes with mournful amusement. “I was always going to put it back once I was done with it. It just- it’s complicated a little bit by the fact that they noticed quicker than anticipated and I’m not allowed to step foot in the hospital. Well, be seen stepping foot.”

 

            Kara hesitated and then narrowed her eyes a fraction, cottoning on quickly to Lena’s intentions before she sighed roughly and put her head in her hand as she groaned. “Don’t. Please.”

 

            “No one will see me, it’s fine.”

 

            Sighing again, Kara raised her head and gave Lena an exasperated look. “This is serious , you know. You could get in a lot of trouble.”

 

            “I know,” Lena murmured, a strained smile on her face as she gave Kara a wary look. “Are you mad at me?”

 

            Closing her eyes, Kara shook her head slightly and scooted across the sofa, wrapping an arm around her girlfriend’s shoulder. Kissing her forehead, Kara sighed again. “No, I’m not mad that you tried to help me. I’m mad that you risked your career though.”

 

            Wincing slightly, Lena shrugged against Kara’s side. “I can get another job.”

 

            “One of the first things I learned about you was that you wanted to be a Healer one day.”

 

            “It’s not like I had a say in the matter.”

 

            “Would you have chosen differently?”

 

            “No,” Lena admitted. “That doesn’t mean it comes above you. Or even above the code of being a Healer. Can I rightly call myself a Healer if I’m helping deny care to someone who’s sick? Besides, we both know what it’s really about.”

 

            Sighing as her shoulders sagged, Kara grimaced, “I know. I just- I hate the idea of you getting into trouble over something so- so … petty.”

 

            “She’s always been a spiteful person. This isn’t new to me. It’s personal though so I guess I have more incentive to not let it go this time.”

 

            Mouth turning down at the corners as she frowned, blue eyes darkening, Kara cupped the back of Lena’s wrist and held her palm in her other hand, smoothing her thumb along the side of her forearm, an inch from the scar but the intention obvious. 

 

            “It wasn’t personal before?”

 

            Shrugging, Lena’s cheek shallowly dimpled with rueful amusement. “It was familiar.”

 

            Exhaling softly, Kara raised Lena’s hand and pressed her palm to her cheek and Lena couldn’t stop herself from stroking her thumb along one of the silver scars, her featherlight touch making Kara’s skin ripple with goosebumps. Shifting onto one knee, Lena cupped the side of Kara’s head and kissed her forehead before pushing herself up.

 

            “Come and eat.”

 

            That seemed to be the end of it for the time being, dinner taking over as they dished up spoonfuls of special fried rice and curry sauce and Lena peppered Kara with questions about her own day to avoid talking about hers. Making a few vague comments about the articles she’d transcribed from someone’s messy handwriting to the precise lettering of a typewriter, the research she’d forked over to bonafide journalists to build their stories around, all around unsatisfying work for someone who craved more mental stimulation than that.

 

            They’d just finished eating, Kara cleaning up as Lena packaged up the leftovers for her to take home, either for Eliza’s dinner or her lunch tomorrow, when there was a knock on the door. Exchanging a glance with Kara, Lena moved towards the door with apprehension on her face, not expecting any visitors that evening. She opened it with a stiff set to her shoulders, which quickly went slack as took in the sight of Sam standing there, fresh from a shift at St. Mungo’s.

 

            “Why is Eve Tessmacher spreading a rumour that you’ve been stood down?” Sam asked as she invited herself inside, unwinding a scarf, her scrubs still on beneath a deep grey robe. 

 

            Kara turned from the sink, where she was placing the dirty dishes to wash themselves, and stared wide-eyed at her old Housemate, feeling as if she’d been caught out. That lingering feeling of secrecy hadn’t worn off yet and while she’d told her friends the truth about the nature of their relationship, she knew Lena hadn’t done the same. Granted, they both had an ex in that one particular friend circle and it would be blatantly obvious what had gone on in the past once they knew, but Lena hadn’t even told Sam, who was separate from her other friends.

 

            “Kara?” Sam said as she blinked in surprise, pausing just inside the mouth of the entryway. 

 

            “Sam,” Kara slowly greeted her, glancing at Lena and then back to the other Healer. “Um … shall I make tea?”

 

            Eyes sliding to Lena, Sam arched an eyebrow and Lena raised her chin a fraction, gesturing to the rack for Sam to hang her robe before she drifted into the kitchen, hand skimming Kara’s back as she murmured how Sam took her tea. Nodding, Kara lined up three cups and Lena turned away from her, meeting Sam’s pointed glance and clearing her throat.

 

            “Um …”

 

            “What the hell is going on?” Sam softly asked, concerned confusion in her hazel eyes as she gave Lena a searching look. 

 

            Closing her eyes, Lena’s mouth thinned and she listened to the faint whistle of the kettle and Kara’s quiet movements around the kitchen as she made their tea. “It’s- nothing, it’s just … my mum, you know?”

 

            Opening her eyes, she watched Sam fold her arms over her chest, a stern look on her face that was shockingly maternal that Lena almost laughed. Carefully floating three cups of tea with her, Kara touched Lena’s elbow and urged her towards the sofa before taking her own cup and supervising the dishes as she gave the two Healers a veneer of privacy.

 

            “Want to try that again? Because it sounds serious. You don’t get stood down for nothing. You got sent home halfway through a shift and your name’s been wiped off all the procedure boards.”

 

            “It’s probably better if you don’t know,” Lena sighed, crossing her legs as she propped her elbow up on the sofa and her chin in her hand. “They’re going to be doing a full investigation. Trying to stir up witnesses, ask some questions, you know?” 

 

            “For what?” Sam softly exclaimed, her gentle demeanour flushed with outrage.

 

            “It’s-”

 

            Kara sighed heavily from the kitchen and Lena’s eyes flickered over to her back, watching her wave her wand as she directed the cleaned and dried plates and cutlery to their respective cupboards and drawers. She didn’t turn around as she wearily spoke.

 

            “Just tell her.”

 

            Eyelids shuttering, Lena raked a hand through her hair. “So … the Wolfsbane Potion,” she haltingly started. “Um … I’ve been helping out with the brewing process.”

 

            “I’m aware.”

 

            “Um … I got Kara a spot on the trial at the start of the year. We’ve been friends since I first started at Hogwarts, actually, and … we, uh, we’re-”

 

            Lena gestured vaguely between herself and her girlfriend, shifting on the sofa and reaching for her cup of tea. Taking a scalding sip, Lena cleared her throat, looking almost sheepish as she smiled tentatively at her friend.

 

            “Oh. Right,” Sam murmured, glancing between the two of them again, a faint furrow between her eyebrows.

 

            “So … my mum’s not pleased. Obviously.”

            

            “Right.”

 

            “She managed to get Belby and Smethwyck to kick Kara off the trial after the last full moon. Um … I had a row with her on the Bite Ward because she didn’t like the technicality that I was a visitor , not working , so I guess that was her petty revenge. Anyway, she kicked her off so I stole all of the papers-”

 

            “You what?”

 

            Rolling her eyes, Lena gestured dismissively, “it’s temporary. Just until I copied it all so I could make the potion myself.”

 

            Closing her eyes for a moment, Sam inhaled deeply and then fixed her friend with a stern look. “Lena, that’s … very, very dangerous. It’s experimental magic-”

 

            “I’ve been brewing parts of it for months.”

 

            “And it’s still in the trial phase. You could find yourself in deep trouble over this if it goes wrong. I mean … what are you going to do, lock her in your bedroom and hope for the best? You could get bitten. Not to mention if Belby accuses you of plagiarising his work.”

 

            “I’m not going to publish it,” Lena protested. “And what else do you expect me to do? Leave her in a cell at St. Mungo’s with nothing so she can rip herself apart? What would you do? If it was Ruby, what would you do? Because if you’re going to sit there and tell me you would willingly let her hurt herself , month after month, with a solution in your hands, you’re a fucking liar.”

 

            Sam sighed, shoulders slumping in defeat as she rubbed her forehead. “You know I would do the same. But that doesn’t make it any less risky.”

 

            “You should listen to her,” Kara softly piped up from the kitchen, holding her cup of tea in her hands as she gave Lena a pained, pleading look.

 

            Shooting to her feet, Lena’s face was furrowed with anger as she ground out a reply. “No. No, I will not . You might not give a shit about yourself because of the things people say about you, but I care and I’m doing it, whether you like it or not. And I’m not asking for anyone else’s opinion so save it.”

 

            They all fell silent, Lena’s chest rising and falling quickly, two bright spots of colour in her cheeks as her green eyes shined with anger. No one spoke and Sam rubbed her forehead as she considered it. Kara didn’t argue any further, her eyes cast downwards, a nervous set to her shoulders as she sipped her tea in silence.

 

            “Where’s the research?” Sam eventually sighed.

 

            “In my office.”

 

            “Go and get it.”

 

            Mouth opening and closing, Lena frowned as she eyed her friend warily. “Why?”

 

            “Just go and get it.”

 

            Grimacing, Lena went and fetched the stack of damning evidence from its hiding spot and re-emerged from the office with hunched shoulders. Hesitating, she set them down on the coffee table and reclaimed her seat, sighing heavily and gesturing to it.

 

            “That’s all of it.”

 

            “Okay,” Sam said, nodding before she drained her cup of tea and climbed to her feet, stooping to pick up the stack of papers.

 

            “Hey, what-”

 

            Giving her a pointed look, Sam’s mouth thinned with exasperation. “You know, being a single mum is hard sometimes. Especially as a Healer. Long hours, no help. It was so easy to accidentally pick up the wrong stack of paperwork after a long session in the Alchemy Room trying to catch up on my brewing hours. Silly me.”

 

            Lena arched an eyebrow in a cool look of disapproval. “Absolutely not.”

 

            “Look, you messed up but I’m not going to let your mum punish you for it. We’ll chalk it up to an accident, I’ll say it was my fault, that I didn’t realise I’d picked up the wrong stack.”

 

            “I’m not going to let her punish you either,” Lena argued. “And she knows we’re friends so she’s not going to believe that you-”

 

            Shrugging indifferently, Sam smiled slightly. “I’ll get a slap on the wrist because I’m not you and she has no reason to stand me down and put on a big song and dance about an investigation. And she might not believe me but what’s she going to do about it? I’ll go to Belby directly and apologise profusely and play the part of a scatterbrained mum and he’ll eat it right up and it’ll all be forgotten about by the end of the week. And then you’re going to give me all your good cases for the next month.”

 

            Her smile widened a fraction and Lena let out a hoarse laugh, running a hand through her hair and then swiping her thumbs over her eyelids as she considered it for a second. “No, I can’t let you do that-”

 

            “You’re my friend . That’s what friends do. Normally, they also tell each other about shit like this-”

 

            “Well, it was a bit impromptu,” Lena peevishly replied.

 

            “And if they’re seeing someone so they can be happy for them. Thanks for sharing.”

 

            Wincing slightly as her face flushed, her expression turned sheepish and she grumbled faint apologies and excuses beneath her breath as she shadowed Sam to the door. Pausing to say goodbye to Kara, who was uncertain and agitated, Sam fetched her robe and safely stowed the stolen research in her bag before fixing Lena with an exasperated look.

 

            “It’ll be fine,” Sam assured her, giving her a quick hug.

 

            Lena rubbed her back, guilt welling up inside as she wrinkled her nose. “Thank you.”

 

            “I’m happy for you,” she whispered back.

 

            “I’ll tell you all about it over drinks.”

 

            “You’re paying.”

 

            “Of course.”

 

            Pulling back, Lena gave her friend a tired smile and Sam squeezed her arm. “Well, I need to get going so I can put this back and get home for dinner.”

 

            “Thank you.”

 

            “Don’t mention it.”

 

            “Have a good night.”

 

            “And you two,” Sam said before stepping out the front door and Apparating away.

 

            Coming up behind her, Kara’s arms encircled Lena’s waist. She kissed her cheek and Lena leaned back against her as they stared at the closed door, anxiously biting her bottom lip as she hoped Sam pulled it off as planned. Letting out a weary sigh, Lena extracted herself from Kara’s embrace and gave her a grim smile.

 

            “Well …”

 

            “You didn’t tell her.”

 

            “No.”

 

            “Why not?”

 

            Wrinkling her nose, Lena shrugged nonchalantly. “I told you I needed some time … this is just- I wanted to be sure before I went around telling everyone. We don’t have the best track record and obviously … with Jack and William, it’s going to cause a bit of a fuss.”

 

            Smiling ruefully, Kara brushed her fingers against Lena’s cheek and kissed her quickly. “Then we’ll avoid the fuss for a while. But I know Sam from school, and she’s treated me a few times in the hospital, so maybe we could start there.”

 

            “You want to come for drinks?”

 

            “Seeing as you’re paying,” Kara said with a quick wink and a grin. 

 

            Snorting, Lena shook her head as she looked down before sobering up. Meeting Kara’s eyes again, she softly sighed, grimacing as her eyelids shuttered. “I’m sorry for dragging you into this. It was impulsive, I know, and I should have told you as soon as I came back from seeing her but … I just want to help you.”

 

            “I know,” Kara murmured, leaning in and giving her a soft peck. “Thank you. You always help me out of my problems, I just- I wish I could do the same for you. Or … that you’d at least help yourself more.”

 

            “I have helped myself. I got away from her, I forgave you so I could have you. Right now, I have everything I’ve ever wanted for myself. So, don’t worry about me.”

 

            “Someone has to.”

 

 

            The next morning, Lena woke to an owl from St. Mungo’s with a letter reinstating her bearing her mother’s signature at the bottom. She couldn’t help the smug curl of her lips as she imagined the bitter sneer on Lillian’s face as she was forced to end her punishment prematurely, and Lena was in a relatively good mood for her as she dressed for work and left Kara sleeping in her bed as she Flooed to the hospital.

 

            Nothing more was said at work about what had happened and Lena had to resist the urge to ignorantly question Lillian on the investigation, settling for a clueless conversation with Belby as he tersely explained another Healer had mistakenly taken it home after a long shift. With the matter closed Lena kept her head down for the next few weeks, slipping Sam her best cases as promised and putting in a request for a few days off around Kara’s birthday, the two of them slipping away to a loch in Scotland, camping on the shore in the shade of the elm trees as they enjoyed the solitude and peace of the unpopulated wilderness. 

 

            She bought Kara a selection of sweets and chocolates from Honeydukes and the new model of a brass telescope for stargazing, which they put to good use, pointing out constellations in between patches of cloud cover on their trip. It was a perfect weekend as far as Lena was concerned, making a campfire with real wood for the novelty of it, sipping black coffee and cooking sausages over the flames, part-way hiking the perimeter of the loch as Kara pointed out herbs, taking cuttings for her mother, and catching sight of bowtruckles in the trees. 

 

            On Kara’s actual birthday, Lena found herself at Kara’s house for dinner, sitting beside her somewhat apprehensively as she hadn’t quite settled into the reality of being known and accepted by Kara’s family. She’d gone over for dinner twice more since the first dinner with them all - three if she was including that night she’d met Eliza after plucking up the courage to seek Kara out - and they were welcoming, even if Alex hadn’t warmed to her completely, but Lena wasn’t used to being around families. It felt strange to watch them together, the easy banter, the easy laughter, all of it so easy when the only thing that had come easily in her family was pain. 

 

            In her spare time, Lena meticulously tended to her cauldron of the Wolfsbane Potion as well, spending hours over the cauldron, only a fraction of the size of the ones they used at St. Mungo’s. Lena triple-checked her calculations as she proportionately decreased the necessary quantities, scribbling down figures and formulas and painstakingly weighing everything with the tiny weights and scales, measuring out fluids and precisely chopping and crushing seeds and leaves and splicing hairs.

 

            Kara knew what she was doing but she didn’t question it, wasn’t curious at all as she resolved to trust her girlfriend to replicate what she’d done before. She liked to think that the worse that could happen was she’d endure the transformation as usual, the red rage of lycanthropy taking over under dawn, when the memories would flood back in with the pain of tearing her flesh open but Kara knew there was a very real possibility that the worst that could happen was worse than that. She tried not to even think about it, her belief in Lena steadfast through the six doses of the potion she was given, tasting identically foul to the previous ones she’d taken for a week each month since starting the trial until she made it to the afternoon of the next full moon.

 

            “Here,” Lena murmured, handing Kara the seventh and final dose of the potion, her face pinched with worry and shockingly pale as she watched Kara drain the goblet with a grimace of disgust.

 

            “It’s a pity you can’t fix the taste,” Kara thickly replied as she swallowed the last of it, her skin holding a greyish pallor in anticipation of the full moon. 

 

            Giving her a rueful smile, Lena took the goblet back. “I’ll work on it.”

 

            Glancing down at her watch, Lena nodded to herself and then glanced up at Kara, giving her a thin smile. “We should get you settled in.”

 

            Wariness flickering in her eyes, Kara nodded and followed Lena to the office. Inside, she started to shed her clothes as Lena put away anything fragile and did what she could for the simmering potions that were in the process of brewing. The Wolfsbane Potion had all been bottled up with the correct doses in anticipation of the next full moon, waiting to see if she’d followed the process correctly before knowing whether to dispose of it or keep it on the stocked shelves. 

 

            Once she had finished, fetching a woollen blanket for Kara for comfort’s sake until the moon rose, Lena lingered, anxious as she went through the process of checking Kara’s vitals next. Her girlfriend endured having her pulse counted, her chest listened to and her pupillary response checked, Lena’s examination quick and efficient, so familiar to those months where she’d treated Kara with that seemingly insurmountable gulf between them that Kara’s heart ached. 

 

            That slight softening, exacerbated by her worry, was enough for Kara to voice her doubts, her voice a frayed whisper as her panic got the better of her. She would never forgive herself for hurting Lena, not again, not even over so much as a scratch, so much as a harsh word. 

 

            “Lena … I think maybe I should go to St. Mungo’s,” Kara hedged.

 

            “It’ll be fine. The potion is brewed correctly, I’m sure.”

 

            “You can’t stay here.”

 

            Letting out a huff of laughter, a little uneven as she momentarily doubted her own skill, Lena swallowed thickly and smiled tightly, the corners of her eyes creasing as she cupped her girlfriend’s face in her hands. Giving her an impatient kiss, Lena tucked blonde curls behind Kara’s ears and straightened, shoulders squaring.

 

            “You won’t get out. I’ll lock you in the office and ward the doors. Don’t worry, you’re not going to hurt me. You’ll just curl up and go to sleep.”

 

            “I-” Kara started to protest, her brow creasing with concern. “What if it doesn’t work? What if I get out? I’ll bite you, at best . At worst I could- I could-”

 

            She couldn’t even say it, her face pinched with fear as her blue eyes widened at the mere prospect. Kara reached out and brushed the back of her scarred fingers over Lena’s cheek, an aching plea in her gaze. 

 

            “But you won’t . I’ve helped brew this potion a dozen times already, and the last dose worked as best as we could hope. I’ll be replicating what’s already been done. Unless you’re doubting my skill?”

 

            “I- okay. Okay, but make sure you ward the door properly. And you’re not allowed to come in. Even if it all goes okay, you can’t open that door until the sun is up. Promise me.”

 

            Holding Kara’s hand in her own, Lena squeezed reassuringly. “I promise.”

 

            Slipping her glasses from her face, Kara set them down on the desk beside her wand and Lena kissed her again before lingering. Pausing just inside the door as a palpable tension filled the air, she felt a funny spasm in her chest as her throat grew tight.

 

            “I love you, Kara,” she softly told her.

 

            “I love you too.”

 

            Shutting the door behind herself, Lena locked and warded it as promised, the entire flat already muffled by the permanent enchantment to ensure no neighbours could hear inside the walls of it, and she found herself restless and anxious as she waited. It was another ten agonising minutes before she heard the first cry of pain from Kara, muted behind the closed door but torn with agony. Immediately stepping up to the door, Lena slapped her palm against it, teeth clenched as she was forced to listen and endure, her promise holding her fast.

 

            Ever the scholar, she timed the duration of the transformation on her wristwatch, from the first cry of pain through the choked gasps and pitiful whimpers, the sharp yelps that turned more obviously animalistic as the minutes crept past until there was a baying howl and a panting quietness that Lena could barely hear with her ear pressed against the wood. She made a note on a scrap of parchment, her mouth dry with fear, her heart beating a nervous flutter in her chest as she was left alone for the night, to hold vigil through the dark hours until the sunrise.

 

            Making strong coffee and slipping one of her potions brewed for work, Lena spent the slowly dragging hours reading through a new healing textbook as she made notes in the margins and periodically checked the time. At one point, she paced back and forth outside of her office, no sound from within save for the rumble of breaths, and she felt relief at that, believing her confidence had paid off and Kara was no threat to herself. Of course, she couldn’t check, couldn’t be sure until Kara verified it herself but the absence of hair-raising howls and the angry snarls and yelps of pain at sharp claws cutting through skin and muscle were reassuring. She would have heard if Kara had been in a fit of rage, trashing Lena’s carefully organised office.

 

            Still, at dawn, once she heard the wolfish whimpers of pain slip into painfully human groans of agony at the transformation reversing, Lena was inside as soon as she was sure it was over. Spread out on the floor, covered in a cold sweat and nauseously grey, Kara was otherwise unharmed. Rushing over to her, Lena dropped to her knees at her side, dragging the folded blanket off the back of the chair and draping it over her as she watched Kara’s eyelids flutter, a wispy whimper slipping from between her lips, turning into faint whine at the ache that suffused her reformed limbs.

 

            “Hey,” Lena whispered, her fingers going to Kara’s pulse at her neck, measuring the tempo quickly as her eyes flitted over Kara’s face, the taut look of lingering pain. “You’re alright. You’re okay. I’m here.”

 

            “Lena,” Kara sighed, her name coming out softly slurred with relief, some of the crumpled look of agony smoothing out. Raising a leaden hand, Kara clumsily brushed the back of it across Lena’s cheek, her bloodless lips thinning with a wavering smile. “You’re a genius.”

 

            Choking on a laugh, the sound coming out as a hoarse surprise, Lena folded over her, face pressed against the soft wool of the blanket as she all but went limp against Kara’s prone figure. Keen relief swept through her and she raised her head again, gently gripping Kara’s chin and pressing a firm kiss to her cheek.

 

            “You did well,” Lena murmured, stroking back Kara’s salted curls from her clammy forehead.

 

            “You did,” Kara rasped with a wan smile.

            

            “Here, drink,” Lena urged her, helping Kara into a sitting position and pressing a glass of water in her shaking hands, holding the bottom to keep her from spilling it. 

 

            As Kara slowly came back to herself, Lena climbed to her feet and quickly located a Restorative Draught from her array of potions, murmuring as she coaxed Kara into drinking it as well, watching her perk up slightly as it hit her bloodstream. Rubbing her eyes, Kara let out a rough sigh and then clambered to her feet, Lena gripping her elbow tightly as she went with her, and fetched her glasses from the desk.

 

            “How- how was it?” Lena ventured after a few minutes.

 

            “The same as last time. Hurts like hell but … I kept my mind. I just- I slept. Not a scratch on me.”

 

            Roughly exhaling, Lena hugged Kara gently, triumph and vindication filling her as a faint smile twitched her lips. “You should eat something.”

 

            “Mm,” Kara hummed, drawing back. “And you. You look exhausted. Did you not sleep at all?”

 

            “Of course I didn’t,” Lena lightly replied. “I didn’t want to leave you alone.”

 

            Expression softening, Kara’s shoulders sagged and she cupped Lena’s chin, kissing her quickly before her eyes travelled around the office. “And not a single thing out of place too, huh? That’s some potion you brewed. You ever going to tell me how you do it?”

 

            Snorting, Lena rolled her eyes and opened a desk drawer, removing the duplicated research and nudging the drawer closed with her leg. Setting the stack down on the desk, she spread out the top few pages and gestured to it with a prickle of pride - although she hadn’t been the creator of it, she’d perfectly replicated the entirety of the difficult process without any assistance.

 

            Kara read over the first few pages of ingredients and let out a low whistle, “bloody hell, this costs a small fortune to make.”

 

            She looked up at Lena with that edge of unease, blue eyes full of doubt and wariness until Lena brushed her hair out of her face. “Don’t you worry about that . It’s a small price to pay for your health, your comfort.”

 

            “I- thank you,” Kara awkwardly managed to get out, surprising Lena with the ease with which she swallowed her pride enough to accept the help offered, before her cheeks turned faintly pink. “Um … it’s just- when this is published, when it’s public knowledge … the other werewolves won’t be able to afford it.”

 

            “Oh, well, I’ll just have to lobby the Ministry for funding to produce it in mass. Or St. Mungo’s to offer a treatment plan. I’ll fight for it when the time comes, don’t worry. And I’m very good at getting what I want.”

 

            She gave Kara a quick smile and then turned back to her duplicated research, tapping a page with the start of the procedure. “It’s not just the cost though; it’s a tricky one to brew.”

 

            Poring over the pages, Kara followed along, muttering and softly cursing or exclaiming at times at the length and complexity of it, renewed bafflement and appreciation for Lena’s intelligence and skill filling her. Up until she got to the end of the stack Lena had pulled out, while Lena talked about the processes and near-misses, laughing self-deprecatingly as she plucked jars and vials from the shelves, showcasing ground moonstone and dried aconite and other ingredients. 

 

            Confusion quickly giving way to ashen shock, Kara slid the last few pages caught at the bottom of the stack out across the desk, her eyes flitting across the repeated sentence as her heart caught in her throat. Picking up the pages, she turned towards Lena, who was reshelving wiggentree bark and cut off mid-sentence of her animated explanation as she looked at Kara and then the pages she held and felt the words turn to dry fear in her mouth.

 

            “What’s this?” Kara asked, her eyes wide and full of sorrowful horror, already drawing a conclusion from the blatant evidence.

 

            Lena opened and closed her mouth, rubbing the back of her neck as she shrugged and gestured indifferently. “It’s some of the pages from when she used to make me write lines. I held onto them.”

 

            “Lena, some of these are fresh.”

 

            “They’re not fresh,” Lena scoffed. “They’re at least a few months old.”

 

            Spluttering, Kara was aghast, her shoulders sagging as Lena confirmed her thoughts. Face white, chin wobbling slightly as tears limned her eyes, Kara’s eyebrows drew together in a bewildered look of wounded panic.

 

            “You said- you said that you didn’t- it was just a memento,” Kara hoarsely stammered. 

 

            Squeezing her eyes shut, Lena swallowed thickly past the tightness of her throat. Shaking her head, she opened her eyes and a thin smile twitched the corners of her lips. “Let’s get you something to wear.”

 

            “Lena.”

 

            “What do you want me to say? I didn’t lie when you asked; it is a memento now. I mean it, I haven’t used the quill in months.”

 

            “Why? Why would you do that to yourself?” Kara choked out.

 

            Lips twisting derisively, Lena’s eyes were hard with anger as she stared at the floor, scuffing her socked foot over the patterned rug as she deliberated before deciding on the truth. “Sometimes … I think I deserve to be punished for things I've done and … it’s familiar, so …”

 

            “Punished, ” Kara breathlessly murmured, her voice appalled and faint as her expression crumpled. She stumbled over her feet in her haste to bridge that gap separating them, almost collapsing into Lena as her knees buckled. “I- no. No, you don’t- you’re not allowed to do that, okay? You can’t-”

 

            “I haven’t,” Lena murmured, feeling hot with embarrassment as she wouldn’t meet Kara’s eyes. “Not since … I don’t know, May.”

 

            “May? What happened in May?”

 

            Kara’s voice was a hollow rasp, her blue eyes desolate and aching and Lena closed her eyes, rubbing her forehead as she let out a rough breath, shaking her head. “Nothing, I- it was work. A patient. I lost a patient.”

 

            “But …” Kara faltered, “but that’s not your fault.”

 

            A frayed laugh escaped Lena as she squeezed her eyes tightly shut, shaking her head. “I’m a Healer; it’s my job to save people.”

 

            “That doesn’t mean you can save everyone. No, you can’t- you can’t do that to yourself.”

 

            “It’s fine, it’s okay,” Lena softly assured her.

 

            “It’s not okay,” Kara exclaimed, her chest rising and falling quickly as she got herself worked up, eyes stinging with tears. “It’s not fucking okay. Don’t stand there and tell me that it’s fine for you to do this to yourself. Not when you have a choice.”

 

            There was steel in Lena’s voice as she replied, eyes flashing dangerously. “I never had a choice at the beginning.”

 

            “But you do now. Why would you keep doing it?”

 

            “I already told you why.”

 

            Shaking her head, Kara ran a shaky hand over her face and drew in a ragged breath. “And the others? When was the time before that?”

 

            Choking on a laugh, Lena gave her a pained look as she gestured helplessly. “I don’t know … March?”

 

            “What happened in March?”

 

            “I left Jack. I felt bad about it.”

 

            “The time before that?”

 

            “What, do you want me to go back through every single time and explain in detail?” Lena snorted. 

 

            “No, I want to know how many times I made you do it.”

 

            Exhaling roughly, Lena pinched the bridge of her nose. “You never made me do any of it.”

 

            “But there was a time, wasn’t there? Maybe a few. The way I treated you …”

 

            Face rippling with pain, all the answers Kara needed, Lena took a small step forward, hand reaching out for her. Blue eyes shining bright with tears as she covered her mouth with a hand, Kara turned around, bare shoulders hunched as Lena was left reaching for her scarred back, the blanket barely held in place. 

 

            “When?” Kara hoarsely asked, gripping the back of the desk chair.

 

            “It doesn’t matter. It wasn’t you, it was me.”

 

            “When?”

 

            Lena’s mouth thinned and she seemed to chew on the words for a moment, deliberating before conceding one answer, one instance that Kara had been partially responsible for the way Lena had felt and had acted. “February,” she whispered, her lips twisting ruefully. “February after the Lake District, when you kissed me and I said … horrible things. When I was too much of a coward to admit how I felt about you, and when I knew I was stringing Jack along. Is that what you want to hear? That I hated myself for hurting people I cared about so I came home and wrote five pages worth and wished it hurt more to make the heartbreak hurt less. Does that make you feel better?”

 

            She knew her sarcasm was unfair but Lena felt hot and uncomfortable revealing so much, running a hand through her hair, exhausted from a sleepless night and dry-eyed and irritable as a result. Lena had never been good at feeling the correct emotion, anger instead of sadness, wariness instead of happiness, numbness instead of pain, it all got mixed up inside her. 

 

            Swiping her thumbs over her eyelids, she sighed heavily and crossed over to Kara, pressing a warm palm against the notches of her spine, feeling the trembling of silent sobs. Reaching for the drooping blanket, Lena hitched it up and wrapped it around Kara’s shoulders before she stepped in close and hugged her from behind, cheek pressed to her shoulder blade. 

 

            “Don’t cry. Please.”

 

            A broken sob escaped Kara as she hunched over, heels of her palms pressed to her eyes as she drew in a shuddering breath, and Lena tightened her grip. 

 

            “I’m sorry.”

 

            “You don’t have to apologise for crying.”

 

            “Not- not sorry f-for crying. S-sorry for ever … ever making you feel like-”

 

            “Not you,” Lena fiercely whispered as she hugged her tighter, her chin on Kara’s shoulder, a stubborn set to her mouth. “Don’t blame yourself. I didn’t tell you to upset you, I-”

 

            Kara turned in her arms, eyes bloodshot, cheeks blotchy. “Upset me? It’s the- the least I deserve. To know that what I did- the way things went badly between us- it’s my fault.”

 

            She dashed a hand over her cheeks, sniffing as she wiped away the tears. Lena softly hushed her, reaching up to brush away an errant tear before her fingertips traced a path along Kara’s jaw. Giving her a weak smile, eyes tightening at the corners with pain, Lena reached out to pull the front of the blanket closed over Kara’s nakedness, the office air cool as rain lashed the windows outside. 

 

            “Stop it. I’ll blame you for a lot of things that happened between us but not this, alright?”

 

            Scowling, cheeks pink and eyes filled with devastation, Kara’s mouth turned down at the corners but she couldn’t quite stop her bottom lip from wobbling. Looking down, she swallowed thickly and then turned around again, head ducked down. It took Lena a second to realise what she was doing, jerking open a desk drawer and rummaging through the orderly arranged supplies.

 

            “What are you doing?”

 

            “Where is it?”

 

            “Where’s what?”

 

            “The quill.”

 

            “Why?”

 

            “Because,” Kara ground out, her voice trembling as she tried to keep her composure, “I’m taking it home with me and you are never using it again. Do you hear me?”

 

            Expression softening, Lena’s shoulders sagged and she gently nudged Kara aside and opened the correct drawer, fishing out the black quill from a stack of papers with the same line repeated over and over, almost two decades worth taking up the entire drawer. Kara’s eyes flickered with agony as she saw and Lena quickly shut the drawer again before she could reach inside and count the times Lena had split her forearm open with the quill. Even if she’d counted them all, it wouldn’t be close to the real number of times, when Lena hadn't saved the pages afterwards. 

 

            “Here,” Lena murmured, picking up Kara’s hand and setting the quill in it, curling her fingers around the feather.

 

            Kara’s fist tightened around it and she gave Lena a wary look, doubt and a prickle of surprise visible there. Her mouth thinned and the corners and she blinked rapidly, the glassy look dissipating as she hung her head and drew the blanket closer around herself, sniffing.

 

            “Thank you,” Kara lightly replied, her voice a sigh of relief.

 

            Lips twitching ruefully, a bright gleam in her eyes, Lena shrugged. “It’s nothing to me. Take it; it doesn’t matter.”

 

            The lie sat in her throat, her chest heavy with the weight of it as she feigned nonchalance, but Lena felt the jolt of panic in her stomach as the crutch of familiarity the quill brought her in moments of deserved penance and punishment was taken away from her. And all the while Kara thought she was helping her but Lena a cold panic settle in as she wondered how difficult it would really be to let go of the quill that had marked her so irrevocably that even if the scar was removed from her skin, the deeper, psychological ones would have remained. 

 

            Meeting Kara’s eyes, she gave her a wavering smile of forced levity and reached out to quickly squeeze her arm, turning away before the impulse to snatch back the quill overwhelmed her. “Let’s have some breakfast.”

Chapter 33

            Lena turned twenty-six a month later, things seeming to settle down somewhat after an anxiety-fuelled month of pissing off her mother, successfully brewing the Wolfsbane Potion and getting used to things with Kara while keeping it a secret from her friends. Of course, they’d lasted a lot longer in the past but it felt different this time. 

 

            There was none of that obstinate determination to keep each other at arm’s length out of fear of where it would lead. There was none of that worry about being found out by Kara’s friends and only a mild interest on Lena’s part in keeping it under wraps for now. Before they’d been holed up in Lena’s flat, or at Hogwarts they’d relied on their secret room or Polyjuice Potion to visit Madam Puddifoot’s but this time it felt more relaxed, more natural. 

 

            One Sunday, they walked through Carkitt Market and toured the Museum of Muggle Curiosities before visiting Sugarplum’s Sweet Shop to sate Kara’s sweet tooth. Kara managed to convince her to go to a Quidditch match one Thursday night with her sister and friends, and while Lena had barely a speck of interest in the sport - most of which had come from watching Kara’s matches at Hogwarts - she found herself sipping hot Butterbeer in the stands of a pitch as the wind bit her cheeks and the roar of the crowd washed over her. There had been dinner at Lena’s, and breakfast at The Hopping Pot, which they both agreed was safer than at The Leaky Cauldron, although they had gone there for drinks with Sam last Friday. 

 

            Of course, Lena was well-versed in a good social and dating life, events and evenings with Jack and her friends were spent doing much the same, but it was different with Kara. It had always been different with Kara. They could spend the entire day together, waking up in Lena’s bed after Kara had spent the night, eating breakfast, doing laundry and dishes and showering together, Kara donning Lena’s clothes that were slightly too short as she reminisced about growing up too poor for well-fitting clothes, heading out to do something together, anything together, and then not wanting her to leave when they made it back to her flat. Lena loved to be alone, had been someone who craved her privacy, so much so that she would never let Jack spend the night at her place, would never shower with him, where he could see her scarred arm, would never invite him in to stay. So many things were different in the little nuances of the mundane things they did together that Lena felt, for perhaps the first time in her life, that she was genuinely and truly happy.

 

            She was working on her birthday, a thirty-hour shift that had her at St. Mungo’s by lunch the day before and clocking out late after a last-minute emergency saw a woman who’d tried to give herself wings come in covered in feathers. It was a painstaking process to remove them all and then reverse the damage to her hollowed bones before Lena was freed just before midnight, almost forgetting it was her birthday until she stepped through the front door of her flat and caught sight of Kara asleep at the kitchen table. She should have been home hours before, just in time for dinner, and Lena felt something in her chest cave slightly at the sight of her girlfriend, blonde head pillowed by her arms with a little iced cake studded with candles beside a bottle of elderflower wine - her favourite - with a label Lena knew Kara couldn’t have afforded and a few wrapped gifts. If it had been within her, she might have cried at how touched she was.

 

            Quietly slipping further inside, setting down her bag and shedding her cloak, Lena crept over to her side and laid a hand against Kara’s back. The full moon was tomorrow and Kara looked peaky, even in sleep, with lavender bruises beneath her eyes as she breathed through parted lips. Lena hated to wake her but wouldn’t leave Kara there all night, and knew Kara would probably be upset to have fallen asleep, even though Lena knew she needed her rest to make it through the exhaustion of tomorrow. 

 

            “Hey,” she murmured, trying not to startle Kara too much.

 

            Jolting away, Kara reared her head, blinking owlishly as she straightened, confused for a moment as she straightened her wonky glasses. Looking bleary-eyed at the table in front of her, she looked up at Lena and then shot to her feet, raking back her messy curls.

 

            “Oh, I- you’re home! Happy birthday.”

 

            A sweet smile creased Lena’s exhausted face as she leaned in to kiss Kara. “Thank you. I’m sorry I’m so late.”

 

            “What time is it?” Kara hoarsely asked, glancing down at her watch as she answered her own question. “Oh. Oh, no. I was going to cook you dinner!”

 

            “It’s alright. You look tired; you should go to bed.”

 

            “I- but your presents . Oh, no, you must be so tired; it can wait until the morning. But the cake! Did you eat?”

 

            Trying not to laugh, Lena smiled crookedly, “I had a pumpkin pasty from the tea shop earlier and split an apple danish with Sam so I’m okay. Go to bed, I’ll be in soon, I just want to shower first.”

 

            “You’re not going straight to bed? Okay, good, great, you still have … thirty-two minutes of your birthday left so … you shower and I’ll make you something to eat. Shit, the wine. Never mind, we can have tea instead.”

 

            Giving in to her laughter, Lena cupped Kara’s face in her hands and kissed her firmly as she cut off her muttered curses at the foiled birthday plans. Murmuring she’d be right back, Lena vanished into her bathroom and made her shower quick, not wanting to waste the remainder of her birthday beneath the hot water, no matter how good it felt against her knotted muscles. 

 

            Emerging soft and pink-cheeked, wet hair dampening the back of her clean shirt as the smell of sandalwood and ylang-ylang enveloped her, Lena walked back out to the open flat and paused as Kara swept a hand over the cake and lit the candles. Her smile was hopeful as she shifted impatiently, so much of the childish warmth that Lena had first fallen in love with shining through.

 

            “Happy birthday!”

 

            A smile grew on Lena’s face and she walked over to the table as Kara’s arms slid around her, a kiss pressed to the side of her head before her girlfriend murmured in her wet hair. “Make a wish.”

 

            So naturally, Lena wished for a cure as she blew out the candles and then folded herself onto a chair, knees drawn to her chest as Kara nudged a plate with a sandwich and crisps towards her and set about cutting slices of the cake. Obediently wolfing down the quick dinner, Lena couldn’t help but marvel at the difference between her birthday last year, or all the years of her childhood, to this one. Lillian had mostly ignored her, although Lex had still cared about her enough to get her gifts, and last year Jack had taken her out for dinner at a posh Muggle restaurant with a little black box that had momentarily filled Lena with dread until it had revealed a pair of diamond earrings inside. This year, she’d worked a knackering shift and came home to a mere handful of minutes with her girlfriend, who’d fallen asleep waiting for her and made her a sandwich and a little cake. Lena knew which one she preferred. 

 

            Saving the wine for their next dinner, Kara pushed a cup of tea towards Lena with the slice of cake and then cleared her throat as she gestured to the presents. “If you want to open them in the morning, that’s fine.”

 

            “I’ll open them now,” Lena quietly insisted as she smiled, setting down the second half of her sandwich and wiping off her fingers as the first one was set down before her.

 

            Opening the brown paper, Lena found herself holding a deep green sweater with a roll neck and sleeves that ballooned ever so slightly and she let out a quick laugh. “Did you take up knitting recently?”

 

            “Me? No. That one is from my mum.”

 

            Pausing, Lena gave Kara a wary look as she held the sweater up. “Eliza made me … a present?”

 

            “Yeah, well, she didn’t know what to get you and she likes knitting. Um … I know it’s not expensive but, you know, it’s your birthday. She wanted to give you a present.”

 

            Throat closing up, Lena’s smile wavered a fraction. It was more than she’d gotten in years. “That’s really thoughtful,” she whispered.

 

            Wrinkling her nose as she smiled quickly, Kara nudged another one towards her. “From Alex and Kelly. I was pretty confident you didn’t already have it.”

 

            Even more surprised to receive a gift from Kara’s sister, Lena opened it up to reveal a new book about potions and smiled with delight. “I don’t. I’ll have to send them all a letter to say thank you.”

 

            “And these two are from me,” Kara said, nudging the last two closer. “It’s not much …”

 

            “It’s from you,” Lena softly replied, all the explanation she had to give to make her meaning known.

 

            The first one was a new pair of dragonhide gloves for work and the second was tickets to see Spellbound, the all-witch group they sometimes listened to over breakfast in the mornings on the radio in the kitchen. Delighted by the gifts and promising to book time off for the concert, which wasn’t until next month, Lena kissed Kara and thanked her earnestly before they ate their slices of cake and sipped their tea.

 

            They didn’t stay up long and Lena was tucked in bed beside Kara’s warmth before the clock hit midnight, a sense of peace in her chest as she breathed in the smell of Kara’s laundry detergent clinging to the pilled cotton top she was wearing. It was the best birthday Lena could ever remember having.

 

            She woke late the next morning to her girlfriend curled in on herself with a pinched, grey look on her sleeping face, no relief found there as the full moon that night loomed closer by the hour. Lena had been rostered on but convinced Sam to switch with her, and let Kara sleep, knowing she should’ve been catching up on sleep as well. Eyes prickling from exhaustion, knowing she’d be in for a long, sleepless night ahead as well, Lena pushed through it as she checked her vials of the Wolfsbane potion stored away for Kara’s use and then checked the latest batch she was brewing, trying to store as much as possible, just in case. 

 

            It was past twelve when she started to make lunch for them both, three cups of coffee into her day in short order and craving something more nutritious. She chopped fruit into a bowl and then settled on BLTs, all she could make with the dwindling food supplies in her fridge after a long week of work, and she felt bad waking Kara up but knew she’d need to eat to have her strength for that evening. Even though they’d found a way to let her sleep through the duration of the full moon, the transformation itself would take a lot out of her, sapping her strength.

 

            Blearily rising from the bed, thick blankets hugged to her chest, Kara squinted through her poor vision until she found her glasses, expression softening with a tender smile. “Good morning.”

 

            “Morning,” Lena murmured.

 

            Kneeling on the edge of the bed, she precariously held a cup of coffee over the mattress with lunch in her other hand. She kissed her softly and pulled back, setting the plate in Kara’s lap and then pressing the back of her cool fingers to Kara’s clammy brow. Mouth thinning, Lena held her hands out for her own plate to carefully drift itself down to her lap and made herself comfortable beside her girlfriend.

 

            “Thank you,” Kara mumbled, her voice thick with sleep as she nudged her glasses up to rub her eyes. “What time is it?”

 

            “Almost one.”

 

            “In the afternoon?”

 

            “Mm, I thought I’d better wake you up so you can eat.” 

 

            Kara had told her mother she’d be staying at Lena’s and then going straight to St. Mungo’s for the trial, the white lie a small thing for the sake of avoiding any further worried lectures from family and friends, so they had the afternoon to themselves. Eating lunch, they both showered and Lena put on her new knitted jumper with unspoken delight, feeding that childish part of her soul that had never had a mother with an ounce of maternal instinct to knit her a sweater. As Kara’s pallor whitened and her restless agitation grew more prominent through the afternoon, Lena tried to distract her with her old family Wizard’s Chess set displayed on the coffee table, playing back and forth as they’d used to as kids while they drank tea and kept eyeing their watches.

 

            Eventually, they unspokenly started resetting the board mid-game and Lena fetched Kara’s last dose and cooked dinner for her before letting Morrigan out into the late afternoon. Watching her owl swoop through the grey skies over Dublin, she felt that old sadness at the approaching full moon, an oppressive presence in their lives that neither of them had been able to escape, even when years and continents had separated them. How often Lena had watched it rise from that very window, old hurt and anger balled up into a knot of frustration and pity for her best friend. 

 

            Prepping her office, Lena left Kara on the sofa to steel herself for the familiar pain of the transformation and then warily stepped back out, softly clearing her throat as she intruded on her girlfriend’s thoughts. Glancing over the back of the sofa, Kara pushed herself to her feet, a tremor to her hands as she buried them in her pockets and walked over to her.

 

            “Ready?” Lena unevenly asked.

 

            Giving her a tight smile as she nodded, Kara stepped into the room and started to undress, Lena putting her glasses and wand safely away for her, prepping a blanket and murmuring for Kara to come closer as she set a fresh page down. Dipping a quill in ink, Lena made a few notes on what she already knew and then checked Kara’s pulse, eyes, lymph nodes and lungs before neatly tidying it all away. 

 

            Smiling thinly, a lump caught in her throat, Lena cupped Kara’s cheek briefly, her green eyes tense with worry. “I’ll be right outside, okay?”

 

            “Don’t look,” Kara echoed her usual order.

 

            Nodding, Lena gave her a quick kiss and touched their foreheads together before taking her leave. Locking and warding the door, she hovered outside until she could hear the cries of pain, making herself endure the sounds of it as she knew she’d never be able to understand the real pain of her body splitting apart and reforming into something else. No matter what her brother and mother had done to her, it wouldn’t be the same as that.

 

            Once the faint, whining pants behind the closed door drifted off into silence, Lena felt some of the tension bleed out of her. Settling in for a long night, she made a cup of tea and turned on the radio as she picked up her new book from Alex and Kelly, trying to occupy herself as she kept her vigil. 

 

            It was a long night, made longer by her late shift the night before, and Lena held out until midnight before drinking down a potion to stave off the urge to sleep. Feeling a farce of energy rush through her, the gritty burning of her eyes alleviated, and she was able to push through until sunrise. The full moon in the colder months was made worse with the duration of the transformation, a few precious extra hours given over to the risen moon and the wolf as the sun set early and rose late. As the grey dawn washed the apartment in its dismal colour, it was a moment of relief, if not quite happiness, for Lena though, the full moon was over for another month.

 

            She heard the sounds of Kara’s wolfish sounds of pain turn back into the human gasps of agony before she fell silent again and only then did Lena open the office door, once she was sure. Sprawled face-down on the carpet, Kara was breathing raggedly, a cold sweat covering her bare skin, and Lena hurried over to her side, sinking to her knees as she pressed her fingers to Kara’s neck, watching her eyelashes flutter as her pulse jumped.

            

            Making a low sound at the back of her throat, Kara tried to push herself up and Lena’s hands fluttered nervously around her. “Easy. Go slowly.”

 

            Helping her into a sitting position, Lena draped the blanket around her shoulders, fetched her glasses and a Reinvigoration Draught. Once she’d had a few minutes to gather herself, Kara gave Lena a thin smile, her shoulders slumped beneath the blanket she held closed at the front.

 

            “The same as last time,” Kara confirmed for her without being asked.

 

            Lips twitching with a faint smile in response, Lena kissed her forehead. “You did very well.”

 

            She went to run a bath after that and couldn’t think further than cereal for breakfast, finding herself spooning Cheeri-Owl’s into her mouth from the bathroom floor as Kara lounged in the hot water, bubbles piled up past the rim. Sipping coffee in between mouthfuls, Lena dwelled in companionable silence and found it a familiar balm to her crowded thoughts, as Kara’s presence had always been in their room in the Astronomy Tower. 

 

            Kara left before lunch, needing to go home to see Eliza before her mother worried too much and tried to track her down at St. Mungo’s, and Lena was left to make a half-hearted attempt at tidying up her flat before she went to bed. It was almost dinner time when Lena was roused prematurely from her sleep, a muffled knock at the front door leaving her irate as she dragged herself out of bed, wand in hand with the urge to hex whoever it was into the following week for disturbing her when she had a shift starting at midnight. A short shift, only twelve hours if no emergencies occurred, but Lena was tired enough as it was.

 

            Yanking open the front door, she blinked at the sight of Andrea and then frowned, smoothing down her dark hair. “Oh. It’s you.”

 

            “Happy belated Birthday,” Andrea greeted her, rolling her eyes and tossing her a wrapped gift. “You never answered my letter about drinks so I took the liberty of coming to collect you myself.”

 

            Scrambling to catch up as she stumbled back or else risked getting bowled over by her friend, who forged her way into the flat with the assurance of someone who was always welcomed everywhere, Lena opened and closed her mouth. “Um, drinks? Now? I have work later.”

 

            “Alright, well, that gives us a few hours at least. Come on, get dressed.”

 

            Heaving a silent sigh, Lena shut herself in her bathroom and was hasty, not wanting to leave Andrea alone with her things for too long - she wasn’t nosy, per se, but she had a wandering eye and was too clever to miss a trick - and dressed in dark, comfortable clothes, packing her bag for work as well. Emerging somewhat put together, Lena opened the gift and found a pair of small gold hoops inside, giving her friend a quick hug before putting them on and ushering her out of the flat.

 

            Andrea grabbed Lena’s arm on the landing and let her Apparate them there, her focused mind always guiding them true, and they were standing in the light drizzle of Knockturn Alley a moment later. Cursing the dismal weather, they ducked into The White Wyvern and Lena saw her friends already gathered at their usual table, with Veronica pouring a round at the bar. At the sight of Lena, they all happily wished her a happy birthday and she was gifted a bottle of Firewhisky by Veronica, who gave her a quick wink, having stolen it from behind the bar, before they settled in with their drinks.

 

            Keeping one eye on the time, Lena drank her elderflower wine slowly, knowing that even by curing her inebriation with a potion, she’d be left feeling woollen-headed and limp and that was less than ideal for a shift starting at midnight. Still, she was never one to sour a party’s mood and accepted any drinks presented to her until their gossip and conversation lulled slightly and Gayle seized her opportunity, rummaging around in her handbag.

 

            “I got this when I was in Romania,” Gayle announced, setting a squat candle in the middle of the round table with a sharp smile on her face. “Who feels like a drinking game to celebrate the birthday girl?”

 

            There was a chorus of agreement, everyone shuffling their chairs around the table so they were evenly spaced. Lighting the candle with a lazy click of her fingers, Gayle’s smile widened in the dim lighting of The White Wyvern, her blue eyes shining with delight as she sent Veronica off in search of a bottle of Firewhisky from behind the bar.

 

            Once they were all seated, Gayle lit a cigarette and passed more around to Andrea, Veronica and Jack, a writhing cloud of multi-hued smoke creating a haze above their heads. Exhaling purple, Gayle cleared her throat.

 

            “The rules are everyone puts their hands over the candle and someone says something they’ve never done. If you haven’t, nothing happens but if you have the candle burns you. And then you have to take a shot. Put your hands out; I’ll go first.”

 

            They all obeyed, some with apprehension, their arms extended until their fingertips were within the radius of the candle’s flame. With a quick wink, Gayle smiled around her cigarette.

 

            “Never have I ever dated anyone at this table.”

 

            Lena’s fingers felt a searing pain as she quickly snatched them back, her lips parting as she sucked in a sharp breath, expression quickly furrowing with annoyance. There were similar reactions of pain and cursing as everyone but Gayle and William snatched their hands back, fingertips red for a brief moment before the pain receded and they all laughed uneasily, draining their shots of Firewhisky with exasperated amusement.

 

            Putting their hands back in, it was Andrea’s turn as she considered her statement for a second. “Never have I ever had my heart broken.”

 

            Feeling her cheeks heat as Lena flinched again at the renewed pain, and a prickle of guilt as Jack likewise jerked his hand back, Lena felt the pointed glances and curiosity as her friends tried to piece it together. Had Lena broken her own heart when she’d dumped Jack or was it a throwback to their Hogwarts days and her fling with Andrea? As it was, they were the only two to drink that round and then it was Lena’s turn.

 

            “Never have I ever cheated on a test.”

 

            Lena, Russell and William were the only ones spared that round with mockery sent their way at their good behaviour, although there was an appreciative air of surprise when Lena got burnt and had to drink over theft. They pestered each other with questions over the surprising ones until answers satisfied their curiosity and they moved on. 

 

            They went around and around, laughing as they tried to think of something that would catch the most of them at once, with William in the lead, having never kissed anyone at the table, while the rest of them had individually kissed almost everyone present. Their fingertips tingled with white-hot pain each time, quickly fading with no lingering injury but it was too uncomfortably close to the effects of the blood quill for Lena’s liking as she endured it, the Firewhisky taking the edge off as the game progressed.

 

            It was a game that was perfect for the cunning minds of the Slytherins present, enjoying the competitive edge as they laughed and snidely made each other divulge little secrets, admit to embarrassing acts and confess to hidden feelings. It was all in good humour until it was Veronica’s third turn and her eyes slid to Lena for a brief moment in a seemingly innocuous glance.

 

            “Hm, let’s see,” Veronica hummed, tapping her chin as she stared up at the ceiling of the pub, candles flickering in the cobwebbed chandelier overhead before she lowered her shrewd gaze and smiled slyly. “Never have I ever fucked a werewolf.”

 

            William scoffed and hunched his broad shoulders, his face ruddy with drink and a wave of embarrassment as he hissed and jerked his hand back, rolling his eyes good-naturedly at the teasing. “Alright, you’ve got me,” he ruefully grumbled before knocking back the Firewhisky.

 

            Lena’s stomach had twisted at the question and she felt her fingertips prickle with pain, shifting her hand away slightly before she held fast, stubbornly determined to not give herself away. Her palms went clammy as she kept her expression impassive, toying with the shot in front of her with her free hand as she tried to stifle the urge to let out a hiss of pain, her fingertips angrily reddening as she kept them near the candle flame. 

 

            “Lena?” Veronica coyly singled her out, arching an eyebrow. “Was that a flinch I saw?”

 

            “Don’t be a cunt,” Lena snapped, her face bone white and hard. 

 

            Eyebrows rising in surprise, Andrea let out a huff of laughter. “That’s a bit harsh, darling.”

 

            Shoulders taut and a stubborn set to her jaw, her mouth pressed into a flat line, Lena could practically feel the blisters forming as she swallowed thickly. “Let’s keep playing,” she ground out through her teeth, feeling a hot flush sweep through her.

 

            Cocking her head to the side, Veronica’s stare was dangerously amused. “No, not yet,” she mused, her smile growing, “hang on a second.”

 

            Eyes widening a fraction as she sharply looked at her friend, Lena’s heart pounded, her skin prickling with sweat as she felt it dampen her lower back, her neck, her hairline, a tightness in her chest as panic settled in and the pain grew more intense. This wasn’t the way it was supposed to come out, some shameful secret burnt out of her to be made a mockery of by her friends, who were too judgemental by half to even consider it was something more meaningful than a dirty joke. It wasn’t that she was embarrassed but rather that Lena resented the way they would try to make her feel that way, as if she should have been.

 

            The table was tense, exchanging glances of unease and confusion as smiles wavered. Lasting a minute longer, Lena let out a small gasp of pain and tore her hand away, cradling it as she looked at the bubbling tips, red raw and weeping. Head hanging, Lena closed her eyes as she stiffly endured the feeling of all eyes trained on her, the humour of the game chased away by the discomfort and surprise of the stand-off between the two witches.

 

            Draping her arm over the back of her chair, Veronica let out a small laugh, looking smug as she drawled, “I thought that was you and that mousy little Hufflepuff getting cosy at The Leaky Cauldron last Friday night.”

 

            Eyes snapping open, Lena’s eyes were a hard green, anger flushing her pallid cheeks pink, too much to drink and that shaky nervousness in her stomach making her feel nauseous. She managed to swallow, a sneer twisting her lips as stewed in the sourness of being called out in such a manner.

 

            “Aren’t you the clever one,” Lena derisively retorted. 

 

            “Wait, you and- you and Kara?” Andrea asked.

 

            Russell let out a quick laugh, disbelieving as he grinned, “you’re joking.”

 

            Lips twitching at the corners, Lena offered no other response as she stared down at her fingertips and watched the blisters slowly start to heal as the magic of the candle faded. Reaching out, Gayle clamped thumb and forefinger over the flickering flame, sensing the game was at an end. 

 

            “I fucking told you something was going on,” William scathingly exclaimed, mouth twisting contemptuously. “Her and that fucking diary .”

 

            Laughing, he drained his pint and set it down hard, muscle working in his jaw as he stared daggers at Lena and clapped Jack on the shoulder, forcing a crooked grin to his face. “Cuckolded with a werewolf. That’s rough, mate.”

 

            Wounded pain flickered in Jack’s eyes as he gave Lena an accusing look of betrayal. Even though she knew what William said wasn’t true, guilt flashed through her and she felt her cheeks redden at the accusation. 

 

            “William, would you ever just fuck off,” Lena snapped, arms coming unfolded as she straightened, bristling.

 

            “Is it true?” Jack asked, his voice soft and hesitant.

 

            Scoffing, Lena tossed her dark hair, bristling haughtily. “No, I never cheated on you.”

 

            “Is it true about you and Kara?” he pressed and Lena’s sheepishly downcast eyes answered for her. “You’re fucking unbelievable, you know that?”

 

            “Jack,” Lena heavily sighed as he pushed his chair back and climbed to his feet.

 

            Closing her eyes as she exhaled sharply through her nose, Lena’s mouth thinned. Hesitating momentarily, she shot to her feet, jaw clenched as she gave the table a scathingly dismissive look, ignoring the looks of delightfully scandalised amusement, and stormed after her ex. 

 

            Pushing out the stiff front door of the pub, Lena pulled up short at the sight of Jack standing in the shelter of the stoop, shoulders hunched as he seethed, trying to pummel his hurt feelings down to nothing. It was raining steadily, a damp night that made the uneven streets of Knockturn Alley flood. Letting loose a weary sigh, Lena rubbed her forehead and then drew the folds of her cloak tighter against the chill.

 

            “It’s not what you think.”

 

            “What else am I supposed to think?”

 

            Shrugging indifferently, Lena gave him a hawkish look of firm insistence. “That I moved on. Just because you don’t like it doesn’t mean it’s wrong.”

 

            “Am I not allowed to have my own feelings on the matter? Am I not allowed this one fucking thing? It’s fine for you to be so- so blasé about the whole thing but what about how I feel?”

 

            Sharp features turning severe as Lena angrily brushed her hair out of her face, subjected to the rain as the wind blew it under the narrow doorstep they crowded under, she scoffed. “What, you’re mad at me for going out with someone else? What did you think would happen? I’d become a spinster without you?”

 

            “I’m mad at you for lying to me. I asked you if there was something else going on between the two of you and you lied to my face.”

 

            “I told you the truth,” Lena ground out. “We weren’t even friends . We were friends for a long time but we fell out.”

 

            “Bullshit.”

 

            Gesturing helplessly, Lena huffed impatiently. “Fine, you want the whole truth? We slept together years ago, in between you and me-”

 

            “Oh. Is that what you’re doing? Bouncing back and forth depending on your mood? Or do you just shag whoever’s giving you attention when you’re desperate for it and then toss them aside when it suits you? Grow the fuck up, Lena.”

 

            “Don’t you fucking dare,” she snapped back. “You don’t know the first thing about me and her.”

 

            He spread his arms and shrugged helplessly. “You’re right, I don’t know you. You wouldn’t let me. All I tried to do was love you and you strung me along.”

 

            “I was honest from the start. What did you expect? That I’d have a change of heart? That I’d become this- this warm person who would dote on you, give up my career to be a loving wife and mother?”

 

            “I thought maybe you’d at least love me. Even a little. But you never did, right? Be honest with me; when you ended things with me, and you said it’s because you didn’t love me anymore … did you ever love me?”
