            “No, it was by itself. Maybe it’s inside.”

            

            “No, nothing inside. Blimey, that’s a lot.”

 

            Leaning in, Alex caught a glimpse of all of the gold inside the purse and took it from Kelly, shaking them out. “Is someone having a laugh? I bet that was Winn with some leprechaun gold.”

 

            “Can’t be. That only lasts for a few hours; it’s been at least a whole day since this was given to us.”

 

            “Twenty galleons,” Alex stressed, counting them back into the purse, looking confused. “Do you think this is from everyone?”

 

            “It can’t be; the rest of these have cards and tags.”

 

            “Well … I guess the honeymoon’s sorted.”

 

            Silent as she took another bite of her sandwich, Lena patiently sat through the rest of the gifts and accepted a slice of leftover cake with some tea, migrating to the kitchen to help as Alex and Kelly tidied up. Sitting at the kitchen table, Lena scooped some cake into her mouth and watched as Eliza left the room to take some in to the couple, allowing Kara to drag out a chair perpendicular to Lena and give her a searching look.

 

            “I know it was you.”

 

            “What was me?” Lena coyly asked.

 

            Mouth thinning exasperatedly, Kara rolled her eyes. “I’m not stupid; none of their friends are that rich. It was very generous of you but it’s a lot of money.”

 

            Opening her mouth to quickly retort, Lena thought better of it and snapped her mouth shut again. Looking down at her plate, she spooned another mouthful of cake up and met Kara’s gaze again.

 

            “Go on, say it,” Kara coaxed her with a wry smile.

 

            Softly sighing, Lena grimaced. “It’s not for me.”

 

            She ate her spoonful of cake and chewed slowly as Kara nodded, leaning back in her chair, her expression looking a little chalky as she raked a hand through her curls. “It’s more than I make in a week.”

 

            Wincing slightly, Lena shrugged nonchalantly and fiddled with her spoon. “They deserve a nice honeymoon.”

 

            “They do. I just- it’s a lot of money.”

 

            “It’s okay. They don’t have to know it was from me.”

 

            “I’m going to guess that you’d prefer it that way, otherwise you would have written a note,” Kara said with a wry smile. 

 

            Shrugging again, Lena returned the smile. “Naturally.”

 

            Sighing, Kara gave her a small smile. “Thank you.”

 

            “I didn’t do it for you.”

 

            “I know. Still, she’s my sister and … she’s prickly and a bit of an arse sometimes, so I don’t think she entirely deserves how kind you are.”

 

            “Ah, well, something about Danvers women, is there?” Lena retorted, arching an eyebrow.

 

            “Unfortunately.”

 

            “She’s never been rude to me, just in case you’re curious. I treated her fairly often before she knew about us and she was always polite. Very grateful.”

 

            “You were healing her; if she’d been anything less than grateful, I would have cursed her for you.”

 

            Lena let out a huff of laughter and took a sip of her tea. “Well, for what it’s worth, the two of them have been very welcoming. It’s nice. I mean … your family is so normal . I like them.”

 

            “They like you too.”

 

            Humming dubiously, Lena watched as Kara opened her mouth to quickly assure her she was telling the truth, watching understanding cross her girlfriend’s face when she realised Lena was teasing her. Mouth closing, Kara gave her an exasperated look and Lena winked before draining her tea and giving Kara the rest of her cake.

 

            “I need to get going.”

 

            “Alright. I’ll see you on Wednesday?”

 

            “Mhm. Make sure you take the rest of your doses.”

 

            “Yes, Healer Luthor,” Kara lightly replied, her voice teasing as she scooped up the last bite of cake.

 

            She followed Lena to the front door, pausing as Lena called goodbye to everyone, telling Alex and Kelly to have fun on their trip, promising Eliza she’d come for dinner soon, and then Kara kissed her goodbye on the doorstep and Lena Apparated home. Unpacking her bag, Lena did some washing and walked through Dublin, using Muggle money to buy some groceries and going through the motions of cleaning and tidying up in anticipation of work the next two days.

 

            Her shift the next day started at eight which allowed Lena to have an early night with a decent lie-in, prepping her meals and making sure Morrigan had enough food and water before she crashed into bed, catching up on lost sleep. She was originally rostered on for the full moon but Sam had switched with her without explanation so Lena was left with a double, gratefully snapping up the long shift so long as it meant she would be able to keep Kara company on Wednesday.

 

            Work was a blur, debriding wounds, wearily lecturing familiar patients about their repeated idiocy, her neck and shoulders aching after what seemed to be endless hours in a theatre, charming organs and muscles back into place, stifling curses as much as she could, losing one man who’d fallen off his broom over Leeds and had so many broken bones and so much internal bleeding from the impact that it was a miracle he’d made it to St. Mungo’s still alive. There were hours supervising her Residents, who in turn were supervising the Interns, and she caught snatches of sleep where she could, the cryptex burning in her pocket as she was paged over and over to assist with small emergencies that overwhelmed the Residents. 

 

            Finishing her shift early hours of Wednesday morning, Lena went home and slept into the afternoon, waking up shortly before Kara would arrive after work and preparing dinner. She kept it simple, knowing Kara would be feeling a little queasy, and when her girlfriend knocked on the door, Lena grimaced at the waxy sheen to Kara’s face, her skin sallow, eyes ringed with dark circles.

 

            They ate dinner together and Lena tidied up as Kara went through the motions of undressing and putting her things safely away. Lena had already secured the office as usual but they were both ignorant of the fact that Kara had technically skipped a dose, having it past midnight, two doses in one day. From their trial, Lena knew it had to be one a day for a week, no more, no less, or else it negated the potion entirely. Neither of them was aware that anything was amiss though, and when Lena left her in the office with a parting kiss, she warded the doors as usual, a little half-heartedly now, confident in the Wolfsbane Potion, and that was one of her oversights.

 

            It all felt so rote now, following the same routine they had for months. Lena locked her in the office, as usual, set the kettle on to boil over the stove for coffee to keep her awake, the same as always, and had her chosen book already on the coffee table for her to whittle away at throughout the night. It was like any other full moon, waiting for the beginning of the transformation to start, to feel that reassurance that her potion worked, that Kara was okay. Only, this time it was different.

 

            She wasn’t sure at what point she realised something had gone awry, only that Kara’s choked, human gasps gave way to the wolfish whimpers of pain and didn’t fall into silence. There was a yelp and then a low growl and Lena listened to the growl roll into a snarl as she wondered if perhaps it had hurt more than usual. There was a lot of thumping around and maybe Kara had bumped into the desk chair or the walls of shelving while writhing about, dislodging a few books in the process. 

 

            Then there was a hair-raising howl, the sound lilting and chilling as Lena realised there was something wrong. Kara never made a sound normally, not beyond the inescapable gasps and whines of pain as she was ripped apart and put back together. Mouth dry, heart beating rapidly in her chest, Lena inched closer to the door, laying her hand against the cool wood.

 

            “Kara?” she softly called out.

 

            The door shuddered in its frame a moment later, the heavy crash of the werewolf’s impact, making Lena jump back, heart going haywire. Mind scrambling for where she’d fucked up, what part of the potion she’d brewed incorrectly, Lena felt pale and faint with worry. All of her supplies were in that office, all of the potions and gauze and bandages, her Dittany and silver. If what she feared was true and Kara didn’t have her own mind, she would carve herself up over the course of the evening and Lena wouldn’t even have the ability to heal her. 

 

            Her hand shook as she pulled out her wand, realising the severity of their situation and how her reckless arrogance had led them here. Lena had thought her potion was perfect, taking so much pride in her skill, and doing what she had to in order to protect Kara. The door shuddered again and the kettle started to whistle, and Lena silently cursed herself as she listened to the following sounds of destruction. The unmistakable sounds of breaking glass, shredding paper, splintering wood. It filled the heavy silence of the evening as Lena listened, standing in the middle of the flat with a slack look of shock on her face, unable to bring herself to move. 

 

            She didn’t move even when the kettle boiled itself dry, the sounds of pain and anguish from the werewolf locked behind the door keeping her rooted to the spot as she envisioned Kara tearing herself to bits, hot blood splattering everywhere. It wasn’t until the door shuddered again that Lena was startled into motion. The door was warded, of course, the hinges tightened, the wood reinforced, and she had to force herself to turn her back on it, turning off the stove, the shrieking whistle slowly dying down, running a hand through her hair and over her grey face as she listened to the sounds. The door muffled it but she still heard everything, all the snarls, yelps of pain, whimpers and growls. 

 

            It made Lena feel sick, her breaths shallow and quick as the realisation that she had failed, failed to keep Kara safe, even from herself, crept up on her. Barging into the bathroom, Lena gripped the edge of the porcelain sink and stared at the clammy, pale reflection in the mirror before her stomach turned and she vomited into the sink. Coughing at the sour bile that lingered, Lena rinsed her mouth out with water from the tap, her teeth aching from the intensity of the cold, and she splashed it on her face as well, her breaths still shallow and quick as she listened to the sound of Kara on the opposite side of the wall.

 

            Reemerging, Lena hovered outside the closed office door and bit her fingernails as she anxiously felt the endless hours still ahead of them. How much blood could Kara stand to lose without a Blood Replenishing potion ready for her the next morning? Lena had only ever treated her the next morning after a night in the cells, with nothing to create additional injuries to Kara’s own claws and repeated collisions with the thick stone walls of the dungeons. Had she gotten glass into her cuts? Had she ingested any of the poisonous plants Lena kept stored in labelled jars? It made her sick with worry.

 

            And then, of course, there was the relentlessness of Kara’s mania in the throes of the full moon’s transformation. She couldn’t help herself, of course, that part of her shut away from her consciousness as the blind rage of the werewolf was let loose, the heavy, repetitive thuds of her body making the door shudder over and over again as her frustration built. She knew Lena was there, her sharp senses thanks to her Lycanthropy lending her the ability to hear her girlfriend’s heartbeat on the other side of the door, pumping blood through her body, the perfect prey if only she could get out of that office. Lena didn’t think she had any reason to worry for herself though, not until the door frame started to shudder as well, fine cracks radiating from it, paint flaking off, dust drifting down.

 

            A moment of fear cut through her concern for Kara and Lena swallowed thickly, trying to quickly figure out a solution. She wouldn’t be able to contain Kara once she was out of that room. Werewolves were notoriously hard to fight off at the best of times, let alone when it was a girlfriend you didn’t want to harm. Lena baulked at the prospect of hexing Kara, of hurting her any more than she was already hurting, knowing she wasn’t in control of herself, would never have hurt a hair on Lena’s head if she was herself. 

 

            But she couldn’t just stand there . The thought of being bitten knifed through Lena’s cool composure as she adjusted her grip on her wand, backing towards the bedroom door, two rooms away from the office. She could taste the lingering bile as she swallowed the lump in her throat, painfully forced down, her hand trembling as she nudged open the bedroom door with her foot. Eventually, Kara didn’t so much as break open the door as break the whole thing down, the frame pulling away from the wall with brick and plaster clinging to it, until there was a gap big enough for Kara to claw the rest of the way free, brittle cement giving way beneath the power of her paws and claws. 

 

            Lena knew she couldn’t afford to wait around for a glimpse of Kara, to gauge the threat, and her heart thudded loudly as the sound of her blood pumping through her practically deafened her. Her hand was clammy around her wand and Lena’s breath hitched in her throat at the shape that emerged from the office, a deep grey pelt illuminated by the moonlight, a long muzzle pulled back over teeth, the lupine form of her girlfriend on four paws and bristling with anger as she turned her attention to Lena. This was Kara’s worst nightmare, to have Lena see her like this, to be a threat to her, but Lena felt no revulsion, no horror at seeing what her girlfriend was. Only the raw cut of empathy and unbridled love, knowing she would rather cut out her own heart and hand it to Kara herself than ever let her think Lena would change how she felt.

 

            But still, Lena knew this wasn’t Kara in her right mind, that if she didn’t make her feet move she’d end up mauled at best, dead at worst. She moved quickly but the werewolf was quick too and as she started to close the door, Kara’s muzzle was already through and her guttural growl turned into a sharp yelp of pain as Lena slammed the door into her. Jerking back from the surprise of it, Kara snarled and Lena slammed the door shut, her heart thudding in her chest. 

 

            She didn’t have the time to ward the door properly, and even that wasn’t as effective as they’d assumed, and she glanced around her bedroom in a panic. Eyes landing on the window, Lena’s mouth thinned and she raised her wand, licking her lips as she verbally shouted the spell, no time to risk messing up a non-verbal one.

 

            “Bombarda!”

 

            Glass splintered outwards with half of the window frame and some of the brick too and Lena heard the door splintering down behind her. Glancing back over her shoulder, she was already tripping over her feet in her haste as she watched Kara force her way through. Tossing aside her wand, useless to her now, Lena launched herself up onto the dresser below the wide windows and scrabbled towards the empty frame she’d blasted open. Kara was quick on four legs though, bounding across Lena’s bed and throwing herself at Lena, who was ducking out the window.

 

            As Lena transformed into her Animagus form, still not quite skilled enough from her lack of practice to bring her clothes with her, she flapped around in the fabric for a second before tumbling off the windowsill. Wings flapping frantically, she managed a wobbly descent to the pavement below her apartment block, the nightlight of Dublin audible around her, Lena landed unsteadily and hopped on one foot, a dim recollection of fierce pain in the calf of her left leg. 

 

            The keening sound of the werewolf above cut through her thoughts and Lena flopped around on the pavement, anxious and panicked. She hated being in her Animagus form, the raven’s body so suited to flying, seeming like a sick joke when Lena hated heights so much, and she wasn’t very good at being a raven because of her usual refusal to transform. It had come in handy occasionally, especially when she’d spied as a bird once or twice, but Lena had never transformed frequently enough to master flying and keeping her belongings with her when she changed in the raven. Still, after a few minutes of flapping about as she hopped on one foot, she managed to flutter back up to the windowsill.

 

            The sight that beheld her was a sandy grey wolf tearing the mattress apart, full of so much rage that Lena knew it could only have come from the agony of being trapped inside that form. And still, she didn’t think Kara was a monster, something so otherworldly beautiful about the werewolf, slightly different from a regular wolf but with that same breathtaking quality to her. She was heartbreaking. But Kara’s destruction turned on herself a moment later as she staggered off the bed on all fours and dragged her claws down the wooden doors of Lena’s armoire before hunching over and digging into her own flesh. 

 

            Panic flashed through Lena and she cawed loudly in exclamation of concern, the sound sharp and wavering in the quiet of the flat. A pair of blue eyes turned to her and she ruffled her feathers, remembering that werewolves weren’t interested in harming animals and that she should be relatively safe in this form as she garnered the attention of the prowling werewolf. Remaining still on the ledge of the broken window, Lena watched as Kara came closer, front paws going onto the dresser as she hauled herself up on the mess of candles, photo frames and books that had been knocked aside in Lena’s swift exit, a splatter of blood amidst it all, and leaned closer, snuffling towards the bird.

 

            Lena let out a small caw this time, hopping a little closer and clicking her beak as she cocked her head to the side, green eyes curious amidst the agonised pity and worry. A low growl escaped the werewolf, almost a bark, bearing no animosity, and Lena ruffled her dark feathers as she stopped, eyeing Kara, who pressed a wet nose into a wing. Skittering away, Lena clicked her beak again and Kara let out a breathless whine, panting as she went back down onto all fours. Talons clacking across the wood as she made her way to the edge of the dresser, Lena looked down at Kara and then fluttered across to the bed unsteadily, landing on the mess of torn feathers and wool.

 

            Kara bounded after her, almost playful, almost puppy-like in her interest, enthralled by the appearance of the raven, the witch no longer existing in her mind. The rabid anger was diminished as well as she scrambled onto the bed, jostling it and the raven as Lena flapped around for balance, quickly fluttering off the bed and through the ruined bedroom door. The kitchen and living room were relatively untouched, save for claw marks outside the bedroom door and the ruins of brick, concrete, dust and splintered wood from her office. 

 

            Swooping up to the kitchen counter, Lena let out a soft caw as Kara followed and somehow a game of tag ensued, her girlfriend following her around the flat, gouging claw marks in leather as she clambered over the armchair, breaking a vase with the clatter of clay, knocking over the empty owl stand with Morrigan’s food and water, snorting at the face full of water that splashed over her snout. Lena had to keep moving, keep catching her attention with her low caws and flapping wings, chirping and hopping, or else Kara would lose interest and turn her attention back on herself or the rest of the apartment.

 

            Blood splattered Lena’s floorboards from various wounds she couldn’t see through the sandy grey pelt, and Kara ripped apart everything within sight as soon as her attention slipped away from the bird. At one point, Lena had to land on her head to stop her from chewing on a half-burnt candle, half a dozen books already gnawed on, pages strewn about the place, sofa cushions ripped open. It was a repetitive process but the alternative of leaving Kara to hurt herself kept Lena active all night, her left leg throbbing, eyelids growing heavier as she ruffled her feathers restlessly as she fought off the urge to sleep. Normally, she would have had a potion by now, drained from work and sleep-deprived, relying on the extra boost to get her over the edge of the full moon when she’d be able to sleep properly.

 

            It felt like an eternity before the moon started to sink towards the horizon, the faint glow of the sunrise cutting through the darkness of the pre-dawn grey. Kara was in the middle of playing with some of the stuffing from the sofa as Lena perched on the back of it when she stopped, shuddering as she let out a soft whine, fear pushing her muzzle back, baring her teeth, the transformation slowly stealing over her. She staggered around, falling until her belly was to the ground, the low keening of pain escaping her as she panted, hair vanishing, bones splitting apart and reforming, snout shrinking back into a human face. 

 

            Lena watched with horror and shock, transforming back into her human form and staggering towards the bedroom, scrambling over the torn sheets and frantically scrabbling through the mess as she searched for her wand. Her fingers brushed over smooth ivy and she pulled it out from beneath shards of glass and loose sheets of parchment and bolted to her feet, her left leg buckling slightly before she rushed out of the bedroom, stumbling out to the unconscious, bleeding form of her girlfriend. 

 

            Mind running too fast for her body, which was readjusting to having arms again instead of wings, Lena staggered to Kara’s side and dropped heavily to her knees. There were claw marks across Kara’s shoulder blade, bleeding freely down the notches of her spine and valley of her ribs as she breathed shallowly. Lena knew she wouldn’t be able to close them up without silver and Dittany but she needed to buy herself enough time to check on the state of her office, to figure out what to do without Kara bleeding out.

 

            “Ferula,” Lena shakily spoke, her wand unsteady in her hand as white bandages tightly bound Kara’s torso. 

 

            She carefully rolled her over, a dazed wisp of a groan slipping past Kara’s bloody lips as her eyelids fluttered. Lena prayed she’d stay asleep, taking in the gaping cuts on Kara’s stomach and lower ribs, bandaging them as well. There was a bite mark on her right arm as well, just before the bend of her elbow and Lena had to swallow past the lump lodged in her throat as she bound that too, trying to stamp down the nauseating worry, a thing she hadn’t felt firsthand since she’d stopped being allowed to treat Kara on the Dai Llewellyn Ward at St. Mungo’s. 

 

            Leaving her on the floor, Lena grabbed the tattered remains of a blanket and draped it over Kara to keep the chill off her and then one of the cushions that hadn’t been completely gutted, raising Kara’s head slightly and setting it down on the pillow. Climbing to her feet again, she walked over to the empty door frame of her office, stepped over the broken door, and took in the destruction. Only the books on the highest shelves had been spared Kara’s rampage, and the same went for the potion ingredients high up in the pigeonholes. Everything else was a mess of paper, parchment, leather, herbs, powders, liquids and animal parts mingling on the floor. There was an overturned cauldron with another batch of the Wolfsbane Potion she’d been brewing, along with the batch of Invigoration Draught she was brewing for them both as well, the two mixed together on the rug and slowly eating away at the fibres of it as the magic went awry.

 

            Lena’s bottle of Dittany was intact but the jar of silver was smashed on the floor, leaving her without any way to seal Kara’s wounds. She found a single intact vial of a Blood Replenishing potion, just enough for two units but better than nothing, and Lena curled her fingers around it and made her way back out. Parting Kara’s lips, she dribbled the potion into her mouth, blocking her nose to force her to swallow and then propping her head up when she started to cough.

 

            Kara’s face was ashen and waxy with sweat and Lena closed her eyes as she thought about what to do next. Red was already spotting the clean bandages and she knew they had to be sealed but she didn’t have the means to do it. Even if she’d felt confident leaving Kara alone momentarily to slip away to Diagon Alley and buy new stores of it, it was far too early for anywhere to be open. But Lena refused to leave her even for that, and knew her only real option was St. Mungo’s, but was reluctant to go there as well. Going there would draw the attention of her mother and Lena wanted to keep Lillian as far away from Kara as possible.

 

            In the end, she had little choice. After five minutes crouched on the floor, neither of them with a stitch of clothing on, Lena almost oblivious to the blood coating her left calf, dried and fresh as the wound bled freely, she climbed to her feet and made her way into her bedroom. She dragged on blue jeans and a black jumper and fetched clothes for Kara as well, knowing they’d be ill-fitting but were better than Lena towing her through the waiting room in a tattered blanket. Sam was working, having taken Lena’s shift on the Charms ward so she could be free for the full moon, and Lena found her cryptex on the bedside table and paged her quickly before changing her girlfriend. 

 

            Levitating Kara, Lena drifted her over to the fireplace and found the Floo powder in a pile on the floor. Scraping enough together in her bloody hands, she tossed it into the cold grate and got in with Kara, her voice hoarse and scratchy as she called out for the hospital and was dumped into the waiting room a moment later. Sam arrived as Lena was carrying Kara out of the fireplace, the Healer’s green robes standing out amidst the early-morning patients waiting to be seen, and Sam’s face immediately paled as she helped Lena get her onto the stretcher she’d brought with her.

 

            “What happened?” she quickly demanded.

 

            “The potion didn’t work,” Lena croaked, wiping the arm of her jumper over her face, still somewhat stunned by the events of the night. “I couldn’t heal her at home. I- all of my things …”

 

            They were already off, Sam directing the stretcher as she strode off with purpose, people moving out of their path. “Are you alright?”

 

            “Fine,” Lena quickly assured her, and she felt it as well, too preoccupied to even register her limp, the dull ache in her leg. “I took care of it-“

 

            They were in the lift now, the metal grille dragged across as Sam fixed her with a wary look. “Took care of it? It takes more than one witch to take down a transformed werewolf - even one as powerful as you.”

 

            “I didn’t hex her. I just- I got away. It’s fine. I just- my silver and potions … they got destroyed. I couldn’t seal the cuts. There was … so much blood.”

 

            “It’s alright. She’ll be alright now,” Sam soothed her. “Did you give her anything? Can you tell me what you’ve done?”

 

            Her friend’s tone was almost condescending but Lena was too cool in the face of such stress to need it. Well-trained to remain calm in the worst circumstance imaginable, she rattled off the little she’d done to Sam in a composed manner, stepping off the lift on the first floor and then pausing.

 

            “We should take her up to-“

 

            “The Bite Ward,” Sam interrupted. “She needs to go to the Bite Ward. Smethwyck will be on duty; he’s treated her before, he knows her.”

 

            “But I-“

 

            “You’re not allowed to treat her, regardless of which Ward she’s on.”

 

            Bristling as she struggled to keep up with Sam, who quietly directed orders at a nurse they passed by just outside the doors to the Dai Llewelyn Ward, Lena darted ahead and pushed open the doors. There was a severe look on her face as she scowled, indignant and slightly arrogant.

 

            “She’s been my patient a dozen times. I know her. I know what she needs, okay? I look after her every month.”

 

            Giving her a pitying look, Sam directed the stretcher over to an empty bed and followed after it. “And now she’s my patient. And you’re not allowed to be here. I know you love her but if you respect me as your friend, you’re going to let me do my job.”

 

            “I won’t go,” Lena stubbornly jerked her chin forward, hands balled into fists. “You can’t make me. Not quietly.”

 

            “Lena,” Sam sighed, flicking her wand and motioning with her hand, directing Kara’s unconscious form onto the bed before she gestured to the chair beside it, “do yourself a favour and sit down on that chair and be quiet. You look like you’re about to faint any moment.”

 

            Feeling a little lightheaded, Lena obediently sank onto the chair and watched as Sam tugged the curtain around for privacy. Lena appreciated the fact that Sam didn’t block Kara from her view entirely as she worked, that Lena could still see her face, pinched with pain, skin greyish and bandages stained with even more red as Sam removed her clothes.

 

            Smethwyk pulled back the curtain a moment later with a questioning look on his face as Sam turned towards him. “Patient is Kara Danvers, sir.”

 

            “Oh,” he muttered, slightly perplexed as he verified her by sight. “Well, dear me, I haven’t seen her on the ward in months. What are we dealing with?”

 

            “Just the usual, sir. A few lacerations to the abdomen and upper torso. She’s already been bandaged and given two units of Blood-Replenishing. The wounds haven’t been debrided yet, no silver or Dittany administered at the scene.”

 

            Ducking his head through the curtain, Smethwyk called orders to a nurse and sent the young man off to fetch Sam supplies. He didn’t so much as spare Lena a look, although she knew he was aware of the circumstances and probably drew his own conclusions from it himself. Clicking his tongue, he shook his head.

 

            “Why the bloody hell wouldn’t she stay here overnight,” he sighed. “Never mind, Arias, can the Charms Ward spare you until she’s seen to?”

 

            “I’ve already paged a Resident to cover my rounds.”

 

            “Very well. Carry on, then.”

 

            Lena remained quiet, tense and tight-lipped, her knuckles white as she curled her hands in her lap, fighting the urge to climb to her feet, to be the one to clean out Kara’s wounds and seal them with the solution. It wasn’t that she didn’t trust Sam to do her job properly, only that Lena had always been fiercely protective of Kara, the one thing that had ever been hers. Countless times, she’d washed away the blood and vomit instead of calling for a nurse, taking care of her even when she’d never wanted to speak to her again. They were tied together so intrinsically that it felt like Lena was being punished to sit there and do nothing.

 

            Once Sam was done, Kara was dressed in a clean paper-thin robe and tucked into bed, her face a shocking shade of white in the glow of the ward’s light. Her breaths were even as Lena watched her chest rise and fall beneath the blankets, and she had to stop herself from taking Kara’s wrist in hand and measuring her pulse. Sam had already done that and listened to her lungs too, and although she trusted few people, Lena trusted her friend and knew her place.

 

            “Thank you,” she rasped, running a hand over her face.

 

            Folding her arms over her chest, Sam gave her a worried look, exhaustion in the bags beneath her hazel eyes. “Lena-“

 

            “Don’t.”

 

            “You’re bleeding,” Sam softly continued, moving closer and sinking to a crouch in front of Lena.

 

            Straightening up, Lena craned her neck and saw that a few drops of dark red dotted the floor behind her foot. As Sam gripped her leg and twisted it, Lena saw the calf of her jeans was bloody and she blinked in surprise, although she remembered her leg hurting her for a while now. Hazel eyes flashed up to Lena’s face, panicked.

 

            “Did she-?”

 

            “No,” Lena quickly cut her off. There was a knot in her throat and she had to force it down as she swallowed thickly, a shakiness in her chest as her stomach swooped. A moment later, her voice softened, wavering vulnerably as she raked a hand through her hair. “I don’t know.”

 

            “Let me look,” Sam murmured.

 

            Lena let her roll the wide jeans up to her knee, twisting her leg as Lena shifted on the chair to help Sam get a better angle. Her face was stiff and she clenched her teeth at the sting of the antiseptic solution Sam dabbed over the mess of blood, cleaning it away as she knelt on the linoleum floor. Tense as she waited for the verdict, Lena glanced over at Kara, hoping for her sake it wasn’t what both Healers suspected. She didn’t think their relationship would survive Kara’s guilt over biting her.

 

            “Just a scratch,” Sam said after a minute, her voice full of relief.

 

            Lena similarly felt it flood through her, shoulders going slack as she let out a pent-up breath. Just a scratch. She could manage that; rare steaks and a scar on her calf would be minimal in comparison to Kara’s suffering. It would be minimal in comparison to what Lena had suffered at the hands of her family. Sitting still as Sam used some of the leftover Wound Cleaning solution and sealed the wound with the powdered silver and Dittany, teeth gritted against the agony, Lena let her wipe away the rest of the blood and bandage it. She pulled the leg of her jeans back down over it and gave her friend a grateful look.

 

            “Thank you.”

 

            Pushing herself to her feet with an armful of supplies, Sam set everything on the tray, wrapping up the bloody gauze and pulling off her dragon hide gloves, she gave Lena a grim look. Squeezing her friend’s shoulder, Sam sighed.

 

            “Be careful.”

 

            Lena was in the middle of murmuring a vague reassurance in response when the curtain was pulled back. Looking up, Lena’s mouth parted and she straightened up, gripping the arms on the chair as if she was about to shoot to her feet.

 

            “Eliza,” she said with surprise, “what-“

 

            “Lena,” Eliza said with relief, looking harried as she crossed over to Kara’s side, pressing her hand against her daughter’s forehead. “I’m glad you were here at least.”

 

            Pushing herself to her feet now, Lena looked down at the scuffed floor, wringing her hands with a sheepish look on her face. “Eliza, I’m so sorry.”

 

            Patting her arm distractedly, Eliza looked up at Sam. “How is she?”

 

            “All of her wounds have been treated. I’ve given her a potion to keep her unconscious for a little while, and another for the pain, but she shouldn’t feel any worse than previous full moons,” Sam explained. “Of course, it has been a few months since she’s experienced that intensity of injury from a transformation so it may come as a shock to her when she first wakes.”

 

            “Of course,” Eliza murmured, the corners of her mouth tightening with concern. “Thank you, Healer.”

 

            Sam nodded, pausing before nodding again and then slipping between the curtains and leaving them alone. Lena couldn’t look at Eliza and didn’t speak as she followed after her friend, limping ever so slightly as she drew the attention of the Interns and Residents on duty that morning. 

 

            “You told her mum?” Lena accusingly asked as she caught up to her.

 

            Filling out the paperwork at the nurse’s station, Sam didn’t look up from the page as the quill scratched across the newest form for Kara’s file. “Yes, she is her next of kin. You know that I had to.” 

 

            “I know,” Lena replied, wincing as she rocked on her heels and fiddled with her fingers. “I just- I was handling it.”

 

            “Well, no offence, Lena, you did a piss poor job of handling it last night,” Sam replied, looking up as she set down the quill, a rare flash of irritation crossing her face. Exhaling forcefully, she lowered her voice, inching closer. “You are very, very lucky she didn’t bite you. Do you have any idea how close you came to being infected?”

 

            “Is that really the worst thing you can think of?” Lena rasped, a spasm of pain crossing her face.

 

            She knew that Sam was right, that if Lena hadn’t been an Animagus, there was a very good chance she would have been bitten inside her flat or ended up bleeding out on the pavement below her window. Her mouth was dry and she had to force herself to swallow at the cutting glance of irritation her friend gave her. Pale face colouring slightly, Lena haughtily raised her chin.

 

            “You’re right. I’m sorry. What else am I supposed to do though? I mean … I can’t lock her up here. I can’t lock her in those cells overnight and just be okay with that. Leave her in the dark.” 

 

            Lena suppressed a shudder, a tightening at the corners of her eyes the only signs of her unease at the thought of the cold, pitch-black cells in the dungeons below. She knew what that was like and wouldn’t let her girlfriend endure that when she would keep her mind and be conscious of her circumstances. 

 

            “It won’t happen again. There must have been an issue with the potion. I messed up somewhere.”

 

            “You can’t afford to mess up, Lena,” Sam gently murmured, her face softening with pained understanding. She pitied her friends, both of them, but Sam couldn’t afford to get wrapped up in this either. Lena already felt guilty for dragging her into this business multiple times now, risking Sam’s career along with her own. “There’s a reason why they try to make them register. If she hurts someone, even if it’s you-”

 

            “She won’t.”

 

            “You can’t know that. You have a scar on your leg that will never go away now. Doesn’t that- doesn’t that bother you?”

 

            Lena blinked in surprise. Truthfully, she hadn’t had time to process it, hadn’t had the chance to see it, to feel the shiny edges of it, take in the silver crescent of the claw mark marring her pale skin. She didn’t think it would bother her much though, once she’d had time to think about it. It wasn’t a scar inflicted on her out of cruelty, it wasn’t self-loathing words she hadn’t even picked out herself to remind her of her worthlessness. In fact, as she stood there, it was the scar on Lena’s left forearm that bothered her, not her leg. She pressed her thumb over the sleeve of her left arm, right over the itching scar, and she swallowed past the painful tightness in her chest.

 

            “No.”

 

            Sam opened and closed her mouth, blinking in surprise before she shook her head slightly. “Right, well …”

 

            Reaching out, Lena squeezed her arm, closing her eyes and drawing in a shaky breath. “I’m sorry, it’s just- it’s … been a long night. Um … thank you for your help, for looking after her. And me too. I really do appreciate it.”

 

            Shoulders slumping, Sam covered her friend’s hand with her own, patting it and then picking up her quill again. Hesitating, she bit her lip and then gave Lena a suspicious look. “You’re not going to tell her, are you?”

 

            “Not if she doesn’t remember doing it,” Lena confessed.

 

            And she wouldn’t, if she could get away with it. She didn’t think she’d be able to, knowing that Kara always remembered, that even if she didn’t remember the slice of a claw cleaving through skin and muscle, she would remember swiping for Lena, would remember breaking down the door and chasing her, watching Lena crawl out the broken window. She would remember tearing apart the office and the flat, perhaps she might even remember the blood - not her own, but the little dots the raven left behind on the countertops and the floorboards - and that would just break Kara’s heart. More than anything, Lena hoped she wouldn’t recall the latter. She could reason with Kara about the rest but it would be more difficult to make her see sense about the danger she’d posed, the threat she’d been to Lena’s life. But Lena’s life had been survival of the fittest since the day she was born and some might have said the sheer dumb luck of not being killed by her mother meant she’d been living on borrowed time anyway. Yet, she was still alive, heart beating solidly in her chest, despite the odds.

 

            “A word of advice, love,” Sam sighed. “Lies don’t make for the best relationships. I don’t know her as well as you do, but she was my Housemate at Hogwarts. I know Kara well enough to say she’d prefer to hear it from you straight instead of finding out later. There’s only so long you can hide that scar from her, and she won’t thank you for trying to spare her feelings.”

 

            “Yes,” Lena reluctantly agreed, mouth thinning. “You’re right.”

 

            Smiling wryly, Sam’s eyelids shuttered with exhaustion. “I usually am.”

 

            “Thanks again,” Lena whispered, enveloping her friend in a rare hug, giving her a quick squeeze before she left Sam to her work and wandered up to the Tearoom, returning with three coffees, leaving one for her friend and carrying the other two onto the Bite Ward.

 

            Shifting the curtain aside, she watched as Eliza’s eyes met hers and lowered her gaze as the guilt of misleading Kara’s mother crept back over her. Clearing her throat, Lena crossed over to her and raised the paper cup.

 

            “I thought you could use something to take the edge off.”

 

            Personally, Lena would have preferred a nice shot of Firewhisky, or three, but considering it was early in the morning, it didn’t seem suitable. She twitched her hand at the curtain to close it tightly again and then sank onto the end of Kara’s bed. Looking at Kara’s pale face as the guilt of her failure crept up on Lena, she took a sip of coffee and felt the itch in her left arm.

 

            “You know, she refuses to let me come anymore. Hasn’t in years,” Eliza wearily sighed.

 

            She’d been roused early by the Patronus sent to inform her of the incident and looked tired in her wrinkled clothes. Lena had never been able to send them herself, one of her failings that she managed to keep quiet, sending other people to notify families and next of kin so she didn’t have to try and fail to summon something happy. 

 

            “Goodness, this must’ve happened right at the end of your shift,” Eliza concluded, taking in Lena’s lack of Healer green robes. “You must be exhausted, sweetheart.”

 

            “I’m alright,” Lena gravelly replied, giving her a wan smile as she sipped her coffee and waited for Kara to come around.

Chapter 37

            Waking slowly with the leaden feeling of a deep sleep aided by the fog of a cocktail of potions, Kara’s tongue felt like sandpaper against her teeth as she struggled to swallow, mouth horribly dry and throat tight. Her head felt heavy, her body floating with the weightless sensation of painless bliss but her thoughts were slow as Kara struggled to make sense of things. It had been a while since she’d woken in such a way, used to the feeling of Lena’s office rug beneath her, bare skin rippling with goosebumps, the smell of paper, leather and potions in the air. This smelled harsh, like the clinical sharpness of antiseptic and bleach to Kara’s sensitive nose.

 

            A sigh slipped from her chapped lips and Kara tasted the coppery tang of blood, her face crumpling as her heavy eyelids stayed shut a moment longer before she managed to part them. It took her a few tries, eyelashes fluttering, vague murmurs of confused objection as the dull ache of her body flickered into awareness, a pounding headache making itself known as her head lolled on the pillow. A minute later, Kara’s eyes were fully open but her poor vision couldn’t make out much save for the white but that alone was enough for her to know she was not at Lena’s. The papery robe covering her body was not Lena’s pyjamas, the scratchy blankets were not Lena’s soft linen sheets, the thin mattress was not the thick firmness of Lena’s bed. That was Lena sitting at the foot of the bed though, her dark hair, the pale oval of her face.

 

            Making a low, inquisitive sound at the back of her throat, Kara twitched her fingers on top of the blankets in an attempt to reach for her. Her attention was snagged by the movement from the corner of her eyes, a blonde figure rising to their feet. She didn’t have to ask who it was, knowing before Eliza even opened her mouth.

 

            “Oh, you’re awake,” her mother said with relief, looming over Kara, touching her cheek. She tenderly brushed Kara’s fringe off her forehead as Kara squinted up at her, clicking her tongue as she sighed. “Dear me, where are your glasses?”

 

            “She forgot them at mine,” Lena murmured.

 

            “Oh. Right, well, it’s a good thing your head is attached, Kara Danvers, or you might forget that too,” Eliza said, her tone soft with amusement as she lightly chastised her daughter to take the edge off her worry.

 

            Struggling to make her mouth work, Kara let out a small whimper, her expression crumpling as she tried to make sense of the memories that were starting to rise through the confusion. Blinking slowly, she flexed her fingers, head lolling as she looked down at the blurry form of her hand on the sheets, clumsily raising it as she remembered the blood. So much blood, so much pain, trying to process what had happened, her ribs and shoulder bandaged, her arm bandaged. 

 

            “What-”

 

            The wispy beginning of her question trailed off into a weary sigh and she clumsily rubbed her tired eyes, trying to make sense of things. She’d hurt herself, she’d gone wild, that feral anger bubbling over as she’d thrown her body against the door, over and over again, thrown herself against the rows of shelves before her frustration led her to tear everything free, breaking the chair, clawing up the rug, overturning the cauldrons and tearing apart almost every book, jar and pot in the office. 

 

            Then Kara’s face went white, a ghastly shade of white that was almost nauseously green, a choked sound of realisation escaping her at the hazy memory of a pale face slack with shock, panic and fear. Kara didn’t know what expression had been on Lena’s face, only that she’d broken down the door and her girlfriend had been there, that Kara had been so out of her mind that she’d gone after her, bursting through the bedroom door, chasing her to the broken window.

 

            It was confusing after that. Kara had never seen Lena’s Animagus form before, had no reference for the raven that had fluttered around the flat all night, cawing when Kara’s mind had dipped back down into that haze of bloodlust and anger as she bit herself and clawed at herself, tore apart the furniture. But she knew it was Lena. She knew it was Lena with the stomach-swooping certainty of mortifying guilt and horror. Kara was glad she didn’t have her glasses with her; she couldn’t bear to look at her.

 

            “The potion didn’t work,” Eliza supplied for her as Kara wrestled with the feeling of dread that was slowly numbing her. “You hurt yourself but you’ve been patched up. You’re alright. Lena was here the whole time.”

 

            Kara’s vision was too poor to see the thinning of Lena’s mouth but her own feelings on the events of the night made a choked sob get caught at the back of her throat. Her eyes started to sting and she closed them as tears pricked, the breath forced from her lungs as she reached up to rub her eyes, mouth turning down at the corners as her chin dimpled and her face flushed red with embarrassment. 

 

            Not for crying, no one could ever make Kara feel embarrassed by shedding a few tears. Embarrassment over what she was, what she’d done. Lena’s flat was a haven for her, as someone who struggled with being at home during her childhood, who had never felt comfortable anywhere until she’d curated her own space, and Kara had torn right through the place in a bout of lupine madness. 

 

            “You’re alright,” Eliza repeated, stroking Kara’s hair. “You’ll be out of here soon.”

 

            The tenderness of her mother’s voice only made it worse, the tightness in Kara’s chest making it difficult to breathe, another sob choking her off as hot tears ran down her temples and into her hair. She couldn’t explain the pain. It wasn’t quite physical, although the awareness of her body was starting to come back, the dull ache growing more intense, but it was agonising all the same. She started to cry freely, her sobs coming as shallow gasps, the ragged sound of them cutting through Eliza’s gentle hushing as she cupped her daughter’s face in her hands.

 

            Thrashing as she tore her face free, Kara was aware that Lena was no longer sitting at the foot of the bed, that she was on the other side, bloodstained hands she hadn’t washed yet reaching out to press Kara back down against the thin pillows. 

 

            “It’s okay, you’re safe. You’re safe.”

 

            “No, no, no,” Kara breathlessly sobbed, trying to sit up, her face stained with tears, a hollow shakiness inside her that made her stomach turn.

 

            “Come on, lay back down. It’s alright.”

 

            Her words fell on deaf ears though and Kara struggled against Lena’s gentle grasp on her, trying to coax her back down, her soothing tone doing nothing to mitigate the sickening terror of Kara’s memories as they swept back in in a torrent of destruction. Lena’s voice shook slightly at her own poorly concealed worry and Eliza was on Kara’s other side, trying to calm her as well but she was inconsolable. Her chest hurt and her head hurt and she couldn’t breathe properly, the ragged breaths sawing in and out of her lungs, making her lightheaded as she gripped the side of the hospital bed and vomited in her lap and partially down Lena’s front. 

 

            Lena let go of her and vanished through the curtain as Kara sobbed, swallowing the bitter taste of bile, trembling as vomit coated her chin and Eliza held her arm, still trying to calm her down. And then Lena was back and Kara couldn’t see her clearly but she felt her grasp on her slick chin and the press of glass against her lips and teeth as a potion was tipped into her mouth.

 

            The effect was almost immediate, Kara’s body going limp as she deflated, Lena easing her down onto the pillows as she tenderly murmured reassurances to her. Kara’s babbling sobs petered out into breathless hitches as her expression went slack, eyes owlishly round as she blinked slowly, mumbling incoherently as the sedative Lena gave her left her deflated on the pillows. Her tongue felt thick in her mouth as she tried to speak as Lena cleaned her up, wiping her face, vanishing the vomit and gently easing Kara’s head up as she slipped water down her throat.

 

            She slept a while after that, exhausted from a night spent wide awake instead of curled up on the office floor, sound asleep. The next time she woke, Kara was frighteningly quiet, remaining still as she stared up at the ceiling, remembering all of it, the memories settling in her mind, glaringly, horrifyingly clear. Her stomach knotted and she had to swallow past the pain in her throat as she blinked slowly, aware of people shifting.

 

            “Hey,” Lena whispered, at her side, stroking her hair.

 

            Turning her head aside, away , Kara closed her eyes, a muscle trembling in her jaw as she clenched her teeth against the building urge to cry again. Her mouth drew into a small knot of barely controlled grief and she was still for a minute before she sat up, a hollowness in her stomach as she tried to get her shaking limbs to cooperate. She hadn’t felt so weak in months , the self-inflicted wounds sapping her strength, despite the Healers’ best efforts.

 

            “Hang on,” Lena cautioned her. “Wait, wait, go slow.”

 

            Tearing the blankets back, Kara ignored her and the rough sigh that followed as she got out of bed on Eliza’s side, staggering slightly, the floor cold beneath her bare feet as her mother righted her, clicking her tongue as she cautioned her as well. Lena’s voice was weary as she tried to get Kara to stop, the IV stand that had been slowly dripping a Blood Replenishing potion through a tube connected to the cannula in her hand skittering across the floor erratically with Kara’s hurried movements. Unsteady and shaking almost violently, Kara looked around blindly, stammering as she spoke.

 

            “I need to- I need to go. My clothes, I- where-?”

 

            “Okay, okay,” Eliza murmured, caught off guard as Kara started tearing off the paper-thin robe, the scarred expanse of her back a shock to her mother, who hadn’t seen her daughter so undressed in over a decade. “Why don’t you sit down? Let me help.”

 

            Sitting heavily on the chair Eliza urged her down onto, Kara put her face in her hands and started to cry, gut-wrenching sobs that shook her shoulders as her greying hair fell in her face. Fetching the folded clothes that Lena had hastily dressed Kara in to bring her to St. Mungo’s, Eliza shook out the jumper and tugged the neck over Kara’s head, murmuring soothingly as she worked her daughter’s limp left arm through the sleeve. Lena crouched at Kara’s side and detached the tube before removing the tape and cannula so Eliza could get her right arm through.

 

            “Where are her shoes?” Eliza muttered, glancing up at Lena.

 

            She had Kara’s pants bunched up around her ankles, urging her quietly sobbing daughter to her bare feet as she dragged them up, buttoning the jeans. If she showed any knowledge of them not being Kara’s clothes, she didn’t question it, looking at Lena as she waited for a response. Head ducked down, Lena floundered for a moment, unable to think of a sufficient lie. In Eliza’s mind, Kara had come to St. Mungo’s as she had been since arriving in England, a packed bag of clean clothes for the next morning, a peaceful transformation for the last few months, and now her daughter was inconsolably sobbing, carved up, shoeless and half-blind.

 

            “I- they’re at my place too,” Lena lamely replied.

 

            “She came here barefoot? Where are your shoes?” she asked, glancing down at Lena’s feet.

 

            Mouth opening and closing, Lena flushed slightly, running a hand through her dishevelled hair before she turned and cast Kara a quick look and then made for the curtains. “I’ll just- I’ll be … back.”

 

            She made a hasty exit, her own socked feet feeling the cold of the floor through the soles as she wove between the Healers, nurses and Mediwizards, riding the rattling lift down a floor and then leaving through the front door. Apparating to her flat, Lena unlocked the door and stepped into the mess, making a beeline for the ruined office and opening one of the untouched desk drawers. Kara’s glasses were stowed beside her wand and Lena took them both before doubling back to the door and picking up the shoes, shoving her feet into a pair of her own before leaving again.

 

            Back at St. Mungo’s, Lena made her way upstairs, almost lunchtime, her stomach grumbling, shoulders sagging with exhaustion, and she brushed through the curtain and set the boots down beside Kara’s feet, grimacing when she realised she’d forgotten the socks. Crouching, Lena slid the wire frames of her girlfriend’s glasses onto her face and watched as Kara blinked, adjusting to the clarity of her vision before she looked away from Lena, who was pressing her wand into her hand.

 

            “I’ll go and sort the discharge papers,” Lena murmured as she straightened back up and Kara raised her head to watch her go.

 

            Lena hadn’t gotten more than a few steps away from her when Kara noticed the faint limp, her eyes dragged downwards to take in the sight of her bloodstained left leg. Horror choked her up and she stumbled to her feet, crossing the space quickly as she grabbed Lena’s arm, forcing her to a stop. Turning to give her a hopefully tender look, reaching to touch her cheek as her lips twitched with a ghost of a smile, Lena was jerked back around as Kara stepped back and looked down.

 

            “No,” she hoarsely choked out.

 

            Letting out a resigned sigh, Lena turned back around and touched Kara’s arm. “No,” she murmured in agreement.

 

            Kara let out a ragged sound that was pure relief, feeling as if her legs were going to buckle beneath her, her heart hammering in her chest as her vision dimmed, a tightness in her chest. She sank onto her haunches, Eliza moving forward, hands on Kara’s shoulders as she leaned over her, speaking quietly, trying to encourage her back to her feet. Lena hesitated before continuing to go and ask for Kara’s discharge papers, returning a few minutes later with a quill and kneeling at Kara’s side, her girlfriend back in the chair. Laying her hand on Kara’s knee, Lena watched her shakily sign her name to the forms and Lena took them back before holding out a hand, rising as she brought Kara with her.

 

            The three of them left together, saying little as Lena handed in the paperwork at the nurse’s station and pressed a hand against Kara’s lower back to urge her towards the lift. Descending to the ground floor, they bypassed the waiting room and stepped out into the street, Muggles brushing past, giving them odd looks. Stepping into the alleyway, Eliza clutched her daughter’s arm and then reached out for Lena’s, whisking them away a second later before the faint tang of salt, damp grass and exhaust fumes greeted them in Cornwall.

 

            They shuffled into the small cottage, crowding the entryway, and Kara brushed past Eliza, who was suggesting running her a hot bath, as she made for the stairs, grasping the bannister and hauling herself up, ignoring the voices calling after her. Barrelling into her bedroom, Kara slammed the door shut behind her and staggered over to her bed, all but collapsing onto the mattress as her shoulders started to shake and she came undone. Hands covering her mouth and eyes as she tried to muffle the sounds, choking them down, swallowing past the tightness of her throat, Kara ignored the gentle knock.

 

            “Kara?” Lena softly called through the door. “Open the door, please.”

 

            Kara didn’t respond, sitting on the edge of the bed with her head in her hands, grey-faced and nauseous. She had her eyes squeezed shut as if she could block the whole world out but that wasn’t enough to shut Lena out. Lena, who had only ever taken care of her and been repaid with a slash across the calf that would bear the same silvery scar that crisscrossed Kara’s body by the dozen, who already had one scar from someone who should have only touched her gently, loved her properly, and now had been gifted another by someone similar. She could remember it now, lunging for her, paws outstretched, snagging on Lena’s pyjama pants, one claw shearing through it and her skin. She thought she might be sick again.

 

            “Kara,” Lena said a little louder this time, her voice breaking on her name. “Don’t do this. Please . I’m not going to force my way in but don’t shut me out.”

 

            Climbing to her feet, Kara balled her hands into fists as she tried to stifle her anger, shaking as she clenched her teeth. Moving towards the door, she pressed a hand against the door and hesitated, opening her mouth and inhaling sharply before she let out a heavy sigh and tipped forward, her forehead gently thudding against the door.

 

            “Please go away,” she rasped, her voice raw and unrecognisable to herself. 

 

            “No.”

 

            The quiet growl of Lena’s response was punctuated with the thud of her palm slapped against the wood on the other side of the door and Kara drew back a fraction, blinking in surprise. Opening and closing her mouth, speechless for a second, Kara swallowed thickly.

 

            “Please.”

 

            “No. Open the door.”

 

            “No.”

 

            There was a momentary pause before Lena let out a rough sigh. “Fine.”

 

            Kara heard the scuff of her retreating footsteps and her shoulders sagged with relief. She scrubbed a hand over her face and braced herself against the door, feeling weak and still somewhat in shock. When she was sure that Lena had truly left, hearing the faint squeak of the staircase, Kara looked at her dirty hands and went to fetch clean pyjamas.

 

            Stepping out of her bedroom, she quickly locked herself in the bathroom and pulled the light string, casting a wan glow over the cramped room. Running the water, she had to heat it by wand, the old pipes not up to the task of producing anything slightly above lukewarm, shedding her clothes and the bandages and stepping into the tub.

 

            Slipping under, she held her breath until her lungs hurt and she had to resurface, the near-scalding heat doing nothing to scour the memories from her mind. Coming back up, she brushed her wet hair out of her face, sleek, brassy strands interspersed with silver, and held up her hands before she sat up and dipped them in the water. Blood had worked its way into the grooves of her palms and her cuticles and she could taste bile at the thought of whether some of it was Lena’s, She grabbed the soap and furiously scrubbed as she felt that nauseous panic settle in again. Hands shaking, breaths shallow and ragged, she scrubbed herself clean, wincing and gasping at the tenderness of the new scars, unable to even look at herself as she screwed her eyes shut.

 

            Once the water started to cool, Kara climbed out and dried off, dressing in clean pyjamas, vanishing the bandages and leaving her curls to dry in a tangled mess as she shouldered her way out of the bathroom. She was heading towards her bedroom to shut herself back inside it but paused at the sound of voices, moving closer to listen and sinking down onto the top step.

 

            “-going to tell me what happened?” Eliza asked. 

 

            “What do you mean?”

 

            Kara could envision Lena’s smooth aloofness, that casual, dismissive air she had perfected, as if nothing was amiss. She’d been on the receiving end of it a few times and had seen it in play as Lena worked, her expression impassive, motions calm as she feigned indifference. Of course, Kara knew Lena had always felt things strongly and more keenly than she would ever let on.

 

            Rising from her step, Kara padded downstairs, eavesdropping as she heard her mother let out a huff of laughter. Pausing halfway down the stairs, just out of sight of the living room, above the step that squeaked, Kara felt a lump lodge itself in her throat. Even now, Lena wouldn’t tell on her.

 

            “You’re a nice girl,” Eliza said with a sigh, “so please don’t lie to me. I’m not as oblivious as you think I am.”

 

            “I don’t think you’re oblivious at all. You have a lot of respect for her, for what she wants, even if you wish she needed you more. She pushes everyone away, I know that, and I don’t know if- … I just think it should come from her - if she wants to talk about it.”

 

            Continuing the rest of the way downstairs, Kara stepped into the doorway of the living room, her face slack with her numb shock, cheeks blotchy and eyes red from crying. Both women turned to look at her and Lena set her tea down on the coffee table, shifting as if she was about to stand, to go to her, before she remained seated, caution in her green eyes.

 

            “You should go,” Kara gravelly told her.

 

            “I’m drinking my tea.”

 

            “After that.”

 

            “I was going to go and pick up some Chinese.”

 

            Clenching her jaw, frustration making her face furrow and flush pink, Kara ducked her head down, fiddling with her fingers. “Alright, after that then.”

 

            “Kara, you’re being rude,” Eliza gently chided her, mouth twisting with disapproval as she frowned, caught off guard by her daughter’s unusually curt tone as she tried to usher Lena out of the house. “Lena can stay as long as she likes. If you’re tired, why don’t you lie down for a little while? You can come back down for dinner.”

 

            Pausing, Kara’s mouth thinned with frustration and she turned without another word, making for the stairs. Lena murmured something behind her and Kara was halfway up the stairs when her girlfriend caught up to her, taking the steps two at a time and grabbing her arm, pulling Kara to a stop as Lena forced her to face her. 

 

            “Kara- wait!”

 

            “Go away - before I hurt you again,” Kara warned her, voice low and wavering, on the verge of crying again.

 

            She loomed over Lena, two steps above her, vision blurring with tears as her chin wobbled. Lena’s lips twitched with a wavering smile, choking on a strangled laugh as she raised her eyebrows dubiously.

 

            “You’re not going to hurt me,” Lena gently replied, keeping her voice low, conscious of Eliza in the living room. “We both know what- what happened last night was not your fault. I’m sorry, I- I failed-”

 

            “Don’t.”

 

            “I must have messed up the potion. You don’t know … how sorry I am, but … I’ll do better next time. I promise. Just … please.”

 

            “Lena,” Kara whispered, shaking her head, her devastation and heartbreak written clearly on her face. “I can’t do this. I can’t live with myself if I- if I hurt you, if I-”

 

            She shook her head again, tears spilling down her cheeks as she cut off, hanging her head with shame. Wiping her face on her sleeve, she turned and continued up to the landing, leaving Lena standing helplessly halfway up, her face pale and taut with panic.

 

            “You think I’m frightened of you? That I care if you bite me?” Lena called after her, her voice rising as her temper flared up.

 

            “Don’t you dare minimise it,” Kara snarled, hurriedly backtracking, her feet thundering on the stairs. “You have no idea what it feels like, not just on a full moon but every fucking day . You have no right to act like it’s- it’s some trivial thing. Don’t you fucking dare.”

 

            “Hey!” Eliza called up from the foot of the staircase, mild surprise on her face as she looked up at Kara, disbelieving. “That’s quite enough.”

 

            “Go home,” Kara fiercely whispered, standing a step above Lena, who was stiff as she leaned back slightly. 

 

            Turning back around, she quickly retraced her steps back up to the landing, the quiet murmur of Lena reassuring Eliza she was fine following her as guilt needled Kara. She opened her bedroom door and stepped inside, a muscle twitching in her jaw as she paused, swallowing  thickly, ashamed at her behaviour but more frightened that she’d hurt Lena worse in the future, bite her, kill her. It was better to behave this way, to drive her away before she got hurt worse than she already was.

 

            She hadn’t heard the soft pad of Lena’s socks quickly following her up the stairs though and as she moved to shut the door, a pale hand gripped the edge of it and pushed back. Stumbling, caught off guard and weak, Kara’s eyes widened and her lips parted as Lena slipped through the gap and then shut the door herself. Rounding on her, Lena folded her arms over her chest, the silence unbearably thick.

 

            They stared at each other for a moment and Lena took in the guilt in Kara’s curled shoulders, the way she had shrunk in on herself, shouldering the burden of what she was as she hung her head, cheeks wet and blotchy. Lena stepped forward, closing the gap between them as she engulfed Kara in a hug that was full of her desperation, holding her close, cradling the back of her head as they swayed unsteadily, hushing her as Kara wept into her shoulder.

 

            “I’m sorry, I’m sorry,” Kara whispered, her voice pleading and meek, so vulnerably small that Lena held her tighter, a severe look on her face as she dug her chin into Kara’s shoulder with stubborn determination.

 

            “It’s okay, it’s okay,” Lena mumbled into the side of her neck, the clean smell of soap, the smell of her skin, the warmth of her wiry body making her heart ache in her chest as some knot loosened in her stomach, relieved to hold her. “You’re okay, you’re fine.”

 

            She shepherded them over to Kara’s rumpled bed and sat down beside her, Kara clutching fistfuls of Lena’s jumper as she hunched over, Lena’s arm around her back, her face almost in Lena’s lap as hot tears dotted the thighs of her girlfriend’s jeans. Softly shushing her as she rubbed her back, Lena let her feel the whole range of it, the broken sounds of her sobs making her feel guilty at the failure of the potion, at letting Kara hurt herself when she’d sworn to keep her safe.

 

            “Your leg-” Kara choked out after a few minutes.

 

            “Just a scratch,” Lena replied, her voice wavering slightly. “I didn’t even feel it.”

 

            “Can I see?”

 

            Kara kept her face buried in Lena’s shoulder, her breaths hitching and rasping, that hollow pit that had opened up inside her still so all-consuming as she grappled with the conflicting agony of wanting to shut Lena out and beg her to stay. She wouldn’t have been able to cope with Lena thinking she was a monster, some rabid beast that deserved the XXXXX rating in the Ministry’s classification, that should be hunted for sport to eradicate them. The logical part of her mind that had been stamped down so small in light of her terrified memories knew that Lena would think anything but that but Kara wasn’t thinking reasonably then. 

 

            Stiffening momentarily beside her, Lena relented with a defeated sigh, knowing Kara wouldn’t be able to move past this or let it go unless she knew that Lena was okay. Raising her left leg, Lena pulled the stiff denim of her bloodstained jeans up to her knee and then vanished the bandage and ripped off the gauze. It was small, perhaps an inch long in the muscle of her calf, catching the waning light as it stood out, silvery against her porcelain skin. Barely a nick to her.

 

            Kara slid off the bed, kneeling on the floor as she cradled Lena’s leg in shaking hands, her thumb tracing over the line of it. She let out a strangled sound of anguish, her vision blurring with fresh tears as she drew in a shuddering breath.

 

            “Are you okay?” she softly exclaimed, looking up at Lena with a wretched look on her face.

 

            Giving her a thin smile, Lena cupped Kara’s face in her hands and leaned down. “I’m fine. It’s you that I- you were bleeding so much. I thought- I thought- I’m sorry.”

 

            “Don’t apologise,” Kara darkly replied, her voice low and ragged. “Don’t do that. Don’t- what I did-”

            

            “Was an accident.”

 

            Swallowing thickly, Kara shook her head. “We can’t afford an accident.”

 

            “I won’t let it happen again.”

 

            “Stop it,” Kara whispered, staring down at her lap, toying with her scarred fingers as she hunched her shoulders, keeping her eyes cast down. “How can you bear to look at me?” 

 

            Lena sat on the bed above her, pressing her hand to Kara’s cheek, forcing her to look up at her. With great reluctance, Kara raised her head, pushing back blonde curls, frizzy and unbrushed, as she stared at Lena with wide, mournful blue eyes that cut right through her.

 

            “It’s my favourite thing to do,” Lena said with a crooked smile.

 

            Choking on a laugh, Kara squeezed her eyes shut and covered her face with a hand, embarrassed and horrified. Nudging up her glasses, she pressed her fingers to her eyelids, inhaling deeply.

 

            “You saw me.”

 

            “I did. And you saw me.”

 

            Kara’s hands shook as she brought them away from her face, a small whimper escaping her as she looked at her long fingers, the neatly filed nails that looked so ordinary and unassuming in the waning light of her cramped bedroom. Curling them into fists, Kara let them fall limply to her lap.

 

            “I’m everything they say I am. What I did … it was nothing short of monstrous. I don’t- how you can- how you can sit there and be … okay with that. How close I came to- to biting you, to kil-”

 

            She couldn’t even finish saying it, her voice faltering as she closed her mouth, swallowing the words along with the regret and guilt. Still kneeling on the floor, her shoulders sagged as she exhaled heavily, so defeated and tired and sick with worry. Lena’s hands cupped her face again, cool and gentle but insistent.

 

            “Look at me. You have never been a monster,” Lena fiercely whispered, echoing her past words from months ago. “Not even on a full moon.”

 

            A bubble of laughter got caught in Kara’s chest and slipped out as a soft groan. “That’s exactly what I am. You can’t tell me you don’t think that; I saw your face. I remember. ”

 

            “I don’t think it. You saw my face? Okay, and I’ll tell you right now that I was not frightened of you. Perhaps for you; I was supposed to keep you safe. I- that’s my fault. You trusted me and I- I let you down. I’m sorry.”

 

            Letting out a forceful breath, Kara shook her head as she stammered an explanation, “you didn’t. I was thinking about it, in the bath … I took that same batch last month. It- it wasn’t you . I found the empty vial the next morning but … I don’t know what time I took it. It was late, I remember that much but we- we were drinking and- and I think I forgot to take it in time. It was me. It’s my fault.”

 

            Some of the tension bled out of Lena as she blinked, the heavy blow of relief making her sag on the mattress as she closed her eyes, rubbing her forehead as she tried to stifle that sting of failure that had plagued her all day. It hadn’t been her fault, she hadn’t failed. Her arm still itched though and there was that sense of responsibility she couldn’t shake, that she should have made sure Kara had taken it in time. But it hadn’t been her potion-making ability, just a small oversight that had almost ended very badly. They’d gotten incredibly lucky, mostly due to Lena’s old curiosity to see if she could manage the magic required to become an Animagus. For once, she was grateful for the raven.

 

            “It’s not your fault,” Lena quickly corrected her. “None of this is your fault and everything’s fine, so … let’s leave it at that, okay?”

 

            “It’s not that simple.”

 

            “It is, it can be.”

 

            “It can never happen again,” Kara gravely replied.

 

            “It won’t but I won’t argue with you over what’s done. We both got complacent, we’ve learned our lessons but that changes nothing. Do you hear me? I’m not leaving and I’m certainly not telling you to go. You told me … next time you’re behaving like an idiot, I should hex you instead of telling you to go. I don’t want to hex you but if you push me away, I’m afraid it’ll qualify.”

 

            Lips twitching with a ghost of a smile, Kara wearily pushed herself to her feet and sank onto the edge of the mattress, wrapping an arm around Lena and kissing the side of her head. “I don’t want you to go but I want to keep you safe. If it- if it comes to it … I know what choice I would make. No matter how much I wouldn’t want to.”

 

            “I know what choice I would make too,” Lena whispered. “I have never left you, not once. Even when you thought I had. That’s the only time I’m ever frightened of you - when I’m losing you.”

            

            “I’m afraid of the same thing.”

 

            Brushing her curls out of her face, Lena paused and then kissed Kara tenderly, her lips lingering and warm as she smiled into it, feeling Kara lean in. Pulling away, she touched their foreheads together and let out a quiet laugh.

 

            “Then it’s a simple solution, isn’t it? We won't lose each other.”

Chapter 38

            Lena went home to her apartment that afternoon to a horrendous mess. Even with the aid of magic, her repetitive mumbles of Reparo as things knitted themselves back together, brick and mortar and splintered wood restructuring into whole doors and furniture, the mattress re-stuffing itself, feathers and threads reforming pillows and the quilt, it still took a long time for Lena to bring order back to her flat. 

 

            Then there was the mess of her office, the destroyed potions and ingredients that couldn’t be sorted out, contaminating each other and no longer stable for future potions. She had to vanish most of that, trying to repair the rug where a few potions had started to melt through it. Most of her vials were able to be repaired, as was most of her equipment as well, but she would need to pen a rather long list of supplies to replenish her potion and ingredients stock, especially if she needed to brew another batch of the Wolfsbane Potion in time for the next full moon.

 

            Her desk was intact, despite the things that had been swiped off its surface and the claw marks scarring the wood, but Lena still double-checked the drawers to ensure her copied notes on the Wolfsbane Potion had survived the ordeal. Reassured as she pulled out the stack of papers, her eyes landed on a different stack underneath, bearing her handwriting as the same sentence was repeated over and over again. It made her pause as she felt the phantom itch in her left arm, swallowing past the dryness of her throat as her mind strayed to her quill. Despite the realisation that she’d brewed the potion correctly, Lena still blamed herself for the oversight of not ensuring Kara took her potion on time while inebriated, and without a shadow of a doubt, if she’d had her quill there then, she would have used it.

 

            A part of her paused at that, torn between finding an excuse to go back to Kara’s and ransack her room to find it, perhaps even succumbing to the weakness of pleading, begging her girlfriend for it back, just to use this once, and holding to her dismissive insistence that she didn’t need it anymore. Except she did but she’d let Kara take it without much resistance, trying to feign nonchalance that had now come back to bite her.
