Setting her notes back on top of the stack of lines, Lena shut the drawer and tried to shake off the nagging urge as she worried her thumb over the scar, digging her nail in deep as she paced a few steps away from the desk.

 

            Scraping her palms over her face and through her hair, she exhaled roughly and shook her head before stalking out of the room and firmly shutting the door behind her. She couldn’t remember the last time she had felt so out of sorts, tense and brimming with unease and guilt. Guilt for what she’d failed to do and guilt for what she wanted to do. If she had been a normal person, someone who could allow herself to be vulnerable, could afford to share so much of herself with other people, she would have gone to Kara then, could have been honest with her, with how she felt and what she craved, but Lena had never been raised that way. 

 

            Instead, she settled on a glass of Firewhisky, hoping to take the edge off as she continued to tidy up, opting for a second glass, and then a third. They were all filled above the standard but Lena didn’t have work until the following afternoon and allowed herself the sloppiness of too much to drink as it fed into her worst impulses. It wasn’t enough though, only serving to exacerbate the itch to feel the pain of punishment, and she had half a mind to Apparate to Knockturn Alley, to see if Borgin and Burkes were still open and had a replacement quill for her. She was unsure of where Lillian had purchased the original one, and while they may not have been standard stock, surely they weren’t that hard to come by.

 

            But Lena didn’t want to let Kara down, didn’t want to give in to the weakness inside her, knowing that if she did, she would just be proving right the words her mother had made her carve into herself. It would be a failure in itself to use the quill after swearing that she didn’t anymore, and she wrestled with the conflicting parts of her as she tried to manage her feelings. It was frustrating and made Lena restless, pacing in her flat until she stumbled upon a thought, crossing to the fireplace and tossing in a handful of Floo powder before slurring an address. 

 

            “Gayle?” she called out as she staggered out of the fireplace, into the dark flat of her sometimes friend. “Gayle, are you home?”

 

            She had no clue if the other woman was even in the country, let alone at home, her work taking her all over the globe and Lena not so involved in her life as to keep tabs on her whereabouts. Perhaps if she had spent more time with her friends over the last few months, which would have been difficult considering she hadn’t spent any time with them since her birthday, she would have known but it didn’t matter to Lena anyway. Gayle’s flat was familiar to her from occasional drinks there, the place bursting with trinkets that she brought back from her trips, a carefully curated clutter that Lena could see no order in. It was a good thing the wards her friend had wrapped her flat in exempted Lena from their effects, a trusted visitor at any time, but she was still cautious as she hurriedly waved a hand at the lights and started scrambling through the abundance of items.

 

            It took her forty minutes, swaying unsteadily on her feet as the Firewhisky hit her hard before her hand closed around a candle. There was nothing particularly special about its appearance, squat with a black wick from being lit before, some of the wax on top melted, and Lena had already lit a few other candles she’d found, testing them out to no avail, but this time, when she lit it and held her hand over the flame, it didn’t hurt. Just to be sure, she spoke a simple lie and felt pain lance through her palm, snatching her hand back and watching as the redness quickly faded.

 

            Relieved and pleased, Lena stole the candle, squashed the glow of the lights and took a pinch of Floor powder from the mantle before heading home. Sitting on the edge of the sofa, she set her candle on the coffee table and licked her lips, eyes bright from the alcohol and her heart beating quickly as her skin prickled with nervous anticipation. Lena rationalised this to herself as being different to the quill, not breaking any promises, not going back on her word, just taking the edge off the desire to repent with a phantom pain that wouldn’t leave a lasting mark. In a way, if she thought about it, realistically, it was better this way because at least there would be no scars, no sign of what she’d done.

 

            Snapping her fingers, summoning a little orange flame to light the wick, Lena drew in a shaky breath and thought momentarily, rubbing her forehead. Leaning forward as she exhaled slowly, she set her fingertips into the flame, feeling nothing, and bit her lip as she hesitated.

 

            “Never have I failed.”

 

            Her voice was a wavering rasp and she hissed as she jerked her hand back a moment later, the quick lick of pain making her heart beat faster, adrenaline coursing through her as she breathed heavily. It had been expected, welcomed, and Lena flexed her fingers as the thrill of the pain soothed something inside her. Putting her hand back over the flame, she repeated the lie over and over again like a mantra, withstanding the pain until it was unbearable and watching as the magic quickly undid itself, leaving no mark of the pain, even if the ghost of it lingered. 

 

            By the time she’s sated the desire within her, Lena’s hand was trembling and she’d sobered somewhat, no more Firewhisky aiding the self-destruction, and as she curled her fingers over her palm, she drew in a shuddering breath and blew out the candle. Wax had spilt over the side and dripped onto the coffee table but she left the mess as she staggered to her feet, head starting to ache and exhaustion catching up to her after almost two days without sleep.

 

            Stumbling to her bedroom, she collapsed onto the quilt with the lingering sensation of her burning palm and fell asleep quickly, the itch satisfied for the time being. It wasn’t the same as the quill, but the acknowledgement of her failures confirmed by the candle drove home the same message. Sleep troubled by bad dreams, Lena woke in the dark room and felt the prickle of unease wash over her until she waved her hand at the lamp, a warm glow suffusing the room as she kicked off her shoes and made herself more comfortable.

 

            Sleeping until late morning, Lena eventually dragged herself out of bed, forcing herself to eat something as she nursed a hangover without any cures on hand, finding paper, a quill and an inkpot and penning a long list at the dining table. It was primarily the ingredients for the Wolfsbane Potion, and a few other necessities she could recall off the top of her head, and she sent Morrigan off with the list attached to her leg with her account number before making another cup of coffee.

 

            Cleaning up the remainder of the mess, including the hardened wax on the coffee table, Lena hid the offending candle amidst a few ordinary ones, hoping it would go unnoticed, and tried to get her affairs in order. She felt a little jittery, guilty for the loophole she’d found, which fed back into the urge to do it again out of punishment, although she abstained for now, and it was a relief to get ready for work, just to have something else to focus on.

 

            Flooing to St Mungo’s an hour early, Lena ferreted out a hangover cure for herself, went up to the tearoom for coffee and then tracked down Sam in the Alchemy Room, handing off a cup and sinking heavily to the stool beside her friend. Taking a sip of coffee, she folded her arms on the high table and rested her cheek on top.

 

            “How are you feeling?” Sam asked, somewhat cordial in comparison to her usual warmth.

 

            “Fine.”

 

            Her friend hummed in agreement, squinting at a pair of scales as she double-checked the balance and then scraped the crushed Scarab beetles into the cauldron brewing a new batch of Skele-Gro. She could tell that Sam was annoyed with her and Lena grimaced, closing her eyes as she hesitated and then reached out to cover the back of Sam’s hand with her own.

 

            “Thank you for your help.”

 

            Softly sighing, Sam finished stirring the potion and then looked at Lena, her mouth thinning with exasperation. “How’s she taking it?”

 

            “As well as expected.”

 

            “You know, I really wish it was simpler for you. But you know this is- this is something that is going to be a risk for as long as you’re with her. Every month.”

 

            “Spare me the lecture. Please,” Lena mumbled, burying her head in her arms again. “It’s a mistake I’m not going to repeat. I can promise you that.”

 

            “I’m not your mum, Lena, I’m not going to lecture you. 

 

            Lena refrained from informing Sam that if she was her mother, she would have subjected her to far worse than a lecture. 

 

            “Thank you.”

 

            “But you should be more cautious about this. Having her transform in your flat? Really? In a Muggle city?”

 

            Her objections getting caught in her throat, Lena’s shoulders sagged slightly and she smiled faintly, eyelids shuttering. “Alright,” she whispered, “you’re right, I’ll think about that more - and I’ll be careful.”

 

            “That would be brilliant if you could. Now, we have patients and if we talk about this any longer, I have a feeling we’ll both get really cross. Thank you for the coffee.”

 

            Standing, Sam picked up her cup and took a sip. Climbing to her feet as well, Lena reached out to snag her friend’s arm before she could stalk off, giving Sam a sheepish smile of gratitude before she gave her a quick hug.

 

            “Thank you. I’m glad I have you. Really.”

 

            Softening, Sam patted her back. “Talk to me if you need to. Preferably before you do something that will get you into trouble.”

 

            Giving her a brief squeeze, Lena let go and looked appropriately chastened as she picked up her coffee and followed her friend out of the room. They nursed their drinks as they walked down the hallway, chatting about work and life, Sam mentioning an upcoming concert she suggested they go to together, Lena inviting her out for drinks next Wednesday after work when they were both scheduled to finish at the same time.

 

            It was a bit of normalcy after a wretched couple of days and it was comfortingly familiar. She was glad to have Sam as a friend, relatively removed from Lena’s life and never involved in the dramas of her other friends or relationships. Sam had her own life to manage, her career and her daughter monopolising the vast majority of it, and it made her an easy friend to weave into Lena’s complicated life. No less cherished for the ease of things though.

 

            Working the overnight shift usually led to a few drunken patients, angry as they attempted to curse the Healers and nurses, and Lena was weary of them as midnight came and went. She hadn’t slept enough the last few days and found herself knocking back extra doses of potions and coffee in equal parts, forking over Knuts throughout her shift and tracking down Sam to hand her another cup. 

 

            While she always seemed to be at St Mungo’s, as an Attending, Lena’s shifts were typically only twelve hours these days. The arduous days of her Residency and the 48-hour shifts of her internship were behind her but Lena picked up as many hours as possible, frequently sleeping at St Mungo’s in an on-call room and picking up any burning pages on her cryptex. 

 

            However, this time, after her twelve-hour shift ended, she didn’t stick around to put in some overtime in the Alchemy Room, didn’t jump in on the new arrival of a critical patient as she left at eight o’clock on Saturday morning. She showered in one of the staff room bathrooms, dressed warmly in one of the jumpers Eliza had knitted her and a pair of jeans, and walked out onto the street before Apparating to Cornwall from the alleyway.

 

            Ordinarily, she would have gone home first and slept off her shift before seeing Kara. Ordinarily, she would have been pulled away for at least a few more hours of work, her dedication to treating as many people as possible an almost manic obsession at times, as if Lena was still proving her worth. That morning, she couldn’t think of anything else but seeing Kara, still a little keyed up about the disastrous full moon, and couldn’t stop herself from showing up on her doorstep at breakfast time to reassure herself that everything was fine.

 

            It was Eliza who answered the door when she knocked, jerking it open with a look of surprise on her face, which quickly turned to warmth. She was already dressed for the day, the knees of her jeans stained with grass and flour dusting the front of her shirt, and she quickly invited the young woman inside.

 

            “Lena! Come in, come in. You look tired; did you just get off work?”

 

            “Morning, Eliza. Yes, it wasn’t a long shift though. I just came to see-”

 

            “Right, of course. Kara!”

 

            The house was quiet, still relatively early in the morning, and Lena waited as she strained her ears to pick out the sounds of her girlfriend’s footsteps overhead. The hallway smelled of fresh mint, old wood and baking bread as she resisted shifting impatiently, a tightness to her throat as she allowed Eliza to coax her out of her cloak and set her bag down beneath the rack. She could hear Kara’s slow steps then, the sound of her bedroom door opening and the creak as she hit the top of the staircase.

 

            “Oh, hi,” Kara said with surprise, pausing momentarily at the top of the stairs before she descended quickly. 

 

            “I’ll put the kettle on,” Eliza said, giving Lena’s arm a quick squeeze before she moved on to the kitchen. “Have you eaten yet, Lena?”

 

            “I’m fine, thank you.”

 

            Moving to the bottom of the staircase, Lena watched Kara slow as she neared the bottom step, dressed in her pyjamas and surprised to see her. Leaning in, she gave Lena a quick peck, so fleeting that it could only have been intentional, and stepped back, gripping the end of the bannister as she averted her gaze.

 

            “I thought you’d be at home, sleeping.”

 

            Lena cleared her throat, trying to mask her nervousness with her usual nonchalance, giving Kara a wry smile, even as her girlfriend didn’t meet her gaze.

 

            “Yes, well, I wanted to see you first. It sort of … felt like you were trying to dump me last time we saw each other, so I just wanted to make sure that you didn’t get the wrong idea. You can’t get rid of me that easily.”

 

            Choking on a laugh, Kara hung her head, all sandy curls and bruised shadows beneath her eyes. She had such rounded edges to her shoulders from slouching and the constant exhaustion of her condition, and she hadn’t fully recovered from the full moon two nights prior. Especially not after the shock of a painful transformation after so many months of relative ease - as easy as it could be.

 

            Raising her head, she smiled unevenly, some of the tension bleeding out of her as amusement shone in her blue eyes. “Right, yeah, I sort of figured that out for myself when you refused to go. Come on then, you can sleep in my bed.”

 

            Turning around, Kara plodded back upstairs with Lena on her heels, moving into the small bedroom and shifting a few books and rolls of parchment off her bed and onto the narrow desk. Her bed was unmade, the sheets rumpled where she’d been lying on them, and she turned to Lena and appraised her outfit.

 

            “Do you want some pyjamas?”

 

            “Okay.”

 

            Fetching her an old pair of plaid flannel bottoms and a worn t-shirt, several sizes too big due to Kara’s penchant for baggy men’s clothes, she placed them in Lena’s hands, their fingers brushing before Kara stepped back. Sitting down on her sister’s bed, she was silent as Lena stripped off her clothes and changed, the smell of Kara’s detergent flushing her with delight as she folded her clothes and set them on the desk.

 

            “Are you joining me?” Lena asked, arching an eyebrow as she sank onto the edge of Kara’s bed.

 

            Running her fingers over the pilled sheets, Kara smiled wanly. “I only just woke up.”

 

            “Well, we don’t have to sleep.”

 

            “My mum’s downstairs.”

            

            “We can be quiet. Or if you don’t want to be, we can ward the room.”

 

            Brooding and quiet, Kara’s mouth twitched slightly and she sighed softly. “You should sleep.”

 

            Falling silent, Lena watched her across the scant feet between the beds, their knees almost touching as their legs filled the space. A yearning ache in her chest made her frustration flare up but, once again, she didn’t have the means to explain how she felt to Kara. She just wanted to feel close to her, feel something that was easy to decipher. For Lena, that was usually intense pain or intense pleasure. Uncomplicated, expected and familiar. 

 

            Raking a hand through her hair, she closed her eyes and blew the air out of her cheeks. “I can just go-”

 

            “Don’t go.”

 

            “Well, if you don’t want me here-”

 

            “Don’t be like that.”

 

            “Well, how about you tell me what I should do to make this not feel so … awkward. I thought we agreed- last time we said that it wouldn’t change anything but now you’re acting as if it- as if it does.”

 

            “It’s not changing anything,” Kara tersely replied, rubbing her forehead and then fixing her fringe. “I just- I’m trying to make sense of it. I need time to … be okay with what happened. I hurt you, almost killed you, and you just- you’re acting as if that’s nothing and I- that’s not nothing , Lena.”

 

            Moving off the bed to sink to her knees in front of Kara, Lena knelt between her thighs, cradling either side of her knees in her hands as she looked up at Kara with a mournful plea on her face. “It’s okay. I’m fine and it didn’t hurt and … I have suffered so much worse . It- it is nothing to me. What hurts me is …”

 

            Her throat closed up and she ducked her head, eyes squeezed shut as she struggled to articulate her feelings without sounding pathetic, without being too vulnerable. It was difficult and she couldn’t get the words out, the silence stretching on too long.

 

            “Tell me,” Kara softly encouraged her.

 

            Burying her face in the soft flannel of Kara’s thigh, Lena swallowed thickly, feeling her girlfriend’s fingers gently brush through her hair. “When you push me away,” she whispered, her voice oddly strained. “I don’t like it when you do that. When you try to leave, when you won’t touch me or- or look at me. I feel like I’m … being punished.”

 

            She felt Kara’s forehead rest against the crown of her head, her arms wrapping around her, not an easy feat with the awkwardness of their positions. Her voice was muffled as she talked into Lena’s hair. “I’m sorry. I’m not trying to punish you, I- I’m trying to protect you.”

 

            “You’re not a threat to me.”

 

            “I am. Maybe not right now-”

 

            “But I’m here right now. ”

 

            “And you should get some sleep. You look tired, darling,” Kara tenderly murmured, lifting her head and coaxing Lena’s up as well, her touch gentle as she thumbed the bruises beneath her eyes. 

 

            Kara’s mouth turned down at the corners with dissatisfaction, her gaze brooding for a moment before she ducked down to kiss Lena. This time it was lingering, soft and apologetic as Kara cupped her face in her rough palms, before drawing back and kissing her chastely twice more on the lips and once on her forehead. Eyes closing, Lena swallowed thickly.

 

            “I’m so tired,” Lena confessed. “I feel so … frustrated.”

 

            “It’ll all be better after some sleep. I promise.”

 

            Delaying a moment longer, Kara’s hands warm against her cheeks, Lena eventually let out a small sigh and pushed herself to her feet. Sinking onto Kara’s bed, she pulled the blankets over her and crossed her arms over her chest, staring up at the ceiling as Kara gestured for the curtains to close themselves and then climbed to her feet.

 

            Lena couldn’t make out the details of her clearly in the sudden gloom but she looked up at Kara’s shadowed figure looming over her before her girlfriend ducked down, thrown into focus. Her expression revealed nothing though as she tucked Lena in, lit a candle on the desk for light and then kissed her once more, leaving with whispered orders to rest.

 

            Despite her frustration, Lena found sleep surprisingly easy to come by. In Kara’s room, in her bed, in her pyjamas with her pillow that smelled like her, it was as close to being wrapped in her embrace without the physical act itself, and Lena found comfort in that. She was also tired, sleeping like the dead through lunch and into the afternoon, waking to a deep grey sky as the dreary day verged on dusk. 

 

            Sitting up, Lena rubbed her tired eyes and attempted to smooth her hair down before swinging her legs out of bed and standing. Changing back into her clothes, she set Kara’s pyjamas back in the dresser and flicked her wand at the bed to straighten out the sheets and pillows before blowing out the candle and padding out of the room.

 

            Walking downstairs, she was still waking up properly as she rounded the bannister, the sound of quiet conversation drifting from the kitchen with the smell of roast chicken and potatoes wafting towards her. Pausing on the threshold, she blinked owlishly as the two women faced her, Kara smiling softly from her seat, knees drawn to her chest with her chin propped on top. Eliza was whisking gravy on the stovetop and brightened at the sight of her.

 

            “Ah, we were just talking about whether or not to wake you for dinner. You must be starving. It’s chicken and roast potatoes tonight.”

 

            “Oh, um … thank you.”

 

            She hadn’t been anticipating staying for dinner, nor for sleeping in Kara’s bed either, but Lena shifted Bastet from a chair and sat anyway. Kara didn’t say anything but was watchful, her gaze piercing and questioning without the requirement of words, and Lena’s small smile seemed to be enough to reassure her that any lingering bad mood had been mitigated by a night of proper sleep. Lena’s worry hadn’t quite quelled but she didn’t feel as tense as she sat in the comfort of the kitchen, the back door cracked a fraction to let the cold air inside as the windows fogged inside.

 

            Helping to set the table, Lena nestled bowls of peas and carrots amidst the pitcher of lemon squash, while Kara carved the chicken and Eliza fetched the potatoes from the oven. Spooning food onto their plates, the three of them talked mostly of work, with Kara’s being rather vague due to the confidentiality of it, and Lena’s more dramatic, although still vaguely confidential. They spoke of the news as well and anything else that came to mind, Eliza planning a trip to Diagon Alley, Kara asking after a certain book, which Lena already had a copy of and promised to send Morrigan with it that night. It was peaceful and Lena felt content, that everything would return to normal after the ordeal two days ago. That was until there was a knock at the door.

 

            They’d finished eating, the three of them cleaning up in companionable silence as Eliza washed the dishes, Lena dried them and Kara put them away, an efficient operation until the knock came. Shaking soap suds off her hands and drying them on a tea towel, Eliza announced that she would get it as Kara moved to set a stack of plates down. As far as they were aware, Alex and Kelly were on their honeymoon and hadn’t scheduled an early return, which left them clueless as to who was at the door. Continuing their tidying up, albeit moving quieter to eavesdrop, Kara and Lena waited to see who it was.

 

            “Good evening, Mrs Danvers. My name is Cecil Lee, I’m here on behalf of the Werewolf Capture Unit. We're a part of the Beast Division of the Department for the Regulation and Control of Magical Creatures for the Ministry. May I come inside?”

 

            In the kitchen, Kara and Lena slowed, exchanging a glance as panic knifed through both of them. Whatever this was about could only bode bad for Kara, they knew that, regardless of the reason Ministry officials had shown up at that time of night. It was mostly dark outside now and Lena had to bite back the urge to whisper for Kara to sneak out the back door and Apparate to Dublin, to go far away until Lena could be sure there was nothing amiss here in Cornwall. She didn’t say a word though, Kara already moving out of the kitchen as Eliza cluelessly invited the trio from the Werewolf Capture Unit into the cramped hallway.

 

            “Mum?” Kara softly inquired, eyebrows rising as she walked closer. “What’s going on?”

 

            “I- Kara, these gentlemen are from the Ministry. The, uh, the Department for the Regulation and Control of Magical Creatures for the Ministry, did you say?” Eliza nervously informed her, wary gaze turning to the three men dressed in deep purple robes.

 

            “Yes, the Werewolf Capture Unit, from the Beast Division. And you’re Miss Kara Danvers, I presume?”

 

            Caution flickered across Kara’s scarred face as she gently cleared her throat, anxiously cracking her knuckles as she shifted uneasily. “Yes, sir.”

 

            “Date of birth twenty-second of September, nineteen sixty-two?”

 

            “Yes.”

 

            “Infected with Lycanthropy in nineteen seventy-four?”

 

            “Yes.”

 

            Brow furrowing, Lena stepped out of the kitchen and positioned herself beside Kara, crossing her arms over her chest. “What’s this about?”

 

            The man’s gaze shifted to Lena and he gave her an appraising look before gruffly clearing his throat, glancing down at a small notebook and then looking back up at Kara. “We’re here regarding a reported incident of an attack against a witch on the full moon of Wednesday, the twenty-second of March involving Miss Kara Danvers.”

 

            “Wha- that’s impossible, she was at St Mungo’s,” Eliza spluttered indignantly.

 

            “Unfortunately, ma’am, that isn’t corroborated by Healer reports at St Mungo’s. At least, not until the morning of the twenty-third.”

 

            Lena stiffened, bristling as she took a step forward, deliberately putting herself slightly in front of Kara as she unfolded her arms. “Thank you for your time, Mr Lee, but there seems to have been some sort of misunderstanding. I was with Kara the night of the full moon.”

 

            “And your name is?”

 

            “Lena Luthor.”

 

            The wizard nodded, removing a quill from his pocket and jotting down a note on the page before nodding again. “Well, Miss Luthor, if you would like to provide a statement at a later date, you can reach us at the Ministry. We’re on Level Four.”

 

            He fished out a business card and stepped forward to extend it to her. Grinding her teeth, Lena stared venomously at him, quietly seething. “That won’t be necessary. There’s nothing to state.”

 

            Shrugging indifferently, her extended the business card to Eliza, who meekly took it, and then smoothed his moustache before fixing Kara with a beady stare. “As for yourself, Miss Danvers, we have a duty to ensure that the magical community is safe from any threats, such as yourself. We’ll need you to come with us to answer some questions-”

 

            Anger lashed through Lena and she reached behind her, hand going to the back pocket of her jeans where her wand was stowed, fingers wrapping around the length of polished wood in a white-knuckled grasp as she anticipated not giving in without a fight. They would have to hex her into oblivion before she let them walk out of the house with Kara, treating her like some common criminal.

 

            But then wiry fingers wrapped around her wrist, stopping her from pulling her wand free, and Lena’s shoulders went taut as Kara stepped around her. She had a knack for making herself seem smaller and cowed, and Lena hated that with a passion at that moment, watching Kara meekly nod her head, murmuring a quiet, “of course, Mr Lee. I’m happy to cooperate.”

 

            “Kara,” Lena muttered, reaching out to grab her arm.

 

            Turning to her, Kara smiled faintly, already resigned to whatever they were going to subject her to, and she cupped the side of Lena’s head and kissed her opposite cheek, lips brushing her ear. “Don’t worry, I’ll be fine. Don’t do anything. Please.”

 

            A plaintive sound of indignation caught at the back of Lena’s throat as she tried to believe what she was hearing. How could Kara expect her to idly stand by and let them tow her off to the Ministry for questioning over something so trivial? It had been an accident, and a small one at that, barely a knick on Lena’s calf after all was said and done. There had been the potential for worse to happen but Lena had managed it and was none the worse for wear. There was only one person to blame for what was happening and she knew neither of them were standing in the cottage then, silently cursing her mother with every fibre of her being, knowing she was the cause of this.

 

            “I’m coming too,” Lena brazenly declared, grabbing Kara’s hand in a tight grip as she stared at the men, daring them to stop her.

 

            “‘Fraid not, miss,” one of them replied, chewing gum, “you’ll have to come when the office is open. That’ll be Monday morning. Nine o’clock.”

 

            Opening her mouth to protest, Lena snapped it shut a moment later when Kara gave her hand a firm squeeze. The whole time, Eliza was quietly trying to reason with this Cecil Lee, her face gone white with fear, her voice low and trembling as she pleaded. Extracting her grasp from Lena’s hand, Kara stepped forward and let her fingers brush her mother’s sleeve, mumbling a reassurance before she slipped her feet into a pair of shoes near the door, still dressed in her pyjamas as she covered them with a robe as well.

 

            With a backwards glance over her shoulder, Kara gave Lena a wavering smile, full of false bravado, before two of the men filed out, their stocky bulk blocking most of her from view. The other one lingered a second, dark eyes roving over Lena’s shockingly pale face as she curled her hands into fists and performed the greatest exercise in self-control since she’d broken off the kiss with Kara in that house in the Lake District the year before.

 

            “Bit of advice, love, you’re too pretty to waste your time with one of them,” he said in parting, giving her a sleazy smile as he stepped over the threshold of the cottage and gripped Kara’s arm.

 

            The four of them were whisked away a moment later and Lena was left floundering speechlessly in the doorway. The night air snatched at her as she stared blankly into the dark, Muggle lampposts casting an orange glow over damp pavements, the sound of distant cars and the voices of local teenagers in the field behind the cottage filling the stunned silence that followed. Eliza reached out and tugged Lena’s sleeve, pulling her inside and firmly shutting the door, resting her palm against the wood for a moment as her other hand covered her mouth.

 

            “Lena … if something happened the other night, I need you to tell me right now,” she said, speaking slowly but curtly. 

 

            Closing her eyes as she fell back against the hallway wall, tipping her head back as she felt as if her knees were going to buckle, all of this her fault once again, Lena couldn’t speak. Mouth a flat line, she shook her head slightly, feeling grey and nauseous as she scrambled for what to do next.

 

            “Lena-”

 

            Blinking rapidly, she stared at the older woman, who was no longer soft and warm but wooden with worry for her daughter, the lines of her face more prominent as she grasped a fistful of her greying hair, staring at Lena with an aching plea in her eyes. Mouth opening and closing, Lena’s throat felt dry and she had to look away, unable to meet Eliza’s gaze as she cleared her throat.

 

            “I don’t know what to tell you. They’re wrong, I-”

 

            Turning away from her, Eliza hurried into the living room and frantically rummaged through the clutter in the drawers and shelves of the hutch, finding a book and flipping through the pages before turning to the fireplace. She grabbed a handful of Floo powder, swishing her wand to douse the flames in the fireplace and then tossing down the gritty powder before dropping to her knees and speaking an unfamiliar address on the Floor Network. She only put her head in and Lena stared at the rest of her kneeling body as she waited, hand creeping up the sleeve of her jumper to gouge crescents into her scarred forearm as a lump lodged itself in her throat. 

 

            Waiting an agonising few minutes, Lena watched as Eliza eventually pulled her head back out of the fireplace and climbed to her feet. Looking exhausted as she turned, Eliza fixed Lena with a bleak stare. “Alex’s boss is going to help.”

 

            Relief cut through Lena at the update, the helplessness she was feeling mitigated somewhat by the thought that there were people who were in positions to help Kara. She might not have been of any use then but an Auror would know what to do. Unable to even form a response, her throat so tight, Lena just nodded, hovering with the uncertainty of not knowing if she was welcome there anymore, as tightlipped as she was about what had happened before she turned and walked into the kitchen without a word.

 

            Finishing the washing up, Lena wiped down the kitchen table as her hands shook, trying to make herself useful, trying to occupy the time, and then set the kettle on to boil. Making two cups of tea, she carried them into the living room and set them down on the coffee table before starting a new fire in the fireplace. The crackling of the flames filled the silence as she sat on the sofa across from Eliza, who was staring sightlessly into the fire as she worried about her daughter.

 

            They didn’t touch their tea and Lena was stiff and still on the sofa as her mind raced, every possible bad scenario passing through her mind, until Eliza climbed to her feet, taking their cups into the kitchen and making fresh cups. They did drink those, both of them sipping absentmindedly as they were left to their thoughts. It was an hour before a word was spoken.

 

            “She’ll be alright,” Eliza reassured Lena, sounding more confident than she looked.

 

            “I’m sorry,” Lena whispered to her lap, shoulders hunched and hands gripping her cup tightly as she expected the harsh backlash.

 

            Softly sighing as she rubbed her forehead, Eliza closed her eyes and was silent. Any further talk after that was sporadic, speculating about how long it would be until she was home, asking if they wanted another cup of tea, if anyone had seen her. All of the unknown details since Kara had stepped outside were making Lena jittery, a hollowness in her chest as she swallowed thickly and then swallowed again, the lump not going down. 

 

            It was past eleven when the front door opened and three witches traipsed inside with a gust of cold air. The bite of it shocked the two waiting witches to their feet, listening to the front door shut and the weary rasp of tired voices hanging up their cloaks. Lena was out of the living room before they could even manage that, her eyes landing on Kara as she pushed past Alex and Kelly, who were very obviously no longer in Greece, and engulfed her girlfriend in a hug, holding her desperately tight.

 

            “Are you okay?” she asked, unable to keep her voice from wobbling.

 

            “Fine,” Kara whispered into her hair, sounding tired.

 

            Pulling back to quickly assess her, taking in the shadows beneath her eyes but otherwise healthy appearance, Lena stepped away as Eliza quickly took her spot, fussing over her daughter as she kissed her cheek and cupped her face in her hands. Stepping further back, almost back in the living room, Lena rubbed her tired eyes as her shoulders slumped, the tension slowly bleeding out of her. Kicking off her shoes, Kelly squeezed her shoulder reassuringly as she passed her by and went into the kitchen.

 

            There was more tea, a tray laden with a pot and the cups as everyone congregated in the warmth of the living room. Alex didn’t sit, her arms folded over her chest as she glanced around expectedly. When no one said anything, she gestured helplessly, eyebrows rising.

 

            “Well? Is someone going to explain what the bloody hell is going on, or did we just have our honeymoon interrupted for no reason?”

 

            “What did they do to you?” Lena quietly asked Kara, practically glued to her side on the sofa, unable to tear her eyes free.

 

            Covering her knee with a hand, Kara squeezed gently and took a swig of tea. “They just asked me questions. It’s their responsibility to make sure werewolves are safe to be out in society. It’s fine, everything was cleared up and … that’s the end of it.”

 

            “Not bloody likely,” Alex scoffed. “I got J’onn to get the report from that nasty prick-”

 

            Wearily sighing, Eliza closed her eyes and knuckled a headache, “Alex.”

            

            “And it came from William Dey - yes, your William.”

 

            Kara rankled at him being referred to as her William, her ashen face flooding with pink as she shifted uncomfortably. “See? So this is all just … some rumour started by someone who dislikes me enough to report me.”

 

            The two of them knew it to be a lie but Lena was all too happy for Kara to lie to the other three women for the sake of peace and ease. Perhaps they would have gotten away with it too if Alex hadn’t seen the report. Her stare burned into her sister’s before it moved to Lena, who frowned slightly.

 

            “Not quite. Who the bloody hell is Eve Tessmacher?”

 

            Lena’s head sharply jerked to Alex, her eyebrows rising. “Eve Tessmacher?”

 

            “You know her?”

 

            “She’s my old Hogwarts Housemate,” Kara supplied. “Why?”

 

            A headache forming right in the middle of her brow, Lena sighed as she rubbed the tender spot and offered some more clarification. “She’s also a nurse at St Mungo’s.”

 

            “She’s shagging Mike, who, apparently, has broken up with Imra and given up on his mediocre Quidditch career, and is now playing three aside Quidditch on the weekends with someone called Jack Spheer-”

 

            Closing her eyes as her stomach sank, Lena went rigid as she listened to Alex continue, her anger a slow thing as it built and built, each word only adding fuel to the flames, stoking it hotter.

 

            “Who told William that she,” Alex gestured offhandedly to her sister, “bit you. So why would she make that up?”

 

            Drawing in a shaky breath as she steeled herself to lie convincingly enough to deceive them, Lena cleared her throat as her mouth turned down at the corners. “I’m not sure, but Kara certainly didn’t bite me.”

 

            From her seat, Eliza’s shoulders caved as a crestfallen look of understanding crossed her face. “She attacked you, didn’t she? I saw the blood on your jeans at St Mungo’s. You had no shoes, her things weren’t there either. That man from the Werewolf Capture Unit said that St Mungo’s couldn’t confirm Kara was admitted until the following morning.”

 

            Masking a wince, Lena felt her cheeks heat at the accusations behind Eliza’s words, while Kara hunched over beside her, hiding her face in her hands as she braced her elbows on her thighs. Reaching out to press a hand between Kara’s shoulder blades, Lena tried to reassure her while she managed the questions as things started to connect in Eliza’s mind.

 

            “I never said I was at St Mungo’s,” Kara gingerly replied, her head in her hands as she refused to look at anyone.

 

            “What do you mean you weren’t at St Mungo’s?” Alex demanded, having missed so much in just a few short days, scrambling to catch up with what had happened a few nights ago.

 

            Clearing her throat as she kept a protective arm around her girlfriend’s shoulders, Lena drew the ire of everyone else in the room to spare Kara having to explain, having the blame cast upon her. “We were at my place-”

 

            “Your place?” Eliza echoed with disbelief.

 

            “Last year, before the Wolfsbane trial ended, my mother found out about us. She wasn’t very … pleased , and she kicked Kara off the trial in an attempt to blackmail me into ending things. Um … obviously I refused and, well, I’d been working on the Wolfsbane trial for years so I knew how to brew it and I-”

 

            Kelly softly groaned, “you brewed an experimental potion and let her transform inside your flat?”

 

            Running her free hand over the thigh of her jeans in a sheepish manner, Lena swallowed thickly. “Yes.”

 

            “So, when you said they were offering free, ongoing treatment to trial participants once it had ended …” Eliza said to Kara, hurt and surprise colouring her voice at her daughter’s lies.

 

            Gesturing helplessly to Lena as her shoulders seemed to hunch over even further, Kara kept her head in her hand as she refused to look up. “Lena has been paying for it. She’s been brewing it for me.”

 

            “And Wednesday?”

 

            “I forgot to take a dose at the wedding - or I lost track of time and took it past midnight,” Kara corrected herself, still somewhat blurry on what had actually happened. “It wasn’t the potion; I took the same dose the month before and it was fine. But obviously, I need to take it every day for seven days or … it doesn’t work. We didn’t know until-”

 

            She couldn’t force the rest of it out so Lena picked up the threads of her explanation, her voice so small as she flushed beneath the scrutiny of the other witches that they all had to lean in to hear her properly. “We didn’t know until the full moon. I warded the doors of my office - that’s where I locked her in each month - but she got out and- and I got away but she nicked me. It’s nothing, just a small scratch on my leg, but I suppose Eve was working that morning and drew her own conclusions.”

 

            Lena finished without any further explanation as to what had transpired the night of the full moon, glaringly obvious gaps in her story that she knew would pick apart the whole thing if she was questioned about it. She didn’t want to reveal that she was an unregistered Animagus, didn’t want to implicate herself any further in dealings with unregulated magic, and was grateful that Kara was tight-lipped beside her. On the other hand, she was less grateful that Kara’s sister was a bull-headed Auror who was looking angrier with each passing second as the ensuing silence filled the living room.

 

            “I’m sorry,” Alex spluttered, her brown eyes wide with disbelief as she stared at her sister, “have you lost all common sense?”

 

            No one responded and Alex raked a hand through her hair. “Kara.”

 

            “What?” Kara snapped, finally looking up, dropping her hands from her face as her cheeks reddened. “What do you want me to say?”

 

            “What were you thinking?” Eliza softly exclaimed.

 

            “It was an accident , it wasn’t-”

 

            “Not about the full moon, about this- this whole plan. You’ve been lying to my face for months. I just- I’m at a loss for words right now, Kara, I really am so disappointed.”

 

            Throwing her hands up, Eliza shrugged helplessly as she shook her head, mystified and concerned. Cringing slightly, Lena swiped her thumb over her eyelids and exhaled softly.  “I’m sorry, Eliza, it was my idea. I convinced her to do it-”

 

            Making a low sound of annoyance at the back of her throat, Kara squeezed Lena’s knee. “Don’t blame yourself.”

 

            “No, I think she’s right to blame herself. And you too. Both of you. How could two such intelligent people come up with a plan so- so idiotic?”

 

            “Alex,” Eliza wearily warned her. “That’s enough now. Leave them be, it's been a long night.”

 

            “Mum.”

 

            Lena’s mouth twitched at the corners and she ran a hand through her hair, grimacing. “No, she’s right. It was reckless, I know that, but it was the only way to help. I just- I just wanted to help her and this was the best way-”

 

            “It wasn’t your place to decide what’s best for her.”

 

            “I’m her Healer. I’ve spent years trying to create a cure for her. What have you done?”

 

            “With all due respect, Lena, you’re not part of this family and this is none of your fucking concern.”

 

            “Don’t you speak to her like that,” Kara snapped, shrugging Lena’s arm off and climbing to her feet. “She’s not the problem here, she was just trying to help make things better for me. That’s all she’s ever done.”

 

            “Dragged off by the Werewolf Capture Unit on a Saturday night doesn’t sound like things have been made better for you, Kara. In fact, that looks a lot worse to me.”

 

            “Oh, so it’s better for me to scar myself every full moon-”

 

            “That’s not what I said. You could be in a cell at St Mungo’s after taking the Wolfbane Potion, transforming peacefully.”

 

            “No, I can’t! I’m not supposed to have access to it but she stole the recipe to keep me safe!”

 

            “What?”

 

            Their voices overlapped as they argued, talking over each other as Eliza exasperatedly tried to scold them. For Lena’s part, she was rigid on the sofa, shrinking in on herself as her heart started to pound, a cold sweat creeping over her as her breaths turned shallow. She raked her hands through her hair, pressed the heels of her palms against her temple and then over her ears, trying to blot out the raised voices. 

 

            A moment later, she shot to her feet and stalked out of the room, the front door the closest exit as she barged outside, leaving the door open behind her as she came to a stop on the damp pavement. The air was damp and cold, tasting faintly of salt as it blew in off the coast, and Lena wrapped her arms around herself as her shoulders went taut beneath her jumper and she scowled at the ordinary Muggle street, the bickering voices still audible but muffled now.

 

            She was only outside half a minute before the voices were suddenly silenced, the front door gently shutting before Kelly joined her on the pavement. Standing side by side, neither of them spoke for a long, awkward moment, Lena sullen and brooding as she shifted her weight and then cast Kelly a sideways glance.

 

            “I’m sorry about your honeymoon.”

 

            Mouth thinning, the other woman rubbed her eyes and sighed, gesturing off-handedly. “We’ll get another Portkey back in the morning.”

 

            Nodding, wondering whether she should offer to pay, Lena didn’t respond, hugging her arms tighter as the wind picked up. Kelly paced a few steps away, scuffing her shoes along the pavement as she swung her arms and then looked at Lena, giving her a grim look.

 

            “She doesn’t mean all of that,” she explained, gesturing to the front door. “She just worries about Kara and … well, Alex usually jumps to criticism first.”

 

            Shrugging indifferently, Lena didn’t know how to explain how she wasn’t any good at talking about her feelings either. Anger wasn’t always her first option but on a deep level of repression, Lena would rather yell at someone than be vulnerable about her true feelings as well. She also didn’t know how to explain that it didn’t matter what Alex said, that she could lay all of the blame at Lena’s feet and Lena wouldn’t raise a finger to defend herself, that she didn’t generally care for other people’s opinions of her, no matter the situation. Lena was under no impression that she was the Auror’s favourite person, although Alex had warmed to her considerably, and she had nothing to lose by pissing her off but everything to gain by doing what she could to protect Kara.

 

            “It’s fine.”

 

            “No, it’s not. It’s not your fault. I mean … you understand the legal ramifications if-”

 

            “Yes,” Lena tersely replied, eyelids shuttering.

 

            “Right, so you don’t need me to tell you-”

 

            “No, I don’t.”

 

            “Still, it’s not for Alex to say.”

 

            “It makes no difference to me. The only opinion I care about is Kara’s.”

            

            “Right.”

 

            They were silent for a few more minutes, listening to the quiet of night, Lena’s frustration creeping back in as she clenched her teeth and tried to rein it back in. She was interrupted before she could decide to go back inside, turning as the front door opened and footsteps stormed towards her.

 

            “We’re leaving,” Kara informed her, extending her cloak and bag. “Do you need to grab anything else?”

 

            Instead of taking her things, Lena stepped in and snagged Kara’s wrist, making her pull up short. Her expression softened with dismay and she reached up to cup Kara’s cheek. “Go back inside. Don’t leave without making it right.”

 

            “I-”

 

            “Please,” Lena quietly begged. “Don’t do this in my name.”

 

            Blue eyes swimming with tears behind her glasses, her fringe dishevelled and her gentle face furrowed with rare anger, Kara dashed her sleeve across her wet cheeks as she let out a rough breath. “None of this is your fault.”

 

            “It is. It’s the consequences of what we both chose to do, and I don’t care - I’d do it all over again to help you and of course they’re going to be mad but … they love you and they’re scared. Please go back inside and fix it.”

 

            Closing her eyes, Kara drew in a deep breath and then exhaled sharply, eyelashes fluttering as she met Lena’s pleading gaze and swallowed thickly. “Okay,” she hoarsely whispered.

 

            Relief cut through Lena as Kara turned and walked back inside. Feet bare as the cold burrowed up through the socked soles of her feet, Lena’s lip trembled slightly as she paced the pavement, feeling Kelly watching her. They didn’t speak though and five minutes later, the door opened again. When Lena glanced up, it wasn’t Kara stepping outside but Alex, who got her wife’s attention and jerked her head back to the cottage. Kelly slipped inside and shut the door, leaving the two of them alone as Alex cleared her throat and fished out a cigarette, lighting it and taking a drag before speaking.

 

            “Sorry about that.”

 

            “Did she tell you to come and apologise?” Lena snorted.

 

            “No, I’m well capable of acknowledging when I’m being an arse.”

 

            Nodding slowly as she buried her hands in the pockets of her jeans, Lena pressed her lips together for a moment. “I’m sorry as well. I know what we’re doing is risky, but … I just want to keep her safe.”

 

            “Did you really steal that man’s work to make it for her?”

 

            “Yes.”

 

            “She said you were stood down for it. Could’ve been sacked.”

 

            Lena shrugged quickly in response, her expression impassive. “I wouldn’t have cared.”

 

            Humming at the back of her throat as she took another drag of the cigarette, Alex exhaled pink smoke and frowned, her eyebrows drawing together. She cast Lena a bewildered look. “So she scratched you then?”

 

            “Mhm.”

 

            “And what does that mean for you?”

 

            “Rare steaks. A little scar on my leg.”

 

            “You sound like you don’t care.”

 

            “I don’t.”

 

            Pausing, Alex gave her a scrutinising look, as if trying to tell if Lena was truly that blasé about the whole thing or was lying to put on a brave face. Lena was being truthful though; it didn’t matter to her in the grand scheme of things. Alex must have seen that because she lowered the cigarette from her lips and folded her arms over her chest.

 

            “And you’re still here.”

 

            “Of course.”

 

            “Why?”

 

            With a scoff of laughter, Lena arched an eyebrow. “What do you mean why?”

 

            “That would’ve sent most people running for the hills, I’d imagine. Mind you, most people wouldn’t have touched a werewolf with a ten-foot broomstick, so maybe there’s something wrong with you.”

 

            “Maybe there is. Either way, I’m not going anywhere. Not even if she does bite me.”

 

            At Alex’s sharp look of warning, knowing that if Kara bit Lena that could lead to all sorts of potential trouble for her sister - especially if this is what a little scratch led to - Lena rolled her eyes and smiled impishly.

 

            “Which isn’t going to happen. Obviously.”

 

            “Right, well, friends then?” Alex mumbled around the butt between her lips, holding out a hand.

 

            Snorting, Lena stepped forward and took her hand, giving it a quick squeeze before dropping it again. “You should get back to your honeymoon.”

 

            “Right.”

 

            Alex stepped up to the door and opened it, crossing the threshold and leaving it open for Lena, who lingered on the stoop without entering. Kara was sitting on the bottom step with Lena’s things in her lap and rose to her feet, looking weak with exhaustion. Crossing over to her, Kara held out Lena’s cloak and Lena folded it over her arm, taking her satchel and slinging it over a shoulder. Her eyes strayed to Eliza, who was further down the hallway, hovering in the kitchen doorway.

 

            “I’m sorry, Eliza,” Lena murmured. 

 

            Clicking her tongue, Kara’s mother shook her head regretfully. “I wish you had told me when I asked the other day but thank you for taking care of her.”

 

            Nodding, Lena swallowed thickly. “I should get going. Thank you for dinner.”

 

            Turning to Kara, she opened her mouth but Kara gripped her hand, already shoving her feet into slippers, sulky and peeved as she cast her family cursive glances. “I’m staying at Lena’s tonight if you two want the beds. Goodnight.”

 

            Ushering her girlfriend outside without further farewells, Kara apparated them to Lena’s landing. It was silent and warm as they stood in the hallway, and it took Lena a moment to move, unlocking the door and stepping inside. She slowly put her things down, hanging her cloak up and removing her shoes, while Kara hovered just inside the doorway, looking around.

 

            “You tidied it all up already.”

 

            “It didn’t take long,” Lena wearily replied.

 

            Walking up behind her, she wrapped her arms around Kara and kissed the side of her neck. Letting out a breathless huff, Kara leaned back into her, tipping her head back. Her voice was gravelly with stifled emotion as she spoke softly. “I’m sorry.”

 

            “You have nothing to be sorry for.”

 

            “I do. I didn’t mean for you to get caught in the middle of it all. Alex was wrong-”

 

            “Alex was called back from her honeymoon by the news her sister had been dragged off by a Werewolf Capture Unit. I think she’s entitled to her feelings, given how confusing and shocking the whole thing was. Now, more importantly, are you okay?”

 

            Turning in her embrace, Kara wrapped Lena in a tight hug, burying her face in her shoulder. “I’m fine, I just- I’m sorry.”

 

            Before she could say anything else, Lena pulled back, taking in Kara’s wrinkled nose as she tried to fight back tears. “Don’t.”

 

            “I am. I’m sorry for making you worry. I’m sorry this relationship, being what I am, makes everything so hard.”

 

            “This relationship is not hard,” Lena whispered, reaching up to fix Kara’s fringe, her touch gentle. “Everything else is hard but this isn’t. You are … my peace in the middle of it all and you are so easy to love when you let me.”

 

            “Who could ever love a monster?” Kara murmured.

 

            “Who are you to decide who’s worthy of love?” Lena haughtily countered.

 

            Kara looked up through her lashes, mournful and fragile, and Lena leaned in to kiss the tip of her nose, then the corner of her mouth, where it turned up in the hint of a smile as Lena tried her best to banish her worries. Leaning in, Kara kissed her softly, her fingers caressing the side of Lena’s neck as she sank into her mouth.

 

            “Someone who’s undeserving of it. Especially by you.”

 

            It felt like a gut punch to Lena, hearing Kara’s doubts spoken to the darkness of the flat as they lingered in the entryway. Her stomach dropped unpleasantly and she had to swallow twice to make her voice work, coming out as an uneven rasp. “Why do you say that?”

 

            “My mind … is not very kind to me.”

 

            “Tell me what it says and I will correct it for you.”

 

            Kara let out a strained laugh, too loud in the stillness of the night. She nestled into Lena’s arms and her lips brushed Lena’s throat as she whispered her confession. “That I will never be good enough for you. That I have nothing to offer you.”

 

            “I will be forever indebted to you for giving me this thing between us, for being the first person ever to treat me kindly, to return my love. You have offered me … so much more than you can ever begin to imagine. I-”

 

            Lena faltered, squeezing her eyes shut as she tipped her head back. Her throat felt tight and she thought she might cry. She almost wanted to, wanted to feel the ordinary weakness of displaying that act of emotion so she could feel more normal about it all, but even though her eyes prickled and burned, there was nothing more than a faint sheen as she tightened her hold on Kara.

 

            “I love you, you know, regardless of what you think you deserve. Falling in love with you is like going home, except … I never had anywhere that felt like home until I met you. I couldn’t love you more if I tried, only better. I don’t know if- if I love you properly because … I never had anyone to show me how, but I love you as much as I can. I’m sorry if I’m failing at it.”

 

            “There’s no failure in loving someone, and your love … it’s so gentle , so kind. It eases the ache in my soul a little and just the sight of you makes me feel relieved and I’m not really sure why but you just- you bring a warmth to my life that doesn’t exist without you in it. I’m only ever at my happiest when I’m with you. I just- I feel like I’m failing at proving myself worthy of you; every time I come into your life … I just bring more problems.”

 

            “You’re not a problem, you’re the only good thing that’s ever happened to me. I promise you that.”

 

            “Another promise?” Kara weakly laughed into her shoulder.

 

            “As many as you’d like.”

 

            “Let me make you one too; I promise you’ll never be without a home again.”

 

            “Then let me make us some tea and then we’ll get into bed and you can tell me what happened, and I’ll tell you all of the ways they were wrong before your mind gets the wrong impression and makes you believe whatever nonsense those pricks were spouting, and then we’ll put it behind us and go to sleep and everything will be fine in the morning. It’ll be just you and me and our promises, and hasn’t that always been enough?”

 

            “You have always been enough."

Chapter 39

            Grey-faced with exhaustion, and ten hours into her shift, Lena was hunched over the gangly body of a fifteen-year-old boy who had come in in Hufflepuff robes, sent in via Madam Pomfrey for trying to charm himself taller. The work was slow but methodical, shrinking his bones and repairing the splintered pieces and torn muscles and ligaments from the botched spell, and the quiet of the Theatre was soothing as she breathed in the medicinal tang of antiseptic in the frigid room. She’d already been at it for three hours and her back was aching, the toll of the intricate charmwork to undo the damage leaving her clammy and gritty-eyed as she worked carefully. She had two Resident Healers with her as well, their questions long since dried up as the procedure dragged on, and after the late night spent worrying over Kara, Lena was itching to finish up.

 

            The procedure ended up running into overtime, her twelve-hour shift turning into fourteen by the time she’d managed to repair all of the damage, an unassuming teenager of short stature laid out on the table, ready to be taken to the Charms Ward. Emerging from the Theatre, shedding her dragonhide gloves and the mask and scrub cap, Lena washed her hands and dismissed the Residents with instructions for the patient’s care, before she left to write up her own patient notes, massaging the tenderness in her neck as she walked through the hallways. 

 

            At the nurses’ station on the Fourth Floor, she requested her patient’s file and stifled a yawn as she dutifully started to detail the procedure, toying with the idea of fetching a cup of coffee from the tearoom upstairs to get her through the last legs of her shift. She would be another hour at least, a few things to check up on before changing and Apparating home, and she hadn’t been able to catch so much as a wink of sleep in an on-call room all day, the effects of the last Invigorating Potion she’d knocked back wearing off and leaving her rundown and exhausted. As absorbed as she was in her note-taking, Lena wasn’t so unaware of her surroundings to not notice the arrival of someone else.

 

            Stiffening as the tall figure in green scrubs, fresh from a procedure in one of the theatres, stepped up next to her, Lena didn’t have to look up from her patient file to know who it was. Her body had a visceral reaction to her mother’s presence, that hair-raising feeling of dread stealing over her, and she didn’t rise to the bait as she continued to write as her mother likewise dealt with her own patient file. After a tense minute, her purpose became apparent.

 

            “Why have I heard a rumour that you’ve been bitten by a werewolf?” Lillian tersely asked, her voice deathly quiet as she fiercely scribbled notes with her quill, the nib gouging holes in the paper. 

 

            Lena’s stomach plummeted at her mother’s words and it took her a moment to clear her throat, mouth dry and her hand trembling slightly as she finished off her own patient notes. Stowing her quill in her robe pocket, Lena swallowed thickly.

 

            “One of your nurses has been gossiping, but that’s all it is, a rumour.”

 

            Silent for a tense moment, Lillian’s fury was palpable even before she responded. “And what is the basis for this rumour?”

 

            “I would imagine the basis would rather obviously be that I’m seeing a werewolf, so …”

 

            “And that’s all there is to it?”

 

            “I think I would have wound up in a bed if I’d been bitten. I’m sure that rumour would have reached your ears within the hour if I’d been admitted.”

 

            “If I find out that you are lying-”

            

            “I’m not,” Lena interrupted, raising her head and turning to face her mother. Her expression was the blank look of someone who had already grown weary of the conversation, and that only served to make her mother’s anger that much colder. “Lock me in a cell on the next full moon if you want proof.”

 

            “I might just do that.”

 

            Her blood ran cold at her mother’s words, rising to Lena’s challenge with a cold look of amusement in her pale eyes. Lena didn’t doubt that Lillian would have her locked up in a cell but she’d been in them firsthand, knew the smell of blood, fear and bleach that infused the walls of the fortified rooms in the basement all too well, and it was a prospect that chilled Lena. Afraid of the dark from the endless hours of punishment in the cellar at her family’s manor house, Lena knew the rank odour of the cells would only worsen that fear. Not to mention, if she was in a cell, she wouldn’t be able to look after Kara.

 

            Whatever her mother read on her face only seemed to please her though, a thin smile at the corners of her lips as her eyes shone bright with triumph. Arching an eyebrow, Lillian closed her file, set it in the tray piled with the rest, and swept off without another word, her threat hanging over Lena as she was left to worry. She had the dreaded feeling that her haughty indifference would come back to bite her in the arse by the next full moon and Lena bit her tongue hard enough to taste blood as she silently berated herself for trying to make a fool of her mother. Whenever Lena assumed she’d gained the upper hand, Lillian always made a point of proving she hadn't. 

 

            Swallowing a curse, she closed her patient’s file and added it on top of her mother’s file, staring flatly at the retreating figure as the Healers, nurses and porters moved out of her way. She cut an intimidating figure and Lena’s gaze was surly as her mouth flattened, glaring daggers at Lillian’s back. Burying her hands in the pockets of her robe, Lena stalked off in the opposite direction, keen to put as much difference between them as possible.

 

            It was just past ten o’clock and her bed was looking more and more desirable as she did a quick check-in with the Residents on her service and then made her way to the Attending locker room. Shedding her robe and scrubs, she changed into clean clothes and left her stethoscope and the contents of her pockets in her locker before slinging her satchel over her shoulder and leaving St. Mungo’s before she could get called into a consult or an incoming trauma.

 

            Apparating to the landing outside her front door, she stared at the comforting familiarity of the engraved wood and let herself into the dark flat. With a careless gesture, she lit the candles scattered throughout the flat and kicked off her shoes, letting her belongings fall where she dropped them, to be picked up some other time. Taking a hasty shower beneath the stream of water hot enough to turn her skin pink, Lena barely spared the time and energy it took to pull on pyjamas, flicked her fingers at the curtains, which drew themselves together, and lit the lamp at the bedside to alleviate the dark, a comforting low glow suffusing the room. Crawling into bed, she pulled the covers over herself and was out almost as soon as her head hit the pillow.

 

            She was up early the next morning, feeding Morrigan and sending her off with a short letter to Kara before she had two cups of coffee and got ready for work. On-call, Lena ended up dealing with several emergency admissions before her shift had even ended, no end in sight as she worked right through midnight, back-to-back procedures leaving her wrist-deep in the chest cavity of an old witch before she managed to catch several hours of rest in a tucked away room. Dry-eyed and dead on her feet, she was still there the following morning for her next twelve-hour stint, a few more potions hastily swallowed to keep her going and multiple sandwiches from the tea room sustaining her. It ended up being four days before she saw Kara again, itching to lay eyes on her girlfriend and reassure herself that all was well.

 

            Kara Apparated to her doorstep straight from the Department of Mysteries, smelling of ink and paper as she swept inside in her blue robes. She shed it to reveal her knitted vest over a baggy men’s shirt tucked into tweed pants, and Lena smiled as she gave her a slow kiss before rubbing an ink stain off her chin as she laughed. 

 

            “Busy day?”

 

            “Like you wouldn’t believe,” Kara wearily exclaimed before pausing, “well, I suppose a Healer would. These are for you.”

 

            Producing a slightly rumpled bouquet, Kara gave her a crooked smile and Lena’s heart glowed with warmth as she took the flowers and kissed her again. Setting the flowers in a vase of water, Lena eyed the paper bag of Chinese food she’d had delivered and glanced over her shoulder at Kara as she arranged the flowers.

 

            “What are you thinking? Dinner and straight to bed, or are we having a drink or two?”

 

            Coming up behind her, Kara wound her arms around Lena’s waist and rested her chin on her shoulder. Her voice was a warm rumble felt where they touched as she replied. “A drink or two. I want to hear about your week.”

 

            Lena let out a rough sound of frustration as she extracted herself from her girlfriend’s arms and fetched a half-empty bottle of Firewhisky and two clean glasses. The glasses clinked as she carried them over to the coffee table, Kara following on her heels as she set down the paper bag and started to remove the containers.

 

            “So … not a good week then?”

 

            Giving her a surly look, Lena sank to the rug and uncapped the bottle of Firewhisky, pouring out generous measures and taking a quick sip of hers as she felt her anger rear back up. “I have something to tell you. It’s about the next full moon and … something to maybe expect-”

 

            “Is it- is it a … side effect? Something to do with the scratch-”

 

            Surprise rippled across Lena’s face as she quickly shook her head, rubbing her forehead. “No. No, it’s nothing like that.”

 

            Quiet as she waited for Lena to elaborate, Kara started peeling back the foil edges of the containers, lifting the lids off to reveal the steaming dishes of their usual order. Seething for a moment, Lena had another sip of her Firewhisky, her eyes hard as she stared at the coffee table, and Kara laid a hand on her knee to pull her from her brooding. Green eyes, wounded and apologetic, met Kara’s searching gaze.

 

            “A rumour has spread around the hospital that I was bitten. Courtesy of Eve Tessmacher, of course. That rumour has found its way to my mother-”

 

            “Oh,” Kara murmured, sinking onto the floor as she felt her stomach drop.

 

            “Who doesn’t quite believe me when I say I wasn’t bitten. Or maybe she knows I’m telling the truth but is just being … well, a cunt, for lack of a better word. Either way, she might just take my suggestion to find out for herself to heart, so …”

 

            “You mean … lock you up at St. Mungo’s?”

 

            Kara’s tone was quietly horrified, her hatred for those cells even deeper than Lena’s fear of being locked inside there. At least Lena’s visits had been for the purpose of her patients, but Kara’s had always been for the agonising night of tearing herself to bits, and she couldn’t imagine anyone locking their own daughter in one of them out of spite.

 

            “She can’t do that,” Kara firmly continued, taking Lena’s silence for confirmation.

 

            “There’s a clause in my employment contract that I have to be fit for duty. Under that, I’m sure ruling out Lycanthropy so I can work future full moons will fit the bill. It’s fine, as soon as the moon rises and I’m still human, she’ll have her proof. Shouldn’t take more than five minutes to clear my name. I’m not worried about me though-”

 

            Quick to cut her off, a pain in her chest, Kara reached out to cup Lena’s face in her palms. “Don’t even think about me.”

 

            Giving her a small smile, Lena closed her eyes. “Of course I’m going to think about you. I can’t leave you at home by yourself and-”

 

            “I’ll be going to St. Mungo’s as well,” Kara quietly interrupted her, dropping her hands and bowing her head slightly.

 

            “No, you’re not coming with me-”

 

            Fiddling with her fingers, Kara swallowed thickly. “No, I’m not going with you,” she whispered. “I’m going regardless of whether she makes you do that. I- that can’t happen again. What happened last week … I can’t go through that again. I can’t put everyone else through it either, least of all you, so …”

 

            Lips parting as her face went slack with surprise, pale and defeated as her shoulders slumped, Lena slightly shook her head. “What, you’re … going to go in a cell every month? You can’t mean that. That’s- I- no. No, I’m not going to let you do that to yourself. This is different to going because you don’t have any other choice - you have a choice.”

 

            “I do have a choice, and I’m choosing to go there.”

 

            “But-”

 

            “Please,” Kara softly cut her off, closing her eyes as her mouth flattened. Swallowing thickly past the dryness of her throat, she was silent for a moment as Lena stared at her, aghast and pleading. “Don’t try to change my mind.”

 

            Expression hardening, Lena drained the rest of her glass, welcoming the searing path down her throat, and set it down gently on the coffee table as she retained control, even as her insides knotted themselves and her throat tightened around the urge to scream. She flexed her fingers, a nervous tic from when her mother had broken them years ago, and folded her arms over her stomach, cupping her forearms. Absentmindedly, she dug her thumbnail into the cotton of her shirt, until she could feel the dull ache of her skin gouged by the act.

 

            “Don’t do that,” Kara whispered, reaching out to pry Lena’s hand away from her arm. 

 

            Giving her hand a quick squeeze, Kara watched her closely and Lena pulled her hand free, rubbing her eyes with the heels of her palms. “Let’s eat.”

 

            She quickly started to portion out her food and refilled her glass, drinking down half of it and then picking up her fork. Shovelling in mouthfuls of fried rice and chips smothered in curry sauce, Lena brooded as Kara ate at a slower pace beside her, shoulders slumped with dismay. For all their intent to talk about their week, no conversation was forthcoming and the silence dragged on, slightly awkward as Lena stewed and Kara sheepishly sat beside her.

 

            Lena finished eating first and helped herself to another glass, hoping it would take the edge off her frustration, and as soon as Kara set her fork down she was on her feet, picking up both plates and carrying them to the kitchen. With a sigh, Kara pushed herself to her feet and followed after her, shoulders tense as she slowly rubbed her palms together.

 

            “You’re angry.”

 

            “Obvious, is it?” Lena sarcastically replied, her voice low and shaking slightly as she set the dishes in the sink.

 

            “It’s not like I haven’t spent the night there before.”

 

            “The difference is you’ll be conscious this time. You’re not going to wake up the next morning with the memory of what happened, you’ll be experiencing it as it happens.”

 

            Pushing her glasses up her nose, a muscle twitched in Kara’s jaw as she found herself growing peeved. “I don’t need you to explain my condition to me.” Hesitating, Kara licked her lips before continuing, her voice meek as she braced herself. “And I won’t be conscious.”

 

            Lena had kept her back to Kara up until that point, but she whirled around with blatant anger in her eyes then. “No.”

 

            Shrugging helplessly, Kara grimaced. “I can’t take the potion-”

 

            “No!”

 

            “They’ll know you’ve been brewing it-”

 

            “You are taking the potion.”

 

            “You’ll get in trouble.”

 

            “I don’t give a fuck what happens to me. You are not clawing yourself to bits for my sake. Have you lost the plot?”

 

            Kara’s eyes widened as Lena advanced on her, cheeks flushed pink and a finger angrily stabbing at her chest. Mouth opening and closing, Kara shrank back and then seemed to straighten, standing her ground. They stared at each other, both pink-cheeked and stubborn to the core, and it was a tense minute of silence, the hardness of their eyes, unwavering, seeming to will the other to cave first. 

 

            “Kara,” Lena achingly murmured, her shoulders going slack as she broke first. “I mean it. You want to have them lock you away in a cell once a month? Fine. But I am begging you, please take the potion. At least do that.”

 

            Her face was bone white and her eyes were wide with panic, her chest rising and falling quickly. Guilt lashed through Kara and she cringed as she ducked her head, nudging her glasses up as she rubbed her tired eyes. After only the briefest hesitation, Kara nodded.

 

            “Okay. I’ll take the potion.”

 

            Relief flooded through Lena and she nodded, turning back around and moving over to the sink. She set the dishes to wash themselves, still irritable and listened as Kara put a record on the old gramophone, filling the flat with the sound of music. Standing at the sink, Lena had her palm pressed to her forehead as she breathed evenly, trying to slow her breaths, and Kara came up behind her, setting her empty glass in the sink and then cradling Lena’s hips in her hands.

 

            “Dance with me.”

 

            Resisting the gentle tugging for a moment, Lena eventually sighed and let Kara turn her, her eyelids shuttering as she felt annoyance pulse through her. Giving her girlfriend a sulky look through her lashes, she let Kara take her hand and put it on her shoulder, before taking the other one up and holding Lena close. They swayed with the music for a bar and Kara touched her forehead to Lena’s.

 

            “I’m sorry for upsetting you.”

 

            Sighing, Lena pulled back to look at her. “Don’t be. Just don’t make any other idiotic decisions.”

 

            “I’ll try my best, but no promises.” Kara said with a crooked grin.

 

            Rolling her eyes, Lena fought back a smile and pressed herself closer to Kara, arm around her shoulders and chin on top. Kara moved them in a slow circle and then pulled away, one hand holding Lena’s at length before she made her duck beneath it to spin her around, laughter coaxed from her. Kara’s laugh was easier and Lena couldn’t hold onto her annoyance as she was pulled back in. 

 

            Kissing the underside of her jaw, Kara murmured another apology and Lena closed her eyes, lips parting as she wove her fingers through Kara’s curls. Head lolling to the side, she felt soft lips kiss a warm path along the curve of her throat and clutched her girlfriend tighter.
