Eagerly rushing through to the Entrance Chamber and through the correct door, she had to cast charms before levitating the brains out of the potion, one at a time as set them on a set of scales, adding weights to balance them out, jotting down numbers as she measured them from frontal lobe to occipital lobe, central sulcus to the base of the cerebellum, right to left hemisphere and the length of the spinal cord. 

 

            By the time she finished, it was noon and her stomach was rumbling, folding an interdepartmental memo for her sister and meeting Alex upstairs at the stand in the Atrium with a sign reading Ministry Munchies . They ate their sandwiches sitting on the edge of the Fountain of Magical Brethren before Alex was called off to a disturbance in Dorset and Kara was squirrelled away back down on Level Nine to sit in on a project meeting for the others assigned to the Brain Room’s mystery of thought. That got her through most of the afternoon and then she was handed a list of books to recover in the Archives, a sprawling room of endless books that put the Hogwarts library to shame. The remainder of her shift was spent combing through the shelves to find the texts on the list, flipping through chapters, taking notes of anything that caught her eye, tabbing important pages and referencing chapters. She was so consumed by her work, engrossed in long essays on magical theory, that she put in a few hours of overtime, dry-eyed and stiff-necked by the time she closed her latest book. Packing up her things with the intent to get back to it all tomorrow, she made her way through the office, nodding farewell to those still hard at it, and went home.

 

            For the next two weeks, Kara was completely consumed with work, Lena and thinking about the house. She thought about it in the shower, on her lunch break, before bed and at dinner with Lena, where they ate Chinese food and listened to music. She thought about it when she helped Eliza weed the garden as September was ushered in, and when she went out for drinks with her friends and Lena and Sam, her hand on her girlfriend’s knee as she sipped her ale, and when Lena came over for a roast dinner with her family, all of them crammed into the small kitchen. Once she was sure she’d thought about it enough, and then given it the extra few days before she had dinner plans with Lena at her flat, Kara had almost certainly made up her mind.

 

            She’d cooked for them, getting to Lena’s early, letting herself in and doing some laundry for her, cleaning the owl perch, wiping down the counters as a chicken roasted in the oven, the windows turning a velvety blue as dusk crept in and the warmth of the flat steamed up the glass. Lena arrived home as Kara was shaking the roast potatoes, still dressed in her green scrubs in her haste to get home, the top tucked into the pants and a cloak slung over her arm, bag over her shoulder. Looking a little tired, she smiled at Kara and gave her a light kiss before excusing herself to shower.

 

            Reemerging, pink-cheeked, hair slightly damp at her hairline, Lena crossed over to her and kissed her properly. Smiling into it, Kara’s eyelids fluttered and she had to brace herself on the kitchen counter behind her, her other arm winding around Lena’s waist. Touching her forehead to Lena’s as they broke apart, Kara softly laughed.

 

            “Hello, you.”

 

            “How was your day?”

 

            “Ah, you know,” Kara shrugged, “very dense, very repetitive, very secretive. It was great!”

 

            Smiling, Lena pulled back and touched her fingers to Kara’s cheek. “Good.”

 

            “And how was yours?”

 

            “Very long, very busy, very tiring. It was also great.”

 

            Kara smiled, feeling a thrum of nervousness as she fiddled with her fingers. She’d come with a purpose today, not just to sit and talk about work and if Lena was free for drinks with her friends, or had she seen that article in The Daily Prophet, and it was taking all of Kara’s self-control to ease into it with dinner first. If they’d both had good days, she hoped that their talk would make it even better, but there was that worry as well, that Kara wouldn’t be able to come up with the money for Lena to live within her current means, that Lena would try to fob her off with made up numbers so she could pay less, that living together would reveal the true depths of their disparities, from money to health. 

 

            “I got a letter this morning,” Lena continued, pulling away. “Drink?”

 

            “Sure.”

 

            “Coffee okay?”

 

            “Perfect. Who was it from?”

 

            As Lena moved over to the kettle, she sighed. “Andrea.”

 

            “Oh. Really? What did she want?”

 

            “She asked if we would like to go for drinks.”

 

            “Would you?”

 

            Considering it for a second, Lena shrugged indifferently. “I don’t know.”

 

            Leaning against the island counters, Kara folded her arms over her chest, mouth thinning at the corners. “Why not?”

 

            Turning, Lena gave her a pointed, withering look, and Kara sighed. Expression softening with an aching plea, Kara’s shoulders slumped. “Come on, it’s been long enough. Don’t ignore her for my benefit, alright?”

 

            “Why does it matter to you so much if I’m friends with her or not?”

 

            “I just- she cares about you, and I don’t want you to lose someone who cares about you because of me. There was a time when we weren’t friends but she was there for you when you needed her to be, so I can’t help but like her for it. I’d hate to come between you two now.”

 

            “But she wasn’t there for you when I needed her to be.”

 

            “She was! She could’ve sacked me after everything that went down at the Lake District, but she didn’t because you asked her not to. And then I quit.”

 

            “You quit to spare her having to sack you!”

 

            Crossing over to her, Kara cupped her arms and let out a scoff of laughter. “I’m glad I quit! Best thing that could’ve happened to me, to be honest. I’ve got my job back, I love what I do like I never loved any of the other ones, I’m happy. I don’t hold it against her because I know she was already doing me a huge favour by keeping me on as long as she did. Say yes to drinks. I’d like to go - we could invite Sam too.”

 

            Giving her a torn look as she frowned, Lena’s mouth thinned. In response, a smile spread across Kara’s face and she raised her eyebrows. “Come on, admit that you miss her.”

 

            “I do miss her,” Lena relented.

 

            “Then stop being so stubborn and just say yes to drinks. No harm in trying to patch things up, is there? I mean, look at us . Now, I have something else to talk about and I think you’ll like it more.”

 

            Rolling her eyes, Lena turned to the kettle, whistling faintly on the stove, and made their cups of coffee. Crossing the open flat, Kara took a seat, feeling her stomach swoop slightly as she studied her girlfriend. She could tell that Lena was itching to know what she wanted to talk about by the fleeting, sideways glances she threw at her while making their coffee.

 

            “So?” she probed after Kara remained silent.

 

            “Come sit,” Kara urged her, a serious look on her face as she patted the cushion beside her.

 

            Sinking onto the sofa, folding one leg beneath her as she sat on it, Lena raised her eyebrows in a silent question as she raised her cup of coffee to her mouth. Taking a sip, Lena balanced her cup on her thigh, and Kara reached out, shuffling closer, to splay her hand over the side of Lena’s leg, staring down.

 

            “I’ve been thinking. About the house.”

            

            “Oh. Have you figured out what you want to do?”

 

            Deliberating, Kara’s face furrowed with thought. “Um … so, I just have a few questions first. So … you own it, obviously, but what about other expenses?”

 

            “Like what?”

 

            “Renovations, rent, groceries, furniture, insurance?”

 

            “Well, I can take care of most things. If you’d like to pay for groceries-”

 

            “I need to pay for more than that. It might not be mine by legal right, but I need to contribute … something to it if I’m living there.”

 

            “Oh, well, it would be yours too. I’ll put you-”

 

            “I can’t let you do that.”

 

            “Why not? I can’t ask you to move in with me and not give you any security; if something went wrong, it would give you a claim-”

 

            “No, thank you. I’m not saying it out of pride but for your own benefit. Just think about what sort of trouble your mum could stir up if she finds out we’re living together and my name’s on the deed. I don’t want more trouble - for either of us. At least if I’m paying rent, it gives me some sort of stake.”

 

            “Fine, I can accept leaving you off the deed, but you’re not paying rent. I haven’t spent a Knut on that place, so it wouldn’t be fair to make you pay to live there. In line with that, if your name isn’t on the deed, you shouldn’t have to pay to fix the place up or insure it. Especially if you’re not set on moving in yet.”

 

            A quick, bemused smile crossed Kara’s face, a crinkle where the bridge of her nose met the divot between her eyebrows. “Lena, I- of course I’ll move in with you, I- okay, I admit, I hadn’t given much thought about the future - ever - but that’s only because … well, things have always been more complicated than I would’ve liked, so it always seemed less painful to focus on the present.”

 

            “What about the future is painful?”

 

            Giving her a thin smile, Kara’s eyelids shuttered and she let out a resigned sigh. Reaching across the gap to snag her coffee from the table, Kara took a sip and then pressed her lips into a flat line. She was stalling, ruing the turn in conversation.

 

            “It’s painful to think that … one day you might come to your senses and realise that you don’t want to settle for me.”

 

            “Settle?” Lena choked out, unabashed shock crossing her face. She looked as if she’d been slapped.

 

            There was a bitter smile on Kara’s face, but no resentment, only gentle acceptance, and she shrugged nonchalantly. “I think everyone who doesn’t know the truth would wonder what you see in me, as poor and as scarred as I am, and everyone who does know the truth would maybe know what you see in me, but also know that you settled . I think even Alex, as much as she loves me, would admit to that.”

 

            They’d been sitting so close, leaning towards each other as they spoke, but Lena withdrew, shrinking away from Kara as she set her coffee cup down on the floor and rose to her feet. Pacing away a few steps, Lena was silent as Kara stared at her back, watching as she bowed her head, facing the window but not looking out of it.

 

            “That’s a very unkind opinion to have of me - and your sister,” Lena eventually said, her voice hoarse and thick, evidently wounded.

 

            Mouth opening and closing, Kara blinked and then hurriedly climbed to her feet. “Wha- no, I wasn’t saying it’s a bad thing. It’s the least I expect-”

 

            “What, because I’ve settled before? You think I’d do it again, to you?”

 

            Pale cheeks were turning pink with anger now and Kara faltered, standing beside the sofa as she looked at Lena with wide eyes, confused by how badly her words were being misinterpreted. Things never managed to come out correctly around her though; that had always been their problem in the past, but they’d endeavoured to not repeat it in the future.

 

            “No,” Kara vehemently objected, frustration shooting through her. “I don’t think you will, I just- I don’t like to think of the future because I’m worried that you might. What do you think it’ll be like in ten years? I’ll look like I’m nearing fifty and you’ll still be mistaken for thirty, so young and beautiful. How am I not supposed to consider that? If that’s something you want to settle for? What else is one supposed to call it?”

 

            “Love. Is it so difficult for you to believe that I love you? That I’m not as shallow as you paint me out to be?”

 

            “I don’t think you’re shallow,” Kara scoffed.

 

            “No? Then why-”

 

            “Because I’m scared! Aren’t you scared?”

 

            The breath was forced from Lena’s lungs as she gestured limply with a hand, a barely audible huff of laughter in the exhale. “Scared of staying with you? No! The only thing that scares me is losing you.”

 

            Her voice faltered as she finished and Kara floundered for a moment before she was spurred forwards, reaching out to take Lena’s hand. Guilt and agony warred on her face and her shoulders slumped with dismay. “I’m not going anywhere.”

 

            “But I am? In this future you’ve made up for us, I would never stay?”

 

            “I didn’t know what future I would make up for us. I told you, I’d never given it much thought, not because I didn’t want to but I just- I didn’t want to get my hopes up. I think the last time I planned for the future was deciding I wanted to be an Unspeakable after school. If I’d thought about what I’d wanted, of course you would be there, you’d stay.”

 

            Looking vulnerable, Lena pursed her lips in a look of discontent, lifting Kara’s hand to her face and pressing it to her cheek as she leaned into the touch. “Then think about it and let me know once you’ve decided what you want.”

 

            “I did think about it. I’ve spent the last two weeks thinking about it.”

 

            “Kara-”

 

            Removing her hand from beneath Lena’s, Kara backed away and sank onto the sofa, throwing her hands up in frustration. “You want to know what future I imagined for us? Fine . We do up your mum’s house and move in together. The kitchen cupboards are yellow, our bed sheets are blue and we have a green front door. We have all of our books on the same shelves in the study and we share the desk; you like drinking tea there while you research a cure.” 

 

            Lena had drawn closer as Kara babbled, her expression unreadable as she lowered herself to the sofa beside Kara, sitting close, arm braced against the back of the sofa as she angled towards her girlfriend, eyes flitting all over her face. 

 

            “My broomstick is in the mudroom and- and you scold me for tracking mud through the house after our friends have come over for five-aside Quidditch. There’s always music playing and we fix up the garden and have everyone over for parties in the summer and they swim in the lake on warm days, but I stay on the shore with you. My laundry smells the way your clothes do because we do them together now, and I bake bread and cook a lot because you work such long hours. The full moon isn’t bad; we converted the cellar and I sleep the whole night and we don’t slip up again. We live there happily for years - I get promoted to a Senior Unspeakable, you get promoted to Head of Charms - and eventually you propose, because I know you truly mean it if you’re the one to ask me, and even after a few years I’m still too insecure to not doubt it - just a little - and I say yes, of course.”

 

            “And what else?”

 

            Drawing in a deep breath, Kara forged onwards as Lena splayed a hand on her thigh, her eyes piercing, a hungry edge to her stare. “We have a small wedding, my family, our closest friends, in the backyard. The winters are freezing but we keep a fire lit and we read beside it at night, or we play Wizard’s Chess. You still beat me at it most of the time. We change the wallpaper colour once we’re bored of it, and I plant you singing daffodils in the garden. I wake up early on birthdays and weekends and- and random Tuesdays to make you breakfast in bed, and you come home with my favourite chocolate and I set the kitchen on fire a few times because we’re too busy dancing or having sex, but we laugh about it afterwards. We go on holidays and we grow old, and we’re so happy together that we sometimes forget that there was a time when we didn’t talk. I’m no longer insecure and you’re safe, and we have a long, long life together.”

 

            Lena had started kissing her cheek, her jaw, her neck as Kara continued to tell her of the future she’s imagined, her words getting a bit breathless towards the end, fingers threading through dark hair as she slumped on the sofa, and Kara fell silent as she closed her eyes. 

 

            “Is that really what you imagined?” Lena shyly asked as she undid the buttons of Kara’s shirt and kissed her stomach.

 

            “Yes,” Kara admitted, her voice raw. “Yes, I’ve spent the last fortnight thinking about it and I think I might die if it doesn’t work out that way.”

 

            “So, you want to move into the house with me?” Lena asked as she looked at her through her lashes.

 

            “Yes! I already said yes, of course I want to! I’ll move in with you right bloody now if you want me to. Now, come up here and kiss me.”

Chapter 41

            Deciding to move in together, they wasted no time making arrangements, although it was Lena who handled most of it, from quotes from contractors and magical tradespeople to shore up the structure of the old cottage, to Gringotts for property taxes and lawyers for drafted contracts before any of the work could get started. Kara had calculated her finances and determined how much of her savings she could contribute towards renovations and bills and Lena vehemently opposed a fifty-fifty split until they both compromised on splitting it proportionately to their income, all of their finances laid bare on Lena’s kitchen table as they tallied and divided and estimated, Lena a little sheepish at the hefty sum deposited weekly into her Gringotts accounts, eclipsing Kara’s rather comfortable pay as an Unspeakable. 

 

            Kara told Eliza one Saturday morning, bare feet against the cold kitchen floors as she nursed a cold cup of water, a little flustered with the delight of sharing the good news. Alex and the rest of her friends were privy to that news shortly afterwards, and things started to feel a lot more real then. It was different to the cheap places Kara had found a room at before, different even to living with her sister after Hogwarts, and there was a nervous excitement to the prospect, even though they were a long way off moving in together still. An anxious overthinker, Kara couldn’t help but wonder if Lena would regret it, if sharing the same bed, the same space and chores, seeing each other more often, eating breakfast and dinner together more often, would be too much for her, knowing she had always been more withdrawn, prone to isolation and liking her own space. 

 

            They both turned a year older, the weather starting to cool significantly, and they picked out paint colours together, starting with a hunter green for the door they’d stripped the old peeling paint off. The holes in the roof had been patched, the overgrown garden somewhat tamer, without losing its charm, the damp plasterboard and water leaks fixed, everything reinforced with magic as they spent their time after work, and weekends for Kara, at the cottage.

 

            One such Saturday in late November, a frost on the grass and fog gathering thickly in the dale, obscuring the lake, Kara was hanging wallpaper as she perched on a rickety ladder. All of the rooms had been emptied by Lena alone, combing through old furniture and dusty belongings, most of it rotting from the damp, vanishing the rubbish and boxing up things that were still somewhat preserved so Kara could take them to The Junk Shop for donation. The sturdy dresser in the bedroom that had been her mother’s and the big stove in the kitchen was all that she’d kept in the end, anything useful already taken on her first visit to the abandoned cottage. 

 

            Lena appeared as she was trying to smooth down the seams of the white and blue chinoiserie wallpaper, levitating two strong cups of tea and bacon sandwiches cooked on the newly cleaned stove. Sitting cross-legged on the freshly polished floorboards of the bedroom they’d claimed for themselves - once Elizabeth Walsh’s - they ate their belated breakfast, the sun already halfway to noon and its light spilling in through the windows. 

 

            Stifling a yawn, Kara took a sip of tea and looked around. They’d panelled the lower half of the walls and painted it white, and the bedroom was a rather drastic change from the moody colours of Lena’s flat, still a work in progress but coming along nicely. Lena had picked the wallpaper to match the ocean blue of the bed sheets Kara had pointed out on one of their shopping trips, and the dark wood of the dresser complimented the light oak of the hardwood floorboards. 

 

            “Do you think we’ll be done by Christmas?”

 

            “Christmas?” Lena sceptically echoed. “What, the whole lot? That’s a little ambitious.”

 

            “Isn’t that right up your alley?”

 

            “We don’t even have a bath yet!”

            

            “Okay, but we could have a bath by Christmas.”

 

            Lena considered that and conceded with a nod. “We could.”

 

            “It doesn’t have to all be finished to move in, does it?”

 

            “No, I suppose it doesn’t. The cellar is ready, so that’s the main thing.”

 

            Basically every room was liveable now, the stone walls and floors downstairs scrubbed clean, the beams reinforced and cracks in between the bricks patched up with cement and magic. Lena’s leather sofa had been brought in, set before the wide fireplace, as well as her kitchen table and chairs. They had to eat their meals around the coffee table in her flat now, furniture disappearing bit by bit as they made progress on the cottage. Her things were in boxes, Lena devising a system for maximum efficiency and importance, while Kara had started last week with the best of intentions, but was sidetracked by bits and pieces that ranged as far back as her Hogwarts days.

 

            Kara wrinkled her nose, grinning, saying, “I think a bed is more important.”

 

            “Well,” Lena hummed around her last mouthful, brushing crumbs off her lap as she narrowed her eyes thoughtfully, “as soon as we finish the wallpaper, I think we could manage to move the bed in.”

 

            Draining her cup of tea, eyebrows rising and falling quickly, Kara was on her feet again, dusting off the knees of her jeans before she climbed the ladder to get back to work. They stayed all day, working tirelessly to get everything ready to move in, the place starting to feel more like a home, bit by bit, as Kara’s family and a few friends helped chip in on their days off. Eliza helped Lena fix up the garden, some of her mother’s old herb plants running wild, weeds taking hold as the grass slowly overtook the garden beds that had been so carefully cultivated once upon a time. Kelly helped Kara paint the kitchen cabinets the soft shade of butter yellow that had been picked out, while Alex fitted the new toilet and sink. 

 

            The Dublin flat grew emptier, Lena’s bookshelves taking up residence in the study, Kara’s small collection of books crammed in alongside hers, her desk set beneath the window, where Kara had envisioned it. Kara’s clothes were folded in the dresser in the bedroom, plates and towels in cupboards, the pantry stocked with the necessities as more and more time was spent there, tea and coffee and ham sandwiches doled out to whoever was around at the time. They had the radio going in the kitchen at all times, and then music once the gramophone and vinyl collection was moved in, Bastet underfoot as the cat got to work chasing any mice that hadn’t been scared off yet, rooting out garden Gnomes and finding places to perch. 

 

            Halfway through December, they spent their first night there together. They’d held off on the bed, keeping it at Lena’s flat until they were ready to move in completely, once they had a finished bathroom, but they were both so eager to spend the night in their new home together that they decided to stay one night, the hour growing late on Saturday night as they sorted through boxes, fixed door knobs and hinges, painted over chips and plastered gaps. They’d ordered pizza and had a bottle of mulled wine and spiced rum, mixing the mulled wine and rum together on the stove, the kitchen windows steaming up from the heat. Now they sat yawning around the coffee table, a fire roaring as it kept them warm.

 

            “It’s all coming together now,” Kara said with a tired but pleased smile, a slice of pizza halfway to her mouth.

 

            “Mhm. Bath is scheduled for next Thursday; I’ll be off work to let them in.”

 

            “You know what that means then.”

 

            “Just in time for Christmas,” Lena smiled slightly, raising her eyebrows a fraction. “We’ll have to start taking the bed down.”

 

            Raising her eyebrows in response, Kara’s expression was more suggestive. “We could bring the mattress in. Sleep on the floor. We could even do it tonight.”

 

            “Tonight? How much wine have you had? Too much to Apparate.”

 

            Kara pouted and Lena laughed, pushing herself to her knees, a glass of mulled wine and rum in hand. She swallowed a mouthful and set her glass down on the coffee table before rising the rest of the way to her feet. Kara watched her go with some confusion, finishing her slice of pizza as Lena walked upstairs and returned a few minutes later with a pile of blankets from the linen cupboard on the landing.

 

            Dumping the pile on the sofa, she gestured to it and smiled. “Here’s your bed for the night. What do you say?”

 

            Cheeks dimpling as the corners of her eyes creased, Kara moved from the rug to the sofa and pulled the edge of a blanket over her lap. Tilting her head back, she reached up for her girlfriend, still smiling, and Lena ducked down to kiss her as her eyes closed. 

 

            “Perfect,” Kara mumbled against her lips.

 

            They sat side by side and finished off the pizza and had another glass each of the mulled wine and rum, lukewarm now but making them feel pleasantly sleepy before the fire. Kara had a deck of Exploding Snap and they played a few hands until their glasses were empty and they were ready for bed. Their muscles ached from crouching or having their arms above shoulder level for extended periods, flecks of paint speckling their clothes and occasionally their hair or faces, and the smell of furniture polish and bleach clung to them as they cuddled up together, feeling themselves start to doze.

 

            When Kara fell asleep, Lena eased her glasses off her face and set them on the coffee table before moving to the front door, opening it to welcome the rain-washed air into the cottage, bitterly cold but refreshing and cleansing as she let it chase away any lingering staleness of old memories. Breath misting before her as she stood in the doorway for a moment, Lena glanced at the dark surface of the nearby lake, catching the glow of the faint moonlight piercing the clouds, and felt her stomach swoop slightly with nerves before she turned away from it and looked at Kara.

 

            The stone floor glowed softly with the firelight and Lena padded across the floor, feeling the cold through the soles of her socks, easing herself onto the sofa and covering them both with the blanket. She fell asleep quickly and slept soundly, the fresh air mitigating the stifling heat of the fireplace and the warmth of her girlfriend pressed up against her side as they slept peacefully.

 

            Kara woke first, the fireplace smouldering with hot coals and the front door standing open. It was raining and she walked over to the front door, standing on the threshold as she watched it pour down, running away from the doorstep as the ground of the dale gently sloped downwards, and Kara breathed in the fresh air, too green and lacking the tang of salt from Cornwall to be familiar. But this was her new home and she couldn’t help but smile to herself as she turned away, leaving it open, and padded to the kitchen to make some coffee.

 

            The radio was a quiet hum as she listened to the morning news and Lena found her there ten minutes later, leaning against the counters as she toasted bread over the open flame of the stovetop, a tub of butter and a knife on the counter beside the loaf. Face creased with sleep, Lena rubbed her eyes and shuffled towards her, stealing her cup of coffee and taking a sip before she pulled a face at the sweetness.

 

            “Morning.”

 

            “Good morning,” Kara murmured, kissing her and gesturing to the kettle on a different burner, setting it to boil.

 

            She made her a cup of coffee and toasted more bread, smothering the slices in butter as they stood in the kitchen, huddled near the stove for warmth, and ate breakfast together. Another cup of coffee followed the first, and Kara cradled Lena’s waist and propped her chin on her shoulder as her girlfriend stared out of the window overlooking the back garden. 

 

            “How did you sleep?” Kara eventually asked, her voice a low murmur, tense but hopeful.

 

            “Good,” Lena vaguely answered, pausing a moment before she let out a quick laugh. “Better if we had a bed.”

 

            “Mm, my back’s killing me. I feel like an old lady,” Kara laughed. “I look like an old lady as well.”

 

            “You do not,” Lena scoffed.

 

            “Maybe I am an old lady.”

 

            “Well, I do have a thing for older women,” Lena conceded, voice flushed with amusement. “So, if you are an old lady, that could only be in your favour.”

 

            Kara let out a snort of laughter and kissed the side of her neck. “Anything that keeps you mine is fine by me.”

 

            Turning in her embrace, Lena gave her a crooked smile, green eyes bright with amusement. “If it’s any consolation, I was yours from the very beginning.”

 

            “Well, I guess keeps is the keyword there; we didn’t do a very good job of that last time.”

 

            “Nothing to worry about now, then, unless another war were to happen to ruin it all again, and what are the chances of that?”

 

            Kissing her quickly, Kara rolled her eyes. “Even on the off chance that did happen, I’d trust you more next time, wouldn’t I? I don’t often make the same mistake twice.”

 

            Deliberating, a smile on the corners of her lips as she tried to fight it back, Lena narrowed her eyes. “Do you not? You know this is the fourth time you and I have had some sort of relationship. Some would say that’s a very big mistake.”

 

            “Ah, well, I didn’t say anything about the fourth time, did I?”

 

            “Let’s not try for a fifth,” Lena whispered as she kissed her, lips a light brush against Kara’s.

 

            Leaning in, Kara was left chasing her lips as Lena leaned back, wrinkling her nose regretfully. “I have to get ready for work.”

 

            Softly groaning, Kara touched her forehead to Lena’s. “You’re a tease.”

 

            “What are you doing today?”

 

            “I don’t know, I’ll unpack a few things, maybe work on the garden a bit if the rain lets up.”

 

            “Well,” Lena kissed the corner of her mouth, and then the scar on her chin, then the underside of her jaw, “if you find time to start taking my bed apart, we can put it together tomorrow when you get off and I’ll show you just how much of a tease I can be.”

 

            Kara’s thumbs pressed firmly against Lena’s hipbone at the feeling of Lena’s featherlight lips ghosting down her neck, and she let out a breathless laugh. “Well, now that’s just cruel.”

 

            “I like to consider it … motivating.”

 

            She kissed her and laughed, and then kissed her again, before extracting herself from the circle of Kara’s arms. Kara waved her away from tidying up, kissing her goodbye before she watched Lena Apparate to her flat to get ready for work. Leaving her to it, Kara straightened up the cottage and then Apparated to her mother’s, showering and changing and spending an hour sitting at the kitchen table drinking coffee with Eliza, before she headed back to the cottage. Arranging candles and organising books, Kara kept herself busy until lunchtime and then Apparated to Alex and Kelly’s flat. They were both home and it was her sister who answered the door.

 

            “Can you give me a hand moving the bed? Just five minutes, please.”

 

            “Fine, fine, let’s go,” Alex said, rolling her eyes and shoving her feet into a pair of slippers by the door.

 

            She was in her dressing gown and shouted goodbye to her wife over her shoulder before grabbing Kara’s arm. Apparating them to Lena’s flat, Kara let them into the near-empty space and Alex stood just inside the doorway, hands planted on her hips as she looked around.

 

            “So this is her flat?”

 

            “Yes.”

 

            “Fancy. Has she sold it yet?”

 

            “What? I don’t know. I don’t know if she is.”

 

            “Why wouldn’t she? Bad omen if she’s hanging onto it in case something happens between you two, isn’t it?”

 

            Giving her a withering look, Kara moved towards the bedroom door. Pushing it open, she started removing the pillows and the quilt, making a careful pile before she noticed her sister hadn’t joined her yet. Stepping back into the open living area, she clicked her tongue and found Alex inspecting the bare office.

 

            “Stop snooping through her things!”

 

            “What things? There’s nothing in here.”

 

            “Hurry up!”

 

            “Is this where you transformed?”

 

            Mouth thinning, Kara softly sighed. “Yes, she used to lock me in here.”

 

            Shaking her head with exasperation, Alex rolled her eyes. “You dolts. Come on then, I’m supposed to be going to The Hopping Pot for lunch with Kelly. Do you want to come?”

 

            “We don’t need to put it together, just move it there, so it shouldn’t take too long.”

            

            “Alright, I’ll take that as a yes then. James is coming too so you won’t be the odd one out.”

 

            “Fine,” Kara relented, leading her to the bedroom.

 

            It took them twenty minutes to levitate the mattress to one side and get everything unscrewed and sorted into neat piles before they could shrink and move it all. Piling slats into the empty grate, Kara sent Alex through with a handful of Floo powder and then followed with two miniature headboards. It took them two trips each to bring everything through and expand it up in the bedroom, and Alex helped her put it together as well, wands directing the parts into position before a charm set the screws tightening themselves. 

 

            Once the bed was put together, Kara fetched new bedding and waved her wand, watching the sheets and pillowcases change themselves and then straighten out on the bed, neatly tucked in. Pleased, Kara made her way downstairs and washed her hands in the kitchen sink before she grabbed her sister’s arm and let her Apparate them to her flat. Sitting on the sofa, Kara waited for the two women to finish getting ready, watching them go back and forth, half-dressed, then looking for shoes and a coat, before they were all ready to go.

 

            Spending the afternoon at The Hopping Pot , tucked away in the far back with the heat of a roaring fire to keep them warm, Kara ate her pumpkin soup and shared a pot of tea with Kelly as they inquired about the cottage and talked about work. Afterwards, Kara lingered to walk around the stalls at Carkitt Market before slipping through to Diagon Alley, finishing off some last-minute Christmas shopping and Apparating to Eliza’s. She had dinner with her mother and then curled up on the sofa, reading in front of the fire as Eliza finished weaving in the ends of her knitted Christmas presents, until it was late and she went upstairs to bed.

 

            She had work all day and then met Lena at the cottage the following evening, her girlfriend coming straight from St. Mungo’s to help unpack a few things, purple shadows beneath her eyes and an obvious desire for sleep in the slopes of her shoulders. Kara kissed her as she stepped through the doors, abandoning her unpacking of kitchenware, and gave her an eager smile.

 

            “Come on, up you go.”

 

            Taking Lena’s hand, she towed her towards the restored staircase and up to their new bedroom, gesturing to the bed with delight. “Ta-da.”

 

            Lena groaned as she stepped inside and flopped onto the made bed, her eyelids closing. “I love you so much right now.”

 

            Climbing onto the bed, Kara hovered over her and kissed her forehead. “Why don’t you put your pyjamas on while I make you a cup of tea and a sandwich, and then you can sleep to your heart’s content.”

 

            Pushing herself up onto her elbows, Lena tilted her head to kiss Kara properly, before Kara climbed off the bed and made her way back downstairs. It was seven o’clock, the sky pitch black outside and the cottage cold without a fire going, but Kara relished it all, making tea and sandwiches and levitating it all upstairs to their bedroom, where Lena was bundled beneath the covers in her pyjamas. 

 

            Setting everything down on the mattress after she’d made herself comfortable, Kara leaned across to kiss Lena’s cheek, asking about her day. She reciprocated as they ate their dinner and sipped their tea, the glow of the lamplight keeping the dark at bay. They had to wash up with the bathroom sink, no bath or shower head installed yet, and they had an early night, the dark and their rather busy lives of late making them tired. Before they fell asleep, Kara ventured the idea of a New Year’s Eve party, doubling as a housewarming, with all of their friends over for the first time. Lena was off work and Kara couldn’t think of a better way to usher in the nineties than at their home together, so of course Lena said yes.

 

            The bath was installed on Thursday, as planned, and they moved in on Friday. It didn’t matter that they’d practically lived there for the last week, it was just as exciting to have the house finished and everything in its place, all of their things mixed together - mostly Lena’s, but Kara’s framed photos, books and candles strewn throughout - and they spent their Christmas there together the following week, getting a tree up just in time, wrapping their chosen gifts for everyone in front of the fireplace. They were still up at the crack of dawn, Flooing to Eliza’s with their armful of gifts, Alex and Kelly monopolising the bedroom upstairs and already in the living room in their pyjamas as her sister sorted gifts into piles.  

 

            Kara had the holidays off, while Lena worked most of it, having to head to St. Mungo’s the evening of Christmas Day and working straight through Boxing Day with the influx of injuries with families reunited. Occupying her time at her mother’s, Kara baked gingerbread and homemade fudge with Eliza, helped sort through old boxes for donating and hauled it off to The Junk Shop herself, spending a few hours in The Leaky Cauldron to chat with Tom while she nursed a pint of Dragon’s Scale at the bar. 

 

            She made arrangements for their party as well, Lena leaving a few Galleons on the kitchen table to add to Kara’s funds. Picking up wine and Firewhisky, ale and mead and then an assortment of foods to feed everyone, Kara spent the afternoon of New Year’s Eve making sandwiches and sliding cubes of cheddar onto toothpicks with pineapple, little cocktail sausages and quiches on platters. Alex and Kelly arrived early to help and Lena was home at lunchtime, sleeping off her shift as they got everything ready.

 

            Emerging at six o’clock, still looking exhausted but perking up with a shower and a potion, Lena helped pour crisps and nuts into bowls, plating up pasties and charming them to stay hot. They hadn’t invited many people, just their friends, a few extended ones and partners or dates, and they slowly started to trickle in. After drinks with Andrea, Lena had caught up with her twice more - once for drinks at The Hopping Pot and again at The Leaky Cauldron, staying away from Knockturn Alley and any other so-called friends - and she’d extended an invitation to her as well, concluding her total of two invitations. The other was to Sam, who was one of the first to arrive, a chocolate log dusted with icing sugar on a plate in her arms, a bottle of wine in hand.

 

            It was a little awkward when Imra showed up with her girlfriend, Gayle, Kara welcoming them both warmly as Lena stared at her old friend with uncertainty. The awkwardness went up a notch when Mike showed up, having heard of the party from Winn, who brought him along. It was nothing a few shots of Firewhisky couldn’t fix, Kara babbling nervously as she doled them out, knocking back two herself in quick succession and giving Lena’s arm a passing squeeze. The tension seemed to diffuse then, Gayle falling into conversation with Andrea and Sam, the latter a little more integrated in this friendship circle than Lena’s other friends, while Mike fell in with Winn, Querl and James, talking Quidditch.

 

            They blasted music from the radio and snacked on the prepared foods, drinks flowing freely and everyone talking loudly or laughing as they all formed little groups and flowed between them, sidetracked on the way for refills. The more they drank, the more they all forgot about exes and past school grudges, and even more recent ones as Lena’s frostiness thawed a little as well. 

 

            It was all going so well until just after ten o’clock, everyone sprawled on seats in the living room or around the kitchen table, leaning against the walls or sitting on the floor when there were no seats left, the windows cracked to let out the smoke from half a dozen lit cigarettes. Empty bottles and glasses crowded the surfaces and the music raged on as they all talked over each other, recounting stories, mostly from Hogwarts, or sharing gossip about people they’d gone to school with. It was fine until Gayle innocently stumbled upon something in her browsing of the cottage decor, something that was only meaningful to Kara and Lena.

 

            “Hey, is that- did you nick this from me?” Gayle laughed around her cigarette, drawing the attention of several people as she picked up a candle and turned it over in one hand.

 

            “No, that’s one of mine,” Lena dismissively replied, although when Kara looked at her, she noticed that her expression was wooden and her spine stiff.

 

            “No, it’s one of my candles, I swear it is. Picked it up on a trip to Romania. You remember, don’t you, Lena? You went off in a strop last time we had a play with it and haven’t spoken to me since.”

 

            Frowning, Kara took a sip of her ale, perching on the edge of the sofa. “Is it … a special candle?”

 

            “What’s it for?” Alex asked, ashing her cigarette and raising her eyebrows.

 

            Smiling in a way that made Kara feel uncertain, Gayle walked over to the sofa and armchairs, weaving between them, and set the squat candle in the middle of the coffee table. She beckoned to everyone and breathed out a plume of blue smoke.

 

            “Alright, gather around if you’re playing, piss off if you’re not. I’ll explain the rules.”

 

            Curious, everyone drew closer, kneeling around the coffee table or snagging a seat if they were lucky. Sinking onto the sofa, Kara’s gaze settled on Lena, who was leaning against the wall, her expression and posture still stiff, and she raised her eyebrows when their eyes met, patting the spot beside her. With a small shake of her head, Lena gave her a quick smile.

 

            Gayle saw it and loudly objected. “Absolutely not , take a seat, Lena. You can’t pinch my game and then weasel your way out of it. Everyone make sure you have a drink. Do we have Firewhisky? Glasses?”

 

            A bottle of the amber short was levitated across the room, and empty glasses were scrounged up for everyone, varying from shots to wine, and Lena sat on the floor in front of Kara, letting Kelly take the spot next to her. Kara was confused by the palpable nervousness of her girlfriend, catching sight of her chewing on her lip, and Kara gave her shoulder a quick squeeze as Lena turned to offer up the bottle of Firewhisky. Draining her ale, Kara splashed an inch of Firewhisky into her glass and passed the bottle on.

 

            “Okay, this is a truth candle, so rules are you put your hand in and someone has to say something you’ve never done - or you have if you want to get caught out too,” Gayle explained with a grin as she snapped her fingers to light the candle. “If you flinch, you drink. Simple. Hands in. We’ll do an easy round first with Lena’s least favourite question. Payback for stealing, ignoring me and trying to get out of playing.”

 

            Drawing in a sharp breath to refute that as everyone leaned in to put their hands in, Lena was interrupted by Gayle as she spoke loudly. “Never have I ever slept with a werewolf.”

 

            Lena was the only one to jerk her hand back, but she delayed a moment, long enough for her fingertips to turn a bright red, letting out a soft hiss as she flexed her hand. Kara’s stomach dropped and she snatched Lena’s hand, watching as the redness quickly faded, leaving unblemished skin behind, relief quick to chase away her concern, until she saw Lena duck her head, avert her gaze, a flush creeping up her neck. Lena laughed, of course, nonchalantly as she wiggled her fingers and rolled her eyes, everyone quickly getting the gist of the game. Kara wasn’t laughing though, and she didn’t want to play anymore as she quickly came to understand why her girlfriend was in possession of a candle that caused pain.

 

            Ashen and silent, Kara didn’t say anything as she put her hand back in with everyone, in a trance as she looked down at Lena, watching the pulse jump at her throat. There were more generic ones after that, and she got caught a few times - detention, fired from a job, had her heart broken, kissed someone in the room - the tips of her fingers burning until she jerked them back, a telltale sign of the truth. Some of them were more pointed, aimed at specific people, mostly in good nature, and Kara could feel Lena’s discomfort when Gayle posed one that was aimed at her, by the unwavering stare sent her way.

 

            “Never have I ever cheated on someone.”

 

            So distracted by her almost unnervingly watchful gaze fixated on Lena, Kara startled at the burning sensation and snatched her hand back, muttering and swearing beneath her breath. Blinking, she felt a few eyes on her as the only one who had jerked away and frowned, processing the question and rolling her eyes.

 

            “I suppose so, if it can be called that.”

 

            “So you weren’t involved then?” Andrea insisted, a smirk on her lips as she jerked her chin to Lena. “We all swore the two of you were shagging-”

 

            “No,” Lena curtly cut her off, “men just take everything so personally, and can’t imagine a woman not wanting to be with them.”

 

            “Too right,” Imra snorted, shaking her head.

 

            Andrea didn’t drop it though, everyone’s curiosity piqued. “Well, what happened then?”

 

            “Well, I kissed Lena. While I was with William,” Kara sheepishly confessed.

 

            “Which means you were with Jack. Nice little loophole there, I suppose.”

 

            Lena just hummed and Kara knocked back her drink. The bottle of Firewhisky passed hands around to her to add in another two fingers of liquor, and Kara swirled it around as she waited for the heat to leave her cheeks. 

 

            They played until it was almost midnight, and then Gayle blew the candle out as everyone started dashing drinks, a few more bottles opened and glasses refilled, everyone too drunk and loud from too many shots on top of too many glasses of beer or wine. Kara felt sick, her skin clammy, a tightness in her chest as she sat on the sofa and willed them all to leave, regretting the idea to ever have them all over in the first place. 

 

            “Alright?” Alex asked as she sank beside her on the sofa, a bottle of Firewhisky in one hand and a glass in the other, leaning across to slosh some into Kara’s empty glass.

 

            Humming vaguely, Kara sipped the whisky and turned her head, seeking Lena out amidst the bodies of her friends. James was loudly corralling everyone together as the radio started a countdown to midnight and Alex was on her feet, seeking out her wife. Spotting Lena, Kara sipped her Firewhisky for a moment before she climbed to her feet, skirting around her friends, Kara drained the rest of her drink on the way and paused at Lena’s side. Looking at her, Lena’s expression was evidently guilty, knowing Kara’s piercing stare meant she definitely knew what she’d been doing with that candle. 

 

            As the countdown dwindled to seconds, Kara swallowed thickly, the taste of Firewhisky caught at the back of her throat, and a funny smile crossed her face, strained and wavering. “Happy New Year.”

 

            Lena murmured the same and they kissed, lingering but nervous, not quite holding the careless joy of their friends around them. They were pulled away then, Alex finding Kara, Sam finding Lena, from friend to friend as they all exchanged kisses on cheeks and hugs, more drinks handed out and cigarettes lit as midnight came and went, 1990 ushered in with dread knotted in Kara and Lena’s stomachs. 

 

            It was past two when their friends started drifting off, Flooing out of the cottage to their various homes, giggly with laughter, unsteady on their feet or holding on to each other. Some stayed - Alex and Kelly in one of the spare rooms, Nia and Querl in the spare room that didn’t have a proper bed yet, just a mattress on the floor and Kara’s camping supplies, James on the sofa downstairs and Sam on the camp bed in the study. It put an end to any type of conversation, or rather argument , that would have ensued between the two of them, as drunk and tense as they were. 

 

            Instead, Lena kissed Kara goodnight while she was sorting out Sam’s bed and slipped away upstairs before Kara could say anything. Once everyone was passed out in their designated sleeping spots, Kara put out all of the lights, left the fireplaces to burn low to keep the ground floor heated for the two down there, and made her way upstairs. Locking herself in the bathroom, she splashed water on her face and scooped a few handfuls to her lips, taking a few minutes to swallow the worry and dismay before she went back into the bedroom. The light was on, of course, but Lena didn’t stir and Kara was too tired as she shed her clothes, playing into the pretence of Lena already asleep as she worked her jeans down her thighs, set her glasses and wand on the nightstand and climbed beneath the covers.

 

            On her back, she breathed shallowly for a while, staring up at the ceiling as she kept fighting to work the lump in her throat down, listening to Lena’s quiet, even breaths, sure that she was still awake too. It felt like an age before sleep came for her, drowsy from alcohol, succumbing to the gentle tug of tiredness as her mind slowed, still caught somewhere in the pit of unease. When she woke late in the morning, Lena wasn’t beside her and she dressed in yesterday’s clothes before heading downstairs.

 

            Everyone else was up and breakfast was underway, Kara mumbling a good morning to the occupied kitchen as she made for the kettle. A hangover cure was nudged into her hand and she thanked Lena, who was frying the eggs and bacon, before knocking it back. Sam was buttering toast and Alex helped her refill everyone’s coffees. There weren’t enough chairs for them all so Kara hovered in the kitchen, eating her bacon and egg sandwich as she leaned against the counters, while Lena sat at the table and talked to Kelly.

 

            “You alright?” Sam murmured to Kara, eating in the kitchen as well.

 

            “Hm? Oh, um, yes, it's just- you know, not as fun drinking when you’re older,” Kara smiled, picking up her coffee.

 

            “And is she alright?”

 

            “Lena? Why?”

 

            “You know her better than I do. Something’s off.”

 

            “Oh … well, we had a little tiff last night. Before everyone got here. Nothing serious, I think she’s still just a little pissed off. You know what she’s like.”

 

            Sam let out a quiet laugh and patted Kara’s shoulder before picking up the other half of her sandwich and asking about work. Kara had always liked Sam, and even though she had been relegated to Lena’s friend, there was a comfort in her presence leftover from their days as Housemates at Hogwarts, and Kara quickly took up the opportunity to talk about something other than Lena, afraid that Sam knew them both well enough to know that Kara was lying through her teeth. 

 

            They all finished their breakfast and attempted to start tidying up the mass of bottles, sticky rings and leftover food but were waved off by Kara and Lena, who insisted that they could do it themselves. As their friends gathered their belongings and left one by one, the tension between the two of them thickened, until Alex and Kelly left last and they were finally alone together.

 

            Neither of them spoke and Lena immediately started vanishing bottles and levitating dirty glasses to the kitchen sink. Suppressing a sigh, Kara got to work helping her, cleaning up the living room as she straightened pillows and used a cloth to wipe down the coffee table, ashtrays overflowing, dried spills and there, in the middle, the reason for the tense broodiness of the two women, the melted stump of a candle. 

 

            She put the camp bed away and folded blankets, returning them to the linen closet and then tidying up the bedrooms before returning to the kitchen. Lena was washing dishes, finishing off the last few glasses, and Kara grabbed a clean tea towel and started to dry the damp ones on the draining board. Lena helped once she’d finished with the glasses and they silently dried and put everything away, moving around the kitchen as the tension grew.

 

            “Are we going to talk about it?” Kara asked once the silence had become unbearable.

 

            Slowing, Lena heaved a heavy sigh. “I’d prefer not to.”

 

            Looking at her through her lashes as she dried off a glass, Kara swallowed thickly, annoyance building in her chest. There was an awkward beat of silence again as Lena drained the sink and dried off her hands, tipping her head back as she breathed in through her nose, eyes closed, and then sighed again as she rounded on Kara, tossing the tea towel onto the counter.

 

            “But you clearly have something to say.”

 

            “Why do you have that?” Kara quietly exclaimed, roughly gesturing to the living room as her eyes smarted with tears.

 

            Lips twitching ruefully, Lena’s throat bobbed as she swallowed. Her haughtiness was slightly marred by the flicker of guilt in her eyes. “You’ve already figured that out.”

 

            “No, I want you to tell me.”

 

            Letting out a huff of laughter, Lena ducked her head, an uneven smile crossing her face. She toyed with her hands but Kara watched as her right hand worked up her left forearm, until Lena’s thumb pressed along the length of the hidden scar.

 

            “You took my quill. I needed something else. I don’t know what else to tell you.”

 

            “Why? I just- I thought you didn’t- you told me you stopped.”

 

            “No, I never said that. You just thought you’d taken away my only option.”

 

            “But … why? I don’t understand, I-”

 

            There was anger or some resentment in Lena’s voice as she roughly replied, her expression turning sullen. “Because you never even asked if it was okay to do that! You just decided to take it and I didn’t want to disappoint you by telling you I didn’t want you to.”

 

            Mouth opening and closing, Kara looked at her with blatant devastation, eyes filling with tears as she floundered. “What was I supposed to do? Let you keep using it?”

 

            “It wasn’t that often,” Lena tightly replied, slightly defensive.

 

            “Any time is too often for me, I- why don’t you tell me things? You never let me help you.”

 

            “You help just by being here.”

 

            “That’s not enough! I want to protect you from all the pain and hurt. Why is that so wrong?”

 

            She couldn’t blink the tears away, a hawkish look on her face as she fought to keep her chin from wobbling, the hot splash on her cheeks as her face reddened. Kara was always incapable of not crying whenever she felt some strong emotion - usually negative - but she wished it picked a better time to happen, her voice fraying and uneven as she tried to reason with her girlfriend. Lena just clicked her tongue and crossed over to her, taking the tea towel from Kara’s limp fingers and dabbing a corner across her cheeks.

 

            “Don’t cry.”

 

            “It’s better than this …” Kara gravelly replied, her voice breaking as she gestured to Lena, her stoic quiet betraying none of her feelings. “You can’t cry for yourself but at least someone can fucking cry for you.”

 

            “I don’t want you to cry for me,” Lena softly snapped, “it’s not helping either of us.”

 

            “And that does?”

 

            “Yes! Yes, it does help me. I’m a self-destructive person, I know that about myself, I know it’s not a good thing, or healthy - why do you think I hide it from you? - but it helps. And at least it doesn’t leave a mark this way.”

 

            A small huff of disbelief escaped Kara and she tipped her head back, pushing her glasses up as she pressed the heels of her palms into her eyes. The silence that fell over the kitchen was heavy and laced with awkwardness, and Kara took a moment to steady her breaths as Lena stared at the old stone floor, waiting for a response. Lowering her head, Kara wiped her face on her sleeve and then cleared her throat, sniffing.

 

            “Fine,” Kara whispered, feebly gesturing. “Fine, show me how it helps.”

 

            “What?” Lena blanched.

 

            Rounding the kitchen table, Kara walked into the living room, the candle melted onto the coffee table, and snapped her fingers at it, the wick lighting with a little flame. She dropped to her knees on the rug and put her hand in.

 

            “What questions do you ask?”

 

            “What are you doing?” Lena tightly asked as she stood at the edge of the kitchen, hand braced against a worn wooden beam.

 

            “I’m trying to … understand. I mean, you think it tells the truth, right? That’s- that’s bollocks.”

 

            “It just … reaffirms what I already know.”

 

            “Okay,” Kara murmured, licking her lips. “I’m not a monster.”

 

            She pulled her hand away at the sharp pain in her palm, hissing as she shook it off, heart thudding in her chest as her throat tightened. It was true of course, by the classification of her condition, but it didn’t stop the sting of affirmation. Lena was livid though, pale-faced as she swept across the room and dragged Kara to her feet, away from the offending candle. Holding fistfuls of her jumper, Lena had her pressed up against the mantle of the fireplace, her eyes bright, her bottom lip trembling slightly. 

 

            “What the hell are you doing? Don’t do that- don’t you ever- you are not a monster.”

 

            Reaching up to brush dark hair off her cheek, the strands stuck to Lena’s clammy skin, Kara’s lips twitched regretfully. “And you’re not a failure.”

 

            Lena unclenched her fists, the wool of Kara’s jumper wrinkled as she smoothed it out, and swallowed thickly. “You- don’t.”

 

            Leaning in a fraction, Kara bumped her nose against Lena’s cheek and kissed her softly. Her lips were chapped and Lena’s were unresponsive, and Kara let out a heavy sigh as she pulled back, feeling the mantle dig into her shoulder blades. Glassy-eyed, unbalanced, and exhausted, she grimaced as she tipped her head back.

 

            “You make me sick with worry, you know.”

 

            “I’m sorry,” Lena whispered, leaning in a fraction, her breath warm on Kara’s cheek. She thought she might kiss her but her arms came around Kara’s shoulders instead, hugging her gently as she pressed her face into her neck.

 

            Something caved in Kara’s chest as she hugged her back, eyes screwed shut, face furrowed with anguish, and she let out a raw sound as she pressed her cheek against Lena’s temple. “Why are you doing this?”

 

            “I don’t know. It just- it’s familiar. I-”

 

            Lena cut off and pulled away, chin to her chest as her cheeks reddened. Kara watched her swallow thickly, pity knifing through her as her face rippled with pain, and she reached out, hands falling short, and then tried again, unsure of how to comfort her, unsure whether Lena wanted that.

 

            “Sit down,” Kara rasped.

 

            Nodding, Lena backed away and around the coffee table before sitting heavily. Disappearing to the kitchen, Kara boiled some water and scooped coffee grounds into two cups, her hands shaking, and added milk and sugar to hers before she levitated them back to the living room, not trusting herself to not spill it. Sitting at the opposite end of the sofa, Kara cradled her cup in her hands, while Lena left hers untouched on the coffee table, shoulders hunched as she tried to make herself smaller, unnoticeable. 

 

            “I didn’t mean for it to happen,” Lena confessed after a long pause. “It was something she made me do and then … I took it with me when I moved out. I don’t know why. And then it was familiar and … I’d mess up and I’d reach for it. There’s a comfort to it. It turned into a way to cope when I- when I felt like I was … not doing well. I got better, I didn’t need it as much, but then you took it and I- I panicked. When I needed it and it wasn’t there, I thought about the candle. They, uh, that’s how they all found out. Um … Gayle’s little question about sleeping with a werewolf, Veronica asked it and- I tried my hardest not to flinch - I can withstand a lot of pain - and it just- it kept burning until I did. So when I remembered that, needed to remember that I- well, I stole it from Gayle’s flat and I used it. Not often.”

 

            Kara looked at the candle, burnt down to a few remaining inches, and wondered what Lena deemed not often. Mouth dry, throat and chest tight, she struggled to drag in a breath. Lena chewed her lip as she kept her eyes on her hands in her lap, flexing the fingers her mother had broken years ago. Setting her cup of coffee down, Kara shifted across the sofa and took her hands. Raising them to her lips, she kissed Lena’s fingers.

 

            “Thank you for telling me,” she hoarsely murmured.

 

            Lena let out a breathless laugh, raising mournful eyes to meet Kara’s. She was pale and looked frightened, as if Kara would feel any of the disgust she felt for herself, and Kara’s shoulders slumped slightly.

 

            Looking back down, Lena’s lips twitched with dismay. “I didn’t want you to know.”

 

            “Why not?”

 

            “I think … admitting it to you would have made me feel like more of a failure.”

 

            There was a spasm in Kara’s chest and she had to swallow a small sound of surprise that worked up her throat. Setting Lena’s hands back down, she slid off the sofa, back onto her knees, and reached out to the lit candle. Looking up, Lena startled and reached forward to pull her back, but Kara held a hand up to fend her off as she spoke.

 

            “Lena is a failure.”

 

            She kept her hand in the flame, not even the slightest tickle of heat palpable on her palm, and she turned her hand over, showcasing her unblemished palm. Lena continued to reach for Kara’s hand, and after a moment, Kara relented and let her drag it away, turning it over in her slender, shaking fingers as she saw for herself that there was no sign of a receding burn. Pulling her hand back, Kara put it back in.

 

            “Never have I thought Lena was a failure. Never have I been failed by Lena. Never have I stopped loving Lena.”

 

            Rattling off a few in quick succession, Kara’s palm remained unburned and Lena sat at her shoulder, knee bouncing with agitation as she watched Kara speak the doubts she had to no effect. Biting her cuticles, Lena eventually let out a frayed sound and put a hand on Kara’s shoulder to stop her.

 

            “Mine always hurts,” she whispered.

 

            “Give me your hand,” Kara gently urged her.

 

            When Lena slipped it into her palm, Kara dragged her forward until both of their hands were over the flame. Her voice wavered as she spoke, uncertain as she felt a prickle of dread, wondering if she was going to end up poking a dragon, but she got the words out before Lena realised what she was doing.

 

            “Never have I thought Kara was a monster.”

 

            Only her palm burned, quickly snatching her hand free from Lena’s as the lick of heat turned it red. Lena’s hand remained over the flame, a slight tremor to it but unburnt as she looked at Kara with aching green eyes, her expression mournful and pained.

 

            “See?” Kara rasped, gesturing to the candle and then wiping her face on her sleeve. “It’s just a daft candle with an enchantment on it. It can’t tell the truth; it just reaffirms what you think , like you said.”

 

            “I know,” Lena whispered, putting her head in her hands. “I know, but … sometimes I need it reaffirmed. It makes me better - makes me try to be better and-”

 

            She trailed off and Kara pushed herself up, sitting beside her again as she wrapped her arms around Lena and kissed the crown of her bowed head. “You don’t need to try to be anything. You don’t- that’s not- I know you think-”

 

            Not knowing what to say, Kara kept stopping and starting, at a loss for words. Closing her eyes, she swallowed thickly. “Lena … she might’ve made you think that you need to do this to yourself when you’re feeling a certain way but … I promise you it doesn’t have to be like this. The pain, it- it wasn’t right what she did to you.”

 

            “I know, I know, I just- I don’t know any different, it’s all I’ve ever known. She started it but I don’t know how to- to stop . I was nine the first time. Nine. It was the worst pain I’d felt in my life and now … it barely takes the edge off. If I stop … I don’t think I’d feel anything at all. Even a little bit of pain every now and then is preferable to … nothing .”

 

            Sighing, Kara rubbed her forehead, trying to blink away the stinging in her eyes as a tense silence blanketed them. She didn’t know what to say to make it better, to change Lena’s mind, undo decades of pain. Her heart ached for her and she was angry too, mostly at Lillian for starting it all but a little bit at Lena as well for hiding it from her. After a tense minute, Lena exhaled heavily and raised her head from her hands.

 

            “I need to get ready for work.”

 

            Panic knifed through Kara as Lena climbed to her feet, and she grabbed her hand to stop her. Swallowing the lump in her throat, her eyes puffy and red, Kara’s mouth thinned with regret. Her voice was raw as she spoke, reluctant and agonised, and she couldn’t quite look at Lena.

 

            “I can’t pretend that I understand it, and I won’t ever give you the quill back, but I’m sorry for taking away your choice. I- I just wanted to help, I thought I was helping, I-”

 

            Lena softly shushed her, reaching down to cup her chin. Kara wouldn’t raise her head though, drawing in a shaky breath as she quickly wiped her cheeks and cleared her throat. Sniffing, she continued, her voice wavering.

 

            “I’d like it if you talked to me about it when you’re feeling that way, but … if it helps, if- if it’s what you need to do,” she rasped, reaching forward to pry the melted candle off the coffee table, offering it up to her girlfriend, “just … do what you need to do.”

Chapter 42

            Things were a little tense after their conversation but it quickly mellowed back out into their usual ease, both of them too anxious, perhaps too insecure, to let things grow between them. A few days of stilted conversation and barely a kiss each time one of them was coming or going exchanged was the extent of their frustration with each other before it was set aside, the ache of longing, of missing each other too much, becoming unbearable. Lena resolved to pretend it had never happened, while Kara waited to see if her girlfriend would be forthright about her feelings, keeping an eye out for the stump of a candle but never asking whether Lena had used it. It ate away at her and Lena could feel that, but still, she never brought it up either.

 

            Life carried on as usual. On the nights Lena wasn’t at the hospital, they had dinner together and slept beside each other, woke up in their bed and ate breakfast together. On the days when they didn’t cross paths, they left little notes, folded into cranes or butterflies and left on the dresser, on the kitchen table, the desk in the study or the windowsill. They went for drinks at The Leaky Cauldron , lunch at The Hopping Pot, breakfast in muggle cafes and dinner at Eliza’s with Kara’s sister and her wife. They were invited to Andrea’s birthday party and went to Madam Puttifoot’s for Valentine’s Day, and Sam covered every full moon shift for Lena as she locked her girlfriend in the refurbished cellar with no evident problems.

 

            Lena tried harder to manage her feelings and her expectations, sometimes wishing to use the candle to know her true feelings about herself, or rather, whether they had changed, but she managed. Not once did she falter, not even when patients died, an uncommon occurrence but always leaving her feeling defeated at her failure, trying to process losses or mistakes in a way that made her feel her emotions instead of using pain to numb her to the rest of it. Without her punishments, Lena felt it all tangle up inside her, a confusing knot of emotion that she was incapable of parsing, unable to bring herself to display her feelings, even though she keenly felt them now. 

 

            As time went by, she’d hoped she’d have more perspective or clarity, but she had never been able to express herself, whether through words or emotions, and it was a rather awkward and embarrassing thought to imagine speaking to Kara about it. Lena would be mortified to divulge so much drivel to her girlfriend, the unimportant minutia of her life, the stinging barbs or upsetting words from her mother, the failure of her Healing, the stress of watching new grey hairs thread through Kara’s hair with each full moon. Lena bottled it all up, as she was used to doing, except she didn’t afford herself an outlet for her feelings this time. 

 

            Over half a year passed by as she silently struggled to find a way to vent it. Drinking didn’t help, always leaving her quieter and sadder and more introspective until she inevitably had to take a potion to sober herself up for some work emergency or another. Work occupied so much of her time that she hoped it would be a good enough distraction but that was so unpredictable and her biggest source of stress, from patients to her mother, that the only balm to ease any of her frustrations was Kara. 

 

            It was easier to forget about her frustration when she was around her girlfriend, the solid warmth of her body, her gentle voice and easy laughter, the way her eyes creased at the corners and her cheeks dimpled with the silvery scars on them, the conversations they had late at night as they sipped tea while Kara evasively spoke on topics she was clearly researching for work, both of them reading in bed as Lena scoured texts for essays for anything she’d missed regarding lycanthropy. She basked in the innocent touches of Kara’s hand on her thigh, the ridges of her spine as Lena pressed a hand to her back, their fingers laced together as they walked through Diagon Alley with ice cream that summer. 

 

            They were coming up to their second anniversary, August starting as a cool summer lingered, and Lena was fifteen hours into her shift after being paged on her cryptex at five o’clock that morning. Eager to get home, she’d finished off her fifth procedure in a Theatre for the day, the muscles in her neck and shoulders aching from the hours spent toiling over unconscious patients, knitting bones and muscles back together, removing foreign objects from organs and body cavities, undoing charms and curses that had gone awry. There had been rounds and Interns, pages that summoned her to stand over shoulders to watch as small wounds and little mistakes, like broken bones or extra fingers and vanished teeth, were healed beneath her guidance, and Lena had a little over an hour left of her shift when her mother paged her.

 

            She was good at avoiding her mother, or if unavoidable, keeping it strictly work-related in plain view of other staff members, but she always dreaded the possibility of being summoned to her mother’s office. It was always harder for Lena to manage her anger and hurt and scorn when left alone with Lillian, regressing to a teenager, a child, someone vulnerable and a little bit frightened. Wondering if there was some emergency procedure she could steal, hole herself up in a Theatre for the next hour or so, Lena wearily made her way downstairs to her mother’s office, too tired for the contemptuous conversation that was sure to follow, although she wasn’t sure what the specifics would be.

 

            Knocking on the door, she let herself in and hovered just inside the threshold as she watched her mother set down a cup of tea and beckoned her closer. “Close the door and take a seat.”

 

            Hesitating, mouth thinning with reluctance, Lena silently obeyed. Dragging out the chair set across from her mother, Lena sank onto it and smoothed out her scrubs, noticing a few spots of blood on the hem of her top from her most recent patient as she tried to avoid her mother’s gaze for as long as possible. Clearing her throat as she turned her cup of tea, lining the handle up straight, Lillian leaned back and studied her for a moment.

 

            “Healer Burke is retiring at the end of August. You’ll be taking over as Head of Charms.”

 

            Mouth opening and closing, Lena absorbed the news in silence for a few seconds too long as a suffocating silence followed. Lillian studied her impassive expression and Lena met her mother’s gaze as she tried to retain her composure.

 

            “I haven’t applied for the position.”

 

            “Nevertheless, you will be taking over.”

 

            “What about Healer Arias?”

 

            Lillian coolly arched an eyebrow. “What about her?”

 

            “She’s got a few more years of experience than me. She’s also a Charms Attending. Maybe she’d be a better fit for the position.”

 

            “I’m well aware of her credentials, thank you, but she is not a contender, and this isn’t up for debate.”

 

            “What if I don’t want it?”

 

            Pausing, Lillian gave her a hard look. Lena swallowed thickly as she felt the prickle of dissatisfaction, of guilt and shame steal over her. Drawing in a deep breath, Lillian shook her head and exhaled sharply as she pushed her chair back. Stomach lurching, Lena struggled to remain rooted to the spot as her body screamed at her to shoot to her feet and back away, feeling small as her mother towered over her.

 

            “You’re exceptionally smart, Lena, that much is known by everyone. But you squander your potential on distractions, like that werewolf . I won’t let you waste your career by turning this up. Have some ambition , for once in your life.”

 

            Her mother said it with venom as she tucked a quill into her gown pocket and picked up her wand. Feeling a cold sweat prickle her lower back and neck, Lena’s throat tightened as she flexed her fingers, chest rising and falling with shallow breaths. 

 

            “She’s not a distraction,” she managed to hoarsely tell her.

 

            “No? Then you should have no objections to the demands of being Head of Charms.”

 

            “I do object to it. How can you think that it’s fair on everyone else to just give it to me, unearned?”

 

            “It’s not unearned; this was always the path your career was going to take.”

 

            “But you enjoy making an example out of me in front of everyone. You enjoy isolating me from them, knowing they’ll say I didn’t deserve it, that it was handed to me, that it will set me apart once again. Why bother having potential or ambition when it’s handed to me anyway?”

 

            “Don’t be so dramatic,” her mother replied, her voice as level and cool as ever as she rounded her desk. “You know I despise it when you let yourself get worked up. There’s no need for all this … melodrama. It’s not up for negotiation, it’s not a request , and while I’m Healer-In-Charge of this hospital, I make the decisions, am I understood?”

 

            Grinding her teeth together, Lena’s eyelids shuttered and she had to bite back the real response she wanted to give her mother as she rose to her feet. “Yes.”

 

            “Good.”

 

            They stood in silence for a moment and Lillian fixed her with a piercing stare, taking in the tight corners of her daughter’s mouth, the hard line of her jaw and the petulance in her eyes. With another sigh, Lillian clicked her tongue.

 

            “It’s a promotion, Lena. Most people say thank you and get on with it.”

            

            “Can I go?”

 

            “I said say thank you.”

 

            “Thank you,” Lena stiffly replied. “Excuse me.”

 

            Turning, she crossed the office and yanked open the door and firmly closed it behind herself, although it was apparent her mother was on her way out as well. Opting for the stairs up to the Charms Ward to avoid a tense ride in the lift with Lillian, Lena wound through the hallways with brimming frustration inside her. Unable to deal with patients or coworkers right then, she slipped into her favourite on-call room and sat heavily on the bed.
