            Raking a hand through her hair, a torrent of swearing ran through her mind as she flexed her fingers again and felt the nagging itch in her left arm, in her palm and fingertips. A blood quill or the enchanted candle would have sufficed, she wasn’t picky when it came to pain, but the former was hidden somewhere by Kara and the candle … well, she’d put that in the bin as soon as Kara had put it in her hands and left her with it. It wasn’t that Lena didn’t want to keep it, only that she was embarrassed that Kara had given it to her freely, that she’d accepted Lena’s weakness, and that had made it impossible for Lena to hold onto it, knowing that she’d hate herself that little bit more when she inevitably used it. How could she look her girlfriend in the eye and feel like she wasn’t pathetic and so undeserving of her if she’d lit the candle and let it blister her palms to numb her to her emotions?

 

            Instead, Lena was left at work with nothing to temper her anger and frustration, the helplessness and guilt over something that was beyond her control. No one paged her on her cryptex but that only meant she had more time to dwell alone with her thoughts without distraction. She brooded there for an hour, digging her nails into the tender skin of her left forearm, before Sam tracked her down, gingerly easing open the door before she was reassured by Lena’s upright position.

 

            “I’ve been looking all over for you. I thought you might’ve gone for the day without saying goodbye.”

 

            Elbows on her thighs, Lena closed her eyes as she let out a forceful breath, head in her hands. She felt the mattress jostle beside her as Sam took a seat, reaching up to press a palm between Lena’s shoulder blades.

 

            “What’s the matter?”

 

            “Burke is leaving at the end of the month.”

 

            “Oh. I didn’t realise you were so fond of him.”

 

            Snorting, Lena’s mouth twisted grimly. “It’s not that, it’s about who’s replacing him.”

 

            “Well, obviously it’ll be you. Your mum would be mad to pick anyone else.”

 

            Lifting her head out of her hands, stung by Sam’s blithe acknowledgement of her mother’s choice, Lena turned to give her friend a mournful glance. “She could pick you.”

 

            Sam gave her a gentle smile, her hand dropping away as she shifted back on the mattress, leaning on her elbows with her long legs stretched out before her. Wrinkling her nose slightly, she hummed dubiously.

 

            “I wouldn’t want it.”

 

            “Wouldn’t you?”

 

            “Are you joking with me? Until Ruby starts at Hogwarts, I’ve got bigger priorities than work. I wouldn’t have the time for it, wouldn’t want that kind of responsibility on top of being a mum.”

 

            “Oh.”

 

            Lena’s response was barely audible and her brow creased with consternation as her shoulders slumped. Pushing herself up a little more, Sam cocked her head to the side, confused but understanding blossoming in her hazel eyes.

 

            “Oh, come on, you didn’t really think I’d want it, did you?”

 

            “You’d deserve it.”

 

            “You would too. You should apply.”

 

            Wincing slightly, Lena rubbed her cheek, feeling the sting of guilt again. It didn’t matter if she felt like she would be good at it or the best fit for the position, there was something distasteful and shameful about having it handed to her. If there had been an application process, she might have felt a bit better about it, but if there had been an application process, she probably would have convinced Sam to apply instead of applying herself, knowing that her mother would undoubtedly pick her to keep her in line with her plan for Lena to become Healer-In-Charge one day. 

 

            “She already gave it to me,” Lena quietly confessed.

 

            “Oh. Congratulations. You’re going to smash it.”

 

            Closing her eyes, Lena’s face rippled with pained amusement. “I don’t think I have much of a choice.”

 

            “Oh, come on,” Sam lightly bumped her shoulder as she smiled warmly. “You know you’re going to be great; you don’t know how to be bad at anything. And, well, surely it was expected, right?”

 

            “What?”

 

            “Head of Charms. You were always going to be the next one, it was just a matter of when.”

 

            “It’s just not … fair.”

 

            “It wouldn’t be fair either way,” Sam shrugged. “You deserve it more than anyone, you’re the best Healer in the department. It’s just complicated by your mum being in charge. But it wouldn’t be fair to deny you the job based on that, and maybe other people will think it’s not fair that you get it because of that, so there’s no way to win, but you and I both know that it will only make you work harder to prove you’re deserving of it.”

 

            Lena was sick of having to prove herself but she knew that Sam was right. She worked hard, she worked long hours with plenty of overtime, went above and beyond her brewing quota and was always working on new magic techniques or research for healing. Lena would never let anyone say she hadn’t worked hard for what she had, but she always felt inadequate, as if it was all tainted by her mother’s hand in things. She would never truly know how she measured up to everyone else on a playing field without Lillian’s involvement, so it was hard for her to accept that she was exceptional, that her mother’s condescension, belittling remarks and all-round abuse had left Lena with so little self-worth that she would never see herself as comparable to others. 

 

            “We should go out to celebrate,” Sam said with a smile. “Fancy a drink?”

 

            “Oh, um … maybe this weekend, if you’re off.”

 

            “Working until five on Friday. The Leaky Cauldron at six?”

 

            “Perfect,” Lena said, returning the smile with a weak one of her own. “Um, I should get ready to go. I need to check on my patients.”

 

            They both climbed to their feet and exited the on-call room, walking together for a short way before Sam was paged to one of her own patients and Lena was left to make her rounds, paging Interns and leaving them with orders before she went to the locker room to collect her things. Her whole body itched and she chose to shower before leaving, gathering her things and making use of the private bathrooms for the Attendings as she stripped off her clothes and let the scalding water pound her skin as she scrubbed herself clean, nails scoring lines across her body as she tried to quell the itchiness that had settled in since her talk with her mother.

 

            Dressing in clean clothes, she packed up her belongings and dirty scrubs and made her way outside to the alleyway and Apparated home. The glow of lights greeted her through the faint dimness of early evening, signalling that Kara was already home, and Lena caught sight of her girlfriend through the front window of the study as she walked up the garden path and let herself inside. Shoulders stooped slightly, Lena smiled softly as she watched Kara push the desk chair back and climb to her feet, coming to kiss her hello as she abandoned her notetaking at the desk.

 

            “Hello, you,” Kara murmured with delight as she cupped Lena’s face in her hands and kissed her sweetly. “I missed you this morning.”

 

            “I missed you too. I-”

 

            Lena faltered and wrapped her arms around Kara’s waist before laying her head on her shoulder. Closing her eyes, she inhaled deeply as she felt a tremor in her chest. Lips close to the skin of Kara’s throat, she sighed as she continued.

 

            “I was called in early.”

 

            “I figured as much,” Kara laughed as she returned the hug, swaying them slightly as they lingered in silence for a moment. Lena felt her inhale and sagged in her arms, anticipating her question. “Everything alright?”

 

            “I just … had a long day.”

 

            Her explanation for her brooding mood was vague but Kara didn’t press her on it. Instead, she kissed her hair and stroked her back as she held her for a moment longer, knowing that Lena needed her, even if Lena couldn’t bring herself to ask or explain. Gratitude welled up inside Lena as she breathed in the smell of her, lingering just a second more before she let her go.

 

            Giving her a small smile, she briefly touched Kara’s cheek. “Tea?”

 

            “I’ll make it. You go and sit.” 

 

            “It’s alright. Let me,” Lena insisted. “You were in the middle of something.”

 

            “Oh, just some work I brought home with me. I’m about done for the day, though.”

 

            Cupping her shoulders, Lena leaned in and kissed the tip of her nose. “Even more reason to let me. Go on, finish up.”

 

            Relenting, Kara backed away through the open doorway of the study and picked up her book before taking it to the sofa. Setting her satchel on the coat rack beside the door, Lena shrugged out of her robe and hung it up as well before she kicked off her shoes and walked through to the kitchen. Afternoon sunlight streamed in through the windows overlooking the garden and she felt immensely tired as she braced against the counters, basking in the warmth as Bastet nudged against her legs. As the kettle boiled, Lena stooped lopsidedly to scratch the cat along her spine, feeling the heat radiate from the stovetop as the day started to cool off.

 

            As she hovered, letting the water boil itself instead of using the impatience of magic, Lena considered burying everything under her usual air of aloofness, but she knew she’d have to tell her about the promotion, and if she told her that, it would be clear she wasn’t thrilled about it. She was good at hiding her true feelings, and it’s not like Kara would have expected her excitement to be loud, but Lena knew her girlfriend would see the confusion and frustration inside her, regardless of what she said. She could either continue as she had been, keeping so much to herself and hidden from Kara, or she could choose to leave all of that in the past.

 

            Making two strong cups of tea, she put some biscuits they’d come home with from Eliza’s on Sunday on a plate and levitated it all through to the living room. A fire was lit in the wide hearth as Kara stretched out on the sofa, eyes flitting back and forth across the page, and it looked so perfectly comfortable that Lena was suddenly hesitant to disturb the peace of their night with her overwhelming feelings that refused to be stamped down and ignored.

 

            Lena directed the two cups and plate of biscuits down onto the coffee table, her hands trembling as she gestured carefully and then rubbed a hand over her face once they were safely down. She would have preferred to do it later, at night when they were in bed, the room too dark for Kara to see her face, to catch the minute changes in her expression, but Lena could feel the building tension inside her chest, the building urge to get it out of her. She might not have been a Gryffindor, but she was no coward, and she wouldn’t shy away from her decision now.

 

            “Can we talk for a second?” Lena slowly asked, wariness in her green eyes as she wrung her hands, gaze flitting about instead of settling on her girlfriend.

 

            Looking up from her book, Kara raised her eyebrows expectedly as she marked her place with her finger. “Of course, my love,” Kara tenderly murmured, setting her book aside. “What’s on your mind?”

 

            Sitting, Lena opened and closed her mouth before clearing her throat. “I got a promotion today.”

 

            “A promotion?” Kara quietly exclaimed, a bright smile lighting up her face as she shifted closer to Lena, blue eyes creasing at the corners, brimming with pride. “That’s brilliant. Well done.”

 

            A weak smile crossed Lena’s face before her brow furrowed and Kara’s delight dimmed. She had one hand on Lena’s arm where she’d braced herself as she’d started to lean in and kiss her, but she withdrew at Lena’s evident dismay, her clouded expression leaving Kara confused. 

 

            “That’s- it’s good, isn’t it?”

 

            Wrinkling her nose, Lena couldn’t look at her, trying to force herself to speak, to formulate her thoughts into words that explained the way she felt properly. A promotion was always a good thing but how could she explain that it felt undeserved, that it made her feel bad about herself, that even though it was an achievement, it felt like a failure? Explaining that to Kara would feel like Lena was ungrateful for the advancements in her career, knowing her girlfriend had struggled to hold a job, and had struggled for every pay rise or modicum of responsibility gifted to her. But she’d promised she’d try to talk to her about these things, about the urge to cut open her arm to numb her feelings instead of dwelling in them, the reassuring comfort of deserved pain. 

 

            “Um …”

 

            Lena faltered, her throat tight, her pulse quick. Concern flooded Kara for unknown reasons as she shifted closer to Lena, her arm smoothing across her shoulders and down her back to cradle her waist as she kissed the shoulder of Lena’s shirt. Propping her chin on top, Kara looked up through her lashes with a strained look of worry.

 

            “It’s okay.”

 

            Nodding, Lena ran a hand over her face, feeling warm and embarrassed as she shifted restlessly. After a moment, she shrugged Kara off her and rose to her feet, pacing away. It was easier with distance between them, or so she imagined it would be, rounding the coffee table to grip the high mantle as she bowed her head. The heat of the fire hit her shins, a trifle too hot, a little painful the longer she stood there, and Lena considered moving but welcomed the slow tingle of it too much. Besides, there wasn’t much further she could go within the same room to speak her words to Kara, who was staring at her, her worry burning a hole through the back of Lena’s shirt as she remained seated, tense as she patiently waited.

 

            Lena knew she’d wait there all night, teeth worrying at her bottom lip, blue eyes wide and shoulders tense. It was that surety that made her finally speak, knowing that Kara wouldn’t leave, would sit and wait no matter how long it took, and would try to help her. A part of her would have preferred it if she didn’t, would have liked Kara to get angry and impatient at being shut out, would have liked her to walk out and spend the night at her mother or sister’s house, would have liked all of the bad things about herself reaffirmed so she could feel relieved to know she’d been right. But if she wanted that to happen, expected the worst of Kara, Lena knew she’d be waiting her whole life. 

 

            “You said you’d like it if I- if I … talked to you about it,” Lena rasped, her voice small and vulnerable. “When I feel like … hurting- if I ever want to use them .”

 

            There was a brief pause before Kara hoarsely replied. “Do you feel like using them now?”

 

            Hesitating, Lena nodded, shallow and quick as she felt her face redden. She couldn’t bear to turn around as she studied one of the framed photos of them on the mantelpiece, Kara’s arms around her, both of them smiling but something a little shy and uncertain about it, as if they were unsure of how to openly display their love and affection around other people. Nothing about their relationship had ever felt conventional, even now.

 

            “Why?”

 

            “I, um, I just … I feel bad.”

 

            “Why?”

 

            Rubbing her fingertips over her lips, Lena was silent for a moment as a lump got caught in her throat. “I don’t know, I just- my mum told me that I’m getting the job and I don’t have a say in the matter and I just- maybe someone else would have deserved it more. I feel bad, I feel like … maybe I don’t deserve it.”

 

            She heard Kara move then, climbing to her feet, the quiet tread of her footsteps. Lena felt her behind her before her arms wound around her waist, the brush of lips against the side of her neck, the comfort of her strong embrace. Closing her eyes, Lena leaned back against her solid warmth as she swallowed thickly.

 

            “Of course you deserve it. I couldn’t think of anyone who would deserve it more. Don’t let your mum take that away from you.”

 

            Wrinkling her nose as she tipped her head back against Kara’s shoulder, Lena exhaled softly. “It’s not fair.”

 

            “Life rarely is, but that’s not your fault.”

 

            She made a low sound of objection at the back of her throat but couldn’t speak. Lena didn’t know what else to say, how to explain the itch in her skin, all over her body, the way she’d scratched her forearm until the skin around the scar was red, how the itch hadn’t abated, how she’d chased the relief of it, scratching herself all over as she’d showered at the hospital at the end of her shift, pale skin crisscrossed with livid red lines. It had never brought relief, the itch still there, craving a bigger distraction.

 

            “Lena,” Kara whispered into her hair, against her neck, her breath warm and her voice gentle. “Your mum has always been horrible to you, she’s always made you feel bad about yourself, made you feel like you were a failure and that you weren’t as good as you are. I don’t think someone who enjoys putting you down so much would promote you unless it would’ve looked silly for her not to do that. She’s spiteful and cruel, and we both know she would prefer to embarrass you in front of the whole hospital instead of acknowledging just how smart you are, but you’re the obvious choice, the best Healer and the smartest witch, so she has to give it to you and she knows you’re going to be brilliant at it so the only way she can try and spoil it is by making you think you didn’t deserve it. It’s not fair for her to do it this way, to try and make it seem like favouritism to people who don’t know the truth, but it’s not your fault and we both know you’ll do everything you can to prove her wrong. Don’t let her have the last laugh.”

 

            Slowly exhaling, some of the tension bled out of Lena. In some ways, she already knew what Kara was saying, the words ringing true, that her mother would try to avoid doing something nice for her at all costs, but until someone else voiced those thoughts, she was inclined to not believe them. Even now, the self-conscious and anxious part of Lena wanted to poke holes in Kara’s argument, doubt the truth to it, but she felt as if she could barely speak, so sensitive and overwhelmed by the confusing feelings knotted up inside her.

 

            They stood there for a few minutes in silence. The fire crackled and Lena’s shins stung from the heat as they breathed in the smell of smoke, Kara swaying them slightly as they both stood in front of the framed photos of themselves, staring at them as they were left to their thoughts. Eventually, Lena swallowed past the painful lump in her throat, her voice barely above a whisper as she spoke. 

 

            “Kara?”

 

            “Mm?”

 

            “I didn’t keep it. The candle. I threw it away as soon as you gave it to me; I haven’t needed it until today.”

 

            “Oh,” Kara murmured, her grip loosening slightly as she pulled away to look at Lena. “I- why did you do that?”

 

            Shrugging slightly, Lena grimaced. “I felt embarrassed.”

 

            “Lena-”

 

            “I didn’t want you to think I was weak.”

 

            “I would never think you were weak. I wasn’t … testing you, I just- I was sorry for taking away what you needed. I didn’t-”

 

            “I know,” Lena interrupted. “I know, but I- it’s me. It’s the way that I- there are things I can’t talk about, I’m not … built normally, and I never will be because of the things that- that happened , but I- I couldn’t use it and then face you afterwards. Not after you knew. I- I would rather die than have you look at me like I’m pathetic-”

 

            Slowly turning her around, Kara looked at her with aching blue eyes, cupping Lena’s face in her hands. “I could never look at you like that, I could never even think that about you. I love you so much , and the only thing I feel right now is so proud of you.”

 

            Mournful green eyes raised slightly to peer at Kara through dark lashes, and Lena’s solemn, pouting lips parted as she drew in a shaky breath. “Will you … say that again?”

 

            An uneven smile crossed Kara’s face as she pressed them against the mantel, brushing dark hair out of Lena’s face before she gripped her cheeks tightly in her hands. “I am so proud of you.”

 

            “Are you really?”

 

            “Like you couldn’t even imagine,” Kara whispered as she rested her forehead against Lena’s.

 

            Eyelashes fluttering, Lena closed her eyes as her lips parted, feeling Kara’s warm breath on her mouth. She wanted her so desperately then that she would’ve done just about anything to be touched by her, the only thing that might drown out the maddening itch in her arm. Pushing against her, Lena kissed her and felt the gentleness of Kara’s lips against her own, too patient and not enough. 

 

            “Lena,” Kara mumbled against her lips, her voice low and cautious. “We should talk-“

 

            Lena made a muffled sound of objection as she continued to kiss her, pausing only as her kisses trailed from Kara’s mouth to her jaw and down her neck, her words coming out between kisses. 

 

            “Talk … later. I … want you … to … distract me.”

 

            With a huff of laughter, as Lena’s lips found a particularly ticklish spot, Kara wrapped her arms around her and pulled her away from the fire. Lena went willingly, her legs hot and vaguely numb, and she all but collapsed on her girlfriend’s lap as Kara backed up to the armchair. 

 

            “You know, if I’m distracting you , you should be beneath me ,” Kara reasoned as she slowly unbuttoned Lena’s shirt for her, pushing softly washed cotton aside and ducking to kiss her stomach.

 

            “Oh, you’ll manage,” Lena breathlessly replied.

 

            Laughing against her sternum, Kara hummed in agreement. When she pulled Lena’s shirt the rest of the way off, baring the faintly pink scar, evidently irritated from her scratching, Kara gently gripped her arm as she slowly kissed the words. 

 

            Gentle, Kara undressed her as she peppered Lena’s skin with kisses as she bared more and more of it. A little frustrated by the gentleness, Lena wished Kara would be rougher, was desperate for the bite of nails or the nip of teeth, bright little sparks of pain that would set her pulse racing, eager for more. But Kara was gentle and tender, and Lena basked in the feeling of being loved by someone. It eased the itch, her desire a welcome distraction, one that bathed her warm contentment as she gave herself over to Kara, the familiar ease of trust and love and longing shrouding her.

 

            At some point, Kara had picked her up and crossed the few steps to the sofa to pin Lena beneath her, bare skin warm to the touch as Lena let her hands smooth over scarred skin. She could never get enough of Kara, of the indulgence of touching her, each scar as familiar to her as her own, and Lena touched each one by memory, her eyes screwed shut and lips parted as she breathed rapidly, breathlessly whispering Kara’s name, breathlessly begging her not to stop.

 

            Afterwards, as the flush was leaving her skin and the sweat had cooled, the heaviness of Kara’s body on top of her as they lay tangled on the sofa, Lena felt peaceful. The crackling fire filled the silence and kept them warm as they savoured the afterglow, feeling the rise and fall of each other’s chests with each slowing breath, both too tired and delightfully dazed to move. Eventually, Kara broke the peaceful silence, her breath warm against Lena’s skin as she pressed into her.

 

            “Lena?” Kara whispered as she nuzzled against her shoulder. “Thank you for telling me. I know it’s not easy for you. It takes a lot of courage. I just wanted you to know that I’m proud of you for that too.”

 

            Eyes closed, a faint smile crossed Lena’s face as she lazily stroked her fingertips down the length of Kara’s spine. “Thanks for listening. And for distracting me.”

 

            The smile on Lena’s face grew a little as her brow furrowed with bewildered amusement, and she pressed her face into Kara’s hair. Her voice was shy as she softly whispered a confession. “It makes me feel better.”

 

            “I wish you always felt better.”

 

            “I do when I’m with you.”

 

            “I want you to feel better even when you’re not with me.”

 

            Lena hummed a laugh, cheeks shallowly dimpling as she ran her fingers through Kara’s blonde tresses. “Are you planning on dumping me?”

 

            “No,” Kara vehemently objected, lifting her head.

 

            “Then I will always feel better,” Lena assured her as she eased Kara’s head back down to her shoulder. “Even on my worst days with you … even then, I’m a million times better than my best days used to be alone.”

 

            “You’re not going to be alone again. I’ll never leave, I won’t be the one to walk away.”

 

            Lena let out another laugh and kissed Kara’s brow. “I’d be horribly cross with you if you did. That would ruin all of my plans.”

 

            “Maybe you should tell me what they are. You know, just as an added incentive, in case I ever find myself thinking like a bloody idiot again.”

 

            “No, I don’t think I will. I like my secrets a little too much, so you’ll have to wait and see.”

 

            Kara groaned, and raised her head again, giving Lena a withering look. “And just how long will I have to wait to find out what plan you’re concocting? This list of things you’re going to tell me one day only seems to grow longer, and you haven’t told me a single thing on it yet.”

 

            “Who knows? There’s no rush; we have all the time in the world.”

Chapter 43

            The months blurred together in a perfect haze of domestic bliss as the witches got used to living with each other, as if they had never lived apart, as if it was the most natural thing in the world. Lena assumed her new position at work, on-call often and using her newfound responsibilities to undertake further research into Lycanthropy, earning a fuming dressing down from her mother when she found out, but uncaring as she worked her hardest to ensure no one could criticise her skill or work ethic as she tirelessly tried to find a cure for her girlfriend. Kara finally managed to earn a spot in the Death Room at the Department of Mysteries, researching the topic that had fascinated her for years, spending an inordinate amount of time staring at that strange veil on the dais, the eerie sigh of whispers that belonged to no one. She knew it would fascinate Lena, who in a sense had her own fascination with death, perhaps tied to the Thestrals that she had studied at school for years, but Kara’s work was confidential, the same way Lena’s was, and she kept the specifics to herself.

 

            They got to know everything about each other. They both worked hard, usually long hours, coming home with the smell of the hospital and potions, or stale coffee and the ammonia tang of ink clinging to clothes and robes. Their days frequently overlapped, Kara coming as Lena was going, takeout or sandwiches on the days they weren’t home, home-cooked meals and lazy breakfasts when they were. Kara knew how Lena tossed in her sleep, and Lena knew which days to make Kara’s coffee with a little extra sugar, how serious her face looked in the mirror as she dried her hair and inspected the strands of grey. Kara knew the look Lena got on her face when she was tired and vulnerable and more likely to scratch at her forearm, in search of some pain to distract herself. 

 

            She’d distract her in other ways, hoping any form of pleasure would eclipse her doubts and worries. She knew that Lena never cried, that it wasn’t just a brave face in front of other people, that she seemed almost incapable of that feat, no matter how often Kara tried to cautiously insist it was okay, even though Kara cried quite often, unable to keep anything buried for long. They were so similar but so different as well, feeling as if no one else understood them better than the other, only to find out some new thing that made them realise that perhaps they would never truly be known to each other. 

 

            Sometimes they fought, but not often, and usually about trivial things when they did, and neither of them had ever felt happiness like that, the years blending together. There had been a time when they’d never imagined speaking again, let alone living together, coming home to each other and sharing a bed. There was a sense of monotony in the ordinary routine of their lives, but they both relished it, so much uncertainty in their childhoods making them eager for something stable and peaceful.

 

            1991 was halfway over when news passed through the wizarding community of Harry Potter showing up, and they couldn’t have known then how little time they had left together, how quickly things would become unstable and violent. At the time, it was just a fascinating piece of information to discuss over dinner as Kara came home from work and Lena shared the news with her after her girlfriend had taken off her robe and shoes.

 

            “I met up with Andrea today for coffee,” Lena said as she washed her hands in the kitchen sink, rinsing away the smell of garlic and rosemary from her skin. “She had interesting gossip.”

 

            “Gossip? Now, that’s never been up your alley,” Kara said with amusement, setting her satchel down on the kitchen table as she rummaged through it, pulling out sheaths of paper and a few work textbooks. “Go on then, what was it?”

 

            “Harry Potter’s starting Hogwarts this year. He was seen all over Diagon Alley today, so I imagine she’ll have him on the front page of the Prophet tomorrow morning.”

 

            Kara cringed slightly as she looked up at Lena, sympathy flooding her eyes. “Poor boy.”

 

            “Mm, that’s what I said.”

 

            “It’s hard enough being stared at all the time with a face like this ,” Kara weakly joked as she pointed at her scars, “let alone being the baby who defeated You Know Who. Is it true he has a scar?”

 

            Drying off her hands, Lena moved towards her girlfriend, “well, I didn’t see him so I guess we’ll have to trust the rumours, and I’m sure I can speak for all when I say we can’t help but stare at you all the time when you’re so beautiful.”

 

            Lena reached up to cup Kara’s face in her hands, kissing her tenderly, and Kara hummed against her mouth, a huff of laughter into the kiss. “Oh, is that it?”

 

            “Of course,” Lena murmured, kissing her again. “There’s nothing wrong with your face. Would you like me to break out the candle?”

 

            “Very funny.” There was a momentary pause. “I thought you-”

 

            Rolling her eyes as she drifted away, back towards the oven, Lena smiled lopsidedly. “I did throw it away. You know, I think that’s usually called a joke. ”

 

            “I did say it was very funny,” Kara insisted with her own wry smile. “Do you want some wine?”

 

            “Please.”

 

            She poured them each a glass and they lingered in the kitchen, taking sips as they talked about their days, while Lena finished off dinner, waving away Kara’s help. It was nothing more than a trivial piece of information, after all, nothing to linger over too long, no sign of Voldemort returning, not even mentioned . It was rather unimportant in the grand scheme of things, and life went on much as usual.

 

            The following year, they heard of Gilderoy Lockhart taking on the cursed position of Defence Against the Dark Arts Professor, and Lena found herself standing beside Kara in Flourish and Blotts with pristine copies of his books in hand for her girlfriend to get signed by the charming wizard. Lena didn’t find him impressive at all, remembered him as rather unimpressive at school as well, teasing her pink-cheeked girlfriend for buying into his stories, which Lena deemed rubbish. Not even a year later, he was a permanent patient in the Janus Thickey Ward at St. Mungo’s for a rather unfortunate case of permanent spell damage after a backfired Memory Charm. That had been after months of whispers that something was going on at Hogwarts, that students were being Petrified, some validity lent to the rumours when the school board had gotten involved and Dumbledore had been suspended. There had been consults with Healers at St. Mungo’s as well, about healing them, Lena making a couple of trips to Hogwarts with Sam, a little nostalgic as they sipped tea in the Hospital Wing and discussed the process for brewing a Mandrake Restorative Draught with Madam Pomfrey, Professor Snape and Professor Sprout. They made a trip down to Greenhouse Three to take a look at the Mandrakes and Lena had a faint smile on her lips as she remembered sneaking in there with Kara beneath her invisibility cloak, back when the most complicated thing between them had been Kara worried Lena wouldn’t want to be her friend if she was a werewolf.

 

            She’d gone home and told her girlfriend all about it, the memory of the smell of rich soil and the growing plants lingering. Kara had in turn told Lena about the reminders she’d faced while teaching there, the way the old castle and surrounding grounds had been saturated with so many memories of their friendship as young girls. They felt so much older now, which was amusing considering how young they still felt, despite the years passing by. Their friends were meeting people and settling down, Andrea getting engaged to Russell, Nia and Querl moving in together. Alex and Kelly were talking about kids. It still felt surprising that they were all grown up, entering their thirties, independent and with their respective careers and responsibilities. 

 

            More often these days, over drinks, their friends would ask when they were going to get married. Both of them brushed the questions off, easily dismissed with eye-rolls and smiles. The truth was they didn’t talk about marriage, not really something either of them considered important, already in love and committed to each other, but each of them still a little insecure, not wanting to ask and face the sting of rejection. It also gave the other an out, no obligation to stay if they got bored, if they woke up one day and realised they’d made a terrible mistake. Each time one of them insisted that things were perfect just the way they were, the other took it as a sign to not overcomplicate it. 

 

            Things complicated themselves as it was though, Kara coming home early in August with an unusual sombre air about her, evidently jittery as Lena watched her come in from the sofa. She’d been sitting by the fire, drinking tea and doing some reading for her ongoing research. It had been a few years and Lena hadn’t made any breakthroughs yet, piggybacking off of Belby’s Wolfsbane Potion as she tried to find a way to improve on it. No such luck yet, but she was committed. Not for her benefit, or for fame or accolades, but for Kara. Lena would love her no matter what, but even though it had been relatively safe and easy to brew the Wolfsbane Potion and lock her girlfriend in the fortified cellar each month, it still took its toll on Kara, and that was the main priority. How could she make it easier for her, unpainful and quicker, how could she stop the transformation at all? Her attention was torn from her reading at the sound of the front door softly swinging open.

 

            “Hey,” Lena softly greeted her. “You’re late. I thought you would’ve beaten me home.”

 

            “Sorry, long day,” Kara sighed.

 

            Lena watched her take off her navy robe, hanging it on the hook, her satchel beside it. Shoes slipped off, glasses flecked with a few specks of rain from the light summer shower outside as dusk was ushered in. Something was troubling her, her countenance pale when she finally met Lena’s gaze, silent for a moment. 

 

            “I, uh, I bumped into Alex on my way out,” Kara said as she loosened the wide tie knotted at her throat, tugging it out of the knitted vest she was wearing over her loose shirt. “It hasn’t come out yet, probably won’t take long though - every Auror in the place was running about like madmen - but, uh, she told me there’s been an escape at Azkaban.”

 

            Lena straightened with shock, her spine stiffening. “Who?”

 

            “Sirius Black.”

 

            She deflated slightly as a prickle of relief ran through her, her book splayed limply in her lap as her throat went dry. “I- how? That’s … not possible.”

 

            It was the first time she’d tasted fear in a long while, the sour taste of bile creeping up her throat as she worked hard to swallow it down. Her stomach lurched nauseously and Lena could feel the way her shirt clung to her back as a sudden clammy coldness stole over her.

 

            “They don’t know yet, the Aurors are still investigating. Um … they don’t know if it’s an isolated incident or if- it’s just … maybe you should take some time off,” Kara said, tripping over her words as she moved towards Lena with urgency. “We could go on holiday for a while. Maybe just … get away.”

 

            “He doesn’t know it was me,” Lena hoarsely replied. 

 

            It was a weak argument to what she knew Kara’s concerns were, and she knew that her brother was no idiot. If he managed to escape in the same manner, he’d never be brazen enough to walk around in public as a wanted man. And even if he did, she still had that hope that he didn’t know she’d turned him in with the others, that she’d written his name in a letter to Dumbledore and helped put them all away. She knew the public accusation had been made by Karkaroff, that she’d only sent to Dumbledore what would inevitably be declared in court, and she clung to the thought that her brother would never expect it of her, that she could be so bold after so many years being downtrodden. But she was still a Slytherin, despite her many Ravenclaw qualities, had been picked for that house for a reason, and despite her evident ambition, she had a cunning streak as much as the rest of her family.

 

            “If we just went for a- a week, just until they’re sure,” Kara tried to convince her, a strained look of worry on her face.

 

            “If he gets out, running makes it seem like I’m guilty of something. I’m sure the Aurors will find out what happened, and good luck to anyone else trying to slip past the Dementors. I’m not sure how Sirius Black managed to do it, but Azkaban’s in the middle of the North Sea, so good luck to him too if he’s planning on swimming to shore. As it is, I have nothing to fear from him.”

 

            Kara’s mouth thinned as she hovered uneasily, silent as she stared at Lena. Leaning forward, Lena picked up her tea, draining it to the dregs, and then met Kara’s gaze. Her breaths felt shallow in her chest, heart pounding, but she wouldn’t let go of her thin veneer of bravado.

 

            “I’m fine, Kara,” she said after a moment, but her face was pale and there was a faint tremor in her hand as she set the cup back down.

 

            “Okay,” Kara eventually replied, moving again as she crossed over to Lena and kissed her. “How was your day?”

 

            Lena gave a vague recap of her shift but it was obvious she was distracted, and she remained in the living room, keeping up the facade of reading as she anxiously chewed her lip and thought of her brother. It would have been impossible for him to know, but it wasn’t even the thought of him finding out that chilled her; her brother had been cruel in the last few years before his capture, no longer the boy who’d played chess with her when she was little, and she wondered what twelve years in Azkaban had done to him now. Raving mad, vengeful and malicious - only a depraved person would have tortured people, she was sure of that much - she would have put him at the top of her list of people she had no desire to lay eyes on again. Even above her mother. Lillian might’ve been responsible for so much of the pain in her life, but it had been Lex that had inflicted it on her command, and it was hard for Lena to stomach even the thought of being in the same room as him again.

 

            Kara made dinner for them and put music on, trying to bring Lena out of her brooding thoughts. She was worried about her girlfriend, knowing that Lena would never speak openly about her family, not since she’d first divulged the true depths of their inhumane brutality inflicted upon her, and she wished she’d kept her mouth shut but knew it would be better for it to come from her. Kara would rather sit beside Lena in silence all night than let her read the news tomorrow, or in a few days - however long it took for The Daily Prophet to get their hands on the story - and find out by herself. 

 

            Despite insisting half a dozen times that she was fine, Lena still wasn’t convincing. She poured them both wine and refilled their glasses a few times, trying to soften the edges of her mind. And she was very forthright as she shed her shirt in the kitchen while Kara finished cleaning up, glancing over at her and doing a double-take as she watched Lena remove her pants as well. Drying off her hands, Kara crossed over to her and kissed her gently, hands in her hair, over her soft skin, feeling the warmth of her, sensing the urgency, the need for something to blot out any negative emotions. She’d gotten used to that, infrequent but always noticeably different to their usual sex, a kind of desperation and aching in Lena’s kisses and touches, as if needing Kara to make it stop hurting. Kara didn’t know whether she should have said something years ago, whether each time she indulged her, she was allowing Lena to get away with not talking about the things that hurt. It was no different this time; Kara picked her up and carried her upstairs to bed.

 

            Afterwards, listening to Kara’s slow, even breaths for a while, Lena assumed she was asleep and carefully slipped out of bed, rising to put on thick socks and a sweater, the cottage cool at night, even in summer. She couldn’t sleep and she didn’t want to wake Kara, so Lena crept out of the bedroom and made her way downstairs. The fire was still burning, Bastet curled up on the armchair, the old cat opening her eyes to narrow slits as she watched Lena move through the still house. 

 

            Morrigan was off hunting and Lena poured herself a glass of water in the kitchen as she stared through the open window above the sink, staring out at the quiet garden. She didn’t know how long she’d been standing there, pensive and restless, didn’t realise that Kara stood behind her until she felt her chin on her shoulder, her arms coming around Lena’s waist. Closing her eyes, Lena clutched the glass of barely touched water tightly and felt Kara’s lips on her throat, just above the pulse of her heart. Throat feeling tight, Lena squeezed too tightly and shattered the cup a moment later, slicing the palm of her hand as the sound of breaking glass filled the silence.

 

            Making a small sound of panic at the back of her throat, Kara drew back and Lena stared at her pale palm in the dark, dark blood welling up. Kara moved away, taking a clean tea towel from a drawer and wrapping it around the wound, but Lena wasn’t all that bothered by it, blinking slowly as she looked at her hand wrapped in the green and white striped linen, dark red starting to spot it as her fingers curled around the fabric. 

 

            “Oh.”

 

            “Where’s your wand?” Kara asked.

 

            “Upstairs. It’s fine,” Lena murmured, unwrapping the towel and turning on the tap.

 

            Cold water made the cut sting, the pressure of it heavy against her palm, and she watched the blood rinse away for a second before crooking her fingers and using nonverbal and wandless magic to close it up. She could still feel the sting of pain, could’ve done a more thorough and better job with a wand, but Lena relished the little prickle of pain as she flexed her hand a few times and shut off the water. Drying her hands on the bloody tea towel, she set it down on the counter and turned.

 

            “Watch your feet,” Kara warned her, gesturing towards the broom propped up beside the door. 

 

            Picking her way across the floor, Lena watched the broom sweep up the mess and decided to deal with the rest in the sink in the morning. She felt drained, too distracted to concentrate on anything else. Kara turned her attention back to her and reached for her hand, which Lena let her take and inspect herself, a soft kiss pressed to the palm.

 

            “Sorry, I didn’t mean to startle you.”

 

            “You didn’t.”

 

            “You had me worried when I woke and you weren’t next to me.”

 

            She would have known that Lena hadn’t been called in, no origami crane or butterfly lovenote on the pillow or nightstand to let her know, and Lena felt a flicker of guilt. Reaching up, she brushed Kara’s greying hair out of her face, knowing how much her girlfriend worried about her, how anxious she could get at times, how much it bothered her that Lena kept so much to herself. Leaning in, Lena pressed her lips to Kara’s, leaving them there a second before she pulled back.

 

            “I’m sorry, I didn’t mean to worry you. I just wanted some water.”

 

            “You couldn’t sleep,” Kara guessed.

 

            “No, I couldn’t. It’s alright, let’s go back to bed.”

 

            “Tell me what you’re thinking.”

 

            Mouth thinning, Lena gave her a tender look. “I’m thinking about how much I’d like it if, just for five minutes, you would let go of your worries and fears. I’m okay, darling. I would tell you if I wasn’t, I promise. I’m just too caught up in memories of the past, but that’s just it - the past .”

 

            Shoulders slumping as she exhaled, Kara wrapped her in a hug and Lena let herself be held for a few minutes, the kitchen dark and silent as she listened to the strong beat of her girlfriend’s heart. Lips grazing the base of her throat, Lena closed her eyes, breathing in the smell of her skin, feeling a sliver of peace pierce the shroud of confusing unease. 

 

            “What guarantee is there that the problems of the past won’t be a problem in the future?” Kara eventually whispered into her hair.

 

            Lena couldn’t argue with her, but refused to let her believe that. Pulling back slightly, she cupped Kara’s chin in her hand and kissed her firmly. “Well … you were a problem of the past, so to speak,” she said with amusement, eyes bright in the dark as she pulled back further to get a glimpse of Kara’s face. “And now you are my future.”

 

            “I just hate the thought of something hurting you,” Kara softly sighed. “You’ve endured enough pain for ten lifetimes.”

 

            Lena shushed her, her voice a little rasping as she tried to remain confident. “He can’t hurt me, he’s in prison.”

 

            And that was true, at least, for a while. They went to bed, put it to rest, and a week passed by, a little tense as they waited to hear more, but eventually it blew over. Sirius Black was the only prisoner to escape, and they couldn’t figure out how , the entire wizarding community on edge and on the lookout, but no more trouble came from it. They read rumours of sightings in The Daily Prophet, and over drinks with Alex at The Leaky Cauldron, but they were nothing more than that.

 

            The following year, Kara caught wind of the Triwizard Tournament starting back up at Hogwarts after centuries of being banned, hearing it from Alex, who’d heard it from Kelly, word spreading through the Ministry of Magic as the Departments of International Magical Co-operation and Magical Games and Sports coordinated with their counterparts to revive the event. Holed up in Kara’s tent as they camped out for the 1994 Quidditch World Cup, all of the previous Hogwarts alums lamented about missing out on the glory of a tournament like that when they’d been at school, bickering back and forth about which of them would’ve put their names in and who would’ve been most likely to be picked. 

 

            It all seemed like fun and games then, late August down in Devon in a misty field, one tent amidst hundreds, placing bets on whether Ireland or Bulgaria would win as they drank Firewhisky and bottles of Dragon Scale, Galleons and Sickles offered up, bickering about who should’ve made it to the grand final and whether they’d remembered to bring the bacon for breakfast. Lena had little interest in Quidditch but was a staunch supporter of Ireland winning out of solidarity with her home country, Kara, Kelly and Querl siding with her, while the others thought Bulgaria had the edge, bringing up players and manoeuvres as it all went over Lena’s head. 

 

            They’d all used a Portkey that had left from Trebah Garden, just south of Falmouth, the night before, finding their spot with the sign that read Danvers , intending for it to be a fun weekend. Lena had gotten three days off work, Sam, Andrea and Russell had come as well, and it was a tight fit even inside the magical tent. They all had sleeping bags stretched out and it felt a little bit like being back at school, all of them older now but left to cause trouble. There were far wilder tents, and they all saw familiar faces as they wandered about, Kara pointing out some of the fancier tents as she walked hand-in-hand with Lena, their wellies sinking into the soft earth of the moors. 

 

            The game itself was too quick for Lena to follow, but the atmosphere was undeniably infectious. Kara had convinced her to get her face painted with the Irish flag, and Lena had bought them both shamrocks and Quidditch jerseys. The noise was deafening and their group grew steadily drunker, pounding back beer, wine and whisky since a little after they’d had breakfast. Each time Ireland scored, the crowd erupted into cheers, beer flung about, soaking into their clothes, making their skin sticky, and Lena even found herself swearing along with the others when a player was fouled, shouting over the boos as she made a diagnosis for his concussion and pointed out the mediwizards from St. Mungo’s to Kara.

 

            Ireland won, despite Krum catching the snitch, and Kara happily accepted the fistfuls of coins from her friends, delighted and pink-cheeked from the alcohol as she pocketed them for Lena as well. They were all loud and a little unsteady as they made their way out of the packed stadium, and Lena laughed as Kara was hoisted onto James’s back, her hands cupped around her mouth as she joined in with the celebratory chants. It was a few days before the next full moon and her girlfriend had looked a little pale beneath her scars earlier that morning, before her face had been painted, but Lena was utterly smitten as she watched her revel in the atmosphere.

 

            They had more drinks back at their tent, filling the space between the haphazard rows as they shouted and set off green sparks from their wands. Even those who’d backed Bulgaria weren’t too sore about their lost bets, singing and laughing, their shouts mingling with the thousands of other witches and wizards. It seemed to go on all night, hallucinogenic mushrooms Querl had brought handed out and ingested, more beer, wine and cigarettes, the strong smell of Muggle weed, and Lena felt dizzy and clammy, finding herself on the grass between their tent and their neighbours, giggling and tired as she watched the sky fill with colourful sparks, predominantly green, Kara’s mouth hot on her neck and her collarbone.

 

            “Merlin, I love you,” she breathlessly whispered.

 

            “I love you too,” Kara murmured, pushing herself up slightly, kissing her slowly. Their friends were all drunk and rowdy and she laughed into Lena’s mouth. “Let’s go somewhere.”

 

            “Anywhere,” Lena readily agreed, kissing her as she raked a hand through Kara’s hair. 

 

            They were on their feet, fingers threaded together, stumbling through the crowds as they stepped over guy lines and around prone figures, passed out already, getting swept up in dancing crowds, laughing together, kissing, pushing their way through as everything seemed to sway and lurch. Eventually, they made it somewhere quieter, the coolness of the woods blanketing them as they entered the fringes of it, the noise dimming somewhat as they put a little distance between themselves and the field, aching for a little privacy. Pulling her behind a tree trunk, Kara pressed Lena up against the bark, kissing her a little sloppily, both of them laughing, off-balance and using the tree for support. 

 

            “Shh,” Lena hushed Kara, although they both continued to giggle together, hands untucking clothes, undoing buttons, trying to be quick and unobtrusive.

 

            “Mm,” Kara hummed against her lips, hand sliding up Lena’s ribs as her girlfriend managed to get her hand past the waistband of her jeans. “I love you, I love you.”

 

            “I love you too. I love- I love hearing you say it.”

 

            “Do you? I’d say it all the time … if- if you wanted me to.”

 

            A shaky laugh escaped Lena as Kara’s lips brushed over her jaw, and Lena turned them, pressing her up against the tree now. “I do. Go on, tell me now.”

 

            She dragged Kara’s jeans down a little further as she ducked her head down, kissing the soft skin of her stomach and then kneeling on the ground, Kara’s breath hitching as her mouth sank lower. “I do love you,” Kara breathlessly insisted. “I love … everything about you. I’d- I’d even marry-”

 

            There was a loud scream, startling them both as Lena staggered upright. She tottered for a moment before pitching forward, palm grazing over rough bark. Letting out a huff of laughter, Lena nosed Kara’s cheek. 

 

            “Frightened the life out of me. We Irish sure know how to- to have our fun, I suppose,” she laughed, teeth nipping at Kara’s lip. 

 

            The shouting seemed to get louder as Lena pressed up against her, Kara’s hands up her shirt again, splayed over her back, and then there was a scream, and another one, making them pause. Their breaths were quick and shallow, nose to nose as they both stiffened, listening.

 

            “Do you think-” Kara whispered.

 

            There were more shouts then, the sound of pounding footsteps, raised voices as the hum of laughter and singing turned into something that was fraught with panic. Lena was already hitching Kara’s jeans up, fumbling with the buttons, trying to think clearly, confused and unsteady, fumbling for her wand in her back pocket, the forest seeming suddenly nefarious as she watched the trees grow bigger, her mind reeling. 

 

            “Something’s wrong,” Lena hoarsely murmured, her eyes wide in the dark as she grabbed Kara’s hand, keeping her behind her as she stepped around the trunk. 

 

            A few people flew past, twigs and leaves crunching underfoot, their sharp, panicked breaths making Lena pull up short. She lit her wand, casting a circle of light ahead of them, hearing people crash through the trees, hearing screams growing louder, more fearful, the loud bang of something exploding sudden and unexpected. Moving towards the edge of the woods, they took in the chaotic sight of hundreds of witches and wizards running in every direction, tents blazing in the dark as the canvas was set afire, voices calling out, people Disapparating and spells rocketing back and forth. And above it all, for the first time in fourteen years, the Dark Mark hanging above the campsite, both of them questioning their sobriety for a moment before Kara acknowledged the truth.

 

            “Alex,” Kara rasped, her voice strangled with terror.

 

            She lurched forward and Lena’s heart leapt into her throat as she moved to stop her, snagging her around the waist and hauling her backwards. Kara tried to twist out of her embrace and they briefly struggled as their feet scuffed the floor.

 

            “No, no, Kara, Kara,” Lena pleaded, dread in the pit of her stomach. “Kara, we won’t find her there. We have to go. We have to go , okay?”

 

            “I- no, we- we have to-” Kara whispered as her face crumpled with confusion, pale and frightened as she turned in Lena’s arms.

 

            “We- we can- we’ll go to your mom’s,” Lena rasped. “She’ll go there. She’ll- Kelly will be with her. They’re together, okay?”

 

            Doubling over, Kara vomited at their feet and Lena wrapped her arms around her, her vision pitching and swaying, her chest tight and her wand slippering in her clammy hand. She closed her eyes, holding Kara tightly. “Shh. It’s alright.”

 

            She Disapparated them out of there as her mind reeled, the knife of panic, the drugs and alcohol, making it hard to concentrate on the cottage in Falmouth, the sounds of screams, the haunting image of the Dark Mark, all of it distracting and terrifying. Lena Disapparated away from the edge of the woods to the pavement outside Eliza’s home with the nauseating, painful experience of Splinching for the first time. Stumbling forward, she let go of Kara, both of them spilling to their knees on the concrete, and pressed her hand to her left shoulder, where the cotton of her Ireland jersey was quickly soaking with blood.

 

          It could’ve been worse, given her state, but Lena felt faint and sick as Kara hauled her to her feet, dragging her to the front door. Eliza looked up from her knitting with a stricken look on her face, eyes going from Kara to Lena, both of them sweating and wide-eyed, grey-faced, especially the latter as the red stain on her shirt continued to grow. 

 

            “What’s happened?”

 

            “Death Eaters,” Kara said as her voice broke.

 

            Disbelieving, Eliza stood there for a moment until Lena sagged slightly, and then she moved quickly, helping Kara sit her down. Her face held a waxy sheen to it and her throat was dry as her eyelashes fluttered.

 

            “It’s fine, it’s just Splinching,” she hoarsely explained. “We- we got separated. The others- I-”

 

            “Oh, well, you know Alex,” Eliza blithely sighed, kneeling at the Healer’s side, trying to pull aside the collar of the jersey to see the damage. “She’ll be there until they’re caught - whoever they are.”

 

            Kara’s mouth thinned at that as she clutched Lena’s hand tightly, already worried enough. Clicking her tongue, Eliza gestured to Lena, “you’ll need to take your shirt off to get a good look at it.”

 

            Stomach lurching with sickening panic, on top of the already nauseating fear of what had just happened, Lena swallowed thickly, licking her lips. “If- if you have any Essence of- of Dittany, I’ll be able to-”

 

            “I’m sure there’s some in the kitchen,” Eliza distractedly replied as she walked out of the living room.

 

            Moving quickly, Lena snatched up her wand where it had fallen in her lap, yanking the sleeve up over her forearm and pointing the wand at the words carved into her skin. Her lips moved in a barely audible spell, hand violently shaking as she tried to glamour the scar before Eliza returned, Kara watching with a tense set to her face as she balled her hands into fists in her lap. She finished in time, letting her wand fall back into her lap and pulling her arm out of the sleeve and pushing it up over her shoulder. Kara got a good look at the rent skin, a few chunks of flesh missing from Lena’s upper arm where she’d Splinched herself, and Eliza’s mouth turned down at the corners as she set down a few things on the coffee table and knelt on Lena’s other side.

 

            “I’ll-”

 

            “You are drunk,” Eliza softly interrupted, unstoppering the Essence of Dittany, “and in no shape to perform magic at the moment. Let me.”

 

            Lena couldn’t really argue, her head aching, her vision swaying, chest beating quickly as she drew in shallow breaths, felt the keen pain in her shoulder as blood ran down her arm. It had all happened so fast, had all been going so well , and then it had turned bad so suddenly that she was struggling to process it at all. As Eliza applied hissing droplets of Essence of Dittany to the wound, Lena’s body going rigid, her face crumpling with pain as she refused to make a sound, Kara squeezing her hand as she flinched and winced the whole way through it, Lena thought of how many people had been there, wondered if any were dead, how many were injured and flocking to St. Mungo’s. She should’ve been at work, helping get through the dozens of patients with broken bones, but Eliza was right - she was drunk, and found herself lacking a hangover cure right then. More importantly than that, she couldn’t bear to leave Kara then, not when she was wrapped tightly in the clutches of her fear for her sister. Eliza was still tending to Lena’s wound where the ghostly Patronus of a foxhound appeared in the middle of the living room to relay a message from Alex that she was safe, as were the rest of their friends.

 

            The relief that swept through the three of them was palpable, and Lena closed her eyes as she dwelled on the at for a moment. Still, she had the dreaded feeling that this was just the beginning, and was proven right almost a year later when two letters showed up at their cottage within the hour of the Triwizard Tournament ending on 24th June, 1995.

Chapter 44

            Kara was home alone when the letters arrived, spat out of the fireplace and onto the rug unannounced and unaccompanied by anyone else. A crease forming between her brows in consternation, Kara set her notes aside, quill set back in the jar of ink as she wiped her stained fingers on the thighs of her jeans and pushed herself to her feet. Stooping to pick up the letters, she saw they were nearly identical, save for the names written above the address. 

 

            Turning over the letter with her name on it, she took note of the scarlet seal set with the image of a phoenix and felt unease wind through her. Nothing good could come of Dumbledore contacting either of them, but Kara had to know why as she slid her finger beneath the folded edge of the parchment and tore it open. It was a rather sparse letter, merely two sentences, quite vague aside from an address and a time. Yet, Kara knew there could logically only be one reason for the contents, and yet, it didn’t make sense.

 

The Order of the Phoenix is reconvened. 

 

Meet at 12 Grimmauld Place, Islington, London at midnight.

 

            Frowning, she rubbed her brow, the letter crumpled slightly in her fist as her throat closed up. Lena wasn’t home yet, should be soon though, and Kara resolved to not do anything until her girlfriend was home. Anxiously checking her watch, she saw that it was half past ten. By eleven, her girlfriend still wasn’t home and by half past eleven, Kara started to worry, pacing back and forth. 

 

            Making herself sit as she overthought everything, midnight ticking closer and closer, the sound of the door opening was met with a rush of relief washing through Kara. The sight of Lena cut cleanly through the air of unease that had shrouded the room, and Kara wasted no time, barely allowing her girlfriend time to step over the threshold and hang up the cloak she had draped over one arm before she was pouncing.

 

            “Oh, you’re still up.”

 

            “You’re late,” Kara anxiously greeted her, scrambling to her feet, snatching up the unopened envelope with Lena’s name on it.

 

            Running a hand over her face, Lena let out a weary sigh, half a groan, looking knackered. She hadn’t even showered at the hospital, still in her scrubs, the rumpled top tucked into the elasticated waistband of the pants, her hands planted on her hips as she blinked owlishly.

 

            “What a fucking nightmare,” she declared, a grim expression on her face.

 

            “You heard?” Kara asked with surprise, pulling up short.

 

            “Yeah,” Lena wearily replied as she crossed over to her, taking Kara’s face in her hands, kissing her softly. “They had to bring his body in for examination; I had to be there to check for any charms involved.”

 

            Confusion flashed across Kara’s face, her brows furrowing together as she pulled back. “Body? What body?”

 

            Lena looked just as confused for a moment, continuing towards the kitchen, stopping to pet Bastet before she moved through to reheat the dinner Kara had left for her. “Wha- I thought you said you’d heard.”

 

            “I- what did you hear?”

 

            “The Triwizard Tournament,” Lena said, looking over at Kara, who trailed her into the kitchen. “The Hogwarts champion - that Diggory boy - was killed.”

 

            Surprise blossomed on Kara’s face, sympathetic and shocked to hear it. “You’re joking.”

 

            Shaking her head, Lena grimaced as she opened a bottle of elderflower wine. Raising her eyebrows as she lifted the bottle, she poured two glasses as Kara nodded, and they took their seats at the kitchen table. Taking a sip of wine, Lena turned her attention to her dinner.

 

            “Looks lovely, thank you, darling.”

 

            “What happened?” Kara pressed her, ignoring her thanks.

 

            “Well, that’s the thing, there must’ve been a dozen Aurors there and not one of them would say a bloody thing. I assumed Alex had spoken to you-“

 

            “No. No, I haven’t heard from her.”

 

            “Oh. Well, it was the last challenge this evening. Some sort of maze, from what I heard. No one knows what went on inside but … well, one of them died. And all of the department Heads took a look at the hospital and it seems- well, there’s only one explanation, and … no one likes that thought. He was killed by the Killing Curse .”

 

            Dread made Kara’s stomach lurch. She felt a chill in the kitchen as if they’d left the back door open to let in the night breeze. Clearing her throat, Kara set her hands on the table, pressing the unopened letter flat.

 

            “A letter came for you earlier. I think … it might be connected.”

 

            Setting down her fork, Lena picked up the letter, turned it over, looked at the wax seal and let out a derisive snort as she tossed it back down. “What does he want?”

 

            “You might want to read it. I got one too,” Kara whispered.

 

            Suspicious, Lena picked the folded piece of parchment up as a wary expression stole over her features. Breaking the seal, she unfolded the letter and her eyes quickly ran over the two sentences. She dropped it back to the table and Kara saw that theirs weren’t quite identical. There was no invitation to 12 Grimmauld Place in Lena’s, but the same notification of the Order reconvening and a request to meet with Dumbledore at Hogwarts at her earliest convenience. 

 

            “Ah,” she murmured, a stiffness to her shoulders.

 

            There was a moment of heavy silence before Lena's gaze slid to Kara. She ate a mouthful of her dinner, the shortcrust pastry of the pie clumping together, like concrete to swallow as her throat tightened with a prickle of fear. Clearing her throat, she drank a sip of wine.

 

            “What do you think he wants?”

 

            “I think there’s only one reason why he’d send a letter like that.”

 

            Lips pressed into a flat line, Lena considered that, cocking her head to the side. “Surely not. Did yours say the same thing?”

 

            “More or less,” Kara said, hesitating as she briefly contemplated lying - or omitting the meeting request - and then relented. “There’s a meeting being held at midnight.”

 

            Lena glanced down at the watch on her left wrist. Eight minutes to. She looked at Kara again, taking in the uncertainty on her face, her blue eyes shadowed, a spark of old anger lingering in their depths. Toying with her food, Lena licked her lips as she cast her gaze down again.

 

            “Are you going?”

 

            Kara swallowed thickly. “No.”

 

            Eyes darting back up in surprise, Lena blinked. “Why not?”

 

            Running a hand through her hair, stressed and worried, Kara shrugged as she shook her head. “I- are you going?”

 

            “I wasn’t invited,” Lena curtly replied.

            

            “I know that, but he asked you to meet with him. We both know what he’s going to ask.”

 

            “Right.”

 

            “So, are you going?”

 

            Lena hesitated, deliberating before she let out a sigh. “I suppose I should hear what he has to say.”

 

            “No,” Kara loudly objected, slapping her palm against the table with enough force to rattle Lena’s cutlery.

 

            Surprised by the vehemence of her outburst, Lena’s eyebrows rose. Kara’s cheeks flushed pink, the tips of her ears red and her scars a livid silver against her pallor, and she closed her eyes, chest rising and falling quickly. Her voice was rough as she continued.

 

            “No, you can’t meet with him again. You know what he’s going to ask you to do. It’s not right of him to do that, not after what- if this is about what we think it is, I’m not letting him do this to you again.”

 

            “Kara-”

 

            “No, Lena. I won’t let him.”

 

            “I suppose that’s why you’re not going?”

 

            Swallowing thickly, Kara gave her a petulant look. “He’s a liar. I want nothing to do with his scheming this time, no matter what’s at stake.”

 

            Lena opened and closed her mouth, genuinely surprised by Kara’s stubborn objection. “You won’t just sit by and watch innocent people get hurt. That’s not you.”

 

            “For your safety, that is me.”

 

            “My safety?” Lena spluttered. “This has nothing to do with me.”

 

            Scoffing, Kara quietly seethed. “What part of this isn’t to do with you? Do you remember last time? Because I do. I remember how he made you do things that- you used to hurt yourself because of what he made you do. There are things that happened that I will never forgive him for.”

 

            “You and I … it’ll be different this time,” Lena hoarsely reassured her, hitting the nail on the head. She set her hands down on the table, palms facing up, an aching look on her face. “I won’t have to lie to you this time; you’ll know what I’m doing, who I’m loyal to.”

 

            Tears stinging her eyes, Kara shook her head, a petulant jut to her lip. “I don’t want to do this.”

 

            Moving her hands forward slightly, reaching for her, Lena’s mouth turned down slightly at the corners. “You don’t have to do anything you don’t want to do. But people will have questions-”

 

            “Let them say whatever they want,” Kara scoffed as she slid her hands into Lena’s, gripping her tightly. “Let them think I’m a coward; you and I know the real reason. And that’s all that matters in the end. I won’t let you be used again. Even if it means I sit this one out too.”

 

            Shoulders slumping, Lena softly sighed and then bowed her head, kissing the backs of Kara’s hands. As she straightened up, her eyes snagged on her watch; the minute hand just past twelve. “Okay,” she murmured. “Okay, we’ll sit this one out together. If that’s what you want to do.”

 

            “Thank you,” Kara whispered, exhaling with relief.

 

            She wiped her cheeks and Lena gave her an aching look. Even then, she had the thought that her girlfriend was someone who couldn’t abide sitting by idly, knowing that at some point, it would eat away at Kara that she wasn’t helping. But Lena was apprehensive to throw herself back into spying anyway, her brother locked away and her mother only a fringe supporter of Voldemort last time, making her a relatively useless spy, so she was happy to oblige if it assuaged Kara’s fears. For how long, she wasn’t sure. 

 

            Hesitating, Lena half-rose from her seat and leaned forward to kiss her before she sank back down and turned her attention back to the steak and kidney pie on her plate. Truthfully, she was putting on a brave face herself, but she felt uneasy. If what they feared was true, she doubted anyone would blame her for that cold knot of dread sitting heavily in her stomach. 

 

            Kara convinced her to eat most of her dinner, although Lena’s appetite evaded her, before they tidied up and Kara pulled her into a tight hug. She could feel the tension in Lena’s body, similar to the tension in her own, and neither of them spoke for a moment, lingering in the comfort of each other’s embrace, before Kara kissed her temple and pulled away. 

 

            “Let’s go to bed,” she whispered, gently squeezing Lena’s arm.

 

            Nodding, Lena slipped her wand out of her scrub pants pocket and silently moved around the kitchen, locking the back door and warding it, the hinges tightening slightly, warding the windows and moving through to the living room, warding the door there as well. They’d kept the entire property warded, mostly out of Lena’s desire to be undetectable by her mother, but she had the sudden thought to set up a Secret Keeper. That could be a job for tomorrow, too tired to have that discussion with Kara right then, not wanting to think about it at all, about what it could mean and what information they were missing, as opposed to meeting with Dumbledore as her girlfriend was.

 

            Once she was sure the house was properly locked up, Lena wearily plodded upstairs with Kara on her heels, the quiet of the house feeling tense. Slipping into their bedroom, the sheets slightly rumpled where Kara had sat earlier, changing into pyjamas as she waited for Lena to come home, her Saturday spent idly pottering about the house and the garden, making the pie for dinner, amused by the Garden Gnomes trying to take up residence in a rabbit’s burrow amidst the Singing Daffodils outside. This wasn’t how she envisioned her Saturday night going, the last couple of hours spent waiting for Lena to come home, with dread in her stomach and the urge to hold her tight and know she was safe - for now.

            

            “I’m going to shower,” Lena murmured, fishing pyjamas out of the dresser, ducking her head to press a kiss to Kara’s shoulder as she scooted past and out into the hallway.

 

            Nudging her glasses up, cold fingers pressed to her eyelids, Kara tried to slow her mind. It was still reeling, so many unknown factors leaving her feeling worse. She had the secret thought that she should’ve gone to the meeting, hid it from Lena until she’d found out more, had all of the facts. But she didn’t want to lie to her, these last six years together with her working because of their candour and trust, because they had worked so hard at the things that had made them so uncertain and secretive and destined to fail so many times before. It wasn’t even something she considered with any type of seriousness, knowing that she would tell Lena, no matter how badly Kara wanted to hide it from her.

 

            She was slowly turning down the bed, listening to the muffled sound of the shower running, when there was a banging knock on the door. With a heavy sigh, having an inkling who it was, Kara’s shoulders slumped as she abandoned the blankets and moved to the door, hoping to intercept her sister and have her gone again before Lena was finished in the shower. She’d tell her she stopped by, of course, but at least she’d be in control of the conversation, could keep Lena out of it. Alex didn’t know of Lena’s involvement anyway, ignorant about the things Dumbledore had asked her to do, only knowing that there was no Dark Mark on her forearm and that she’d turned in her own brother. 

 

            Socks slipping on the stairs in her haste, Kara was slightly breathless as she answered the door, trying to block the way with her body but not doing a very good job as Alex stepped forward. “Hey, I was just heading to bed. Can we talk tomorrow?”

 

            “Where the bloody hell were you?” Alex demanded as she swept inside.

 

            There was something panicked about her sister’s appearance, a rare restlessness to her movements as she flexed her fingers, curled her hands into fists, eyes darting around the dark living room as Kara eased the front door shut and cast her hand around, illuminating the space. She hadn’t got that far in her plan to brush her sister off and floundered for a moment, playing with her fingers.

 

            “Um …”

 

            “You got a letter, right? We all got letters,” Alex continued, momentarily confused as if she thought Kara might’ve been excluded for some reason.

 

            “Oh, yes, the letter, right, um …”

 

            Looking bewildered, Alex’s brows furrowed. “What’s the matter with you?”

 

            “What?”

 

            “I- Dumbledore reconvened the Order, and you just didn’t show up? You know he wouldn’t have done that unless-”

 

            “I know,” Kara roughly cut her off. There was a beat of silence as she rubbed her brow, swallowing thickly. “Um … is that the reason why?”

 

            She watched her sister’s face pale slightly, a stiffness to her shoulder, her eyes wide with fear that Kara knew she rarely felt. “Yes,” Alex gravelly confirmed. “He’s returned. Or so Dumbledore says.”

 

            “And we should believe everything he says?”

 

            Scoffing, Alex gave her a surprised look. “What, now you’re doubting Dumbledore?”

 

            “No, I just- what proof does he have? I mean … where did all of this come from?”

 

            “If you’d come to the meeting, you’d know all of that.”

 

            “Okay, well, I didn’t go to the meeting, so can you just tell me what the bloody hell is going on?”

 

            Raking a hand through her hair, scowling, Alex licked her lips, hesitating briefly before she lowered her voice. “Is Lena home?”

 

            “Yes, she’s upstairs. It’s late; she just got home from work, so if we could-”

 

            “Is that what this is about?”

 

            “I- what do you mean?”

            

            “You haven’t told her, have you? I mean, it’s supposed to be a secret. I know it was years ago but … does she know?”

 

            “I- this has nothing to do with her,” Kara softly replied, “and it’s going to stay that way.”
