            Alex scoffed loudly, throwing her hands up in frustration as she paced back and forth. “Oh, come on, Kara. What, you’ll go out with her, you’ll move in with her, but you won’t tell her you’re an Order member? Do you think she’s not going to find out?”

 

            “It has nothing to do with that,” Kara said with a little more steel this time.

 

            “I know I was harsh, I know I judged her a lot last time, and that wasn’t fair to either of you, but I was wrong and she’s not on their side, so you can’t keep this from her. Ask Dumbledore to let her join-”

 

            “No.”

 

            Blinking as surprise crossed her face, Alex’s mouth opened and closed for a moment, her eyebrows rising. “What do you mean no?”

 

            “No , I’m not asking Dumbledore to let her join and no, I don’t want any part in this.”

 

            Spluttering, Alex shook her head, utterly bewildered. “Last time, you wouldn’t shut up about joining the Order until you finally got an invite. Now, you don’t want any part in this? What happened?”

 

            “How many people died last time?”

 

            “I- well, it’s war . People die in war, that’s just the sad truth of it. But people have to fight for what’s right as well.”

 

            Looking down at the floor underfoot, Kara felt a lump in her throat as she scuffed her sock over the stone. “I have fought hard for the life that I have, for my job, for my relationship, and to help my condition. You don’t understand that, and I don’t expect you to, but I won’t sacrifice my peace to die in another war.”

 

            “Oh, right,” Alex flatly replied. “Well … I never took you for a selfish coward, but …”

 

             “It’s not selfish or cowardly to stay out of it,” Kara rasped.

 

            Still, she felt a prickle of shame at her sister’s accusations. They weren’t true in the sense that she meant it, but there was a kernel of truth to it. Kara was doing it for Lena, out of her grudge she still held towards Dumbledore, nursed over the years as more information had been divulged by her girlfriend, the fear of what he might coerce her into doing this time, and if that made her selfish and a coward, then she would happily be selfish and a coward. She didn’t expect Alex to understand, and had no intention to get into it with her; it wasn’t about her not telling Lena, but rather Lena not telling anyone else.

 

            With a quiet scoff, Alex’s mouth thinned with dismay. “Well, if you grow a spine, you’ll know where to go.”

 

            Her sister moved towards the empty grate of the fire, reaching up to take a handful of Floo powder, and Kara spluttered as she stepped towards her. “Aren’t you going to tell me what happened?”

 

            “No, Kara, I’m not . That’s for Order members to know.”

 

            Casting her handful of Floo powder into the grate, emerald flames burning high, Alex ducked into the fireplace and spoke her address, an angry look on her face before she vanished a moment later. Frustrated, quietly cursing her sister, Kara banged her hand on the back of the sofa, her hand sinking into the cushion, as she seethed for a moment.

 

            “That could’ve been handled better.”

 

            Cupping her forehead, Kara exhaled sharply. “Yeah.”

 

            She lifted her head and then turned, moving to the bottom of the stairs to look up at Lena, wrapped in a towel, her face in shadow. With a weary wave of her hand, plunging them into darkness, Kara stomped upstairs, her fingers grazing the soft towelling at Lena’s waist as they made for their bedroom. In the lamplight, she watched Lena dry off and change into the pyjamas she’d pulled out, reclining on the bed with her arms folded beneath her head and a brooding look on her face. 

 

            Sinking onto the edge of the mattress, the time almost one o’clock now, Lena grimaced as she touched Kara’s arm. “Tell her,” she hoarsely murmured.

 

            Kara’s eyes widened a fraction and she pushed herself up onto her elbows. “What?”

 

            “Tell her why . I- don’t let this come between the two of you. Not something so trivial.”

 

            Sitting the rest of the way up, Kara took Lena’s face in her hands, palms warm and lightly calloused. They trembled slightly, steadying as she cupped Lena’s cheeks, thumbs gently ghosting over her soft skin, flushed faintly pink from the shower, and Kara swallowed thickly.

 

            “You are not trivial,” she said, her voice wavering, dropping her hands and picking up Lena’s left arm, her fingers pushing up the sleeve to bare the old scar. “This is not trivial.”

 

            Her head dipped down, mouth hot as she kissed the words, and Lena’s face rippled with a pained smile. They’d been together so many years now that it no longer bothered her to have Kara see the scar, to touch it so easily, but it was still a source of shame to speak about how she’d continued what her mother had started. And yet, she hadn’t done that in years, had no clue what Kara had done with the quill, even after all this time.

 

            Swallowing with some difficulty, Lena smoothed her sleeve back down. “It’s been a long time since I did that.”

 

            “That doesn’t mean that it’s nothing . It doesn’t mean that he wasn’t responsible for making you do things that made you hurt yourself more. I’m not explaining that to my sister, I’m not explaining that to anyone ; that’s none of their business.”

 

            “Okay,” Lena whispered, her eyelids shuttering.

 

            “Go to sleep,” Kara urged her, cradling her face again and kissing her sweetly. “I’ll find out more tomorrow.”

 

            They both got beneath the blankets, moving into their usual positions, Kara pummelling her pillows into shape, scooting closer to Lena’s back, an arm around her waist. It was warm, late June leaving the day muggy, and they were both restless for hours, shedding clothes, whispered deliberation over cracking open the window, kicking off the blankets and moving apart. It couldn’t be attributed to the weather though; it was unseasonably hot, so it wasn’t the first warm night they’d had. It was late when they both drifted off, Kara first and then Lena, but neither of them felt well-rested when they woke.

 

            Clammy and flushed, Kara had a cool shower when she woke, Lena joining her a short while later, hiding a yawn behind her hand as she tore back the shower curtain, grumbling a good morning. She had the day off, on account of her long shift, but neither of them was in the mood to do much, trying not to think about what was going on, Kara making them coffee and toast, Lena reading that morning’s copy of The Daily Prophet , no mention of Voldemort tainting the pages yet. 

 

            They kept the front and back doors open to let in what little breeze there was, going about their distractions. Kara settled at the desk overlooking the front garden as she leafed through tomes of mythological deities of death, while Lena holed herself up in the cellar, working on a new variant of the Wolfsbane Potion. They were supposed to be having dinner at Eliza’s, a near-weekly tradition for a Sunday, and when Lena came to enquire about what time they were leaving, Kara put up a half-hearted fight, insisting that she didn’t want to be around her sister, but ultimately found herself on her mother’s doorstep at the appropriate time. 

 

            Letting herself in, Kara kicked off her shoes as she sullenly looked down at her sister’s boots, and then moved further into the little cottage, catching sight of Alex in the kitchen. Eliza appeared in the kitchen doorway, her cheeks rosy from the heat of the oven, the open back door doing nothing to dim the stifling warmth of the house, the news talking of an incoming heatwave, despite them being situated on the coast. 

 

            “Hi,” Kara murmured, letting her mum kiss her cheek, scooting past her.

 

            “I thought we’d eat out the back today. It’s boiling; Lena, surely you’re too warm in that.”

 

            “Oh, I run a bit cold,” Lena said with a thin smile, tugging at the cuffs of her shirt, which she had folded back once, enough to bare her wrists but not much else. “Shall I put the squash in the fridge, Eliza?”

 

            She raised the bottle bearing the label Tongue-Tying Lemon Squash , and Kara turned back to her, holding a hand out for it. “I’ll pour us a glass now.”

 

            “Did you say there was an umbrella in the shed?” Alex called out, stepping outside, already trying to put distance between herself and Kara.

 

            “It should be behind the dragon manure, sweetheart - and mind yourself with the Devil’s Snare!” Eliza called after her before rounding on her other daughter. “Now, whatever argument you two have had, I’ll have no word of it here, okay?”

 

            Rolling her eyes as she stepped into the kitchen, setting the squash down on the counter, Kara scoffed. She reached for five clean glasses, lining them up as she unscrewed the bottle. “It’s nothing. She’s just being- you know how she gets.”

 

            “Yes, I do,” Eliza agreed, gently resting her hands on Kara’s shoulders before moving past her. “But I know how you get as well.”

 

            Grimacing, Kara filled the glasses and levitated them towards the door, letting Lena follow Eliza out first before pausing to meet Kelly’s stare as her sister-in-law leaned against the counters. “Did she tell you?” she murmured.

 

            “Of course,” Kelly sighed, her cheek dimpling with exasperation. She unfolded her arms and snagged a glass out of midair. “She hasn’t told your mum, though.”

 

            “Is she taking the piss? She’s mad at me because I don’t want to drag Lena into it and she won’t even tell our mum?”

 

            “Well, I think it’s a bit different - mums aren’t girlfriends, and Alex is-”

 

            “An arse.”

 

            “Alex is getting involved,” Kelly patiently finished, an understanding look on her face as she reached out to touch her arm. “Look, Kara, I don’t know what changed, why it’s so important for you to keep this to yourself and stay out of it - that’s fine by me, it’s nobody’s business what you decide to do - but you have to understand that she’s not going to see it that way. She runs headfirst into trouble, it’s literally her job. It’s just … well, you do the same, usually for different reasons, like getting caught up in experimental magic and all of that, but I just think she’s confused that you’re not leaping at the chance this time. It’s not personal , she just- she’s upset her sister won’t have her back.”

 

            With a surly look on her face, Kara glowered and swallowed past the lump in her throat. “Yeah, well, it is personal, actually. And you’re right … it’s nobody’s business.”

Chapter 45

            A fortnight passed by quickly, the news bleaker by the day as word spread throughout the Wizarding community. It was perhaps worse that most people seemed to brush it off as a rumour, no pit of dread in their stomachs as they blatantly refused to acknowledge what Dumbledore had vocally proclaimed. For all of Lena’s mixed feelings for the old man, she trusted that he wasn’t lying about that. She said as much to Andrea over coffee five days after the news had broken, after reading The Daily Prophet over breakfast and Apparating to Diagon Alley to poke her head into her friend’s office and ask if she was free.

 

            Andrea was surprised by the unexpected visit but happily obliged, leaving behind the smell of paper, ink and owls for the balmy air of the cobblestoned streets as they found an empty table and ordered coffee. Sitting in the shade of an umbrella, watching shoppers and workers pass by, they bickered back and forth when Lena finally broached the topic.

 

            “An interesting spiel in the Prophet,” Lena said as she raised her cup to her lips, raising her eyebrows.

 

            With an annoyed glimmer in her blue eyes, Andrea made a scathing sound at the back of her throat. “Don’t give me that. We have to print what the Ministry says; you can’t expect me to go against Fudge.”

 

            “Oh, that idiot,” Lena rolled her eyes, clicking her tongue as she set the cup back down. “Well, be careful, alright?”

 

            “I am. This is me being careful.”

 

            Still, Lena wasn’t sure it was the right decision. She could understand her friend pandering to the Ministry and the story they wanted to spin, but it felt fraught with danger and she thought that people deserved to know the truth. How else would they take it seriously? It was none of Lena’s business though, and aside from the palpable tension over drinks with friends, and aside from the absence of Alex from her life during that fortnight as the sisters ignored each other, everything was relatively normal. Lena had drinks with Kelly, both women commiserating over the stubbornness of their partners, she went out for dinner with Kara, Querl and Nia, the latter warily mentioning the bad dreams she’d been having, her dark eyes shadowed with worry as her gaze kept flitting between Kara and Lena. It felt like everyone was walking on eggshells, the Wizarding World waiting to see who was right.

 

            At work the following Wednesday, Lena had finished a procedure on a child whose magic had started to show signs, rolling the stiffness out of her shoulders as she walked through the hallway in her scrubs. It wasn’t even lunchtime yet and she’d been slammed from the moment she’d shown up early that morning, her scrubs dotted with blood she hadn’t had time to vanish, her fingers slightly pruned from washing her hands. Healers sidetracked her, snagging her attention to glance over a chart, asking for a consult, and she patiently fielded their questions until she was distracted by a familiar voice.

 

            “I’m fine. No, I don’t want to sit, just- is Healer Luthor here today? No, not the Chief. Why would the Chief deal with this?”

 

            Excusing herself from the Intern she had been speaking with, Lena rounded the nurse’s station and turned left, facing the lift. Another Intern Healer was trying to make Alex sit in the wheelchair, blocking the grille of the lift from shutting. Lena’s attention snagged on the bloody leg of the Auror, and she quickened her pace.

 

            “Alex.”

 

            “Oh, good, you are here.”

 

            “I’ll take it from here,” Lena said to the Intern, touching the young man’s arm to dismiss him. “Fill out the paperwork to admit her; she already has a file. Danvers, Alexandra.”

 

            He nodded, getting back in the lift, and Lena grabbed the wheelchair and Alex’s shoulder, firmly pushing her sister-in-law down onto the seat. “Sit. What the bloody hell happened?”

 

            Rolling her eyes, Alex pushed her reddish hair back and sighed heavily. “Work-related.”

 

            Lena wheeled her down the hallway, flicking her wand at a mop leaning against the wall, which started to trail after them, mopping up the dripping path of blood left in their wake. Moving through to the general ward in the Charms Ward, Lena wheeled Alex to an empty bed, jerking the curtain around slightly and helping her stand. Unable to put much weight on her injured leg, Alex leaned on Lena for a moment before sinking onto the thin mattress.

 

            Once she was settled, Lena worked on her dragonhide gloves and rolled up the hem of the pants, taking in the shredded calf as it bled freely. Clicking her tongue, Lena glanced over her shoulder, looking for an Intern.

 

            “Can I get two units of Blood-Replenishing in here, please?”

 

            Moving over to the cart stocked with supplies, she rifled through a drawer for pads and gauze, another for a pair of tweezers, and hooked the little wheeled stool with her foot, dragging it closer. Taking a seat, pumping the stool higher, Lena lifted Alex’s leg to arrange the pads beneath it and then hummed disconcertingly as she gently prodded along the length of the gashes, eliciting a sharp hiss of pain as Alex reached for her leg, scowling.

 

            “Ow. That hurts, you know.”

 

            “I’ll give you something for the pain in a minute,” Lena patiently replied. “I just need to take a look first, make sure it’s not damaged-”

 

            “Obviously it fucking is.”

 

            With a quiet chuckle, Lena smiled, glancing up at Alex, who was looking a little green. “I mean your nerves, you dafty. Keep still.”

 

            After a quick inspection, the lit tip of her wand revealing the relatively clean wound, Lena lightly pressed gauze to it to stem the bleeding. An Intern returned with the Blood-Replenishing she’d requested and Lena had them start an intravenous line, hooking Alex up with some saline and injecting the draught into it. While that helped to replenish the blood seeping from her leg, Lena used a syringe to draw out some of a local anaesthetic and numbed the area as Alex detailed what had happened.

 

            “We were on the tail of a suspect and he dropped a load of Peruvian Instant Darkness Powder and then tried to use a Blasting Curse to escape through the wall. Bloody bastard couldn’t see and nearly took my fucking leg off.”

 

            “Well, you’re lucky; it must’ve grazed you.”

 

            Mouth thinning, Alex leaned back on the pillows as Lena slowly cleaned out the wound, dabbing Essence of Dittany into the cuts before carefully murmuring under her breath as she drew the edges of the wounds together, a patchwork of pink lines on Alex’s leg once she’d finished. They would heal with no scar, and Lena applied a salve on top before bandaging Alex’s leg.

 

            “Right, let me get a listen of your chest as well,” she said, beckoning for Alex to sit up as she unlooped the stethoscope around her neck.

 

            Listening to her heart and her breath sounds, Lena was satisfied and made her lean back against the pillows, the bed inclined slightly. Looking surly and a little pale, Alex clicked her tongue with annoyance. “Kelly’s not going to be happy.”

 

            “Do you want me to notify her?”

 

            “No, she can give me an earful when she’s home.”

 

            “Right, well, you need to stay under observation for a bit, so …” Lena glanced down at her watch and deliberated. “I can take my lunch now. Coffee?”

 

            “Please.”

 

            Nodding, Lena said she’d be right back, making her way to the Tea Room and buying two coffees and some sandwiches, hesitating before buying two Chocolate Frogs as well - one to give Alex’s blood sugar a spike, the other for Kara’s sweet tooth - and then made her way back to the ward. Setting everything down, Lena dragged a chair closer to the bed, picking up her own sandwich and opening it.

 

            “Here,” she said, pausing to toss a Chocolate Frog onto Alex’s lap, “get some sugar in you as well. You’ll be fine in an hour.”

 

            “Ta.”

 

            “So … we missed you at drinks the other night.” 

 

            “Been busy,” Alex evasively responded.

 

            “Mm. Kelly said when we got lunch. Wouldn’t have anything to do with you ignoring your sister, would it?”

 

            Snorting, Alex rolled her eyes. “If she hasn’t told you why we’re arguing, I’m not going to.”

 

            Nodding, feigning ignorance, Lena took a bite and chewed thoughtfully. Swallowing, she hesitated. “She misses you.”

 

            Rubbing the bridge of her nose, Alex sighed. “How is she? How was the full moon?”

 

            “Uneventful.”

 

            “I heard- I mean, I’ve been asked- I had to speak to Professor Dumbledore about something,” Alex evasively spoke, her eyes fixated on the paper coffee cup in her hand as she affected a nonchalant air. “Um, he said he’d sent her a few letters. Do you know anything about that?”

 

            “Letters?” Lena echoed. “Like … plural?”

 

            “Mhm. A few, apparently. He’s been trying to get in touch with her. She hasn’t responded.”

 

            “Oh, uh, no, no, I don’t know about any letters. You know me, I’m usually here, so …”

 

            “Yeah, I thought so. Anyway, if you could maybe ask her to reply … it seems important. I’d ask her myself, but …”

 

            “You’re both being pigheaded.”

 

            Scoffing, Alex rolled her eyes. “If you knew why , you’d know it’s her-”

 

            “If I knew why , I’m sure she’d have a good reason.”

 

            “I don’t know why she doesn’t just tell you.”

 

            “I’m fine not getting involved,” Lena shrugged, which was true, despite the different context in which she meant it.

 

            “What, it doesn’t bother you that she’s keeping something from you?”

 

            Lena gave her a thin smile, “everyone’s entitled to secrets.”

 

            Groaning, Alex rolled her eyes again and opened her sandwich. They didn’t continue down that avenue of conversation any further, eating their sandwiches, sipping coffee and talking about work, an upcoming concert Alex asked if they wanted to get tickets for, if they should go away for Kara’s birthday at the end of September. Of course Alex knew Lena had heard the rumours, although she didn’t suspect Lena of knowing the specifics of the Order or that she’d received a letter that night herself, but still, neither of them voiced the possibility of what might be happening by the time September rolled around. 

 

            In two weeks, nothing had changed, but there was that air of unease, especially with the ones who believed Dumbledore’s word. Lena might not have trusted his methods, but she believed him. By the time she discharged Alex, she was itching to get home herself and interrogate her girlfriend about these supposed letters. Lena hadn’t been lying about that; aside from the original one delivered the night of Lord Voldemort’s return, she knew nothing about Kara receiving any letters from Dumbledore.

 

            Fortunately, she wasn’t pulled into any emergency procedures on her way out, Disapparating away from St. Mungo’s and walking towards the picturesque patch of countryside, before she crossed the newly warded boundary and the air seemed to waver, the cottage suddenly appearing. They had decided on Kara being the Secret Keeper for the property, with the reasoning that Kara was the most likely to need to invite someone over to the cottage, so it made sense for her to have the ability to divulge the address. Lena let herself inside, hanging up her robe, calling out for Kara as she stooped to scratch Bastet behind the ears as the old cat came to greet her. 

 

            She heard Kara’s footsteps upstairs, the creak of the floorboards approaching the stairs. Pulling down the hem of a t-shirt, Kara quickly descended the stairs, giving her a warm smile. “You’re home earlier than I expected.”

 

            “Mm, I managed to avoid anything too crazy on my way out,” Lena said as she leaned in to kiss her. “And I’m not on-call tonight; shall we have Chinese for tea?”

 

            “You know I’d never say no to that.”

 

            “How was work?” Lena conversationally asked, slipping off her shoes, inching the cuffs of her long-sleeved shirt up a little at the warmth of the evening. 

 

            “Not bad. We’re working on something interesting at the moment; I wish I could bore you with the details. Think … research into a sort of veil between life and death.”

 

            “Sounds interesting.”

 

            Kara hummed in agreement, padding away, moving towards the window to open it for Morrigan, who opened one eye slightly to give Kara an irate look. “How was your day?”

 

            “Mostly uneventful. Your sister was admitted.”

 

            Head quickly jerking to look at Lena, face taut with worry, Kara’s eyes widened with panic. “Is she alright?”

 

            “She’s fine. I treated her myself, had her out of there in no time,” Lena soothingly reassured her, crossing over to Kara and taking her face in her hands. She cocked her head to the side, grimacing slightly. “She was more worried about you.”

 

            “Me?”

 

            Still holding her face in her hands, Lena’s shoulders slumped slightly as she softly exhaled. “She told me about the letters. I’m just wondering why you didn’t tell me about them.”

 

            Closing her eyes, a furrow formed between Kara’s eyebrows. “Ah,” she muttered. “How’d she know about them?”

 

            “Dumbledore.”

 

            “Dumbledore?” Kara repeated, her eyes flying open in surprise.

 

            “What’s this all about?” Lena murmured, smoothing her thumb over Kara’s cheek.

 

            With a sigh, Kara ducked her head, reaching up to cover Lena’s hand with her own. She moved out of her touch, crossing the room to duck into the office. It was a shared space but Kara did most of her work there, while Lena had relegated herself to the cellar, with half of the space dedicated to her brewing - not just Wolfsbane, but other experimental varieties. Opening the desk drawer, Kara rifled through the contents and pulled out a few unopened envelopes, all of them stamped with Dumbledore’s seal.

 

            Lena reached to take one and saw that it wasn’t unsealed. Brows furrowing together slightly, she met Kara’s gaze. “Aren’t you going to see what he wants?”

 

            “We said we weren’t-”

 

            “Yes, but four letters in a fortnight?”

 

            Kara shrugged, crossing her arms over her chest, a brooding look on her face. Lena turned over one of the letters, studying the elegant calligraphy and then held it up, arching an eyebrow.

 

            “Do you mind?”

 

            Gesturing indifferently, Kara shrugged. “Have at it. I’ll go and get dinner.”

 

            Nodding, Lena drew out the desk chair, sinking onto it as Kara shrugged on a jacket and put on some shoes, the front door opening and closing as Lena broke the seal of the first letter. She paused before reading, watching Kara walk away from the cottage through the little window overlooking the front garden and the sliver of lake. Watching her Apparate away, Lena sighed softly before returning her attention back to the letter.

 

Dear Miss Danvers,

 

In the hopes that my previous letters have not gone unanswered, but have merely been waylaid, I am writing to you again with the request to meet at your earliest convenience to discuss a matter of great importance.

 

I look forward to your response.

 

Professor Albus Percival Wulfric Brian Dumbledore

 

            Lena opened the other letters, finding three other iterations of a similar kind, spreading the four pages out on the desk as she pressed them flat with her hands. She was still sitting there, her chin cupped in her hand, dark hair falling around her face as she stared at the words, when Kara returned with a paper bag and the smell of sesame oil filling the cottage.

 

            Gathering up the letters, Lena tucked them back into the desk drawer and climbed to her feet, pushing the chair back in. Sighing, she walked through to the kitchen, where Kara was unpacking the bag, setting down foil containers. Lena brushed her hand across her back as she passed by, fetching plates and forks, levitating a bottle of elderflower wine and two glasses after her. Taking a seat, she uncorked the wine and poured them both a glass.

 

            “I think you should speak with him.”

 

            Shoulders slumping, Kara grimaced as she picked up a container of fried rice. “I thought you’d say that.”

 

            “Just find out what he wants. You don’t have to say yes-”

 

            Kara let out a sharp laugh. “I’m not going to.”

 

            “Look, you have a lot of people you love involved in this. I’m not daft; I’m sure every single one of your friends is a member, or at least involved. You’re sitting it out because you’re holding a grudge on my behalf, but I don’t need you to do that for me.”

 

            “It’s not a grudge. It’s about making sure he can’t use you again.”

 

            “He’s not.”

 

            “Can you look me in the eye and tell me that if I meet with him, if I say yes to whatever request he has, you’re not going to get involved? If I do this one thing to help, you’re not going to say yes to anything he asks you to do?”

 

            Fixing her with a level stare, Lena swallowed thickly but her voice was firm as she replied. “Yes.”

 

 

            It wasn’t her first time returning there and she knew what she would find, but Kara was still apprehensive as she walked through Hogsmeade, the day cool but clear, and the Scottish Highlands surrounding the little town. The castle in the nearby distance was unchanged, as ever, and she felt a pang of nostalgia for the place, as a previous student and a teacher. Both times, it had been a place of stability amidst so much uncertainty, and while she had mixed feelings about everything that had happened, about taking the job even though she knew a bit of what had happened with Lena, about quitting over her pride instead of her morals, she still felt a fondness for the place as she returned.

 

            The walk was quiet and pleasant as she passed through parted gates and followed the path to the open doors. With it being school holidays, Hogwarts was virtually empty, only a few members of staff occupying it, so it felt oddly vacant and silent as Kara lingered on the threshold for a moment, the smell of cool stone, furniture polish and the outdoors washing over her. The crumpled letter in her pocket informed her to head straight up to Dumbledore’s office, and Kara knew the way well enough, stepping into the empty castle after a moment and making her way through the maze of passageways and staircases.

 

            Stopping outside of the Gargoyle statue, Kara fished the letter out, despite committing the contents to memory, and spoke the password. “Cockroach Cluster.”

 

            The statue moved, revealing the spiral staircase, and Kara stepped onto it, standing still as she moved up through the stairwell, coming to a stop outside of the office door. Swallowing, she raised a hand and knocked, the door opening on silent hinges a moment later. Stepping inside, she met the piercingly pale eyes of her old Headmaster, feeling a little uncertain and wary as she moved further into the office.

 

            “Professor Dumbledore.”

 

            “Miss Danvers. Thank you for coming. I trust you’ve been keeping well?”

 

            “Quite. And you, sir?” she couldn’t help but add, unfailingly polite as she approached his desk.

 

            He gestured for her to take a seat, and they went through the niceties for a moment, Dumbledore making a few vague comments about the school and alluding to everything that had happened of late. Reaching for a kettle on a laden silver tray, he poured them both a cup of tea and set the plate of Ginger Newt biscuits in the middle of the desk between them.

 

            Holding her cup and saucer in one hand, Kara felt a little awkward, shifting restlessly and taking a biscuit out of politeness. Dumbledore dunked one in his cup of tea and took a bite, humming appreciatively. 

 

            “I appreciate you coming so late in the afternoon,” he said a moment later, adding sugar to his tea and stirring as he studied her over the half-moon rims of his glasses. “Am I correct that you've come straight from work?”

 

            “Yes, sir.”

 

            “And you’re still employed in the Department of Mysteries, yes?”

 

            “Yes, I’m still an Unspeakable.”

 

            “Good, good. That is very good to hear. The work is to your liking?”

            

            “Oh, yes, it’s very interesting,” she earnestly replied. “I’ve worked my way up to more complex projects since I started back there, so it’s very mentally engaging.”

            

            Nodding, he smiled kindly and took a sip of tea. “Would any of these projects be related to the Hall of Prophecy?”

 

            “The- I’m not sure-”

 

            Uneasiness wound through Kara as she shifted restlessly, cramming half of her biscuit in her mouth as she tried to avoid answering. There were rumours, of course, but only Unspeakables were privy to what actually went on within the Department of Mysteries - and the Minister, she had to suppose, although she’d never seen Fudge down there - and Kara was sworn to secrecy. She wouldn’t even confirm that it existed, setting the uneaten half of her biscuit on the edge of the saucer and smoothing a hand over her thigh, brushing off the crumbs.

 

            “I understand that you’re unable to go into detail about your work,” Dumbledore softly continued when she remained silent. “However, if there was a Hall of Prophecy, and you undertook work related to it … that would be extremely helpful, if you were interested in aiding-”

 

            “I’m sorry,” Kara murmured, her eyes on the cup clutched in her hands, her knuckles turning white as her throat guiltily closed up. “I can’t.”

 

            “I understand your predicament, that your situation is precarious and you wouldn’t want to jeopardise your career, but I wouldn’t ask you to risk-”

 

            “It’s not just that, sir, I-”

 

            She closed her eyes, swallowing thickly. Pressing her lips together, she hesitated.

 

            “You sent Lena a letter as well. A different letter,” she met Dumbledore’s gaze as she spoke, her words becoming a little more accusatory as she continued. “You didn’t invite her to the meeting. You don’t want people to know because … you were hoping she’d spy for you again, weren’t you?”

 

            He cleared his throat, leaning forward slightly in his seat. Kara was glad he didn’t dare to look ashamed of what he was asking of people, appreciating his conviction as he ducked his head in agreement. 

 

            “That was my intention, yes, although I haven't heard from Lena since.” He hesitated briefly. “I take it she has no interest in aiding us this time?”

 

            “No, she doesn’t,” Kara brittly replied. “And I’d appreciate it if you could leave her out of it, sir.”

 

            “Thank you for passing on her decision-”

 

            “No, that’s not her decision, it’s mine. Last time- it wasn’t right, sir. The things she had to do. She still holds onto that guilt, and I get that you have more important things to worry about, but she is my important thing to worry about. So, you can send me letters and ask me to do things for you, that’s fine, but she has nothing to do with this.”

 

            Her voice wavered and she had to curl her right hand into a fist to stop it from trembling in her lap. Drawing in a shaky breath, she gave him a solemn look, watching as he steepled his fingers and studied her for a moment.

 

            “Well, that is very admirable, Kara. I confess, I had anticipated the reason for your silence on that matter, although I had hoped I was wrong. It would be a great contribution to the Order to have your assistance, even if it’s only in the capacity of which I brought you here today. But I understand your reservations. If it’s any consolation, you have my word that I won’t reach out to Lena again, but I must ask you again if you’ll reconsider.”

 

            Biting her lip a moment, her expression guarded, Kara felt a flicker of relief but was still wary as she studied that lined face of her old Headmaster. “What did you want my help with, exactly?”

 

            “There’s a prophecy in the Hall of Prophecy.”

 

            Brow creasing with confusion, Kara took a moment to sip her tea, thinking. “Can I ask what’s so important about the prophecy?”

 

            “It pertains to Lord Voldemort personally. That’s all I can say on the matter, but I believe he will come for it soon. Or rather, others on his behalf.”

 

            “And what would you have me do? They can’t be removed unless it’s by the person it’s about; no one else can steal it.”

 

            “Yes, I had heard that they were well warded. I still believe he will try. I was hoping to have someone within to report back to me on anyone behaving unusually, anyone who might’ve been targeted.”

 

            Nodding, Kara set her cup of tea down on the edge of the desk and anxiously ran her palms over her thighs as she considered it for a moment. Hesitating, lips parting, she slowly pushed herself to her feet, keeping her head ducked down as her cheeks warmed.

 

            “Thank you for your time, Professor, but I don’t think I’ll be able to help you with that, sorry.”

 

            “Ah. That is a pity.” Swallowing thickly, she kept her gaze on his neatly cluttered desk as he climbed to his feet. “Thank you for your time, and if you should ever change your mind, please do send word. The Order would greatly benefit from your help once more.”

 

            He extended a hand and Kara hesitated before taking it, his grasp gentle, covering her other hand with his as he patted the back of it. Glancing up, Kara’s face rippled with a sheepish smile, pained and guilty.

 

            “I’m sorry, sir. I wish it was different. I just- I don’t think you have much use for someone who isn’t going to follow orders without question.”

 

            “I shall disagree with you there, Miss Danvers,” he softly replied, patting her hand once more before letting go. “Everyone has their uses, even if it is not apparent at the time.”

 

            She frowned faintly, nodding uneasily before she picked her bag up from the floor. “Have a good night, sir.”

 

            “And you, Kara. I hope to hear from you soon.”

 

            He smiled kindly and it was almost maddening, his response eliciting a flicker of irritation as Kara felt like her words had fallen on deaf ears. Nodding, she made her way out of the office, the stairs winding back down and spitting her out into the hallway. Running a hand through her hair, Kara exhaled heavily and walked back through the empty castle, only crossing paths with Mrs Norris, who hissed at her and skulked away, no doubt to fetch Filch.

 

            Kara emerged out into the fresh air and paused to stare at the view spread out before her, dismay and frustration welling up. A few owls flew away from the castle and she breathed in the smell of the Forbidden Forest on the wind, the daylight lingering. The walk down towards the castle gates, which she’d always found rather meditative and pleasant, now felt plagued by her anxious thoughts, her guilt. If she could help stop Voldemort, shouldn’t she do it? Even if it meant risking her career, even if it meant putting her trust in a man who’d hurt someone she loved. But it felt so distant from her daily life that it was easy for Kara to think of him in the abstract, as not a real threat. But for how long would that be true?

 

            Stepping through the gates, she Apparated home, letting herself inside, hanging up her robe and unbuttoning her waistcoat, throwing it over the back of the kitchen chair before she poured herself a glass of water. Sipping slowly, she brooded in the kitchen and then walked through to the study, leaving her wand on the desk and trying to distract herself with a thick book on prophecies that she’d plucked from one of the stocked shelves behind her. Thumbing through pages, she read until it started to get dark, Lena not home yet, and jotted down notes on a blank piece of parchment, unsure why she was doing it, unsure what difference it would make to know more about them. It had nothing to do with her. 

 

            As night crept in, the hour growing late, her eyes started to burn, reading by candlelight with the cat curled up on her lap. Taking her glasses off, she rubbed them clean with a handkerchief from her pocket, putting them back on and then startling at the sound of the front door opening. She accidentally elbowed over the inkpot, spilling the contents over the pages and narrowly missing her lap as she swiftly climbed to her feet. Blotting it up with her handkerchief, she sighed, a divot between her brows.

 

            Sinking back onto her chair, she crumpled her page of notes and then cupped it in her palm, setting it on fire, aware of Lena taking off her shoes, setting down her bag. “Hello, my love,” she called out, closing her book, her shoulders feeling tense.

 

            Walking into the study, Lena stopped at her left side, stooping to kiss her. “Hi, darling, good day?”

 

            “Mm,” Kara hummed, nudging her glasses up as she rubbed her eyes. “Just a lot on my mind.”

 

            “Such a serious girl,” Lena laughed, rubbing Kara’s back. “Anything you can share?”

 

            Hesitating, Kara deliberated briefly before looking up at Lena. Her gaze was solemn and Lena’s gentle curiosity dimmed slightly with concern. “I went to speak with Dumbledore after work.”

 

            “Oh. Oh, and how was that?”

 

            Rubbing the bridge of her nose, Kara frowned as she shrugged. “Not particularly eventful. I don’t think we have to worry about him bothering us again.”

 

            She smiled crookedly and Lena gave her an uncertain look, expression clouded. Crouching at her side, Lena rested her forehead against Kara’s arm, her hand splayed over her thigh. “What did he want?”

 

            “Oh, just the same as before. Apparently, everyone has their uses. It’s okay though, I told him we didn’t want to get involved.”

 

            “Okay,” Lena whispered after a pause, and Kara brushed her dark hair back, leaning down to kiss the side of her neck.

 

            She’d forgotten to eat dinner and the hour was late, so they ended up eating beans on toast, drinking tea at the kitchen table as they talked about their day. Kara was evasive, trying to skirt around Lena’s questions about her conversation with Dumbledore, and the dregs of her tea were cold by the time they finished talking, both tired from a long day, both eager for bed. Wrapping Lena in her arms, Kara held her close and felt the knot in her chest loosen as she tried to push aside her worries.

 

            The next day, after she’d been through the stack of paperwork on her desk, had her coffee and a project meeting that ran on far too long, Kara found an excuse to slip into the Time Room. Clocks filled the room, of varying sizes and designs, a relentless ticking filling the space, almost maddening , with a towering crystal bell jar monopolising the far end of the room. There were only three other Unspeakables in the room at the time, looking bewildered by her presence, but she had the clearance for it so they just nodded politely before returning to their quiet bickering over a piece of paper one of them held.

 

            There was a door leading off the cavernous chamber, and Kara made a bee-line for it, moving through the narrow path between desks crammed inside the cluttered room. Bypassing a few of the other offices branching off, Kara pushed open the door to the Hall of Prophecy and stepped inside. The vaulted ceiling of the room soared high above her, identical to the other chambers in the Department of Mysteries, but this one was filled with nothing but towering shelves covered in small, dusty glass orbs, which glimmered in the blue light of the candle brackets on the walls. It was dark and cold, a few footsteps echoing in the distance, the soft whistle of another Unspeakable deeper in the rows of shelves, following up on a reference, and Kara slowly started to make her way up and down the rows, starting at Row 53 directly opposite the door. 

 

            It was agonisingly painstaking work, requiring the use of a ladder as she checked every single orb in the row by wand light, the brackets at the end of each row dimming the deeper in she went, making her feel rather alone. She missed lunch, deep in the stacks as she was careful to avoid touching any of the orbs, moving through the dusty room, hearing others come and go, until she finally reached Row 97. Moving her wand in closer, Kara peered at the label attached to it, taking in the initials in neat lettering. 

 

S.P.T to A.P.W.B.D 

Dark Lord 

and (?) Harry Potter

Chapter 46

            Adamantly sticking to her decision to keep her nose out of it, Kara went about life in much the same fashion as always, July bleeding into August, busy with work and tired from another full moon. She’d barely seen her sister at all, except on Sundays when Lena didn’t have work, her girlfriend inevitably dragging her to Cornwall for dinner, as few words exchanged between the sisters as possible. Kara was noticeably absent from drinks with her friends, choosing to go out with Lena and Sam, sometimes Andrea, other times Nia and Querl, who’d always felt more like her friends than Alex’s. It wasn’t ideal, but she was sulking and very open about it, much to the exasperation of everyone around the sisters.

 

            Kara had more important things to worry about anyway, another anniversary with Lena, seven years together, gone by quicker than she could’ve believed. That was longer than they’d been friends at Hogwarts, longer than the years they’d spent apart, so different to the shy teenagers and angsty young adults they’d been. And their lives, drastically different too. For the better. Those difficult years, burning through jobs and places to stay, seemed so far away to Kara now, in the distant past, exchanged for a comfortable life of stability with the woman she’d loved for more than half of her life. And for Lena too, a home remade into a place of love and safety, her dependable girlfriend, who was warm and gentle, who didn’t hurt her and didn’t raise her voice loud enough to make Lena flinch, who ran her hot baths and cooked them breakfast and dinner and liked to dance in the kitchen.

 

            It had all gone so well, even with a blood quill well-hidden somewhere in the house, unfound, unnecessary now, and a little box with a ring inside, just as well-hidden in a different spot, awaiting the right time. It was such a shame that a seemingly ordinary Thursday, on the last day of August, was the slow unravelling of their perfectly ordinary life.

 

            She’d been at work, discussing the latest theories with Snapper Carr, the Senior Unspeakable leading the Death Room research, when the fuss had started. Raised voices, angry and surprised, catching the attention of the remaining few Unspeakables fitting in some overtime. Cutting off mid-sentence, Kara had swapped a look with Snapper and set down her quill, climbing to her feet as the other two witches in the office made for the door as well. 

 

            Stepping out into the Entrance Chamber, she frowned at the sight of a familiar wizard. She wasn’t friends with him, hadn’t spoken to him in years, but she remembered Sturgis Podmore from the last time she’d been in the Order, and he was definitely not an Unspeakable. He was behaving strangely, his wand out as another Unspeakable tried to order him back through the open door, the chamber rotating at the intrusion. One of the witches ran back into the office and Kara stepped forward to help, hand in her pocket as she gripped her wand.

 

            “Sturgis,” she softly called out, “you’re not supposed to be in here, this is off limits.”

 

            He stared at her with a blank look on his face, stiffly walking further inside as the walls continued to spin. It was disorienting, making Kara feel nauseously dizzy, never experiencing it before as she’d only ever stepped inside with permission. The room stilled a moment later and his eyes glanced around at the identical doors, hesitating, uncertain as he licked his lips, blonde hair damp with sweat. It was silent for a moment and Kara watched as a memo drifted through the air and out of the door, and then he lurched towards a door, finding three wands pointed at him as Kara and two others fanned out before him.

 

            “Sturgis,” she tried again, her voice strained, “I need to ask you to leave, please.”

 

            Things unravelled quickly and she managed to fire off a spell first as he lunged forward, her non-verbal spell disarming him in a flash of red light, his wand clattering to the floor. It didn’t stop him though, something strange about his behaviour, something desperate , and Snapper managed to get his arms around Sturgis, pinning his arms and cursing him out as the wizard refused to give up.

 

            Within five minutes, a night guard was there, stunning the intruder as Sturgis Podmore went rigid and keeled over as Snapper let him go. Wincing, Kara stared at the prone body as the Department of Mysteries went quiet, everyone looking at the wizard. As the night guard started to cuff Podmore, calling for someone to alert the Auror’s Office to a break-in attempt, Kara slipped back through to her desk and hurriedly packed away her belongings into her briefcase, removing a letter in the process, and slipped on her robe before making a quick exit. She called the lift and had to stand aside as three Aurors rushed out, before riding it up to the Atrium.

 

            Pulling a rumpled letter out of her pocket, Kara peered down at the address as she hurried through the Ministry of Magic, the Atrium cavernous and virtually empty, everyone leaving for the day. Taking the telephone box up to street level, Kara ducked into a side alley and closed her eyes, envisioning the address, nothing else to go off of except that. She’d been to Islington before, the streets of tall townhouses crammed in together, and she pictured it in her mind before Apparating to her destination.

 

12 Grimmauld Place, Islington, London

 

            A quick stomach-lurching whirl later, she was standing on a street corner. The afternoon was wearing on, the sky blue overhead but the narrow road between houses cast in the shade, the townhouses too tall to let in the sunlight of late afternoon. Glancing up at the street sign, Kara set off down Grimmauld Place, glancing at the numbers on the front of houses as she kept an eye out for number 12, which seemed to spring out of nowhere as she stopped on the pavement, watching as the house elbowed the adjoining townhouses aside to make itself visible to her. 

 

            Lingering on the pavement a moment, Kara stared at the worn set of front steps leading up to the battered front door, chewing on her lip as she deliberated over following through with her visit. But she’d already Apparated there, and knew she wouldn’t turn back now, too curious, too filled with dread to let it rest. Looking up at the damp bricks of the building, a few grimy windows lit from within, she sighed and wearily trudged up to the silver serpent knocked on the front door. Lifting it, she banged it and heard the loud clanging of a bell, followed by the muffled sound of wailing take up behind the door.

 

            She wasn’t waiting long, just a minute or two, before the front door opened and she found herself staring at a familiar witch. “Imra. Hi.”

 

            “Oh. Kara. You’d better get inside.”

 

            Glancing down the street, Kara hesitated and then crossed the threshold. It soon became obvious that the source of the screaming was a portrait of a woman in a black cap stuck to the wall, one among many. Wary, Kara eased the door shut behind herself as Imra glanced back over her shoulder, waving a dismissive hand to the painting.

 

            “Just ignore her. She doesn’t bloody shut up.”

 

            An apprehensive look clouded Kara’s face as she stood in the dingy hallway. The air had a faintly sweet smell of decay to it, adding to the odour of dampness and dust, a distinctly derelict air about it as she took in the peeling wallpaper and cobwebs. The whole place was putrid, dirty walls, an appalling smell, the threadbare carpet on the floor and a thick layer of dust covering everything. Then there was the house itself, cracking, creaking and groaning as Kara warily followed after Imra, wan light illuminating the gloomy hallway from the old-fashioned gas lamps on the walls.

 

            “Whose house is this?”

 

            “Sirius Black’s,” Imra quietly replied. “He’s given it to the Order to use.”

 

            Brow furrowing, Kara tailed her past the closed doors and grand staircase to a set of stairs leading down to the basement. The stone walls were wet with seeping moisture as they started to descend, what Kara thought was black mould growing like veins across the damp stone, and she felt repulsed by the squalid home as she stumbled on a cracked step, coming to a stop as Imra opened the kitchen door and stepped inside. 

 

            The kitchen was just as gloomy as the hall above, a leak staining the stone wall from an apparent burst pipe, the cavernous room dingy as it was lit by nothing more than the large fireplace at the end of the room. It was crowded inside, pipe and cigarette smoke wreathing the air in a haze of colours, a long table spanning most of the space, with chairs crammed around it, only half of them occupied. Taking in the sight of filched newspapers, rolls of parchment, dirty tea cups, empty wine bottles and what looked to be a tin of biscuits and someone’s clean laundry, Kara found a dozen pairs of eyes on her. She tried to shut the door behind her but it was so swollen with damp that it sprang open again.

 

            “Here, you just-” Querl leapt up to help, slamming the door shut and then gallantly gesturing to his chair for Kara to take.

 

            Looking around as she sank onto the chair, Kara found herself staring at familiar faces. Some were friends she regularly saw, others were people she hadn’t seen in fourteen years, and a few new ones as well. The ones she knew were older now, so much time passed since the last time they’d found themselves cooped up in living rooms and kitchens, drinking too much as they tried to compensate for the fear of dying young, and Kara swallowed thickly.

 

            “Is Dumbledore here?” she asked, leaning in to whisper to Querl.

 

            “He stops by whenever he can. He’ll probably be here later on.”

 

            “Oh. I need to talk to him. Urgently . Is there-”

 

            “J’onn?” Querl called out to a man that Kara recognised as Alex’s boss. “Can we send word to Professor Dumbledore?”

 

            He nodded and climbed to his feet, excusing himself from the room, and Kara looked up in surprise as someone set a goblet of wine down in front of her. “Oh. Thank you, Molly,” she murmured, blinking in surprise at the red-haired woman at her side.

 

            Taking a sip, Kara drank a little more, hoping to squash the jitteriness filling her. Her sister was noticeably absent, most likely still at work, potentially even involved in the incident Kara was there to get the jump on. Draining half of her goblet, she shifted in her seat, a few separate conversations going on around her. Falling into conversation with Querl, Kara continued to drink her wine and had her goblet refilled again, someone passing around the tin of biscuits, one Ginger Newt and then another anxiously wolfed down as her stomach tied itself in knots.

 

            Nia showed up while she was there, dragging a chair over to join them, and others left, everyone looking harried and serious as they went about their business. Kara was tense the entire time, waiting for Dumbledore to show up, periodically glancing down at her watch. Lena would be getting home now, was probably wondering where she was, and Kara felt a stab of guilt. She hadn’t had time to go home and talk to Lena about what she should do with the information she had, she’d just gone straight to Grimmauld Place.

 

            Eventually, two cups of wine later, J’onn appeared at the door, beckoning to Kara as he quietly called out to her. Shoving back her chair, Kara followed him upstairs, back down the hallway and into a sitting room. The room was dimly lit, heavy curtains covering the windows, and it smelled of musty old books, the room cluttered with antiques in cabinets. Dumbledore was eyeing the wall, a tapestry of the Black family spread across it with a few faces burnt off, and Kara paused on the threshold, Professor McGonagall and Mad-Eye Moody inside the room as well. 

 

            “Miss Danvers,” Dumbledore kindly greeted her. “What a welcome surprise.”

 

            “Sir,” she nodded, easing the door shut, her eyes glancing to the others. “Professor McGonagall, hello.”

 

            “I’d invite you to sit, but the sofa seems to be infested with Doxies.”

 

            “Oh, that’s alright, sir, it won’t take very long.”

 

            There was a pause, all eyes on her, and she opened and closed her mouth, tugging nervously at the cuffs of her robe. Clearing her throat, she frowned slightly, head cocking to the side as she cast her eyes down to the ebony table set before a sagging sofa.

 

            “Um, that thing we discussed at our last meeting-”

 

            “Please, you may talk freely within this room.”

 

            “Oh, right, um, well, I found the prophecy in the Hall of Prophecy, so … you were correct that it would be there. It’s only- well, you said someone might come for it. I think that happened today, sir. It’s just- I remember last time … Sturgis Podmore was an Order member. I was working overtime tonight; he was just caught trying to break into the Department. He didn’t seem like himself. I just … thought you’d like to know.”

 

            Expression solemn, Dumbledore nodded, the others sharing glances. “Thank you, Kara. J’onn? I imagine he would have been arrested by your Department?”

 

            Nodding, J’onn’s mouth thinned. “I’ll be on my way now, Albus. See if I can get to the bottom of it.”

 

            Murmuring his goodbyes, he made straight for the door, letting himself out as Kara shuffled aside, and then shut it behind himself. Hovering a moment, Kara swallowed thickly and nodded.

 

            “Well, I should be off too, sir.”

 

            “A moment longer, if you please,” Dumbledore stopped her, a pensive look on his face as he studied the crown moulding. “You have the Order’s thanks for your tipoff; you would have our gratitude if you could continue to keep an eye on things. You might’ve guessed, but we have set up a guard ourselves; Sturgis Podmore was on duty tonight. I imagine this is just beginning to unfold, that this won’t be the only attempt.”

 

            Inhaling deeply, Kara winced slightly, “sir, I-”

 

            “I understand your reservations,” he cut her off. “I would not ask if it wasn’t of the utmost importance.”

 

            Wringing her hands, her briefcase held in a clammy grasp, Kara’s blue eyes were wide with apprehension. “What would you need me to keep an eye on?”

 

            “The Hall of Prophecy. Anyone attempting to access it-”

 

            “Sir, the Department of Mysteries is well-warded against intruders. It would be nigh on impossible for them to navigate their way through if they made it inside.”

 

            “I’m not concerned about intruders.”

 

            Blinking, her eyebrows rose a fraction. “Oh. You think they’ll get an Unspeakable to do it?”

 

            “Yes.”

 

            “Oh. Well, any Unspeakable would know they can’t remove a Prophecy.”

 

            “Yes, but I don’t believe Voldemort’s Death Eaters are aware of that fact. If you could just make note of anyone spending an inordinate amount of time there, behaving unusually , and feed that back to us, it would be very appreciated. You don’t have to engage or stop them. I won’t ask any more of you than watching.”

 

            “So … spying?” Kara surmised, a wry smile curling the corners of her mouth.

 

            Deliberating, Dumbledore returned her smile, his blue eyes bright with amusement. “Not in such a fashion, but if you would like to describe it as such.”

 

            “Mm. Well … you know my stance on the matter, sir. I was just coming to pass on what I saw, so …”

 

            Nodding, he grimaced slightly. “In that case, thank you, Miss Danvers. We won’t keep you from your dinner.”

 

            Sensing his disappointment, dissatisfaction perhaps, she nodded, swallowing thickly again. Feeling her cheeks flush, she fiddled with the handle of her briefcase and ducked her head as she murmured her goodbyes. Opening the door, she stepped out into the hallway, aware of voices starting up behind her as she left, and heard a knock on the front door a moment later. Pausing in the hallway, Kara hesitated, looking around for assistance as Walburga Black’s portrait started screaming and ranting again, and watched as Nia jogged up the staircase, rolling her eyes at the portrait as she flicked her wand at a moth-eaten curtain to cover it.

 

            Jerking open the front door, she stepped back to let the new arrivals in, and Kara moved towards her to wait her turn and slip out into the dusk. A witch around Nia’s age, evidently a Metamorphmagus if her pink hair was anything to go by, came inside first, bumping into an umbrella stand made from a troll’s foot. Pulling up short, Kara blinked at the sight of Kelly stepping over the threshold after the pink-haired witch, and Alex after her, the chatter of others drifting in from outside as the hallway became congested.

 

            A sullen look stole across Kara’s face as she pressed herself against the hallway wall, watching as James stepped inside, and then Lucy after him, avoiding her sister’s bewildered gaze as her cheeks flushed. The new arrivals filed through to the basement stairs, taking their noise with them, and the warm breeze of northern London swept in through the open front door as Nia waited patiently. Ducking her head, Kara wove past Kelly and was tugged to a stop as Alex grabbed her arm. Jerking herself out of her grasp, Kara stepped outside before her sister could speak, hurriedly descending the front steps and walking away. 

 

            Moving past a puddle of light from a lamppost, she sought out a shadowy patch in the street and Disapparated, going home. Tense and irate, she let herself into the ivy-covered cottage, eager to see her girlfriend, in need of some reassurance that all was well. Just stepping into their home loosened the knot in her chest and Kara sighed heavily as she shut the front door behind herself.

 

            “Is that you, darling?” Lena’s voice drifted from the open door leading down to the basement.

 

            “Yeah,” Kara wearily called back, curls coming loose from her bun, shoulders sloping as she loosened the tie around her neck.

 

            Kicking off her shoes, dropping her briefcase to the floor, she walked through to the basement door, her heavy tread on the creaking steps announcing her approach. Lena was seated at a high wooden stool before a cauldron, working by candlelight and the flickering flame beneath the cauldron, a serious look on her face as she measured out powdered moonstone on a set of scales. She glanced up as Kara appeared, relief in the lines of her face but confusion in her eyes.

 

            Crossing over to her, untucking the rumpled shirt beneath her knitted vest, Kara smiled tiredly, leaning down slightly to kiss her. “Hello.”

 

            “Mm, wine?” Lena mumbled, drawing back. “I didn’t know you were going for drinks after work; I would’ve met you there. I got off hours ago.”

 

            Smoothing down her errant curls, Kara grimaced. “I wasn’t at drinks, I- there was an incident at the Department of Mysteries. I thought Dumbledore should know about it.”

 

            “Oh.”

 

            Running a hand over her face, nudging her glasses up, leaving fingerprints on the lenses, Kara squeezed her eyes shut and then sighed. “Last time I spoke to him, he was concerned about someone breaking in to steal something for You Know Who. Someone tried it tonight.”

 

            “I thought- you said that we weren’t getting involved.”

 

            “I’m not, I just went to speak to him. To let him know. That’s all.”

 

            Apprehensive, Lena’s mouth thinned at the corners and she put the lid back on the container of powdered moonstone. Silent for a moment, she pressed her lips together, head bowed, and then cleared her throat.

 

            “That’s all?”

 

            “Yes. He asked me to keep an eye on some things as well-”

 

            “I hope you told him no,” Lena tersely interrupted.

 

            Blinking in surprise, Kara’s eyebrows rose before her face furrowed. “I- of course I did.”

 

            Nodding as some of the tension bled out of her, Lena’s eyes shuttered and she let out a soft sigh. Confused and a little indignant, Kara folded her arms over her chest, the basement slightly humid as the cauldron simmered away, a slight tension in the air.

 

            “Why did you say it like that?”

 

            “It’s just- you’re awfully involved for someone who was adamant about not meeting with him in the first place.”

 

            “You told me to meet with him!” Kara softly exclaimed.

 

            “Yes, to tell him no. And now you’re … what, spying for him? I hardly think it’s fair for you to make me sit by while you do what you like.”

 

            Scoffing, Kara scowled. “I’m not spying. I was just … passing on some information.”

 

            She winced as Lena gave her a pointed look. “I- but that’s different.”

 

            “How is it different?”

 

            “Well, I- it was about you. We aren’t staying out of it for my sake , so I thought it didn’t bother you if I helped.”

 

            “Of course it bothers me!”

 

            “Why didn’t you say so, then?”

 

            Lena spread her hands helplessly, pink-cheeked with annoyance. “I didn’t think I had to when you were so opposed to the idea of joining the Order again.”

 

            “I’m opposed to you getting dragged back into it, getting mixed up with bad people, being made to do things that will drag you straight back into hurting yourself again when it gets too much.”

 

            Angry now, green eyes bright with it, Lena let out a scathing sound as she raked her hair back, face hard as she turned away, placing the powdered moonstone back on the well-stocked shelf of potion supplies. “It’s been years since I did that - in any capacity. Quite frankly, it’s insulting you think I’d fall straight back into it at the first sign of difficulty.”

 

            Turning again, there was a wounded look to Lena’s gaze, vulnerable as she smiled bitterly. Shock flashed across Kara’s face as if she’d been slapped and she hurriedly closed the distance between them, sheepish and pleading as she reached to cup her girlfriend’s face in her warm hands.

 

            “No, no, that’s not what I was saying, I just- I wouldn’t want you to be in a position where you might-”

 

            “I’m not in that position. I’m so far from it; who do I even have to spy on? My mom?” Lena snorted. “She’s not even a Death Eater. I wouldn’t be useful there even if she was because we can’t fucking stand each other.”

 

            “It’s still dangerous. ”

 

            “Which is why I don’t want you involved!”

 

            “I’m not!” Kara protested, growing frustrated. Her blue eyes were full of it but her touch was gentle as she smoothed a thumb over Lena’s cheeks, frowning but scared. “But it’s not about me , anyway. I just want to keep you safe, how is that so difficult to understand?”

 

            Mouth tightening at the corners, Lena jerked her face out of Kara’s hands. “Don’t patronise me.”

 

            “I’m not,” Kara said with weariness this time, her expression aching as she reached out to snag Lena’s shirt. “I mean it. I’m not involved, I’m staying out of it for you .”

 

            “I don’t want you to do it for me. You should keep yourself safe too,” Lena softly snapped.

 

            “I’m not in any danger. I promise. He asked me to spy and I told him no. We’re in this together, okay? Or, we’re not in it together; I won’t go behind your back or lie to you.”

 

            “Yes, but you can’t impulsively act and then come home and tell me about it after the fact and consider that you being honest.”

 

            “I know that,” Kara muttered, trying to swallow her indignation. “But this wasn’t me acting impulsively. I was just … a witness. I didn’t know it was going to happen, it wasn’t anything Dumbledore asked me to do for the Order, I didn’t even really engage, I was just there. All I did was tell him it had happened; guaranteed it’ll be in the papers tomorrow anyway.”

 

            Sighing, Lena grimaced and reached up to fix Kara’s curly fringe, her gaze softening. “Okay, well, next time, just let them find out through the papers.”

 

            “Okay,” Kara murmured, a small smile at the corners of her mouth.

 

            Shoulders slumping, relieved, Lena gave her a tender look, faint circles beneath her eyes, and leaned in to kiss her. Kara wrapped her arms around her, holding her tightly as she kissed her back, her hands sliding down the back of Lena’s shirt, pressing her close.

 

            “And stay away from that man,” Lena mumbled against her lips in a warning.

Chapter 47

            September flew by, days blurring together, the warmth of summer finally dimming as autumn was ushered in, cooler days followed by colder nights. Kara hadn’t changed her mind about aiding the Order but she kept her eyes peeled at work, putting in a request to join the project of a Senior Unspeakable, Bode, in the Time Room. It gave her more access to the Hall of Prophecy, which led on from the Time Room, and she spent her days in the room filled with all manner of clocks, studying Time-Turners and theory, offering to assist the new batch of Junior Unspeakables in dusting the seemingly endless rows of glass orbs in the Hall of Prophecy. It gave her the opportunity to keep a close eye on things, even if she wasn’t getting involved.

 

            Nothing happened, weeks passing by in its monotonous routine. Crossing paths with her girlfriend for breakfast or dinner, depending on which shift Lena was working and whether she was on-call, meeting friends at various pubs and cafes for drinks or coffee, shopping in Diagon Alley, visiting her mother on Sundays, conversation with her sister still somewhat stunted as she refused to even tell Alex what she’d been doing at Grimmauld Place. 

 

            Her thirty-third birthday came around quickly, a quiet affair by her own design, her friends and family filling the kitchen and living room. It was a Friday, half of them still dressed from the work day, talking about mutual colleagues and trips they were planning on taking, what they were doing for Christmas, nursing wine or beer as the cool day slipped towards night. 

 

            A little tired, although the full moon had come and gone at the start of the month and was weeks away from the next, Kara was too quiet, too introspective for the house full of people. Some of them had been drifting inside and out through the back door, alternating between picking at the food laid out and smoking beneath a cloudy sky in the garden, so it was easy for Kara to steal a few minutes to herself, slipping out when a few others came back in.

 

            She’d been hoping for a breath of fresh air, the house quite warm, and she felt tense and troubled as she paced slowly, shoulders slumped. The trees rustled and a few sparrows flitted through the branches, the neatly tended garden still flourishing, despite the cooling weather, and Kara kicked off her shoes, stripping off her socks too as she felt a little claustrophobic, unable to arrange her thoughts as she raked a hand through her hair and then tried to flatten her fringe into something neater.

 

            The back door opened, the sound of voices swelling momentarily, and she turned around, her peace disturbed. The sight of her sister made her pause, taking in the uncertain expression on Alex’s face as she patted down the pocket of her corduroy pants, pulling out a slim cigarette case and lighting one. The few metres between them seemed thick with tension, and Kara folded her arms over her chest as she paced back towards the house, while Alex slowly rolled up the sleeves of her flannel shirt, taking a drag of her cigarette and then scuffing her shoe over the trimmed grass.

 

            Considering heading back inside, still annoyed with her sister, hurt, Kara hesitated. Instead, she stopped and turned, leaning against the side of the cottage and looking out at the quaint garden. Neither of them spoke for a moment, only the sound of the evening to fill the silence, and it wasn’t until she finished her first cigarette that Alex crossed over to her, taking up position at her side. They’d spoken of course, but not like they were sisters - or perhaps exactly like that, disgruntled and sniping at each other, but love beneath it all - and it felt suddenly awkward as the two of them stood alone in the garden.

 

            “So … how’re things?”

 

            Shrugging indifferently, Kara chewed on her bottom lip. “Fine.”

 

            “Good, good. Full moon was okay?”

 

            “Yeah.” After a moment, Kara tried to swallow her indignation, clearing her throat. “Things are going well with the Order?”

 

            “Mhm. Or, well, Dumbledore seems to know what’s going on, so …”

 

            “Right. Good.”

 

            Drawing in a deep breath, Alex opened her mouth to speak and Kara quickly interrupted, going tense as she intercepted the believed attack. “Don’t-”

 

            “I’m not,” Alex cut her off. “I was going to say that I don’t want this to come between us, alright? I hate not talking to you, and yeah, it was my fault, I know that, but I just- it’s not for me to offer up your life to risk, so … you’ve made your decision and I’ve made mine. I just want my sister back.”

 

            Eyelids sliding shut, Kara tipped her head back against the stone, her lips curving with a faint smile as she whispered, “okay.”

 

            “Sorry for being a cow about it all,” Alex sheepishly apologised, lighting a cigarette as she narrowed her eyes at the garden, the encroaching dusk blurring the treeline. “I didn’t mean anything I said, I was just … confused.”

 

            “Yeah,” Kara heavily sighed, rubbing her brow. “It’s all confusing.”

 

            There was a beat of silence, Alex shifting her weight, blowing smoke from the corner of her mouth, out of her sister’s face. “What’s going on?”

 

            “Mm?”

 

            “I don’t know, you just- you were adamant you weren’t going to help, then you were talking to Dumbledore at Grimmauld Place, and then nothing. I’m still confused.”

 

            “I don’t expect you to understand,” Kara murmured, arms wrapped around herself with a serious look on her face. “I just- I want to keep her safe. That’s all there is to it. Um … it just- it wouldn’t be possible for me to do that if I was involved. ”

 

            “Right.”

 

            “I’m not a coward,” Kara curtly continued a moment later, getting defensive as she expected another jibe.

 

            Sighing, Alex pulled her cigarette from her mouth and reached for her sister, pulling her into a brief, rough hug, her regret palpable. “I know you’re not. I’m just an idiot.”

 

            Kara laughed, feeling some of the tension that had plagued her dissipate. Although it had taken them years to get on, now it never felt right when they were arguing, when they didn’t agree on something. She loved her sister; it was just tricky because she loved Lena too. Both of them in different ways, for different reasons, but Kara knew she’d put Lena’s well-being over Alex’s opinion of her any day, no matter how much she loved her hotheaded sister. 

 

            “Thanks for coming,” Kara murmured, standing shoulder-to-shoulder with Alex, leaning against the cool stone of the cottage, tipping her head to the side to rest it on her shoulder for a second. “I wasn’t sure if you would.”

 

            “Of course I would.”

 

            “I just- the last couple of months … everything’s felt so- so shit. I’ve missed you.”

 

            “I’ve missed you too.”

 

            They lapsed into silence again and a few minutes later Lena stepped outside, levitating a few drinks with her, smiling softly as she spotted them leaning against the exterior of the cottage. Levitating bottles of beer to the sisters, she clutched her own glass of elderflower wine and Alex stubbed out her cigarette on the stone, kissing her sister’s cheek before slipping back inside.

 

            “You alright?” Lena asked as she took Alex’s spot, kissing Kara’s cheek as well.

            

            “Mhm.”

 

            Staring at her for a moment, Lena took a sip of wine and looked down, letting out a laugh. “What happened to your shoes?”

 

            Looking down at her bare feet, poking out from beneath the hem of her baggy pants, Kara softly laughed. “They were impeding my ability to think.”

 

            “What were you thinking so hard about on your birthday?”

 

            “Oh, you know, just everything.”

 

            “Well, it’s just about time for cake, if you were ready to come back inside.”

 

            “In a minute,” Kara murmured, her fingers brushing Lena’s arm.

 

            Nodding, Lena stood at her side, both of them enjoying the evening. The air had a chill to it, the smell of damp grass and their flourishing garden perfuming it, and Lena glanced at Kara and then kissed her shoulder.

 

            “You look beautiful tonight.”

 

            “You always say that.”

 

            “You always do,” Lena insisted, planting delicate kisses over the shoulder of Kara’s shirt, moving towards her neck, her breath ticklish as she kissed a path up to the base of her jaw. “And now I really wish everyone else had gone home already.”

 

            Laughing, her hand smoothing down the length of Lena’s spine, Kara hummed low in her throat. “Well, I’d better cut that cake then.”

 

            Raising her head, lips quirking into a smile, her red lipstick faded over the course of the night, Lena’s green eyes sparkled as they creased at the corners. Taking Kara’s hand, she tugged gently and led her towards the back door. The sound of music, conversation and laughter washed over them and Kara took a sip of her beer as she stepped over the threshold, the house warm and cast in a cheery glow from the lit candles scattered around.

 

            Lena fetched the birthday cake from the fridge, a triple layer of chocolate and ganache baked by Eliza, thirty-three candles lit on top as it was levitated to the table, where Kara was pushed down onto a chair, pink-cheeked as everyone sang happy birthday to her. Kelly had Kara’s old camera, the blinding flash filling the kitchen as she took photos, everyone a little tipsy, despite the relatively quiet dinner party.

 

            Blowing out the candles, her face bathed golden, eyes bright and deep dimples in her cheeks as she laughed, Kara’s eyelashes fluttered as she closed her eyes, making a wish. In the kitchen, surrounded by all of her family, all of her friends, and a few others besides, she was surrounded by more people than she’d ever thought she would have in her life twenty years ago and freshly bitten.
