In just a couple of years, some of them would be dead.

 

            Cutting the cake as her friends cheered, Kara let her mother take over for her, portioning out slices for them all, and let Lena wrap her arms around her waist. Leaning into her, pleasantly drunk, very grateful but with a weight on her shoulders that she couldn’t shake. She knew it was a feeling shared by all of her friends who were part of the Order, perhaps even some of them who weren’t, trying to feign ignorance so they could linger in the peace of society for a little while longer. Just how much longer remained to be seen, Kara knowing that sooner, rather than later, Lord Voldemort would tire of the shadows.

 

            It was something she’d discussed with Lena before, about how long they could go about their lives as usual, how they’d know when it was too dangerous to continue going to work, if the cottage was warded enough, if a Secret Keeper was enough. Even now, with the Order guarding the door to the Department of Mysteries every night, unbeknownst to all Unspeakables within, save one, Kara wondered how long things would remain peaceful. There hadn’t been any other break-in attempts over the last three weeks, but that didn’t mean the risk had been mitigated.

 

            Eating chocolate cake, standing in the kitchen, the soles of her bare feet dirty from the garden, her scarred forearms tanned from that unseasonably hot summer, Kara tried to push her troubled thoughts aside. They lingered though, unshakable even amidst so much easy laughter and chatter, and afterwards when they’d all gone home, and in the weeks after, her stomach knotted with unease, waiting for the other shoe to drop. That was how it felt to her, because as much as she had to blame Dumbledore for, even if it was on Lena’s behalf, she didn’t think he was lying about this, and even as the weeks went by with not much in the way of drama or excitement after the debacle with Podmore, she still knew that he was right.

 

            It irked her more than she cared to admit that he was right, after all he’d done, that even though she had little cause to trust him, others didn’t. There was so much vitriol being published in The Daily Prophet that she knew caused some tension between Lena and Andrea, who argued that she had little say in the matter. Kara supposed that was true, and she wasn’t that fond of Fudge either, but she couldn’t believe he was choosing to bury his head in the sand, ultimately digging himself a deep hole. It almost made her want to reconsider her stance on helping the Order, rejoining to help in ways the Ministry wouldn’t. But there wasn’t any fighting yet, not like there had been the last time she’d joined, only old enough towards the end of the war. 

 

            She thought it must have been the same in those early days of the first war, sitting around, drinking and plotting, scouring the news, trying to ferret out information. A lot of spying, she assumed, to a less dangerous extent than what Lena had been convinced to do for the Order, and it was reassuring to know she wasn’t missing out on much, that she’d given all the useful information she had access to anyway. Kara wished it would stay that way, that it would all be nipped in the bud before things got worse again. But she’d seen how bad it had gotten last time, at the end, seen the list of names in The Daily Prophet for those killed, had seen her fellow students pulled out of class or received a letter via owl with bad news, had seen the sombre expressions on faces at Order meetings, their numbers dwindling as they were picked off. She didn’t want to go through that again. If it meant Lena was going to be in harm’s way, she couldn’t go through it again.

 

            The last week of September passed by quickly and October was wet and miserable, nothing out of the ordinary, nothing that wasn’t expected. Sunday dinner at Eliza’s was back to its usual ease, the sisters back on good terms, Lena apologetically absent as she was scheduled for a night shift. Drinks with their friends drew the usual crowd, breakfast in Diagon Alley on the weekend, a day spent weeding the garden and prepping for the winter weather, the trees changing colours and sweaters layered over shirts. The cottage grew chilly, a fire lit every night, Kara’s old cat curling up before the heat, and their mess made the place feel homely, Kara leaving books scattered about, Lena kicking off her shoes and leaving empty coffee cups strewn throughout the house, wherever she left them as she swept into the fireplace to Floo to the lobby of St. Mungo’s. She still came home with nothing of concern beyond the usual scope of magical mishaps and injuries, Kara anxiously awaiting her arrival each time they were home together, wondering if that would be the day someone had been attacked.

 

            As it happened, Kara was privy to the first attack since the Quidditch World Cup, or rather, Cedric Diggory’s death, but that was still widely disputed by most of the Wizarding World. After the full moon on the 9th October, missing a day of work for it, she decided to fit in some overtime once she was back in the office, staying behind late, knowing Lena was working that night and wouldn’t be waiting for her at home anyway. The other workers had slowly drifted off once five o’clock hit, a few Unspeakables lingering for thirty, forty minutes before they clocked off too, leaving Kara seemingly alone.

 

            At least, she’d thought she was alone, Professor Croaker doing the rounds just after six, mumbling goodnight to her and asking her to make sure she extinguished the candles before leaving. It was still inside the Department of Mysteries, no sound save for the turning of the pages as Kara thumbed through a thick tome, the ceaseless ticking of the hundreds of clocks filling the Time Room, the scratching of her quill and the scrape of her coffee mug lifted and set back down. Ink stained her fingertips and little wisps of curls had freed themselves from her ponytail over the course of the day as she’d pored over her research.

 

            Her watch silently ticked on her wrist as six dragged towards seven, and Kara took a break, stretching her back as she leaned back on her chair, flexing aching fingers and considering dinner. Eyes dry from concentrating, stomach rumbling, Kara decided to call it a night. Packing up her desk, cleaning off the quill nib with a cloth, screwing the lid back on the ink pot, she closed the thick tome and packed away her papers, fetching her briefcase. Leaving her packed bag on the desk, Kara carried the heavy book through to the stacked shelves in the adjoining hall, her footsteps echoing as she passed the end of the rows, turning right and stopping at the correct section on the shelf. Double-checking the interior of the book, Kara wedged it in between a copy of The Predictions of Tycho Dodonus and Xylomancy by Selina Sapworthy. 

 

            Pausing at the door, Kara extinguished the lights in the room and then pushed the door open, stepping back out into the Time Room and pulling up short at the sound of another door shutting. Wariness stole over Kara as her brow faintly furrowed, and she felt her body tense as she listened. The sound of so many ticking clocks eclipsed any other movements and she cautiously reached for her wand, slipping it out of her back pocket and gripping it firmly as she swallowed thickly. Nothing looked out of place, and she considered chalking it up to exhaustion, perhaps not quite fully recovered from the full moon the day before, but Kara couldn’t shake the feeling that someone else was there. Especially considering she was in the very room that led through to the Hall of Prophecy, the exact room that Dumbledore had asked her to keep an eye on. Not that Kara had been, not in any real capacity, but she was inside that room for at least eight hours a day, five days a week, so she’d obviously been aware of people's comings and goings. 

 

            Still, she drifted towards the closed door to the Hall of Prophecy, licking her lips as she eased it open, hoping for the dimly lit room with the blue tint of the lit sconces. Instead, there was a brightness to the room, as if someone was inside, wandering the dark rows of shelves with a lit wand to guide the way. Making a spur-of-the-moment decision, Kara slipped inside the room and silently lit her own wand, casting a small circle of light around her.

 

            Her footsteps were quiet as she padded along, making straight for the row with the prophecy, knowing that if someone was breaking in, that’s where they’d be going. She’d been in the Hall of Prophecy to walk past it more times than she’d care to admit, especially for someone staying out of it all, so she knew exactly where it was, easily navigating through the cavernous hall with the lit sconces illuminating the way. 

 

            Reaching the end of the row, a halo of light obscuring the person walking down the aisle, Kara swallowed thickly, holding her wand up. “Who’s there?”

 

            She watched as the halo of light turned, making her narrow her eyes as it was trained on her, and Kara held a hand up to shield her eyes slightly as she crept down the aisle. “Lower your wand,” she said with some annoyance. “It’s after hours and this place is off-limits. I’m not sure how- ”

 

            Only a dozen feet separated them now and Kara cut off, relief sweeping through her as she lowered her wand slightly, the tension immediately bleeding out of her. “Oh. Bode. It’s you. Sorry, I thought you were-”

 

            The Senior Unspeakable, technically Kara’s direct supervisor in the Time Room, didn’t lower his wand as she babbled about how she thought it had been an intruder, that she’d thought everyone else had left for the day. Kara was still finishing her sheepish explanation as he stared vacantly at her, before a spell was suddenly blasting her backwards. It knocked the wind out of her as she went flying ten feet back, wand slipping from her clammy grasp, the tip of it going dark as the spell guttered, and she landed in a crumpled heap, head smacking against the dark tiled floor, the frame of her glasses bending, biting into the socket as she blinked back black spots, wheezing as her mouth filled with the taste of blood.

 

            Pushing herself up, dizziness making her stagger off-balance, Kara tried to spot her wand in the dark, her glasses sitting crookedly on her face, her left eye smarting. Fingers scrabbling over tiles, her heart pounded in her chest and she hit the floor hard as another curse flew overhead. Dull pain flared in her knees and Kara fumbled around for a few minutes until she found her wand, a spell already on her lips as she raised it.

 

            “Expelliarmus!” 

 

            Bode’s wand went flying out of his hand, clattering somewhere in the dark, and Kara felt some of her panic abate as she staggered back to her feet. Her hand trembled slightly as she kept her wand trained on him, advancing slowly as she drew in ragged breaths.

 

            “Leave it alone, Broderick,” she warned the man as he stood in front of the prophecy, ghostly blue light cast over his strained face. 

 

            She watched as he seemed to struggle with himself for a moment, confused as she licked her lips, trying not to frighten him. It was evident he wasn’t himself, fighting off the enchantment as his hand jerked up and down, as if torn between reaching for the orb and leaving it be. Kara knew what would happen if she touched one of them, and knew that Bode definitely knew, so she wasn’t surprised that he was fighting against it so hard, but it was futile. As another warning fell from her lips, she watched as the man’s fingers grazed the orb, his whole body going rigid as his eyes went wide, mouth open in agony.

 

            Swearing, Kara couldn’t think of anything to do except throw Bode’s own charm back at him to try and get him away from the prophecy. “Everte Statum!”

 

            He was blasted several feet away, landing hard on his back, head bouncing off the tiles. Cringing, Kara hurried over to him, wand still pointed at him as a precaution, and cast a circle of light over his limp body, his eyes wide and vacant as his lips moved soundlessly. Unsure what to do next, Kara deliberated for a moment, letting out a small huff of frustration before she cast a full body-bind curse on him to keep him temporarily paralysed.

 

            Shoes squeaking on the tiles, she ran back through the Hall of Prophecy, skin prickling with unease, dread filling her as her face ached and her shirt clung to her damp back. Her breaths were coming quickly now, the fear of someone else showing up, of being caught in the middle of this heist gone wrong, making her frantic as she burst through the door and found herself back in the still confines of the Time Room and its incessant ticking. Lurching towards the nearest desk, Kara fumbled for a stack of internal memo pages, finding a quill and some ink as she scribbled out a barely legible message and folded the paper into a little plane, tossing it into the air.

 

            With that done, she ran back into the Hall of Prophecy and found Bode exactly where she’d left him. Unsure whether she should move him or leave that up to the Aurors once they’d secured the area, Kara deliberated and then cast another full body-bind curse to ensure that he’d be held in place until someone arrived. She stood over him for a few minutes, ears strained for anyone else trying to sneak in, but had to leave him there to make her way out to the Entrance Hall, anticipating the arrival of the Aurors. If they’d stepped inside, the room would’ve continued to spin until they were so thoroughly disoriented that they’d never be able to make it through to the Hall of Prophecy unaided.

 

            Opening the entrance to the Department of Mysteries, her wand held in a tight grasp, sweat beading her forehead, her left eye swelling and something wet on her face, Kara didn’t have to wait long until the lift descended, four Aurors visible through the grille. One of them was immediately identifiable, J’onn yanking back the grille and stepping out first, his maroon robe flaring behind him as he quickly approached, looking stern and alarmed.

 

            “What happened?”

 

            “It’s Bode,” Kara rasped. “He was- he was under the Imperius Curse, I’m sure of it, otherwise he’d never- he touched it! No Unspeakable would ever touch them if- if they were sane.”

 

            J’onn had placed a hand on Kara’s shoulder, steering her through the door to the Department of Mysteries, the walls staying put with Kara’s authorised presence, and she breathlessly babbled as her bruised knees felt weak with relief. Guiding him across the chamber, to the door to the Time Room, Kara slipped her wand into her back pocket, running a hand through her messy hair.

 

            “Is anyone else here?” J’onn asked. 

 

            “I don’t know, I thought- I thought I was alone. ”

 

            At a gesture to two of the Aurors, they went ahead with their wands drawn, and then J’onn gestured for Kara to go ahead of him and the other Auror. He stuck close behind her, his voice low and gentle, his wand in his hand. Kara felt a lump in her throat, her left eye smarting, barely able to see out of it now as it quickly swelled.

 

            “Did he take anything?” J’onn asked, and Kara knew what he was asking about in particular.

 

            “No,” she said, fighting down a hysterical laugh. “No, he couldn’t. That’s what he touched.”

 

            “What happened?”

 

            “They’re enchanted. I’m not- I’m not sure how to explain the specifics for the enchantment, but everyone just- well, if you touch it, you lose your marbles. He touched it. I tried to stop him, I did, but he knocked me on my arse. I thought he just- well, he’s my supervisor, so I didn’t think- but I’ve got him laid out. I didn’t want to move him just in case you needed to … I don’t know.”

 

            “Good. You did good, Danvers.”

 

            Nodding weakly, Kara directed them to the Hall of Prophecy as they passed through the cluttered Time Room, the noise of the clocks overwhelming as she wiped her palms on the thighs of her pants. Inside the Hall of Prophecy, she anxiously wrung her hands as she barely spoke above a whisper to direct them to Row 97, their wand light illuminating the way as the dim blue light of the sconces faded behind them. Their breaths seemed too loud in the confines of the aisle and Kara felt jumpy, as if expecting to be ambushed by someone lurking in the stacks.

 

            Instead, they found Broderick Bode exactly where she’d left him, still stretched out on his back, unable to move, his unblinking eyes staring up into darkness. The Aurors fanned out, one of them casting a spell to see if anyone else was there, another knelt by Bode’s side, murmuring Finite Incantatum to undo Kara’s curse, while J’onn and the other Auror kept their wands trained on him. He didn’t so much as blink though, remaining exactly where he was, and J’onn dispatched one of the Aurors to send for a Mediwizard.

 

            “I should- I should inform Professor Croaker,” Kara said in a daze, dragging her eyes away from Bode to blink up at J’onn.

 

            “Word has already been sent. You should sit. We’ll need to take your statement once this has been sorted; stay put for now.”

 

            Nodding, Kara sank to her haunches, running her hands through her hair. She should’ve been home, eating tea and curling up before the fire with Bastet, turning in for an early night without Lena in their bed, the right side cool as Kara stole one of her pillows to bury her face in the smell of her. Instead, her night wasn’t shaping up as she’d expected, and she felt oddly faint and a little hollow, done in from the full moon and a nasty bump to the head to top it all off. She wished Alex had been one of the Aurors.

 

            There was a flurry of activity then, Professor Croaker showing up in a tizzy, catching sight of Kara’s face and Bode’s prostrate figure and blusteringly demanding an answer. Kara gave a jumbled explanation and one of the Aurors scribbled down notes in a little book, repeating questions until she’d gone through it all at least six times over, while Mediwizards loaded Bode onto a stretcher and carried him off to St. Mungo’s.

 

            “Thank you, Miss Danvers,” J’onn quietly spoke as he crouched in front of Kara, an elbow on his knee and a sombre expression on his face.

 

            He brushed off his pants and climbed to his feet, extending a hand, which Kara slowly took, and pulled her upright. With a hand on her shoulder, he gave her a coaxing push towards a waiting Mediwizard. 

 

            “You should get that checked out as well.” 

 

            “Oh. Right. Yes,” she said, blue eyes wide as she tried to process it all. “Is there- should I … tell anyone about this?”

 

            J’onn smiled faintly, understanding her meaning. “I have your statement; I’ll pass it on. I’m sure they’ll be grateful for the detail, and your quick thinking.”

 

            Nodding, Kara tore her attention away from him at the polite voice of the Mediwizard waiting to escort her. She followed the man through to the Time Room, pausing to snag her briefcase and drag her cloak off the back of the chair, and then through to the Entrance Chamber and out into the hallway. They rode the lift up to the Atrium and Flooed to St. Mungo’s in the same fireplace, the man keeping a firm grip on her arm as he tossed a handful of Floo powder into the grate, as if he feared she might fall out at the wrong stop.

 

            In the busy reception of St. Mungo’s, Kara was made to take a seat in the waiting room, waiting for an Intern to come and check her vitals. It wasn’t bad, she knew that, knew that if Lena had been home she would’ve objected to the Mediwizard and let her girlfriend patch her up, but Lena was at work, somewhere else in the hospital, and Kara didn’t want to worry her, so she waited patiently. A nurse made the rounds with potions for pain management and Kara gratefully knocked back the mouthful offered to her, which dulled the ache in her head somewhat but didn’t fully banish it. 

 

            She was in the waiting room for two hours before Sam appeared, her eyes widening as her gaze passed over the occupants and caught sight of Kara. Hurrying over to her, she crouched in front of Kara, hazel eyes anxious as she observed the left side of Kara’s face. Kara wished there was a mirror handy so she could see the handiwork of Bode’s attack.

 

            “Does Lena know you’re here?” were the first words out of Sam’s mouth, before she scoffed and shook her head. “What am I saying? Of course she doesn’t know, or you wouldn’t be sitting here.”

 

            Kara let out a frayed laugh, wrinkling her nose, which made the pain flare up. “I didn’t want to worry her.”

 

            “Come on. Let me patch you up before she finds out. Blimey, she’ll have a fit if she sees you like this.”

 

            Wearily pushing herself to her feet, Kara sighed and attempted to roll her eyes, which was difficult when one of them was swollen shut. “She’s seen worse.”

 

            Clicking her tongue, Sam grabbed her arm and Kara barely had time to grab her things before she was staggering after the Healer. Shuffling past the occupied chairs of other patients, Kara followed Sam to the lift, the grille dragged back to admit them. Jabbing a thumb into the button for the fourth floor, Sam glanced at Kara with open concern.

 

            “What happened?”

 

            “Um … work stuff,” Kara evasively replied, giving her a weak smile.

 

            Looking mildly alarmed, Sam gave her a sceptical look. “Okay, well, whatever’s going on in the Department of Mysteries, they’re definitely not paying you enough to deal with it.”

 

            Kara let out a quiet chuckle, which quickly died in her throat as the lift dinged and they stopped at the fourth floor, finding herself locking eyes with her waiting girlfriend through the grille. Sheepishly wincing, she watched as a dozen emotions crossed Lena’s face, experiencing the whole range in a matter of seconds before the grille was roughly yanked across.

 

            “Oh, bollocks,” Sam softly sighed.

 

            “What- I- wha- you-” Lena stammered, inside the lift, as whatever purpose she’d been waiting for the lift for was forgotten, her hands already reaching for Kara’s face as her face paled.

 

            “I’m alright,” Kara quietly assured her.

 

            Lena made a small sound of objection at the back of her throat as her fingers gently touched Kara’s cheek, careful where she applied pressure. Trying not to wince, Kara gave her an uneven smile as the grille started to close, the lift summoned to another floor. Sam quickly stopped it and stepped out, holding the grille back.

 

            “Okay, out, out, let’s get you to a bed.”

 

            “That’s not necessary,” Kara tried to protest. “It’s a black eye; just put a salve on it and I’ll be fine.”

 

            “A black eye? Darling, your eye is swollen shut. And you have blood all over your face,” Lena fretted. “You could be concussed.”

 

            “I’m not concussed, I’m fine.”

 

            “Whether you’re fine or not, I still need to-”

 

            “You won’t be doing anything,” Sam interrupted, pulling Lena away from Kara and taking their arms as she started to tow them through the hallway. “You know the rules.”

 

            “I’m Head of Charms ; who’s going to stop me?”

 

            “Your mother?”

 

            Lena snorted, rolling her eyes, and Sam grimaced. “Fine, me. Now, you , sit here.”

 

            She directed the latter to Kara, through the doors of a ward and urging her towards an empty bed. Taking a seat on the hospital bed, Kara set her briefcase and cloak down beside herself and let out a weary sigh. Hovering nearby with a worried look on her face, Lena stared at her with wide eyes, chewing her lip as she stared at Kara’s face, biting back her questions as Sam pottered about.

 

            “Alright, sit tight, I’ll be back in two ticks.”

 

            As soon as she moved off, Lena stepped closer, running a hand over Kara’s hair, her face taut as a muscle twitched in her jaw, trying to keep her worry at bay but failing miserably at it. “What happened?”

 

            “Just a bit of an accident at work,” Kara murmured.

 

            “To do with that Unspeakable the Mediwizards brought in a few hours ago?”

 

            Hesitating, Kara’s mouth thinned as she nodded. “Yes, but he got the short end of the broomstick.”

 

            Giving her a searching look as she continued to stroke the right side of Kara’s face, Lena waited for Kara to continue, to explain what had happened. Instead, Kara swallowed thickly and gave her a pained smile. “Can we talk about it later?”

 

            Nodding, Lena clicked her tongue and ghosted her fingers over the bruised side of Kara’s face. Her face softened, so tender with concern that it made Kara want to cry. Looking down, she toyed with her fingers in her lap until Lena reached out to take her hand, and neither of them spoke for a moment, until Sam returned with an armful of supplies.

 

            Setting everything down on a tray, she sank onto a stool and boosted it higher, letting out a harried sigh as she worked on dragonhide gloves and started tearing open packages. “Alright, let’s see what we’ve got.”

 

            Lena perched on the bed, sitting right beside Kara as she continued to hold her hand, gripping it tightly, wincing when Kara winced as Sam removed her glasses. The left lens was cracked, the wire rims bent, the metal biting into Kara’s skin where she’d whacked her face against the tiled floor of the Hall of Prophecy. It was the main source of swelling of her eye as well, but nothing Sam couldn’t fix with a few drops of Essence of Dittany in the shallow cut, and more in the cut on the side of her forehead, where she’d been bleeding from. 

 

            It didn’t take long at all, a matter of minutes, and Lena insisted on wiping the blood away once Sam had finished. By the time she’d been cleaned up, there were two sealed cuts, soon to be scabbing over, and a bruised black eye and Lena had fixed Kara’s glasses for her, setting them back on her face and dispelling the hawkish look on her near-sighted girlfriend’s face. Giving her a crooked smile, her left eye still mostly swollen shut, Kara raised Lena’s hand to her lips and pressed a kiss to the back of it, saying nothing about the bruises she could feel on her knees as she insisted she was fine.

 

            “All better,” she murmured.

 

            “You’re staying here another hour at least.”

 

            “I’m fine, Lena. All I need is dinner and sleep. I’ll meet you at home after your shift-”

 

            “Not bloody likely,” Lena spluttered, indignant. “My shift’s over.”

 

            “You said you’re working tonight.”

 

            “Have you gone mad? You were injured at work and you think I’ll be working the rest of the night, while you sit at home by yourself, possibly concussed-”

 

            “I’m not concussed!”

 

            “That you know of.”

 

            Sam chuckled, trying to hide a smile as she filled out Kara’s chart. “She’s a pain in the arse, but there’s no use fighting her, Kara. Rest for an hour, just so I can rule out any immediate risks, and then I’ll discharge you and Lena can take you home. In the meantime, she can buy you an atrocious dinner from the tearoom.”

 

            Mouth thinning, Kara relented and Lena gave her a stern warning to stay put, vanishing through the doors to the ward as Sam grinned, cleaning up the mess of opened packaging and bloody gauze. She measured out another dose of a pain relief potion, which Kara knocked back, and waited at her bedside, making quiet conversation with her about work, about Ruby and if Sam could make it to Lena’s birthday drinks in a couple of weeks. Returning ten minutes later, looking peeved and impatient, Lena set everything down on the tray at the bedside and wheeled it closer.

 

            “Sorry, it’s slim pickings after lunchtime.”

 

            Still, it seemed like Lena had bought everything available, three cups of tea in a tray and an assortment of greasy paper bags holding pasties, sausage rolls and cakes. She’d also bought Kara a Chocolate Frog, of course, and perched on the foot of the bed with a brooding look on her face as she nursed her tea. Sam took the tea offered to her and then left them to it, called off for a consultation with another patient with the promise to be back in an hour.

 

            Sipping her tea, Lena was silent for a minute before she gestured to the curtain, which neatly drew itself around the bay, and gave her girlfriend an aching look as her shoulders slumped. “Are you okay?”

 

            Giving her a small smile, Kara reached for Lena, holding out a hand as she waited for Lena to set her tea down and shuffle closer on the hospital bed, taking it. Raising her hand to her lips, Kara kissed the back of it again and then pressed Lena’s palm against the uninjured side of her face.

 

            “I’m fine. Better than I’ve felt all day, to be honest with you. It’s always better when I get to see you.”

 

            With a quiet scoff, Lena smiled grimly. “Well, don’t get it into your head that you have to injure yourself to spend time with me.”

 

            Laughing, Kara’s eyes creased at the corners, and she felt the stinging pain of her swollen eye from the act. She didn’t show it though, dropping Lena’s hand and pushing herself up into a more upright sitting position as she sighed and rubbed her hands together.

 

            “Right, what’s on the menu then?”

 

            Insisting that she’d already eaten, Lena tore open the paper bags to reveal two pumpkin pasties, a sausage roll and a jam doughnut, and two packets of crisps as well, taking one of the latter and leaving the rest for Kara to get through. They talked about their days, skirting around what had happened, although Lena questioned why she’d been at the office so late, gently chastising her for not going home to rest more after the effects of the full moon. 

 

            Kara had made it through most of the food, splitting one of the pasties with Lena and saving the Chocolate Frog for last, when Sam returned. The Healers babbled back and forth in medical terminology that went over Kara’s head before Sam smiled at her and said she’d get an intern to sort out the discharge paperwork. Within twenty minutes, they were out of there, almost midnight now, Kara’s eyes burning, her whole body slumped with exhaustion.

 

            Outside, her cloak wrapped around her shoulders, and Lena with a robe over her scrubs, they shivered from the chill and ducked around to the alley and Apparated home. Letting them inside, Lena ushered Kara in ahead of her and waved a hand to light the cottage, dumping her satchel and taking Kara’s briefcase from her hand. Moving towards her, Lena reached up to cup her face in her hands again.

 

            “Let me look at you,” she anxiously murmured, even though she’d been staring at her face for the last hour and a half.

 

            “My goodness, you fuss less on a full moon,” Kara murmured, a smile in her voice.

 

            Making a sound of annoyance, Lena carefully cradled Kara’s neck in her palms and pressed delicate kisses all over the left side of her face. The swelling had lessened over the last hour, her eye half-parted and the bruise already starting to fade, and Kara smiled crookedly as Lena’s lips brushed over her cheekbone, her temple, the corner of her eye.

 

            Wrapping her in a tight hug, Lena buried her face in her shoulder for a moment as she exhaled forcefully. Then she straightened and Kara kissed her, holding her close, trying to reassure her that she was okay. Really, she was just trying to minimise it all before she told Lena just how she’d gotten hurt, knowing that her girlfriend wouldn’t take it well.

 

            “How’s Bode?” Kara asked as she stroked Lena’s dark hair, tucking a lock behind her ear.

 

            “That remains to be seen,” Lena sighed, raking a hand through her hair and then over her face. “We’ve had to put him on the Janus Thickey ward for now; we’re not sure what the extent of the damage is.”

 

            “It’ll be quite extensive,” Kara hedged.

 

            Glancing at her, Lena’s brow furrowed slightly and she shed her robe, making for the stand near the door and hanging it up. She was quiet for a moment, and a sharp tapping caught her attention, eyes dragging to the window before she quickly crossed over to it. A little grey owl hopped closer, ruffling its feathers, and Lena removed the letter from its leg before carrying the bird inside and setting it on Morrigan’s empty perch to have a drink before it flew off.

 

            “It’s for you,” Lena said, extending the letter.

 

            Kara recognised the handwriting and felt a flicker of panic shoot through her as she tore it open. “It’s from Croaker.” Her eyes quickly ran over the words and she felt relief wash through her as she let out a hoarse laugh. “He’s apologised. Told me to take the rest of the week off.”

 

            “Too right he should apologise,” Lena quietly fumed, lifting the owl from the perch and carrying it back to the window, setting it loose before shutting the window. “Endangering his employees lives like that.”

 

            “Oh, well, he wasn’t- he wasn’t involved. Um … it wasn’t strictly work-related, it just- it happened at work.”

 

            Mouth opening and closing, Kara shed her cloak and kicked off her shoes before taking Lena’s arm and towing her over to the sofa. They sat side by side and Kara laid a hand on Lena’s knee as she pressed her lips in a flat line, trying to phrase it in a way that wouldn’t alarm Lena. But Lena was smart and Kara didn’t have to say anything for her to read into the silence.

 

            “What happened?”

 

            “Another break-in. Well, not technically; they used Bode to do it because he’s authorised to get inside. They must’ve thought everyone had gone for the day when they sent him in. Not that it made a difference - he couldn’t steal it for them anyway. I mean, you saw him. They’re protected by strong enchantments. Only the people the prophecies are about can remove them, and he- he would’ve known that. I could see him trying to fight it off.”

 

            Lena let out a weary sigh, dark circles beneath her eyes, her face pale and taut, stressed and confused as she rubbed her hands over her face. “You stopped him?”

 

            “Not as such. He touched the bloody thing so I blasted him away from it. Not before he knocked me on my arse though; I wasn’t expecting my supervisor to attack me. As soon as he touched the orb, he was gone, though, so I- well, I didn’t have to try very hard to contain him.”

 

            Letting out a quiet groan, Lena closed her eyes. “You shouldn’t have engaged with him.”

 

            “What was I supposed to do? Let him touch it without trying to stop him?”

 

            “I- well, he touched it anyway, so yeah, if that would’ve stopped you from getting hurt. You’re not supposed to be getting involved-”

 

            “It happened at work. ”

 

            “But why are you always there when things happen?” Lena exclaimed, the breath catching in her throat as she ran her hands through her hair, face agonised. “You could’ve been injured a lot worse - you could’ve died.”

 

            Quietly scoffing, Kara resisted the urge to roll her eyes. “It was never that serious.”

 

            “Death Eaters are trying to break into your place of work, are having employees attack each other, and it’s not that serious? It might not be to you, but it is that serious to me.”

 

            “Darling-”

 

            “No. Why am I the one who has to idly sit by and watch you put yourself in harm’s way, over and over again, and has to be okay with that? How would you feel, if it was reversed? I already know how you’d feel, that’s why I agreed to idly sit by. For your peace of mind.”

 

            Lips pressed into a flat line, Kara adjusted her glasses on her face, trying to stamp down her annoyance. “I don’t think you’re being fair.”

 

            “Fair?” Lena echoed, scoffing as she climbed to her feet, pacing away. 

 

            “I didn’t know it would happen. I was just working overtime, I was packing up to come home. If I hadn’t been there … I would’ve never known about it, but I can’t change the fact that I was. And I could’ve gone running straight to Dumbledore to fill him in on what happened, but I didn’t . I gave my statement and I went straight to St. Mungo’s because I knew that it would worry you if I didn’t get looked at. But now I don’t care about your peace of mind because I got caught in the middle and got a fucking black eye out of it?”

 

            “I never said you didn’t care-”

 

            “Then what are you implying? And how is any of this my fault?”

 

            “I never said it was your fault. I’m just- I’m worried. I’m allowed to worry about you. Especially when everything was normal when you left for work and then you showed up in the middle of my shift covered in blood.”

 

            Cupping her forehead, Lena shook her head and Kara let out a soft breath before pushing herself to her feet. Crossing over to Lena, she stopped her, mid-pacing, and wrapped her arms around her, lips brushing the side of her face before she rested her forehead against Lena’s temple.

 

            “Let’s not fight,” Kara murmured. 

 

            Letting out a forceful sigh, Lena returned the hug, both of them wrapped up in each other as the quiet cottage shifted around them, pipes groaning, the wind outside, rattling the windows and doors. After a moment, Lena audibly swallowed, turning her head, her nose brushing Kara’s.

 

            “I don’t want to row with you,” Lena agreed, “it just- it feels like … this is the beginning of something really ugly. I don’t want you to get caught in the crossfire. I couldn’t- I couldn’t bear that. Anything but that.”

 

            “It’s alright. No matter what happens, we’ll be okay, we’ll look after each other. As long as we have each other, we’ll get through whatever comes our way. I’m not planning on anything happening to take me away from you, so you don’t have to worry, okay? Now, let’s go to bed. It’s been a long day.”

 

            Lena hummed distractedly, feeling Kara’s kiss pressed to her head, but she didn’t push the topic any further, relenting as Kara pulled away, moving to check all of the doors were locked. They made their way upstairs, extinguished the lights and got changed for bed, their room chilly as they climbed beneath the thick quilt, Kara’s glasses on the nightstand beside her wand, laying on the right side so she didn’t agitate her bruises.

 

            Lying with her back to Kara’s stomach, Lena let out a tired sigh and Kara wrapped her arm around her waist, faintly feeling her heartbeat beneath the cotton of Lena’s shirt. Kissing her shoulder, Kara closed her eyes to the dark.

 

            “Goodnight. I love you.”

 

            “I love you too,” Lena whispered back.

 

            And while nothing was wrong , as per se, there was a heaviness in their chests as they struggled to fall asleep, both of them fretting over what could go wrong, what inevitably would go wrong.

Chapter 48

            December was ushered in with light snows and wet weather, the full moon coming and going, leaving Kara’s joints aching afterwards in the cold weather. The news in The Daily Prophet was unassuming, or spinning some story about Dumbledore or Harry Potter that painted them in less than favourable lights, but whispers still reached them, none of it boding well, and yet, they did nothing to help, Kara still finding it somewhat difficult and shameful to be around her sister, even though Alex didn’t speak of anything related to the Order. Still, Lena could see how it affected her girlfriend, head ducked down in her plate of shepherd’s pie at family dinners, the tips of her ears turning pink. But Kara didn’t ask to help - not once.

 

            Somehow, even though she was getting exactly what she’d wanted, it didn’t comfort Lena. Instead, each day she was plagued with an uncomfortable knotted feeling in her stomach, knowing that she was asking a lot of Kara, hating to see her so grimly resigned to making Lena happy that she was making herself miserable. And she wasn’t even sure if Kara noticed how unhappy she was about their circumstances, not even on either side of the full moon, silently brooding as her patience wore a little thin, and that just made Lena feel worse. It was gutting to know that their decision was making them both unhappy, that it was taking its toll on their relationship, after so many already difficult years they’d worked their way through. 

 

            The worst part was she was at work so often that it made it difficult for them to talk properly when they were home at the same time, and if she was home, there was a good chance she was knackered from a long shift. Being the Head of Charms afforded her more flexibility with her shifts, but there were times when she was at St. Mungo’s for days on end, and when she was home, she felt as if she was walking on eggshells, not wanting to ruin what time they were able to spend together. And most of their time together was with other people around, still meeting up with friends at The Leaky Cauldron or The Hopping Pot for drinks, or holed up in Alex and Kelly’s flat, or someone else’s, which made it nigh on impossible for Lena to make more than perfunctory check-ins on her girlfriend, who was always quick to give her a soft smile and assure her that everything was fine.  

 

            Lena wondered how long they could survive being just fine , but she couldn’t have guessed that December would be the turning point from which there was no coming back. The month was halfway over, Christmas only a week away, when she found herself wrapped up in Order business, against her best attempts. And it was by choice, which was the part that would bother her later on, and she often wondered in the weeks and months after that night if she might have made a different choice, knowing what would come from it.

 

            A hammering on the front door made them both jerk awake in bed in the early hours of the morning on the 18th of December, and Lena was immediately alert as she bolted upright, chest pounding, while Kara fumbled blindly for her wand on the nightstand, and then her glasses a moment later. It was chilly in the bedroom and she rolled out of bed, barefoot on the cold floorboards, holding a hand out to Lena to keep her at bay as she tried to climb out as well.

 

            “It’s alright, I’ll see who it is. You stay here.”

 

            Before Lena could respond, Kara was slipping out onto the landing, floorboards creaking under her feet as she padded towards the top of the staircase, feet thundering down them in her haste. She approached the front door with wariness though; not many people had been given a scrap of paper with their address on it, and as Secret Keeper, Kara felt the responsibility to open the door to whatever trouble was on the other side of it rested with her. Dread immediately pooled in her stomach as she opened the door to find Kelly bundled up in a robe and scarf against the frost, her sister-in-law restless and her wide dark eyes frantic.

 

            It was the middle of December, bitterly cold even though it hadn’t snowed that night, and Kelly’s quick breaths were visible in the air before her as she huddled on the doorstep, her shoulders seeming to slump slightly with relief at the sight of Kara. Fearing what might come out of her mouth, Kara moved back a step to let Kelly over the threshold of the front door.

 

            “I know you don’t want anything to do with this, but we need your help. Quickly.”

 

            “I- wha- is it Alex?”

 

            “No, no, it’s not her - she’s at work, or we would’ve gone to her first, or J’onn - but Arthur Weasley’s been attacked at the Department of Mysteries and … well, no one can get inside. No one else. ”

 

            “What, you- you want me to let you in? How do you even know this?”

 

            “I can’t tell you that, only … well, he has seven kids, Kara, and if our intel’s correct, he’s dying and no one can get to him.”

 

            Closing her eyes, thumb and forefinger digging into her eyelids as she pinched the bridge of her nose, Kara swallowed thickly, her voice still hoarse with sleep. “Stay here.”

 

            Turning away, she hurried to the stairs, long legs taking them two at a time, and almost ran into Lena hiding in the shadows at the top of the stairs. In stride, Kara grabbed her arm and towed her back into the bedroom, Bastet’s eyes glowing in the dark from where the cat lay curled up on top of the blankets. Easing the door most of the way shut, Kara’s breaths were quick in the silence.

 

            “How much did you hear?”

 

            “Enough.”

 

            “I promised I’d talk to you first but this is- this is an emergency, so I need you to tell me now what you want me to do.”

 

            In the dim light of the lamp, Kara could see the way Lena anxiously bit her lip, deliberating as she tried to stifle her unease, the stab of resentment - not at Kara, who was only asking, just like Lena had wanted her to - but at Dumbledore for putting them in this position again. But this time a person’s life was at stake, and Lena had taken oaths as a Healer, and couldn’t, in good conscience, say no.

 

            “Go,” Lena said, barely getting the word out before Kara was cupping the side of her head, kissing her cheek as she breathlessly thanked her. Before her girlfriend could vanish out the door she was pulling wide open, Lena grabbed Kara’s arm, pulling her to a stop. “But I’m coming with you.”

 

            That gave Kara pause, her mouth opening and closing as she hesitated momentarily. “But-”

 

            “A man is dying, he’s going to need a Healer,” Lena insisted, keeping her voice low. “Make up whatever lie you’d like about what I know, but I’m coming with you.”

 

            The urgency of the situation didn’t give Kara much time to object, but she still opened her mouth to argue before clamping it shut and continuing out the door, dragging Lena with her without a sound. Their feet pounded on the steps as they hurried downstairs and Kelly blinked in surprise at the sight of Lena, her gaze cutting to Kara, who keeping bypassed her in favour of the coat stand, grabbing the first two things her hands fell on before shoving her feet into a pair of muddy wellies. Lena donned a pair of slippers and buttoned up her coat, both of them still in their pyjamas, and looked at Kara, who was making for the fireplace and the pot of Floo powder on the mantle.

 

            Without preamble, she scatted a handful in and vanished in a swirl of emerald flames, quickly followed by Lena, who gave Kelly a confused look before the living room of her cottage distorted into a disorienting whirl of grates, before it spat her out onto the dark, marble floor of the Ministry of Magic’s Atrium. Kelly appeared a moment later, and Kara set off at a run, her footsteps echoing in the silence of the vast chamber, leaving the other two women struggling to keep up with her long strides. It was early hours of the morning, not a single other soul about - security must have been sweeping through another level at that moment - and they climbed into the lift and dragged across the brass grille with a palpable tension between the trio.

 

            Sinking down to Level 9, Kara jittery on the balls of her feet as she watched the numbers slowly tick up, Lena felt wariness coil in her stomach. She was already preemptively running through spells, trying to judge what might’ve happened, how to help before she even laid eyes on the man. While never having met the man, she was familiar with the Weasleys, had seen his wife at St. Mungo’s a few times earlier on in her career, a few red-haired children in tow, and she felt tense as she waited for the lift to stop.

 

            Level 9 was dark as they sprinted down the hallway, two unfamiliar people waiting near it, and Kara opened the door as she led the way, crossing a circular chamber with familiarity. Lena wanted to slow down and peer around, curious about the secretive Department, but there was no time for that as they ran through the next room, bizarrely filled to the brim with clocks, only narrow paths between desks allowing them room to pass through. Other doors were visible through the clocks, off-shoots to different rooms, but Kara made a bee-line for the door at the end. Lena’s heart pounded in her chest, keeping time with the maddeningly overwhelming sound of too many clocks ticking in tandem.

 

            The room at the far end was dark, only wan blue sconces casting light over the hall of towering shelves disappearing into darkness. The darkness unnerved Lena, the air cold and an eerie feeling making the hairs on her arms stand on end, but she followed on the heels of her girlfriend, Kelly and the other two - a witch and a wizard - crowding in close with their wands lit as Kara guided them to the correct row with familiar ease. Lena wondered how often in the last few months she’d come into the hall and walked the route, curiosity getting the better of her. She wanted to be angry but had no justification for it.

 

            Before they’d made it very far down the row, at an intersection between shelves, wand light illuminated a shadowed figure sprawled on the cold floor of the Hall of Prophecy. The other two Order members brushed past Kara, swearing as they bypassed the figure with their wands held up, cagey, as if expecting to be attacked. It gave Lena the chance to move forward and drop to a knee at the side of the man, blood soaking his clothes and splattered on his pale face. Fingers finding his pulse, she felt the weak patter of his heart as her eyes assessed the blood, before she tore open his robes and shirt and quickly bandaged the puncture wounds, not pausing to try and treat him there; he was losing far too much blood.

 

            “I need to move him,” she said, climbing to her feet and levitating him to waist height. “He needs to get to St. Mungo’s now.”

 

            “Okay, let’s go,” Kara softly agreed, moving to Lena’s side. 

 

            Mouth thinning, Lena gently touched her arm. “No, you can’t come. You’re not family and you’re not a Healer. You should … go home.”

 

            Floundering for a moment, knowing that she couldn’t argue too much without revealing what Lena knew - what Lena wasn’t supposed to know - and Kara nodded after a pause but didn’t look happy about it. Instead, she grimaced and looked down at the blood pooled on the floor, almost indistinguishable from the dark tiles.

 

            “I’ll clean this up first.”

 

            Lena glanced down at the pool of blood, and her attention snagged on something else, barely there but emitting a slight sheen against the tiles. Stooping, her fingers brushed over silky material and her stomach swooped as she grabbed a fistful of the fabric and straightened up. Weighing it in her hand, knowing what it was, she was silent for a moment as she tried to think of a way to play it off.

 

            “Um, I think this is his,” Lena called up to the others, holding up the Invisibility Cloak. “His cloak must’ve come loose when he was attacked. Will someone hold onto it until he’s discharged?”

 

            The wizard looked at it with wide eyes, obviously recognising it for what it was, and he quickly moved over to Lena to take the cloak from her. She relinquished it willingly and turned her attention back to her patient, preparing to move him when someone else spoke.

 

            “Kelly?” the other witch called out, and Lena eyed her pink hair, the youthfulness of her face. She had to be a decade younger than them. “Why don’t you head to St. Mungo’s with her? Make sure he gets there okay. We’ve got it from here.”

 

            Nodding, Kelly laid a hand on Lena’s shoulder to urge her onwards, and Lena lingered a moment, staring at Kara, her gaze so intense. Looking tired and worried in her cloak and wellies, the hems of her flannel pyjamas endearingly tucked into the tops of the boots, Kara gave Lena an encouraging nod. Returning the nod, Lena turned and moved quickly, levitating Arthur Weasley’s body behind her as she moved back through the stacks of crystal orbs and out into the room full of clocks. From what little she’d seen of the place, it was an odd place to work, and she could see why it fascinated Kara so much, the strange obsession she had with her work, and the insatiable desire for the mysteries she worked on even outside of office hours.

 

            Back in the entrance chamber, the walls started to spin and Kelly swore. “Fuck. We need-”

 

            “Hang on,” Kara’s breathless voice sounded from a door to Lena’s right as she appeared in the chamber, chest rising and falling quickly. “The walls … they move.”

 

            “Oh,” Lena mumbled, realising the purpose of her girlfriend’s presence.

 

            Making a bee-line for a door that was as non-descript as the others, knowing her way around the place with ease, Kara opened the door to the hallway beyond and Lena paused to give her a quick peck before she left her behind. She didn’t like that she left her there, inside the Department of Mysteries with other Order members, a part of her doubting whether Kara would clean up the blood and go straight home, or if she would be lulled into helping elsewhere, sitting with Dumbledore and the others as they ran over the events. Lena didn’t want to doubt her, but she knew how persuasive Dumbledore could be, and she knew even better how eager Kara was to help.

 

            Back in the Atrium, Lena levitated Arthur Weasley into the wide fireplace before she and Kelly followed him in and she Flooed them to St. Mungo’s. It was the middle of the night but the reception area held a dozen people waiting to be seen, their various ailments clearly not as emergent as the man bleeding through his bandages as she guided him out of the fireplace, already calling for help.

 

            “I need a gurney over here!”

 

            The staff, who had been enjoying the relative peace and ease of their night shift, were startled into action, and in short order, Lena was wheeling the gurney through to the Trauma Ward, leaving Kelly to wait behind, slippers slapping on the floor as she rattled off a list of supplies to the Resident who’d leapt to assist. They got him onto a bed in the Trauma Ward and, after a second assessment, baring the man’s chest in the bright light of the ward, Lena realised they were bite wounds. She had her Resident page Healer Smethwyck for a consult, hoping the ageing wizard was on duty, and was hurriedly presented with another Resident, Augustus Pye, who was working the night shift on the Serious Bites Ward. 

 

            Biting back her frustration, Lena had multiple units of Blood-Replenishing Potion hung to replace the alarming amounts of blood that were pooling in the bite marks and running in rivulets down the unconscious man’s chest. From what she could gather, it looked like snake bites , and she concluded that whatever venom had been meted out from the snake had anticoagulant properties and was making it difficult for her to close up the wounds. While she waited for Healer Smethwyck to answer his page, Lena ran through her knowledge of charms that might help, cursing her mother for limiting her time spent on the Serious Bites Ward, where Lena might’ve been able to learn more about that specialty. It could’ve helped a lot then, but Lena had to concede that she hadn’t really been interested in that area; she’d been interested in werewolves, or more specifically, Kara.

 

            Smethwyck showed up within twenty minutes of being paged, dark circles beneath his eyes and yesterday’s rumpled Healer robes thrown over pyjamas, taking note of Lena’s slippers and coat as he pushed in next to her at the bed to assess the patient. Deferring to his area of expertise, Lena ran through the course of treatment so far and her diagnosis and then listened as Smethwyck ruminated on what to do next. After administering two different antidotes with little success, Lena left the Healer to it, leaving the Trauma Ward with him as he wheeled the gurney towards the lift. Smethwyck and Pye took him up a level to the Dai Llewellyn Ward, while Lena took the stares down to the ground floor, exiting the hospital and Apparating back home.

 

            It was almost five o’clock in the morning by that point, still pitch black and bitterly cold as she hurried up the garden path and let herself inside. The house was damp and chilly, all of the rooms dark, but as her eyes adjusted to the gloom, she noticed a shadowed shape stretched out on the sofa with a blanket covering her and watched as Kara sat up. Her voice was slightly husky, clinging to sleep, and she waved a hand to the nearest lamp, casting a warm glow over the living room.

 

            “Is he alright?”

 

            Raking a hand through her hair, Lena heavily sighed. “He’s stable, for now, but his injuries are extensive. It looks like it was a snake bite, so that’s outside my area of healing. I had to hand him over to Healer Smethwyck; you know how good he is at his job, so I’m sure he’ll find a cure.”

 

            “Oh. Well, it’s good that he’s been treated. Good that he was found in time,” Kara tried to reassure them both.

 

            “Mm,” Lena hummed, rubbing her tired eyes and then slowly taking off her coat and kicking off her slippers.

 

            There was blood on the cuffs of her coat and pyjama top, but she was far too tired to concern herself with that right then. Hunger gnawed at her stomach and she let out another sigh, crossing over to the sofa and ducking down to kiss her girlfriend, glad that she was at home, that she was safe.

 

            “I could murder a cup of tea. Do you want one?”

 

            “If you don’t mind. Ta.”

 

            Lena walked into the kitchen, gesturing vaguely to the lights, and boiled the water, making two cups of tea while Kara made her girlfriend a sandwich with some leftover slices of beef from their Sunday roast at Eliza’s two days before. Slumping in a chair, Lena hummed gratefully around her first mouthful of food, and Kara hid a yawn behind her hand as her eyes squeezed shut, blinking owlishly as she sat cross-legged on her chair and sipped her scalding tea.

 

            “You should go to bed,” Lena urged her, glancing down at the watch on her left wrist.

 

            “I have to be up for work soon anyway. May as well start the day early.”

 

            Nodding, Lena was quiet for a moment as she eyed her sandwich. “What time did you get home?”

 

            “About … twenty minutes after you left.”

 

            “Oh.”

 

            “What?”

 

            “I thought they might … have questions, I don’t know.”

 

            “Oh. Well, not really. They were all there when Dumbledore asked Kelly to fetch me. They, uh, they did ask about you though.”

 

            Green eyes slid up to meet blue, and Lena swallowed thickly. “What did you tell them?”

 

            “Only that I told you Arthur was working with the Department as a contractor on some classified research that I couldn’t discuss - even with you. Um … they seemed to buy it, anyway, and Dumbledore knows the truth about you, so it’s- well, hopefully, that’s the end of it.”

 

            “Hopefully,” Lena murmured, doubtful about it.

 

            She moved onto the second half of her sandwich, yawning now too, taking a swig of tea as her shoulder slumped, and Lena could sense that Kara wanted to say something. It was something born from years of knowing her, of loving her and living with her, picking up on the way Kara chewed on the inside of her bottom lip, kept her eyes downcast as she tried to think of the correct way to ask, to phrase what she had to say. Waiting patiently, Lena cast her furtive glances in between bites of her sandwich, until Kara lightly cleared her throat.

 

            “Lena?”

 

            “Mm?”

 

            “Arthur Weasley had an Invisibility Cloak with him.”

 

            “Yes, I gave it back to that wizard.”

 

            “Kingsley, yes, it’s just … well, they’re extremely rare and hard to come by. Mad-Eye Moody had a spare one that was lost when Sturgis Podmore was arrested - I know that because Alex was complaining to me about it because she couldn’t get it back from evidence in the Auror Department - so I was just thinking about where they might’ve gotten another one from. I was just wondering about your one … because Moody would know that you have one because you told me about how he saw you in the first war, when you came to find me, so I guess I was just wondering where it was, if you still had it.”

 

            Lips pressed together, Lena felt weary resignation sweep through her as she finished off the last bite of her sandwich. Brushing crumbs off her lap, she drained the rest of her tea and cleared her throat before fixing her girlfriend with a piercing stare.

 

            “I think you know the answer to that already.”

 

            “I think I do,” Kara apprehensively agreed, her forehead furrowing, “but I’d like to think I’m wrong because we agreed that we’d tell each other first before we did anything.”

 

            “We did,” Lena conceded, guilt prickling in her gut now. “But I wouldn’t consider mailing an Invisibility Cloak as me being involved.”

 

            Looking put out, Kara adjusted her glasses and seemed to puff up as she inhaled deeply and exhaled gently through her nose as she stamped down her anger, or perhaps it was merely annoyance, but either way, Lena fought the urge to cringe. She hated to upset her, had thought nothing would come of the letter from Dumbledore asking if she’d be willing to lend her Invisibility Cloak to the Order, didn’t think Kara would find out about it after she’d neatly wrapped it up and sent it off with Morrigan months ago, before she’d been so insistent on being kept out of it. And Lena knew that it wasn’t fair of her to hold Kara to that standard when she’d been guilty of the same, and maybe she should’ve told her when they’d had that talk about telling each other before acting, but it was too late for that now.

 

            Unimpressed by her reasoning, Kara gritted her teeth, a muscle twitching in her jaw as she chose her words carefully. “That’s not the way I see it.”

 

            “Well, the way I see it, I was keeping us both out of it.”

 

            “How is that us staying out of it?”

 

            Spreading her hands slightly, trying not to be too haughty, hating how that was her natural inclination to any sort of confrontation, Lena shrugged, licking her lips. “It hasn’t gone any further than that, has it?”

 

            “I- well of course it hasn’t - you don’t want it to.”

 

            “But you do.”

 

            Floundering, mouth opening and closing as she slumped in her chair, Kara flushed. “Well, I’m not going to lie and say that I don’t , but we decided that we wouldn’t. That’s why I asked if I could go tonight, and you came with me, so where does that leave us now?”

 

            Elbows on the table, Lena put her head in her hands, closing her eyes. “I don’t know. That’s what I’m trying to figure out, because … it feels like everything is balancing on a wand tip right now and I’m scared.”

 

            Kara reached out, her fingers brushing over the sleeve of Lena’s pyjama top, gentle and aching. “What are you scared of?”

 

            Raising her head, hands dropping to the table, Lena’s eyes were bright, her gaze brittle as she stewed in her frustration. “We were so young last time, but you remember how it was - you were there at the end of it. So many people died. And it might not have progressed that far yet , but it’s only a matter of time. And I won’t be seeing injured people at work, I’ll be seeing dead bodies , and I’m scared that if you get too involved in this, one of them will be you . And if it’s not you, it could be your family, our friends. Every day I wake up and I dread the day, because I’m never sure if that will be the day that everything comes crashing down, because I can see how miserable it’s making you, but I can’t give you what you want because I’m terrified it means you’re going to get hurt and I just- I can’t- I don’t want it to get to that point, but the only way to do that is to help nip it in the bud before it does, but I’m not any use to anyone right now. But what happens when there comes a point where I could be? You don’t want me to help, but can I rightfully be a Healer if I don’t do everything in my power to help preserve life? And if - when - I get involved, you’ll get involved, because you won’t sit by, and, honestly, I think you’ll be happy for that to happen because I know how … frustrated you’re feeling about the whole thing, but then what does that mean for us? Because they don’t need more wands in the fight, they need information, so I’ll need to spy again, and that means I need to be around horrible people, and they’re not going to trust me if I’m in a relationship with a werewolf, and your friends, your family , won’t trust me as far as they can throw me once they find out who I’m associating with, because there’s only one reason why anyone would willingly be around known bigots, and you- you would never be able to bring yourself to be a spy and let people think the worst of you, turn your back on your family to do it - you’d find the whole thing … cowardly , and that’s- that’s fine, but what about us? If we go down that path of helping, when we go down that path … it’ll be the end of it all. That is what I’m scared of.”

 

            There was a faint sheen of tears in Kara’s eyes, a look of hurt on her face as she hugged her arms to herself. “You say that as if it’s the only way-”

 

            “It is,” Lena snapped, “it is because you would never come with me, but I would be useless if I stayed for you.”

 

            Eyes widening a fraction, Kara opened her mouth to respond but quickly shut it, the colour in her face further reddening as she swallowed thickly. Her surprise quickly darkened to scorn, her voice thick as she spoke, abruptly standing as the chair legs scraped over stone. “Well, seeing as you have it all figured out already ...”

 

            Heaving a sigh, Lena rubbed the bridge of her nose. “Oh, don’t be like that.”

 

            “I have to get ready for work.”

 

            Slipping out of the kitchen, Kara vanished upstairs, leaving Lena alone at the kitchen table, rubbing her forehead as exhaustion made her cranky and angry. Roughly pushing her chair back, she climbed to her feet, taking her plate and cup into the kitchen. She set the kettle over the heat again, letting it come to a slow boil without the aid of magic, leaning back against the counters as she listened to the sound of running water above her. 

 

            Taking her fresh cup of tea through to the living room, Lena sank onto Kara’s vacated spot and dragged the blanket over her lap. It was frigid inside the cottage so she slipped her wand from the waistband of her pyjama pants and pointed it at the empty fireplace, the cheery glow of flickering flames radiating heat as she curled herself into a ball. Stressed and gritty-eyed, Lena sank into the cushions as she listened to her girlfriend move about upstairs, emerging thirty minutes later with a sullen look on her face.

 

            Watching from the corner of her eye, Lena didn’t speak as Kara slipped on a robe and shoes, a scarf wound tightly around her throat, but she felt the keen ache in her chest for her girlfriend to speak to her. Lena didn’t want her to leave with things so up in the air, but any apology she might’ve spoken got stuck in her throat. Briefcase in hand, Kara let out a weary sigh as she approached the sofa, hesitating only briefly before her gaze cut to Lena. Her eyes were slightly red, evidence that she’d been crying in the shower, and Lena’s stomach sank like a stone as she sat up. 

 

            “I’ll see you later,” Kara murmured, leaning down to give her a mere peck on the cheek. 

 

            As she withdrew, Lena reached out to snag her hand, holding her in place. “Hey … I love you, okay? I know things are … confusing right now, but I- it’s you and me , right? We’re going to grow old together, okay? And all of my laugh lines will be because of you, because of how happy you make me, so … just ignore me. I don’t mean anything by it, I’m just … scared.”

 

            Kara’s face spasmed with a ghost of pain and she couldn’t manage more than a whisper. “Okay.”

 

            Feeling defeated, Lena raised Kara’s hand to her lips, pressing a soft kiss to her knuckles before letting go. “Have a good day.”

 

            Fingers brushed over her cheeks, smoothed the dark circles beneath her eyes. “You too. Get some rest, darling.”

            

            Nodding meekly, Lena sank back into the cushions with a brooding look on her face, extinguishing the fire as Kara approached the fireplace. With a handful of Floo powder, she disappeared in a whirl of green flames before Lena relit the fire and sat in silence, the wind howling as it buffeted the cottage, filling the quiet of the old house. Somewhere in the middle of her brooding, fretting over things that hadn’t happened yet, things that she hoped wouldn’t happen at all, Lena fell asleep on the sofa, her untouched cup of tea growing cold on the coffee table.

Chapter 49

            Christmas was ten days later and it was a tense ten days, to say the least. Not between Lena and Kara, although there was a palpable tension, a quality of unhappiness between them, from the self-imposed deadline Lena had given their relationship and the worry that it would happen sooner, rather than later. Kara didn’t want to talk about it, and while Lena felt a pang of guilt for shining a light on that which they’d been avoiding for too long, calling attention to the obvious outcome of going down that road. There wasn’t much Lena could do to comfort Kara, though; they both knew she was telling the truth, that if things continued to worsen to the point where they both got involved, one of them would have to compromise, or they’d have to end things. And they didn’t want to lose each other, would have rathered anything but that, but they wouldn’t be of much use to the Order if they weren’t able to do what they were good at. For Lena, that was spying, and for Kara, that was duelling in offensive skirmishes.

 

            They tried their best though, Kara coming home with flowers for Lena, Lena coaxing her to a dreary Diagon Alley for some last-minute Christmas shopping, making time after work to play Wizard’s Chess in front of the fire, Kara’s ageing cat curled up in one of their laps as they sipped tea or glasses of Firewhiskey. Christmas Eve, they found themselves at Alex and Kelly’s house, the couple relocating to Inverness the month before for something more scenic, more secluded, and their friends all huddled in the spacious living room as they celebrated Christmas together a day early, trying to make the most of their time together, all of them into their thirties now, with no promise of tomorrow. It was a forced sort of levity, though, as they all clinked glasses, laughing together as the windows turned a velvety blue from the heat of the roaring fire, everyone so full of life but a strain to the sound, at the corners of their eyes, in the set of their shoulders.

 

            Lena had work the next morning, leaving before five o’clock, the house still dark and still, lighting a fire to warm the place up for Kara and leaving a hangover cure beside a folded paper crane on the kitchen table. There were a few presents beneath the decorated tree in the living room, and she left them untouched, knowing that Kara would want to open them together later that evening at Eliza’s. Dressed warmly for work, Lena stepped outside into the frosted morning, the air cold in her lungs as she trudged down the garden path and then Apparated to the alleyway beside St. Mungo’s, stepping into the hospital with a sudden enveloping of warmth.

 

            It was a busy morning from the moment she arrived, making her way to the Attendings lounge to fetch clean scrubs and get changed, a long-sleeved shirt beneath the scrubs for warmth and her green Healer robe over the top, brusque Merry Christmases exchanged with the staff as she fetched herself a coffee from the tearoom before her Residents started bombarding her. This time of year was always busy, an endless stream of injuries - most minor, some a little more severe - and she doled out jobs to the Resident assigned to her service that morning before catching Sam at a nurse’s station. She’d been at Alex and Kelly’s the night before, dropping in before her night shift started, and was getting towards the end of it now, ready to go home to her daughter and open presents.

 

            They parted ways when they reached the lift, Sam going down to the Attendings lounge to get changed and leave, while Lena went off to check on a patient on the receiving end of a particularly bad Confundus Charm. After that, she was called to consult on a man whose hand had been hit by a shrinking charm, quickly assessing him and delegating to her Resident for the treatment plan before she made her way down to supervise a few Residents in the Alchemy Room before leaving them to rack up their brewing hours. 

 

            By lunchtime, she was up to her wrists inside a chest cavity, trying to restart a heart after a shattered rib cage had torn through the walls of the left ventricle, two Residents assisting as they vanished the fragments of bone. The patient survived, fortunately, after a long hour of siphoning blood away, hanging more units of Blood-Replenishing potions and repairing the tears before closing up the chest cavity. The woman was given an intravenous dose of Skele-Gro and taken to the Charms Ward to regrow her ribcage, while Lena filled out post-op notes and sent an Intern to fetch her a cup of tea.

 

            In a never-ending stream of patients, as Christmas Day wore on and family get-togethers and too much alcohol led to all manner of injuries, Lena found herself dealing with more menial treatments as they were rushed off their feet. There were blistering burns, broken bones, a man whose voice box had been charmed to sound like a goose, a young girl mauled by a Hippogriff her uncle had bought as a Christmas present, and a boy who couldn’t stop hiccuping up bubbles, and a few who were merely too drunk too early in the day. Her shift didn’t end until five o’clock, and by the time she’d showered and dressed back into her clothes, it was nearly six.

 

            Outside, it was pitch black and bitterly cold, London damp and dreary as usual, and she Disapparated out of the alleyway and was assaulted by the briny air of Cornwall as she appeared in the shadows at the end of Eliza’s street. Her breath steamed in the bitter cold as she jammed her fingers into her armpits, the wind blowing her about as she made for the cheery glow of the cottage in the near distance. The road was glistening wet and slightly icy and she hurried to the front door, reaching out to knock, even though she’d been welcome there for years, Eliza finding it endearingly amusing that Lena still insisted on waiting to be let in instead of walking straight inside.

 

            It was her mother-in-law who answered, the fine lines at the corners of her blue eyes creasing a little deeper as she smiled, giving Lena a fondly exasperated look. “Quick, quick, inside, before the wind carries you away.”

 

            “Merry Christmas, Eliza,” Lena greeted her, somewhat breathless as she stepped into the warmth, meeting the other woman’s hug halfway.

 

            The narrow hallway was brimming with shoes, bags, cloaks and coats, and Lena called out to the others in the living room as she unwound her scarf and hung it and her coat up with the others, before dropping her bag. From her angle, she could see Kelly practically sitting in Alex’s lap and Querl sitting on the floor, and was hunched over slightly as she unzipped her heeled boots, glancing up as Kara stepped into the hallway, wearing her new navy jumper. Giving her a quick smile, Lena got her shoes off and reached out for her girlfriend, giving her a lingering kiss, tasting eggnog and wine on her lips.

 

            There was a flush to Kara’s cheeks, a brightness to her eyes as she smiled, and Lena wrapped her in a hug. “Merry Christmas, darling.”

 

            “Mm, Merry Christmas,” Kara murmured, her cheek warm against Lena’s, squeezing her tightly as she lifted her slightly, letting out a shuddering laugh.

 

            She gave her another kiss and then grabbed her hand, towing her into the living room. It was cramped, with Nia there as well, and Eliza reclaiming her seat nearest to the open archway, a roaring fire surely making Kara and Kelly’s skin prickle from their closeness to the heat. Kara insisted that Lena have her seat, moving to the floor so her girlfriend could rest comfortably after a long shift, but it wasn’t for long.

 

            “Can we eat now?” Kara hopefully asked, handing Lena her half-empty glass of wine over her shoulder.

 

            Taking it, Lena swallowed a mouthful and rubbed her girlfriend’s shoulder. “Did you all wait for me?”

 

            “Of course we did,” Kara said, leaning back against her knees, tipping her head back to look up at her, smiling.

 

            “Don’t worry, they’ve had plenty to eat,” Eliza insisted, pushing herself to her feet again. “Come on then, everything’s hot and ready to go.”

 

            Everyone filed into the kitchen, Lena murmuring belated greetings to the others, squeezing Kelly’s arm as they exited the living room together, patting Querl’s back. The kitchen was cramped at the best of times, a table for four usually squeezing in five, but with another two, it felt like they were packed in like sardines. No one minded though, the bang of crackers and laughter filling the small space as they donned paper hats, while drinks were refilled and Lena was handed her own glass of wine, dishes levitating due to the limited surface space of the table. 

 

            Knives and forks scraped on plates and they all talked over each other, the way only people who knew each other that well could, pink-cheeked and laughing, talking about their day, making fun of each other.
