Aside from Lena and Alex, everyone else had been home all day, with Nia and Querl coming over just after lunchtime, on account of having nowhere else to go, and the Healer and Auror spoke wearily of their days, wedged in beside each other.

 

            “So, I heard Arthur Weasley was discharged,” Alex said, taking a sip of wine as she glanced sideways at Lena, her tone casual.

 

            “Mhm, I heard. He wasn’t on my Ward; Serious Bites, where Kara used to stay,” Lena replied with nonchalance, although her sister-in-law’s probing was evident.

 

            “Oh, right. Well, I bet he’s glad you were there at the time, though.”

 

            “Probably. I doubt he’ll be in a rush to consult with the Department of Mysteries again anytime soon. I guess that’s why they leave it up to the professionals, isn’t that right, darling?” Lena said, turning her attention to Kara, letting go of her fork to smooth a hand over Kara’s shoulder, giving her a soft smile.

 

            “Pardon? Oh, sure, that’s why Croaker pays me the big money,” Kara said with a quick wink to her as her mind registered the tail-end of Lena’s question.

 

            With a soft chuckle, Lena shook her head and picked her fork back up, raising her eyebrows quickly at Alex as she smiled. “I just hope she comes home in one piece. I’ll be cross if she doesn’t; only I’m allowed to fiddle with experimental magic.”

 

            Alex scoffed, the look in her eye telling Lena she wasn’t entirely convinced that the Healer bought the flimsy excuse that Arthur Weasley had been hurt helping out as a consultant, but she let it slide. Lena wouldn’t have minded if she hadn’t, her stoicism and general air of aloofness making her remarkably good at lying. She wouldn’t have survived long around her family if she hadn’t been able to keep her feelings under tight wraps.

 

            “Well, don’t go telling me about any new illegal activities or I’ll have to ruin Christmas,” Alex joked. “And we’ve already got enough on our plates with the state of things. Did you see what your mate printed in The Daily Prophet this morning?”

 

            Lena groaned, although she hadn’t seen it, knowing she was in for another sheepish conversation about Andrea and her bowing to the whims of the Ministry of Magic. Wondering what sort of anti-Dumbledore sentiment was being splashed across the front page now, she welcomed the change of conversation, feeling Kara’s hand on her knee beneath the table, squeezing gently in reassurance. 

 

            By the time they’d all eaten so much they thought they might burst, Kara was practically vibrating with excitement, leaving the others to clean up as she grabbed Lena’s hand and hauled her into the living room, where a haphazard pile of gifts had been set aside for her. There were the ones Lena had bought for Kara there too, and she smiled tenderly, gesturing to them as she took in the bright-eyed eagerness on her girlfriend’s face.

 

            “Go on then, you first.”

 

            Dropping to her knees with the childish enthusiasm of one who knew what it was like to not have much, and cherished every opportunity for new things, Kara tore open Lena’s precise wrapping paper. Lena had bought her a new briefcase for work, a leather belt, two new quills, a Muggle book on the theory of time and a mixed bag of sweets from Honeydukes. When it came to Lena’s turn to open her presents, she was first presented with few wrapped gifts that could only be books, happily staring down at the covers of new releases on a variety of topics that were of interest to her. The next was a small parcel that revealed a pair of Instant Warming Socks in a shade of forest green, Kara excitedly explaining how she’d seen an advertisement for them at Gladrags Wizardwear in The Daily Prophet and thought about how Lena always ran a little cold. Lastly was a roundish gift that was quite large and took some effort for Kara to shift in front of Lena, the clumsily taped wrapping paper torn away to reveal a new Copper Cauldron, Lena letting out a sound of surprise and clicking her tongue as she ran her hands over the polished metal.

 

            “Kara, this is far too expensive.”

 

            “I know, I know, but,” Kara goadingly grinned, on her knees as she reasoned with her, bright-eyed and pleased with herself, “it’s the best there is, so you should have the best. And you’re in desperate need of a new cauldron because you melted the bottom of your spare one. And really, you could’ve just spent this much on yourself, so …”

 

            “I love it,” Lena sighed, leaning in for a kiss, “thank you. And , for the record, I only melted the bottom of it because someone distracted me.”

 

            Kara laughed against Lena’s jaw, her voice low with satisfaction as her hand found a strip of exposed skin at Lena’s waist, thumb smoothing over her hip. “Well, that’s why this one is so good; it brews faster, so now I won’t have to tear you away from your potion-making to get you to-” 

 

            “Kara, don’t forget the rest, they’re under the tree,” Eliza interrupted, her voice drifting down the short hallway and getting closer. 

 

            Muffling a groan against Lena’s neck, her lips pressing a soft kiss, Kara pushed herself to her feet and went to fetch Lena’s other presents. Eliza had bought her a new journal, the same one she bought Kara every year for her birthday, baked a tin full of peanut brittle, fudge and gingersnaps, and knitted her another jumper, this one a dark plum with wide sleeves and a mock neck. Eliza appeared in the doorway, hands on her hips as she watched her open them, a motherly look of affection on her face as Lena earnestly thanked her, climbing to her feet to hug her.

 

            “You’re welcome, dear. I thought the purple would suit your colouring nicely.”

 

            “I love it,” Lena insisted, smiling as she glanced down at it. “Let me get changed into it quickly.”

 

            Kara had been cleaning away the wrapping paper but followed after Lena as she carried her jumper upstairs. Inside Kara and Alex’s old bedroom, not a thing changed since they’d moved out, Lena quickly took off her jumper as Kara eased the door shut. She didn’t have a chance to put on her new one though before her girlfriend’s arms wound around her waist, her chest pressing up against Lena’s back.

 

            “Not so fast,” Kara murmured as she kissed her bare shoulder. “Let me enjoy the view for a moment, at least.”

 

            Snorting, Lena turned in her embrace, arms going around her neck as she arched an eyebrow. “As if you don’t get an eyeful every day.”

 

            “Ah, but I can never get enough,” Kara laughed, kissing the underside of Lena’s jaw and then down her neck.

 

            She reached her collarbones and Lena tipped her head back, her laugh slightly strangled as her lashes fluttered, running her hands over Kara’s arms and shoulders as she basked in the feeling of her warm mouth on her skin. Wishing they were at home, Lena let out a soft sigh, which turned into a groan.

 

            “I really don’t like our odds of not getting caught having sex in your mum’s house on Christmas Day,” Lena murmured. “Not with your meddling sister downstairs.”

 

            “Mm, perhaps you’re right,” Kara agreed, straightening up and hesitating before stealing another kiss, “but I’m tempted to test it.”

 

            Affectionately squeezing her chin, Lena snagged her new jumper from the bed and pulled it on, tugging down the hem and looking down at herself. When she looked back up, Kara smiled as she cupped her face in her hands once more, giving her the gentlest of kisses.

 

            “I love you, you know.”

 

            “I know,” Lena murmured, a faint smile on her lips. “I love you too.”

 

            They left the bedroom then and made their way back downstairs, Lena opening a few presents from Alex and Kelly, the two of them thanking her in turn for the ones Kara had already gifted them earlier. They had trifle and sticky toffee pudding with fresh glasses of wine as they played charades in the crowded living room, and as tired as she was, Lena wouldn’t have wanted to be anywhere else, cherishing every rowdy Christmas she’d spent with the Danvers, especially now that things were getting worse again. Her cheeks grew rosy the more she had to drink, and her stomach hurt from laughing too much, Kara curling in on her as she buried her face in Lena’s shoulder, shaking with laughter, kissing her cheek, blue eyes bright and full of life. If only it could have stayed that way.

 

            New Year’s was quick to follow Christmas, Lena working almost every day between, while Kara spent time with her mother or friends, making the rounds to houses for tea and conversation but always home when Lena was. It was a lazy few days for Kara, and Lena eagerly indulged in the same when she was home, both of them sprawled on the sofa, reading with copious cups of coffee, taking damp walks down to the lake and back, making a variety of stews for dinner. Lena had New Year’s Eve off, finding herself out the back garden of Alex and Kelly’s house, her breath clouding before her as they all let off sparks and Dr Filibuster’s Fabulous Wet-Start, No-Heat Fireworks at midnight, clumsily kissing her girlfriend as Kara wrapped her in a tight embrace, both of them drunk and laughing. 

 

            If only they’d known they wouldn’t be celebrating the next New Year’s together, nor Christmas, their birthdays, anniversary, and not even Easter . That in a mere week, there would be news that would change everything, that in less than two weeks, it would be as if the last seven years had never happened, as if they had never lived together, slept beside each other, had a whole life planned together. They weren’t to know then that everything Lena feared would come true.

 

            It was on the full moon, the early hours of 7th January, 1996, when Lena was downstairs in the cellar, that it slowly fell apart. She’d been there since sunset, winter making the full moons a longer ordeal, and she sat with a fresh mug of coffee on her workbench as she kept herself awake with potions and an old text of lycanthropy she’d ordered from Italy, making use of her Latin for her research. It was rote by then, seven years of full moons spent in much the same way - even longer, if you factored in those nights at St. Mungo’s, volunteering for shifts and waiting for Kara to awake - yet, Lena still insisted on those monthly nights in the cellar, her girlfriend sleeping behind a thick, reinforced door, while she kept her candlelit vigil and researched.

 

            That night had been no different to the many others, but it was almost three o’clock by the Ouroboros snakes on Lena's wristwatch when she heard footsteps overhead. There were a few people who would enter without knocking, but being so late in the night, Lena was immediately on edge, snatching her wand from the workbench and extinguishing the lights as she eased herself off her stool to move over to the shadowed corner near the bottom of the staircase, slipping into a duelling stance with familiar ease. When the door was flung open, she tensed, before her whole body went slack at the sound of her sister-in-law.

 

            “Lena?”

 

            With a wave of her wand, Lena relit the candles as she stepped out of her hiding spot, staring through the darkness as Alex’s silhouette hurried downstairs. Pausing mid-stride in surprise as she watched Lena lower her wand, Alex continued until she reached the bottom, her hazel eyes wide and dark circles beneath them as she raked a hand through her hair, the smell of leather and cigarettes enveloping her in a comfortingly familiar perfume as Lena moved away to give her room.

 

            “What’s happened?” Lena asked, jumping to the worst-case scenario. “Who?”

 

            Shaking her head, Alex sighed, eyelids shuttering. “No, everyone’s fine. It’s-”

 

            She cupped her brow as she stood there silently for a moment, her eyes flitting to the locked door, hiding her sister’s werewolf form from sight, before she collected herself, shoulders sloping beneath her leather duster.

 

            “There’s been a mass breakout at Azkaban,” Alex said, pale and stressed, eyes trained on Lena’s face. “Ten prisoners; we’re still verifying who. I just- I thought you should know, straight away, just in case.”

 

            Lena’s mouth thinned as she pressed her lips together, dread pooling in her stomach at the thought of her brother being free. For a moment, she let herself believe that he wouldn’t have been one of them, that he was still safely tucked away inside Azkaban, where he couldn’t hurt anyone - least of all her - but she knew , she knew in her gut, that he would’ve been one of them. 

 

            Swallowing thickly, trying to force the lump in her throat down as a heaviness pressed on her chest, making it hard to breathe, Lena’s voice was hoarse as she replied. “Thank you.”

 

            She moved over to the workbench and hesitated before climbing back onto her stool, setting her wand down with a hand that was shaking slightly. Running a hand over her face, she felt the tightness in her throat, how pale she must have looked, the eyes of her sister-in-law drilling into her back.

 

            “Is there- is there a chance he knows it was you?”

 

            “No, I don’t think so. Igor Karkaroff was questioned by the Wizengamot; he gave the same names I put in my letter.”

 

            “Okay,” Alex murmured, her boots scraping on the stone floor as she restlessly shifted her weight. “I know she’s Secret Keeper but … maybe you should both consider staying with Kelly and me for a bit, if- if he is one of them. Just in case.”

            

            Shaking her head, Lena’s mouth thinned. “Thank you, but no. I don’t want to bring trouble to you both. And she needs the cellar.”

 

            “She can go to St. Mungo’s. It’s one night a month.”

 

            “Let’s wait and see first. I’ll speak to Kara then … see what she wants to do.”

            

            “Okay.”

 

            There was a pause and Lena turned on her stool, smiling wanly. “Thanks for coming.”

 

            Nodding, Alex stood with her hands braced on her hips, face clouded with worry. “Will you be alright by yourself? Technically, I’m supposed to be helping with the search, but I can stay if-”

 

            Making a shooing motion, Lena let out a frayed laugh, slightly breathless as her eyes closed for a moment. “No, no, you go, I’ll be fine. Stay safe, though, okay?”

 

            “And you,” Alex gravely replied, hesitating briefly again. “And, uh, maybe don’t tell her until we’re sure. She’ll be knackered in the morning.”

 

            “Of course,” Lena murmured, giving her another smile, tight-lipped as she thought of her girlfriend, of her brother, of what it would all mean.

 

            “I’ll let you know as soon as I hear, okay?”

 

            Lena nodded, distracted now, barely even listening to Alex, who stared at her for a moment longer before she crossed over to squeeze Lena’s arm reassuringly and then left, seeing herself out. Sitting there for a few minutes, knowing Alex would’ve locked up securely on her way out, Lena couldn’t resist going upstairs to double-check every door and window, knowing that Kara was Secret Keeper and her brother never would’ve laid eyes on their address to even find her. It was a comforting reassurance though, and she wandered back downstairs with dry-eyed exhaustion, reheating her coffee with a tap of her wand and seeing the rest of the night through.

 

            When dawn came, she paced outside the locked door until she heard the ragged sounds of pain from within fall silent before entering, Kara sprawled on the floor beside the low bed they’d set up for her. Lena had an Invigorating Draught in hand and grabbed the plaid blanket folded at the foot of the mattress, wrapping it around her girlfriend and helping coax Kara to her feet and onto the bed. A groan slid past Kara’s lips as her lashes fluttered, and Lena cradled her head in her lap, stroking her hair until she was conscious enough to sit up and drink the potion, perking up as it took effect.

 

            The cellar was cold and Kara started to shiver, holding the blanket tightly around herself, and Lena kissed her clammy brow, quietly murmuring to her as she shifted her head out of her lap and climbed to her feet. Fetching warm pyjamas for Kara, she helped her dress and then brought a cup of tea downstairs for her, letting her rest down there awhile before getting her upstairs to the sofa. Kara didn’t make it further than that for the remainder of the morning, sleeping on the sofa as she regained some colour in her pallid cheeks, while Lena anxiously sat in the nearby armchair, chewing her lip as she watched her. 

 

            At lunchtime, Kara woke again, sweat dampening her hairline and rosy-cheeked from the heat of the fire, and Lena brought her some soup to eat, another cup of tea and a potion to wash it all down. They didn’t speak much, but Kara haltingly asked her if everything was okay on several occasions, picking up on Lena’s agitation, the tense set to her shoulders. Dismissing it as merely being tired from her sleepless night, which in turn had Kara apologising, guilt flashing across her face, which likewise had Lena feeling guilty, she ushered her girlfriend upstairs to take a bath.

 

            Joining her in the steaming water, Lena let Kara’s head loll against her shoulder, grey light filtering in through the bathroom window, and she kissed her temple, the shell of her ear, the softness of her cheek, her arms wrapped tightly around her as they lingered there. Afterwards, they went to bed, early in the afternoon but both of them tired in different ways, the curtains drawn over the windows with enough light filtering through the gaps to alleviate the dark. With the warm presence of each other’s bodies as they pressed up close, Lena’s back to Kara’s chest, they were both fast asleep in no time, even with the weight on Lena’s mind.

 

            They slept all through the night, and Lena woke in the early hours of the morning to the total darkness of their bedroom, her heart hammering as she blindly looked around, easing out from under Kara’s arm as she snatched up her wand. The wooden floor was icy beneath her feet as she crept out of the bedroom, the window at the end of the landing letting in only the faintest moonlight, the sky overcast. Padding downstairs, Lena lit a fire and sank onto the sofa, head in her hands as she felt sweat cool on her back, feeling cold and stiff. 

 

            The impatient tap of a beak on glass roused her then, and Lena wondered if that had been what had initially woken her, the loud sound cutting through the stillness of the early morning, and she recognised the snowy owl as Kelly’s. Climbing to her feet, wondering how long the bird had been left out in the cold, Lena let him inside, the annoyed click of his beak and a quick peck letting Lena know the answer was too long. The snowy owl fluttered over to Morrigan’s perch, her ageing owl cracking an eye at the intrusion, and Lena left the window open, cold, damp air flooding in as she broke the seal and unfolded the parchment. It was Alex’s familiar handwriting and didn’t say much, mindful of a possible interception.

 

He’s out. Keep a low profile. We’re working on it - Alex 

 

            Crumpling the letter in her hand, Lena felt frustration slam into her, her stomach lurching with dread as she restlessly paced. Stopping near the fireplace, she swept everything off the mantle with the tinkling of broken glass as it crashed to the stone floor, anger pulsing at her temples, making her vision dim as she buried her face in her arms, elbows on the mantle and shoulders hunched as the fire stung her shins through her pyjama pants.

 

            She didn’t move until the light tread of footsteps creaked on the stairs, her girlfriend’s sleep-roughened voice softly calling out. “Lena?”

 

            Drawing in a deep breath as she raised her head, Lena glanced down at the mess of broken photo frames, a ceramic vase with a trailing plant smashed amongst dark soil, a few candles dented slightly from the impact. With a wave of her wand, she watched them all repair themselves and drift back onto the mantlepiece as if she’d never swept them off. Kara had drifted closer while she did that and Lena flinched at the feeling of her warm palm ghosting over her shoulder blade, shame washing through her as she slowly turned.

 

            “Go back to bed,” Lena murmured, reaching up to cup Kara’s chin.

 

            “What’s wrong?”

 

            “I’ll tell you later.”

 

            “Tell me now.”

 

            A pained ripple of amusement crossed Lena’s face and she leaned in to give her girlfriend a quick kiss. “So demanding.”

 

            Kara didn’t so much as smile, her eyes wide and mournful as she stared at Lena with concern, holding onto her sleeve as if she was afraid she might try to run away. Swallowing thickly, her mouth thin with regret, Lena raised her other hand, the crumpled letter held tightly in a fist. Kara looked down as she uncured her fingers, glancing back up at Lena before she took it from her, reading the short letter by firelight.

 

            Glancing back up at her, Kara’s expression was severe, brows furrowing over fearful eyes, the silver scars crisscrossing her face limned orange by the fire. She looked tired as well, despite how much she’d slept, taking advantage of the weekend, and Lena didn’t want to worry her, even as she felt her own fear, chilling and hair-raising. 

 

            “What’s this?” Kara asked, her voice hitching with wary uncertainty. 

 

            Eyes shutting as she softly sighed, shoulders slumping with weariness, Lena ran a hand over her face. “Alex came over yesterday morning, while you were still transformed, to let me know there had been a breakout at Azkaban. They didn’t know who , but she wanted to warn me, in case it was him. Well … it looks like it is.”

 

            Kara sharply inhaled, her eyes widening. “What does that mean?”

 

            Hesitating, Lena took the letter back, carefully folding it into quarters before she turned and tossed it into the fire. Bracing her hands on the mantle, she hung her head as she watched the parchment curl up at the edges and burn down to ash, Kara still standing behind her, brimming with nervousness.

 

            “Lena, what does that mean?”

 

            “I don’t know,” Lena rasped, her voice faltering slightly, breaking with uncertainty and fear.

 

            They stood in silence for a few minutes, Kara waiting for more, Lena not wanting to move on from that last moment of peace, knowing that once it ended, things would never be the same. She wasn’t quite sure how yet, needed time to think it through, all of the things she’d said to Kara in her frustration over the last few weeks and months now seeming more real. When nothing more was forthcoming, Kara went into the kitchen to make them coffee, the aroma filling the cottage, homely and comforting, and they sat side by side on the sofa as they sipped in silence.

 

            Once she’d finished hers, Lena glanced down at her watch and sighed. “I need to get ready for work.”

 

            Kara made a small sound of objection but let her go. Setting her mug down on the coffee table and kissing her girlfriend’s head, Lena made her way upstairs, taking a short shower and then dressing warmly, applying minimal makeup and staring at the shadows beneath her eyes as she brushed her teeth. All she could think of was her brother, of Kara, or two worlds that couldn’t interact, and only one possibility to help ensure the safety of the person she loved most in the world. But Lena didn’t even know if that was possible either; she would need to know for sure before any decisions were made.

 

            Finishing getting ready, Lena went downstairs and put her shoes on, her satchel at her feet, reaching for a dark wool robe and a mustard-coloured scarf - one of Kara’s, smelling of her perfume and an endless source of comfort - before she walked over to her girlfriend, who was still curled up on the sofa. Sinking to a crouch before her, Lena splayed a hand over Kara’s knee, her green eyes aching and worried as she met her gaze.

 

            “I’ll see you later, alright? But everything is going to be okay, I don’t want you to worry. We’ll talk about it later.”

 

            Leaning forward, Kara kissed her, her lips bruisingly hard, a desperate edge to it, as if she could feel the inevitability of it all, of the limited time they had left, like sand slipping through her fingers. Kissing her back, Lena stroked a hand over her hair as she pulled back to look at her, before fetching her satchel and leaving for work.

 

            It was still dark out, but the harsh white lights of St. Mungo’s greeted her as she Flooed into the reception, bypassing the near-empty waiting room. She went to the lounge to stow her bag and fetch clean scrubs and her Healer robe, getting changed before she walked through the hallways of the hospital, breathing in the clean, faintly medicinal smell. It eased something in her, the cold air soothing the clamminess of her skin as her trainers squeaked on the floor, feeling dread weigh heavily in her chest as she followed the way to her mother’s office.

 

            Her interactions with Lillian had been strictly professional for years now, regular meetings with the Head Healers of each Department meaning Lena was forced to speak with the Healer-In-Chief often. Still, it was evident to all staff that there was a strain to the relationship between mother and daughter, a palpable contempt whenever they exchanged curt words. To this day, despite achieving every goal her mother had set for her, jumping through hoops to please her, Lillian was still condescending and haughty with her, even in work-related matters, reserving a special coldness for her daughter. 

 

            But now, Lena willingly sought her out, after years of leaving anything personal behind her and focusing solely on the work. Knocking on the closed door, waiting for the sound of her mother’s voice, curt and business-like, Lena turned the knob and let herself in, watching the barest hint of surprise ripple across Lillian’s face as she leaned back in her chair. Stepping inside, Lena shut the door behind herself and moved closer, remaining standing behind the chair set across from her mother.

 

            “To what do I owe the pleasure?” Lillian greeted her, lips twitching with a faint smirk, arching an eyebrow.

 

            “I’m assuming you’ve heard the news?”

 

            Reaching for a folded copy of The Daily Prophet, Lillian shook it out, slapping it down on the desk for Lena to see. “Of course. It is front page of the news.”

 

            Nodding, her hands feeling clammy at the mere allusion to her brother, the nape of her neck tingling in warning, Lena swallowed thickly. “And … do you know where he is?”

 

            “Well, now, that would depend on where your loyalty lays,” her mother replied in a cold, pointed voice.

Chapter 50

            It was late when Lena got home from work, staying behind as she assisted on a few emergencies that the other Attendings could’ve managed just fine, trying to delay going home for as long as possible. She knew why that was, of course, had spent all day with that pit of dread in her stomach as she tried to rationalise it all to herself, tried to find a different solution and came up empty-handed. If she could’ve stayed at St. Mungo’s in indefinitely suspended time, she would’ve. Instead, it hit seven, eight, nine o’clock, hours after she should’ve been home from her shift, and she finally made herself leave.

 

            She Apparated to the damp grass on the boundary of the warded cottage, the night chilly and wet from the rain, and she couldn’t bear to go inside. She didn’t pace, didn’t so much as move, standing with squared shoulders as she stared at the glow of the cottage, the fire in the living room filling the bottom windows with a welcoming orange light, and Lena struggled to swallow the lump in her throat. A light rain beaded on the wool of her cloak and the cold burrowed into her as the minutes slipped by, her bottom lip trembling slightly from the effort it was taking to retain her composure, before she eventually started up the garden path.

 

            The door softly creaked as she slowly opened it and crossed the threshold, her head ducked down, unable to bring herself to look up, even though she could see Kara sitting on the sofa through her lashes. Keeping her eyes cast down, Lena unwound the scarf around her neck, hanging it up, her robe following, but she kept her shoes on. She was moving as slow as possible, as if prolonging the last few moments of normalcy, and Kara knew it, a wave of prescient grief slamming into her where she sat, watching her girlfriend, taking in the guilty hunch to her shoulders, the way she would not look up.

 

            “It’s okay, Lena,” Kara softly said, her voice wavering, despite her best effort. “You can say it.”

 

            And to the surprise of them both, Lena let out a strangled whine of pure pain, her feet moving quickly as she crossed over to Kara and fell to her knees, head burying in her girlfriend’s lap as she collapsed into gut-wrenching sobs. She hadn’t cried since she was fourteen years old, not a single, solitary tear, and Kara was ashen-faced as she curled over her, hugging Lena’s head as she felt her violently shake, coming apart completely. 

 

            Kara had never seen Lena cry, not even on their first meeting when it had been evident that Lena had been crying, and it terrified her more than anything else ever had. All she could do was gently hush her, her own eyes filling with tears, even though she stamped down her feelings, shakily shushing Lena as she stroked her hair, her voice thick and broken as tears wet her cheeks.

 

            “It’s okay, it’s okay.”

 

            It was minutes before Lena could even speak, gasping as she breathlessly wept into Kara’s lap. “I’m sorry, I’m so sorry.”

 

            “Shh, it’s alright, it’s okay. You- you don’t have to do this if you don’t want to. We can- can stay out of it, we can-”

 

            Shaking her head, still buried in Kara’s lap, Lena let out a pitiful sound of disagreement, her hands gripping fistfuls of Kara’s jumper as she drew in a loud, heaving breath. “We can’t. I’m sorry, we can’t. You know that- it was always going to- to come to this, I just- I’m sorry. I didn’t want it to. I just … I just want to keep you safe.”

 

            Shushing her again, the sound wavering as Kara smoothed her dark hair, kissed the crown of her bowed head, did anything she could to comfort Lena as she got the words out between broken sobs, Kara felt the hot stinging of more tears. They’d both known it, that’s why she’d been sitting there all day, waiting for Lena to come, biting her nails and staring vacantly at the fire as the dread built. It had always been a vaguely acknowledged notion that if there ever came a point where Lena would be of use, she would have to take it, even though Kara would’ve done everything and anything to stop her. Anything but take away her choice in the matter.

 

            And while she’d given up joining in the effort out of solidarity with Lena, who was, up until now, not a spy, she’d also spent the last six months filled with that certainty there would come a point where she was no longer a bystander. It had been easier to ignore, still stuck in the early days of the war, but the last two, perhaps even three, months, it had built and built, had been the cause of many arguments, of this tension between them as they worried in silence, neither one of them wanting to voice their concerns, rehashing the same panicked fights. And now, this, all of it culminating in this quietly devastating implosion of their lives.

 

            “I’m sorry,” Lena whispered again, her voice torn with anguish, and Kara just kissed her hair again, her face furrowed with mystified confusion as Lena just kept apologising.

 

            “It’s okay,” Kara murmured in reassurance, rubbing her back. “It’s okay, we knew this would happen. We didn’t want it to but … we knew. And we’ll get through it, okay? I’ll keep you safe, I won’t let them hurt you.” 

 

            Stilling beneath Kara’s touch, Lena pulled back slightly and then slowly raised her head, looking at her with bewilderment. And Kara looked at her, taking in the redness of her cheeks and eyes, already swollen and raw, the tears wetting her face and Kara’s thighs. Cupping her girlfriend’s face in her hands, Kara gave her an agonised look as she brushed her hair back, softly tutting, while Lena’s lower lip trembled and she drew in a hitching breath.

 

            “Kara, I- we can’t-” Lena shook her head, her green eyes filling with more tears, an alarming sight as Kara quickly wiped them away with the cuff of her jumper as they fell. Sniffing, Lena’s shoulders slumped, guilt and grief crumpling her face as yet more tears fell, breathless sobs still escaping her as her fingers encircled Kara’s wrists. “You know that’s not- that’s not possible.”

 

            “What’s not, baby?” she murmured, blue eyes wide and clueless as she wiped away more tears.

 

            And Lena’s eyes filled again, a choked sob shuddering out of her as she ducked her head, shame and agony making it impossible for her to speak while looking at the love of her life as she broke her heart. “You and me … we can’t- I already told you this, but we can’t do this if we- if there’s an us.”

 

            “Yeah, I- I know that,” Kara insisted, her brow creasing with confusion, “I can- I’ll tell everyone we’ve split up, we’ll just- we’ll have to be careful.”

 

            “Kara,” Lena pleadingly replied as her voice cracked, her hands smoothing down Kara’s arms, up to her shoulders, running over her face, her chest, her shoulder blades as she knelt between her knees, touching their foreheads together, noses bumping. It was as if she was drinking her in, trying to memorise every inch of her, but she’d already done that a long time ago, and her girlfriend’s body was as familiar to her as her own, every scar and freckle. “We can’t keep it secret, it- it won’t work. My mother, my brother , your family … they’re smarter than that. It- it has to be real.”

 

            And then it started to dawn on Kara, who sat back slightly, her expression falling even as a puzzled smile curved the corners of her mouth. She looked so baffled by what Lena was saying, as if the thought had never even occurred to her, and Lena raised her head, locking eyes with her as she watched half a dozen emotions cross her face, from shock to panic, to devastation as it all registered.

 

            “No,” Kara managed to croak, her blue eyes filling with fresh tears, shaking her head as she cocked it to the side. “No, no, that’s- no, you’re wrong, we can do it, we- we did it for years -”

 

            “We were just kids then,” Lena whispered, her sorrowful gaze tender with so much reluctance as she watched Kara try to reason with her. “And that was over … school rivalries. There was- there was never any danger, but this … this could get us …”

 

            She didn’t want to say it, the word getting stuck in her throat as she swallowed it down like a stone that sat heavily in her stomach. Kara drew in a sharp breath but didn’t speak, the moment of silence stretching out between them as a log crackled in the fireplace, but then she seemed to blink herself out of her stupor, her eyes running over Lena’s face as she thought, her mind running through possibilities.

 

            “I’ll come with you,” Kara rasped, a firm set to her expression as she scowled, blinking tears away, her chin wobbling slightly. “I’m not leaving you.”

 

            Lena’s heart broke a little more then, an aching look on her face as it rippled with pain. She reached out, fingertips ghosting over Kara’s face, over her scars, as she gently spoke. “You can’t. They wouldn’t accept you, my love.”

 

            Flinching as if she’d been slapped, the reminder of her affliction, of how Lena’s family would never consider her trustworthy enough to divulge anything around her, nothing more than a bloodthirsty monster in their eyes, Kara was speechless for a moment. Her mouth opened and closed, nothing coming out but wordless sounds of objection, of reasoning, as her face paled and she realised the gravity of their situation.

 

            “And I couldn’t put you in harm’s way, I couldn’t put your family through that,” Lena quietly continued, raising Kara’s hands to her lips and kissing her knuckles. 

 

            “Lena-” Kara started and then faltered, shaking her head as her throat bobbed, trying again. “Don’t do this. Please. Please.”

 

            “I’m sorry. I’m sorry, but I have to. I want to keep you safe, I- this is the only way to do it and keep you safe.”

 

            Eyes filling with fresh tears, Kara continued to shake her head, the breath hitching in her throat. “No, no, no.”

 

            “I’m sorry. You know I didn’t- I didn’t want it to get to … this point. I didn’t want to make you hate me, but … you can scream at me or- or hex me, or-,” Lena rasped, her face taut with devastation, tensed in anticipation as she cut off, her throat closing up.

 

            “I don’t want to,” Kara whispered, a horrified look in her eyes as she reached out to smooth Lena’s hair back, her touch so gentle, her face so wrenched with agony. “I could never do that, I could never hate you. Not even for this. In fact, I’ve never loved you more.” 

 

            Lena let out a choked sound of surprise, sniffing as she looked at Kara with aching green eyes, so bloodshot and bright with a film of tears that it was still shocking and unsettling for Kara to see in such a way. In all their years together, through all of the difficult talks of what Lena had suffered, talking about how she felt, how she was managing her bad thoughts without hurting herself, she’d never once shown anything close to the raw display of emotion then. Kara wanted to wrap her in her arms and keep her there, and not to spare herself the heartbreak, but to spare Lena. But Lena wanted to do this, thought she had to ferret out what information she could to help put a stop to all of this before things got so bad that they’d hurt the people she cared about, so Kara let her. She loved her so much that she would’ve given her anything, even if it meant cutting out her own heart. And Lena loved her too, which left her frightened of what this path would bring.

 

            “Promise me that this won’t change anything,” Lena pleaded. “You’re going to hear … horrible things about me, but please don’t believe everything you hear. I’ll do what I have to do, but please promise me that you’ll always know that I would never intentionally hurt anyone. And afterwards … there will still be us. You have to promise me that, because I love you. I love you. I can’t-”

 

            Removing her hands from Lena’s, Kara jerkily climbed to her feet, walking away from her. Kneeling on the floor, lips parting in surprise as a cry of distress fell from them, Lena’s eyes stung with fresh tears as a breathless sob made her chest ache. Pressing a hand to her sternum, as if checking to ensure her rib cage was still whole, Lena covered her face with a hand, dark head bowed as her shoulders shook until warm hands were urging her to her feet and settling her on the comfortable sofa, sinking beneath her weight. 

 

            Kara perched on the edge of the coffee table, their knees knocking as she sat across from Lena, holding a pale hand in her scarred one, running a thumb over Lena’s knuckles while her other hand held a little velvet box, the one she’d been hiding for a while now, waiting for the time when they would finally talk about it, waiting for the time she felt like she was deserving of someone like Lena. Seven years and so many dismissive insistences that things were fine the way they were had stayed Kara’s hand of late, but she’d bought it nonetheless, on the off-chance that one day, Lena might want to marry her. And now they were breaking up.

 

            She murmured, trying to coax Lena’s head up, moving the ring box forward, into her field of view as she ran a thumb over the worn velvet of it. When Lena saw it, she lifted her head, her shoulders gently sloping as her eyes softened with surprise, lips parting.

 

            “I promise that it won’t change a thing,” Kara said as her voice wobbled, trying to keep it together, knowing this was so far from how she’d imagined this going, but needing to tell her, needing Lena to know . “I know that last time- but I know the truth now, and I will never believe what I hear, okay? I know you, I love you. I love you so much that I- I’ve had this hidden away in here for so long … just in case you ever thought about making a different kind of oath, and I- I didn’t know if you wanted to but I need to tell you now … when this is all over, I want to marry you and I want to- to keep making promises with you until we die.”

 

            Lena choked on a laugh that was half a sob, wiping tears from her eyes as she stared at the closed ring box, itching to open it, to slide it onto her finger then and there. Drawing in a shuddering breath as her shoulders slumped, she gave Kara a bittersweet smile, wiping at her cheeks as she laughed again.

 

            “Of course I want to marry you. I would’ve married you years ago if you’d wanted to marry me,” Lena said as her voice broke.

 

            “Really?” Kara timidly asked, hope in her voice and face. 

 

            Leaning in, Lena kissed her softly, bumping her nose as she let out a quiet laugh, warm and loving but tinged with regret that they were having this conversation too late. “I’d love nothing more than to be your wife.”

 

            Tears pricked Lena’s eyes again as she bit her lower lip, a heaviness in her chest like she’d never experienced before. Not even through all the awful things she’d endured at the hands of her family, not even all those years ago, having her heart broken by Kara. This was seven years of her life, all the love and comfort she had in her life being ripped away from her, her home, her heart, her best friend. It was a loss that she couldn’t even truly feel the magnitude of right then, with Kara still sitting before her, both of them crying their eyes out as they muddled through this confusing breakup, going against the very fabric of their beings out of necessity, out of their safety. A part of Lena wanted to indulge in Kara’s fantasy and believe that they could risk staying together, that they were sneaky enough to pull it off, but she knew it in her heart that her mother, her brother, someone would find out, and it would result in something a lot worse than heartbreak - for one or both of them. 

 

            And perhaps she wouldn’t have minded if she knew it would be her who would suffer the consequences of being caught spying, had endured so much suffering at such a young age that she imagined most of it would be much the same, but there was no guarantee it would be her. And even if it was her they targeted, her they found out, she could never put Kara through something like that, knowing that as grateful as Lena would be that it was happening to her, Kara would have switched places with her in an instant, would even let her go now. And for that reason, Lena lied to her, just a little white lie.

 

            “I should- I should pack my bags,” she hoarsely said after a heavy pause, both of them lingering in the longing for a different future, a different path where she had a ring on her finger by the end of the night. “I’ll go to the flat in Dublin.”

 

            She wouldn’t. Lena already knew she would be going home, to the manor house just outside of Wicklow, to the house that hadn’t been the beginning of her trauma, but had inflicted a lot more. She knew that if Kara even suspected she’d go back there, that she’d sleep and eat and live alongside the mother and brother who had been so cruel, she would never let Lena walk out of the door. It was a mercy, she told herself, to keep Kara in the dark about it. Kara, who had promised Lena so many years ago that she would never have to go back to that house, who would hold to that promise if she had an inkling as to what her girlfriend was thinking. But she trusted Lena, and she believed her when she said she’d go to the flat in Dublin, thinking that she’d perhaps go back to the Luthor estate purely to sit and socialise with her brother to coax out information for Dumbledore, that she would leave after that and be somewhere safe, even if she was alone. It was for the best that she didn’t tell her.

 

            “I should pack one too,” Kara rasped.

 

            Lena blinked in surprise at her words, lips parting as she gave her a confused look. “Why?”

 

            “I can’t … stay here without you. I’ll … go to my mum’s, or Alex’s, just … not here. I can’t do that.”

 

            Slowly nodding, her mouth thinning as she thought about how she was tearing two lives apart in pursuit of this, that she didn’t have to help the Order, that both of them had stayed out of it for half a year already, Lena hesitated and then pushed herself to her feet. They both knew that it had been a long time coming, that they’d both been restless to sit by, only doing so out of solidarity with each other but chafing at it all the same, so she stood and she moved to the stairs, each step making her heart weigh a little more as she walked to her doom, Kara on her heels with the closed ring box in her hand. 

 

            Side-by-side, in the bedroom they’d slept beside each other in on the nights they were home together, they packed a bag each with their clothes, their personal effects, anything important that they would need, leaving behind so many things of lesser importance but perhaps more significance. The framed photos of the two of them, the cushions they’d picked out, the books they’d bought each other and their favourite mugs they drank their morning coffees out of. So much of their lives were left behind as they packed a meagre bag each, no number of extension charms able to account of how much they didn’t take with them, and they carried them back downstairs, standing in the living room with an oppressive feeling to the cottage, the silence shrouding them as they stared at each other.

 

            Lena set her bag down and fetched Morrigan’s cage, hastily scribbling a letter for the old owl to carry to the Luthor estate, so she could find her own way there, before she let her loose out the front window, soaring away into the night. She wrote another letter and folded it up, turning to Kara and holding it out.

 

            “Can you please get this to Dumbledore for me? Let him know- let him know what I’m doing, um, to expect letters.”

 

            “Of course,” Kara murmured, hesitating as she held the folded parchment in hand, staring down at the drying wax seal.

 

            “There’s just … one more thing.”

 

            Staring at her, eyes mournful as she waited, Kara didn’t anticipate Lena’s next words.

 

            “It needs to be believable,” Lena rasped, her eyes raw, pale cheeks blotchy as she stood before Kara, hands hanging limply at her sides. “I need you to- to hit me, hex me, just-”

 

            “No,” Kara said, aghast, her voice rough and low as her eyes went wide with revulsion at the mere thought of laying a single finger on her. “No, you can’t- you can’t ask me to- to do that to you. I can’t- please, don’t.”

 

            Fresh tears ran down her cheeks as she drew in a hitching breath, and Lena nodded, stepping in closer, cupping Kara’s face in her palm, “okay, okay, I won’t.”

 

            Nodding as she shakily inhaled, looking relieved, Kara’s face quickly blanched as Lena turned away, wand slipped out of her back pocket, moving quickly as she pointed the tip at her face and hexed herself. She staggered back a step from the impact, feeling the stinging numbness of a broken cheekbone, the ghostly memory of a similar pain over a decade ago creeping up on her, and then Kara’s hands on her shoulders, turning her around as Lena blinked owlishly, her ears ringing as Kara’s mouth moved. The pain made her feel slightly nauseous but she stamped it all down as she shook her head, a hand reaching up to shush Kara, wiping tears from her face.

 

            “It’s alright, it’s okay. I have to, I have to, okay? But it’ll be fine, it’ll be easily fixed, I just- I need my mom to see me like- like this. She has to think that we- that you-”

 

            “Oh,” Kara choked out, her face furrowing with stunned realisation. She hesitated then, nodding as she wiped her cheeks. “Should we- I’ll have to … do the same.”

 

            “No,” Lena objected. “No, you don’t have to-”

 

            “My family wouldn’t believe me either. They wouldn’t believe me if I told them you- you’d joined them. This way … maybe they will, I just- I don’t want them to think that you’d-”

 

            She cut off, grim with reluctance to paint Lena as the villain, as someone who would hex her and hurt her, but they both knew that Kara was right. As much as Alex had mistrusted her at the beginning, even she would be shocked to hear that they’d broken up, that Lena had turned, and only seeing her sister bloody and bruised would be able to cement that truth. And as much as it shamed Lena to have people she cared about, people who had been more of a family to her than her own had ever been, to think that she would ever do something like that to Kara, that she would even lay a finger on her, she knew that it would sell it like nothing else would.

 

            “It’s okay. You- do what you have to do. You and I both know what’s true; I can- I can live with them all thinking badly of me, as long as you don’t.”

 

            “Never.”

 

            “I can’t do it though,” Lena hoarsely told her, teeth bared in agony as she gave her an apologetic look. “I can’t- I could never hurt you like that, not- not even for a lie.”

 

            Nodding, Kara swallowed thickly and pulled her wand out, pointing it at her nose and then pausing as she quickly removed her glasses. Squinting slightly, a hawkish look on her face as she struggled to see without them on, she inhaled deeply and then hexed herself in the face with the same spell Lena had used, the sickening crunch of her nose breaking. Lena sucked in a sharp breath, watching as Kara covered her nose with a hand, making a muffled grunt of pain, bright red seeping through her fingers.

 

            Lena rushed in, smoothing a hand over Kara’s golden hair, the side of her face, her stomach roiling nauseously as her breaths turned shallow. Despite the numbing pain in her cheek, that was nothing to the pain of seeing Kara hurt, and Lena felt guilt twist in her chest to have brought this upon them. The bruising set in fast, two black eyes forming as Kara put her glasses back on, her mouth and chin covered in blood as it dripped onto the floor, and she wrinkled her broken nose, tears in her blue eyes as she swallowed thickly, while Lena breathlessly apologised over and over, fighting the urge to heal her, to take away her pain.

 

            “I’m okay,” Kara murmured, although neither of them were.

 

            “I-” Lena faltered, feeling it all come to a close, gritting her teeth together as she shook her head. “I don’t want to leave you. Can you- can you go first? Please.”

 

            Eyes smarting, Kara’s face rippled with pain. “Okay. I’ll go first.”

 

            Relief flooded through Lena, who didn’t think she’d have the strength to walk out of the door and leave her behind. At least if Kara left first, it would make it that little bit easier. “Thank you. Thank you. I- it won’t be for long, okay? And you have to promise me you’ll stay safe. I’ll brew Wolfsbane for you; I’ll send Morrigan here with it for you. And ask- ask Alex or your mum if they’ll stay with you … don’t go through a full moon alone. And you look after yourself - for me. I need you to look after yourself, because I can’t cope if you’re not and … I don’t know when I’m going to see you next, so you need to- you need to promise me, please.”

 

            “I promise,” Kara said, both of them crying freely again now, their faces swelling, sobs catching in their throats as they reached their goodbyes. “And you have to promise me too. You have to promise me you’ll look after yourself, and that … you’ll put yourself first. Above anyone else. If- if it gets too dangerous, you have to leave. You have to come back to me, okay? You come back at the first sign of danger.”

 

            “I promise.”

 

            Nodding, swallowing past the lump in her throat, Kara drew in a deep, shaky breath. The blood dripping from her broken nose was slowing now, and she sniffed, wincing, before she hesitated. Then she stepped in and pulled Lena into her arms, sobs escaping both of them as Lena buried her face in Kara’s neck and wept, Kara shaking as she cried quietly. Pulling back a moment later, Lena cupped Kara’s face in her hands, running her fingers over her cheeks, and then Kara leaned in and kissed Lena’s eyelids tenderly, leaving blood on them both, before she kissed her. Lena could taste the blood, copper and salt, coating her lips as she crushed them closer together, nothing passionate about it, only desperate and frightened. 

 

            Her chest was heaving when she let her go, her eyes flitting all over Kara’s face, drinking in the sight of her that she loved so dearly, while Kara was likewise committing her to memory. “I’ll miss you,” Kara whispered, her voice so soft and sad.

 

            “I love you, Kara. You’re my whole heart.”

 

            “I love you too.”

 

            Kara gave her one more kiss, gentle and lingering, before picking up her bag and moving towards the front door. Even though she said she’d leave first, she still faltered, hesitating on the threshold as she glanced back, blowing Lena a kiss as tears streamed down her cheeks, mingling with the blood, before she was gone, out into the darkness of night.

 

            A ragged sound of pain escaped Lena at that and she collapsed to the stone floor, like a puppet with all of its strings cut, burying her face in her hands as she sobbed and sobbed, exhausting herself quickly, already so drained. And then she pulled herself together, the creator of her own misery, and quickly started to tear apart the house, searching for it, looking for the one item she hadn’t looked for even once, not since it had been taken from her, not even when she’d needed it. And she’d needed Kara gone so she could look for it, twenty minutes of fruitless searching finally leading to her hand slapped against the stone wall, her palm stinging. Then it was her head, swearing as she smacked her brow bone against it, hard enough to split the skin, to bruise her orbital bone and make her eye swell shut. And again, the skin breaking at her hairline, bleeding freely from it. 

 

            And then, adrenaline pumping through her, the pain making her a little dizzy but quieting her thoughts some, Lena drew in a deep breath as she tried to stifle the pain in her chest, a pain that wasn’t quite physical but could’ve been mistaken so, she fetched her bag and the empty owl cage and stepped through the front door with a wave of her wand, plunging the cottage into darkness. She didn’t linger to look around the place one last time, knowing that the thing that had made it a home had left thirty minutes ago, just walked down the garden path and Apparated to Wicklow.

 

            Lena showed up at the front door of her childhood home a little after twelve-forty in the morning, unsteady on her feet as she pounded on the front door, waiting until Hope answered it, the little House Elf looking up at her with round eyes of surprise. Her voice was a stunned squeak as Lena staggered over the threshold with her little travel case in hand, packed with everything she’d need for the indefinite future. The noise of her arrival roused her mother, as she’d hoped, and Lillian appeared with a heavy brocade dressing gown pulled on over pyjamas, looking irate at the noise she presumed had come from the House Elf until she caught sight of her daughter.

 

            Blood was ribboning down Lena’s face, sewing her left eye closed, sliding over her lips, and she tasted the copper of it as she opened her mouth. Nothing came out, she just stood in the foyer of the cavernous manor house, staring up at her mum as Lillian slowly descended the stairs. The left side of Lena’s face was already starting to purple from where she’d broken her own cheekbone, and she looked shaky and unfocused, her skin deathly pale, although Lillian wasn’t to know that was purely from the fear of having to come back home.  

 

            Stopping in front of her, Lillian observed her daughter’s bloody and battered face with pale eyes as Lena stared at her face, drawing in shallow, hitching breaths as she waited for her to speak. Her throat felt so tight that she couldn’t imagine getting a word out. Even worse was the horrible sensation in her stomach as she met her mother’s gaze and saw no love for her there, watching as Lillian lifted her chin, looking down at her with her usual haughtiness.

 

            “What are you doing here?” was all her mother asked.

 

            “You asked where my loyalties lie,” Lena haltingly rasped. “It’s with my brother; I want to see him. I want to come home.”

 

            Fixing her with a flat look of mistrust, Lillian’s lips twitched at the corners with a faint smile, and she reached out, a slender finger pressing under Lena’s chin, urging her face up. Blood dripped off her jaw and Lena swallowed thickly, watching Lillian study the bruises, the swelling of her eye and cheek.

 

            “And how did this happen?”

 

            Lena had pins and needles in her face and hands and chest, and her voice quivered as she made herself lie, eyes stinging to lay the blame on the woman who’d only ever loved her gently. “I was attacked. By her.”

 

            “Well, well, a monster after all, is she? Although, I would have thought you’d be more capable of defending yourself.”

 

            Lillian’s smug smirk was almost more than Lena could stomach, seeing red for a moment as her vision dimmed, blood pounding in her head. Lips twitching slightly, Lena hummed at the back of her throat, the sound frayed and somewhat contemptuous. Her mother read it as if she hated to be proven wrong, which made Lena rankle all the more.

 

            “Well, you haven’t seen her ,” Lena stiffly murmured, a thin smile on her lips.

 

            Snapping her fingers, Lillian cast a dismissive look at Hope, oblivious to the way Lena’s heart leapt in her chest out of fright, and gestured to the travel case and bird cage still clutched tightly in Lena’s hands. “Take them up to her room.”

 

            Hope relieved Lena of her luggage and hurried to do her mistress’ bidding, while Lillian crooked a finger at Lena and moved towards the main drawing room. It was a large space, tall ceilinged and always chilly, even when a fire was burning in the wide hearth, Lena remembered. As she neared the open doors, she saw the orange glow of the fire, still burning this late, and stepped into the dimly lit room, pausing in the doorway as she watched a shadowed figure rise from a sofa. Pausing in her tracks, Lena felt a cold shiver creep up her spine as she took in the sight of her brother for the first time in fifteen years. 

 

            He was dressed in his old clothes, a row of black suits still hanging in his bedroom wardrobe, but it was ill-fitting, hanging off his thin frame as he stared at her, gaunt and wasted, cheeks hollow and his dark eyes sunken. His head had been freshly shaved and she could see a small nick on his throat where he’d cut himself trimming and cleaning up his beard. As old and sallow as he looked, he was still every inch of the brother she’d turned in, something hard and cruel about the set of his features as he smiled slowly, spreading his arms as he reached for her.

 

            “There she is! Look at you, you’ve grown up.”

 

            “Lex,” Lena murmured through numb lips, somewhat breathless as she stood rooted to the spot a moment longer before she could make herself move.

 

            It was the last thing she wanted to do, her body so cold, craving the arms of her girlfriend, not the touch of her brother. Yet, she made her feet move, hurrying forward and wrapping her arms tightly around him, her breaths quick and quiet as she breathed in the smell of him. It took her straight back to being a child, the familiar scent of his soap and cologne, nauseating as she drew in shallow lungfuls through her mouth, trying to dispel the panic that suffused her.

 

            A frayed laugh escaped her, slightly hysterical, and her brother took that as delighted surprise from his little sister, instead of the anxious edge of fear. She held onto him a moment later, the scar on her arm itching as she struggled to breathe, the pain pounding in her head, adrenaline keeping her moving, keeping her together as everything fell apart. Pulling away, she smiled, blood on her teeth, looking up into his dark eyes as she laughed again, low and husky this time.

 

            “I knew you’d come,” he said, firm but pleased as he gripped her arms.

 

            “Of course,” Lena rasped. “I’ve missed you.”

 

            It was a lie, but her brother had always been so narcissistic that he’d believed her to be the doting sister, even after everything she’d suffered at his hands. Even now, he never suspected that it was she who had turned him in, that she’d ever even considered doing such a thing. Even her mother, with all of her doubts, wouldn’t have thought Lena would have the nerve to do that, as young and meek as she’d been. Still, she knew that she would have to tread carefully around Lillian, would have to prove that whatever love was lost between mother and daughter, Lena felt differently about her brother. It was the main reason she knew she’d have to come home, put herself under her mother’s watchful gaze as she struck a dangerous balance between spy and dutiful daughter and sister.

 

            “Sit,” Lillian curtly ordered her a moment later, putting an end to the reunion as she gestured to the sofa.

 

            Lena crossed over to it and sat, her mother looming over her as she brusquely jerked Lena’s chin up to inspect her face. “I can do it-”

 

            Her insistence was cut off as her mother jabbed the tip of her wand into Lena’s cheek, eliciting a slight flinch, although Lena never made a noise. As Lillian murmured, Lena felt the relief of her cheekbone knitting back together, of the cuts to her hairline and brow closing up, the blood vanished and a bruise healing salve procured by Hope at Lillian’s instruction, smoothed over the swollen, black eye and left to work its magic. Lena sat with a wooden look on her face, back stiff and straight as she endured her mother’s healing, all too familiar to the times when she or Lex would break her fingers, her wrist, her nose in a temper and then leave Lillian to patch her up afterwards. It left a lump in her throat, and relief wound through her once Lillian finished.

 

            Her brother had moved over to the fire, a glass of Firewhiskey in hand as he braced against the mantle, his head lowered as he stared at the flames, and Lena itched for a drink as well, her face tingling, residual pain making her feel out of sorts. Clearing her throat, she softly thanked her mother and then pushed herself to her feet, taking everything in her to not collapse back down, before moving over to the unit with the crystal goblets and decanters of liquor. With a slightly shaking hand, Lena poured some for herself and then hesitated, pouring another glass for her mother before picking hers up and levitating the other one over to Lillian, who was observing her with shrewd wariness in her pale eyes.

 

            “Well,” Lena murmured, her eyes on the rug as she drifted back towards her family, goblet clutched tightly in her hand as she raised it a fraction. “To family.”

 

            Mother and son raised their glasses, her brother smiling, her mother’s eyes narrowed a fraction, and sipped their Firewhiskey. Lena knocked hers back in one mouthful, draining the contents of her goblet as it seared a path down her throat, warming her through as she tried to retain her composure. Licking her lips and pressing them into a flat line, Lena swallowed the honeyed taste of the Firewhiskey as she hesitated momentarily.

 

            “I think I’ll go to bed now.”

 

            “I’ll see you in the morning,” Lex nodded, moving over to her to cup the side of her head, smiling, before he took her empty goblet. “I’m glad you’re home.”

 

            Her lips twitched at the corners, eyes creasing at the corners, even though it was somewhat strained. “Me too.”

 

            She wasn’t tired, she just wanted a moment alone, to fall apart, to cry in privacy. It had been a long day and an even longer night, taking its physical and emotional toll on her, and Lena felt weariness dragging her shoulders down, pale-faced and defeated as she glanced at her mother, mumbling a goodnight before she drifted out of the living room in a daze.

 

            Walking through the foyer, towards the curved staircase, the marble and dark wood leaving little warmth to be found there, especially at night, Lena felt like she’d been transported back in time. She felt sixteen, thrust back into the midst of a war that she felt obligated to help with, shouldering the responsibility of so many people’s lives that it was unbearably heavy to even think about sitting by while something bad happened to them. And it all came back to her brother, the lynchpin of her plan, the common factor that would allow her to effectively spy.

 

            Slowly making her way upstairs, she followed the path to her childhood bedroom, pausing outside the closed door as she pressed a hand to the cold wood, a tightness in her chest as she waited a moment before opening it and crossing the threshold. Despite the years she’d been gone, it looked exactly the same as the day she’d packed her bags and left. Everything was neat and clean, the dark wooden furniture polished and the bed made up with clean sheets, courtesy of Hope and her housework duties. 

 

            The floorboards creaked under her shoes, shutting the door behind her as she moved further inside, until she hit the rug. Her clothes had already been put away in the empty cupboard, Morrigan’s cage on top of it with the little case, and Lena held it together long enough to open the doors and fetch pyjamas, undressing slowly, her fingers clumsy as she shed her clothes, leaving them scattered on the rug alongside her shoes. 

 

            Blowing all of the air out of her lungs, she paced in the middle of the room then, running a hand over her face, her hair, eyes stinging as she glanced up at the ceiling. Then she hunched over, covering her face with her hands as her breaths hitched in her throat, until she was standing in the middle of the room, crying, but trying not to cry as she breathed slowly, knowing that she couldn’t show any weakness in that house, her mother and brother just downstairs.

 

            It was hard not to, though, and Lena moved over to the bed, melting onto the dove grey quilt, pressing her face into it as she wept, trying to muffle the sound of it. She felt so wretched with guilt, crying as she hadn’t for years, until her throat was raw, until she had no more tears left to shed. Lena cried all night, red-eyed as she lay on her side, facing the windows as she eventually watched the sky lighten and the sun rise. And through it all, she felt a deep pain in her chest as she ached for Kara.

Chapter 51

            Kara arrived in a field on the outskirts of Inverness just before midnight, bleeding and heartbroken, nothing but her work briefcase and a knapsack with her as she staggered towards the hedgerow, stumbling on clumsy feet as the breaths caught in her chest. She could hardly see through her tears, making for the dark treeline beyond the field, where her sister’s warded cottage sat in a wooded area near the banks of the River Nairn. Climbing over a step stile overgrown with ivy, her boots sank into soft mud and grass, and she carried on, the night bitterly cold so far north, the noise of the small city absent on the fringes.

 

            It was a short walk from the field, and Kara banged on the door as she kept her sobs at bay, her chin wobbling as she shivered, shoulders stiff, and waited for someone to answer the door. It was a few minutes, a light coming on through the windows, footsteps on the stairs and fiddling with the locks, before her sister opened the door with her wand in hand, blinking herself awake with a hawkish look of annoyance on her face. Alex was quickly wide awake as she took in the sorry sight of her sister, though, a panicked sound of surprise escaping her as Kara dissolved into loud, gut-wrenching sobs again.

 

            She stumbled over the threshold, Alex reaching out to steady her, speaking, even though Kara couldn’t even hear her, head ducked down as her shoulders shook, while Alex brushed her hair out of her face, trying to get a better look at all of the blood she’d caught a glimpse of. Unable to even formulate a single word of explanation, loud sobs bursting out of her in frantic breaths, filling the silent house as Alex steered her into the living room, pushing her down onto a sofa. Her bags falling from her hands onto the carpet, Kara curled in on herself, face buried in her hands as she cried, Alex crouching in front of her, fingers encircling her sister’s wrists as she tried to pull her hands away.

 

            “It’s okay, it’s okay, let me see. Let me look,” Alex babbled, her pulse spiking from the panic that stole over her, woken in the middle of the night to her bloodied and bruised sister banging on her door, with no knowledge of what had happened to bring about those events.

 

            The blood had stopped dripping from her broken nose, but the constant stream of tears kept it from fully drying, red tears falling off Kara’s chin as Alex forced her hands down, eyes wide as she took in the mess of her sister’s face. Cupping one bloody cheek in her hand, Alex swallowed thickly as she took in the two black eyes, the slightly crooked set of Kara’s nose.

 

            “What happened?” Alex hoarsely asked, tipping Kara’s chin up a fraction, pale-faced as she tried to get an answer out of her sister.

 

            Kara just shook her head, trying to curl in on herself again, but Alex firmly held either side of her face, a little rough but frantic now. “What happened? Were you attacked?”

 

            Kelly was in the room then, rubbing sleep from her eyes, sucking in a sharp breath of shock as she turned on the lamp and took in the sight before her. Kara managed a nod as she drew in a shuddering breath, her lip wobbling as Alex blanched, asking her follow-up question.

 

            “Where’s Lena?”

 

            Letting out a choked sound, Kara shook her head. Jerking back, Alex opened and closed her mouth, speechless for a moment as her face paled with dread, quickly assuming the worst and then talking herself out of it. “No. No, no, no, she’s not- where is she? Was it her brother? Did he- did he take her?”

 

            Shaking her head again, Kara scrubbed her palm over her cheeks, letting out an agonised groan as she looked up at her sister, blue eyes aching as her shoulders went slack. “No, she-”

 

            Cutting off, Kara drew in a shuddering breath. She didn’t want to do it, she didn’t want to make people think badly of Lena, to think she was capable of hurting Kara, that she wasn’t on their side. But Kara knew that she had to, that it was necessary to keep her safe, that Lena couldn’t keep her cover if the people who’d been her friends and family for the last seven years didn’t cut her off, nothing but disgust and hatred left for her. Still, Kara faltered, just for a moment.

 

            Inhaling deeply, wiping her face as she gritted her teeth, Kara blinked rapidly as she tried to squash her feelings. It was an impossible task. “It was- it was Lena. She- we had a fight. ”

 

            Her voice broke again, throat closing up around any further explanation as the words hung heavily in the stunned silence. Alex just stared at her for a moment before she let out a strained laugh, her face crumpling with confusion as she knelt in front of Kara, a hand on her knee as she haltingly shook her head.

 

            “Wha- no. No, she didn’t. She wouldn’t ,” Alex stubbornly objected.

 

            Nodding, Kara swallowed thickly, wiping tears on the cuffs of her jumper as her face reddened from the shame of the lie. “She did. We- her brother …”

 

            Kelly was sinking onto the sofa beside Kara then, pressing tissues to her bleeding nose, urging her to tip her head back. Mumbling a thick thank you, the breaths still hitching in her chest as her eyes stung fiercely, Kara swallowed again, tasting copper at the back of her throat as she drew in shallow breaths. Frowning, Alex floundered for a moment, pushing herself up and sitting on the edge of the coffee table as she let the presumed truth of Kara’s words sink in. Running a hand through her hair, Alex’s mouth opened and closed as she struggled for a moment.

 

            “Well … what are you saying?”

 

            Kara was silent, closing her eyes as she allowed herself another second before she well and truly ripped up her whole life for the woman she loved. It didn’t feel that way, it didn’t feel as if she was doing something good, every part of her in pain, but they’d already gone too far for her to back out now, to risk putting Lena in danger all because she was too selfish to let her go. She let out a small whimper, hands cupping her brow as she hunched over, her face practically in her lap.

 

            “She’s … not on our side,” Kara lied, her voice strangled and breathless.

 

            The silence was deafening for another beat before Alex scoffed, on her feet now, running a hand over her face. “No,” she firmly objected after a moment, her face hard as she looked down at her sister. “No, I don’t believe that; she turned her brother in.”

 

            Kara scrambled for an excuse. “She- she said that was to … protect him. Keep him … out of the way.” 

 

            “But … we raided her house, they checked her arm; there was no Dark Mark. She’s- she’s no Death Eater.”

 

            It was laughable to Kara that after years of worrying about her sister’s opinion of Lena, something that had effectively driven a wedge between any chance of a relationship for so long, until she’d plucked up the courage regardless of what Alex would have thought, now it was a near-impossible task to convince her sister that Lena was everything Alex had assumed a Slytherin was. Kara had hoped the blood and bruises would do it, and it did, to an extent, but Alex was struggling to rationalise it, that the woman who’d become a part of her family, practically a second sister, who’d patched her up at St. Mungo’s for years , could be capable of hurting Kara like that.

 

            “I don’t- she’s not with-with us, but I’m not sure if she’s with them . But … she was too young,” Kara whispered. “She was still at school back then.”

 

            More tears fell, and Kara felt so angry, so devastated. She wanted to blame it all on someone, but there wasn’t anyone to blame, both of them knowing this was always a possibility, something that they’d agreed on together. Still, she had to blame it on Lex, Lena’s brother forcing their hand by escaping from Azkaban. If only he’d stayed exactly where his sister had helped put him, Kara might be crying over putting a ring on her girlfriend’s finger instead.

 

            “I don’t understand,” Kelly haltingly murmured, confused as she sat beside Kara, a hand pressed against her spine, meeting her wife’s gaze.

 

            Turning her head, Kara looked at her, mute and unblinking, her eyes bruised black and her pale face coated in dark blood. “Neither do I,” Kara whispered, fresh tears welling up.

 

            “Where is she?” Alex asked, a hard set to her jaw. 

 

            “Why?”

 

            “Because I want her to look me in the eye and tell me why.”

 

            Exhaling roughly, Kara cupped her forehead as she braced her elbow on her thigh. “Just … leave it.”

 

            “No, I want to know what the fuck is going on. You don’t just- you don’t wake up one day and attack your girlfriend and crawl back to the man you helped imprison. None of this- none of this makes sense.”

 

            “I don’t know what to tell you.”

 

            “Tell me where she is.”

 

            “No.”

 

            Aghast, Alex stared down at Kara with wide eyes. “Why are you protecting her?”

 

            More tears poured from Kara’s eyes, and she felt like they would never stop, wiping them away as she choked on a sobbing laugh. Shrugging, she removed the bloody tissues and sniffed, making her broken nose throb with pain. “I just- don’t hurt her, please. I’ve already … done things- she looked worse than I do-”

 

            “Good.”

 

            Giving her sister a withering look, Kara shook her head, the corners of her mouth twitching down as she cast her gaze down to her lap. “I don’t know where she went, um … and she doesn’t know where he is, it just- she’s not on our side and I just- I can’t switch it off like- like that, how I feel- I still love her so … it’s going to take some time for me to- so just leave it alone, please.”

 

            She was sobbing again, breathless gasps interrupting her words as she kept wiping and wiping tears away, her hands wet and bloody, the cuffs of her jumper damp. It wouldn’t have been believable for her to pretend that she didn’t love Lena, despite everything, that the presumed attack would erase a seven-year relationship, and years of history and friendship before that too. It was easy to play the devastated ex; that’s exactly what she was.

 

            Alex was silent for a moment, her mouth a flat line, before she reluctantly nodded. Relief flooded through Kara, although she tried not to show it, wiping at her cheeks, sniffing as she looked down at her shaking hands, fingers wet and red as her tears made the dried blood run. With a sigh, raking a hand through her hair, Alex stepped towards Kara, reaching out to rest a comforting hand on her shoulder, squeezing gently in encouragement.

 

            “Come on, come into the kitchen and let me look at your nose.”
