            “Don’t go anywhere. Just in case there’s a response,” Moody told her as he made for the front door, his eye roving around as he took the letter and pocketed it, his scarred face leaving his expression unreadable. 

 

            “I’m on watch tonight.”

 

            He paused, scratched his chin and hummed, shaking his head. “Still best if you sit tight until I get back.”

 

            Nodding, running a shaky hand over her face, Kara watched him leave, the door shutting behind him before she walked back down to the kitchen and sank onto a chair at the table, white-faced and on edge. Kelly stood and moved over to the sink, fetching a clean glass and filling it with water, before she walked over to her sister-in-law and sank to a crouch at her side, looking at her with concerned dark eyes.

 

            “Are you alright?”

 

            “I’m okay,” Kara reassured her, thanking her for the water and taking a sip.

 

            The whole time, her stomach was in knots. She was ignorant of the contents of the letter, but it was clearly important for Lena to have sent her a red alert in the middle of the night, and she wondered if she was safe, if she’d risked her life to get that letter to them. And on top of that, leaving her post at the Department of Mysteries, the night after Nia had a dream about Death Eaters there, made Kara feel anxious, dread filling her as her heart hammered. She couldn’t mention the letter picked up from Lena, but she could bring up Nia, wondering what had come of that.

 

            “Do you know if Nia spoke to Dumbledore?”

 

            “Nia? I don’t know, I only got here an hour ago. Why?”

 

            “She came to pass on a message,” Sirius evasively confirmed.

 

            “Why?” Kelly pressed, still looking at Kara.

 

            “She … she had a funny dream. Um … Death Eaters, at the Ministry. In the Hall of Prophecy.” Taking another sip of water, Kara met Kelly’s gaze and grimaced. “She’s had dreams like that before. Dreams that have come true.”

 

            “Did she say when?”

 

            “No, it’s not … specific.”

 

            “You’re supposed to be on watch tonight,” Winn noted.

 

            Closing her eyes, Kara rubbed her brow, letting out a soft sigh. “Yeah, I- there was something more important I had to report to Dumbledore.”

 

            “Is someone else there?”

 

            “No. I’ll head back when Moody comes back. He told me to wait.” There was a beat of silence, a few glances exchanged, and Kara looked around at them all, frowning slightly as she understood their unspoken concern. “This isn’t a setup. If Nia’s dream is right, they can’t have planned it around me leaving the place unguarded. My information is good, it’s solid . ”

 

            “You’re sure?” Winn asked.

 

            Nodding, very firm in her belief that this wasn’t some ploy by Lena to get her out of there - Lena wouldn’t have even known she was on guard duty to start with - Kara’s face was stubbornly set. “Yes. Besides, they’d just attack anyway. I mean, look at Arthur. They’re quite brazen about attacking or using anyone they can; I wouldn’t have been too difficult to overpower.”

 

            “Mm, you’re right about that,” Kelly murmured, standing and folding her arms over her chest. “Something seems off about it all, though.”

 

            “Something’s off about everything these days,” Mike grumbled from where he leaned against the wall, raising a bottle of beer to his lips and taking a thoughtful swig.

 

            Checking her watch, Kara saw that it was twelve-twenty now, the minutes flying by as she waited for a response. They all sat in silence as the fire crackled, all discussion cut off as the other sipped at their drink of choice, and it was another five minutes before the front door opened and footsteps descended. It was Moody, quickly descending the stairs with his heavy-footed prosthetic, and his voice was an urgent, almost indecipherable growl as he corralled them all into action.

 

            “Everyone up! Dumbledore’s called it in; fetch anyone you can and get to the Ministry as quickly as you can. We’ll meet outside Scotland Yard. Don’t want to tip the bastards off before we even get inside. No one enters until we’re situated. Understood?”

 

            There was a flurry of movement as everyone immediately started to move, drinks drained, a last mouthful of alcohol to bolster them. Winn said he’d fetch James, Mike going for Querl, and Nia by extension of that, and Kelly was intent on getting word to Alex, who was on a stakeout with J’onn. Moody assured her he’d notify his Aurors, and she left with Kara instead, stepping outside and taking the werewolf’s hand, Apparating them to Whitehall.

 

            Slinking into the deep shadows across the street from Scotland Yard, they clutched their wands in their hands as their eyes darted about. Drawing deeper into an alleyway, trying to be quiet, skirting around puddles as they drew further away, Kelly touched Kara’s arm to bring her to a stop, and they leaned against opposite walls of the alleyway, their dark cloak and coat helping them blend in with the dark.

 

            “You alright?” Kelly whispered.

 

            “Fine.”

 

            “It’ll be fine.”

 

            “If Nia’s dream is right, if Dumbledore is calling us in … it’s not going to be fine.”

 

            “What information did you have?”

 

            “I don’t know,” Kara muttered, rubbing her eyes as she nudged up her glasses. “It was a letter.”

 

            “From whom?”

 

            Shrugging, her brows drawing together in a frown, Kara idly twirled her wand in her fingers. “I don’t know. He has me ferrying messages from an anonymous source; I’ve never met them, we just have a drop point. Guess it’s safer that way, in case one of us is caught.”

 

            Nodding, Kelly’s mouth thinned at the corners. “Smart man, Dumbledore.”

 

            “Mm.”

 

            The faint sound of someone Apparating killed any further talk, and they both crept back towards the mouth of the alleyway, taking in a shadowed figure aimlessly looking around, as if they were lost. Tightening her grip on her wand, Kara nodded at Kelly, who kicked an empty beer can, the sound loud in the quiet of the night. The person whirled around, wand arm raised, and warily approached as Kelly quietly drew back, while Kara sank to a crouch at the base of the wall, the deep black of the alleyway hiding her as the person approached. 

 

            As footsteps slowly passed her hiding spot, Kara leapt up, a fistful of fabric in her grasp as she pressed the person against the rough brick wall, wand under their chin, while Kelly bore down on them with a lit wand. The light illuminated the pale face of Winn, whose expression went slack with relief at the sight of familiar faces. Kelly killed the light as the three of them let the tension bleed out of them slightly, although they were still on edge.

 

            “Are they coming?”

 

            “James is fetching Lucy,” Winn confirmed.

 

            Nodding, Kelly gestured him further down the alleyway and crept closer to the mouth again. Mike showed up next with Querl and Nia, the three of them joining the trio wedged in the alleyway as Kelly set off a gust of wind to catch their attention. Across the street, Tonks and Shacklebolt lurked in the alcove of Scotland Yard, and they all started to spread out as more and more of the Order arrived. Sirius arrived not long after, arguing quite animatedly with Moody and Lupin down the end of the street, until they were silenced by a warning hiss from Shacklebolt. Alex was one of the last to arrive, appearing with J’onn and glancing about. 

 

            “Alright, move off, you lot,” Moody ordered them, his voice carrying down the street.

 

            Alex singled Kara and Kelly out and briskly crossed over to join them, her hand finding her wife’s, squeezing encouragingly. There was a lump in Kara’s throat, and she could feel her sister’s confusion; she knew Kara should’ve been on Level 9, tucked away in the very hall they were now intent on descending upon.

 

            They all made their way towards the Treasury, the toilets on Whitehall providing access to the Ministry, and flushed themselves inside in quick succession, the Aurors entering first to sweep the Atrium. Stepping out of the fireplace, Kara felt a prickle of unease steal over her at the number of people inside the Ministry so late in the night, or rather so early in the morning, and they all made their way towards the bank of lifts, piling into them and making their way down a level, a few who couldn’t fit taking the flight of stairs down. Spilling out into the dark hallway, they all shuffled forward, and Moody’s voice drifted back towards Kara in a low growl.

 

            “Danvers, you’re up.”

 

            She didn’t have to wonder if he meant her sister, just started pushing her way through the throng of witches and wizards. Slipping out to the front, she gripped her wand tightly and made for the entrance to the Department of Mysteries. Taking a deep breath to steel herself, feeling the ripple of activity behind her as everyone else readied their wands, the ranks of them close together, tensed and ready to rush in, Kara eased the door open and stepped into the Entrance Chamber. The walls and doors stayed put, and they spilt into the room behind her as she strode for the Time Room.

 

            “You stay here,” Moody instructed her. “Keep it steady. The rest of you, fan out.”

 

            Doing as she was instructed, Kara pressed up against the wall, giving her a good view of the entire chamber, in case anyone came in or out, watching as the other fourteen Order members trickled through various doors. It didn’t take long for the door to the Time Room to burst open, a shout of warning preceding the few who’d gone to the Hall of Prophecy, alerting her to the presence of Death Eaters, and the news that they’d destroyed the stacks of orbs. Gobsmacked, Kara floundered for a moment, unsure whether she should stay put any longer, watching as Moody limped with urgency to the centre of the room.

 

            “Keep looking,” he barked to those following him out. “Danvers, you keep track of which rooms we’ve cleared.”

 

            Nodding, Kara mentally checked off the Time Room, and when Nia, James and Remus traipsed out of the Space Room, she checked that off too. Watching as everyone streaked in and out of rooms, going from door to door in the circular Entrance Chamber, Kara mentally tallied them until she watched her sister enter the Death Room. No one had come out of that one yet, and when Alex opened the door, the sounds of shouting, of hexes being cast, and the flickering light of spells drifted out. Watching her sister plunge headfirst into danger, Kara didn’t linger to keep track of which rooms had been cleared, she went with her.

 

            All Kara could think about was the archway. She’d spent her fair share of time in the Death Room, reading old research articles by Unspeakables who had come before her and assisting with current projects, so she knew what was said about that veil on the dais; anything that went through it didn’t come back out. It was a true death, that much she was sure of, except her sister didn’t know, and her sister always ran headfirst into trouble, thinking she could hex and curse her way out of it. While somewhat similar in her approach, Kara was more rational, less impulsive, so she had time to think about the danger she was rushing into before she continued to rush into it. Her mother might kill them both if she ever found out.

 

            Inside the Death Room, standing at the top of the tiers mirroring an amphitheatre, Kara’s eyes went wide with shock at the sight. Order members and Death Eaters duelled, and what seemed to be a few teenagers as well. Sparing the briefest second for how they’d gotten there and who they were, Kara lurched after her sister, scrambling down two tiers to grab Alex’s arm, yanking her back. Trying to pull herself free, angry and slightly panicked as she turned around, wand raised, as if expecting a Death Eater, Alex frowned, confused.

 

            “The veil!” Kara shouted over the noise, pointing to the middle of the room, far below them and ominous in appearance. “Stay away from the veil!”

 

            Curtly nodding, Alex pulled her arm free and dashed off, Kara quick to follow. There seemed to be just over a dozen Death Eaters, and the Order members who’d already congregated in the Death Room, coupled with the teenagers present, almost evenly matched them. Still, more of the Order were spilling in as they came out of other rooms, experiencing the disorienting moving Entrance Chamber without Kara there to steady it, and then staggering into the Death Room to assist. Some of them looked a little worse for wear, but she barely noticed, throwing herself into the thick of the fighting, dodging a Stinging Curse, stunning a masked man and watching him drop to the stone floor.

 

            Ducking behind the base of the dais, Kara breathed heavily for a few moments before she popped back up and caught sight of Kelly on the dais, being driven backwards towards the veil as she duelled two Death Eaters. Stomach lurching, watching her sister-in-law step back, deflecting the spells but getting far too close to the archway, to that eerie veil that Kara heard whispers from, she levelled her wand at Kelly and blasted her out of the way, watching her go flying off the dais, across the other side of the room. Wincing, hoping she was okay, Kara shot a disarming spell at one of the Death Eaters and ducked, a chunk of stone blown out of the dais right above her head, where she’d been standing.

 

            Crouching, she circled around the base of the dais, watching one of the teenagers, a mousy boy with wide, fearful eyes, try to fight off a woman with dark, wild hair. Catching her in the back, sending her stumbling forward, Kara staggered to her feet and watched the witch turn around, a manic look in her eyes, before a man with long dark hair intercepted her. Sirius. Leaving them to it, recognising the woman as his cousin, Bellatrix Lestrange, Kara moved off in search of another target. 

 

            She almost didn’t recognise him at first. She’d seen photos of him when he’d been arrested, articles in the Prophet about the trial, more from his sentencing, but he was older now, his face harsher, a neat beard covering his cheeks and jaw, and her stomach dropped as she realised the man with the cruel twist to his features, busy duelling J’onn, was Lex Luthor. And he was Lena’s source, the reason they were apart, and so she had to try to incapacitate him. If the Aurors could take him into custody and send him back to Azkaban, Lena would be safe, Lena could come home. Skidding to a stop at J’onn’s side, Kara lashed out with a disarming spell, watching Lex block it with a Shield Charm, his dark gaze flitting to her as he adjusted his stance, duelling them both with his borrowed wand.

 

            Sweating by that point, her palm slick as she clutched her wand, heart racing a mile a minute, Kara cast spell after spell, hexes, curses and charms hurled in rapid succession, and she felt her frustration grow as Lex shielded and deflected. They had him on the backfoot, though, his reactions getting slower as she and J’onn kept their assault up, and she doggedly wore away at him as she likewise tired. Except, then another Death Eater caught J’onn in the shoulder, dislocating it as his left arm hung limply, and he turned to engage that attacker, leaving Kara to fend for herself.

 

            A good dueller, she held her own, a minute, two, five, longer. She could see sweat on Lex’s brow, his eyes dark and the twist of his mouth contemptuous as they exchanged blows, ducking and dodging, shielding and deflecting, the amphitheatre getting blasted apart as spells struck the stone tiers. Dust filled the air, making it harder to see, and the room was already dim enough, making it easy for both sides to lose track of each other. Kara had been struck by chips of stone, and the dust made her eyes smart, but she fought on until he got past her guard.

 

            Fortunately, he’d only sent a blasting charm at her, and she half-managed to block it, but the force still sent her flying backwards. Crumpling to the stone floor, Kara tasted blood, blinking back dark spots as she wheezed, feeling the grit of stone under her hands as she took a moment to shake off her dizziness and climb to her feet. He’d turned his back on her almost immediately, a job done, and as she swayed slightly, Kara sent a slashing spell his way, cutting up his leg as Lex stumbled, the dark fabric of his pants shredding. He’d once taught Lena Sectumsempra , and while that had been the cause of much strife in their relationship, once upon a time, she was glad for it then, watching him hobble to the bottom tier to lean against it, his face darkening with anger, wrenched by pain. She knew it would be bleeding, badly, and she felt a flicker of triumph.

 

            Aiming to stun him, she was interrupted by the arrival of Dumbledore. He seemed to glow, radiating power as he swept down the tiers, performing magic the likes Kara had never seen. The Death Eaters scattered like rats, and she cursed as she watched one of them grab Lex, Disapparating before she could send a stunning spell their way. Only a couple got away, though, the rest of them already stunned on the floor, a few still mid-duel, and Bellatrix Lestrange fleeing as she laughed maniacally. Kara watched a teenage boy with dark hair chase after her, and frowned as she leaned against the base of the dais, a hand to her ribs as she breathed raggedly, feeling as if perhaps she’d broken something when she landed, she watched the fighting peter out and blinked at the sight of her sister in front of her.

 

            Alex was sporting a few cuts on her face and a few smudges of dust, the sleeve of her leather duster torn at the shoulder seam, and a look of relief on her face as she clapped Kara on the shoulder. Kelly was behind her with a split lip, favouring her left leg as she gingerly put her weight on her right ankle, which was possibly sprained, and Kara wondered if that had been her doing. Still, all three of them were mostly unharmed, and Kara braced her hands on her hips, blowing the air out of her cheeks as she winced at the state of the room, while Alex tapped out a cigarette and lit it, purple smoke shrouding her.

 

            “Croaker’s going to have a fit,” Kara stated, nudging her glasses further up her nose, eyes darting around. “Is everyone accounted for?”

 

            Alex tensed slightly, lowering her cigarette and grimacing, a shadow of grief passing her face before she shook her head slightly. “Sirius. He- he fell through the veil.”

 

            Blanching, Kara’s eyebrows rose a fraction in surprise, and she blinked, nodding as she processed that. “Right.”

 

            “Is it- is it permanent? I mean, has anyone ever … come back?”

 

            “No,” Kara sighed. “No, it’s- this is the Death Room. Anyone who goes through it … well, there’s no coming back from death, is there? That’s what we’re researching here in the first place.” 

 

            “Right,” Alex muttered. “Shame. Um … I’d better go help take them into custody.” 

 

            Nodding, rubbing the bridge of her nose, Kara swallowed thickly. Her sister kissed Kelly and then went to assist the other Aurors, while the other Order members dispersed, a few of them helping to shepherd the teenagers out of the room, and Kara noticed a few of the other members were injured too. Nothing too bad, but they’d need healing, and they couldn’t go to St. Mungo’s for it without tipping off anyone at the hospital sympathetic to Voldemort, namely Lillian Luthor, that they’d been in a fight. She had no doubt that word of this would spread.

 

            As they all trekked back through the Entrance Chamber, Winn vomiting at the vertigo of the spinning walls, until Kara stepped out and made it stop, she was the last to leave, Tonks and J’onn sweeping each room and ensuring no one was left behind before they preceded her out of the Department of Mysteries. Riding the lift up, Kara felt gritty-eyed and exhausted, flagging slightly as she leaned back against the wall of the lift, the ride up a level so short that she barely got a reprieve from making her body move before they were walking out. Walking towards the main area of the Atrium, Kara’s mouth fell open at the state of the place. 

 

            It was a complete wreck, and she watched as Ministry officials started spilling in, Fudge at the forefront, ashen-faced in his pyjamas as he kept repeating the same thing over and over again. It didn’t take very long for Kara to realise what had transpired, with Dumbledore there, and the dark-haired boy she’d seen chase after Bellatrix familiar from his photos in The Daily Prophet. Word would no doubt spread within the hour that Lord Voldemort himself had been present at the Ministry of Magic and fought Dumbledore, before fleeing, but not before he’d been sighted by enough Ministry officials for it to be undisputed. She supposed that was truly the moment the Second Wizarding War began.

 

            As Order members started to Disapparate before they could be identified, Kara felt the ring on her finger burn, letting out a surprised hiss as she looked down and saw that it was red again. Swallowing thickly, she glanced up at the scene in the Atrium, the aftermath rather anticlimactic as a reporter appeared, the camera flash of a photographer lighting up the place, non-Order member Aurors conversing with Order member Aurors as they explained the eleven Death Eaters in custody in cells on Level 2, while the Minister for Magic’s support staff all spoke over each other in raised voices. Her presence wouldn’t be missed, not for some time, if at all, and Kara closed her eyes, Disapparating from the Ministry as she felt a deep ache in her chest. She hoped she was right.

 

            The faint glow of firelight seeped through the windows of the cottage as she walked up the garden path, and she forgot all about her aches and pains as she apprehensively opened the front door and crossed the threshold, as a chair scraped over the stone of the kitchen floor. She barely had time to shut the door behind her before she was almost knocked back into it by Lena engulfing her in a tight hug, getting her arms around her for the briefest moment before she pulled back, hands shaking terribly as she cupped Kara’s face in her hands, tilting it this way and that, giving her a bruising kiss and then letting out a choked sound of raw relief.

 

            “Are you okay? Are you hurt?”

 

            “Come here,” Kara whispered, weak in the knees as she pulled Lena towards her, holding onto her, not letting her go so easily this time.

 

            Breathing in the smell of her, feeling the shape of her body in her arms, the rise and fall of her chest, Kara drew in a hitching sob of a breath, her eyes stinging fiercely. She’d hoped when the ring turned red for the second time in under three hours that this one might be a misuse of its purpose, and she didn’t know how badly she’d needed it to be just that until she had Lena in her arms. Clutching her tightly, Kara closed her eyes and swallowed the lump in her throat, her jaw working as she tried her hardest not to cry.

 

            Lena held her waist, her hands gripping Kara so tightly that she thought they might leave marks, but it still wasn’t hard enough. Feeling a pain in her chest, Kara managed to make herself pull away, if only for the pleasure of looking at her. Looking even more tired than last time she’d seen her, more than two and a half months ago now, Lena’s expression was pinched with worry, and a wavering smile crossed Kara’s face as she raised a dusty hand and trailed a fingertip along the lines of Lena’s face, her eyes, her mouth, her chin and cheeks.

 

            “Tell me you’re not hurt,” Lena demanded, her voice strained and wobbling, green eyes bright with what might’ve been a film of tears.

 

            Cupping her face in a dirty hand, Kara sniffed and gave her a brave smile. “I’m okay. Just … bruises maybe. A cracked rib. I’m- it’s nothing. Your brother-”

 

            “My brother?” Lena hoarsely echoed, her gaze hardening, hatred surfacing so easily.

 

            “I duelled him,” Kara admitted. “I thought- well, most of the others are heading to Azkaban. I’d hoped he’d be joining them again. He would’ve if I’d had anything to say about it. But he gave me a good bollocking before he escaped.”

 

            She weakly laughed, pressing a hand to her ribs. Lena was white-faced with fear, letting out a soft hiss as she shook her head. “You stupid, stupid woman,” she scolded her, running a hand over Kara’s dishevelled and dusty hair, giving her another hard kiss. “Don’t do that, okay? He’s not your fight.”

 

            “I just- I wanted you to come home,” Kara tearfully confessed, her eyes swimming with tears all of a sudden, her throat closing up.

 

            “I know, darling,” Lena murmured, swallowing painfully as she gave her an aching look. “I dream about that every night. Nothing’s right without you.”

 

            Drawing in a hitching breath, Kara closed her eyes, trying to pull herself together, the events of the night, which had been exceedingly long and tiring, leaving her knackered but brimming with so many emotions. Adrenaline still coursed through her, slowly waning as the danger passed, but it did funny things to her emotions, and she felt so sad , so heartbroken to know that he’d slipped right through her fingers. And she had Lena here, in front of her, beneath her touch, but it wasn’t forever.

 

            “How long do we have?”

 

            Lena hesitated, her gaze softening, a faint smile at the corners of her mouth as she reached up to gently smooth her thumb over Kara’s grazed cheek, the shallow cuts healing up instantly. “We have a little time. Let me get a good look at you.”

 

            She was in her Healer green robes, which meant her family expected her to be at the hospital, working hard, and Kara was grateful for the time that bought them. Lena led her over to the sofa, removing the white dust sheet draped over it, and Kara sat, the warmth of the lit fire washing over her as Lena made her take off her robe, and then loosen her tie and undo her shirt. The right side of Kara’s back was already mottling a nasty shade, and Lena’s cool, probing fingers gently confirmed a fracture, easily fixed with a bit of wandwork, but other than a few more nicks and grazes, Kara’s was fine. Her grey-dusted hair seemed a little more grey with the fine powder of pulverised stone, and her exposed skin was covered in a layer of it too, but that was easily washed away in the kitchen sink as she scooped a handful of water to her mouth and dried her hands off.

 

            Lena hovered in the open space between the kitchen and living room, watching Kara with anxious eyes, and there was so much left unsaid, so much that they didn’t dare speak, everything on hold for now. Setting the tea towel down, Kara turned around, still shirtless, her back still bruised, waiting for a salve that she’d have to apply back at Eliza’s, and her blue eyes softened with tenderness, weary shoulders slumping. It was two-thirty by her watch, and she wished for nothing more than to go upstairs to their bed and fall asleep with Lena in her arms.

 

            “Was there a warning in your letter?” Kara asked her as she moved away from the sink, drawn back over to her.

 

            “Yes. It was quite late when I found out he was leaving. I had to pretend I was called into work so I could get the message here; my mother’s watching me like a hawk. She’s at St. Mungo’s now, but I told an Intern I was going to lie down and they’d better not wake me unless somebody’s dying, so we have time.”

 

            “Not enough.”

 

            “No, not enough,” Lena bitterly agreed, her mouth turning down slightly at the corners. Kara chuckled and reached up to tweak her chin, giving her a soft kiss. “What happened?”

 

            Taking her hand, Kara drew her back into the living room, and they sat on the sofa together, Lena pulled into her side, Kara’s cheek pressed to the top of her head, and she recounted the events of the day before, starting with Nia’s dream, through her disrupted watch to fetch the letter Lena had left, all the way through to right before she left the Ministry. Lena listened without interrupting, and then she asked some follow up questions, and Kara answered them as best as she could, and they talked until almost three o’clock, before they fell silent, Lena’s legs across Kara’s lap, cuddled into her, Kara’s arms around her, and fell asleep without even meaning to.

 

            It was still dark, although there was a faint lightening of the sky through the cottage windows, when Kara was gently shaken awake. Blinking owlishly, her glasses crooked on her face and a stiffness to her joints, Kara rubbed her tired eyes as she realised where she was, who was speaking to her in hushed tones.

 

            “Kara? I have to go. I have to go, okay? I’m sorry. I love you,” Lena was softly speaking, looming over her, fastening her Healer robe over her scrubs as she leaned down to kiss her.

 

            Her hand came up to cup Kara’s chin, the kiss sweet and lingering, and Kara melted into it, her eyes closing as she cherished it, prolonging it a second longer as she chased after Lena’s retreating lips, before she caught her hand as she straightened up, kissing her palm, Lena’s fingers cool in her grasp. Staring up at her, Kara’s stomach sank as she felt the ache of missing her fill her chest before she’d even walked out the door. Climbing to her feet, Kara ran a hand through her tousled hair and followed Lena to the door, opening it to the pre-dawn darkness as the cold night air raced in, and she kissed her again, indulging herself while she could, not knowing when she’d next see her. It felt like heartbreak all over again.

 

            “I love you,” Kara murmured, her voice thick with sleep, reaching up to tuck a lock of dark hair behind Lena’s ear. “Stay safe, my love. And come back to me soon.”

 

            “I promise,” Lena whispered, stepping outside and then hesitating, before she blew her a kiss, and Disapparated with a sad look in her eyes.

Chapter 57

            Despite the battle at the Department of Mysteries, Kara continued to go to work. Those first few days were horrendous, the destruction so bad that it took them a week to catalogue all of the damage to each Chamber, the entirety of the Hall of Prophecy reduced to nothing but smashed orbs and empty shelves, which had all been knocked over, many of the clocks splintered and broken, and the Ministry’s full inventory of Time-Turners destroyed. That wasn’t including the fragile, experimental magic that had been tampered with in some of the other rooms, or the stone amphitheatre in the Death Room, which had been blasted apart. Not to mention that a fellow Unspeakable, Augustus Rookwood, was one of the Death Eaters arrested at the battle, something of a shock to Kara, although she’d never been particularly fond of the man, and there were all sorts of rumours spread throughout the Department as Croaker broke the news. As one of the Senior Unspeakables, Kara was privy to her boss’ worries about the state of things, the security of the place now, and his opinion that he was getting too old to deal with these sorts of things. Still, the mess was cleaned up, a few Unspeakables stopped showing up for work, and the rest of them made do.

 

            There wasn’t really much else they could do. They all had bills to pay, and this new development, which Kara had already been in the thick of for six months and on the fringes of for half a year before that, too, didn’t change much for most of the Wizarding World. Of course, now there was indisputable proof of Voldemort’s return, which couldn’t be denied anymore, but the day-to-day runnings of things hadn’t been so disrupted that most ordinary witches and wizards were ready to pack in their jobs and flee just yet. Kara wished that she could, that she could grab Lena and take her to Paris, relying on Lena’s excellent French and her passable ability while they waited it out in relative safety. But last time, the war had been a slowly forming thing over years, and if it repeated that this time, in this new budding war, it was a long time to hide away somewhere, and who knew how far his reach would spread this time.

 

            Already, Kara knew of Voldemort’s influence reaching Minsk, where giants lived in the remote mountain regions. Hagrid had returned unsuccessful in his plight to gain the friendship of the tribe there, and they’d had to concede the loss of powerful allies to the Death Eaters who’d been courting them too. Still, it was a bitter blow that struck a little too close to home a few weeks into the early days of the Second Wizarding War, when giants were responsible for an attack in the West Country, primarily targeting Muggles, and explained as merely a hurricane by the Ministry. Fortunately, Falmouth was left unscathed, but Kara heard it from Alex, who’d been dispatched to help protect the Muggles, that the destruction left in their wake had been shocking and had missed them by merely a dozen miles. 

 

            And despite everyone’s belief that things could go on as normal, the Second Wizarding War developed far quicker than the first. It was almost as if Voldemort was making up for lost time, picking up right where he’d left off last time, but in that first month, it was a slog of bad news after bad news. First, word had come that Voldemort had demanded Fudge step down as Minister for Magic, resulting in two fatal attacks on both the Brockdale and Millennium Bridges, primarily targeting Muggles again, and the subsequent resignation of Fudge and the instatement of their new Minister, Rufus Scrimgeour. Following that were the attacks on Diagon Alley and the disappearances of Florean Fortescue and Mr Ollivander. On her last visit there, Kara had seen the destruction of the ice cream parlour she’d frequented when she’d lived at The Leaky Cauldron , and the locked-up shop of Ollivanders, which presented a bigger mystery, as it showed no signs of a struggle, as if the old wandmaker had merely closed up and left. 

 

            A little more personal was the news towards the middle of July that Emmeline Vance had been killed. Losing two Order members back-to-back so quickly was a shock to them all, and as many of them as possible had crammed into Grimmauld Place two Saturdays in a row to raise a glass to Sirius and Emmeline, a despairing edge of desperation to the cramped kitchen as they all silently wondered which one of them would be next. Already, their numbers had started to fall, and Kara was filled with dread as things started to feel very real. Every day, she woke with a heaviness in her chest, worrying for Lena, for Alex and Kelly, the rest of her friends. The only person she was relatively assured of being safe was Eliza, who worked from the back garden and the kitchen, and could mail her products to the various apothecaries she sold to. So far, she’d fought her daughter on going that far, but Kara pestered her about it every morning as she ate breakfast before heading to work. 

 

            In a sense, she was putting herself in more danger than her mother was, now a known Order member to the Death Eaters present at the battle of the Department of Mysteries, but Kara had nothing else to do but go to work. As July bled into August and into September, she endured the full moon as St. Mungo’s, wondering whether it was a good idea to allow herself to be locked inside a cell for the night but feeling fairly confident that even the most hardened Death Eater wouldn’t want to open the doors to a fully transformed werewolf on a full moon. She grew paranoid, more observant of her surroundings as a precaution, but nothing happened, each day much like the one before, but she never let her guard down, not thinking for an instant that it was luck, that she might’ve gone unidentified as an Order member. It was just shy of her thirty-fourth birthday, towards the middle of September, when they eventually came for her.

 

            Since there was no need to guard the Hall of Prophecy anymore, and with the general air of unease and fear spreading, Kara no longer worked late, wrapping up her work with the rest of the Department and heading home. It wasn’t that the Ministry wasn’t safe, no further incidents since the battle on her floor, but people were paranoid, and the news printed in The Daily Prophet grew bleaker by the day. A lot of the time, Kara went straight to Grimmauld Place, still in use by the Order, and threw herself into more danger than would’ve transpired from sitting at her desk to fit in some extra paperwork, and her mother’s relief was palpable whenever she walked through the door. Eliza waited up every night, no matter how late it was, asking after Alex and Kelly as well, the lines of her face deepening with worry for her family. Leaving work, much as she had every night for weeks now, she intended to go to Grimmauld Place and see if there was anything for her to do to pass her evening, so she didn’t have to be alone with her loneliness, but she knew that something was within the first minute she stepped out of the Department of Mysteries and into the dark hallway.

 

            Walking to the lift, she called it down from the Atrium, the floor above, and it arrived a moment later with someone already inside. She recognised the woman as Siobhan Smythe, a secretary to Fudge from up on Level 1, and Kara didn’t question why she was coming down to Level 9, assuming that the woman would be taking the stairs down to the Courtrooms on Level 10. Instead, as the grille slid across, Siobhan stayed firmly inside the lift, making Kara momentarily hesitate, confused, before she stepped into the lift and pushed the button for the Atrium. None of the other buttons were pushed, which was even more bewildering, and Kara tucked herself into the corner of the lift as she went up a level, the trip brief and ordinary. When she stepped out, she heard the other woman follow her out and caught sight of a man with a visitor’s badge pinned to his chest looking at her. Stomach swooping as unease filled her, Kara avoided looking at him directly, but was aware of him peeling away from his position against the wall, falling into step level with Siobhan, although the two of them stayed ten feet apart, as if it was coincidental.

 

            Keeping her pace leisurely, Kara quickly ran through her options. She knew she’d been made, and there weren’t any familiar faces in the Atrium for her to cleave to, so she kept walking, as if nothing was amiss. They didn’t seem to realise that she’d made them as well, and Kara made for the bank of fireplaces to exit the Ministry, thinking quickly. Going to Grimmauld Place or home would only give up their secret locations if either of these two grabbed onto her robe and came with her, so after a split-second, Kara decided to take the exit into London, coming out into Whitehall, the dreary early evening greeting her with a drizzle of rain. Muggles rushed past with ducked heads and umbrellas, and Kara increased her pace, not looking behind her to see if they’d followed after her, just making for nearby Scotland Yard and that alleyway she’d hidden in with Kelly.

 

            It wasn’t quite so effective in the late afternoon grey, but she pressed up flat against the wall, hoping she was unnoticeable in the shadows as she shuffled further into the alleyway. Once she’d gone far enough, Kara sank to a crouch, the hem of her robe settling in the puddle spreading from a blocked drainpipe, and her wand gripped in a sweaty hand as she peered at the mouth of the alleyway. The rectangle of grey light was narrow, but she caught sight of two figures in robes prowling past, silent but moving in tandem, their eyes scanning the street as a few Muggles in suits, bike messengers, and tracksuits walked by, oblivious. They didn’t see her hidden in the alleyway, and Kara felt a wash of relief, but she didn’t move for a few minutes, not so careless as to think they’d moved on so easily.

 

            She was just starting to think that they were far enough away for her to climb to her feet and Disapparate without the hazard of Splinching herself or ending up miles away from her intended destination, when the bricks above her head blasted apart. Flinching as she huddled at the base of the wall, Kara looked to the opposite end of the alleyway and saw the burly, blonde man rushing towards her, splashing through a puddle as he drew his arm back to send another curse her way. Fear widened her eyes, and Kara scrambled up, bursting out of her hiding spot as her stiff muscles protested at the sudden motion. Feeling like an old woman from years of dealing with her affliction, Kara ground her teeth together and ran, before she pulled up short at the sight of Siobhan penning her in from the opposite end. Panicking for a moment, Kara looked back and forth between them before turning to Siobhan as the witch sent a hex straight for her, ducking beneath it and hearing the man shout as it struck him in the chest. 

 

            He keeled over, going down hard into a puddle, and Kara stumbled back towards him as she cast a Shield Charm in front of her, just in time as Siobhan cast another spell. Teeth gritted, Kara kept her shield in place as she kept backing up, pausing at the man and kicking his wand out of his hand before she reached the opposite end of the alleyway. Siobhan advanced on her as she shot curses and hexes, one after the other, as Kara’s Shield Charm started to buckle beneath the onslaught, and as soon as she stepped onto the pavement at the mouth of the alley, Kara dropped the spell and ran.

 

            Her mind was too frazzled to Disapparate now, so she ran as fast as she could, circling the block and running down a side street so narrow that the tall buildings scarcely let in any light. Muggles frowned as she bumped into shoulders, pushing them out of the way and cutting across the street, and she was nearing the Thames now, feeling the heat of a spell tear through her robe as she tripped, skinning her hands and knees on the asphalt as a taxi screeched to a halt, horn blaring. Picking herself up with her open briefcase, scattering pages, quills and books across the street, Kara darted around the car, staying ducked down as Siobhan tried to spot her, before she continued to run towards the river and cut across to Victoria Embankment Gardens. The grass was wet, the rain coming down harder, and Kara gasped for breath as she made for a memorial statue with a wide base, sheltering behind it as her heart thudded in her chest. Her left arm was tingling and numb, the knees of her pants torn and bloody, and Kara wasted no time Disapparating from the gardens before Siobhan had the chance to find her, or before the blonde man caught up. As much as she wished to duel, it wasn’t the time nor the place, and Kara had to recognise the wisdom in that, knowing when it was best to swallow her pride and choose safety. 

 

            She didn’t go home, though, somewhat stunned by the sudden attack. Apparating to the stoop of Grimmauld Place, Kara looked so tired that a light breeze probably could’ve knocked her over, rivulets of water running down her pale face, face scratched from shards of brick, palms scraped bloody and the left side of her wet robe in tatters. Knocking on the door, Kara tried to catch her breath as she waited for the minute it took for someone to answer, Querl looking surprised at the state of her.

 

            “Merlin’s beard, what happened to you?”

 

            Sweating and clutching her ribs, a stitch in her side, Kara gave a brief explanation between breaths. “Death Eaters. Followed me … from work.”

 

            Grabbing her arm, Querl towed her inside and shut the door on the rain, and Kara let her open briefcase drop to the floor. A few items had remained safely stowed inside the elasticated pocket inside the lid - her journal, her coin pouch, a spare scrunchie and an unopened Chocolate Frog - but the work she’d brought home with her was scattered across Whitehall. There wasn’t much she could do about that, and none of it pertained to the Order, at least, although she wasn’t really supposed to let confidential Department of Mysteries documents get into anyone else’s hands either. Wiping her wet face on her equally as wet sleeve, Kara sniffed and followed Querl to the stairs leading down to the kitchen, tasting blood in her mouth where she’d bitten her tongue when she’d gone sprawling in the middle of the road.

 

            Alex was there with J’onn, James, M’gann and Tonks, the kitchen almost humid as the warmth washed over Kara. Shivering, or perhaps trembling from the shock, Kara stepped inside and dragged a chair out, slumping onto it. Her shoulders slumped, and a headache started to form at her temples from the sudden burst and then dissipation of adrenaline, her hand shaking as she raked wet hair out of her face. Her sister’s attention was immediately on her, going from casual curiosity to a flicker of panic as the chair legs scraped across the floor and she rose to her feet.

 

            “What the bloody hell happened to you?”

 

            “Death Eaters,” Kara explained, closing her eyes, nudging her glasses up as she took a moment to gather herself and then straightened up in her seat. “Tailed me out of the Ministry and cornered me in an alleyway. One of them took out the other and chased me through Whitehall, but I lost them. I think. But … well, I’ve been made.”

 

            “Who?” Alex demanded, dropping into the chair beside Kara.

 

            James set a strong cup of tea down in front of Kara and sat on the edge of the table, arms folded over his chest. Thanking him, Kara took a scalding sip and let out a heavy sigh, eyeing her scraped palm and then wiping it over the thigh of her ruined pants.

 

            “One of them was Siobhan Smythe. The other was some big, blonde bloke. He wore a visitor’s badge. I don’t know his name.”

 

            “Mm, could be Rowle,” J’onn murmured. “Neither of them was at the Department of Mysteries, though. Rowle’s been a suspect for a while now - if it’s him - but Smythe … she’s a new one.”

 

            “I can’t imagine she’s got herself a Dark Mark yet,” Tonks mused. “Not if she’s that new. Blimey, even the partners and siblings of some of his inner circle haven’t been branded yet, and they’ve been loyal for years .”

 

            “Branded or not, if she’s helping hunt down Order members, she’s clearly picked a side. And that was either very brazen or very stupid to go after you without a mask on.”

 

            “I don’t think they expected me to get away to tell anyone,” Kara weakly laughed.

 

            No one else was amused, a solemn air filling the kitchen as they all remained silent.Taking another sip of tea, tracing a hot path down her throat, she sniffed and pressed her mouth into a flat line. After a moment, she let out a heavy sigh, setting the cup back down. “Well, that’s me done, then. I don’t think I’ll be going to work tomorrow.”

 

            “You’re bloody right about that,” Alex grimly agreed, brow pinched together with worry.

 

            “And you shouldn’t, either,” Kara continued, glancing up at her sister. “If they know about me, they know about you, and they’ll be on your tail too.”

 

            Waving a hand dismissively, Alex had a stubborn set to her jaw. “Oh, they know about me, alright. But I’ve been doing this for years , so regardless of whether they know I’m an Order member or not, they’ll be after me. And any Auror, for that matter. But that’s just part of the job.”

 

            “Well, I’m not going to sit at home all day, though.”

 

            “The Order will have plenty for you to do to help,” J’onn cut in, giving her a reassuring nod. “Without you being tailed. Just sit tight and keep at your stakeouts and passing messages; that’s more useful than losing more of us. We’ve few enough members as it is.”

 

            Unhappy about it, but knowing it was the best course of action, that next time there could be more Death Eaters waiting to corner her, that she might not be so lucky to escape relatively unscathed next time, Kara reluctantly nodded. There was a long silence as everyone was left with their thoughts, and Kara continued to drink her tea, thinking about how she hadn’t even lasted three months since everything had happened at the Ministry before it had all gone awry. And worse than that, she hadn’t even lasted a year as a member of the Order without being found out. It made her worry about Lena, thinking about how her safety hinged on not being found out, and how much worse it would be for her if she were. Wondering if she should write her a note and leave it at their cottage, Kara sat with a lump caught in her throat as her body calmed, but it left her with an awful pit in her stomach.

 

            She wished she could go back to sitting on the sidelines, thinking about how unrecognisable her life was now. There had been friction between her and Lena because of their conflicting desires to each be involved while keeping the other out of it, and Kara wondered if it would’ve been different if she’d firmly stayed out of it instead of skirting around helping, but she knew it wouldn’t have changed. They both could’ve remained on the sidelines, but she knew that as soon as Lex had broken out of Azkaban, Lena would’ve insisted upon going home. She was too self-sacrificing to have stayed out of it, and the fact that she hadn’t budged, despite Kara begging her on her knees, convinced her that there was nothing on earth that would’ve convinced Lena to give up her plight. Nothing but the end of the war. Even now, relegated to skulking around because she was known to the Death Eaters, Kara knew that if she asked Lena to run away with her, she would’ve been rejected. It left her feeling a little bitter, but so long as Lena was only risking her own life, she would hold to her cause. If Kara’s life was at stake, it would’ve been a different story, but Kara was as safe as could be, even now, with Death Eaters on her tail.

 

            Letting Querl apply Essence of Dittany to her palms, the grazes stinging fiercely, Kara was too preoccupied to follow the conversation and plotting that ensued. Others showed up, Mad-Eye Moody limping in twenty minutes later with a couple of red-headed Weasleys, Lucy and Imra ten minutes after them, Alex indignantly informing them of Kara’s close brush with the Death Eaters. Suddenly very tired, Kara pushed her chair back, giving Alex a small smile as she rubbed her nose, her clothes still damp, and gave her sister’s arm a quick squeeze.

 

            “I’m going to go home.”

 

            “Alright, but I’m serious about work. Don’t go back there. There are too many of them unidentified, and we don’t know who might be waiting for you next.”

 

            “I know,” Kara murmured, wrinkling her nose as she was filled with dismay. “It’s a shame. I thought this time it would be forever.”

 

            Alex gave her a sad smile, reaching up to stroke her sister’s wet hair. “It will be. This is just a temporary break.”

 

            “I don’t know if Croaker will see it that way.”

 

            “Write to him. Maybe he’ll be more understanding than you think. More and more people are quitting at the Ministry each day; I’d be surprised if he doesn’t follow suit soon enough.”

 

            “And what about you? Kelly?”

 

            “Ah, we’ve already rowed about that at least once a week since that night at the Ministry, but she won’t have a bar of it.”

 

            “Mm, yeah, well, I’m on her side. It’s not fair to expect her to sit at home, hiding, while you’re out there in the thick of it. I- I regret that myself.”

 

            Expression clouding with annoyance, a hard look in her eyes, Alex made a dissatisfied sound at the back of her throat. “Well, it’s not like she picked the right side, anyway. Better to know where she really stands, even if it ruined everything else for you. You dodged a bludger there.”

 

            “Right,” Kara muttered, her mouth twisting with wry bitterness. “Better off. Single, living at home, newly unemployed. Funny, this feels a lot similar to when I was twenty- three, not thirty- three.”

 

            They were at the top of the staircase now, and Alex prodded her in the back, clicking her tongue. “Better safe than sorry. Just … keep your head down, alright? Kelly doesn’t like it much, but even she’s accepted that she’ll be packing it in soon enough. With the way the Ministry’s going, we all will be. We just have to be all wands at the ready with the Order. Not much else for it, I’m afraid.”

 

            Calling goodbye down the staircase, hearing the varied responses drift back up to her, Kara wrapped Alex in a quick hug, holding onto her for a second longer as she felt a bleak helplessness fill her. She so badly just wanted to keep everyone safe, but it all felt so up in the air, and she didn’t know how to make it stop. And it was so lonely , having to keep so much of it to herself as well. Kara was utterly alone with her fear for Lena, nails bitten down to nothing, bags beneath her eyes that seemed a permanent fixture these days. She attributed as much as possible to the full moon, but it was getting harder to keep dismissing it as such, unable to really explain what had her looking so drawn and anxious these last few months. Of course, there was the obvious answer, but they were all worried and cautious, but Kara’s agitation went beyond that. 

 

            Giving Alex a pat on the back before reluctantly letting go, Kara softly sighed and gave her a small smile. “I’ll see you later. Stay safe, please.”

 

            “You too. And tell mum not to worry,” her sister rolled her eyes.

 

            Walking to the front door, Kara picked up her briefcase and let herself out, the evening darkening quickly as the rain continued to pour, and she Apparated to Cornwall, landing on her mother’s doorstep and letting herself inside. Easing the door shut, Kara set her mostly empty briefcase down and undid her tattered robe, hanging it up on the hook and leaving it for tomorrow. She’d have to sew up the knees of her pants as well, darning them as well as she could, or getting Eliza to do a better job if she wanted to admit that she’d fallen while being chased down by Death Eaters, and she called out to her mum as she hastily retreated upstairs, hoping to avoid any questions from Eliza.

 

            Changing into pyjamas and applying an ointment to her scraped knees, Kara padded back downstairs, finding her mum reading a novel as she idly stirred a spoon in her cup of coffee, sitting at the kitchen table in her dressing gown. She glanced up and smiled at Kara as she appeared in the kitchen, and Kara weakly returned it.

 

            “Good day?”

 

            “Oh, um, it was … eventful,” Kara evasively replied, moving over to the kettle and giving it a shake before refilling it and setting it on to boil. “I, uh, I was thinking … with the way it’s all going, and with how many people have already left … I think it might be time for me to pack it in.”

 

            Head jerking up from the novel again, Eliza turned to look at her with surprise. “Really?”

 

            Nodding as she bit her lip, Kara’s shoulders were slumped, and she couldn’t quite meet her mother’s eyes, knowing that she was withholding so much, but not wanting to make her worry. It wasn’t lost on her that she was doing exactly the same to Eliza as Lena was doing to her, and it made her feel guilty, but it also made her wish that none of them had to be in that position to lie to comfort the other. And her mother saw straight through her, anyway.

 

            “What happened?”

 

            “It’s nothing,” Kara murmured, turning and fishing a mug out of the cupboard. “It’s just- it’s going to get worse. A lot worse. Um … I think it’s better to be safe than sorry, isn’t it? And with all these recent Muggle attacks, and with him demanding Fudge’s resignation, well … it’s not going to end well. I’ll be better off doing other things to help than sitting in the Ministry all day, waiting for them to come and take over.”

 

            “We both know something has happened, but I won’t pretend I’m not happy that at least one of you will be safe,” Eliza said with exasperation as she shook her head at the thought of Alex. “You’re right that it’s going to get worse. Have you been to Diagon Alley recently? The whole place feels off; I don’t like going anymore.”

 

            The kettle finished boiling, and Kara made her tea, staring down at it as the steam warmed her cheeks. “We’re all going to be okay. We defeated him last time; we’ll be able to do it again.”

 

            Softly sighing, Eliza shut her book and pushed her chair back, climbing to her feet with a grave look on her face. “A baby defeated him last time. And now our fate is thrown in with that boy doing it again. I’m fairly sure of that . But you’re right; we’re all going to be okay.”

 

            Nodding, Kara pressed her lips into a flat line, considering her mother’s morbid words. Taking a sip of tea, she looked up and raised her eyebrows. “Fish and chips for tea?”

 

            With her plan to quit in the morning, or rather, just stop showing up for work, Kara’s income was about to dwindle down to nothing, and she doubted Ministry benefits would be afforded to werewolves for much longer, with the way things were going. Still, she thought one last takeaway wouldn’t do any harm to the savings she’d managed to squirrel away in her Gringott’s account over the years, and she knew that even with the way things were, even with the necessity for secrecy, for keeping them apart, if she needed money, she need only ask Lena and it would be freely given. She’d always felt guilty about letting her girlfriend pay for things, even after so many years together, and Kara had always made a point to be financially independent, but the memory of the times she’d had to scrimp and struggle, starving herself and living in dire situations, made her worry once more. It was just one more stressor to the long list she’d accumulated. 

 

            Walking into Falmouth, she placed an order and fiddled with the Muggle money before carrying home the vinegar-dampened parcel and eating in front of the fire with her mother. They played a game of Wizard’s Chess afterwards, before Kara felt too tired to stay up, even though it was still relatively early. The rain had stopped, but the streets were damp and the night held a chill, and Bastet followed her upstairs to curl up in Kara’s blankets with her. Burrowing under the covers, Kara found sleep hard to come by, and she pretended to drift off until she eventually did, dead to the world as she dreamt of Lena.

 

            It was all she seemed to do of late, thinking of her in sleep and in her every waking moment, and with no work to distract herself with, Kara had far too much time on her hands to think of her even more. She thought about Lena as soon as she woke, she thought about her when she made her narrow childhood bed, and when she showered and dressed, when she ate breakfast at the kitchen table and when she stood in the back garden in weak morning sunlight. Helping her mother with her plants and parcels to be mailed off via owl post, Kara thought about Lena some more, and then again after dinner, sitting by the fire with a book she wasn’t reading, and then went to bed still thinking of her, until she fell asleep and dreamt about her once more. 

 

            It was a constant cycle of torment, her days bleeding into one another as a week passed by, her birthday coming and going, a green alert on the ring resulting in a folded crane and a Chocolate Frog left on the kitchen table of their cottage, bringing tears to her eyes but filling her with relief too, as Kara was also gifted the knowledge that she was alive for another day . She could never be sure what state Lena was in, whether she was hurt or not, but she was alive , and that was all Kara cared about, each time the ring burned filling her with relief. She had little else that was important to her and was left with too much time to worry, which took its toll on her as much as the full moon did, another one following on the heels of her birthday. At St. Mungo’s, she’d hoped to catch a glimpse of Lena, despite knowing she worked on an entirely different floor of the hospital, and left the next morning, disappointed and aching for even a tiny scrap of her. 

 

            Each day that passed by was agonising, and Kara spent more and more time at Grimmauld Place, sometimes for the sole purpose of waiting for people to come and go as she listened to the gossip. Wherever she could make herself useful, she did, although her ability to walk freely through the Wizarding World had been hampered somewhat, and there were many late nights, standing in the rain and watching from the shadows with other Order members, tailing suspects, risking the occasional visit to The Leaky Cauldron to eavesdrop on conversations or see if Tom had seen anything of note from the constant flow of visitors. If it wasn’t somewhere she was scheduled to be, it wasn’t so risky, the Death Eaters not expecting her to be making a visit to Carkitt Market on a Thursday afternoon, although going anywhere these days had its own dangers as things grew worse. 

 

            Kara slept a lot as well, but the purplish bruises beneath her eyes never seemed to vanish, and she felt so adrift in her life, feeling aimless as she tried to help, but could never do enough to satisfy her, to distract her enough from her thoughts. Lena’s birthday was at the end of October, and Kara had to pretend like she didn’t know that as she sat at Grimmauld Place with her friends and sister, sipping on wine as they swapped new from the Ministry, news of attacks, and what tasks Dumbledore had assigned, divvying them up between them all. She’d already been to the cottage that morning, a singular singing daffodil left on the table with a folded butterfly, risking nothing more than that as she left with the ring on her finger changed to green. Kara just hoped that Lena knew she was thinking of her, that she knew how badly Kara wished they were celebrating together, that her family were buying her presents and singing to her with a cake covered in candles, making Lena feel loved the way the Luthors had failed to. Instead, Kara was left with the gutted knowledge that they were probably treating it like just another day, that even if they did remember, it was very likely they would’ve pretended not to, if only to make Lena feel even more worthless. And Kara vowed to try her very hardest to ensure that by Lena’s next birthday, they would be back together again. She would do anything to make that happen, anything to have her in her arms and let her know how much she loved her, with every word imaginable, with a ring on her finger, whatever it took.

 

            As if sensing her frustration and desperation, a week into November, Kara received a letter asking for her attendance at a meeting at Hogwarts in a few days’ time, signed by Dumbledore and bearing his seal on the unopened letter. She had a reluctant sort of respect for the man, disliking him for his helpless sacrifice of innocent people while he did nothing to mitigate the risk, but appreciating his intelligence, his power. He wasn’t the most powerful wizard for no reason, but skill was a different matter to his character, and Kara had a handful of reasons, mostly kept to herself, to find him flawed and condemnable. Still, she went. What else could she do but go? Taking umbrage at being summoned at his beck and call, she still Apparated to Hogsmeade and walked up to the castle, a wave of nostalgia hitting her as she wondered in which manner Dumbledore planned on manipulating her this time, what he would ask of her now. She’d already given up everything to assist the Order, and while it hadn’t been what she’d wanted, in a way, it had , and Kara was still bitter about that. She’d wanted everything ; she hadn’t wanted to choose.

 

            And that was part of Dumbledore’s manipulation, too, offering up choices, which weren’t choices, as per se. This time it was no different, wandering through the relatively empty hallways, the occasional student with a free period passing her by with a curious glance, while Kara swept through the school with a gut-wrenching ache to be fifteen again, holed up in their secret room in the Astronomy Tower. How simple it had all been then, playing Wizard’s Chess, doing homework on the windowsill, sharing sweets and stories, too afraid of the world beyond their secret room to even think there would be a day when they’d publicly been friends, let alone in a relationship, in their own home. One thing hadn’t changed at all; they were still each other’s secret. 

 

            Lamenting all that she’d lost, most of it at her own hastiness, Kara gave the statue the password to Dumbledore’s office before riding the staircase up and knocking on the door, resigned to finding out what her old Headmaster and boss wanted. Seated at his desk a few minutes later as he poured her a cup of tea, she was somewhat awkward and stiff as Dumbledore poured a stream of amber from the teapot with a blackened hand. He set it down and shifted one of the saucers closer to her, eyeing her over the rim of his glasses as he caught her staring at his injury.

 

            “An old man’s carelessness,” he said by way of explanation, shaking the sleeve of his robe over it and lifting a milk jug, adding a splash to his tea before offering it to her with a wry smile. “Sometimes, wisdom can be lacking, even at my age.”

 

            Taking the jug, Kara added some to her tea and used a little pair of silver tongs to add two sugar cubes as well, gently stirring them in before setting the spoon on the saucer and shifting in her seat. She hadn’t seen him in person in months, and was curious about what he’d done to wither his hand in such a manner, a mistake like that seeming beneath someone as clever as Dumbledore, but she politely kept her questions to herself.

 

            “But we have more important matters to discuss than silly accidents. First, I hope you’ll indulge me in trivial niceties; it is rare that I’m afforded that opportunity these days. I trust you’re keeping well?”

 

            “Well enough, sir.”

 

            “And your sister?”

 

            “Yes, sir.”

 

            “Good, good. I hear she’s a fine Auror. A valuable asset to our cause, most certainly. As are you.”

 

            Masking a flicker of surprised amusement with nonchalance, Kara picked up her cup of tea and smiled thinly, feeling a little clammy. “Am I?”

 

            “All members of the Order are valuable assets, as are necessary allies. I believe many qualities make a person useful, and not all of them are necessarily brute force, although I remember you being quite the adept dueller in your Hogwarts days. And while you’ve been most useful in passing messages with invaluable information, and have shown your worth in many fights, I was hoping you might be open to making use of another asset of yours.”

 

            He paused a moment, taking a sip of tea as she was left waiting with a prickle of impatience. Sipping her tea as well, she bit her tongue and resisted the urge to ask what he wanted her to do, eyes sliding over to Fawkes, the phoenix sitting on its perch, resplendent in his crimson and gold plumage. Drawing her eyes back to her old Headmaster, Kara set her cup back down and shifted in her seat. He leaned forward and set his cup down as well, seemingly unhurried for someone embroiled in a worsening war, and considered the head of their army, if they were such a thing.

 

            “I heard of what happened to you when you left work in September, and that you have not returned since. I hope you know that I’m relieved you escaped unscathed, as so many of our number have been unable to over the years. Life is a precious thing these days. It’s also been reported back to me the duties you’ve been undertaking in your free time since resigning from the Ministry, and that you are most willing to take on any task required. There is another task I’d like to discuss with you that I’m hopeful you’ll be just as willing to undertake. I do not ask it of you lightly, and it will differ greatly from the tasks you’re used to, but you are almost singular in your ability to aid the Order in this.”

 

            “Almost singular, sir?”

 

            Smiling faintly, Dumbledore nodded approvingly as she picked up on his wording. “Most astute, Miss Danvers. You see, Remus Lupin has been assisting the Order of late by going underground.”

 

            “Underground?”

 

            “There are groups of werewolves Voldemort is interested in recruiting.”

 

            With a quiet scoff, Kara’s lips twitched with a jaded smile. “I find that hard to believe, sir. What would he want with monsters? His whole ethos is about blood purity; he’d treat a Muggleborn better than he’d treat a werewolf. ”

 

            “Yes, in his ideal world, he would. Yet, the prejudice against those infected with Lycanthropy has made them easier to manipulate, and he can be quite coercive. I’ve no doubt that whatever he is offering is a lie, but he will cast the Wizarding World in a negative light, paint them as the root cause of the injustice of werewolves, which I would agree with, but he will merely use them as a means to his ends. I’m certain that if he’s successful, they will not find themselves equal in society, no matter what he promises.”

 

            “What about Fenrir Greyback? He seems to like keeping him about.”

 

            “Ah, yes, Fenrir. Well, he is merely a tool as well. One that is quite effective at striking fear in the hearts of ordinary folk and validating their prejudice against all werewolves. He drives a wedge between the two, and yet, he himself is not afforded the privilege of a Dark Mark on his arm. Even he, so loyal, is seen as lesser than by the master he serves.”

 

            “So, Remus has been helping to recruit them to our cause instead?” Kara deduced, already aware of Hagrid’s failed attempt to do the same with the giants.

 

            “Up until recently, yes. However, he’s been largely unsuccessful and finds that they have a hard time trusting him, given his proximity to Wizarding society.”

 

            There was a beat of silence as Kara figured out her use. Almost singular in her ability, she was the next logical choice to take over for him, to garner support for the Order, as the only other werewolf in their ranks. They couldn’t send an ordinary witch or wizard, and she was out of a job now, which freed her up nicely to take over. If she agreed.

 

            “It is a risk, bigger than any you have taken so far, and will require the sacrifice of family and comfort. It may be weeks, months, at a time that you’re underground, and I mean that literally; Remus has spent the last few weeks in one of the abandoned coal mines in the Brecon Beacons.”

 

            Silent a moment longer, Kara cleared her throat. Her words caught Dumbledore by surprise, not the question he’d anticipated. “And what about the letters?” she asked, thumb rubbing over the stone on her finger.

 

            Eyebrows rising slightly, Dumbledore blinked and then shifted forward slightly in his seat. He was smart enough to know her true concern was Lena. Kara would miss her mum and sister, her friends, but she could leave them to do this. But being gone for weeks or months at a time could mean giving up the ring on her finger, the random alerts that meant Lena was alive, could mean the difference between Lena having a safe place to flee to if things got hairy. Kara knew that if she wasn’t at home, there would be no chance of Alex helping Lena if she showed up on the doorstep. But she had hope that Eliza might be a little more understanding, showing weakness to the young woman she’d welcomed into her home years ago. But that hope wasn’t enough to convince her.

 

            “I’m not convinced I’d be able to rely on anyone else to take over that responsibility, or that it would be feasible to facilitate an exchange in its current location without betraying our source. And I don’t believe changing the location would benefit Lena, who is already under scrutiny and has small windows to make sudden trips for urgent messages without arousing suspicion. It will have to be you, but that will likewise cast some doubt upon your sudden disappearances. I would be more confident of your safety amidst werewolves than Lena’s amongst Death Eaters, though, which I’m sure you’ll agree with.”

 

            Nodding, Kara’s mouth was a flat line as she didn’t respond. The office was silent for a few minutes, almost uncomfortable in its oppressiveness, only interrupted by Fawkes and a few silver instruments making noises and letting out puffs of steam. Dumbledore finished his tea and poured himself a new cup as Kara considered his proposal. And as was usual, he gave her a choice, but it didn’t seem to really be one. She was their only option to continue Remus’ efforts, and she knew she had to shoulder that responsibility, like it or not. And while she’d wanted Lena to stay out of it, Kara had never had any qualms about her own safety, so it felt easy to agree, so long as she could continue passing messages.

 

            “Where do I begin?”

 

 

            St. Mungo’s felt busier with each passing day, a constant influx of patients, both magical and Muggle, coming through their doors as attacks that required advanced magic to fix up brought them in. The Muggles were handed over to the custody of the Ministry for Memory Charms before they were taken back home, and it made Lena’s life more difficult to manage the panic and hysteria of confused patients on the Charms Ward, on top of the ordinary chaos of magical injuries and mishaps. On top of that, they lost a few staff members, bad tidings leaving many who were financially able to resigning without a word. They just stopped showing up for their shifts, making more work for those who remained, and for the first time in years, Lena found herself dealing with more of the menial healing tasks usually relegated to Residents, on top of her usual hours spent in a Theatre.

 

            Tired, stressed and irate, she was finding it harder to keep it together. She had to take a Sleeping Draught most nights, even when she didn’t have work the next day, sleep harder to come by these days as her mind refused to slow, leaving her tense and leaden as she tried to tread carefully, Lex’s moods growing worse as he was kept cooped up inside most of the time. He had more freedom now that Voldemort had come out into the open, but that didn’t mean the entire Auror Department didn’t have him on their list of most wanted people. And Lena was confident he would be high up on it at that. There were many nights after dinner, or on the occasions he had a few disciples over for drinks, where he grew brooding and nasty, smashing things, ranting as his face twisted with anger, like a petulant child as he bemoaned the way his potential was hindered by Voldemort’s desire for him to remain undiscovered.

 

            There had been two more raids over the months, revealing nothing as Lex hid beneath the Invisibility Cloak Lena had to ask Dumbledore to return, a simple solution to their problem with the Floo Network’s tracking capability. Lena had only been home for one of them, her wand turned into the possession of an Auror with pink hair as she was detained in the foyer of the manor house, while her room had been torn apart with routine efficiency. They didn’t find anything, of course, a rather bare room of clothes, toiletries and a book where she’d rewritten as much of her research as she could remember, rehashing some of it, somewhat glad for her brother’s games, as it had allowed her to reframe it all in a new light, starting over with a solid foundation. And there, between the pages, a pressed daffodil, no longer singing but left to dry between the covers of the notebook, along with a little paper butterfly. They could look as much as they wanted to, but Lena had nothing to hide from them; it was her brother she was more afraid of.

 

            For his part, Lex had made her sit in on drinks with the social climbing hopefuls on numerous occasions, spending her evenings in various people’s living rooms as a haze of smoke hung over the group of gathered witches and wizards, all of them Purebloods, save for Lena. Not that anyone knew that, not that it was advertised by her brother, not even to be spiteful. She hated those nights, though, sitting stiffly in her seat, drinking wine or Firewhisky, reluctantly engaging in the same scornful conversations about those lesser than them and how they’d be returned to their rightful places soon enough. It was always the same people, the same topics, the same fanaticism, and she didn’t see the point in Lex bringing her to them, but she also didn’t object. They were always opportunities to ferret out new information, not even trivial gossip too insignificant for her to report back to Dumbledore, and she played her part well, throwing in her opinion, agreeing with the general sentiment, laughing along with the others and their wishful thinking about what they could do to Muggles and Muggleborns. 

 

            She preferred the nights he went off about his business, answering the summons of the Dark Mark on his forearm, leaving the admirers to their hungry desire to be a fully-fledged Death Eater like him. Lena could never follow him on those trips, unless he let slip where he was going, and only then could she follow in the form of a raven, staying relatively unseen, and trying to behave like a normal bird if he happened to acknowledge her swooping past to perch on a tree branch or a lamppost. It was all so tiring, the pretence of it all, the plotting and scheming, tucking away information and trusting her memory to recall it correctly, knowing incorrect information could spell someone’s death. It was at Lena’s word that Dumbledore knew Voldemort had sent Death Eater’s after her old Potions professor and Head of Slytherin House, Slughorn, tipping Dumbledore off that there was valuable information that Slughorn held secret, and it was she who confirmed what Dumbledore already suspected about Florean Fortescue’s disappearance from his ice cream parlour, although, Lena was yet to find out anything further about Ollivander, whom Dumbledore was very interested in, although Lena hadn’t been told why.
