One, she would’ve known anywhere, seeing his face in the papers often enough over the years, even after the war. Fenrir Greyback. It was fortunate that he didn’t know her , though, and the other man was a smug-faced man who worked with Kelly. Benjamin Lockwood. The knot in her chest loosened slightly, even though her heart continued to race, and Kara thought she was safe and would be able to pass herself off as Linda Lee. They probably wouldn’t even look twice at her, dirt caked onto her face and hair, old blood beneath her fingernails, her lips chapped and peeling, looking every bit the feral werewolf slumming it in the woods, downtrodden by society.

 

            Unfortunately, as their eyes raked over the trio arriving with the deer, Kara had overlooked the possibility of more of them. The morning was quiet, a cold snap having passed over in the night, leaving frost in its wake, and that cold had driven many of them inside, sleeping late or drinking tea in the shelter of the mouldering hovel. When another figure stepped outside, this one dressed in ordinary black robes, not elevated to Voldemort’s inner circle quite yet, Kara felt sick with dread as the blood drained from her face. Whatever her face showed, Veronica Sinclair smiled at the sight, wolfish and predatory, as she took a step forward.

 

            “Well, well. Kara Danvers. We’ve been looking for you.”

Chapter 59

            Lena had left for work at the crack of dawn that day, spending hours in various procedures, spreading herself thin as she helped repair legs shattered from some idiot falling off a Hippogriff, painstakingly reversed a curse that had a woman’s lungs filled with feathers , and assisting with a Transfiguration-related case, where Lena had to charm a man’s pulmonary system to keep functioning as the Transfiguration Attending managed the unfortunate case of undoing a backfired spell that had partially changed him into a shark, leaving him struggling for air and making his blood run cold. Tucked away in St. Mungo’s, she worked tirelessly, just another day, or so she thought. 

 

            She wasn’t to know any better, didn’t know the trap that she was walking into, the snare tightening around her for months now. And she didn’t know that brother’s suspicions had essentially dog walked her into it, testing her loyalty in the most brutal way he knew how. A true test. He was unsatisfied with how Lena had gone about it all so far, her rejection of a Dark Mark in January forcing his hand, or so he’d frame it, and she’d done little else to prove her worth since then, stalling for as long as she could. Lena would run before she had to hurt someone else, and she’d lasted until April purely out of sheer luck that it had taken Lex that long for his lackeys to carry out his orders. Still, if she’d known what she was walking into, she would’ve gone home that morning and brought the house down around him before she let him lay a finger on her. But she didn’t know that, and he had Kara in that house for over ten hours by the time she left work.

 

            Outside, the day paled. Soon it would be night, and Lena was hoping Lex wasn’t in the mood for company, that he might let her unwind with a bath and dinner, instead of being dragged to one of his outings, forced to bite her tongue and stay her hand as she listened to the litany of horrors they described in detail. All Lena could do was report it all back to Dumbledore and hope the Order were able to put a stop to some of the planned attacks, while she sat there, culpable as well, for doing nothing to stop them herself. Mouth a grim line against the overcast sky, she Apparated to the fringes of the Luthor estate and hurried up the long path to the front door, gravel crunching underfoot as the weak warmth of the day fled, dusk falling quickly. Hands in the pockets of her green Healer robes, Lena felt the ache in her feet from so many hours of standing as she briskly walked towards the suffocating house, wondering how much longer she’d have to endure it. If she’d known the answer to that, she might’ve wished she could stay longer, if only to spare her heart the pain of the last ten hours.

 

            Ignorant, Lena let herself into the quiet house, the large front door groaning shut, and she stood in the darkness of the foyer for a second before her footsteps sounded on the floor, echoing faintly. There was no glow of firelight on the polished floor, so she thought her brother might’ve been out, premature relief flitting through her, but his voice called out a moment later, as calm and authoritative as usual, not even questioning whether she’d obey or not. 

 

            “Lena. Come here a moment.”

 

            Swallowing her annoyance, her resentment, she went, of course. He’d gotten worse, these last months, his temper quicker to flare, his patience wearing thin, and if Lena didn’t already permanently wear long sleeves, regardless of the weather, she would’ve had to start with the amount of bruises he left on her arms and wrists, grabbing her too tightly as he seethed, quietly raged, lecturing her, ranting about things that didn’t concern her at all, but she was the closest thing at hand. Sometimes, when he was angry at her, he’d grab a fistful of her hair and jam his stolen wand into her cheek or under her chin, threatening her with the old things he’d used to torment her with, although he never did take her down to the dark cellar. Usually, he just stared at her in heavy silence, over their meals, across a chessboard, from the other side of the room, watching and waiting. Any reason would’ve done, she supposed, so Lena tried her hardest not to give him one. But she didn’t exactly give him any new reasons to trust her, and her old good deeds, saving him from raids, lying to Aurors, counted for less and less as they faded from his mind.

 

            Wandering into the sitting room, Lena was surprised to find he wasn’t alone. The room was dark, making her skin prickle, and she saw him sitting there on the sofa, a glass on the coffee table, his shirtsleeves rolled up to show off his Dark Mark. A few dark flecks were staining his white shirt, but Lena barely noticed them as her eyes darted from him to another Death Eater sitting in an armchair. Benjamin Lockwood. Otis Graves lingered in the shadows of the door to Lena’s left, his brawny arms folded over his chest as he flashed his teeth at her in a creepy smile, while Mercy prowled back and forth behind the sofa Lex sprawled on, polished and proud, her dark eyes glimmering. That left Veronica Sinclair, loitering near a tall window to Lena’s right, a smug look on her face as Lena met her gaze. 

 

            “I didn’t realise we were having guests tonight,” Lena murmured, feeling her skin prickle with the usual unease to be in such company. 

 

            “Come,” Lex beckoned her, straightening up, leaning forward to snatch up his drink and knock the rest of it back.

 

            “I should get out of my robes first.”

 

            Shaking his head, Lex made a sound of objection and set the glass back down heavily, before he pointed to a spot in front of the cold hearth. “Stand there. Graves, help my sister with her bag.”

 

            Glancing sideways at him, Lena felt wariness wind through her but didn’t offer any further objections, slipping her satchel off her shoulder and handing it over to Graves. Her footsteps were loud in the stifling silence of the room, and her pulse quickened as she stood in the wide gap between the hearth and the low pouffes set across from the sofa. Trying to feign nonchalance, Lena arched an eyebrow.

 

            “Well?”

 

            “I have a present for you,” Lex informed her, a smile twitching the corners of his mouth, shadows making his face seem gaunt and cruel, despite it. 

 

            He turned his attention to Otis and nodded, his lackey slipping out of the room, heavy footsteps thudding across the foyer. Lena’s mouth was dry, and she could feel each second passing with agonising awareness. Lex seemed unhurried, enjoying himself as he levitated some more Firewhisky over to the table, adding a dram to the glass and swirling it around. Lena didn’t move an inch, a voice at the back of her mind whispering for her to keep still, to comply, to try and see a way out of this without blowing her cover. She needn’t have worried; her cover was almost entirely blown anyway. He just needed his proof.

 

            A few minutes later, footsteps returned, and Otis Graves stepped over the threshold of the room, dragging a limp figure by a fistful of a filthy, tattered long-sleeved top, bare feet squealing against the floor as the figure scrabbled to find purchase, lank hair obscuring their face as they reached blindly for something to catch their balance on. Otis adjusted his grip on them, grabbing the back of their shirt with both hands as he heaved and threw them into the sitting room, the thin, lanky figure sprawling on the floor, striking their chin with a painful thud, a whimper passing between fat lips. It took everything in Lena to remain where she was standing; it took everything in her to keep her expression blank, because she recognised her. How could she not? She hadn’t even seen her face, but she knew her. She knew her even with her hair greasy, she knew her from the flannel pyjama pants, from the sight of her dirty hands. Lena would have known Kara even if she were blind, just from the feeling of how much space she took up in the world.

 

            “What is this?” Lena asked, her voice impressively level, neither fury nor fear showing through. 

 

            But she couldn’t hide her glassy eyes, even though she didn’t cry, and she couldn’t hide the way her throat bobbed when she swallowed. Lena was not that good at lying. Icy sweat trailed down her spine, and her mind was screaming, an unending rage of pure agony as she tried not to look at Kara. If she didn’t look, maybe it wouldn’t be real. If she didn’t look, maybe he’d think he’d misjudged. The anger that filled her made her vision dim at the edges, and she felt cold and hardened by it, silently vowing that she’d kill him. One day, she’d kill him for what he’d done to Kara, she’d kill him for even breathing the same air as her. But for now, she listened to her heartbeat loud in her ears and didn’t look at her, didn’t move a muscle.

 

            Snapping his fingers, Lex impatiently shot Otis a cutting glance. “Don’t forget her glasses.”

 

            Otis pulled a pair of frames from his pocket, one of the lenses cracked, and grabbed a fistful of Kara’s hair to pull her up to her knees. Lena couldn’t help but look. How could she not? He grabbed her by the jaw, squeezing tightly, and set Kara’s glasses on her brutalised face, so swollen and bloody that if Lena didn’t know her from the shape of her shoulders and the lanky length of her limbs, she might not have recognised her at a first glance. Even in the dark, Lena could see the bruises ringing both eyes, the left one swollen shut, lips split as she dribbled blood, nose smashed across her cheeks, dried blood caked over her face. Sweating profusely as she tried not to react, feeling as if she was firmly outside of her body, inhabited by a stranger as she managed to keep her mouth shut, Lena glanced at her brother again. Heat shot up the back of her nose, her chest rising and falling quickly as she couldn’t stop the dread that suffused her, the way her vision dimmed, the room seeming to sway as she felt an anger like she’d never felt before fill her. And still, she didn’t lift a finger, didn’t move an inch to go to the love of her life, who was kneeling on the floor, drawing in quick, painful breaths.

 

            “I think we both know what this is,” Lex icily said, his amusement vanishing as he pushed himself to his feet.

 

            He approached Lena and paused before backhanding her across the face. Kara let out a hoarse sound of outrage, and Lena’s eyes darted to hers, widening a fraction in a silent warning as her cheek smarted, the right side of her face going numb from the force of it. Swallowing, the taste of blood in her saliva, Lena straightened and faced her brother, trying to drown out Kara’s quiet sobs as she breathlessly pleaded. Closing her eyes, Lena breathed slowly, trying to retain her composure as her brother seethed in her face, flinching slightly at the feeling of his spit on her cheek as he snarled.

 

            “You’ve failed abysmally to prove yourself worthy to the Dark Lord, so I’ve fetched her for you. I’ll give you one more chance; take care of her. Take care of her, and at the next meeting, you’ll have a mark on your arm. And you will go, even if I have to drag you there kicking and screaming.”

 

            Lena’s blood ran cold, and she took a moment, shifting on her feet as she worked to swallow past the tightness in her throat. Her voice came out rough, and she forced an uneven smile to her face as she reached into her pocket and pulled out her wand. And then she understood why the others were there, five of them against their two, and Kara had no wand at that, and was in no state to fight even if she did. The threat was clear, and Lena rolled her shoulders, letting out a short bark of laughter. 

 

            “Is that all? Fine,” Lena shrugged, gesturing dismissively. “She’s nothing to me.”

 

            Turning to the hearth, almost as tall as she was and monstrously wide, Lena stared into the cold grate as her mind ran a mile a minute. Her face was shiny with sweat, tendrils of dark hair stuck to her temples, and she swallowed painfully as she paced away, then turned and looked her brother in the eye as she paced back towards him. Drawing in a shaky breath, she turned on her heel again and then flicked her wand in Kara’s direction, jerking it sharply and watching as the love of her life was ripped out of Otis’ grasp and was dragged across the floor towards her. It was humiliating, it was degrading, and Lena hated herself for doing it, feeling her wand hand shake as she directed Kara’s trajectory, bringing her to a stop in front of the hearth.

 

            Crumpled in a heap, raising her tear-stained face, Kara let out a breathless sob as she pushed herself to her knees, her battered face crumpled with pain as she looked up at Lena. She didn’t look frightened; she looked devastated, and there was only love in her eyes as she drew in a hitching breath, hands curled in her lap as tears wet her cheeks.

 

            “I’m sorry, I’m sorry, I’m sorry,” she quietly babbled, and Lena knew she wasn’t trying to get her to spare her life, that she knew that Lena couldn’t do it either, and that Lena was going to have to watch her die at her brother’s hand and probably endure a pain worse than death for her failure. That was what Kara’s apology was for. For allowing herself to be caught and putting them both in this situation.

 

            Steeling her heart, her eye stinging fiercely, Lena drew in a shuddering breath as she postured for her brother and his friends, full of false bravado and mockery. “Well, let’s not have a bawling act,” she laughed, the sound catching in her throat.

 

            Lex let out a soft chuckle, and she could envision the glee on his face as he felt himself triumphant and relieved to have been wrong about her. This was the sister he’d always wanted. Someone he could break and mould into a tool to break other people. This was a woman who’d serve the Dark Lord well with a Dark Mark on her arm to go with the Death Eater robes she’d paraded around in for months now at get-togethers and stakeouts. He didn’t know that she’d sabotaged him at every turn, that she’d thrown hexes and curses wide, tipped off hiding Order members to their arrival to give them their best chance at fleeing or fighting back. He didn’t know the half of it, and his biggest mistake of all was thinking that nobody loved her. Because Lena already had a family, who’d accepted her as she was and had never inflicted any pain upon her before she’d left them, and she had a woman she loved so completely that she would suffer any imaginable amount of pain to spare her even a single ounce of it. And he would never understand that, just like he would never understand how she was just so damn good.

 

            But she didn’t seem like it then, her wand trained on Kara as she advanced on her, pushing her away as Kara slid towards the fireplace on her knees, still breathlessly pleading with Lena. And then Lena came to a stop, looming over her with wide eyes, begging her to understand. It was then that she faltered, the tense set to her shoulders caving slightly as she breathed out her own apology, certain that her luck would run out with this final act of sacrifice. How badly she wished she could kiss Kara’s swollen lips one more time, even caress a bloody cheek, to have the feel of her again before the end. Lips twitching with a weak, pleading smile, Lena’s voice was a whisper as she held Kara’s gaze.

 

            “Forgive me.”

 

            Crooking her left hand, Lena wandlessly summoned the little pot of Floo powder from the mantel of the hearth and tossed it into the empty grate, emerald flames swirling to life as she flicked her wand at Kara, sending her flying into the fireplace as Lena shakily spoke the address for her Dublin flat. In a whirl of flames, Kara vanished from sight, and Lena had just enough time to turn around, dragging her wand up as she cast a silent Shield Charm, feeling the impact of three spells barrel right into it.

 

            And there her brother was, his face hard with pure anger as he kept his wand trained on her, lip curling back with contempt as he bitterly spat his words at her. “Is that truly where your loyalties lie? She’s a werewolf.”

 

            “And she’s mine,” Lena snarled through her teeth, eyes blazing as she kept up her Shield Charm.

 

            “You pathetic, useless twit,” he raged, advancing on her as she was backed up against the fireplace, only a couple of feet before she’d hit the lip of the hearth. “I should’ve known the second that she carved me up with Snape’s spell that there was more to it than a mere experiment. Rid us of their scourge, was it? I’m going to make this so painful, you’ll wish you’d killed her because it would’ve hurt less. Do you hear me? I’m going to break every fucking bone in your body until you can’t move an inch , and then I’m going to break your mind so you can’t even think . I’ve done it before; I’ll enjoy this time even more.”

 

            As he cursed her out, she took a few more hits to her Shield Charm, which started to buckle, and managed to duck at the last minute as Veronica came at her from the side, trying to disarm her. It made Lena lose her slipping control on her spell, and as her shield fell, she caught a blast to her left shoulder, feeling the nauseating pain of her collarbone break as her vision turned white. But she’d learnt how to duel from her brother’s advice, had been most adept at it in her school days, so Lena didn’t even falter, her wand clutched tightly in her right hand as she deflected a Full Body-bind Curse, dodged a Stinging Jinx and then shot off a few spells herself, shouting them to ensure she was accurate, unwilling to go down without a fight.

 

            “Impedimenta! Oppugno!”

 

            Otis Graves slowed in his movements, momentarily frozen as he dumbly tried to wade towards her, while the second spell was cast at Benjamin Lockwood, making his Death Eater ropes attack him. She managed another Shield Charm as she moved to her right, her brother getting angrier now, rushing towards her with the intent of physical violence as she countered his spells, unable to keep a smug smile off her face as she bared her teeth at him, daring and manic. Mercy was smarter than a few of the others, blasting the floor at Lena’s feet, wood and stone buckling under, making her twist her right ankle as she stumbled and overcorrected. Hissing as she tried to put her weight on it and almost buckled, Lena’s Shield Charm fell again, and her brother’s Severing Charm scored a line across her right bicep, cutting deep into the muscle as she felt hot blood instantly well up.

 

            Swallowing a grunt of pain, Lena was almost to the window now, although the tall panes were closed, and she held her wand aloft, spitting out a spell through gritted teeth, right before a Stinging Hex from Veronica caught her in the face. “Fumos.”

 

            A fog immediately poured from the tip of her wand, clouding the air in front of her and providing a much-needed screen, greatly outnumbered and outmatched as well. She wouldn’t mind so much if she could take her brother down with her, but that wasn’t a possibility with the others present, so Lena attempted to uphold her promise. One she’d made a year and a half ago, that she would get herself out alive, that she would fight her way back to Kara. Lena was no oathbreaker, and as the fog filled the sitting room, she pointed her wand at the ceiling.

 

            “Bombarda Maxima!”

 

            As the ceiling was blasted apart, a huge section crumpling under the impact of the spell, plaster and stone raining down on everyone, Lena turned and pointed her wand at the tall window and spoke one more spell. No sooner had the word Reducto passed her lips, shattering the glass outwards, onto the neat flowerbeds and gravel in the front garden, did her shape shift, shrinking, darkening as feathers sprouted. And another of her closely kept secrets came out as a raven fluttered about on uneven wings, one hanging at an awkward angle as she tried to stay aloft with a broken collarbone. As she crookedly flew out of the window, she heard her brother’s angry roar and was startled by a bolt of green narrowly streaking past her as he cast off a spell she hadn’t thought he’d ever have the audacity to use on her.

 

            But she was already free, flapping her wings as quickly as she could, off-balance but desperate, hearing the sound of loud voices behind her, below, as Otis was forced through the window, Veronica on his heels, both of them eager to prove themselves, longing for a Dark Mark and the status it would afford them. Night had fallen since Lena had set foot inside the Luthor estate, though, and her black feathers made her little more than a shadow against a cloudy sky, and she slipped right through their fingers, hardly daring to believe her luck. It was the most frantic flight of her life, straining to go as fast as she could, aware that as soon as she was over the spelled perimeter, she’d be able to Disapparate and never return. She’d failed in her task, most spectacularly, but she could only focus on Kara right then. 

 

            Kara, who was hurt and frightened, who she’d sent off alone with no promise that she was coming after her. While she’d sent her to Dublin, with no wand and no way of getting back through to the Luthor manor house without the address linked to the Floo Network, Lena knew where she’d go. She would go to the first place she’d think of when she thought of help, when she thought of comfort, even if they wouldn’t believe Kara for a second. Fluttering over the hedgerows of the estate, Lena flapped down to the damp grass, listening to the distant sound of footsteps hurrying across gravel, and transformed back into her human self. In a rush, desperate to get away, she Disapparated with a grave lapse of concentration and felt a wash of pain as she Splinched herself, landing too far from the cottage in Cornwall to walk as she felt warm blood trickling down her right leg, her twisted ankle making her hobble a few steps forward before she buckled.

 

            Too dazed to Apparate again, Lena had to transform into her Animagus form once more, her hands shaking so badly as she tried to concentrate, her whole body smarting from the sudden turn her night had taken. So distracted, Lena ended up leaving her Healer robes in a puddle on the street corner with her scrubs and shoes as well. Hopping on one leg, flapping one wing a little weakly, she managed to take flight again, getting enough height to make sense of where she was, fluttering and swooping her way to the cottage and landing awkwardly on the windowsill of the living room. She could hear frantic voices inside, aware that no more than ten minutes had passed since the whole ordeal had started, and she pecked madly at the window pane as she tried to make her presence known.

 

            It was Kara who threw the window open, as if she knew it would be Lena. She was breathlessly sobbing, her face a mess, and she let out a wordless cry of pure relief at the sight of the raven. Hopping inside, Lena swooped across the room, briefly noting that there were too many people inside it, before she clumsily lurched midair. Landing in a heap on the hallway floor as a human once more, her feet were left inside the living room as her wand rolled from her grasp. Dimly aware that she’d lost her clothes, she let out a pitiful moan as she heard Kara’s broken voice, the gentle caress of something soft draped over her bare back as her eyelids fluttered.

 

            “It’s okay, it’s okay,” Kara choked out, trying to wrap her up in the cloak.

 

            But they’d both made an oversight, because while Kara knew the truth of the matter, and Lena knew the truth of the matter, Alex didn’t. And the Auror had been at her mother’s house for dinner that night, three at the table when they’d been suddenly disturbed by the shocking arrival of Kara, beaten and bloody and babbling incoherently as she stood in front of them for the first time in two months. They hadn’t even been able to calm her down or get a straight answer out of her before Lena had shown up on the windowsill, so Alex leapt to conclusions, as she was wont to do, and she reacted with the brute force of an Auror, as she was wont to do.

 

            On her knees now, drawing in gasping sobs as she finally came apart, the shock and adrenaline catching up with her as tears blurred her eyes, Lena was reaching for Kara with her right hand, fingers fluttering nervously around her as she stared in horror at her face, while the other tightly clutched the cloak around her shoulders. It wasn’t until a hand grabbed a fistful of the cloak and hauled her to her feet that Lena was rather rudely reminded that they weren’t alone, and she was very unwelcome there as she found herself face-to-face with a very angry witch.

 

            She didn’t even have her wand in hand to defend herself as Alex flicked her own at the front door to open it, dragged Lena towards it and threw her outside. Stumbling backwards down the short path, Lena’s Splinched leg and twisted ankle buckled beneath the weight of her body, and she went sprawling onto the wet pavement, scraping her right elbow as she landed awkwardly. Advancing on her with her wand aloft, Alex’s face was hard with her hatred, and Lena was a pitiful sight before her, left hand still clutching the cloak around her shoulders, face pale and tear-stained as she scrambled backwards to the lip of the curb, in the gutter now. There was nothing she could do to help herself, knowing she’d caused this, that she’d created this rift, this lie, which had turned the sister she’d never had into a person who hated her so completely that Lena knew there was not a single word she could say that Alex would believe. 

 

            But in the few seconds it had taken Alex to haul Lena outside, Kara had found Lena’s wand on the floor, her shouts filling the cramped hallway as Eliza and Kelly rushed out of the living room, everything chaotic, everything happening so fast. And it was Kara who barrelled into her sister from behind, pushing her off-balance, darting in front of her and levelling Lena’s wand in her face as her hand shook and her words came out spitting and hoarse from the sheer desperation and fear that filled her.

 

            “Don’t you fucking touch her!”

 

            “Get out of the way, Kara,” Alex fumed.

 

            “No.”

 

            “She’s a Death Eater. Get out of the way.”

 

            “No! No, she’s not!” Kara shouted, desperate and panicked as Alex advanced, forcing her back a few steps. “A spy! She’s a fucking spy.”

 

            That gave Alex pause for a moment, her mouth opening and closing as her face crumpled. Kara managed to force her back two steps, roughly shoving her away and then holding her arm out to bar her sister’s access to Lena.

 

            “What?” Alex flatly asked.

 

            “She’s a spy,” Kara breathlessly explained through her ragged sobs, letting out a frayed laugh as tears ran down her cheeks. “She’s been a spy the whole fucking time. Ask Dumbledore. Go on, ask him. This- this whole thing is his doing. She’s been spying for us . All of the letters I was passing; who do you think my source was, huh?”

 

            Licking her lips, Alex glanced back over her shoulder, and she didn’t have to say a word as she looked at Kelly, who grimly nodded and turned away. Through the doorway and windows, Lena watched Kelly Floo somewhere to go and corroborate Kara’s story, and Lena felt a flicker of relief that maybe things would be okay, that they’d be able to resolve this quickly, that Alex would believe her sister. But Alex was stubborn to a fault, too arrogant to accept that she’d been wrong without irrefutable proof of it, and she jerked her chin towards Lena, gesturing with her wand as her brown eyes darted down to where she was kneeling on the pavement.

 

            “If you’re not a Death Eater, show me your arm.”

 

            “No,” Kara exclaimed with such vehemence and horror that it only served to spur Alex on.

 

            Forging ahead, grabbing Kara’s wrist as she propelled her backwards, closer and closer to Lena, Alex let her sister go once Kara’s feet hit the pavement. Right hand reaching for Kara, Lena crawled towards her on her knees, fingers clutching at the filthy pants she was wearing, half-hidden behind her as she hugged Kara’s leg, eyes closing as she clung to her for reassurance. Drawing in deep breaths to steady herself, Lena listened to them argue for a minute more as she tried to pluck up the courage, tried to swallow her pain and her shame.

 

            “No,” Kara echoed, standing squarely in front of Lena as she faced down her sister, her wand pressed into Alex’s chest. “You lay a finger on her and I swear I’ll curse you into the next fucking fortnight.”

 

            Alex would never hurt her sister, that much they all knew, but her patience was thin right then, and Lena could see the way she wrestled with her exasperation and her anger. Trying to snare Kara’s wand arm, Alex curtly tried to reason with her, their voices overlapping as they argued, while Lena clutched Kara’s leg, her own bleeding into the street, while she couldn’t even feel her left collarbone, so numb that it didn’t even hurt. Breathlessly sobbing, the sounds hitching in her throat, she couldn’t even bring herself to tell Kara it was okay , that she could step aside. Her throat wouldn’t work, so tight around the painful sobs that worked up from her chest.

 

            “I mean it,” Kara warned her, her voice wavering as she fiercely protected the woman she loved, the intensity of it so unfamiliar that her family were shocked by her behaviour as she stood in front of Lena, hand shaking and chin stubbornly jutting forward. 

 

            “It’s okay,” Lena finally managed to speak, the words coming out broken and tired.

 

            Cold and shivering as she knelt in the cloak, Lena just wanted it to be over, and she didn’t want to wait for however long it would take Kelly to come back. At the very least, they could move this indoors; she just had to show Alex her arm. The right one was easy, letting go of Kara’s leg to shake the cloak off it, extending it as Kara let out a small sound of disbelieving panic as she glanced down, following Alex’s shifting attention. Lighting her wand, stepping in close, a small scuffle between the sisters as Kara shoved her away, and Alex stepped in closer again, she illuminated the unblemished skin of Lena’s right arm. Tucking it away again, Lena had to swallow her resentment over the humiliation of it all before she hesitantly uncovered her left arm and held it out. She heard the whimpered groan of objection as Kara’s shoulders slumped, her wand arm lowering as she turned and sank to a crouch, drawing Lena into her, holding her tightly as Alex inspected her left arm.

 

            Wand illuminating her pale forearm, Alex didn’t find the black stain of a Dark Mark, but when she saw the silvery scar, she peered closer to read the words before she flinched back, her face crumpling with confusion. “What’s that?”

 

            Whispering apologies into Lena’s hair, both of them quietly crying, shaking with the traumatic events of their day, not quite believing they were in front of each other either, Kara ignored her sister. But Alex had checked both of her arms and found nothing incriminating, so Kara started to gather Lena up, helping her to her feet, her trembling hands pulling the cloak securely over Lena’s bare body before she started to shepherd her up the pathway, no matter what her sister said or thought.

 

            White-faced and wide-eyed with disturbed confusion, Alex stammered soundlessly for a moment as she faltered, before she repeated herself with more urgency. “Kara, what is that?”

 

            Turning so quickly Alex didn’t have time to flinch, Kara smacked her across the face so hard that her sister let out a small grunt of surprised pain as the blow rocked her. It was the first time Kara had ever hit her, and even Eliza didn’t scold her for it, their mother standing in the doorway, pale-faced as she merely pressed her fingers to her lips and swallowed her shock. Voice low and fraught with fury, Kara couldn’t keep it from trembling as she quietly spoke.

 

            “I will never forgive you for this.”

 

            Lena made a small whine of objection at the back of her throat, her shoulders slumped as she looked at Kara’s back with an ache in her teary eyes. She hated this, hated the division she’d caused, had hoped that when the moment to clear her name had come, it would have been more amicable, slowly earning back the trust she’d purposely broken, instead of this muddled arguing with aching injuries on a quiet Muggle street at night. But that was the end of it, for now, as Kara turned away from her speechless sister and moved towards Lena. Her anger faltered as worry took its place, her hands gentle as she helped Lena to the front door, where Eliza stepped aside to let them both in.

Chapter 60

            Limping over the threshold, Lena drew in shallow, gasping sobs as she stumbled over the scattered boots, slippers and muddy wellies in the narrow hallway, her teeth chattering as she moved in a daze, shepherded into the living room by Kara’s strong hands. Made to sit on the sofa, Lena trembled as she held the cloak tightly closed around herself, reeling from the confusion of being in Eliza’s living room, the cramped space filled with comfortable furniture and the cosy glow of candlelight. It could’ve been indistinguishable from any of the nights Lena had spent there over the years, except for the bedlam of the last fifteen minutes, and the horror of the last fifteen months.

 

            Kara was on her knees, wedged into the narrow gap between the sofa and coffee table as she cupped Lena’s chin in a filthy hand, devastation on her lacerated and bloody face as she took in Lena’s makeup smeared across her cheeks, and the reddened skin of tomorrow’s bruises. And all Lena could look at was Kara, a pitiful sound escaping her as she examined her beaten face, eyes tracing over the injuries as she catalogued them with a dangerous gleam in her teary eyes. Softly crying, Lena reached out and pried her wand from Kara’s hand as Alex hovered in the archway, arms crossed over her chest as she brimmed with anxiety, brown eyes wide in her pale face as she bit her nails. Eliza was in the kitchen, the frantic sound of cupboard doors banging open and closed drifting through to them. 

 

            With shaky hands, Lena reached up and took Kara’s glasses off her face, her bottom lip quivering as she took in the black eyes, the swelling of her right eye from the cut in her eyebrow, which had bled freely. Her left cheekbone was split as well, and her lips, thick and swollen, and Lena felt a keen pain in her chest as she looked at what her brother had done. Maybe not by his hand, but by his orders, most definitely. Drawing in hitching breaths, Lena ran a hand over her wet face as she tried to compose herself, unable to speak as she kept choking on the words for a spell to heal Kara, to fix her crooked nose, to take away her pain. And Kara was whispering apologies as her hands ran over Lena’s shoulders, tears running down her cheeks as she cried without making a sound, in contrast to Lena’s quiet sobs.

 

            Eliza hurried back in, a bowl of steaming water levitating behind her, carrying an armful of whatever healing supplies she could find as she let them spill onto the sofa cushions beside Lena. Eyes dropping to them, Lena reached out, fumbling through the paraphernalia as her eyes ran over labels, finding a Wound-Cleaning potion, some Essence of Dittany, a tub of bruise salve and some gauze, clean flannels and a Sleeping Draught. Grabbing the vial of Dittany and a flannel, Lena’s fingers were clumsy as she worked to unscrew the lid, pinching the dropper before she pulled the pipette out of the vial and moved it towards Kara’s face, to the little cuts and scrapes. 

 

            Stopping her, Kara shook her head slightly as she took the pipette from Lena’s fingers. “No, no, we need to get you healed up. You need to- you need to tell me what to do, okay? I need you to- please, tell me how to help you,” Kara breathlessly begged, her hand cupping Lena’s cheek before she dropped it, eyes roaming over her cloaked figure, at a loss for what to do.

 

            Lena opened her mouth, but the only thing that came out was a small, helpless sound as she shifted and felt nauseating pain radiate from her left shoulder. Her pain was obvious to see in the pinch of white around her mouth, the sheen of sweat on her face, and she could feel every break, every bruise as she sat there, unable to heal herself because she couldn’t stop crying. And it wasn’t even in the frightening way she’d fallen apart for the first time in front of Kara; it was quiet and constant, the breath catching in her throat as she shallowly inhaled, unable to calm herself, nose blocked, cheeks blotchy and her tears endless. If she could’ve spoken past the lump in her throat, Lena’s words would’ve been healing spells to fix Kara, but she couldn’t even do that, and was dimly aware that she might’ve been in shock, adrenaline waning and leaving her feeling weak and exhausted.

 

            “Mum,” Kara pleaded, turning her face slightly but not even looking at Eliza, unable to tear her eyes off Lena. “Mum, please. Please help her.”

 

            Floundering, unsure what to do, used to healing scrapes and bruises and the occasional mishap with one of her plants, Eliza grabbed a blanket from the back of the sofa and warily approached. She shook it out and draped it over Lena’s lap, offering her extra warmth and cover. Blue eyes full of worry, Eliza eased the clean flannel out of her tight grasp, her expression aching, and spoke softly and slowly, as if speaking to a wild animal.

 

            “It’s alright, sweetie. You’re alright now. Just … tell me where it hurts and I’ll see what I can do.”

 

            Alex let out a huff, running a hand over her face, and turned, walking towards the front door and leaving. No one even acknowledged her departure, and Lena just kept shaking her head as she swallowed painfully, then swallowed again, the ache in her chest so keen that she couldn’t stop the tears. She could taste them in her mouth, and she wiped her face in the cloak, sniffing, her face still stinging slightly from the hex that had caught her in the nose, but that didn’t seem to matter then. Trying to keep her left arm still, Lena rummaged through the pile of supplies on the sofa and picked out the bruise salve, passing it to Eliza.

 

            “H-here.”

 

            “Okay,” Eliza murmured, “okay, where do I need to use it?”

 

            “K-” Lena choked off, drawing in a hitching breath and then pressing her mouth into a flat line before she tried again. “Kara.”

 

            “No, no, I’m okay,” Kara insisted, her hands balled in the cloak, a desperate edge to her words as she stubbornly set her jaw. “You- you’re bleeding. Tell me where it hurts. Please.”

 

            Lips moving soundlessly in a plea, Lena’s eyelids closed as she drew in ragged breaths, and she felt Kara’s grip tighten in the worn fabric, feeling the weight of her in her lap as she opened her eyes again to find her hunched over, forehead pressed to Lena’s thigh. Feeling somewhat faint, a little dizzy, a headache pounding behind her eyes, Lena was angry at herself, feeling so helpless. 

 

            But the door was opening then, a waft of cold air drifting in before the door was slammed shut, Alex making a hasty reappearance with someone else in tow. Three pairs of eyes looked over at the intrusion, and Lena blinked dumbly at the sight of Sam, who was likewise looking at her, and then at Kara, with a pale look of shock on her face. Hurrying over to them, dressed in her Healer robes, dragged from a shift at St. Mungo’s that Lena had left her to finish when she’d clocked out half an hour ago, Sam didn’t ask any questions, just sank to a crouch beside Kara and reached out for her face. Flinching in surprise, Kara jerked her head aside, face crumpling with frustration.

 

            “I’m fine,” she said as her voice cracked. “It’s- she’s hurt.”

 

            Nodding, Sam turned her attention to Lena, hazel eyes wide and searching, worry in the depths of them as she tried to retain her professional composure, treating her like any other patient. Her voice was gentle as she spoke, a wavering smile at the corners of her mouth as she tried not to let it show how unnerved she was by the sight of Lena crying.

 

            “Alright, Healer Luthor, what’s the diagnosis?” Sam lightly asked as she sifted through the healing supplies on the sofa and clicked her tongue.

 

            Picking up a Calming Draught from the pile, Sam uncorked it and raised it to Lena’s lips, sobering up as she stared at her with concern. “Drink this for me. Go on.”

 

            Turning her face aside, trying to shrug off her friend’s gentle grasp, Lena made a sound of objection at the back of her throat. “Kara.”

 

            “I’ll take a look at Kara in a minute,” Sam assured her. “The quicker you let me sort you out, the quicker I can get to her, okay? Come on, that’s it.”

 

            Lena let her force the potion past her lips, swallowing the cloying sweetness of it, coughing as a sob hitched in her throat as it worked its way down. The effect was quick, a few seconds dragging by before she felt it spread through her, an ease radiating through her chest as her sobs stopped, as she felt peace blanket her emotions. It was strange, it left her feeling oddly vacant, but Lena calmed down as the potion seeped into her bloodstream. There was a palpable air of relief in the room as well, as she finally stopped sobbing, and she looked at Kara, fixing her with a bloodshot stare.

 

            “Let me,” Lena rasped, holding her right hand out.

 

            “Let- let Sam heal you first,” Kara softly urged her, still holding the pipette of Dittany in her hand. “Mine’s all … superficial.”

 

            Despite calming down, hot tears spilt from Lena’s eyes as her lips twitched with anger. She couldn’t feel it properly, her emotions muffled by the potion, but she was going to kill her brother one day. And she wasn’t just saying that to soothe the anger; Lena really did believe that if she saw him again, she wouldn’t be able to stop herself from doing it. Keeping her eyes glued on Kara, all Lena wanted to do was touch her face, heal her wounds, trace the lines of her features, each facet of her memorised. This wasn’t how it was supposed to be; this wasn’t how she was supposed to come home. She cared more about Kara’s safety than her own, but Lena was forced to endure Sam’s gentle questions as she mumbled answers to them and kept her eyes glued to Kara’s face.

 

            “Where does it hurt?”

 

            Lena pulled the blanket aside with shaky hands, pushing the cloak up, and Sam took in the chunk of flesh taken out of Lena’s calf, wet blood sheeting down her skin, and sucked in a breath. She manoeuvred Lena’s leg so she could get a better glimpse of it, and Eliza retreated to the archway to give her space to work, Alex already relegating herself to the bottom steps of the staircase, while Kara stubbornly remained where she was, although she perched on the edge of the coffee table for comfort. 

 

            Taking a Wound-Cleaning potion from the collection, Sam unstoppered it and poured a generous dose into the gaping wound on Lena’s calf, before she picked up the uncapped bottle of Dittany and looked around, before Kara handed her the pipette. Taking it, Sam squeezed the dropper full of it into the wound, Lena going rigid as it hissed and smoked, the pain almost blinding. Murmuring spells as well, Sam knit new flesh together as the Dittany worked to seal it, before she pushed the cloak up higher, not questioning where Lena’s clothes had gone as she got to work on the larger cluster on her friend’s thigh. Wrapping both wounds in bandages when she was done, Sam moved onto Lena’s right arm at her instruction, the laceration not deep but quite long where it cut across her bicep, and she followed the same process, cleaning, sealing and binding it, wrapping her right ankle as well, which was merely sprained, before Lena hoarsely informed her of her left shoulder, the collarbone definitely broken, perhaps even the top of her humerus.

 

            Lena had to let go of the cloak to let Sam check, had to bare her left arm, and Kara silently reached out to adjust it over Lena, making it seem casual as she draped the cloak over her forearm, as if trying to shift it across her chest. Sam didn’t see the scar on her arm, and Lena was able to breathe a little easier as her friend cast spells and felt by hand to determine how she was injured, what was broken. Humming to herself, Sam grimaced as she nodded slowly.

 

            “Clavicle and the coracoid process are both broken. In several places.” She hesitated a moment, hazel eyes flitting up to Lena’s impassive face, tearstained and pale. “What was it? A Blasting Curse?”

 

            Making a vague sound of confirmation, Lena’s mouth twitched at the corners with contempt, and Sam didn’t question her any further as she quietly spoke over the broken bones, casting complex spellwork requiring her full concentration as the bones were knitted back together and wrapped in bandages. Taking her left hand, Sam guided it to her right shoulder, making Lena keep it bent in that position to alleviate some of the pressure on her freshly healed collarbone, nothing to make a sling out of as she wished for St. Mungo’s stock of supplies. There were a few scrapes and bruises, but they weren’t important enough to warrant Sam poring over every single one with her wand and a salve, and no sooner had she finished with Lena’s shoulder did Lena gesture to Kara.

 

            “Her turn.”

 

            She seemed incapable of saying more than a word or two at a time, residual pain lingering in her body, the cold in her bones leaving her trembling on the sofa as her bottom lip quivered and she stared intently at Kara. Shifting her attention to Kara, Sam loomed over her, gently probing at her face, washing blood away with the warm water and a flannel to get a better look. When she healed Kara’s broken nose, Kara let out a small yelp before clamping her split lips closed, swallowing the rest of it as the cartilage was wrenched back into place. Thumbing the cut above her eyebrow, the cut lip, the swollen side of her face, Sam wordlessly healed them before smearing the bruise salve over her face and quietly asking where else she was hurt.

 

            Lena didn’t want to know the answer to that, her eyes smarting as Kara uncurled her left hand, the last two fingers crooked and swollen. Tracing her fingers up them, Sam murmured a spell to heal them, setting them straight again, before Kara pulled up her filthy long-sleeve shirt to reveal one large, dark bruise covering the left side of her prominent ribs. She looked as if someone had stomped on her or repeatedly kicked her, and Sam drew in a sharp hiss through her teeth before her fingers probed along Kara’s ribcage, finding two fractures and patching them up, before she smeared some of the bruise salve over it and then wrapped her torso in bandages.

 

            “That’s it,” Kara murmured, looking a right sight better, but thin and dirty from months spent roughing it.

 

            Nodding, Sam vanished the bloody water in the bowl and gathered up the healing supplies, thanking Eliza when she stepped forward to take them from her. Turning back to Lena, Sam sank to a crouch and laid a hand on her knee, looking up at her with that confused concern again as she quietly spoke to her. She didn’t try to drag an explanation out of her, recognising the distant look of shock, of exhaustion, just tried to comfort her as best as she could.

 

            “You get some rest, okay? I’ll come and see you tomorrow.”

 

            Nodding, wiping her face, Lena sniffed but couldn’t speak. Kara thanked Sam in her stead, climbing to her feet and moving aside so Sam could Floo back to St. Mungo’s, ducking into the fireplace with a pinch of Floo powder and leaving with an uneasy expression on her face. The silence inside the house was suffocating, and Kara moved to help Lena stand, the ghost of pain making her wince with the effort it took to push herself up, before she led her out of the room past Eliza, who didn’t speak, unsure what to say, looking stressed and uncertain, to the bottom of the stairs, where Alex was sitting with her head in her hands.

 

            At their approach, Alex raised her head, blinking herself out of her thoughts as she hurriedly scrambled to her feet, stepping off the stairs and pressing herself up against the front door. Hands on Lena’s back, Kara urged her up each step as Lena’s teeth chattered, shoulders stiff as she hunched, and led her to the bathroom instead of the bedroom when she realised she needed to get her warm. Shutting the door, Kara made her sit on the closed lid of the toilet and ran the bath, putting the plug in and then sinking to a crouch in front of Lena, her fingers ghosting over her cheeks.

 

            “Hey,” Kara murmured, touching their foreheads together. Lena’s eyes shut as tears stung them, and she let out a choked sob, her chest cleaving at the tender sound of her voice, at the presence of her. And neither of them had to leave this time, rushing off to keep their cover or pass a message. “It’s okay, it’s okay. You’re safe now. I’m sorry. I’m sorry that I- I didn’t mean for- for this to happen, for you to-”

 

            Cutting off as she found herself unable to speak, Kara let out a shaky breath. Her chin dimpled with the effort it took not to cry, and Lena cupped her face in her cold hands, keeping their foreheads pressed together as she drew in ragged breaths, the effects of the Calming Draught quick to work but quick to wear off as well, cracks appearing in her facade again. Her lips chased a ghost of a kiss, merely a brush over Kara’s chapped mouth, and she wanted to hold her tightly, annoyed by the residual pain in her collarbone from the simple act of moving to touch her face, let alone wrapping her in her arms.

 

            Pulling away a minute later, the tiles of the bathroom sweating in the steam of the bath, Kara climbed to her feet and shut off the water before turning back to Lena, coaxing her to her feet and out of the cloak. Disappearing her bandages, Kara helped her into the bath, and Lena sank into the too-hot water, watching as it clouded with not-quite-dried blood. As Lena studied her hands below the water, pink started to bloom across her pallid skin as the heat worked into her, her shivers subsiding the longer she sat there. 

 

            The water started to cool as they both remained silent, Kara kneeling on the floor at the side of the tub, and she eventually moved to start washing Lena’s skin for her, gentle movements forming suds as lingering blood and sweat were rinsed away. The ends of her dark hair dipped into the water, fanning across the gritty surface, and Kara grabbed a towel to help her out, swaddling her in the softness of it and gently rubbing it over her skin to dry her off. Guiding her back onto the toilet seat as the bath drained, Kara went to grab the door handle, and Lena finally spoke more than two words as her head jerked up, eyes fearful and pleading. 

 

            “Don’t go,” she begged, her voice cracking as she held the towel around herself. “Please don’t leave me.”

 

            “I’m just going to get you some pyjamas to put on,” Kara assured her, taking a step back towards her, cupping the side of her head and ducking to press a kiss to the top of her dark hair.

 

            Shaking her head, bottom lip wobbling as her emotions crept back up on her, a deep pit of dread in her stomach, chest beating madly in her chest, Lena felt hot tears on her cheeks. “Please don’t. I don’t want you to go.”

 

            “Okay,” Kara whispered, ducking to kiss the top of her head again. “Okay, okay, I won’t.”

 

            Instead, she sank to a crouch with Lena’s wand in hand and cast a spell to rebandage Lena’s various injuries on her leg, then her bicep and opposite shoulder. Aware that she was filthy, a mess of old sweat, dirt and blood mingling with the new, caked on over weeks without a proper wash, Kara apologetically made Lena wait as she washed herself, shedding her clothes and bandages and getting into the tub with a mere inch of water in it as hot water poured from the taps. Lena watched her as she drew in quiet, gasping sobs, wanting to tell her not to rush, wanting to help wash her tangled, bloodstained curls, but she remained where she was seated, watching as the tub filled, the water clouding with all of the dirt and blood Kara washed away. 

 

            Kara had to drain it before it even got above halfway, scrubbing old blood and dirt from beneath torn fingernails, shampooing her hair as brown water sluiced down her back, staining the bath, tide marks left on the sides of it when she let the water out a second time. Hurrying out of the bath, Kara hastily dried herself off with a towel and then wrapped it around her body, wincing gingerly at the pain in her ribs, ignored in favour of fretting over Lena as she jammed her broken glasses back on her face and ushered her out of the bathroom and into the bedroom, murmuring softly to her. 

 

            “Come on, let’s get you dressed,” Kara whispered, easing the bedroom door shut.

 

            She hadn’t seen her family in months, unbeknownst to Lena, yet she had no intention of going downstairs to explain it all to them, to fill her in on where she’d been and what had happened to lead up to the events of that night. Kara just deposited Lena on the edge of Alex’s bed and rummaged through her drawers for pyjamas for them both. Soft, pilled pants were worked over Lena’s legs, and then Kara helped her into a long-sleeved top, and then into bed. Enveloped in the smell of her, Lena beneath the blankets as she watched Kara dress, her hair wet and tangled, her ribs still horribly bruised as she’d washed off the salve, and her glasses cracked as she took them off and put them on the desk with Lena’s wand, before crawling into the narrow bed beside Lena and wrapping her in her embrace.

 

            Closing her eyes, tears she thought she’d spent stung Lena’s eyes once more, and she cried in Kara’s arms as the weak light of a candle kept the dark at bay. Face pressed into her chest as she shook with quiet sobs, Lena gripped handfuls of Kara’s top as she was held close, breathing in the smell of her, while Kara kissed her hair, holding it together remarkably well, if only for Lena’s sake. Feeling like a child, Lena burrowed into the solid warmth of her, her mind furring at the edges now, everything catching up to her now that she was safe and warm and healed. 

 

            Still, she cried herself to sleep, and then slept peacefully for the first time in fifteen months. Pale sunlight shone in through a gap in the closed curtains when she woke, confused for a moment as she found her face inches from the wall, everything wrong. Everything so blissfully right as her mind caught up and her hand ghosted over the cold mattress at her back, the narrow bed empty of her girlfriend. She sat up quickly, panic filling her as she turned, her shoulders immediately slumping as she found Kara sitting on Alex’s bed, watching her with intense blue eyes as the shaft of morning light spun her hair to silver and gold. 

 

            There were hollows under her eyes that Lena could see clearly now, and she took in the scratches and faint shadows of bruises, the leanness to Kara’s face and body. They hadn’t seen each other for nine months, and Lena didn’t know what to say. She wanted to cry again, her eyes still swollen, a shiny, tight feeling to the skin on her face. They stared at each other for a moment before Kara stood and crossed the few feet between the beds, the mattress jostling as she sat on the edge of it, reaching out to cup Lena’s head as she bowed her own to press a kiss to her brow.

 

            “Hey, you,” Kara murmured, her voice tender and aching as a wavering smile curled the corners of her mouth.

 

            The breath caught in Lena’s throat as she scrambled to kick the blankets off and threw herself at Kara, face crumpling as she buried her face in the crook of her neck. Her hands restlessly roamed her body, splayed over her ribs, ghosting up her spine, cupping the back of her head. Lena couldn’t get close enough to her, pulse racing, throat tight around her desperation. Letting out a small sound of pure agony, Lena pulled back, her fingers featherlight over Kara’s freckled and scarred cheeks, before there was enough space between them for her to crush her lips against Kara’s, bruising and deprived.

 

            Kara kissed her back, softer, lingering and sweet as she sighed into it, her dry lips parting slightly, mouth gentle as she pressed her fingertips firmly against Lena’s back. Breaking it off a moment later, Kara stared at her face with wonder shining in her eyes and let out a frayed laugh, sniffing as the shininess turned to glassy tears, overcome with her emotions. Leaning in, Lena lightly bumped her nose against Kara’s, a rasping laugh stuttering out of her mouth as elated relief swept through her, so strong that she felt weak.

 

            And she was. Lena had been strong for so long, the mental burden of her spying, of her brother’s company, that she was tired. Already flagging, she went limp in Kara’s arms, her breaths shallow and quick, but she didn’t cry again, no energy for it. As if sensing her exhaustion, Kara eased her away, reaching behind Lena to fix her pillows so she could prop her up against them. Sinking back with relief, Lena’s body willingly gave in, but so long as she could look at Kara, she didn’t care.

 

            “Are you okay?” Kara asked her, apprehension in her mournful eyes, as if she didn’t really want to know the answer to that. It was obvious that beneath the surface, Lena was definitely not okay.

 

            “I’m okay,” Lena murmured, her voice thick with emotion as she nodded firmly. 

 

            And she was. She was better than she’d been for the last fifteen months. The only thought that filled her mind right then was that it was over. Of course, they weren’t even a year into open war, and things would undoubtedly get worse, but there was no going back for Lena. There was no chance she could step back into her family’s home without endangering herself now, which meant she wouldn’t have to leave again, wouldn’t have to leave Kara. But fifteen months apart would have inevitably changed something between them, and Lena was a bit unsure of herself right then as she stared at her, wondering what came next.

 

            Reaching out, she took Kara’s hand, her fingers warm and rough in Lena’s. “And you? What did he-”

 

            Unable to finish the question, swallowing the tail of it, Lena closed her eyes and shook her head slightly. Looking at Kara again, her throat bobbed, and she drew in a shuddering breath. Reaching out, cupping the underside of Lena’s jaw, thumb swiping over her cheek, Kara smiled thinly.

 

            “Let’s not talk about that right now,” she whispered, hesitating a moment as her gaze lowered, a shadow of pain crossing her features, before her eyes were back on Lena’s, intensely blue and full of relief. “I’m okay. I’m- I’m just glad you’re safe.”

 

            Running a hand over her face, Lena cleared her throat, feeling dehydrated and sore, and let out another laugh. It sounded strange coming out of her, unfamiliar and hesitant, and Lena pressed her fingertips to her closed eyelids for a moment before dropping her hands. She didn’t know what to say, still somewhat reeling from the way it had all happened, the sudden change in it all, ambushed at home as she’d fallen into her brother’s trap, to wake up in her girlfriend’s bed in her mother’s home, safe and sound.

 

            “Don’t you ever do that to me again,” Kara softly said after a moment, her voice low and stern.

 

            Meeting Kara’s eyes, Lena’s lips twitched faintly with amusement. “Which part?”

 

            Giving her a reproving look, head tilting to the side as the corners of her mouth turned down disapprovingly, Kara’s shoulders sloped as she slowly exhaled. “I’ve never been so terrified in my life. I didn’t know if you- he could’ve-”

 

            “He didn’t. But … I was okay with that, as long as you were safely away.”

 

            Drawing in a few ragged breaths, a scowl on her face as she blinked rapidly, Kara’s mouth was a small pout as she gathered her composure and then replied. “Never again. Okay?”

 

            “Okay,” Lena whispered in agreement.

 

            Taking her word for it, relief washed over Kara, and she nodded, smoothing a hand over Lena’s dark hair. “It’s almost lunchtime; let me get you something to eat. No, you stay here. Rest. I’ll be back in a minute, okay?”

 

            Easing back against the pillows, a flicker of panic filling her at the thought of being away from Kara, Lena nodded. There was nothing to fear; Kara would only be downstairs, safe inside her mother’s house, within earshot if Lena needed to call for her. And Kara had her wand stuck through her twisted curls, keeping it held up and out of her face. No harm would come to her if Lena wasn’t there. Nodding again, Lena sank further into the pillows at Kara’s insistence and watched her slip out of the room. Pulling the blankets up to her chest and laying her arms flat on top, Lena stared up at the ceiling as she heard footsteps descend the staircase.

 

            Not even a minute later, too soon for Kara to have gone down and come back up with something, there was a light tap on the door. Lena didn’t speak, just lowered her eyes to the door, and she watched it warily open as Alex stuck her head inside. She looked a wreck, like she hadn’t slept a wink all night, with the faint shadow of a bruise on her cheek. When Lena didn’t object to her presence, she crossed the threshold and eased the door most of the way shut, nervously running her hands over the thighs of her pants as she padded down the gap between the beds with hunched shoulders, like a sheepish dog. Sinking onto the mattress of her own childhood bed, Alex didn’t speak, and Lena didn’t look at her, just turned her attention back to the ceiling as a lump got stuck in her throat. 

 

            The silence was heavy, each second dragging on, until Alex moved. She practically slithered off the bed, folding as if she were boneless, kneeling on the carpet at Lena’s bedside as she folded her arms on the edge of the mattress and pressed her forehead to them. Lena could hear the quiet, shallow breaths she drew in and out, before she inhaled deeply, her shoulders expanding, before she sighed. Lifting her head, she licked her lips, eyes glassy as she swallowed thickly and reached out to cradle Lena’s hand between her own, and her voice was ragged with guilt when she spoke, breaking as she struggled.

            

            “I am so … unbelievably sorry.”

 

            “It’s okay,” Lena mumbled, wanting to wince at the awkwardness of it.

 

            She didn’t feel like it was fair to blame Alex for falling for Lena’s deliberate deceit. It wouldn’t have worked if she hadn’t believed her, and Lena had gone through this before, years ago, a hurt teenager who’d blamed Kara for believing her too easily, when that had been her intention. She was an adult now, with more perspective, and was more secure in herself to not feel unjustly blamed for the purposeful persona she’d portrayed. Making Alex believe the worst of her had kept Lena safe; it was Lena’s love that had been her undoing.

 

            “No,” Alex murmured, “no, it’s not.”

 

            Kneeling there, frowning as she rubbed the bridge of her nose, Alex was silent for a few more seconds before she spoke, halting and confused. “I didn’t believe her, you know. When you left. Not at first. She showed up … like that, and I thought- I thought you were dead. I didn’t think for a second that you- that you’d ever-”

 

            “I didn’t,” Lena hoarsely interrupted, swallowing past the tightness in her throat. “I never laid a finger on her, I swear. She did it to herself; I did the same to myself. To sell the lie.”

 

            “It worked. I’d never needed a reason to distrust a Slytherin before, but when she gave me one … I didn’t want to believe it. Not until she said you’d done that to her. And then the second time she said you’d done that …”

 

            “Second time?”

 

            Running a hand over her face, Alex shook her head, blinking as she thought. “My mum saw you in Diagon Alley. She thought something was wrong, that … it wasn’t what Kara said it was. She said she saw bruises. Um … she tried to talk Kara into helping you, and then … she went to see you. Came back covered in blood. When I saw you at the hospital … I just saw red.”

 

            “Oh,” Lena choked on a laugh as understanding swept through her, and a keen ache of fondness for her mother-in-law’s compassion. “I never did figure out what I’d done that time.”

 

            “I’m sorry.”

 

            “It’s okay. If I had , I would’ve expected much worse.”

 

            Hesitating, Alex’s eyes flickered to Lena’s, her lips parted as she deliberated over whether to ask. “The bruises …”

 

            “My brother,” Lena croaked, eyes closing as she rubbed her eyes. “Um … did Kelly speak to Dumbledore? I mean, you- you believe it all?”

 

            “She didn’t, but she spoke to others. J’onn - my boss - and Moody and Shacklebolt, too. They all confirmed it. I think- I think I knew it, or I wanted to believe it, when she said it, but, um … well, I didn’t trust her. You’ve always been her strength and her weakness; I wasn’t sure if she was protecting you out of misplaced love.”

 

            “You weren’t wrong for thinking that. You- you did the best you could with the information you had. No one can blame you for that. It’s- I hated doing that to you, to you all. I understand how … confusing it must be for you, how your opinion of me might’ve changed, so I know it might take some time to earn back-”

 

            Alex let out an almost hysterical laugh of surprise, her brown eyes bewildered but amused as she fondly shook her head. “Merlin, you silly cow, we loved you. And then you left her. And I’ve been so mad at you for hurting my sister and taking away my other sister, all to support them . But you’re our family, and I have never been so relieved to have been proven wrong.”

 

            “I’m sorry,” Lena said with a wan smile. “It was horrible. I- it wasn’t just her; I left you all. But … she knew the real reason, at least. I just- I was trying to keep us all safe.”

 

            Heaving a sigh, letting go of Lena’s hand and rubbing her tired eyes, Alex hummed. “I know. I know that now . And, well, I’m glad she knew. I’m glad- I’m glad you didn’t break her heart, too. And I’m sorry for slagging you off to everyone.”

 

            Lena laughed at that, the sound hoarse and uneven, surprised amusement flashing through her before she sighed. “I’ve missed you, Alex.”

 

            “Yeah, I’ve missed you, too. I hope- I hope you can forgive me. At some point.”

 

            “There’s nothing to forgive,” Lena dismissively replied.

 

            “Yes, there is. I think I- whatever trust there was between us … I know I broke it, and I can’t take back what I did, I’m just- I’m sorry it happened the way that it did. I wish it hadn’t.”

 

            “Me too,” Lena murmured.

 

            “And … are you okay?”

 

            Reaching out to pat her arm, Lena nodded as she swallowed thickly. “Yeah, I’ll be fine.”

 

            Mouth a grim line, guilt in the way she lowered her gaze, in the lines of her shoulders, Alex was silent for a bit longer this time, seconds dragging by, and Lena could see the urge building in her. She could see the perturbed look in her eyes, the pained look of apprehension, and she knew what she wanted to ask. It was only natural, she supposed, but she felt a flush working its way up her neck and into her cheeks before Alex had even asked. But of course she did, because it was how she’d broken Lena’s trust, by forcing her hand, making her offer up her arms for inspection to prove her innocence.

 

            “The scar …” Alex haltingly started, the building tension of waiting for her to ask snapping, almost a relief for Lena. “Where-”

 

            Fumbling with the cuff of her long-sleeved top, Lena dragged it up to her elbow, exposing the pale forearm with the silvery words scarred into the skin. Her arm was on top of the blankets, right in front of where Alex knelt, and Lena swallowed thickly, her cheeks stained red and a tremor in her voice as she spoke fast, as if getting the words out quicker would make Alex forget about it quicker, move on from it.

 

            “My mum- um, when I was younger- well, she always expected me to do well, to get perfect marks, and all that, so even before I went to Hogwarts, I had to study and work hard. And if I misbehaved, or if I got a question wrong, or even if I just looked at her wrong and she was in a bad mood, I’d be punished for it. She had a Blood Quill, and she’d make me write lines with it. This went on for- for a few years, um … right up until I graduated from school and moved out. There were other things as well. The quill … well, I got used to it after a while, but the other things … I’d prefer not to talk about that, but … I’m sure you can imagine why I’m not so fond of my family.”

 

            Lena turned her head on the pillows, giving Alex a weak smile. Looking at her, she took in the white look of horror and shock on her face, and Lena started to work her sleeve back down, covering the words again. Eyes darting down to Lena’s forearm, then back up to her face, Alex wordlessly stammered for a moment, mouth opening and closing, before she managed to speak.

 

            “They did worse things to you than that?” she softly demanded.

 

            “Yes.”

 

            “And you still went back there? You put yourself in that house again to spy?”

 

            “Yes.”

 

            Lips thinning, Alex swallowed thickly, and her regret seemed to intensify as she nodded to herself. Rubbing her eyes, raking a hand through her hair, she let out a sharp breath, eyes bright with anger when she looked back up at Lena, reaching out to take her hand in both of hers again, holding it gently between them.

 

            “I think I understand what it cost you to leave us, and … I understand the risk you took to come back, as well. Thank you.” Then she hesitated, her face rippling with some unreadable emotion as she reflected for a moment. “You might’ve been a Slytherin at school, but … you’re braver than any Gryffindor I know.”

 

            “Don’t get daft on me now,” Lena murmured, rolling her eyes.

 

            The door opened then, Kara nudging it with her foot as she carried a plate and a steaming mug. Her face immediately crumpled into a scowl at the sight of her sister, and while she spoke to Lena, it was obvious who her words were aimed at. “You should be resting.”

 

            Alex’s mouth turned down slightly at the corners, but she must’ve felt like she deserved Kara’s ire, because she didn’t argue, didn’t try to speak to her at all. Giving Lena a grim smile, she raised her hand to her lips, pressing a quick kiss to the back of it before gently patting it and setting her hand back down on the covers.

 

            “I’ll leave you to rest.”

 

            It was a tight squeeze for her to brush past Kara without touching her as Kara angled herself away from her sister, and Alex left the room, gently shutting the door behind her. Thin-lipped with annoyance, Kara crossed over to the desk, setting the mug down, and perched on the edge of the mattress as she put the plate in Lena’s lap, as Lena sat up against the pillows. Reaching out, Kara ran a hand over Lena’s hair, her blue eyes sullen and brooding.

 

            “She didn’t know any better,” Lena quietly pointed out.

 

            “I don’t care,” Kara petulantly replied.

 

            Smiling as her eyes shuttered, Lena softly sighed. Picking up her plate, she set it on the desk beside her mug of tea and then held her arms open to Kara, taking in the furrowed look of sadness as she tried to suppress her feelings. But she couldn’t hide the pout, the way her chin dimpled with the effort to stop it from wobbling, just as hurt and conflicted and confused as they all were.

 

            “Come here,” Lena softly ordered her, and Kara went willingly.

 

            Crawling over her to sprawl across her lap, Kara pressed her ear to Lena’s chest and listened to the drum of her heartbeat for a minute. Then she let out a choked sound, reaching up to thumb her fixed glasses up and wipe at her teary eyes. Gently shushing her, reaching up to stroke her curls, Lena kissed the top of her head.

 

            “I was so scared,” Kara confessed in a small voice.

 

            “I know, but you don’t have to be scared anymore. It’ll all be okay now. We can- we can sort this out. Figure out what we do from here.” Stiffening slightly, Lena had to work hard to swallow as a prickle of fear stole over her. Her voice was nervous and wavering as she hesitantly spoke. “I understand if things have changed for you-”

 

            Kara’s head rose from her chest, a crumpled look of confusion on her face as she looked at Lena. There were tears in her waterline, and Lena reached up to thumb away the divot between her eyebrows as Kara gave her a worried look, an anxious edge to her gaze.

 

            “Has it changed for you?”

 

            “Me? No, no. Not at all. I- it’s been- it’s been agony. I can’t lie, I think it’ll take me a while to- to not be bitter about the whole thing. I know we decided … we decided what we did, but … nine months. How has it been so long since we last saw each other? And even then, a handful of minutes,” Lena muttered, her bitterness evident in her voice, her words flush with it as she resented the way the last fifteen months had played out.

 

            “Okay. Good. Because it hasn’t changed for me. Not at all,” Kara murmured, settling back down on Lena’s chest. “I love you; I’d be cross with you if you left me now.”

 

            Lena let out a weak chuckle, tucking a loose curl behind Kara’s ear and then smoothing her hand down her arm. “Well, I’d hate for you to be cross with me.”

 

            Kara’s laugh was a quiet huff, and she tilted her head up to brush her lips over Lena’s throat, over her hummingbird pulse, and then settled back down on her chest. After a moment, she cleared her throat, but her voice was still strangled as she spoke. “Was it … like last time? Not … last night, but the whole time.”

 

            “Um … no. No, it- it was nowhere near that. But it- I think it’ll take me some time before I can … talk about it.”

 

            “Okay. That’s okay. You take all the time you need.”

 

            “And you? What he did-”

 

            “I don’t think I want to tell you,” Kara admitted. “Um … it’s just- none of it was your fault.”

 

            “He was looking for you because of me.”

 

            “I was caught because of my own stupidity. I didn’t have my wand with me; I would’ve been able to Disapparate if I had. It was my fault.”

 

            “You didn’t have your wand? What-”

 

            Kara cringed slightly, a flush in her cheeks. “Well, it’s a long story, but I’ve been away for a few months. They were trying to gain followers for You Know Who, you know, talk others into joining him, so they weren’t after me in particular. I was on their list, but there was another Order member they were searching for, too, so, um, well, I don’t think your brother was after him . It was just a bit of bad luck and shit timing. Not your fault.”

 

            Her hand crept over to Lena’s left forearm, her thumb smoothing over the hidden scar, as if trying to dissuade any thoughts of failing, any self-blame or other negative emotions Lena would attribute to herself. It eased some of Lena’s guilt a bit, and she swallowed past the lump in her throat, holding Kara a little tighter. After a moment, Kara sat up, and Lena studied the thinness of her cheeks, the signs of her absence in her haggard appearance. She leaned in to kiss Lena before pulling away, moving to squeeze in beside her on the single bed.

 

            “Eat your lunch.”

 

            Obliging, Lena grabbed the plate and then took a swig of tea before starting on the sandwich. It was chicken, and she realised that she was starving after the first bite, wolfing down the rest of it and chasing it with the tea. Then, she rubbed her tired eyes and looked over at Kara, leaning in to kiss her scarred cheek as she felt a twinge in her chest; it was peaceful, for the first time in a long time, and it was strange how even Eliza’s house felt more like a home to Lena than the one where she’d grown up.

 

            “If you’ve been away for a few months … was last night the first time your family has seen you?”
