            Wincing a little, Kara nodded as she rubbed the bridge of her nose. “Yeah.”

 

            “Oh, Kara,” Lena whispered, pained by the memory of the state she’d been in. She’d looked worse than Lena by far, and Lena didn’t want to think about what she’d endured, but could only imagine how distraught her family would’ve been, seeing her in that state after a months-long absence. “You should go down and spend some time with them. Let them know you’re okay and fuss over you a bit. I’ll be okay up here.”

 

            “No, I don’t think- they’re going to have questions, um, and I don’t want to answer them right now. I want to stay up here. Unless you don’t want-”

 

            “Don’t be silly. I might actually use a permanent Sticking Charm to glue myself to you.”

 

            “I wouldn’t oppose,” Kara murmured, working the edge of the blanket up so she could join Lena beneath them.

 

            Shuffling over to make room for her, Lena pulled the blankets up to Kara’s chin and rested her cheek against the top of her head as they cuddled up together. Kara reached for Lena’s left hand and toyed with her fingers, threading their hands together, kissing her knuckles as Lena played with her hair. They dwelled in silence, basking in each other’s company without needing to say a word. It was healing, in a way, filling that wretched loneliness that had dogged them both for nigh on a year and a half. 

 

            They spent the rest of the day in Kara’s childhood bed, holding onto each other as they both fell asleep, Kara’s fingers knotted in the front of Lena’s top, Lena’s arms around her, both of them needing that reassurance. They slept fitfully, not quite so exhausted this time to slip into unconsciousness without memories resurfacing, and Lena jolted awake twice, heart hammering, a cold sweat on her skin, and Kara woke with a hoarse shout at one point as well. After that, they couldn’t get back to sleep, just lay in the warmth of the bed, aware that hot water bottles had been piled about their feet at some point by Eliza, who had crept in to check up on them and left them in bed.

 

            When the room started to get dark, Kara waved a hand at a dusty candle, the faint glow keeping the deep blue of dusk at bay, and a tap at the door disturbed them as they lay in a warm stupor. Neither of them made a sound, but the door opened and Sam poked her head inside. Lena blinked in quiet surprise, although she didn’t speak or move an inch. Hesitantly stepping into the room, Sam’s face softened with a smile as she eyed them both, looking relieved as she looked about and then sank onto the edge of Alex’s bed.

 

            Struggling to sit up, Kara raked a hand through her hair, half undone now, although her wand was still stuck through the loose mess of curls, and she nudged her glasses up to rub at her eyes. Feeling a little stiff from lying in one spot for so long, Lena sat up too and cautiously rolled her left shoulder, rubbing her collarbone, a ghost of an ache persisting. 

 

            “How’re you both feeling?” Sam asked.

 

            She was dressed in normal clothes and looked rested, and Lena correctly presumed she’d finished her shift, slept it off at her home and then came straight to check on them. Lena could see the questions in her eyes, but Sam was more tactful than that and didn’t ask, her primary concern their wellbeing.

 

            “I’m fine,” Lena said, her voice scratchy with sleep.

 

            “Me too,” Kara murmured, giving Sam a small smile. “Thank you. For last night.”

 

            Nodding, Sam’s eyes darted between them, and she frowned slightly, cupping her chin in her palm, elbow braced on the arm folded across her chest as she asked an easier question, but no less pressing in her mind. “So, the two of you …”

 

            “I told you I’d explain it all to you one day,” Lena said with a wavering smile. “Just … not right now. But you should know that I lied to you a lot, and I’m sorry for that, but … none of it was what it seemed. Including what happened between us . Um … just- give me a- a few days. I just need … a little bit of time to adjust again.”

 

            “Okay,” Sam accepted her evasive response without complaint. “I’m just- I’m glad you’re okay. Whatever happened … you do what you need to stay safe, okay?”

 

            Running a hand over her face, Lena let out a short breath, grimacing. “You too. My mum … she might ask if you’ve seen me-”

 

            “I haven’t,” Sam easily lied.

 

            Giving her a weak smile, Lena was filled with a rush of gratitude for her friend, who’d been her only friend over the last fifteen months, as Lena had isolated herself from them all as much as possible. Even her brief encounters with Andrea had been fraught with frustration and scorn, but Sam had been there at work, mostly silent as she reserved judgment and tried to be supportive, while not understanding Lena at all. But with that came the guilt of Lena’s lies and secrecy, and how she’d put Sam in jeopardy, even now.

 

            “Thank you, but … I don’t want you to risk your safety. Don’t lie for me. You need to put yourself first; you have Ruby to think about. If I were you, with the way this is all going, I’d start thinking of a way out, in case you need it.”

 

            “What does this all mean for you?”

 

            Lips twitching with dismay, Lena sighed. “I don’t think I’ll be able to go to work for a while. Maybe not until this is over - however long that takes.”

 

            Nodding, Sam paused and then reached into the pocket of her jacket and pulled out two potions, reaching to set them on the desk. “Just a little pick me up for you both. Um … you’re sure you’re both fine?”

 

            They nodded, faces soft with exhaustion. All Lena wanted to do was sleep some more, everything finally hitting her after so many months of being on edge, of not being able to properly relax. But the house was protected by the Fidelius Charm, and no one could find her there. She could’ve slept for a week , she thought.

 

            “Alright. And you’ll let me know if you need anything?”

 

            Lena smiled slightly. “Yes. I’ll send you a letter in a few days so we can talk more. Just … stay safe, please. Um … here.” Working the ring off her index finger, no longer necessary, she shifted on the bed to hold it out to Sam. “It’s got a Protean Charm on it; Kara has the other one. If you need help, change the colour to red, okay? I’ll meet you at your flat.”

 

            Eyeing the ring, Sam smiled faintly. “Ah. Well, I can’t wait to hear the rest of this story.”

 

            She slipped it on her finger and then rose to her feet, holding out her hand for Lena to take. Squeezing her fingers, Sam’s smile grew, and she looked from Lena to Kara. “It’s good to see you, Kara; it’s good to see you both together . Rest up, alright? Healer’s orders.”

 

            Rolling her eyes, Lena shooed her away. “Piss off. I’ll see you later.”

 

            “Let me see you out,” Kara quickly insisted, kicking off the blankets and climbing over the mattress, making for the door.

 

            She led Sam out onto the landing, and Lena listened to their footsteps descend, the sound of voices drifting up, then the front door shutting. No one else stuck their head in this time she was left alone, leaving her to rest, and it was five minutes before Kara reappeared, levitating steaming mugs and bowls with her, setting them on the desk and then picking a bowl up, handing it to Lena.

 

            “My mum made soup. I’ve fended her off for the night, so you can rest a bit more.”

 

            “Poor thing,” Lena commiserated, “she probably just wants to make sure you’re okay.”

 

            “Oh, me, she already has, it’s you she’s worried about.”

 

            “I don’t think she’d find it reassuring if I told her that I hadn’t endured anything new. Well, until last night.”

 

            “No, I don’t think she would,” Kara grimaced, spooning soup into her mouth. “Neither do I. And neither should you.”

 

            “I find it reassuring that … it’s over. And I never have to go back. Never again.”

 

            “Never again.”

Chapter 61

            After doing little else but sleeping all day, Lena woke the next morning feeling tired from idleness, Kara still asleep beside her in the narrow bed, her arm thrown across Lena’s waist as her face was furrowed in a stern look. She’d woken twice in the night with quiet cries of panic, chest heaving as she bolted upright, waking Lena with her, and so Lena didn’t move as she let her sleep a little while longer. Lena couldn’t remember the last time she’d had so little required of her, and was left with little else to do but think. That was a dangerous prospect, but she tried to process the last few days, to take stock of it all with some sort of detachment, piecing things together, trying to answer some of her questions. There was a lot she didn’t know, though, and she knew that Kara would be able to fill her in, but Lena wouldn’t push her to talk about it. She knew all too well how brutal her brother could be, and she wasn’t sure she was ready to hear the horrors he’d inflicted on Kara, either, if she was being honest.

 

            Kara stirred an hour later, her face creased with sleep, as she woke slowly, stretching out stiff limbs as she sat up, leaning over to kiss Lena’s cheek. Fumbling for her glasses, she wedged them on her face and stifled a yawn before she hummed vaguely and then looked down at Lena, raising her eyebrows slightly.

 

            “Should we have a bath?”

 

            Toying with the ends of Kara’s hair, Lena smiled faintly. “That would be nice.”

 

            Nodding, Kara ducked down to gently kiss her before she scrambled off the bed and slipped out of the room. Putting the plug in the tub, she ran hot water from the taps and went back into her room while it filled, rifling through her drawers for clean pyjamas for them both, making two separate piles as she felt Lena’s gaze on her. Turning to meet her eyes, Kara smiled slightly, her eyes creasing at the corners as her cheeks shallowly dimpled. Shutting the drawers of her dresser, she gathered up her armful of clothes as Lena dragged herself out of bed and straightened out the sheets with a wave of her hand.

 

            Locking them in the bathroom, Kara started to shed her clothes, and Lena clicked her tongue as she reached out, light fingers brushing over the prominent ridges of her ribs and spine. “What on earth were you doing while you were away? You look like you haven’t eaten a proper meal in weeks?”

 

            “You’re not far off,” Kara told her with a weak smile, self-consciously wrapping her arms around herself. “I, uh, well, it’s a long story. It’s all connected. Um …”

 

            Lena’s hand was cool as she pressed it to Kara’s back, fingers splayed across her ribcage, and she stepped in to kiss her shoulder. “We have time. You don’t have to tell me right now.”

 

            A flicker of relief crossed Kara’s face, and she uncrossed her arms, continuing to undress before she shut off the water and then ushered Lena into the tub first, before she joined her. The water was mercifully hot, stinging the little scrapes and cuts peppering Kara’s body, and they squeezed into the tub together as if the time that had passed was nothing, as if this was an ordinary weekend where they were home from work together, albeit in a different bath, the familiarity of each other’s body unchanged, even though their bodies had changed, both of them thinner from the stress of the last fifteen months, Kara’s just exacerbated by the circumstances of her living conditions since the end of last year. It was so strange, the keen ache of missing each other now smoothed over so suddenly, so unexpectedly, and while there was a lingering tension of things unsaid, of feelings not quite processed, they picked up exactly where they’d left off, because not for a single second had they ever loved each other a little less. Not even in nine months without laying eyes on each other, not in fifteen months of calling it off for the sake of the greater good.

 

            Basking in the peace of the mundane, something not to be taken for granted ever again, Lena let Kara wash her hair for her and then coaxed her girlfriend into her arms, Kara’s back to Lena’s chest as they lay like that until the water cooled. Feeling refreshed and a little more lively that morning, they dressed in their clean pyjamas and Kara brushed her teeth, while Lena had to make do with some mouthwash, floss and magic. Neither of them spoke about going home to their cottage, although they undoubtedly would, and Lena was glad of the reprieve from having to look after herself, make decisions or have thoughts and opinions for a couple of days. In Eliza’s house, she was afforded a little break to take stock of things and reevaluate, and Kara was likewise able to readjust to a proper bed, to meals and magic, the easy comfort of her normal life. It was strange for them both, to say the least.

 

            Back in Kara’s room, Lena sat on the made bed, while Kara tidied up a few things, gathering up plates and cups to take back downstairs. Ordering her back to bed, Kara slipped out of the room and went downstairs with their dirty dishes, but Lena felt too restless. She didn’t cope well with bedrest, had never been afforded the luxury of it even when she had been sick, and she decided to write a letter to send to Sam, a brief thought of concern for Morrigan crossing her mind before she swept it aside, knowing her owl would fare just fine until Lena could find a way to fetch her. As Lena rummaged through the desk drawers for a quill, parchment and ink, she was sidetracked, and she tuned out the sounds of other people arriving at the house, Kara’s trip downstairs stretching out to ten minutes by the time she returned.

 

            Pushing open the bedroom door, lips already parted as she went to speak, Kara froze, her stomach lurching at the sight of Lena sitting on the edge of the bed with a quill in her hands. It could’ve just been an ordinary quill by the look of it, the black feather slightly crumpled as Lena twirled it in her fingers, but they both knew exactly what quill it was. Kara had hidden it at the back of her bottom desk drawer when she’d packed up her things and left the cottage almost a year and a half ago. After all the time that had passed since she’d taken it from Lena, she couldn’t bring herself to throw it away, though. It was never her property to toss out, no matter how much she wanted to, and a part of her had always anticipated Lena doing it one day. But the years had passed by, and they’d argued over other methods Lena had taken to sate the craving to hurt herself, and the quill had remained hidden away. 

 

            A lump of fear in her throat, aware of how long she’d been downstairs, wondering if the words hidden beneath the sleeve of Lena’s top were a livid red with freshness, Kara shut her mouth and eased the door shut. Slowly walking over to Alex’s bed, Kara sank onto it, sitting directly across from Lena, their knees almost touching in the narrow gap. She didn’t say anything, didn’t know what Lena was thinking, but her pulse raced and her palms were clammy as she balled her hands into fists in her lap. Lena looked up at her then, her expression unreadable.

 

            “I should’ve known you had it with you,” Lena murmured, wry smile curling her lips as she twirled the nib of the quill between thumb and forefinger. “I looked all over for it after I made you leave, you know.”

 

            “I thought you might.”

 

            Lena let out a soft laugh and then sighed heavily. “And now … it’s funny, I had one task, one job to do; gather information and don’t get caught. And I failed at that. Miserably.”

 

            “Lena-” Kara tried to interrupt, her name coming out hoarse, agonised.

 

            Dismissively waving her hand, Lena’s eyes narrowed as her brows pinched together, and the corners of her mouth curled up in a bewildered smile as she continued to talk, cutting Kara off before she could try to reason with her. “It might be the first time I’ve actually failed at something so badly, but the truth is … I don’t feel like I did. I should- I should want to fill a book with that line, over and over again. My skin should be itching with the urge. But … I got you out alive, and I kept my promise that I’d come back. And I failed at my task … but I wasn’t a failure.”

 

            With a surprised laugh, looking up to meet Kara’s eyes again, Lena blinked. And then the quill in her fingers burst into flames, making Kara jump slightly, a little startled, a little confused. Mouth opening and closing, she didn’t know what to say, relief sweeping through her as the quill burnt to cinders, making her feel weak. Running a hand over her face, she exhaled forcefully and was just about to speak when Lena picked up something else. Another thing Kara had hidden for a long time, another thing she’d brought with her when she’d left their home together. Turning the ring box over in her hand, Lena glanced up at her.

 

            “For the last fifteen months, I’ve been trying to forget the look in your eyes when you talked about us getting married someday. All I’ve thought about since leaving is- is our life together. Cooking in the kitchen, the cat sleeping at the foot of our bed, and games of Wizard’s Chess or reading by the fire, and how it- how it felt to come here for a Sunday roast with our family, go out for drinks with our friends. All of it. I’ve wanted that so badly since I left. To go home to our house, and not find it dark and empty. I would’ve given anything to come home to the sound of you singing in the kitchen, to just … lie in bed with you, doing nothing, just … being together once more. And I kept thinking about the ring. And how you said you wanted to marry me when this is all over.”

 

            Fiddling with the box, Lena hesitated and then held it out to Kara, who slowly reached out to take it, a wary look on her face, unsure of what was happening. Drawing in a shaky breath, Lena jerked her chin towards her.

 

            “I don’t want to wait until it’s all over.”

 

            “What?”

 

            “I want you to ask me now.”

 

            Kara felt like her heart might lurch right out of her chest, her blue eyes widening as she stammered for a moment, looking down at the box in her palm and then back up to Lena. There had been many ways she’d thought of proposing, if the time ever came. Neither of them had constituted a heartbroken farewell in their living room, or being asked to do it while sitting in her bedroom at her mother’s house. But things between them had never been normal, or loud, or grand, and the only thing they’d ever cared about was each other. It had always come back to the two of them, and the small world they inhabited together, a little secret space where things had always made sense. And it made sense now, because why would they ever want to wait a moment longer than they already had?

 

            Slipping off the bed, Kara knelt on both knees in between Lena’s legs, reaching out to cup her waist as she stared up at her with an achingly tender look on her face. Reaching up, Kara brushed the hair out of Lena’s face, her thumb lingering over her temple, where the first few strands of grey had crept into Lena’s dark hair, and Lena reached out to trace her fingertips over Kara’s scarred face, cupping her cheek as she looked down at her, lips parted as she drew in quick, shallow breaths, bated with anticipated. Flipping open the lid of the ring box in her hand, Kara held up the silver band with an oval moonstone surrounded by tiny diamonds, her voice shaking slightly as she spoke.

 

            “I know that things have never been easy between us, even from the very beginning, but … I would do it all again, you know. All of it; not just the good parts, but every fight, every hurtful word, every goodbye. And I really do mean that. It took me a while to believe that I could be deserving of someone like you, and we’ve both grown and changed so much over the years, but one thing that’s never changed for me is how much I love you. Knowing what I know now, everything that happened, I’d do it all over again just so I could grow enough to ask you, will you marry me?”

 

            Lena had tears in her eyes, and Kara could barely see the look on her face through her blurred vision, her chest aching so painfully in the best way as she was filled with the joy of being loved so wholly. She’d known it, of course, but they’d been apart for so long that they’d both almost forgotten what it felt like to have the person they loved right in front of them, to feel it in their chests, the intensity of it so consuming that it engulfed them. And Lena laughed, the sound so delicate in her mouth, the most beautiful sound Kara had ever heard, and she was kissing Kara then, their lips crushed together as tears wet Kara’s cheeks. She didn’t have to say yes, it was already a given, but Lena didn’t want to give her any reason to doubt, whispering it over and over again into Kara’s cheek and neck and hair as she kissed her face everywhere she could reach.

 

            Slipping the ring out of the box, Kara slid it onto Lena’s ring finger and then kissed the knuckle of it, holding her hand as she ran her thumb over the backs of her fingers, while staring up at her with adoration in her eyes. Letting out a choked laugh, Kara sniffed and wiped at her eyes, laughing again as Lena joined in, basking in a handful of minutes of the two of them and their little world. And then she was reminded of reality, blinking as she let out a small sound of surprise.

 

            “I’m really sorry, it’s such shit timing, but I- Dumbledore’s downstairs. I was supposed to come and get you, I-”

 

            “Oh,” Lena murmured in surprise, her eyebrows rising a fraction as she floundered for a moment. “Well, we’d better go and see what he wants.”

 

            Giving her a pained, sheepish look, Kara pushed herself up taller on her knees to kiss Lena once more, her lips soft and lingering, before she pushed herself to her feet. Hesitating, Lena’s mouth opened and closed as she looked down at the ring on her hand, and Kara cocked her head to the side, studying her as she waited for her to voice what she was struggling with.

 

            “Do you think we could … not tell anyone for a few days? I’d just- it’s all been such a big adjustment; I think I’d like this to be our secret for a little bit.”

 

            “Ah, well, there’s nothing we keep better than each other a secret,” Kara fondly murmured as she reached out a hand and hauled Lena to her feet, taking her left hand and working the ring free, before she kissed her bare knuckle. 

 

            Slipping the ring back into the box, she tucked that back into the desk drawer and then laced her fingers through Lena’s. Leading her downstairs with trepidation, Kara kept glancing back at Lena to ensure she was okay, that this wasn’t asking too much of her. Alex and Kelly were there as well, the former having brought their old Headmaster to the house to circumvent the Fidelius Charm, and the latter having stopped showing up to work at the Ministry three weeks prior, after a few more public attacks in Wizarding areas showed the increasing danger of congregating in well-populated areas. Kara didn’t want them all to overwhelm Lena; it had been a little overbearing for her , and that was without her family having spent the last year and a half suspecting her of being their enemy.

 

            The stairs creaked under their footsteps as they descended, the house peaceful with the low hum of conversation coming from the kitchen, where everyone had gathered. The smell of bacon, oil and coffee wafted towards them as they reached the bottom, and another glance back showed Lena’s reservation, the slightly pinched look of worry on her face as she looked past Kara to the trio of women visible within the kitchen. Squeezing her hand encouragingly, Kara approached the doorway to the kitchen, and the quiet conversation fell silent at her appearance.

 

            She didn’t let go of Lena’s hand, standing solidly in front of her with squared shoulders and her jaw set, her eyes darting to her sister and away again at the flicker of resentment that welled up. Kara was having trouble reconciling the fact that Alex was supposed to think the worst of Lena, that Kara had helped engineer it all, and the fact that she would toss Lena out on the street with a wand pointed at her. It wasn’t anyone’s fault that it had happened that way, but she wasn’t happy about it, regardless. And then her eyes moved to Dumbledore, whom Kara was arguably more resentful towards, disillusioned over the years, and even more recently so. She’d done what he’d asked, on numerous occasions, if only to see this war over as quickly as possible, but she had little respect for the man’s morals, even if she respected his power, his intelligence.

 

            Lena dropped her hand as she stepped into the doorway behind Kara, hugging her arms to herself as she hunched her shoulders slightly, apprehensively lingering on the threshold of the kitchen. Eliza was near the stove and let out a frayed sound, setting down a tea towel as she moved towards them both, bypassing Kara as she opened her arms. Lena looked surprised as she found herself engulfed in the embrace of her mother-in-law, Eliza rubbing her back as she exclaimed over the sight of her.

 

            “Oh, it’s good to have you home, sweetheart,” Eliza sighed, giving Lena a quick squeeze before holding her at arm’s length. “Come and sit. You must be hungry; I’m just making breakfast. Do you want tea or coffee?”

 

            A little overwhelmed, Lena opened and closed her mouth before she answered that tea would be nice, and Kara reached out to pull a chair away from the table, urging her down onto it. She took the seat adjacent to Lena, and they both turned their attention towards Dumbledore, seated at the head of the table, directly across from Lena, while Alex gripped the back of an empty chair and Kelly remained standing near the back door. Eliza moved about as if it wasn’t the most bewildering thing in the world that her daughters’ old Headmaster was sitting in her kitchen. He already had a cup of tea in front of him, and his blue eyes were solemn as he looked at Lena.

            

            “Healer Luthor, I’m glad to find you safe and whole.”

 

            With a serious set to her face, Lena nodded slightly, her mouth pressed into a flat line. “Thank you, sir.”

 

            “I hope you don’t mind my coming. I wasn’t present at Grimmauld Place to exonerate you two nights past, but word did get back to me, and I wished to visit and see that you and Miss Danvers were both well. And ask a few questions, if you will permit. I imagine you both have quite the tale to tell.”

 

            Kara’s lips twitched with annoyance, and she reached beneath the table to squeeze Lena’s knee. Neither of them wanted to talk about it just then, but there was a part of them that also wanted to get it over and done with. It was better, in a sense, that they were all gathered there in the kitchen, so they would only have to say it once, only have to endure all of the questions once. Mumbling her thanks as Eliza set a cup of tea in front of her, Lena wrapped her hands around it and glanced at Kara before responding.

 

            “What would you like to know?”

 

            Irritated that he would come so soon, although she thought she might’ve been irritated if he hadn’t come to see how Lena was faring after what he’d put her through, Kara ran a hand over her face and picked up the coffee her mum had made her upon Dumbledore’s arrival. It suddenly felt like that brief moment upstairs hadn’t happened, Kara’s emotions all over the place. Taking a sip, her stare was brooding as she looked at Dumbledore, waiting for his response.

 

            “I take it your brother knows your loyalties are not with Lord Voldemort?”

 

            “Yes, sir. He- I’m unsure whether he already knew, or whether I blew my cover myself. He had Kara, so I-” she faltered, swallowing thickly as she raised her chin a fraction. “I did what I had to do.”

 

            “I would not have expected anything less than that. I believe I should first offer my gratitude for your assistance in this. The information you’ve provided has been most helpful. And perhaps it might reassure you to know that you are not our only informant; I believe no harm will come from telling you this now, as it is not so much a secret within the Order, but Severus Snape has been reporting back to me as well.”

 

            “Snape?” Lena echoed. “But … he is a Death Eater. I’ve seen his Dark Mark.”

 

            “A reformed Death Eater. A mistake from his youth, but loyal to our cause, nonetheless.”

 

            Kara glanced at her sister and could see the effort it took Alex not to disagree with Dumbledore. No one disputed his claim, and Kara could see the way Lena’s shoulders loosened slightly, as if that part of her that had been waiting for punishment or beration for failing to uphold her duty was finally assuaged. If she were thankful to Dumbledore for one thing, it would be that.

 

            “I don’t believe I have to caution you against attending work.”

 

            “No, sir,” Lena murmured, her lips twitching with disappointed amusement. “But I’ll be able to assist the Order with any injuries, now that my cover is blown.”

 

            “That’s most generous of you.”

 

            Frowning slightly, Kara rubbed her fingertips over her lips, slouching slightly in her chair as she toyed with her cup of coffee with her other hand. “Have you told everyone yet, sir?”

 

            His pale eyes slid to Kara’s face, and his eyebrows rose a fraction in a silent question. She felt a flicker of annoyance that she had to clarify; it was obvious what she meant.

 

            “That Lena was spying for you. I’m sure you can understand I’d be concerned for her safety, letting her walk into a room full of Order members with everyone thinking she’s a Death Eater. It’s fortunate as it is that she wasn’t injured too badly coming home.”

 

            It was uncharacteristic, but Kara couldn’t help the snide barb sent her sister’s way, watching Alex stiffen slightly, her eyes cutting to Kara’s face and then away as a muscle twitched in her jaw. It didn’t serve to make Kara feel better, and her eyes met Lena’s warning glance before she took a sip of coffee and waited for his response.

 

            “No, I haven’t, as yet. But I don’t expect Lena to be showing up to Order meetings so soon after returning home, so there will be time.”

 

            “Why not?” Lena asked, frowning.

 

            “Fifteen months is a long time to be away from your home, your family. I can understand if you’d prefer to take some time to readjust.”

 

            “I- no, I don’t need time to adjust. I’d rather spend my time being useful, so this can all be over. I’d particularly like to help bring my brother down.”

 

            His face was full of understanding, but he offered her no promises of that, his fingers laced together on the worn tabletop as he looked at Lena over the rims of his half-moon glasses. “I understand your impatience on the matter, but that isn’t our most pressing concern at the moment. However, if a time comes when the moment is opportune, of course, Alexander will be apprehended. I ask that you don’t risk your safety, or that of any other Order members, to seek out your own revenge, Lena.”

 

            Nodding, a hard look on her face, as if she’d been considering doing just that, Lena didn’t object, and Kara was quietly relieved he’d asked that of her. She didn’t think she’d be able to reason with Lena, and she wasn’t in the business of making demands of her partner that often. While Kara wouldn’t have minded enacting her own revenge - or justice, as she preferred to view it - on Lena’s brother for the years of pain and torment, she knew Lena would have something to say about that as well. She hated the idea of him walking freely about, but they would both just have to wait for the right time.

 

            “Now, if you’re both willing, I would like to hear what transpired before asking further questions.”

 

            They both hesitated, and Lena looked to Kara to go first. It was the most logical starting point, for her to explain what had led up to where Lena’s story began. Still, Kara didn’t know where to start. It had all gone so horribly wrong after months of relative boredom, and she was still trying to process it herself. Taking a sip of her coffee, Kara rubbed the bridge of her nose and then exhaled shortly.

 

            “I was still with the group in the Cairngorms,” Kara haltingly started, her eyes glued to the table as she spoke quietly. “Um … a few weeks ago, the day after the full moon, I was helping- someone accidentally bit a hiker, so I was helping the leader, Manchester, take care of … that. While we were gone, a couple of Death Eaters showed up. It wasn’t until later, after we came back, that Hat - um, that’s one of the other guys - told Manchester, and he asked me about it. He knew I was a witch, but I told everyone my name was Linda Lee and that I hadn’t been properly schooled and didn’t have a wand, just to be safe. I’m not sure who showed up asking, but they asked if any of them knew Remus or me. They went on their way, and Manchester asked me about it, just in case I knew them from Wales, but I told him I’d never heard of the people they were after. I thought- I thought that would be it , but … well, obviously it wasn’t. I was considering leaving, maybe heading to Northumberland. Someone had said there were more werewolves there, and I wasn’t having much luck getting Manchester on our side - he didn’t seem too keen about joining You Know Who’s side either, though, sir, even though they kept showing up to convince him - but I didn’t have time to think about it that much. We’d been off hunting a deer, me and a couple of others, when we came back to the bothy we were staying in. Um … I think it was just a bit of bad luck. Fenrir Greyback was there with Ben Lockwood, and neither of them knew me by sight, so I thought I’d gotten lucky, but then Veronica Sinclair came out of the bothy, and, well … we knew each other well enough, years ago.”

 

            Faltering, her mouth twitching at the corners, Kara ran a hand over her face and then raked her hair back. Shifting in her seat, Kara let out a short sigh, feeling restless, frustrated by her own helplessness as the memories of a few days past cycled through her mind. 

 

            “I didn’t have my wand, so I couldn’t Disapparate. I tried to run, anyway,” she said with a wan smile, wincing slightly. What else could she have done? Even though it was futile, Kara wouldn’t go down without trying. “Um … I didn’t get very far. Veronica got me with a Body-Binding Curse, and Greyback dragged me over to them. They said that there was someone who was … interested in getting his hands on me. Manchester got into it with Lockwood, telling him he had the wrong person. I think he scratched him up a bit; there was a bit of a scuffle. I’m not sure what happened there, who was hurt, um, they just Disapparated and took me with them. I didn’t know where I was at first, but they took me inside the house.”

 

            Suppressing a shiver, Kara tightened her jaw. That house, so big, so cold and quiet, was a bleak place, and it broke her heart to think of all the summers Lena spent there, the childhood she’d had within those walls, the long months after returning there once more. A lump got stuck in her throat, and it took her a moment to swallow it, her throat bobbing painfully.

 

            “Um … Lex Luthor was there. They gave me to him; he asked me questions, but … I didn’t give him anything. The Graves siblings were there too, so … he had them take me down to- to a cellar. Um … Otis, well, he was the physical one, and Mercy the mental. I don’t know how long it went on for. I still wouldn’t give him anything. He was mad. They left me alone for a while, but it was- it was so dark down there that I- it was morning when they took me, so I guess- I guess by the time I got away, it must’ve been half a day. Almost. I don’t know. They came back once, took up where they’d left off, um … I still wouldn’t answer them. It wasn’t- it wasn’t just about Lena, but he did try to get me to tell him what had happened there. Mostly, it was about the Order. I’d duelled him at the Ministry last year, and I’d cut him up badly, so I think- well, I think he put the clues together, with- with the scars of my face and a spell that was made by Slytherins. I guess it must’ve been obvious it had come from Lena. I was stupid to even use it.”

 

            Lena’s hand smoothed over Kara’s shoulder, her face tender and agonised as she stared at Kara with wide eyes, full of pain and guilt. When Lena’s cool hand cupped the side of her neck, Kara tilted her head to the side, leaning into it as her eyelids shuttered. Drawing in a shaky breath, she forged onwards.

 

            “Otis came to bring me back upstairs, eventually, and, um, I was dragged into a room with them all. Lena was there. He wanted her to- it was a test. I don’t know if he already knew and was waiting to see what she would do, or whether he thought she might. Um … but she Flooed me away before I could- she got me out of there, sent me to her old flat. I- I couldn’t get back through, or Floo to Grimmauld Place, because you took it off the Floo Network, so I went to my sister’s house, but … no one was home, so I came to my mother’s. Alex and Kelly were already here, having dinner, um, and before I could- before I could explain - no one was listening to me; they wouldn’t- they wouldn’t go after her for me. I didn’t have my wand. But she showed up, she got herself out, so ...”

            

            Her eyes held a sheen to them as she looked at Lena, questioning and slightly desperate for answers. Rubbing her brow, Lena frowned slightly, her hand slipping off Kara’s shoulder, drawn back to her lap. Kara watched her eyes flit around to the other women, and she made herself look as well, the horrified, ashen faces of her family, not quite looking at her as they listened intently. She hadn’t detailed anything that had happened, but they knew what must’ve happened for her to have shown up in the state that she had, covered in blood, bruised and broken.

 

            “It was a few months in the making, sir. My letter to you, about my meeting with the Dark Lord, well, I’d bought myself some time before I would have to get a Dark Mark, so … I think my brother was trying to force my hand. I’m also unsure whether he knew the truth - he certainly suspected - or whether it would be two owls, one stone. Either way, he got his answer with his trap. You knew that I would never get a Dark Mark; I’d made that quite clear, so from the moment I stalled, I knew I was working on borrowed time, now. Um … I got home from work and they were all there. Greyback had left, so it was just the five of them. He, um, my brother- he got Otis to bring Kara in. I tried to play along with it, I tried to convince him that I would do it myself - he threatened to do it, otherwise - um … I dragged-”

 

            Cutting off, Lena winced, closing her eyes as she covered her face for a moment, before heavily dropping her hand to the table, palm slapping against the wood as she worked to swallow. Beneath the table, Kara squeezed her leg, shifting her chair slightly, to be as close as possible. 

 

            “I dragged her in front of the fireplace,” Lena explained, her voice rasping and hollow as she recounted it flatly. “I had my wand trained on her, and I- I closed the gap as much as I could, so I could be close to the fireplace. I summoned the Floo Powder and threw it into the grate, and then I banished her into it and sent her to my flat. I managed to get a Shield Charm up in time to block the spells when they- when they realised what I’d done. Veronica got me from the side, broke my collarbone, um, and I was outmatched, so I knew that I couldn’t- I couldn’t fight them all. I got in a few shots. I blocked some more. I got hurt a little, but I was lucky. I brought the ceiling down and blasted apart a window. I- you said before that you suspected there was … more to my spying, well, I’m an Unregistered Animagus. I have been for years , since I was at Hogwarts. Luckily, I’m a raven, so I managed to fly away. I beat them to the boundary of the estate and Disapparated. I couldn’t concentrate properly; I Splinched myself. I’d already twisted my ankle, so I couldn’t walk properly, had to transform again and fly the rest of the way here. And that’s it.”

 

            “I threw her out,” Alex immediately picked up where she left off, a grim set to her face, her eyes flitting to Dumbledore’s with a prickle of shame and anger in them. “I didn’t know she was a spy. I almost hexed her; I was ready to, until my sister got between us, explained the situation. That’s why Kelly went to find out if it was true or not.”

 

            Nodding, Dumbledore was silent for a few moments, and Eliza slipped out to the back garden. Whether it was to process what she’d heard or because she’d heard what she’d wanted to, Kara wasn’t sure, but she knew her mother would be upset. It was enough to upset any of them, but they were all mostly silent. Kara took a sip of her coffee and waited for their old Headmaster to speak.

 

            “Thank you to you both, not just for recounting it all, but for your services to the Order as well. It was not a small sacrifice, asking you to be separated from each other and lying to your loved ones, but I hope you know how much we have been able to achieve from your actions. As for you, Lena, rest assured it was always my intention to make public the lengths you went to to provide us with vital information. Now that, well, for lack of a better term, the Kneazle’s out of the bag, I will rectify the misinformation within the Order in short order. You may rest assured that no harm will befall you from well-intentioned members.”

 

            His eyes briefly slid to Alex, and then to Kara, as he forged onwards. “I will afford you some time to mend what has been damaged, on several fronts, before you attend any future Order meetings.” Lena opened her mouth to object, but he gestured for her to let him continue, a smile on his lips. “I quite insist. After your ordeal, take some time to enjoy being home. Rest, recover, and then you may assist however you see fit. It is not solely for your benefit; I would like to ensure all of this has blown over before the two of you are out and about again.”

 

            Mouth closing, disgruntled but accepting of it, Lena didn’t argue. Kara was quietly relieved as well; it would be nice to have a few days, a couple of weeks even, for just the two of them. There was a lot of hurt to wade through, so much time apart as well, and it would be a relief to just go through the motions of ordinary life for a little while. They could tidy up the cottage and move back in, have those ordinary days together that they both wanted, had both missed. Kara could make her dinner, and they could read by the fire, and Lena could get used to being in a warm house, with noise and comfort. A longing ache filled her with such intensity that she felt her pulse race, her eyes on Lena.

 

            “Okay,” Kara murmured, gaze flitting to Dumbledore and then back to Lena. “We’ll take some time. I’d- I’d like it if we could attend the next Order meeting, though. Just for everyone to know, for us to be up to date on everything that’s gone on.”

 

            Deliberating for a moment, Dumbledore conceded with a nod. “I can accommodate that. I’d planned on convening an emergency meeting tomorrow night. Perhaps the next one-”

 

            “We can make it tomorrow,” Lena insisted.

 

            He glanced at Kara, and she nodded in agreement, her hand scrabbling for Lena’s under the table, squeezing her fingers. She might’ve preferred to wait for that, despite her insistence that Lena’s name be cleared, so that everyone else might not treat her as Alex had, but they were a team. If Lena was ready to walk into a room full of Order members tomorrow night, Kara would be right there beside her. 

 

            “If that’s what you’d prefer. I’ll send word once I’ve confirmed the time. Now, I have a few questions, if you’ll permit them.”

 

            It was another half an hour inside the kitchen, both of them answering the questions he posed to them. Kara provided relative numbers for the werewolf communities in Wales and Scotland, from what she’d seen, and the information teased out of Manchester and the others about previous Death Eater visits, of what promises had been made and what Kara deduced they wanted from an ally. Lena offered up names and locations, tidbits of information she’d left out of letters, the things that had ensured she wouldn’t be embroiled in a raid, had that information been acted upon by the Aurors within the Order. She’d given Dumbledore many names over the years, though, so none of them were surprising, but she offered more evidence, information on their comings and goings, whispers and rumours. 

 

            By the time he left, thanking them and stepping into the back garden to thank Eliza for the tea, Kara felt thoroughly exhausted. The bacon had gone cold in the frying pan on the cooker, and she made herself climb to her feet as Alex saw the Professor out, reheating it with the wand her sister had brought back to her and making sandwiches for herself and Lena. With fresh cups of tea and coffee, they remained around the table, eating their breakfast as Kelly remained silent, leaning against the counters with the black tea Kara had made for her. She hadn’t said anything, her dark eyes anxiously darting to Lena over and over again, as if wanting to say something, wanting to apologise or ask for further clarification, and Kara took that in, wondering what her sister-in-law made of it all. Kelly’s temperament was so different to Alex’s, but there was a righteousness there too, a stickler for laws but willing to bend for justice or morals. Kara had always hoped Kelly might be more willing to forgive their lies, readily accepting Lena back into their fold at the realisation of how wrong she’d been, but then things had gotten a little out of hand, and she was sure Alex had filled her in on the parts she’d missed when she’d gone in search of answers.

 

            Eliza came back in, shedding muddy gloves as she looked between Kara and Lena, before walking over to her daughter, squeezing her shoulders and ducking to press a kiss to Kara’s hair. Reaching out a hand, she rubbed Lena’s back and then vanished through to the living room to stoke the fire and continue her work. Finishing off the crusts of her sandwich, Kara joined her in the living room, giving Lena a minute with Kelly, and found Alex perched on the arm of the sofa, while Eliza made meticulous notes in a ledger. Flopping down onto a seat, Kara startled slightly as something leapt at her, before she relaxed, Bastet kneading at her lap, rubbing against her chin. She scratched the cat behind the ears and listened to the quiet conversation coming from the kitchen, while her mother’s quill scratched over pages.

 

            “I’m sorry,” Alex murmured after a long minute.

 

            There seemed to be a weight in the air, a tension thickening as Kara slowly turned her head and blinked at her sister. The resentment in her chest was unwanted, but she couldn’t shake it, still so angry. She thought it would be a while before she could speak to her sister without feeling it, and Kara knew that her words had rung true; no matter how Alex made amends, she would never forgive her for what she’d done.

 

            “It’s not me you need to apologise to,” Kara stiffly replied, her first words said directly to Alex in over a day, despite her sister lurking about.

 

            “I did. Of course I apologised to her,” Alex softly said, her voice thick with remorse. “If I’d known, then I wouldn’t have-”

 

            “You shouldn’t have had to know to not act like that.”

 

            “So, if it was a real Death Eater breaking into mum’s house, was I just supposed to invite them to stay for tea?”

 

            “Girls,” Eliza wearily sighed, setting her quill in the inkpot and giving them both chastising glances as her brow furrowed.

 

            “You’re being ridiculous-”

 

            “I didn’t know any better. If you hadn’t lied to me for over a year-”

 

            “We were trying to keep her safe.”

 

            “And I was trying to keep everyone safe.”

 

            Kara scoffed, her mouth opening and left hanging open as Lena stepped into the mouth of the living room, grimacing as she folded her arms over her chest. Her eyes were glued to Kara’s face, exasperated and pointed. It made Kara falter, a rush of adoration and a wince of heartache flooding her, unused to Lena’s stubbornness, the way she was able to get Kara to do what she wanted by giving her that stern look. It was strange to feel that so much time had passed and yet none at all, this thing between them so unchanged.

 

            “Well, some things never change,” Lena dryly commented, a beat of silence following her words. “I’d prefer it if you didn’t put me in the middle of one of these again. I think we can all agree that it was a misunderstanding, and we’re all friends now.”

 

            “A misunderstanding? She doesn’t even understand why-”

 

            “What, why I have a scar on my arm? Yes, she does. I told her why.”

 

            “You shouldn’t have had to.”

 

            “Well, that was my decision to make. I made it. Now, I get to be safe at home, and I don't want everyone arguing over something so- so silly , now that we’re all finally back together again. And if that means no more secrets, then fine. Especially if we’re getting married; I’d prefer not to hide things from my family.”

 

            A jolt ran through Kara, and she cocked her head to the side, face furrowing at Lena divulging that secret, one they’d only just made, intending to keep for a couple of days at her request. Yet, Lena just helplessly spread her hands and shrugged slightly at Kara, eyebrows rising quickly in a goading manner, waiting for her response.

 

            “Okay, well, I thought you wanted to wait to tell everyone,” Kara mumbled, feeling a warm flush creep up her neck and into her cheeks as her mother and sister’s eyes landed on her face.

            

            “Well, it’s apparent that secrets only cause more problems, so,” Lena shrugged again. “Now, you can sit there and be angry on my behalf, or … we can celebrate.”

 

            Unable to be annoyed at her, Kara relented, climbing to her feet and marching upstairs to fetch the ring box from her desk drawer, before walking downstairs with the ring. Taking Lena’s left hand, Kara slipped the moonstone ring onto her finger and gave Lena a withering look as her fiancée murmured softly with amusement. “Cheer up, it’s only the rest of our lives.”

 

            Pecking her on the cheek, Kara turned to face her family, shrugging as she pressed her lips together and clapped her hands on her thighs. The three of them looked like they didn’t know what to say, having gotten used to Lena’s absence and Kara’s brooding heartbreak, to have Lena thrust back amongst them with it all a lie, and standing there with a ring on her finger and a nervous smile on her lips. Pink-cheeked, Kara adjusted her glasses and let out a breathless huff of laughter.

 

            “I thought everyone would be happier about it, but … well, I can see it’s a bit of a surprise.”

 

            Lena prodded her from behind, clicking her tongue, and Kara reached behind her to grab her hand, squeezing it reassuringly. Stepping up close, Lena cradled Kara’s waist with her other hand and ducked her head to kiss her shoulder. They all seemed to snap out of it then, Kelly still halfway in the hallway, never having made it past Lena, and reaching Lena first as she wrapped her arms around her from behind, while Eliza held her arms open to her daughter. Dropping Lena’s hand, Kara hugged her mother, that bubble of happiness returning at the delight that filled the room.

 

            Drawing back from Eliza’s embrace, Kara found herself staring at Alex, taking in the aching tenderness in her sister’s sad eyes, the way her shoulders slumped slightly, tired and uncertain. It was awkward for a beat before Kara sighed and stepped forward to hug her, rolling her eyes slightly. Truthfully, she didn’t like fighting with her sister, so she made the effort to push it aside in light of the moment, even if it was unforgivable, even if it would take a long while for her to let go of that anger.

 

            “I am happy for you,” Alex whispered, giving her back a firm pat. “I’m glad it worked out this way. I never- I never wanted to be right.”

 

            “I know, and you weren’t anyway, so,” Kara murmured, her voice a little hard but a slight softening in her chest, even if she couldn’t quite let go of that resentment, couldn’t forgive her for it yet. “I just- you believed it so easily, treated her like that after everything-”

 

            “Well, when my sister tells me she was attacked and dumped, I tend to believe her. And just for the record, I also tend to believe her when she tells me her Dark Mark-less ex-girlfriend was spying the whole time, so-”

 

            With a scoff, Kara pulled back and almost made a snippy reply, but kept her mouth shut so she didn’t spoil the moment by reigniting the argument, turning instead to find her mother returning from the kitchen, levitating five glasses ahead of her with a bottle of wine in her hands. Swallowing a groan, she glanced down at her watch, restored to her wrist, courtesy of her sister, and then laughed. “Mum, it’s not even nine o’clock.”

 

            “Oh, never mind that. We’ve got plenty of reasons to celebrate, even without an engagement. Here.”

 

            Popping the cork, Eliza started to fill each glass, flicking her fingers towards each one as she sent them drifting towards each woman in turn, before plucking her own from midair. Meeting Lena’s eyes, Kara’s lips curved into a small smile, and while the secret was no longer theirs, when they glanced at each other, the world still shrank to just the two of them and the little bubble they inhabited. Raising her glass slightly, Kara’s smile grew a fraction bigger as she clinked it against Lena’s glass.

 

            “Let’s hope the next twenty-five years will be more peaceful than the last.”

Chapter 62

            Waking late the next morning, still feeling wrung out, not rested enough, Kara found herself alone in her narrow bed, and her sister’s bed a few feet away, likewise empty. Sitting up, pushing frizzy curls out of her face, she fumbled for her glasses on the desk between the beds and pushed them on her face, bringing the room into focus and confirming what she already knew. Kicking the blankets back, Kara got out of bed, flicking her fingers at the bed in a dismissive manner to make itself, she grabbed a fluffy dressing gown from the back of the bedroom door and worked it on over her pyjamas before walking downstairs.

 

            She could see that Lena wasn’t in the front room as she descended the stairs, her mother busy reading a book with Bastet curled up in her lap, and Kara said good morning through a yawn. Eliza smiled warmly at her as she lowered her book and answered Kara’s question before she could ask it, telling her Lena was out in the garden. Trying to fuss over her then, offering up breakfast, trying to get her to sit, Eliza was waved away by her insistent daughter as Kara sat on the bottom step and worked on a pair of her mother’s wellies. Wandering through to the kitchen, Kara held off on breakfast for the time being and boiled the kettle, making two cups of tea and a coffee, taking the latter in for her mum, letting Eliza pat her cheek as she thanked her, before she went back through to the kitchen and picked up the cups of tea.

 

            The back door opened on faintly squeaking hinges at a jerk of the chin from Kara, and she stepped outside into the mild morning, breathing in the tang of salt air as she eyed her fiancée, still somewhat shocked by that new term for her. Leaning back against the stone wall of the cottage, Kara watched her with a tender look on her face, so overcome with emotion that it threatened to choke her. It didn’t seem real that she’d gone from being far away, lonely, stressed and tortured over the last week, to this peaceful moment at her mother’s house, engaged and watching the love of her life garden.

 

            Lena was kneeling at the edge of a flowerbed, tending to Eliza’s plants as she pruned and weeded, dragonhide gloves covering her hands and a split sack of manure at her side as she liberally sprinkled it over the neatly organised plants. Approaching quietly, making no noise without even meaning to be so silent, Kara walked up beside her with the two mugs of tea in hand and let one go, levitating it midair to lean down and touch Lena’s shoulder to get her attention.

 

            “Hey, oh-”

 

            Kara watched Lena practically jump out of her skin, so lost in her own thoughts that she violently jerked away from her, scrambling for her wand on the grass beside her as she rushed to point it at Kara with a shaky hand. Frightened in turn by the intensity of her reaction, Kara slopped tea all over the grass, her face paling with shocked panic, and she was left floundering, mouth opening and closing without a sound coming out as she stared at Lena with wide eyes. 

 

            She dropped her mug without a thought for it and sank to a crouch as Lena returned to her kneeling position, her chest rising and falling quickly as she let her hair fall around her face in a dark curtain. Remaining crouched a foot away from her, keeping her hands to herself, Kara swallowed thickly past the tightness in her throat.

 

            “I’m sorry.”

 

            “You didn’t do anything,” Lena murmured, sounding annoyed.

 

            Shoulders slumping, Kara cocked her head to the side, her face etched with sadness, with concern. Pressing her lips into a grim line, she set the mug of tea down within Lena’s line of sight and then slowly reached out to touch her arm. Lena didn’t flinch that time, and Kara slowly smoothed her hand up her arm, to her shoulder, and then gently brushed her dark hair back, out of her face, giving her a glimpse of the hard set of Lena’s jaw. Green eyes flitted sideways to look at her and then back to the task at hand.

 

            “It’s okay,” Kara thickly whispered. “I know it’s going to take some time for you to feel safe.”

 

            “I do feel safe,” Lena frustratedly replied, picking up a trowel and stabbing it into the dirt of the flowerbed. “I just- I didn’t hear you. You caught me by surprise, that’s all.”

 

            Face softening with aching understanding, Kara’s mouth thinned at the corners. “That’s not all.”

 

            Pausing, straightening her back as she knelt on damp grass, Lena raised her arm to brush away a few tendrils of hair with the back of her wrist, sniffing and softly clearing her throat. “Well … the rest of it isn’t anything new, so … I’ll get over it.”

 

            Letting out a long, quiet sigh, Kara rubbed her eyes. “I wish you would talk to me.”

 

            Turning to face her, Lena gave her a tight smile, small and apologetic, her eyes glassy with tears she wouldn’t let fall. That was still unusual for Kara to see, sending a stab of panic through her, and she had to stop herself from fussing, wanting to wrap Lena up in her arms and hold her tightly, but knowing that wasn’t what she wanted, that she would’ve hated that even more.

 

            “I know,” Lena regretfully murmured, “but you know that’s hard for me. I’ll be okay, though, don’t worry.”

 

            “Of course I worry,” Kara choked out, pained amusement flitting across her face. “What happened to me … well, if what happened to you was anything like that, then I’m worried.”

 

            Pinching the fingertips of the left glove, Lena worked it off her hand and reached out to cup Kara’s cheek in her hand. She stroked it gently with her thumb, her palm cool, and then leaned across the gap between them to give Kara a soft kiss, lingering and light. Drawing away, Lena reached for the steaming mug of tea and picked it up, taking a sip.

 

            “Thanks for the tea.”

 

            Suppressing another sigh, just exhaling slowly through her nose, Kara nodded and remained crouched at her side as she watched Lena set the mug safely aside and work the glove back on. Kara wanted to snatch up her hand, those delicate Healer’s fingers, so precise and capable, and warm them in her own, but she kept her hands to herself, silent for a moment as the words got caught in her mouth.

 

            “We don’t- … we don’t have to do this. You can take some time. Um … whatever you need. If it’s too much-”

 

            “Being away from you was too much,” Lena cut her off. “Having you back, or being back with you … that helps. More than you think. I don’t want to talk about it right now, but don’t make me go. That would be worse.”

 

            “Okay,” Kara whispered, hesitantly reaching out to cup the back of Lena’s head and leaning in to press a kiss to her dark hair.

 

            She pushed herself to her feet then, groaning slightly at the ache in her knees, feeling far too old for her age, and retreated a few feet to the middle of the garden. Her spilt tea forgotten about, Kara shed the dressing gown and shook it out over the grass, before sinking down to the fluffy blanket she’d made and stretching out. It was a mild day, but the weak sunlight in the pale sky was more warmth than she’d had in months, sequestered to the national parks in Wales and Scotland, rain, snow and bitter cold keeping her company. On her back, she kicked off the wellies and tugged the legs of her pyjama bottoms up, and then the hem of her top, exposing her pale stomach as she basked in the weak warmth.

 

            “You don’t have to babysit me,” Lena called over her shoulder.

 

            “I’m not,” Kara insisted, “it’s been bloody freezing where I’ve been. It’s nice to have a bit of sun.”

 

            Lena looked over her shoulder then, a quick smile crossing her face as she watched her sunbathing, before returning to her work. Keeping her eyes closed, face upturned towards the sun, Kara continued to sunbathe, not entirely lying about how nice it was to not be shivering in some bothy in the Highlands, but she was primarily staying to keep an eye on Lena. Well, not so much to keep an eye on her, but keep her company, a hopefully calming presence, that would remind her, over time, that there weren’t any threats about.

 

            That calming presence was shattered forty minutes later, when the back door was thrust open and Alex stalked out, a determined set to her jaw, her leather duster flapping about her knees as she carried a trunk and a cage, with a stack of paperwork under her arms, and the telltale sign of Healer robes and a pair of trainers dangling from her fingertips. Both Kara and Lena startled at the intrusion, fingers inching towards their wands, hearts pounding, and then came a second bout of surprise as Lena scrambled to her feet, her face pale with confusion as her eyes locked onto the cage, and more importantly, the owl inside it.

 

            “Morrigan,” she quietly exclaimed, hands extending towards the cage as she rushed to Alex, crouching to open the door and letting the sooty owl climb out onto her wrist.

 

            Overwhelmingly relieved, Lena stroked the owl’s beak as Morrigan snapped it, ruffling her feathers irritably, and looked up at Alex, as Kara stood on the dressing gown, tugging down the hem of her top. Disgruntled at the sight of her sister, fresh resentment welling up, Kara reached a hand out to Lena, as if to coax her back to her side, to put herself between the two of them, although she knew that was unfair towards her sister, now that Alex knew the truth. Letting her hand fall back to her side instead, flexing her fingers, Kara’s brows furrowed together.

 

            “What’s this?”

 

            “I brought you your things,” Alex explained to Lena with a pleased lift of her chin, although it was Kara who had asked.

 

            Looking up at her, confused, Lena rose to her feet, moving her hand to her shoulder for the owl to perch there instead. “I- wha- how did you get her? All of it? I left it at the estate.”

 

            “I got a warrant.”

 

            “What?” Lena sharply responded, paling even further. “Dumbledore said not to go after Lex. Was he- was he there?”

 

            Alex’s mouth turned down slightly at the corners, and she stooped to set down Lena’s trunk, still holding an armful of robes and paperwork. “No, he wasn’t. But … it wasn’t for your brother.”

 

            Lena blinked in surprise, her mouth opening and closing, and she stammered, “I- my mo- what? Why?”

 

            Alex gave Lena a pointed look, and Kara stepped up beside Lena, squeezing her arm as Lena’s eyebrows rose, speechless with her shock and disbelief. She looked at Kara and then back to Alex, who was suddenly uncertain, realising she might have misread the situation.

 

            “There were several charges,” Alex hedged.“Harbouring a criminal. Hindering apprehension. Aiding and abetting a crime.” She hesitated then, clearing her throat, before forging onwards. “Grievous bodily harm. Child endangerment. And torture.”

 

            Even Kara’s mouth was open by the end of the list, aghast at her sister’s audacity as anger swept through her anew. She couldn’t speak, though, her throat tight as she just blinked at her sister, while Lena’s pale face turned positively grey with dread.

 

            “Why did you do that?” Lena quietly asked.

 

            Alex spluttered, gesturing helplessly with the pile of belongings in her arms. “I- well, all of your things were there, and it’s my job. There was more than enough to charge her with after what you told me-”

 

            “That was a secret,” Kara hotly cut in, her hand going to Lena’s back, a light, reassuring touch as she felt her cheeks redden. “She told you it was a secret, why would you- why would you tell people?”

 

            “I- well, I didn’t tell people,” Alex defensively replied, then turned to reasoning. “But J’onn knew. Or, well, he knew something about it. And she should be in Azkaban; surely you agree with me.”

 

            “I do. Of course I do. But that’s not my decision to make, and it wasn’t yours either. Don’t you think if she wanted people to know, she would’ve gone to the Auror Department herself? Did you even think about the fact that they’ll want proof? They’ll want to see her arm, and- and for her to talk about it, and to see her memories.”

 

            Abashed, realising the severity of her overstepping, Alex’s mouth opened and closed for a few seconds as she struggled to speak, cringing slightly as she flushed. “I didn’t think-”

 

            “No, you didn’t,” Kara snapped. 

 

            “I- sorry, I just- I wanted to help. I thought-”

 

            “I know what you thought, but this isn’t about you. This is only going to make things worse, so just stop. If you want to make things right, then leave us alone. Stop meddling and thinking you know better than us. You don’t.”

 

            Lena reached up to move Morrigan from her shoulder to her hand, and then threw the bird into the air, the owl hurriedly flapping her wings and then soaring off to perch in the branches of a Wiggentree. Pressing a palm between Kara’s shoulder blades, Lena grimaced.

 

            “It’s okay-”

 

            “No, it’s not,” Kara firmly insisted.

 

            They were all silent for a moment, Alex’s regret visible in the uncomfortable shifting as she clutched Lena’s belongings to her chest. Swallowing further angry words, Kara quietly scoffed and brusquely beckoned to her sister.

 

            “Give me that.”

 

            She was already reaching out to drag it all from Alex’s arms before her sister could offer it all up, a few sheets of paper fluttering to the grass. Lena crouched to pick them up, her shoulders slumping at the relief of seeing her Wolfsbane research once again, thinking it had been lost a second time. Shifting the armful into a secure position, Kara stooped and picked up the trunk as well, before she stepped around her sister and stalked back to the house, listening to Lena thank Alex, only adding to Kara’s ire.

 

            Fumbling with the door handle, she shouldered her way inside and marched upstairs, spilling everything onto Alex’s bed, before running her hands through her hair. She felt like crying, anger and frustration always inevitably leading to tears, but she took a few deep breaths, and then turned back to the door, making her way back downstairs just as quickly, Eliza hovering in the kitchen now, Kara’s anger drawing their mother’s attention to come and mediate, or at least try to.

 

            Lena was holding the owl cage, cupping the back of her head with a strained look on her face, as Alex sheepishly hung her head, nodding. They looked up at Kara’s reappearance, and Alex straightened, giving Lena’s arm a quick squeeze before she meekly trudged back towards the cottage, Kara refusing to move aside as she stood with her arms folded over her chest, forcing Alex to squeeze behind her to get through the open door. Once the door shut behind her, Kara dropped her arms and walked over to Lena, wrapping her in her embrace, cradling the back of her head, her voice trembling as she spoke in a low voice.

 

            “I’ll get her to make this right,” she promised. “I won’t let you go through that.”

 

            “It’s okay,” Lena whispered, her lips ghosting over Kara’s throat as she tucked her face into her neck. “She meant well.”

 

            “Yeah, she always thinks she does. But that’s not for her to decide.”

 

            “She’s going to speak to her boss. I know you’re angry at her, and I wish you weren’t, but give her a chance to fix it, at least. Please, for me.”

 

            Kara loosened her arms so she could draw back, a petulant pout on her lips as she frowned. “I’ll do anything for you. But you have to let me look after you; I just want you to be okay.”

 

            Reaching up, gently pressing her fingertips to Kara’s temples, Lena gave her a small smile. “I am okay. I’m not the one who was unrecognisable the other night; you went through a lot. I know what that does to a person’s head, and that your mood might be … off for a bit, but don’t worry yourself about other things, okay? Besides, I thought you’d be happy for my mum to get flown off to Azkaban.”

 

            Lips twitching with a ghost of a smile, Kara leaned in to softly bump her nose against Lena’s. “You know nothing would give me greater joy, but that should be your decision, and yours only. You’re the one who’d have to be on the witness stand.”

 

            Right cheek dimpling shallowly as she smiled unevenly, Lena traced her fingers down the side of Kara’s face and then let her hand drop to her shoulder, softly sighing. “Well, maybe one day I will be. And I’ll need your sister’s help for that, if that’s what I decide to do.”

 

            “How can you forgive her so easily?” Kara softly asked, her face crumpling with bewilderment.

 

            “Well,” Lena sighed, taking Kara’s hand and tugging her towards the dressing gown and down onto it, “the way I see it, she’s only made innocent mistakes, and I don’t think it’s fair to hold them against her. Not when she meant well.”

 

            “She threw you out into the street. Bleeding. In what world is that meaning well?”

 

            With another sigh, sitting with her legs tucked beneath her, while Kara lay back, propped up on her elbows, Lena reached out to cup her knee, stroking her kneecap through her pyjama pants. “Well, logically, she saw me in your mother’s house, after being told I was on You Know Who’s side - or at least sympathetic towards him - and she put herself between a possible Death Eater and her family to keep you all safe. That’s very brave, and I would be grateful to her for doing that in another situation where it didn’t turn out to be a miscommunication. And she heard that I’d been hurt when I was younger, by my mum, and she thought she was helping by trying to put her away, and she brought back all of my things for me, too. Storming into a house where you know a dark wizard is hiding, to bring back an owl, and not even your owl, is also brave. It was stupid, but admirable. And I’ve recently spent a lot of time around people who didn’t mean well, who went out of their way to hurt people on purpose, so I don’t want to pick fights with people who have made innocent mistakes. I’ve made them. So have you. In fact, you and your sister both made the same innocent mistake in thinking I had a Dark Mark on my arm. Should I not have forgiven you either?”

 

            Kara’s cheeks flushed as Lena finished speaking, her slow, reasonable words making her bristle indignantly. “I was seventeen, not thirty-six.”

 

            Softly clicking her tongue, Lena cocked her head to the side as she shifted so that she was lying on her side, next to Kara, cheek cupped in her palm as she propped herself up on her elbow. Kara was flat now, her knees still bent, but her head back against the grass, and she was blinking quickly up at the sky, her pale face a delicate pink as her throat bobbed with a thick swallow.

 

            “Come on,” Lena murmured, reaching out to gently stroke the back of her fingers over Kara’s scarred cheek. “This isn’t you. Where’s my sweet Kara?”

 

            Letting out a choked breath, Kara clapped a hand over her eyes as she quietly sniffed, tears pricking her eyes. Lena shifted closer to her on the dressing gown, pressed up against her side, cupping the other side of her face as she softly shushed her.

 

            “It’s alright.”

 

            “I’m sorry.”

 

            “Don’t be sorry,” Lena whispered. “You have nothing to apologise for. It’s a lot. I know it is, but it’ll be okay. I can help you.”

 

            Weakly shaking her head, chin dimpling with the effort it was taking not to sob, Kara let out another choked breath. “No, I need to help you. I was supposed to keep you safe, but I just- I’m scared.”

 

            “I am safe.”

 

            Dropping her hand from her face, Kara gave her a mournful look. “You sent me away, you made me think you were going to die. I should’ve been protecting you. And then for her to be like that … I’m mad. I’m so mad. At everyone, and you, too. I know I shouldn’t be, but I’m mad that you would’ve died for me and you wouldn’t let me do the same for you. It’s just- it’s- it’s shit. And I keep thinking about it, because I made my peace with it, in the cellar, when they were doing- … doing what they did. I didn’t give them anything because I didn’t want you to get hurt, but you did, and you don’t even feel safe-”

 

            Tears were running down her temples now, wetting her cheeks, and she drew in shallow, breathless sobs as Lena wiped them away for her, softly shushing her, face wrenched with guilt and pain.

 

            “I know, I know,” Lena whispered, her fingers gentle, “but I had to keep you safe, too. And what they did … I was scared, too, and I had to get you away, for the same reason you wanted to stay. I’m sorry for frightening you, for letting it all get out of hand like that. I’m sorry for what he did to you.” Lena’s fingertip ghosted over Kara’s healed nose, and Kara could see through her teary eyes the clouded look on Lena’s face as she remembered the blood, the bruises and swelling, how Kara had been beaten to a pulp. “I’m mad, too. I know exactly how you feel, so you’re not alone in this. But that anger needs to be directed at the right people, and I don’t want what happened to change us, and if you let it sit, if you stew in it, that resentment is going to grow, and you’re going to need your sister to get through it.”

 

            “I don’t need her - I have you,” Kara thickly murmured, nudging her glasses up as she scrubbed away more tears.

 

            “Always. But you need your family, too. And so do I. We need other people we love, because this- this pain, and anger, and hurt … that’s too much to put on you when you went through the same thing. So, I know it’s asking a lot, but I need you to make friends with your sister again, so you can let her help you, so we can help each other, and move past this. We’re going to get married; I want that to be such a- a happy day that we forget any of the bad stuff even happened.”

 

            Kara let out a snort of laughter, her mouth twitching at the corners as her eyelids shuttered briefly, before she reached up to smooth a lock of hair out of Lena’s face. “Okay.”

 

            “Yeah?”

 

            “Yeah, okay,” Kara agreed, sniffing, palming away a few stray tears, before she pushed herself up onto her elbows. “Or- well, I’ll try. I can’t forgive her - you know that I can’t let it go that easily - but I won’t- I won’t bring it up all the time, and I’ll try to get past it. But she has to not make it worse either.”

 

            “Okay,” Lena sighed, “that’s a start, I suppose.”

 

            Sighing, Kara sat the rest of the way up, cupping Lena’s chin and kissing her softly. “Now, I’m starving, and I need a cuppa, so will you come inside and have breakfast with me?”

 

            Lena kissed her back, and Kara could feel her smile, her eyelashes fluttering as she felt some of the tension in her chest dissipate. “Of course. I should probably give your mum her garden back, anyway.”

 

            “Oh, I think she’s glad for the break. She was busy reading a book when I came down. Well, the first time. She was pretending to be busy in the kitchen the second time.”

 

            “If I didn’t know how relieved she must be to have you back, I’d think you were both doing her head in already,” Lena chuckled, climbing to her feet and reaching a hand down.

 

            Kara took it and let her haul her up, before she snagged the dressing gown, wellies and the abandoned mug, while Lena held a few sheets of her research in hand, grabbed the bird cage, and then held her hand aloft, softly whistling for Morrigan. The two women and the owl filed back into the little kitchen, and Kara set the wellies inside the door and draped the dressing gown over the back of a chair before lighting the stove and fetching a clean bowl to crack eggs into.
