Lena deposited Morrigan on the back of a different chair and then continued upstairs with her cage and research, while Kara got started on breakfast.

 

            She had butter melting in the pan, bread toasting and the kettle boiling in short order, and Morrigan flapped up to her shoulder. With a soft hoot, she nibbled on Kara’s ear, and Kara let out a small laugh, reaching up to run the back of her finger over the small feathers beside the owl’s beak.

 

            “Hello, Morrigan, I missed you too,” she murmured, turning back to the pan and upending the bowl of whisked eggs, before starting to scramble them. “Mum! Tea? Coffee?”

 

            “Coffee, please,” came the nearby response from Eliza, squirrelled away in the living room once more. 

 

            Moving about the kitchen, feeding the owl the crust of a piece of toast when Morrigan wouldn’t stop nipping her ear, Kara made two cups of tea and a coffee, and was plating up their breakfast when Lena wandered back in. She had dirt on the knees of her jeans and washed her hands before she walked up behind Kara and wrapped her arms around her waist. Glancing over her right shoulder, Kara smiled softly, a simple sort of happiness flooding her at being able to engage in such a simple act of affection after so long apart, and she didn’t think she’d ever tire of the luxury of it. 

 

            Picking up both plates, she turned in the circle of Lena’s arms and stole a kiss. Smiling faintly, Lena reached up and ran her fingertips over the scars on Kara’s face, lightly skimming over her cheek, her chin, the bridge of her nose. Her fingertips reached up to tuck Kara’s hair behind her ears, and Lena hummed slightly, her smile growing a little more. 

 

            “Your fringe has gotten long.”

 

            “I didn’t trust anyone to give me a trim - including myself,” Kara huffed with laughter. “Why, do you miss it?”

 

            “Yes, you know I love the fringe,” Lena murmured, leaning in to kiss her. “But I think you look beautiful any way you are.”

 

            Her eyes slid sideways at the flicker of movement, and Kara turned to watch Eliza shuffle out of the living room. Giving Lena a quick peck, she let her take her owl and set both plates on the table, before picking up their mugs and levitating her mother’s over to her as Eliza stepped into the kitchen.

 

            “Thank you, darling,” her mother said, claiming her cup. “Are you done fighting with your sister?”

 

            Scoffing, Kara took a seat, scooting the chair in a little roughly. “For now. I won’t tell you why - that’s private - but it’s warranted, even if you think I’m being a cow.”

 

            Clicking her tongue, Eliza walked up behind her daughter and smoothed her hair down. “I don’t think that. I think your sister acts before she thinks, and that’s gotten her into trouble one too many times, even if she was doing what she thought was best. I think it’s okay for you to be angry, but I hope you don’t let it come between you two for long.”

 

            “Don’t worry, Eliza, I think I’ve talked some sense into her,” Lena said with a quick grin.

 

            “Or talked the sense out of me,” Kara snarkily replied.

 

            Sighing, Eliza continued to smooth her daughter’s wayward curls down, a grim set to her face. “I know you’re upset. I think she’s upset, too. So am I.”

 

            “We’re both adults; we can fight without having to drag you into it.”

 

            “That’s not why I’m upset - although I wish you wouldn’t fight. You lied to us all, even if it was for a good reason, and we’ve all spent almost a year and a half worrying about you. Both of you, mind you. You took away a piece of our family in a terrible, terrible way, and none of us were happy about it. It’s not the time or place for me to scold you about that, Kara Danvers, but don’t think your sister is the only one who’s mad at you for lying.” Eliza turned her attention to Lena then, sighing as she shook her head. “And what were you thinking, Lena? I don’t care how helpful you were being; you put yourself in the dragon’s den with no thought for your own safety. I’m glad it was all a lie, but what if we’d lost you for good? I should talk some sense into you.”

 

            Taken aback by the light scolding from her mother-in-law, Lena blinked, mouth opening and closing. Her eyes quickly filled with tears, and she dropped her eyes to her plate as her cheeks warmed. “Oh.”

 

            Kara made to move her chair back, but her mother clamped a hand down on her shoulder to keep her seated, before rounding the table. With a soft murmur of surprised understanding, Eliza stood over Lena as she rubbed her back. “It’s alright, sweetheart. Come on, up you get.”

 

            Lena set her cutlery down and rose to her feet, a tense set in her shoulders, which quickly melted to weak relief when Eliza wrapped her in a tight hug, continuing to rub her back. “You worried us, that’s all. But I’m so glad to have you back.”

 

            “I’m sorry.”

 

            “Don’t worry about all that, you just rest now. You’re back home, safe and sound, and that’s all that matters,” Eliza said as she let her go, patting her shoulder and picking up her cup of coffee again.

 

            Sinking back to her chair, eyes a little glassy, eyes cast down as she swallowed thickly, Lena picked up her cutlery as Kara tried to catch her eye. She wouldn’t, though, and Kara’s mouth thinned at the corners with dismay as she took a sip of her tea and got started on her own scrambled eggs. Chewing thoughtfully for a moment, she looked up at Eliza, who was directing the dirty frying pan into the sink, the loaf of bread into the pantry, and swallowed her mouthful.

 

            “Mum? Will you give me a haircut in a bit?”

 

            Eyebrows rising slightly as she met her daughter’s gaze, Eliza’s face sweetened with a smile. “Of course, sweetheart. Let me know when you’ve finished eating.”

 

            She vanished back through to the living room, and Kara cut another piece of toast and scooped eggs onto the back of her fork. “You okay?” she quietly asked.

 

            With a heavy sigh, Lena gave her a grim smile. “Yeah. I just- I feel bad. She’s not wrong, you know. We lied to them all. For a long time. And they thought I hurt you, and they thought I was … a terrible person, and then we’ve just sprung it on them that none of it was true. It has to be confusing for them - hell, it’s confusing for me - and I just- I wish we hadn’t done it. I didn’t … I didn’t know he was using Snape. Not until yesterday. I thought I was the only in we had. Um … if I could go back … I wouldn’t have done it. None of it was worth it.”

 

            Kara paled where she sat, a grey look of dread on her face as she gripped her fork tightly. “When you said Snape is a Death Eater, because you saw his mark … you mean you believed that, because Dumbledore never- he never told you he was a spy for us?”

 

            “No, he didn’t. Um … I don’t know if he told Snape about me, either.”

 

            “I- wha-” Kara stammered for a moment before pressing her lips together in a flat line. “When we go to the meeting tonight, when he lets everyone know you’ve been spying for us, we’re leaving. We’re leaving the second he clears your name. We’re done.”

 

            “No,” Lena started to shake her head.

 

            “Lena-”

 

            “No. I said I wouldn’t have done that. Not that I wouldn’t have helped. If I’d known the truth, I would’ve openly joined the Order, I would’ve fought my brother face-to-face instead of- of sneaking around, sabotaging him. I’m not a coward; I won’t be one now. I just regret that I had to be so secretive about it.”

 

            “He’s done this to you twice. He’s made you do things to feed him information under false pretences twice. He’s not a good man, Lena.”

 

            “He’s a better man than my brother, than him. I’ll take false pretences for the greater good over cruelty and bigotry any day.”

 

            “You don’t have to take either.”

 

            “Someone has to fight. I’m not leaving it up to other people to protect the people I love, and I know you feel the same way. We tried this before. This is what got us into this position in the first place; we both want to help the Order. This time, at least I’ll be able to do it without the shame of people thinking I’m like them.”

 

            “Fine,” Kara reluctantly agreed. “But, for the record, there was no shame in it. No one should make you feel otherwise. Not even yourself.”

 

            Lena’s lips twitched with a small smile, her gaze softening, and they finished their breakfast in silence, Lena slipping her last few bits of eggs to Morrigan before Kara took her plate for her, kissing the top of her head. 

 

            “I love you,” Kara whispered, kissing her head again before dumping their plates in the sink to wash. “Mum! All done.”

 

            She fetched a tea towel and dragged the chair out, while Lena started boiling the kettle again, and Eliza came into the kitchen a few minutes later with a comb and a pair of scissors and set about wetting Kara’s hair. The peace of the kitchen was filled with the quiet snip of the scissors and the bubbling kettle, hair piling on the floor around the chair as Eliza trimmed off split ends and Lena made more tea and coffee, watching the careful brushing of Kara’s hair, the attentive snipping. Eyes closed, Kara let Eliza cut her fringe back in and felt the strands brush her eyebrows when her mum finished, feeling more like herself as she reached up to touch the newly cut fringe.

 

            Once Eliza had dried her hair for her, Kara swept the floor and pushed the chair back in, and Lena smiled when she met her eyes. Thanking her mother and then Lena for the tea, Kara picked up her mug and took a sip as Lena pushed off the counters and stepped towards her. Reaching out, Lena fluffed the fringe with her fingertips, her smile growing wider.

 

            “There you are.”

 

            “It’ll take some getting used to,” Kara wryly murmured, reaching up to touch it again. Then she reached out and brushed Lena’s hair out of her face. “You look tired. You should lie down for a bit.”

 

            “Mm, maybe. No letter from Dumbledore yet? I don’t want to miss the meeting.”

 

            “I’ll let you know if something turns up,” Eliza assured them, shooing them both towards the door as she made for the back door. “Go on, upstairs and rest, please.”

 

            Taking their tea, they filed upstairs, and Kara looked at the bed full of Lena’s things, pausing in the doorway, before stepping into the small room and putting her mug down on the desk. Lena followed her inside and clicked her tongue at the mess, scooting behind Kara to set her mug down as well, before reaching for her trunk.

 

            “Don’t worry about that now. There’s probably no point unpacking, anyway. We’ll just have to repack it when we go home.”

 

            Lena glanced up at Kara and slowed, straightening and taking a seat on the edge of Alex’s bed. Her mouth opened and closed, and she toyed with the unfamiliar weight of the engagement ring on her left hand as she remained silent for a moment. Looking up at Kara, she looked apologetic and meek.

 

            “I don’t think we can go home yet.”

 

            “Oh, well, that’s okay. We can stay a few more days if you’re-”

 

            “No, Kara,” Lena interrupted, her voice rasping and regretful. “I mean, we can’t go home at all. Not while it’s unsafe. The house is protected, but he knows the area it’s in; he could wait for someone to Apparate to the lake, or spell the place to alert him we’re there. He could hurt you, your family, or anyone who comes to the house if they happen to come at the wrong time.”

 

            “Oh. Then we’ll just stay here.” 

 

            Lena looked disappointed, though, her expression softening with dismay as she reached out for Kara’s hand. “I’m sorry. I didn’t think it would end up like this. I thought … when it was all over, I’d come and find you and we’d be able to go home.”

 

            Sinking to a crouch in the space between the beds, Kara gave Lena’s hand a firm squeeze, her eyes creasing at the corners as she gave her a tender smile. “Don’t even worry for a second, okay? I get to have you back earlier than we thought, and you’re all in one piece, so I’m happier than I could ever be, no matter which house we’re staying in. And my mum would be happy for us to stay here, too. For as long as we need. We just- we might need to lock the door. And ward it.”

 

            Scoffing, Lena rolled her eyes and swatted her arm. “Is that your biggest concern?”

 

            “No,” Kara quietly laughed, pushing herself up to kiss the underside of Lena’s jaw. “But you can’t blame a woman for proactively planning ahead.”

 

            “Oh, I’m not blaming you,” Lena said a little breathlessly, “I just wasn’t envisioning a quick shag in your childhood bed when I got my hands on you again.”

 

            “Well, it doesn’t have to be quick.”

 

            “Stop it,” Lena snorted, giving her a gentle push. “Come on, help me unpack.”

 

            “No, let’s have a kip and we’ll do it later,” Kara wheedled, wrapping her arms around Lena’s waist as she knelt between her legs.

 

            With a quiet chuckle, Lena let out a soft sigh, cupping her face in her hands. “You’re a menace. Go on, then. Get into bed and drink your tea.”

 

            Smiling impishly, Kara was on her feet, pulling the quilt back and climbing into bed, patting the narrow empty space beside her on the mattress. Shedding her muddy pants, Lena slid into bed and passed Kara her tea before reaching for her own, and they both lay beside each other, squeezed in as they sipped their tea, legs tangled together. It was quiet and peaceful, and Kara felt a ghost of an ache in her chest, thinking about how painful it had been without her, how she’d forgotten how dull it had all become, that numb loneliness her new ordinary for so long. Kara had no intention of letting her go again.

 

            Draining the rest of her tea, Kara leaned across Lena and put her mug on the edge of the desk before snagging Lena’s left hand on her way back and pressing a kiss to her ring finger. Sinking down against the pillows, she held onto Lena’s hand as she smiled up at her, and Lena looked down at her with a tender expression in her green eyes. Finishing off her tea, she set her cup on the desk as well and stroked Kara’s hair before reaching down to slip her glasses off her face and set them aside for her.

 

            “Go to sleep.”

 

            “You go to sleep,” Kara murmured.

 

            “Mm, I will. I just- I’m thinking.”

 

            “About what?”

 

            Lena didn’t reply for a long minute, shuffling further down the bed, so her head was beside Kara’s. She turned then, shifting backwards so she was pressed up against Kara, who rolled onto her side to hug her from behind, chest to her back. Kara dropped a kiss on Lena’s shoulder and held her close, feeling the light patter of her heartbeat through her shirt.

 

            “I keep forgetting I’m not there. When I sleep, I mean. And it’s funny, because he never got me in that cellar this time, not even once, but I think … I managed it so much better when I was younger. I didn’t know any better; that was my normal, and I think … that was a good thing. I was away from that normal for so long that I had a new normal, and I don’t- I don’t think I’m handling it as well.”

 

            “It’s okay,” Kara whispered. “I’ll be right next to you the whole time. I’ll be here to remind you where you are when you wake up. I’ll be right here until this is our normal all over again.”

 

            “I keep thinking about what he did to you, too.”

 

            “Don’t think about that.”

 

            “I just want to look after you, like I promised I would.”

 

            “You do look after me. Just by being here. And you remind me I’m not there either, that it’s all over, and he can’t reach me when I’m with you. You keep me safe, and I’ll keep you safe, okay?”

 

            “Okay.”

 

            “Now close your eyes. Don’t think about him, think about me. Think about something nice. We’re in the garden together, and it’s sunny. We’re in our tower at Hogwarts, playing chess. We’re at The Leaky Cauldron with our friends. Or we’re by the fire in our house, and we’re reading our books. It’s so peaceful, and we’re together, and none of it- none of it happened. It’s just you and me, the way it was always supposed to be. And we’re going to get married, and it’ll be like that all the time, just the two of us, and we’ll be so so happy, and we’ll laugh so much together, and nothing bad will happen.”

 

            She rambled until she became aware of Lena’s slow, even breaths, telltale signs she’d fallen asleep, and Kara buried her face in the back of her neck, inhaling the smell of her washed hair, eyes closed as she felt the heaviness in her eyes. Trying to take her own advice, Kara tried to get her body to relax, tried to lose herself in thoughts - or were they memories? - of days spent with Lena. It worked for the most part, but her mind couldn’t help but stray when she was asleep. 

 

            As normal as it had all been for Lena in her youth, it was far from normal for Kara. She was all too familiar with pain, enduring her fair share of it every month, to a lesser extent with the Wolfsbane Potion or the luxury of running free, but there had been many months of clawing at her own skin once it had been pulled apart and put back together all wrong, and then the undoing of that as every cell of her being splintered apart once more to reform in her human shape. And still, it had been a different sort of pain in that cellar. It wasn’t something she knew how to talk about, although she was sure Lena was familiar with it, too, but Kara didn’t want to know if she was right in that assumption, and she didn’t want to add to Lena’s pain by letting on that her fate had been similar. Lena wasn’t stupid; she knew what her brother would have done to Kara, but until Kara told her the harrowing details of it, she would never know the extent of it. And it had been extensive, a pain unlike anything else she’d endured, but not unbearable, her body fortified against physical pain. It was the mental side that had been the worst. She could manage the feeling of her nose breaking, had even done that to herself, could cough and retch her way through hard kicks to the ribs, stealing the breath from her as her ribs cracked, could handle the heavy-handed blows of punches to her cheeks and jaw, splitting her skin, her lips, her face swelling and bruising. Even the spells to splinter little bones in her fingers, her wrist, weren’t outside of the realm of pain Kara endured on a monthly basis, even with the Wolfsbane Potion, but that splintering pain in her mind, the Cruciatus Curse blotting out everything but that all-consuming feeling of pain, was a kind of torment she’d never endured. 

 

            It hadn’t broken her, but it had felt endless, and still, she hadn’t cracked, had held the walls of her mind iron tight against the needling pressure of Legilimency, able to withstand anything to keep Lena safe, to protect her secret. Kara was just glad she hadn’t had to find out just how long she could withstand it, that Lena had saved her once again, as she always had. But she couldn’t save her from her dreams, which dragged it all back up, confusing in their terrifying intensity, so real, but so surreal as well, because how had that happened only a few days ago? How had she suffered so much in one day and then been dropped back into ordinary life, as if it hadn’t happened? And part of that was Kara’s determination to sweep it aside, to not think about it, but her unconscious mind was incapable of sticking to that. She dreamt, sweating profusely as she writhed, until she woke with a small cry at a knock on the door.

 

            Lena jolted awake as well, drawing in quick breaths, and Kara ran the sleeve of her shirt over her clammy face as another knock on the door made her realise she’d been woken up. Scrambling up, Kara climbed over Lena and padded to the bedroom door, rubbing her bleary eyes as she opened it to find Eliza standing there with a letter in hand. Her mum offered it up to her with a small smile.

 

            “Letter for you, darling.”

 

            “Thanks,” Kara mumbled, blinking and widening her eyes as she tried to wake herself up properly. She glanced down at her watch but couldn’t read it without her glasses, and peered back up at the blurry shape of her mum. “What time is it?”

 

            “Almost three o’clock.”

 

            Nodding, Kara started to open the letter, working the wax seal free from the parchment, walking back over to the bed as Eliza walked away. “Thank you,” she called out to her as she sank onto the bed and then handed the letter to Lena.

 

            “Half past five,” Lena surmised, her voice scratchy with sleep. “At 12 Grimmauld Place.”

 

            “I know it,” Kara said with a faint smile twitching the corners of her mouth. “I think that’s for your benefit; he’s the Secret Keeper of it. Used to be Sirius Black’s place, and he gave it up to the Order.”

 

            “Oh. Well, how nice to be clued in on the secrets now,” Lena dryly murmured. “I’m going to start getting ready.”

 

            Kara nodded, rubbing her eyes again, as Lena got out of bed, raking dark hair out of her face. She slipped out of the bedroom and into the bathroom, and Kara reached for her glasses on the desk, putting them on and standing, her eyes on Lena’s packed bags. Reaching for the trunk, she undid the clasps and then opened the trunk in half and set about making neat piles of clothes, Alex’s hasty packing leaving everything balled up and creased in a pile. It was soothing, separating shirts, jumpers, robes and pants from each other, shaking them out and folding them, until she’d emptied the trunk and got started on the narrow chest of drawers near the foot of her bed, emptying a drawer of her things and stowing Lena’s clothes in there. The armoire beside the bedroom door needed sorting as well, but for now, Kara just put Lena’s shoes in a jumbled pile with her own, and doubled up robes and coats on hangers to fit them all in. 

 

            When Lena reemerged, wrapped in a towel, hair wet, she looked surprised by the tidied room, her trunk beneath Alex’s bed, Morrigan’s birdcage on the desk, her books neatly stacked on one of the shelves on the wall. Smiling, she moved over to Kara and kissed her cheek.

 

            “Thank you, darling.”

 

            “I put your things in the top drawer,” Kara gestured to the dresser. “And your robes and shoes are in the cupboard.”

 

            Lena grabbed her arm and pulled her in for a proper kiss. “You’re a wonder.”

 

            “Go on, get dressed or you’ll get cold.”

 

            Humming in agreement, Lena fetched clean clothes, Kara’s clothes, despite the return of her own, and Kara watched her dress with some satisfaction to know that she wanted to be shrouded in the smell of her, in the comfort of her baggy, soft-worn shirts and jumpers, instead of her own clothes. Needing to shower herself, Kara eventually made her way into the bathroom, climbing into the tub and dragging the shower curtain around as the water sprayed over her, cold as it was slow to warm, and then scalding as she basked in it. Too many frigid dips into the lochs had made her appreciate the warmth of a hot shower, and she lingered in there a while before getting out and dressing in jeans and a jumper.

 

            They still had plenty of time, and Lena was downstairs playing chess with Eliza when Kara found her way down. Taking a seat on the same sofa as Lena, Kara picked up an old copy of Witch Weekly and started flicking through it, reading the articles and recipes she’d never make, mentally filling out a crossword for lack of a quill and inkpot within her vicinity, while the other two played chess. After Lena won, they reset the pieces, and Eliza stood to go and finish off a bit of work.

 

            “Will you be home for dinner?” she asked as she walked out of the living room and made for the kitchen.

 

            “We should be. Might be a little late; we can sort ourselves out. Or I’ll pick up fish and chips if you fancy it and don’t mind waiting.”

 

            “Go on, then, but mind you stay safe wandering about town. If they know you’re here-”

 

            “No one knows we’re here,” Kara sighed. “And they won’t catch us by surprise.”

 

            “Alright, well, you both stick together, and stay out of trouble, please. I’ve got enough grey hairs as it is, without you giving me more stress,” Eliza clicked her tongue.

 

            With a small smile, Kara climbed to her feet, smoothing out the thighs of her jeans, and stepped into the hallway, shoving her feet into boots and fetching a robe for Lena and a cloak for herself from the hooks. Lena opted for the pair of wellies Kara had abandoned that morning, and then they were out of the door, Kara reaching for Lena’s hand as they stood on the doorstep, lacing their fingers together and Apparating to Islington.

 

            It was still light out, and they were a few minutes early to the meeting, so Kara brought them to the alleyway they all used to remain inconspicuous, not wanting to appear out of thin air right outside of 12 Grimmauld Place for the Muggles to see. Still holding Lena’s hand tightly, wand in her other hand and eyes furtively darting about, Kara led them down the street with a hard set to her shoulders, her palms a little clammy, her pulse racing. She wasn’t sure why she was so nervous, except she knew that things would be tense, that there would be a lot of accusing stares and sheepish excuses offered up in defence. And she was angry, too, at Dumbledore, at the judgment she knew was incoming from her friends, and it didn’t matter that she’d lied to them; she was already pre-emptively angry to have to deal with the fallout of it all.

 

            The house seemed to appear out of nowhere, pushing in between the adjoining townhouses, and Kara squeezed Lena’s hand as they walked up the stoop and she tried the door handle, letting them in without disturbing the curtained painting stuck to the wall. There would be so many of them coming and going tonight that it seemed easier to just leave the door unlocked, so they didn’t have to contend with the racket of constant knocks. The muffled sound of voices drifted up from the kitchen in the basement, and Kara eased the door shut, keeping a tight grip on Lena, and towed her towards the staircase. She stepped into the kitchen first, several pairs of eyes shifting to her face.

 

            “Kara!” Winn exclaimed, his expression brightening. “You’re back!”

 

            The pleased look was quick to vanish as Kara continued into the kitchen and brought Lena in with her. There was only the briefest flicker of surprise on his face, before Mike, who was sitting beside him, shot to his feet, wand in hand and pointed straight at Lena. Immediately, Kara was in front of Lena, shielding her as she raised her wand in retaliation, hand trembling slightly at the thought of a fight breaking out here, with people she’d known for years, with most of her friends, with Order members she’d fought alongside in the first war. James was on his feet then, too, wand levelled at Kara, but Alex had jumped up as well, and her wand was pointed at the men across from her.

 

            “Put it down. Now,” Alex barked.

 

            There was a slight division, with other Order members training their wands on Kara, technically on Lena, who was no coward but couldn’t step around Kara to hold her hands up in defence, and a considerably smaller number defending them. Their sole defenders were Alex, Kelly, J’onn and Shacklebolt. Querl, Nia and Tonks were all unarmed, trying to defuse the situation, caught in the middle without any facts but knowing those who were defending Lena must have had probable cause.

 

            “What the bloody hell are you pointing that at me for?” James spluttered at Kelly, scowling at his sister. “She’s a Death Eater. Or have you all gone mental?”

 

            “She’s not a Death Eater,” Kara haughtily replied.

 

            “Like hell she isn’t,” Mike scoffed, gesturing to her with her wand. “Go on, show us your arm. I bet you’ve got a Dark Mark, just like your brother.”

 

            “Shut your trap, Mike,” Alex snapped. “And lower your wand.”

 

            “How did she get in here?” Imra quietly asked, her wand held loosely at her side, but the threat of it by no means small.

 

            Kara swallowed thickly, her wand still levelled at her friends. “Dumbledore invited her. If you wait, he’ll explain it all. But she’s on our side. She always has been, I just had to lie to you all to help keep her cover.”

 

            “A spy, then?” Querl deduced. “Well, that would seem to explain a lot.”

 

            “She’s telling the truth,” J’onn interjected. “Dumbledore has kept it a secret from the Order, out of necessity and for Lena’s safety, but I can vouch for her. As can Kingsley, and Alex.”

 

            “You think I’d be defending a Death Eater if she were one?” Alex followed up, arching an eyebrow at James.

 

            “For your sister? Yeah, I think you would.”

 

            Kelly sighed, gesturing impatiently with her wand. “Give it a rest, James. You weren’t there the other night.”

 

            “What night?” Mike demanded.

            

            “The night I was captured and tortured by Lex Luthor,” Kara firmly replied, her jaw clenched hard as she spoke through her teeth. “And Lena’s cover was blown getting me out alive. Kelly went to J’onn’s to get in touch with Dumbledore to verify the whole thing after Alex threw Lena out into the street.”

 

            “You knew about this?” James asked his sister, surprise and indignation crossing his face. “You never said anything.”

 

            “I haven’t seen you,” Kelly defensively replied.

 

            Everyone was talking over everyone then, bickering and arguing, Order members, who Kara knew but weren’t friendly with, chipping in with their opinion after learning who Lena was, until footsteps descended the staircase. Dumbledore swept into the kitchen with Mad-Eye Moody, Professor McGonagall, Professor Snape and Remus Lupin. There was a near-immediate dimming in the volume of the kitchen, Alex and Mike two of the last to quieten down as they argued with the long table between them. Kara could feel a headache forming already, stress and worry leaving her jittery.

 

            “I see the first order of business for the evening is already underway,” Dumbledore said, his voice clear and smooth, everyone falling silent to listen as he stepped past Kara, standing at the head of the table. He gripped the back of the empty chair with his good hand, the cursed one hidden by the sleeve of his robe. “I will put an end to the confusion now; Lena has been a spy for the Order, not just in this war, but in the first, at my request. She has been a useful asset in gathering intel and is the reason many of you are still with us today. Now, it is time for her to join us in the open, so I hope that will put the matter to rest without the need for further explanation. So, if everyone would like to get comfortable, we will proceed with more important matters.”

 

            “Here, Lena,” Alex called out, stepping away from the table and gesturing to her chair, “sit.”

 

            Pocketing her wand, Kara sullenly cast a look at her friends and gently tugged on Lena’s hand, guiding her over to the chair. Sitting somewhat meekly, keeping her eyes downcast on the tabletop, Lena was silent, while Kara stood behind her chair, hands tightly gripping the back of it, and Dumbledore swiftly moved onto the next order of business as everyone took whichever seats were empty or took up a position against the wall. There were more than twenty of them crammed in there, a couple running late, a few missing as they went about their Order business. It had been a while since Kara had made an appearance at one of them, months of missing out on regular check-ins after work, the occasional overnight stakeout to tail known or suspected Death Eaters, and she felt cut off from a lot of the happenings, but she couldn’t imagine how Lena must have felt.

 

            The whole time, while Dumbledore was talking about developments, of the movements of Death Eaters, doling out tasks and singling out people for updates, Kara kept moving her hand from the back of the chair to squeeze Lena’s shoulder, to move her hair back, fingertips stroking the side of her neck. She could barely concentrate on the information she’d had to insist on being there for, but then, her main motivation had always been to let it be known that Lena was innocent, that she’d sacrificed so much to help them. Still, Kara was called on to offer up information on the werewolves, reiterating what she’d already told Dumbledore in her mother’s kitchen. He called on Lena, too, and Kara felt her shoulders stiffen, giving her a reassuring squeeze as Lena softly cleared her throat and straightened. She was a Healer, professional under duress, and Kara watched her pull herself together to muster that same professionalism as she answered questions, elaborated further on some of her answers, and offered more information than was asked of her, the wariness filling the room making for an uncomfortable atmosphere. A few of the more mistrustful attendees questioned her, voiced their doubts, and verged on reigniting the arguing that had preceded the meeting, Kara biting out answers before Lena had a chance to speak in her own defence.

 

            The meeting was just shy of two hours, and Dumbledore and the Professors left once they’d finished discussing the matters, a few others trickling out with them to go about their newly issued orders. Kara was quick to follow on the tail end of them, all but pulling Lena up from the chair and making her go ahead, so Kara’s back was to the room of confused, hurt and angered friends that lingered behind. At least half of the Order members who’d been there would split up into groups for drinks, but Kara had no intention of socialising right then. There was too much going on, everything too overwhelming, too draining, and she was eager to get home, to let the tension bleed out of her as nothing more was required of her than eating dinner and cuddling up with Lena in their tiny bed.

 

            Alex followed after them, waylaying Kara in the hallway. “Hey, can we talk for a minute?”

 

            “What now?” Kara sighed, turning.

 

            “I just wanted to let you know that I spoke to J’onn, and to Moody, and they’re going to drop the charges related to … you know, all of what went on, um …” Alex haltingly explained, avoiding looking at either Kara or Lena as she rambled.

 

            “And the other charges?” Kara asked.

 

            “Well … we don’t really need to drop those ones.”

 

            Spluttering, Kara’s face crumpled into one of angered surprise. “What do you mean?”

 

            “We have proof she was harbouring a known criminal.”

 

            “Proof that comes from Lena. Don’t you think the Wizengamot will think she was complicit if you make her get up in front of them and serve as a witness?”

 

            “I- well … she was acting on Dumbledore’s orders.”

 

            “And they’ll just accept that? Never mind the law, as long as she was operating under Order business, they’ll just … let it all go. How do you see that playing out? Because I’m fairly confident she’ll find herself in a cell in Azkaban if that’s the defence she has to rely on.”

 

            “Okay, well, I thought-”

 

            “Did you? Do you ever think things through?”

 

            “Kara,” Lena murmured, tugging on her cloak.

 

            Mouth opening and closing, Alex blinked, and Kara just scoffed. “Keep your nose out of it, okay?”

 

            “I’m just trying to make things right.”

 

            “Well, if you didn’t have a wand up your arse about the whole thing, maybe it wouldn’t have turned out this way to start with,” Kara softly snapped. “We don’t want your help. I don’t care how well intentioned it is, you just keep making things worse.”

 

            “I’m sorry.”

 

            “Sure, fine, just- give me some time, okay? We have bigger concerns than coddling your guilty conscience.”

 

            Chastened, Alex swallowed thickly and gave her a meek nod. “Okay.”

 

            “I need to go,” Kara brusquely replied, too frustrated to linger, needing to leave before she said something she’d regret. 

 

            She didn’t like being unkind, didn’t like the way she had a bad habit of saying something in the moment and then being plagued by guilt afterwards. Even now, as angry as she was with Alex, she didn’t want to hurt her any more than the truth already did. Instead, she gripped Lena’s hand and led her to the door, Lena saying goodbye before they stepped out into the cool night. Apparating them back to Cornwall, a little side street in town, she navigated her way to the local fish and chips shop, and they stood in the corner, very conspicuous in their garb, and then walked home with a bundle of newspaper, damp with vinegar.

 

            Back inside the cottage, Kara kicked off her shoes and carried their dinner through to the kitchen as Eliza climbed to her feet and followed after them. Draping her cloak over the back of the chair, Kara pushed up her sleeves and started to unwrap the parcel, and the three of them sat down to eat, a bottle of wine uncorked, a glass each quickly downed by Kara and Lena and topped back up. Neither of them acknowledged the need for a drink, the relief of something to take the edge off, and they both finished their second glasses quickly, too, not wanting to admit that the things that had happened were affecting them more than they would’ve liked them to.

 

            After finishing her portion, Kara offered more wine to her mum, who declined, and then split the rest of the bottle between Lena and herself. Climbing to her feet, she drained the rest of her glass and then set it in the sink, picking up her cloak and walking through to the hallway to hang it up. She could hear Eliza’s quiet voice and the hum of Lena’s soft response, but couldn’t make out the words. Pressing her fingertips to the bone of her eye sockets, she drew in slow breaths for a moment and then exhaled, walking back through to the kitchen.

 

            The tense set to her face softened slightly at the sight of Lena, her shoulders dropping as she buried her hands in the back pockets of her jeans. When Lena looked over at her, Kara gave her a small smile, blue eyes tender, and her expression was mirrored on Lena’s face. Finishing off the last few chips in front of her, Lena drained her wine as Eliza started to ball up the newspaper with the scraps inside.

 

            “I’m going to have an early night,” Kara quietly told her mum, nudging her glasses up to rub her eyes, feeling irritable.

 

            Walking towards her, Eliza gave her cheek a quick pat. “Alright, sweetheart. I’ll see you in the morning.”

 

            “Goodnight.”

 

            She stepped aside to let Eliza squeeze past and watched Lena rinse out the glasses and wash salt and oil from her fingers. Turning, drying her hands, Lena smiled faintly and walked over to her. Reaching up, she pinched Kara’s chin and gave her a chaste kiss.

 

            “Let’s go to bed.”

 

            Humming at the back of her throat, Kara turned and plodded upstairs, Lena calling goodnight to Eliza before following her up, and Kara walked into her room and collapsed onto the bed with a groan. Shutting the door, Lena softly sighed, and Kara pushed herself up onto her elbows.

 

            “Well? Was that everything you dreamed an Order meeting would be like?”

 

            Shrugging, her arms folded over her chest as she leaned back against the door, Lena smiled lopsidedly. “It was a meeting like any other meeting. Good to put faces to names, though. Or just see who’s on the inside in general. Although it probably could’ve gone better.”

 

            “Sorry for my friends. They’ll come around, I just- I hate the way they treat you. I know we did this, but I still hate it. It makes me so- so angry.”

 

            “I know. One good thing to come out of all of this,” Lena murmured, pushing off the door and stooping to rifle through the dresser, tossing pyjamas on the foot of the bed. She straightened and worked her shirt over her head as she continued, “I think I have a defender for life out of Alex, now. I thought she was going to leap across the table and smack Mike across the face.”

 

            “She wouldn’t have had the time. If any of them so much as laid a finger on you, I would’ve come up with a curse so terrible even you wouldn’t be able to put them back together again,” Kara moodily assured her.

 

            “Oh,” Lena quietly scoffed with laughter, “well, I’m disappointed I didn’t get to see what you planned on doing.”

 

            Kara didn’t respond, just scrunched her nose, her face furrowing into a pout. Lena let out a quiet chuckle, an old t-shirt in hand as she gave Kara a tender look. “It’s alright. It’ll pass; tomorrow is a new day.”

 

            Running a hand over her face, squeezing her eyes shut and then blinking as she sighed, Kara pushed herself up onto her elbows. “I’ll still feel the same tomorrow.”

 

            “Will you? I hate to see you so frustrated. I wish I could take it all from you, but I know that I can’t. It’s driving me mad; I hate having a problem I can’t fix.”

 

            “I hate it too,” Kara said, sitting up, hands balled into fists as a muscle twitched in her jaw. Her voice wobbled as she continued. “I just- I hate that everything happened. I hate- I can’t stop thinking about it, um … and I’m so angry, and I just- I want to hex someone, or- or punch something. But that’s not who I am, and it’s making me- this whole thing is just so-”

 

            She couldn’t formulate her feelings properly, brow creased with her discontentment. Moving between the beds, Lena tossed the pyjama shirt onto the sheets and stood between Kara’s legs, reaching down to cup her face in her hands. Leaning down, she kissed her slowly, and Kara melted into it, her irritation dimming, Lena’s touch an immediate balm.

 

            “Maybe you need another outlet for that anger,” Lena suggested, her fingers going to the hem of Kara’s jumper, slipping beneath to find the scarred stretch of skin at her waist.

            

            “Oh? And what outlet would that be?”

 

            Kara closed her eyes as Lena’s mouth kissed a hot path from her mouth, along her jaw, to gently suck right over her pulse. It made her heart race, skin prickling with goosebumps, and Kara felt the rest of her frustration gutter as it was replaced with anticipation. Her hands cradled Lena’s waist as she felt her laugh against her throat, stomach swooping in response. She still hadn’t gotten used to hearing that again. It was enough to fill her with peace - for now.

 

            “Go on,” Lena murmured against the side of Kara’s neck. “Lock the door. And ward it.”

            The next morning, Lena woke up with a heaviness in her chest, shaking off bad dreams and keeping her eyes closed as she tried to bask in the solid warmth beside her. It was cramped and not ideal, but neither of them could bring themselves to sleep in separate beds. It wasn’t just making up for lost time; it was comfort, a silent reassurance throughout the night, calming nightmares when they jolted awake, sometimes with a shout, or subconsciously soothing each other before it reached that stage. Lena woke with her hands knotted in Kara’s t-shirt, white-knuckled as she drew in quick breaths, and she knew it would’ve been far worse than that if she weren’t wedged in beside her every night.

 

            That heaviness didn’t dissipate with the rest of it, though, and she had to open her eyes eventually, when sleep didn’t return, grey light turning sepia as the sun rose behind clouds, working its way into the small bedroom through a gap in the curtains. Shifting carefully, trying not to wake Kara, she propped herself up on her elbow and studied her fiancée’s scarred face in the morning light. Eyes moving to the grey streaked hair, Lena gently stroked her fingers through frizzy curls, finding a moment of peace, despite the knot inside her.

 

            She didn’t know how to pin down what she was feeling. It felt silly to say the events of the last few days - not even a week had gone by yet - had left her so stressed that her pulse just kept racing, a twinge in her chest every so often, palms turning clammy. Lena’s job was one full of stress, but it had never affected her like this; being a Healer was exhausting, and she’d seen more than her fair share of gruesome injuries, harrowing deaths, had been threatened and cursed out, but none of that came close to how she felt in the aftermath of the fallout with her brother.

 

            It wasn’t just that night, though; it had been a year and a half, on top of those school years, on top of a childhood worth of her mother’s treatment. But that night had knocked Lena for a loop, seeing Kara in such a way. She’d seen her bloody and broken so many times after a full moon, but that was different to the violence inflicted by another, different to what her brother would’ve done to her. Lena’s throat felt tight as her fingers stilled in Kara’s hair, and she leaned down to press a soft kiss to her brow. All she wanted was to keep Kara safe, to make her happy; Lena didn’t really care about looking after herself all that much and was happy to brush it all aside to help keep the peace, to trick herself into thinking that everything was as it should be.

 

            When Kara woke with a hoarse shout twenty minutes later, it was difficult to pretend. Trying to calm her with soft kisses to her cheeks, her brow, smoothing her hair and murmuring softly, Lena felt her stomach wrench with dismay. Raking her hair back as she sat up, Kara plucked her glasses from the desk and put them on, before she plucked at the front of her sweat-soaked t-shirt, roughly clearing her throat.

 

            “I’m alright,” she weakly tried to reassure Lena.

 

            “I know,” Lena murmured, moving her curls off her shoulder so she could place a kiss there. “Let me get you some water.”

 

            Nodding, Kara sank back against the pillows and started to kick the blankets off herself as Lena extracted herself and climbed over her. Walking downstairs, she filled a glass at the kitchen sink, catching sight of Eliza through the window, and stooped to pat Bastet before traipsing back upstairs. She found Kara with the heels of her palms pressed into her eyes, glasses pushed up onto her forehead, and paused in the doorway to watch her for a moment.

 

            Crossing over to the bed, Lena knelt on the edge of it and leaned down to give Kara a quick kiss. Dropping her hands, Kara opened her eyes and gave her a small smile, reaching out to grab the hem of Lena’s shirt. Sitting up, she took the glass from Lena and took a sip, as Lena stood back up and anxiously picked at her nail beds. There was an uncertain look in her green eyes, so serious and full of worry, but she didn’t know how to voice her concerns, how to coax answers out of Kara to try and placate that gut-deep panic that things would never be okay again. Instead, Lena just kept quiet, mouth closed, biting the inside of her lip as she watched Kara drink half of the glass and then set it down.

 

            Cross-legged on the narrow mattress, eyes narrowed slightly, her glasses still on her head, Kara ran a hand over her face. “How’d you sleep?” she asked after a moment.

 

            “Fine,” Lena lied.

 

            Kara fixed her with a pointed look, and Lena gave her a weak smile. Swinging her arms uselessly at her sides, she softly sighed. “I’m just … bored. I think. I’m not used to having so much free time; I don’t know what to do with myself.”

 

            “I wish you didn’t have to be cooped up.”

 

            “There are worse places to be cooped up.”

 

            “Mm. I’m familiar with a few of them,” Kara replied with a crooked smile.

 

            Pacing a little in the narrow space between the beds, Lena sighed again. “At least I’m cooped up with you. I can’t complain about that. I’d happily never leave this house again if it meant we were both safe inside. But I can’t lie, it feels wrong not to be at work. I know I’ve had more than a few days off before, but at least I knew I was going back.”

 

            Climbing out of bed, Kara wrapped her arms around Lena’s waist as she paced away from her, stopping her in her tracks and resting her chin on her shoulder. “You’ll go back. One day, it’ll all be over, and you’ll be so busy with work that you’ll forget what it’s like to be bored.”

 

            “Ah,” Lena murmured, turning in the circle of Kara’s arm, giving her a small smile. “So, you’re telling me to enjoy it?”

 

            “No. I guess I’m just hoping you’ll use this time to … process things, maybe. Take time to readjust, to get used to being back somewhere safe.”

 

            “I’m hoping you’ll do the same.”

 

            Rolling her eyes, Kara gave her a weak smile. “I’ve been off with werewolves. It was like an extended camping trip; hardly dangerous.”

 

            “Oh?” Lena scoffed. “You just so happened to be caught while doing the safest thing on earth?”

 

            “Well … even camping has its risks.”

 

            “I would kill you for agreeing to do that if I didn’t love you so much.”

 

            “You know how he is,” Kara sighed, letting go of Lena, raking a hand through her curls, adjusting her glasses on the bridge of her nose. “It was a job that was almost singular in the ability to get it done. I was the second option; it didn't seem like there was a third. Maybe I just wanted a distraction from missing you.”

 

            “I could think of better distractions than freezing my arse off in the Highlands.”

 

            “Would that distraction entail putting yourself back into the dragon’s den as a spy? I don’t think that qualifies as better.”

 

            “Ah, but that wasn’t a distraction. I thought of you morning, noon and night. You were the only comfort I had in that house,” Lena admitted with an uneven smile. “The thought of you got me through it all.”

 

            Reaching up to cup her chin, giving it a slight squeeze, Kara smiled sadly. “Hopefully, my presence will get you through this, too.”

 

            “I don’t doubt it.”

 

            “But,” Kara continued, a shallow divot between her brows, creasing the bridge of her nose, “you should go and speak to Sam today.”

 

            “Oh,” Lena murmured in mild surprise. “Why?”

 

            Shrugging, Kara dropped her hand from Lena’s chin, letting her fingers linger as long as possible as they slid over smooth skin. “You told her you’d catch up within a couple of days. To explain what had happened. All of it. And it’ll get you out of the house for a bit. A change of scenery might do you some good, even if it’s just another house.”

 

            “I- yeah, maybe you’re right.”

                        

            “I am. Not as often as you, but it’s been known to happen.”

 

            Lena let out a quiet huff of laughter and pressed a quick kiss to her lips. “And what will you do today?”

 

            Turning to the desk, picking up her half-empty glass, Kara shrugged and took a sip as she thought. “Help my mum in the garden. Work on my tan, maybe.”

 

            She eyed her pale arms, criss-crossed with scars, and then raised her eyes to meet Lena’s, a smile growing on her face. Leaning in, she kissed Lena and then tried to usher her out of the room. “Come on, let’s have some breakfast.”

 

            In the kitchen, they stood shoulder to shoulder, one shaking Cheeri-Owl’s into bowls, the other adding milk, and took a seat next to each other at the table. Eating their breakfast in silence, Lena considered Kara’s suggestion and thought it might be a good idea, trying to figure out which day it was, where it would be in Sam’s roster. A glance down at the watch on her wrist let Lena know that Sam would be home by now, unless she’d run into overtime. Finishing off her breakfast, Lena went upstairs to shower and dressed in something other than pyjamas for the first time in days, buttoning on pleated pants, a thin cashmere sweater tucked in at the waist, and carrying a pair of shoes downstairs with her.

 

            Kara was standing just outside of the back door, hands on her hips as she scuffed a socked foot over the shorn grass, talking to her mother. Pressing a hand to her shoulder blade, making enough noise to warn Kara of her approach, Lena said a quiet goodbye, kissing her cheek, and said a louder goodbye to Eliza, before she walked back through to the hallway and put on her shoes. Lena didn’t bother with a cloak or a coat, taking a pinch of Floo powder and speaking Sam’s address, her head reeling as a thousand grates whirled past, before it went still and she stepped out into the familiar living room of her friend’s flat in Bristol. Dusting off her jumper, Lena raised her voice as she found the living room empty. 

 

            “Sam?”

 

            It briefly crossed her mind that Sam might be at work, picking up extra shifts outside of her usual roster, given that they were definitely short-staffed now and had an influx of injuries, now that the Death Eaters didn’t have to rein in their rampant violence. It seemed that she’d been correct in her assumption, though, Sam’s voice drifting through the flat a moment later.

 

            “In here, love.”

 

            Lena knew her way about the place and walked through, stopping in the doorway of Sam’s room, hands in the pockets of her pleated pants. Sam was fresh out of the shower, no doubt just home from a twelve-hour shift, and was pulling a thin shirt over her head as Lena patiently hovered. Tugging down the hem, fluffy socks on her feet, damp hair around her shoulders, Sam turned to face her and cocked her head to the side, a grim smile on her face as her shoulders slumped. Walking over to Lena, she hesitated and then wrapped her in a gentle hug, rocking her side to side for a moment.

 

            “Come on, let’s have a cuppa,” Sam said as she let her go and squeezed past her.

 

            Trailing her to the kitchen, Lena sank onto a dining chair at the table and felt a strange lump in her throat, a nervous buzz in her chest as Sam pottered about, filling a kettle, asking if Lena wanted tea or coffee. Steering clear of too much caffeine, Lena opted for tea, listening to the soft wheeze of the kettle, the clink of china as Sam got mugs out, the fridge door opening as she grabbed milk.

 

            “Sam,” Lena managed to get out, her voice oddly strangled, rasping and hesitant. “Sam, I’m getting married.”

 

            “What?” Sam whirled around, dropping a mug.

 

            It cracked on the kitchen floor, and Lena gestured vaguely at it, watching the pieces knit themselves back together again, before levitating it back up to Sam, who snagged it from the air. She was staring at Lena with disbelief and no small amount of confusion as the faint whistle of the kettle grew louder and higher in pitch. Turning, Sam took it off the stove and extinguished the flames with a wave before she frowned at Lena, waiting for some sort of explanation.

 

            “Kara and I are getting married.”

 

            “But you just got back together.”

 

            “I know,” Lena murmured. “Um … sit down. I’ll fill you in on … everything.”

 

            Shaking her head, Sam turned and started to make two cups of tea, briskly stirring sugar into hers to help keep her awake until she could get to bed. Levitating both cups to the table, Sam dragged out the chair adjacent to Lena’s and curled up on it, picking up her own mug and holding it between her palms.

 

            “Explain,” she softly demanded.

 

            Closing her eyes, Lena rubbed her brow and then let out a resigned sigh. “I probably shouldn’t even be telling you this. No one’s supposed to know - it’s an open secret, but no one knows who - but you know the Order of the Phoenix?”

 

            Groaning, Sam tipped her head back. “Why are you always in the middle of a bloody problem? What’ve you gone and done now, you silly mare?”

 

            “It goes back a lot longer than now,” Lena weakly chuckled, picking at her left sleeve. “You’d already graduated by then, but in the First War, I was spying on my brother for the Order. Dumbledore asked me to. It … didn’t go very well - for me, at least - um … but I turned my brother in. He doesn’t know that bit. Obviously, or I’d be long dead by now.”

 

            “Thank Merlin for that.”

 

            “Yeah,” Lena murmured, rubbing the bridge of her nose. “Well, I … sort of got dragged back into it this time. Again. When Lex escaped, I offered to spy on him again. Um … I had to end things with Kara to keep us both safe. You know how I moved back home? It’s because he was staying there, and I needed a reason to be close to him.”

 

            “Oh, for fuck’s sake, Lena.”

 

            “I know.”

 

            Aghast, Sam stared at her with horrified hazel eyes, “why the bloody hell would you do that?”

 

            Shrugging slightly, Lena grimaced. “I thought it was our best bet to gather intel to help nip this in the bud a bit quicker. Apparently not.”

 

            “So this whole time-”

 

            “Well, they had to think it was real, didn’t they?” Lena reasoned, taking a scalding sip of tea. “What if I were caught? I couldn’t implicate other people. I didn’t actually know many other members; I suspected a fair few, though. Anyway, I did what I had to.”

            

            “For a year and a half?”

 

            “Just about, yes. It would still be going on if it hadn’t all gone to shit.”

 

            “What happened?”

 

            Wincing, Lena cleared her throat. “He caught Kara.”

 

            Sam softly groaned, covering her face with a hand. “The other night …”

 

            “Yes. That’s what he did to her.”

 

            “And what he did to you.”

 

            “Yes,” Lena whispered, her face spasming with pain. “Um … she was part of it. Kara. The Order, I mean. We both agreed to end things to keep each other safe, to sell the lie. Well … I’m not sure I gave her much of a choice, to be honest.”

 

            “So, that day at the hospital-”

 

            “No, that was real. Um … Kara was under the impression I’d be at the cottage; she wasn’t too happy that I went home, instead. Wouldn’t have worked if I didn’t, though, so …”

 

            Rubbing her eyes, Sam quietly huffed as she processed the onslaught of information, most of it confidential, things Lena should’ve kept to herself. But she trusted Sam with her life; she trusted Sam only second to Kara. Taking a sip of her tea, Sam shook her head and gave Lena a pointed look.

 

            “Why would you do that?”

 

            “I didn’t want people to die, not if I could stop it. It was … the logical thing to do.”

 

            “Logic- Lena,” Sam said with exasperation. “You can’t tell me you think it was worth it when that’s the state she was left in.”

 

            “No, it wasn’t,” Lena bitterly muttered, taking a sip of tea. “Not in hindsight. She wasn’t supposed to be involved, though. We hadn’t seen each other in months, so I didn’t know she was up north with some werewolves, without a wand. A stupid mistake. Of course, he’d heard of our relationship, so I guess he wanted to test my loyalty to the Dark Lord. I’ll admit, it was smart of him. He’d know for sure whether I was telling the truth about using her, where my loyalties truly were. It all went to shit, though, but I got us both out alive. That’s some good news, at least.”

 

            Her voice wavered slightly as she curtly recounted it, still angry, still reeling as she tried to stamp it all down. Lena was quite good at that, having spent most of her early life suppressing negative emotions, but she found it harder when it came to Kara. She always had. It was doubly hard because Kara had been caught in the middle of it, instead of being the one to hurt Lena this time.

 

            “You’re very lucky you did,” Sam solemnly said. “Very lucky.”

 

            “I know.”

 

            “So that’s the reason why, for the last year, you’ve been so- so … withdrawn? Because you’ve been holed up with your brother while he- what did he do to you?”

 

            Lena glanced up, her eyes meeting Sam’s before she lowered her gaze again. Pressing her lips together in a firm line, Lena didn’t speak, a lump lodged in her throat. After a moment, Sam put her mug down on the table and reached a hand out, taking one of Lena’s and giving it a gentle squeeze.

 

            “Lena, you’re my best friend. I didn’t mind that you were pulling away, isolating yourself, after the breakup, because I thought it was a breakup. And I didn’t ask any questions when you moved back in with your mum. Honestly, it wasn’t exactly out of character for you - any of it - because I’ve known you long enough to know that you’re not exactly … forthcoming with personal things. Um … I’m starting to think that maybe I should’ve asked more questions, especially about your family, instead of keeping the peace.”

 

            Rubbing her eye, Lena hummed noncommittally, “I wouldn’t have told you anyway.”

 

            “And will you tell me now?” Sam gently pressed.

 

            Swallowing thickly, Lena looked down at her lap, a pink flush creeping up her neck as she struggled to speak for a moment. “No, I don’t think so. I think … I’m too ashamed.”

 

            Eyes stinging, Lena drew in a shuddering breath, Sam’s hand still holding hers, and her voice was raw as she continued. “I don’t think … I’m coping very well.”

 

            Giving her a pitying look, eyes tender with concern, Sam squeezed her hand. “What can I do to help?”

 

            Shrugging, shakily exhaling, Lena sniffed. “I don’t know. I think- I need to work. But I can’t go back, because he’ll find me. And my mum- they arrested her, um …”

 

            “Yes,” Sam murmured, “everyone’s spreading rumours, but no one really knows what happened.”

 

            “Alex got the Auror Department involved. My mum knew he was there, obviously, so that makes her complicit. Me too, technically, but … well, Alex is trying to sort that out. It’s just- it’s all so … shit. It’s a fucking mess. There’s the- the rest, too, um … but that’s all just- I don’t know.”

 

            Pressing her fingertips into her eyelids, Lena huffed. Taking a minute to gather herself, the kitchen quiet, Sam patient, Lena dropped her hands and sniffed, gesturing helplessly. “But we’re getting married, so that’s good.”

 

            “Are you sure that’s the right decision?” Sam hesitantly asked.

 

            “Of course it is. We both- it was temporary. We were always-”

 

            “No, I know that, I know you love her, I just- are you sure you’re not rushing into a wedding as a distraction?”

 

            Falling silent again, Lena pressed her lips together, a flicker of embarrassment shooting through her at how accurately Sam’s question hit. She’d be lying if she said she hadn’t found that vaguely familiar ring box in Kara’s drawer and hadn’t leapt at the opportunity to have something good happen. It was rushed, it was desperation, but she didn’t regret it. They should’ve gotten married years ago, but there had always been that reservation, that desire to not change anything between them, always so much time to get to that one day. Until Lena had left with the hopeful knowledge of a proposal, when they found their way back to each other. Maybe she’d forced Kara’s hand, like she had when they’d gone their separate ways, but they’d both already said as much about getting married when it was all over, so it wasn’t like it had come out of the blue.

 

            “No,” Lena firmly replied, “no, we spoke about it before. We planned to get married once it was all over, but I guess there’s no sense in waiting. Not when things are the way they are. I think I’d regret waiting if- if the worst happened. It very nearly did. Maybe I am being impulsive because of that, but it’s not a rash decision.”

 

            “Okay,” Sam readily agreed, moving past it, “but that doesn’t help fix the rest of it. So, what do you need? If you don’t want to tell me what happened, that’s fine, I understand, but how can I help?”

 

            Exhaling roughly, Lena rubbed her eyes, feeling frustrated. “I don’t know. I don’t know how to … not feel this way. Um … it’s just- it’s a lot. Mentally.”

 

            “Well, there are people who can help with that. They can erase or alter your memories-”

 

            “No,” Lena softly cut her off. “No, I don’t- I wouldn’t be myself if I did that. It’s not just- it’s not the other night. It’s … my whole life. There’s … so much … that happened, um … if all of that was removed, I wouldn’t even be the same person. There would be too many holes.”

 

            Sam was looking at her with apprehension, clueless as to what Lena had endured, but able to make her own assumptions. Those assumptions would surely pale in comparison to the reality, the idea of Unforgivable Curses used against a child by their own family, not within the realm of normalcy, but Lena wasn’t about to confirm or deny anything. And it didn’t seem like Sam was going to ask anyway, too much tact for that. Lena didn’t like the way she kept that calm facade, though, only years of friendship making her able to read the emotion in Sam’s hazel eyes; it felt too much like she was a Healer speaking to a patient, trying to remain professional and empathetic, gleaning facets of information to help treat them.

 

            “It’s okay,” Lena said, clearing her throat and running her clammy palms over the thighs of her pants. “It’s fine. I got over it the first time; I can do it again. It’s Kara I’m worried about.”

 

            “How’s Kara doing?”

 

            Spreading her hands helplessly, Lena shrugged, the corners of her mouth turning down with dissatisfaction. “If you ask her, she’s fine.”

 

            “Just like you are.”

 

            Giving her friend a withering look, Lena smoothed her fingers over her dry lips as she frowned. “I don’t have to imagine what he did to her - I think I know exactly what happened - but she won’t tell me, either way. If it’s what I think … she’s not okay. Nowhere near okay.”

 

            “Just like you aren’t.”

 

            “It’s different for me. I grew up with them.”

 

            “That doesn’t make it different.”

 

            “It does. I was used to it. It wasn’t anything new. I willingly put myself back in that situation - Kara didn’t.”

 

            “Lena,” Sam softened her voice, covering Lena’s hand with her own again. “That doesn’t make it okay.”

 

            Swallowing the lump in her throat, constricted tight enough to make her gasp slightly with the effort, the sound hitching unevenly in her throat, Lena felt her face burn, eyes stinging again. “Um …” she said, voice wavering embarrassingly.

 

            And she knew she had to give Sam something. She’d told her the basics, but the specifics wouldn’t make it past Lena’s lips. She knew herself well enough to know she wouldn’t be able to speak the words. She’d only ever told Kara the extent of it, and it hadn’t been that bad this time, so she shouldn’t have been struggling as much as she was. It was almost funny, and the thought made her face spasm with amusement. Picking an easier truth, but no less hurtful, Lena took a sip of tea to clear her throat.

 

            “Before you got there … well, I showed up at Kara’s mum’s place. I’d gotten Kara out, and I came after her. Alex was there for dinner. She didn’t … take it too well when I showed up, because she thought- Kara told everyone we’d split up because I … was a Death Eater sympathiser.”

 

            “You?” Sam scoffed.

            

            “It’s what we’d planned. There were things we did that, uh, well, I guess convinced people. My family and her family. Um … obviously, that didn’t sit too well with Alex, so she dragged me out into the street. Kara put herself between us. Things got a bit messy. Kara convinced her that it had been a lie, that I was spying, and then Alex came to fetch you. It’s just- it’s all been a little stressful since that night. No one is really talking properly. Kara won’t forgive Alex, Alex is trying too hard to make amends. I’m caught in the middle because they’re both doing it for my sake, but I wish they’d both just stop. It’s all just … a bit much.”

 

            Rubbing her eyes, Lena let out a sharp breath, frustration filling her, making her feel restless with agitation. There was no way to fix it from what she could see, and she knew better than anyone; the best way to move past it was time, but that wasn’t good enough for Lena. They had other things to worry about; Kara had the next full moon to contend with. They didn’t need this piled on top of the rest of their problems. But Lena had to try and console herself with the knowledge that they were together now. At least it was all in the past, instead of an ongoing, waking nightmare, and she would be by Kara’s side throughout it, however long it took for her to process it, to get past it. There had to come a point where it faded into a distant memory. Lena didn’t think she’d forgive herself for placing Kara in a position where she could be used against her otherwise, even if it hadn’t been a direct result of Lena’s actions in the first place. She’d been born into that family; that was enough to blame herself for it all.

 

            Dropping her hands from her face, her right hand went to her left forearm, thumb smoothing over the scar, the cashmere of her jumper soft against her skin. If she did it for long enough, Lena knew it would become abrasive, turn her skin red and sore, and she tried to stifle the urge to slip her hand beneath the cuff, scrape her thumbnail over the words until the bite of pain soothed her. Forcing herself to stop, she picked up her mug and took another sip. Sam was silent for a moment, staring at her, utterly aghast and completely bewildered.

 

            “Have you tried talking to either of them about it?” Sam eventually asked.

 

            “And say what? I’ve tried to convince Kara it’s fine. I’ve asked Alex to leave my mother to me. None of that’s fixed the mess.”

 

            Running a hand over her face, Sam softly groaned. “Lena.”

 

            “What?”

 

            “Why did you do this in the first place? I mean … what?”

 

            “I didn’t have much of a choice,” Lena hoarsely replied, a little curt, a little defensive.

 

            “So you said, but … you could’ve told me. I could’ve helped you. You could’ve let Alex know. I know she would’ve helped, too.”

 

            “No. No, I couldn’t have. If I’d done that, you could’ve gotten hurt as well.”

            

            “So that’s your excuse? For pulling away, for barely speaking to me outside of work for months?”

 

            “I told you it was. Look, I know I’ve been a shit friend. I know that, and I’m not trying to excuse it, but you can understand why I didn’t want you in the middle of it. Ruby. And I’m not proud of it, but I couldn’t have that on my conscience. Just like I couldn’t have Alex, or Kelly, or anyone. You know, I can’t even remember the last time I spoke to Andrea. And it was shit. I have been … so lonely. Merlin, I wish I could’ve told you everything, I wish I’d had someone to speak to. The only person outside of Dumbledore and a few Order members he trusted to know was Kara, and we were stuck to passing notes back and forth to Dumbledore. I didn’t even trust myself to tell her any of it because I didn’t want to worry her, and it was so … isolating. I haven’t felt right since I left.”

 

            “I know,” Sam replied, her tone softening, tender with understanding. “You haven’t been yourself for a long time. I don’t blame you for pulling away. I understand why, but I’ve missed my friend. I’m grateful you tried to keep me safe, though, keep my daughter safe, but I want to do the same for you.”

 

            “I am safe. I’m not going back there,” Lena firmly replied with a choked bark of laughter.

 

            “You’re not safe if you’re not at peace inside,” Sam reasoned. “You look tired.”

 

            With a weak laugh, Lena gestured vaguely. “It’s the nightmares. Kara’s, too.”

 

            Softly sighing, Sam pushed herself to her feet, shoulders stooped with exhaustion that she was fighting off to sit with Lena. “Well, I can remedy that. Come on, let’s see what we can find you.”

 

            Taking another swig of tea, Lena set her mug down and followed after her. She knew where Sam was heading, and followed at a slower pace, stepping into the doorway of a third bedroom converted into a potion-making room. The walls were lined with shelves, and a small desk pushed up against the little stretch of wall inside the door held a cauldron, scales, pestle and mortar and a few drawers of weights, tongs, ladles and other potionmaking paraphernalia. Most of the shelves were full of boxes, jars and pouches, holding a litany of ingredients, but a section had been delegated to neat rows of labelled potions for everyday medicinal purposes. Sam was rifling through them, a few already in hand, and cleaned out her supply of the chosen ones by the time she turned to Lena.

 

            “Here. Dreamless Sleep. Calming Draught. Draught of Peace. What else do you need? Euphoria Elixir, just in case? Here, a normal Sleeping Draught, too, just to be safe. Buggar, I’m out of a Headache cure.”

 

            Lena’s arms were soon full of vials as she tried to stammer her way through objections. They didn’t need half of that, but Sam was insistent, and Lena accepted them to make her happy. She hadn’t brought a bag with her, so she set them all down on the table top when they found their way back in the kitchen, Sam putting the kettle on for another round of tea, while Lena brooded over the labels.

 

            “I don’t have much time for brewing these days, but if you need anything in particular, just let me know. Or you can brew it yourself; you know you can come and go as you please.”

 

            Blinking, Lena’s head jerked up. “Actually, I need the Wolfsbane Potion for Kara. I can’t go back to the cottage to fetch it in case my brother’s watching the place, or has it spelled to alert him. Fuck, I forgot about that; I left a cauldron full for her. It should’ve got her through the next two.”

 

            “Well, help yourself. I might not have all the ingredients, though.”

 

            “That’s fine, I’ll put an order in. I wouldn’t expect you to fork out the money for it; it’s an expensive one. Now that I think about it, if she’s been away, she wouldn’t have been taking it for months, now. What the bloody hell has she been doing with it all?” Lena wondered aloud.

 

            “Trying not to worry you, I presume,” Sam replied, refilling their mugs with boiling water.

 

            Lena hummed in agreement, knowing that was the likely case. If she’d shown up to the house and found the untouched vials measured out into seven doses each month, the cauldron with the remainders of the batch waiting for the next month, she wouldn’t have been able to stop herself from turning the stone on the ring to red. A prickle of anger stole over her, but was gone quicker than it came, Lena knowing there was no point in dwelling on the past, on the unimportant things. Kara was okay in that part of her life, and that was all that mattered. They turned to lighter topics then, catching up as they often had in the past, outside of work and leaving talk of work behind as well.

 

            “How’s Ruby doing?”

 

            “Fine. I wish she were home with me, but I don’t think it’s bad enough for me to pull her out of school yet.”

 

            “It’s the safest place for her,” Lena agreed. “I don’t like the bloke, but I have to give him credit there; Dumbledore will keep the students safe.”

 

            “Yeah, you’re right. It’s all such a- a mess, though. Did you hear about the attack in Liverpool last week?”

 

            Humming around the rim of her mug, Lena swallowed her mouthful of tea and set the mug down heavy-handedly, “yes, I tipped off Dumbledore. The Order were able to head them off. Still, three dead. I hate to think how many more will die because I blew my cover.”

 

            “You can’t think like that. Think about the people who are alive because of you. I can’t believe you were even put in a position where they had to become your responsibility to save, but you must’ve done a bang-up job both times, or Dumbledore wouldn’t have you doing it, would he?”

 

            “He’s someone who likes useful people,” Lena mumbled. 

 

            “Exactly. I can’t pretend I know him well, I think the only time I ever spoke to him was when I became Head Girl at school - blimey, that was a long time ago; when did we become so old? - but he’s a smart man, and it’s not a secret that You Know Who is afraid of him.”

 

            “But-” Lena cut off, frustration filling her as she tipped her head back, feeling her face warm as she gritted her teeth. “He’s not a good man, Sam. I try to tell people that, but no one seems to pay attention. Except Kara. But he’s happy to sacrifice people for the greater good. I get it, I understand that he is a threat to the safety of the Wizarding and Muggle world, but I don’t think that’s a good enough reason to sit on information that could save people just because it’s not the right time to play his hand. That’s what Dumbledore does; that’s what he’s made me complicit in. The things I had to do, had to see …”

 

            Her hands were shaking slightly, and Lena buried her face in her palms, drawing in ragged breaths. Sam’s chair scraped across the floor as she quickly stood, hovering over Lena as she pressed a hand to her back, talking gently in her Healer’s bedside manner.

 

            “It’s okay, it’s okay. Here, take this.”

 

            Sam grabbed a Draught of Peace from the table, forcing the stopper out of the vial and trying to push it into Lena’s hands. Pale and defeated, Lena knocked it back and felt the effects immediately. Closing her eyes, she exhaled, shoulders dropping, and let the knot of worry loosen in her chest. Setting the empty vial down, she rubbed her forehead and then looked up at Sam, shifting with embarrassment.

 

            “Sorry.”
