            Patting her shoulder, Sam just smiled unevenly, a spark of worry in her eyes. Reclaiming her seat, she scooted it in and picked up her mug. Watching Lena, she sipped her tea in silence for a minute, while Lena drew in deep, even breaths, the tension bleeding out of her as her pulse settled, and the trembling in her hands subsided.

 

            “Better?” Sam asked after five minutes.

 

            Nodding, Lena swallowed, her throat dry and tight. Gripping her mug of tea, lukewarm now, she ran her thumb over the pattern of chickens on the china and stared at the grain of the wooden table. Drawing in a shaky breath, Lena raised her eyes to meet Sam’s patient stare.

 

            “Thank you.”

 

            “That’s alright.”

 

            “I don’t know what’s happening, but … ever since we split up … I don’t know, I just- I feel like crying all the time. Everything has felt … overwhelming. Before that, I hadn’t cried since I was … fifteen? Sixteen?”

 

            “Well … that’s not exactly healthy.”

 

            “Yeah. Maybe not. Still … my mum didn’t like it when I cried. But now it’s- I think I could cry and never stop if I let myself.”

 

            “Maybe you should.”

 

            Lena laughed at the absurdity of that notion and took a sip of tea, grimacing at how cold it had grown, before she placed her mug down. “It seems silly to cry. What good will it do? And it would just make Kara worry more.”

 

            “I think she’s probably more worried you’re bottling it all up, love.”

 

            “Probably,” Lena choked on a laugh, rubbing her chin.

 

            “Maybe working on that will help.”

 

            “Maybe.”

 

            “You’re a pain in the arse,” Sam clicked her tongue. “You could at least pretend you’re going to take my advice.”

 

            Giving her a genuine grin, Lena’s eyes brightened with amusement. “You’d know I was lying, anyway.”

 

            “Yes, because you’re a pain in the arse.”

 

            “Hey, will you be my Maid of Honour?”

 

            Sam blinked at the question, the abrupt change in conversation, her mouth opening and closing as she looked at Lena in surprise. “Really? Are you having me on?”

 

            “I know I haven’t been very good at it lately, but you are one of my best friends, you know.”

 

            “Of course I bloody will.”

 

            Lena’s cheek dimpled slightly as she smiled, feeling relieved, a sense of normalcy in the act of planning a wedding. “Thank you.”

 

            Hesitating, Sam raised her eyebrows, head tilted to the side. “What about Andrea? I’m guessing you haven’t told her yet, but I would’ve imagined you’d want her there with you, too.”

 

            “Um, no, I haven’t told her. I think it’ll take a bit longer to fix that friendship; you know how she is. Things haven’t been the same between us since she sacked Kara, and I haven’t exactly made much of an effort to reach out lately, but she kept getting stroppy with me when I did, for telling her to be careful about what she was printing all the time. I should probably send her a letter, even if it’s just to warn her to be even more careful now. I don’t want anything bad to happen to her.”

 

            “It’s not your responsibility to keep everyone safe.”

 

            “I know,” Lena sighed, shoulders caving, “but I don’t think I’d ever forgive myself if I didn’t try.”

 

            “You have tried. I don’t know what information you passed on, but it had to have saved at least some people. You’ve done your bit; leave it up to the Order now. Just … plan your wedding, spend some time with Kara. It’s the least you deserve.”

 

            “It’s not over yet. Nowhere near over. I can’t rest while my brother’s still out there, let alone the Dark Lord. He-” she cut off, swallowing thickly, eyes closing. “I met him, Sam. He knows me. I was supposed to get his mark on my arm. I don’t think I can just … walk away from this.”

 

            When Sam didn’t reply, Lena opened her eyes to find her friend’s face a shocking shade of white, lips parted in shock, eyes wide. Floundering for a moment, Sam’s voice was hoarse with dread when she spoke. “You met him? You Know Who?”

 

            At Lena’s nod, she buried her face in her hands. “Oh, fuck. Oh fucking hell, Lena. What the fuck.”

 

            Mouth thinning at the corners as she dropped her gaze, Lena listened to her panic with a sort of dismay. She hadn’t wanted to bring anyone else into it, but she’d asked too much of Sam over the last fifteen months to keep her in the dark, but it wasn’t lost on her how normal it all seemed to Kara, who’d been involved in it from the beginning, who had taken it in stride that Lena had met Lord Voldemort, had been consorting with Death Eaters - even if she hadn’t necessary been happy she’d been doing it - but to someone like Sam, who’d known of the Order as some fringe organisation she wasn’t a part of, it was shocking, terrifying. She didn’t even know how to gloss over it, how to make it go away, and Sam was starting to realise the severity of her circumstances. Lena was essentially a dead witch walking.

 

            “I should let you sleep,” Lena said after a heavy moment of silence, scooting her chair back to stand.

 

            With a scoff, Sam quickly rose too, a stubborn set to her mouth as she gave Lena a firm stare. “You know I’ve worked longer shifts than that. I’m not going to bed, and I’m not finished talking. Now, sit back down and tell me more about the Order - and how I can sign up.”

Chapter 64

Chapter Notes

soz for the lack of updates, it's not abandoned!! i had some personal stuff going on so had to take a break

            The days started to blend together, indistinguishable from each other with nothing to do but potter about the house, cleaning and cooking, sitting in the living room together to play Wizard’s Chess or Exploding Snap, walking laps around the garden or reading through books they’d already read before. They helped Eliza with the weeding, pruning, harvesting and packaging of her plants and herbs, and Lena enjoyed that, while Kara found comfort in the familiarity of it, and very quickly, a fortnight had passed since that night at the Luthor mansion.

 

            They’d both been sleeping a bit better with the potions Sam had given Lena, and they’d both been eating regular meals, so they didn’t look quite so haggard anymore, but that didn’t mean they didn’t flinch, didn’t brood. Kara spent plenty of time sunbathing in the weak sunshine when it wasn’t raining, and Lena visited Sam’s flat several times to get started on the Wolfsbane Potion for the full moon at the end of the month. It wasn’t particularly busy, but they both found something to do to fill their days, to stop themselves from dwelling too much on what had happened.

 

            Alex and Kelly had stopped by twice, resulting in Kara sitting upstairs in the bedroom for the entire duration, still stewing in her anger towards her sister, and Lena tried to smooth things over as best as she could. She was glad Alex didn’t come around every day, though, able to let go of some of the tension when they were pretending that everything was fine, that there wasn’t a rift in the family. Eliza never said anything, didn’t try to mediate like Lena did, but she was clearly unhappy by the way it had all unfolded as well, the aftermath resulting in a fragile truce that wasn’t exactly peaceful. 

 

            Still, Lena didn’t expect the letter that showed up via Alex’s owl early Tuesday afternoon, Maximus tapping on the kitchen window as Lena read in the living room. Eliza was outside and got the letter untied from the owl’s leg before Lena went to investigate, opening the back door to poke her head inside, holding the letter up between her gloved thumb and forefinger as she noticed Lena standing there. Giving her a quick smile, she held it out. 

 

            “For you, sweetheart.”

 

            Brows furrowing together, Lena murmured a thank you as she took the letter, breaking the wax seal and opening the piece of parchment. It was brief, Alex asking her to come to her house in Inverness to discuss something in private. She told Lena to ask Eliza for the slip of paper with her address written on it to circumvent the Secret Keeper charm, and Lena stepped outside to ask where it was, before she followed Eliza’s instructions, rifling through the organised mess of a desk in the living room. Reading the address and committing it to memory, Lena went upstairs to where Kara was putting away a load of washing.

 

            Walking up to her, Lena wrapped her arms around Kara’s waist and kissed the side of her neck, before resting her chin on her shoulder. “I’m going to go out for a bit, okay?”

 

            Turning her head a fraction, Kara hummed curiously, folding a t-shirt into a neat square. “Going to Sam’s again?”

 

            “Mhm. I won’t be long.”

 

            “Okay,” Kara whispered, setting the t-shirt down and then fully turning to face Lena, cupping her cheek as she gave her a small smile. “Be safe, okay?”

 

            “I’ll be right there and back,” Lena promised, leaning in to meet Kara’s kiss halfway.

 

            Giving her a lopsided smile, Lena left and plodded downstairs, shoving her feet into shoes and donning a cloak, before she stepped out the front door. Disapparating from the doorstep, Lena found herself staring at the unfamiliar cottage at the address she’d memorised, taking in the sight of the Highlands surrounding the fringes of Inverness, a fine drizzle misting around her as she walked towards the front door. Huddling on the stoop, beneath the shelter of the porch, she knocked and waited for someone to answer.

 

            Alex pulled it open a moment later, looking unsurprised to find Lena there, as if she’d anticipated how long it would take for her owl to deliver the letter and Lena to show up. “Hey, come in,” she wearily greeted her, opening the door wider and standing aside.

 

            “Hey,” Lena murmured, unclasping her cloak, stepping inside out of the rain and hanging it up on the rack beside the door.

 

            Alex anxiously rubbed her palms together. “Take a seat. I’ll put the kettle on for some tea.”

 

            They brushed past each other in the hallway, and Lena stepped into the living room and sank onto the sofa, hands on her thighs as she listened to Alex potter about in the kitchen. A minute later, the stairs creaked slightly as Kelly came down, smiling warmly as she made a beeline for Lena, collapsing onto the sofa beside her and wrapping her in a hug before Lena could move.

 

            “How’re you doing?”

 

            “Oh. Yeah, I’m … fine,” Lena quietly replied, giving her back a quick pat.

 

            Pulling back, Kelly looked at her with concern in her eyes. “And Kara? She’s okay, too?”

 

            “Um … she’s managing.”

 

            Truthfully, Lena didn’t know what to say. They hadn’t spoken much about it, and that was because neither of them wanted to get into the details, but they were going through the motions each day, and there was a certain relief that came from being with each other. It was easier to ignore the lingering damage Lex had caused when they were intent on focusing on each other, both of them relegating their problems to the bottom of their priorities in favour of caring for the other.

 

            “Good, good. I wish she’d answer my letters; I’d like to help. Even if it’s just to talk, but I know … things are a bit … tense at the moment. Can you tell her I’m thinking of her, though? Of both of you. If you need anything, just let me know-”

 

            “Thank you.”

 

            Nodding, Kelly covered Lena’s hand with her own, giving it a reassuring squeeze. They both looked up as Alex reappeared, levitating three mugs with her. Two were directed onto the coffee table, and she snagged the other from midair, handing it to Kelly and ducking to kiss her wife’s head.

 

            “Can you leave us for a minute, please?”

 

            Giving Lena’s hand another squeeze, Kelly climbed to her feet and moved further into the house, giving them some privacy to talk. Lena heard the sound of the back door groaning open and then shutting, and turned her attention to Alex, who was hovering apprehensively, fiddling with her fingers. After a moment, Alex met her stare and cleared her throat, straightening.

 

            “I just wanted to talk about your mother. They’ve let her out on bail, for now, but the charges still stand.”

 

            “Right,” Lena curtly replied, rubbing her brow, her shoulders tense.

 

            “But I don’t want you to worry about it; we’ve taken Veronica Sinclair into custody, so-”

 

            “What?”

 

            Hand dropping from her face, Lena stared at Alex with surprise, her lips parted and face paling. Hurrying to elaborate, to finish her explanation, Alex drew nearer and sank onto the sofa, in the spot Kelly had vacated.

 

            “Mundungus Fletcher has been using her for years to flog his black market wares, all of his stolen shit, so I used that to bring her in before we pinned her with battery and kidnapping. She’s one of the ones who caught Kara, so when she identifies her, we’ll be able to-”

 

            “No,” Lena firmly cut her off, her face hardening.

 

            “Just listen a second,” Alex tried to reason, “Kara can identify her as one of her kidnappers, and then we’ll be able to cut a deal with Sinclair if she sells out your brother and the other Death Eaters who’ve been frequenting your mum’s house. Then we’ll be able to convict your mum with a trial and-”

 

            “No,” Lena snapped, shooting to her feet, pacing away a few steps as she raked her hand through her hair. “No, you will not drag Kara into this.”

 

            “But-”

 

            “And I don’t want my mum to stand trial,” Lena said, rounding on Alex. “If you do that … I’ll get in trouble-”

 

            “No, there are ways for us to protect you-”

 

            “You’re not listening to me. I don’t want you to do any of this. Why won’t you just- just listen?”

 

            Blinking in surprise, a stunned look on her face at Lena’s sharp tone, Alex opened and closed her mouth as she was struck speechless for a moment. “I’m just- I’m trying to help.”

 

            “I know, but I don’t want you to help. You keep making things worse, and that is- that is not helping me. And I don’t want to be angry at you, but you just- you’re making it very hard for me not to be. I’m trying- I’m trying so hard to keep it together … keep the peace between us all … for Kara, but I- this is not helping.”

 

            Stammering wordlessly, Alex shut her mouth and swallowed thickly. “I’m sorry, I just- I fucked up, and I want to undo it.”

 

            “Well, you can’t.”

 

            Wincing, Alex’s face crumpled, and she drew in a shaky breath, curling her hands into fists in her lap. “I know … what I did was- I’m sorry. I am. I know it was unforgivable-”

 

            “I have forgiven you,” Lena curtly interrupted again, running a shaky hand over her face. “That doesn’t mean I’m not angry.”

 

            There was a beat of silence, and Lena could feel that hollowness in her chest, the sting in her cheeks as embarrassment slammed into her. There was a heat behind her eyes, and she had to rapidly blink to dispel the urge to cry, gritting her teeth.

 

            “I’m sorry,” Alex hoarsely rasped.

 

            “I know you are,” Lena roughly exclaimed, her voice cracking. “That doesn’t make it any easier. To know that you know. That everyone knows. That I had to explain it to you. Do you know how … humiliating that was for me? And I’m trying not to be upset about it, but you’re making it harder by dragging it all back up over and over again. I don’t need to keep reliving it - I already lived it the first time. I’ve lived it since I was a child. I’m just- I’m trying to forget about it because I-”

 

            Face covered by her hands as she hunched over, Lena let out a forceful breath, feeling clammy and breathless. There was a tightness in her chest, and her throat felt dry. She could’ve done with the cup of tea cooling on the coffee table, but that was the last thing on Lena’s mind. Eyes stinging, despite her best efforts, cheeks burning, she tried to cling to her composure. It was still so strange to her that she could be so emotional, that she could be so out of control of herself, and it was mortifying as well. So much of Lena’s personality could be summed up as repressed, but the last year and a half, and all the years of loving Kara, had changed her irrevocably.

 

            “I’m trying to forget about it,” Lena repeated, her voice an uneven whisper as she squeezed her eyes shut.

 

            “What happened?” Alex quietly asked. “What did he do to you?”

 

            When she’d been in the kitchen while Lena and Kara had explained what had happened, they’d glossed over the details, leaving so much of it out so they were able to get through their tales, and they hadn’t even told each other, let alone Alex. With the way things had gone, it made sense she still didn’t know, Kara unwilling to confide in her sister, but Lena couldn’t talk about it with her. She couldn’t talk about it with Kara, so there was no chance she’d talk about it with Alex.

 

            “I can’t- don’t ask me that. Please don’t ask me to tell you. I can’t-”

 

            Curling in on herself, Lena’s breath hitched in her throat. Alex quickly rose to her feet, reaching for her, but the second her fingers touched Lena’s shoulder, her hand was shirked, Lena twisting away from her. Without a word, she left the room and jerked open the front door, stepping outside without her cloak and hurrying away from the cottage. 

 

            Alex came after her, calling Lena’s name, a light rain battering them as they both hunched their shoulders and stormed ahead. She was quicker than Lena, though, catching her arm, pulling her to a stop. Turning around quickly, angry now, Lena’s eyes flashed dangerously as a muscle jumped in her jaw, but she faltered as she watched Alex quickly shrink away, letting go of her. There was worry in her brown eyes, which might’ve been glassy, if Lena wasn’t mistaken. A lump caught in her throat, and Lena swallowed past the tightness.

 

            “Leave me alone. Please.”

 

            Feeling a stab of guilt at the wounded look on Alex’s face, the guilt mirrored in her eyes, Lena turned and continued to walk off. She didn’t trust herself to Disapparate then, a shakiness in her chest as she walked, a mile through damp countryside leaving her actually shaking as the rain soaked into her clothes, made her fingers numb from the chill, but it wasn’t until her mind felt scoured clean by the biting wind that finally Lena Disapparated. It wasn’t to go home, but to the landing of Sam’s flat in Bristol, unlocking the front door when no one answered her knock and making her way through to the small room where she’d been working on the Wolfsbane Potion.

 

            Sam found her there an hour later, hair frizzy where it had air-dried, clothes still a little damp as she hunched over the workbench, carefully measuring out powdered moonstone she’d painstakingly ground to dust. Stepping into the open doorway, Sam caught Lena’s attention, her dark head rising as she blinked.

 

            “Oh. You’re home,” Lena murmured, her face impressively blank. “I thought you would’ve been hours ago.”

 

            “I got paged back in,” Sam grimaced, bags beneath her eyes. “And I’ve got to be back in at six in the morning.”

 

            Blinking, reaching up to rub her tired eyes, dry from her unwavering concentration, Lena hesitated and then started moving. “Um … I should let you sleep.”

 

            “Wait,” Sam stopped her, reaching out a hand to touch her sleeve. “Is everything okay?”

 

            “Fine,” Lena blithely replied, raising her eyebrows questioningly. “Why?”

 

            Giving her a searching look, Sam shrugged slightly. “You look …” she trailed off, as if searching for the words, or perhaps she didn’t want to be honest about how Lena looked. “Like you’ve had a rough day.”

 

            With a hoarse laugh, Lena raked a hand through her frizzy hair, a fleeting smile crossing her face. “Just needed some alone time.”

 

            “Come and have a drink,” Sam suggested, jerking her head towards the door.

 

            Swallowing thickly, Lena nodded, abandoning her potion and following her friend to the kitchen. The sky was already growing dark beyond the windows, and Lena knew she should be getting home for dinner, but she needed something to take the edge off. That jitteriness inside her would be as plain as day to Kara, who already worried enough, so she thought a drink, maybe even two, would help mellow her out a little first. Sam was already fetching two glasses, a bottle of Firewhiskey levitating from a shelf, and Lena hovered in the kitchen as she watched her pour two sips worth into the glasses.

 

            Handing Lena one, Sam snagged the bottle and moved through to the living room, sinking onto the sofa and setting the bottle down on the coffee table. Taking a seat at the opposite end of the sofa, Lena sighed and then knocked back her glass in one gulp, the searing heat of it spreading through her, right down to her tingling fingertips. Blinking, she rubbed the bridge of her nose.

 

            “I was speaking with Alex. About my mum and … all of that. Um … it wasn’t a fight, per se, but I think she knows that I’m not happy with her, about … everything, so … well, that’s another Bludger to the peace, isn’t it?”

 

            Reaching for the bottle, Sam uncorked it and topped Lena up, sighing. “No good keeping the peace if it comes at the expense of your own feelings, is it?”

 

            Humming dubiously, Lena took another sip, slower this time as she frowned. Lowering the glass, her shoulders slumped. “Why is everything always … shit? For once, I’d just like it to be easy.”

 

            “It’ll all be over one day.”

 

            “Yeah,” Lena weakly chuckled, “if we’re alive then.”

 

            “Don’t say that,” Sam clicked her tongue with annoyance and leaned forward to rap her knuckles on the coffee table. “It’s bad luck.”

 

            “All of my luck is bad.”

 

            “Well, you’re in a shit mood, aren’t you?”

 

            Giving her a withering look, Lena drained her glass again. “I’m just … angry. And there’s nothing that will make me feel better, so … well, except a few more drinks, maybe.”

 

            As Lena leaned forward for the bottle of Firewhiskey, it shot towards Sam’s outstretched hand as she summoned it towards herself. Letting out an indignant splutter, Lena frowned at her friend, who grimaced and shrugged.

 

            “We both know drinking yourself silly isn’t really going to make you feel better. It’ll actually make you feel worse in the morning, and I’m not sure I’d take pity on you and give you a hangover cure on the way home. Besides, you can’t go home to Kara’s mum’s house in a right state, so I think that’s enough for now, sorry, love.”

 

            With a soft huff, Lena sank back against the cushions, her mouth a flat line as she gripped her empty cup. After a moment, she rubbed her nose and straightened up. “Yes, I think you’re right.”

 

            “I often am.”

 

            “Not as often as I am,” Lena teased with a wry smile. “But I should get home, then.”

 

            “Yes, I think so. Or you’ll have Kara forgiving Alex, if only to have her send the whole Auror Department out looking for you.”

 

            With a snort of laughter, Lena pushed herself to her feet. “You know, that might be the way to do it, actually. Perhaps I should bait my brother into kidnapping me to solve one of my problems.”

 

            “You stay away from that man,” Sam sternly warned her.

 

            “Yes, mum,” Lena rolled her eyes, setting her glass down on the coffee table and then giving her friend a pat on the head. “I’ll see you soon, you drip.”

 

            “Bring Kara over for drinks one night. Might do you both some good.”

 

            “Yeah, I think so. I’ll send you a letter.”

 

            “Alright. Be good.”

 

            “Get some rest. And stay safe.”

 

            “You too.”

 

            Rounding the coffee table, Lena took a pinch of Floo powder and stepped into the emerald flames, grates whirling past her before she stepped out into Eliza’s living room. Shedding her cloak, Lena squeezed through the living room and hung it up on the hook before taking her shoes off and shuffling down the hallway to the kitchen, already catching a glimpse of her mother-in-law as she hovered near the front door. Stepping into the kitchen, the air warm with steam, the windows a velvety blue as night started to fall, Lena watched Kara turn and gave her a small smile.

 

            “Just in time for dinner,” Kara beamed, setting cutlery before three places.

 

            “Smells good. What’re we having?”

 

            “Beef and ale pie,” Eliza answered, removing the said pie from the oven. “Kara gave it a good crack.”

 

            “Oh, really?” Lena sceptically laughed, arching an eyebrow as she watched Kara roll her eyes.

 

            “Under supervision. Obviously.”

 

            “Well, it looks lovely.”

 

            Looking pleased with herself, Kara gripped her fingers as she passed by, leaning in to give her a quick peck and then raising her eyebrows when she pulled back. Lena gave her a weak smile, shrugging slightly as she whispered an explanation.

 

            “Sam poured us a drink when she got home.”

 

            “How is she?”

 

            “Fine. She wants us to go over for drinks one night.”

 

            “That would be nice. I feel like I haven’t seen her in ages.”

 

            Lena laughed, her face crumpling. “Well, you haven’t. Not really.”

 

            “Yeah. I guess I haven’t seen anyone, really.”

 

            “Maybe we could invite a few more people.”

 

            “You mean Alex, obviously,” Kara curtly replied, their conversation no longer a contained whisper between the two of them.

 

            Dragging out a chair before the plate that levitated to the table, briefly pausing to thank Eliza, Lena took a seat. “Yes, obviously. She’s friends with Sam, isn’t she? Kelly, too. And Nia. Maybe we can have a girls' night.”

 

            “What a great idea,” Eliza brightly interjected.

 

            Humming dubiously, Kara took the plate her mother handed her and took a seat at the table, grumpy as she frowned at her plate and pursed her lips. She didn’t respond, just picked up her cutlery and started to eat, letting her mother change the subject. 

 

 

            Despite Kara’s reluctance, Lena arranged drinks with all of the girls for that Friday night, knowing that Sam was off, and Kara wearily caved when Lena asked her to come as well. They’d settled on Alex and Kelly’s place for their drinks, with more space than Sam’s flat or Eliza’s cottage, and they were glad for the extra space when they showed up late to find more than the six of them Lena had anticipated, and more than just the girls. Kara had baulked at the thought of showing up on the dot and being left to make small talk with her sister, and Lena had relented on that, knowing it would’ve been left up to her and Kelly to fill the awkward silence, but they hadn’t thought there would be a dozen other people there, some familiar to Lena and others not at all. 

 

            Kara knew them all, of course, familiar with every Order member from her numerous meetings over the two wars. There were a few newer faces, though, barely out of Hogwarts but eager and bright-eyed with the rush that came from being part of something secret, something exciting, the thrill of danger not yet stamped out by death, grief or pain. The rest were all seasoned, there at the Department of Mysteries or members during the First Wizarding War. They were all at least one drink in by the time Kara opened the door to her sister’s home, two bottles of wine in hand, the sound of music, laughter and loud voices washing over her as she waited for Lena to slip inside and shut the door behind them.

 

            Querl was the first one to spot them, eyes glazed and a smile on his face as he breezed past, two drinks in hand as he went to find Nia. Kara gave him a one-armed hug, glad to have other allies within the house to help diffuse what was surely to be an awkward night. She’d already spotted James chatting to J’onn, and knew that he would probably sulk all night about Lena being there, and Kara hadn’t exactly been keen on coming in the first place, let alone with the drama that was sure to unfold after a few drinks were in everyone. She just hoped that they kept it to snide remarks instead of duelling. That would be all she needed.

 

            “Come on,” Lena murmured in her ear, standing close behind her, “have a drink, and stop walking around with a face like a slapped arse.”

 

            Kara could hear the amusement in her voice and reached behind her to squeeze Lena’s ribs, smiling at the indignant squawk that escaped her from being tickled. Finding her hand, Kara towed her through the house to the kitchen, raiding the cupboards for clean glasses and uncorking a bottle of elderflower wine. Pouring Lena a glass first, and then one for herself, Kara gently clinked them together and leaned in to kiss her. Taking a sip of wine, she looked around the kitchen, taking in the group clustered around the table, spotting Mike with Imra, Winn and a few of the newer members. Taking Lena’s hand, Kara led her back through towards the living room and almost poured her glass of wine over the front of her sister when Alex stepped out into the hallway as she went to step into the living room.

 

            “Oh,” Alex said, shifting awkwardly, “you’re here. Good. I, uh, I was hoping you’d come. So we could talk.”

 

            “Not tonight,” Kara said over the music, trying to be cordial but hating the awkwardness.

 

            She brushed past Alex and forged deeper into the living room, and Lena was surprisingly quiet, instead of trying to coax her into being friends with her sister. Kelly spotted them and gave them both a hug, leading Kara over to an empty spot on the sofa, and Lena perched on the arm of it, the rest of their first bottle of wine cradled in the crook of her arm. Finishing her first glass quickly, Kara asked her to refill it, sitting there with a rather dour expression on her face as she watched everyone animatedly chat and laugh, the music giving her a headache.

 

            The full moon was fast approaching, just over a week away now, but Kara was feeling the effects already. A little pale, feeling tired, she knew that it was likely just the lingering aftermath of their ordeal, but she almost wished she’d played it up, pinned it on the full moon at the end of the month, if only to get out of the party. She knew Lena would’ve immediately caved, would’ve sat at home with her, fretted about the early onset of symptoms, theorising whether the condition worsened the longer you’d been inflicted with it, and Kara didn’t want to cause her any extra stress. Not when she could suck it up and play nice with her sister for one night, if only for a distraction from everything else. It almost felt normal, like so many nights spent drinking with Order members to try and forget the danger, and to celebrate surviving another day.

 

            But she was there with Lena, whose help to the Order was finally acknowledged, and Kara wanted her to be there, with other people who’d risked their lives, so she could at least be shown the same respect, feel the same pride of being on the in of a group who were on the right side of things. So, she sipped her second glass and slipped into the conversation Nia and Tonks were having beside her on the sofa, until the wine started to work, and Kara stopped thinking about Alex throwing Lena out into the street, and Lex looming over Kara, gripping her face hard, and Lena’s white face when she’d sent Kara into the fireplace, and Otis Graves’ face before he slammed his fist into Kara’s face, or the cold cellar she’d been locked inside, and how dark it had been, and how much her head had hurt as blood seeped from her cuts, and how loud her screams had been as they’d echoed through the space. There were a lot of things she didn't want to think about, and she kept drinking until the edges of her mind blurred, and the tension bled out of her.

 

            They were onto the second bottle, Lena wrapped up in conversation with Sam and Kelly, Kara refilling her glass in the kitchen, leaving the bottle on the counter, and she was walking back down the hallway when Alex materialised in front of her again. Kara had managed to avoid her since first bumping into her, but she’d caught her sister watching her a few times from her spot on the sofa, clearly biding her time to confront her. Grabbing Kara’s arm, Alex pulled her towards the foot of the staircase as Kara spluttered.

 

            “Let go.”

 

            “We need to talk.”

 

            “I don’t want to talk to you.”

 

            “This isn’t optional,” Alex curtly replied, propelling her up a few steps, until Kara accepted her fate and continued upwards.

 

            Alex didn’t let go of her until she’d shut them both inside her bedroom, and remained in front of the closed door to block the route of escape. Scowling at her, Kara rubbed her arm, as if it had hurt, and then swallowed a gulp of wine. Closing her eyes, Alex leaned back against the door and sighed, the silence tense for a moment before she broke it.

 

            “I’ve been trying to get in touch with you.”

 

            “I’m aware.”

 

            “You didn’t want to respond?”

 

            “I didn’t think it was necessary.”

 

            “I sent you three letters, and you didn’t question if it was important or not?” Alex grumbled.

 

            “Well, they were very vague. You didn’t say what they were for.”

 

            “I never had to before. I’ve always been able to ask you to come, and you always would without question.”

 

            Softly huffing as she ducked her head, fiddling with her glasses, Kara swallowed her annoyance. “You know why, so we’re not getting into this again. I don’t want to spoil the night with another row.”

 

            “I’m not trying to have a row with you, you numpty, I’m trying to help your fiancée.” 

 

            “She doesn’t need you meddling any more and calling it helping, so-”

 

            “If you’d just listen for five seconds-”

 

            “Well, out with it then. Stop beating about the flutterby bush.”

 

            Drawing in a sharp breath and huffing, Alex straightened and squared her shoulders, a serious expression on her face as Kara met her steady gaze. “I don’t think Lena’s doing very well.”

 

            Blinking, Kara stared at her expressionlessly for a moment before she let out a scoff of laughter. “Thank you for pointing out the obvious.”

 

            Walking towards her, trying to reach past her for the door handle, Kara was stopped by Alex’s hand on her arm. Glancing up at her, irritation flashing across her face, Kara opened her mouth to give a sharper retort when her sister gave her a pleading look.

 

            “Kara,” she said in a softer tone, “I’m serious. I spoke to her the other day; she’s putting on a brave face for you, but she’s not coping. And I think she was still holding so much back. She’s hurting a lot, from what I did, what happened before, from what happened when she was younger. She wouldn’t say what exactly, but it’s clearly affecting her more than she’s letting on. With you, too, I bet. I mean, she said as much to me.”

 

            “What did she say to you?” Kara hoarsely asked.

 

            “That she was angry with me. Still. That she forgave me, but she’s still angry, but she’s trying not to be to keep the peace. Because she doesn’t want to encourage this rift between us. But I care about her, and you know that I do, even if I behaved rashly because I believed what you told me. I never wanted to believe it, and I never wanted her to get hurt, and I’m sorry to have been part of that, but I can’t not tell you she’s struggling, no matter how mad you are at me. You can both be angry at me all you like, but she needs help, and that’s all that matters right now. You both do.”

 

            Kara was silent for a moment, staring at the floor as she rubbed her brow, a furrowed look of concern on her face, and Alex didn’t speak for a second, the silence tense and thick again, before she audibly swallowed.

 

            “I just thought you should know.”

 

            “Yeah. Thanks,” Kara muttered.

 

            “Let me know how I can help.”

 

            Nodding, Kara waited a few seconds before her sister moved aside and let her go. Pulling open the door, the muffled sound of music grew louder, and Kara hesitated before she made for the bathroom. Opening the door, she locked herself inside and blindly fumbled for the light string, yanking it to turn on the overhead light, a bright glow filling the room. Stumbling towards the toilet, she sat on the closed lid and put her head in her hand, elbow braced on her thigh, and closed her eyes, breathing slowly for a couple of minutes.

 

            Snapping herself out of it, Kara rose to her feet, drained her wine and then splashed some water on her face. Drying it off with a hand towel, she stared at her pallid reflection in the mirror before jerking the door open and stepping out into the hallway, the loud thump of music disorienting as it seemed to pulse through the floorboards. It might’ve been the wine, too, or the tight feeling of panic constricting her chest, and she walked downstairs with a pit in her stomach.

 

            Pushing through the other party guests, she froze at the sight of Lena, a soft smile on her face as she nodded, then elegantly tipped her head back as she laughed, cheeks dimpling, gesturing with her glass of wine. She looked fine. But then, she always had, even back at Hogwarts, when she’d endured unimaginable things on the summer holidays. She’d been broody and cynical, but that was just taken as part of her personality, as much as her quiet studiousness, her quick intelligence, and even Kara hadn’t known the truth until it was far too late to do anything to help stop it. But she knew her. She knew her now better than she ever had, and even at school, she’d picked up on the fact that something was wrong, even if Lena was a closed book on it all. And of course Kara knew she wasn’t coping well now, that Lena flinched when someone moved suddenly, that she’d had nightmares until she’d started taking the potions Sam had given them, that even if there weren’t signs, Kara knew it anyway, because how could Lena be okay? But for the rest of the night, she couldn’t shake that feeling of everything being wrong.

 

            She watched Lena closely as the party raged on, lingering in the muffled hum of tipsiness while everyone else drank themselves silly, watching her fiancee knock back shots of Firewhiskey like water with Sam and Kelly, watching her laugh, her eyes bright and glazed when she searched for Kara, face splitting with a smile, cheeks flushed from the drink and clammy from the warmth of too many bodies in one room. It reminded Kara so much of that first party she’d brought Lena to, for Kelly’s birthday all those years ago, trying to mediate her friends who didn’t trust Lena and Lena’s comfort, except Lena seemed to be doing just fine on her own, and Kara didn’t know how much of it was an act.

 

            When the party started to wind down, she was filled with relief. People trickled off, the music was turned down, and no one had started a duel in the kitchen, which was a relief. Alex had taken the house off the Floo Network and neither of them were in the right condition to Apparate back to Cornwall, Lena more so than Kara, so they took up the offer of the spare room, sitting in the living room until everyone else left, Lena perched on Kara’s lap as they drank bottles of ale that had been handed to them at some point. Winn was staying as well, and when Alex fetched blankets for him to sleep on the sofa, they made their way up to bed, Kara’s hands on Lena’s waist as she led her up the stairs.

 

            Inside the dark room, Kara shut the door and was pushed up against it as Lena kissed her roughly. Caught by surprise, she let her kiss her for a moment before she gripped Lena’s waist and gently but firmly pushed her away, putting a few inches between their faces. Reaching up, fumbling in the dark, Kara tenderly stroked Lena’s cheek, their breaths loud in the silence, and she swallowed thickly.

 

            “I spoke to Alex,” Kara quietly spoke.

 

            Lena leaned in and kissed the corner of her mouth, across her cheek, a rasping hum catching at the back of her throat. “Mm, good.”

 

            “About you.”

 

            Freezing, her breath warm on the side of Kara’s face, Lena was silent for a moment. When she spoke, her voice was still just as quiet in the stillness of the room. “Don’t say anything,” she urgently whispered, “Please don’t.”

 

            “Lena-”

 

            Reaching up to press her fingertips to Kara’s lips, Lena hushed her, and Kara swallowed the lump caught in her throat, catching her hand and pressing a kiss to her fingertips before she squeezed gently and let go of her hand.

 

            “Let’s go to bed,” Kara conceded.

 

            Watching the shadow of her fiancée turn away from her, Kara kicked off her shoes and unbuttoned her jeans, listening to the soft sound of fabric as Lena pulled back the blankets, undressed and climbed into bed. Getting in beside her, Kara moved across the mattress until she felt her, pressing herself up against Lena’s back and wrapping an arm around her as she softly sighed. Dizzy and full of worry, Kara found it hard to fall asleep, not quite reassured by the solid warmth of Lena in her arms, and the sky was a shade lighter when she finally drifted off.

 

            Waking a few hours later, exhausted and dry-eyed in an empty bed, Kara fumbled across the cold sheets for Lena and then rolled over to pick up her glasses on the nightstand, confirming what she already knew when she looked at the empty side of the bed. Staggering up, her knees aching, Kara fetched her clothes from the floor and dressed before stepping out of the bedroom. The smell of coffee and bacon greeted her, the chatter of voices drifting upstairs with it, and she plodded down to the kitchen, stifling a yawn as she stepped into it. James, Nia and Querl seemed to have spent the night as well, and Kara mumbled a greeting as she padded towards the stove, where Lena was overseeing the bacon.

 

            Wrapping her arms around Lena’s waist, Kara kissed her shoulder. “Morning.”

 

            “Morning,” Lena lightly replied, no wariness in her voice, no panic that she might be questioned in front of Kara’s friends.

 

            “Coffee?” Alex asked, three cups arrayed before her as the kettle whistled.

 

            Kara gave her a brief glance and nodded, “ta.”

 

            In short order, she had a bacon sandwich in front of her and was sipping her coffee as she watched Lena from across the room, a brooding look on her face as she tuned out the conversation around her. Everyone seemed to have pulled through okay, although there was more than one green face, no hangover cures doled out by Lena that morning, considering it was supposed to be just a few drinks with the girls, and Kara didn’t feel like talking to anyone. Anyone but Lena, who stayed across the room the entire time.

 

            After she’d finished eating, Kara put her dishes in the sink, a few others already being cleaned by the sponge, and suggested they leave. She said a general goodbye to the room and fetched her cloak from the hook near the front door, and stepped out into the crisp morning, standing on the stoop as she waited for Lena to fasten her cloak and follow her outside. Giving her a wavering smile, her stomach twisting uncomfortably, Kara held her hand out for Lena to take and thought hard about their destination before Apparating.

 

            It wasn’t far, or not as far as Cornwall, where Lena was expecting them to end up, and Kara breathed in the cold air of the Highlands, the bite of it familiar, perhaps even warmer than she was used to. Dropping Lena’s hand, she rounded on her, standing in the shade of the trees surrounding the empty bothy. Kara knew it would have been empty, cleared out after the wannabe Death Eaters had come through and taken her, and brutalised a few of the other werewolves for good measure before leaving. She could see the confusion on Lena’s face, drawing her cloak around herself a little tighter as the wind blew through the trees.

 

            “Where are we?” Lena asked, her eyes darting around beneath furrowed eyebrows, before her gaze settled on Kara.

 

            Drawing in a shaky breath, Kara let out a short sigh and gestured towards the bothy. “This is where I stayed for a while. We moved from bothy to bothy, to stay away from Muggles. And that’s where I was attacked.” Kara pointed to a spot in the shade of the trees. “I ran. Made to … about there.”

 

            Her finger strayed maybe two metres away from that spot, her lips twitching with a bitter smile. Lena’s face paled, a stiffness to her features as the corners of her mouth tightened. “We don’t-”

 

            “Yes, we do,” Kara cut her off. “We have to talk about it. Because I’m not okay, and you’re not okay, and we can’t just- we can’t keep pretending that we are. I need to know what happened.”

 

            “You know what happened,” Lena said with an impatient huff, shifting restlessly as she looked away, a muscle twitching in her jaw. “I told you what happened, years ago; it wasn’t any different to that. It was actually better this time.”

 

            “Lena.”

 

            There was an agonised note in Kara’s voice as she took a step forward, reaching for her, but her hand fell short as Lena gave her a cutting glance and then turned away. Shoulders caving, a quiet devastation in her chest, Kara let out a soft breath and then straightened, squaring her shoulders as determination filled her.

 

            “Alright, then. You don’t have to talk, but you can listen,” Kara firmly told her, before forging onwards. “It was stupid of me, in hindsight, not to have my wand on me. I thought it would make them trust me more if they thought I was an uneducated witch, if I hadn’t been to Hogwarts, didn’t have a wand. It worked, until it backfired. All I could do was run, but I didn’t get very far. I scratched up Benjamin Lockwood quite well, though, and Greyback got in a few bites. They seemed amused, let us scrap for a little while, after they’d already stopped me from running. Manchester tried to get them to stop, but he got hexed in the process, and then they took me. I couldn’t have stopped them, no matter how hard I tried. I didn’t even know where they’d taken me at first. Not even when I met your brother.”

 

            Kara fell silent for a moment, waiting for a response, gauging Lena’s thoughts by the stiff line of her shoulders. When nothing but the wind through the trees broke the silence, Kara cleared her throat and continued, her skin clammy and cool as she balled her hands into fists in the wool of her cloak. 

 

            “I don’t know if he remembered me from the Department of Mysteries when I duelled him, or whether he just assumed from the scars, or maybe Veronica told him who I was, but he knew. He knew about us, as well. He asked me a few questions, but I refused to answer. Um … he had me taken down to the basement, then. The big guy - Otis Graves, isn’t it? - he had a fair crack at it first, but the funny thing is, I’ve been a werewolf since I was twelve, and that’s over two hundred full moons. I know pain. I know what it feels like to have every piece of my body pulled apart and put back together wrong, and then again. A broken nose? It didn’t bother me that much. I could live with that. I was more worried about protecting you, keeping my mind shut so your brother wouldn’t know you were a spy.”

 

            Her voice wavered then, and Kara ducked her head down, fiddling with her fingers, picking at her cuticles. “Um … I guess he realised I wasn’t going to break over a beating. It hurt like hell, I’ll say, but it was bearable. All I could think about was you. Keeping you safe, wondering if he’d already caught you, if you’d been hurt - worse - um … and I thought a lot about how you must’ve felt when you were little. It was so cold down there, and dark. You said your mum used to leave you down there for days. I think it hurt more to think about you down there than it did to have Otis break every bone he did. Um … but then she had her go. I don’t know why … your brother didn’t do it himself … um, but I couldn’t- I would’ve let them kill me before I told him a single thing about you. But I thought I knew pain. That was … something else. And I know it was all in my head, but it just- it went on and on, and I didn’t know how long it had been. It could’ve been days, and I wouldn’t have been surprised. And I knew that he’d make it stop if I just … talked, but I couldn’t. And then you were there, and I would’ve rathered the Cruciatus Curse every day for a year straight if it had meant that you’d stay safe. And I wanted you to kill me when he asked, and I was sorry for wanting you to do that, but I knew he’d kill me anyway, and I just wanted you to be okay.”

 

            Tears were swimming in her eyes now, and Kara rubbed the bridge of her nose as she fought for her composure. “Um … and then you sent me away, and I didn’t- I didn’t know if you were- I don’t know what I would’ve done if you were. But we both got out, and it doesn’t feel like it’s over, because I’m just so … worried all the time, and … I remember how much it hurt, and how nothing has ever hurt that much, but that’s not what I’m worried about. I just- I want you to talk to me, and I don’t want you to blame yourself, and I knew that if I told you … you would blame yourself, even though you had nothing to do with what happened. I was caught, whether your brother wanted me or not. But I didn’t want to tell you what happened, because you burnt the quill, and you don’t have the candle, so all I can think about is what new way you’ll find to hurt yourself, um … but I don’t think it’s helping to not talk about it, and I know … nothing feels right, but I don’t want it to get worse. Not when I just got you back.”

 

            Lena still had her back turned to her, and Kara raised her head, eyes reddened as she wiped her nose on her sleeve, mouth turned down at the corners, and watched her. It was a long minute, the tension unbearable, with Kara so badly wanting to be held by her, but she didn’t move. Eventually, Lena tipped her head back, and Kara knew her eyes would’ve been closed, that her brow would be furrowed together in a stern look as she silently agonised over her words. Slowly but surely, they came.

 

            “The night I left … he was at my family’s estate. You know I didn’t tell you I went there, but it was fine. I hate being in that house, but it wasn’t anything new. And he was pleased, at the beginning. He was out of Azkaban, and I lied and told him my mum was wrong, that you were nothing more than an experiment, a test subject for my Wolfsbane research, so that I could rid us of werewolves. I had to tread carefully, had to earn his trust back. Nothing really changed at the beginning; I went to work, I came home, I ate dinner with him, and played Wizard’s Chess over a drink. I agreed with his ideas, his beliefs. I started to join him for drinks when everyone would come over, all the bottom feeders hoping to earn a Dark Mark. I think he liked inviting them over because it fed his ego; he would go out with Death Eaters, of course, but I wasn’t allowed to join him then. Not for a while. I would follow him if I knew where he was going - in Animagus form, of course. It took months; he barely laid a finger on me. There were times, of course - he’s a cruel man, but he wasn’t at first - and they became more frequent as time went by, when he lashed out. But he never got me down to the cellar. Not once. The worst I suffered at his hands was a slap across the face, but the threat was there. It was always there. Some nights, I couldn’t sleep out of fear of him coming home in a rage. And he made it quite clear, too, especially after he took me to meet him. I thought I was done for there and then, didn’t think I could shield my mind against someone supposedly so powerful, and he tried to give me his mark. It makes my skin crawl to think about it. I guess I’m a Slytherin through and through, though; I talked my way out of it, bought myself more time.”

 

            Lena let out a hoarse laugh, raking a hand through her dishevelled hair. Kara could hear the roughness in the sound but knew she wasn’t crying, that she would’ve been fighting hard not to be. Even now, just the two of them, Lena would try her hardest not to show an ounce of emotion that could’ve been contrived as weakness - no matter how much she was hurting. Hugging her arms to herself, keeping her distance until Lena finished speaking, Kara remained silent, waiting patiently.

 

            “I knew I was on borrowed time, then. He was fuming when he got home from that meeting. He dragged me out of bed, grabbed me before I could get my wand. I don’t know if I would’ve defended myself even if I had reached it in time. I slapped him; I thought that might be when he snapped, but my mother stopped him. I don’t know why. She never stopped him before; she instigated it in the first place. I think maybe he was frightening her with how far he’d gone, how much it had changed him. Either way, I got off easy that time. He threatened to take me down to the basement, to use the Cruciatus Curse against me again, but he never did. He told me … he told me to prove myself, and that the best way I could do that was by finding you and … putting you down like a dog. Um … that’s why he was after you. He brought you to me as a test. But that was all. He would grab me, sometimes he’d hit me or- or choke me, grab my hair. There were a lot of bruises, but that was the worst of it until that night. I got off lightly, I just- I was on edge the whole time because I expected worse, and I think he enjoyed the mental torment of it.”

 

            She finally turned, her eyes hard and jaw firmly set as she met Kara’s stare. There was a haughtiness to her expression that Kara was used to, the way that Lena stifled her emotions, feigned nonchalance to cover up the pain. Kara knew what was beneath it, though. Finally moving, she stretched out her hand and took another step, her blue eyes pleading, as if worried Lena might shy away. Instead, she took two steps towards Kara and reached out for her hand.

 

            “I’m not okay,” Lena confessed, staring down at the dirt underfoot. “And part of that is because he got inside my head without a spell, and the other part is because, as I’m sure your sister told you, I don’t want things to get worse, either, but this thing isn’t right because you won’t talk to Alex, and I’m trying to keep the peace, but …”

 

            “But you’re angry at her.”

 

            “Yes,” Lena admitted with a sigh, her shoulders slumping. “And I don’t want to be, because I know why she reacted like that, but it was … so humiliating for me. And I can’t get past it. And I can’t forget how badly you were hurt, and what it felt like to think you were going to die. All I can do is pretend that I’m okay, but … none of it is okay, and I’m afraid of what will happen when it all catches up to us. What he will do to someone I love. I just- I need a distraction. I need something good to focus on, like being back with you, and your family, and drinking with my friends, and- and planning a wedding, just … something good.”

 

            “None of that will help fix things,” Kara gently reminded her. “Especially not when you keep it to yourself.”

 

            “I know. I’ll try to talk to you more, but I … I don’t want to make things worse for you, either.”

 

            Reaching up with her other hand to tenderly stroke Lena’s cheek, Kara smiled slightly. “You never could. You could only ever make things better. I want to make things better for you, too.”

 

            “You do,” Lena murmured, turning her face so she could kiss Kara’s palm. “But it really would fix things a little to marry you.”

 

            Her mouth curved into a smile, and Kara let out a quiet laugh, cocking her head to the side as she pressed her lips together, her cheeks dimpling with amusement. “Then let’s get married.”

Chapter 65

            Lena glanced over her shoulder at the sound of grass crunched underfoot, squinting her eyes slightly against the pale glare of the sky as she watched Alex approach.

 

            “Hey,” she quietly greeted her, turning her attention back to the Fluxweed seedling she was planting, patting down damp soil and then grabbing a fistful of perlite to sprinkle around the base of the seedling.

 

            “Hey,” Alex replied, standing a foot behind her left shoulder.

 

            She was wearing her beloved leather duster, surely freshly off-duty, and pulled a pack of cigarettes from her coat pocket, plucking one out and touching a flaming fingertip to the unlit tip. Puffing for a second, green smoke exhaled from her mouth, she took a step forward and sank to a crouch at Lena’s side, glancing at her.

 

            “How’re you doing?”

 

            Shrugging indifferently, Lena grabbed the trowel and dug a hole a foot away from the Fluxweed, scooping out some more soil with her gloved hands to make it deeper. There was an Asphodel seedling that had sprouted in a small pot as well, and she carefully tipped the clump of soil and roots out of the pot and gently teased the roots apart, before she started to plant that one in the ground as well. Alex waited silently for a few seconds, smoking as she studied Lena, before she softly cleared her throat and continued.

 

            “I’m sorry for telling her, but she needed to know.”

 

            “It’s alright,” Lena mumbled, smoothing soil onto the buried roots and firmly patting it down.

 

            Licking her lips, Alex drew in a quick breath. “I’m just trying to help you both. I know you said not to, but … well, you at least need to be able to talk to each other.”

 

            “Yeah.”

 

            Wincing slightly, which didn’t go unnoticed by Lena as she quickly glanced sideways and then back to her gardening, Alex held her lit cigarette between her fingers as a column of ash started to consume it, while she chewed her lip. Wind blew through the garden, rustling the leaves of the neatly tended trees, shrubs and flowers, and Lena shuffled across the grass to prune a few lower branches on a Dittany plant to help shape its growth. Remaining crouched where she was, Alex cleared her throat again.

 

            “I know Dumbledore told us not to seek our own revenge, but I’ve been looking for your brother as well.”

 

            Lena’s head whipped around as she looked at her properly, then her brow furrowing together as her mouth flattened. Staring at Alex for a moment, she swallowed thickly, wiping her muddy Dragonhide gloves on the thighs of her jeans as she felt her stomach twinge.

 

            “Why would you do that?”

 

            Alex let out a quick laugh, giving her a bewildered look. “He hurt you, he hurt my sister. I’m trying to help in a way that I actually can.”

 

            “You’re wasting your time,” Lena murmured, turning her attention back to the Dittany, her face a shade paler. “You won’t find him unless he wants to be found.”

 

            “That’s not true - we caught him and locked him up before.”

 

            “That’s because I turned him in. And he’s smart enough to have moved out of the estate by now.”

 

            “He took you with him to Death Eater meetings, didn’t you? You must have some idea where to find him. Look, I’m not saying you have to get involved, although you have more right than any of us to bring him down, but if you have information-”

 

            “I don’t,” Lena cut her off, looking her squarely in the face with a tense set to her shoulders. “He always took me by Side-along Apparition; I’m not sure where he took me half the time, and they all have Secret Keepers, so …”

 

            “If you could just get us in, you wouldn’t have to stay-”

 

            “You’re going to get people killed. I know you think you can bring him down, but it won’t just be him. You’re asking me to walk you into a death trap, and I won’t do it. I’m sorry, but I said no.”

 

            There was a beat of silence, and Alex swallowed any further argument, stubbing her forgotten cigarette out in the grass and nodding. “Okay,” she whispered.

 

            Some of the tension bled out of Lena’s shoulders, and she nodded, a serious expression on her face. “I need to focus on my relationship right now.”

 

            “Right. I just- I know I’m in the dragon’s den right now, so I just- I thought it would bring you some peace if he was put away again.”

 

            A thin smile crossed Lena’s face. “It would, but it’s just not that simple.”

 

            She paused, raising her head, and thought for a moment as she stared at the fence, where a trellis of Sopophorous Beans was growing upwards, before she turned to Alex. Shifting her weight so she could sit cross-legged on the grass, pinching the fingertips of her muddy gloves to pull them off, Lena hesitated and licked her dry lips. “If you want to help, there’s something you can do for me.”

 

            “Of course, anything,” Alex eagerly leapt at the opportunity to make amends. Lena felt a stab of guilt for taking advantage of that willingness, but she knew that Alex would help her with it regardless of any perceived debts owed.

 

            “It’s the full moon next week. She can’t go home or to my flat in case my brother’s lurking in the area. She can’t go to St. Mungo’s either, because my mum might send word to have her captured again.” Lena shrugged helplessly, a slightly panicked look on her face. “There’s nowhere to keep her safe. Could you-”

 

            “My house, of course,” Alex offered before Lena could even finish asking. “It’s always open to you both, you don’t even need to ask.”

 

            Nodding, Lena felt a knot loosen in her stomach. “Thank you,” she said with relief. “You and Kelly can’t be there, though.”

 

            Waving a hand, Alex gave her a small smile. “We’ll spend the night here; my mum will be happy.”

 

            “Thank you,” Lena repeated, relieved to have one worry off her mind.

 

            They lapsed into silence again, and she dusted her clammy palms off on her dirt jeans and suppressed a sigh at the dirt she transferred, and then gathered up her gardening tools and gloves before pausing. Giving Alex an apprehensive look, Lena pressed her lips together in grim understanding. “You’re not going to stop looking for my brother, even without my help, are you?”

 

            Alex’s expression turned sheepish. “This is what I do for a living; how could anyone expect me not to?”

 

            Wearily sighing, Lena closed her eyes and ran a hand over her face as frustration filled her. “Alex.”

 

            “It’s fine. Just … don’t tell anyone. My mum will worry, and Kelly will have a fit, and Kara … well, she’ll probably say I’m sticking my nose in again, but-”

 

            “Shouldn’t four people thinking it’s a bad idea be a deterrent for you?”

 

            “I’m an Auror. I know how to go about this safely, and I’m not going to go rogue on it. I’ll go through the proper channels, through work, so I won’t be alone. I just- I’m not a vengeful person, but this is personal, so ...”

 

            “Well, you’re an adult, so I can’t stop you,” Lena pragmatically replied, climbing to her feet with her armful of supplies. “But leave me out of it. Please.”

 

            “Sure,” Alex murmured. 

 

            Moving over to the small garden shed, Lena put away Eliza’s things and crossed the patch of grass not overtaken by flowerbeds and plant pots, and opened the back door. Alex followed her inside, and they didn’t speak of it again. Washing her hands with soap and hot water, Lena dried them and rounded the table to fetch the kettle from the stovetop.

 

            “Tea?”

 

            Glancing at her watch, Alex hesitated before nodding. “I’ve got time for a cup. Ta.”

 

            Checking in on everyone else, Lena made four cups and doled them out before settling in the living room. Alex sat beside her mother, who remained seated for a second before insisting on making an early lunch for everyone and roping in her daughter’s help. Left alone beside Kara, Lena ghosted a hand down her back and adjusted the blanket so it was across both of their knees, sharing a small smile with her, and sipped her tea. Kara was making a list in her lap, a roll of parchment laid flat against an old stack of Witch Weekly issues, and she tapped the feather of the quill against her chin as she hummed softly to herself. Lena knew what it was - the guest list to their wedding that she’d left Kara to draft up while she went outside to do some gardening.

 

            “That’s quite a long list,” Lena murmured as she craned her neck to glance at the page.

 

            “We can cull as we go. I just don’t want to forget anyone.”

 

            “Invite as many people as you’d like,” Lena insisted. “It’s your day, too.”

 

            With a quiet snort, Kara glanced up and flashed her a smile. “How many friends do you think I have?”

 

            “Judging by your list, a lot more than I do.”

 

            Clicking her tongue, Kara rolled her eyes. “I’ve already got Sam and Andrea on here. Is she still going out with Russell? I assumed he’d be coming with her. Who else should I add?”

 

            “That’s it for me.”

 

            “Two people?”

 

            “Well, three, if you’re including Russell.”

 

            “You need more than that at your wedding.”

 

            “Like who? Surely you’re not expecting my mum to get an invite.”

 

            Grimacing, Kara hesitated a moment. “Well, you can take my sister for your side.”

 

            Swatting her arm, Lena softly huffed. “Enough of that. Besides, surely she’ll be your maid of honour? I’ve already asked Sam.”

 

            Kara’s expression turned to guilt. “If you’d asked me that a month ago, it would’ve been obvious. It’s still obvious, I just-”

 

            She cut off, frustration tearing her in two, and Lena caressed her cheek and leaned in to press a gentle kiss to it. “Yes, it’s still obvious. Don’t let your rash judgment make you do something you’ll regret.”

 

            “I think I would regret it,” Kara agreed, a mournful look on her face. “But how am I supposed to just-”

 

            Cutting off again, she shook her head, mouth thinning. Chuckling, Lena reached for her cup of tea and leaned back, wrapping an arm around Kara’s shoulders as she took a sip. Her eyes slid to the open archway as Alex carried two plates in, levitating them over towards the couple. Thanking her, Lena eyed the thick slice of pork pie and pickled onions on the plate, leaning forward to set her cup back down.

 

            “Kara was just saying she has something to ask you,” Lena told Alex as Eliza walked in with the other two plates.

 

            Already taking a bite of her piece of pie, Kara inhaled to argue and choked on a few flakes of pastry, dissolving into a coughing fit as she covered her mouth, face reddening. Patting her back, both in encouragement and to help clear her airways, Lena smiled innocently as her fiancée’s blue eyes sharply cut to her face. Picking up a little pickled onion, Lena popped it in her mouth and her smile sweetened. Reaching for her tea, Kara took a swig and then cleared her throat, looking a little displeased at having her hand forced, but seeing no way out of it. She could’ve asked a completely unrelated question, of course, but Lena would just manoeuvre them into another situation where Kara’s hand was forced again. She was quite stubborn like that.

 

            “Um … we were just talking about wedding plans,” Kara hedged, shifting uncomfortably.

 

            “Oh, have you set a date?” Eliza brightly asked.

 

            “Er, no? Not yet. Um … soon. It’ll be soon, though.”

 

            “We want a summer wedding,” Lena agreed.

 

            They hadn’t decided on a particular season they wanted it in, but time was of the essence. Summer was approaching, and the weather would be marginally warmer, if not any drier, but it would be their best bet for a nice day. A day they deserved. Flowers would be in bloom, and the evenings would be longer, and Kara’s full moon transformations would be shorter as a result. There were a lot of things to look forward to in summer, and at the top of the list was them all still being alive. That wasn’t a given, especially with Lena being high on her brother’s list, no doubt, so they didn’t want to delay too long. No matter how they dressed up the decision, that would be obvious to many people. Kara had been invited to a few weddings as well, with others rushing to make the same decision as them.

 

            “That’s lovely,” Eliza replied, smiling warmly.

 

            “Your question?” Lena prompted Kara with a gentle elbow to the ribs as the conversation paused momentarily.

 

            “Oh. Um. Well … I need a maid of honour. Obviously. And you’re the obvious choice. Obviously.”

 

            “Oh,” Alex awkwardly replied, looking almost as uncomfortable as her sister, who looked pained at the stilted way she’d phrased it, but too mulish to ask again, properly. 

 

            Flushing pink, Kara finished a sip of tea as the atmosphere in the living room took on an unpleasant air, and she shifted restlessly, fiddling with her cup and the plate in her lap. With a soft sigh, she cleared her throat. “It would mean a lot to me. If you would. So …”

 

            “Of course,” Alex quickly replied. “Yes, I’d really like that. Thank you.”

 

            Nodding, Kara turned her attention to the fireplace, unusually fascinated by the empty grate as she took a bite of her pork pie. Giving her knee a reassuring squeeze, Lena returned to eating her lunch with a pleased look on her face, and a rush of respect for her fiancée, for swallowing her anger so she didn’t make a mistake she’d regret in the future.

 

            Alex left after they finished eating, and Kara was making more tea in the kitchen while Lena reemerged, having left their plates in the sink. Lingering in the hallway as she watched her sister-in-law put her boots on and grab her cloak from the hook, Lena smiled slightly as their eyes met. Shoulders going slack, Alex gave her a crooked smile as she fastened the cloak at her neck and adjusted it over her coat.

 

            “Thank you,” Alex murmured, conscious of Kara’s banging around in the kitchen as she put the kettle on the hob and rummaged through tins of tea. “For making her ask me.”

 

            “I don’t know what you’re talking about,” Lena feigned ignorance.

 

            With a quiet scoff, Alex rolled her eyes. “Still, thank you.”

 

            Giving her arm a quick squeeze, Lena nodded and stepped aside, letting her through the front door and locking up after her. When Kara joined her in the living room a few minutes later, she gave her a quick grin and received a doleful look in response, but when Kara stooped to kiss her, Lena knew she was forgiven.

 

 

            Kara knocked back the final dose of the Wolfsbane Potion, grimacing at the taste of it as she set the vial back down on the counter. Lena smiled wanly and rubbed her back, studying the pallid colour of her fiancée’s face, the dark circles beneath her eyes. Glancing at her watch, then, she figured they had a little over an hour before they needed to be at Alex’s, and she ushered Kara through to the living room as she listened to her complain.

 

            “I just wish sugar didn’t negate its effects - it would taste so much better,” Kara sighed, stepping around the cat and flopping onto the sofa.

 

            “I’m still trying to work around that,” Lena said, stepping over her feet and taking a seat beside her, pressing up close as she soaked up the presence of her before they were parted for the night. “Well, I plan to. When I have time again. I haven’t really been able to experiment since going to my mother’s; it would’ve been far too obvious why.”

 

            “Mm, well, I’m just grateful to have the potion,” Kara assured her. “No matter how bad it tastes.”

 

            “It must’ve been hard while you were away,” Lena commiserated, her mouth thinning as she was reminded of how many months Kara had been without the Wolfsbane Potion. At least she’d been in the open wilderness, free to run through forests or the hilly Highlands - it was second-best. “And I had no clue. What were you even doing with the vials I portioned out for you? They were never there when I came back to brew the next batch.”

 

            “Oh, um, I had J’onn fetch them and give them to Remus every month. Seeing as he knew about you, it didn’t seem like much of a risk,” Kara explained, looking a little sheepish.

 

            “At least it didn’t go to waste,” Lena softly sighed.

 

            Reaching out to tuck a strand behind Lena’s ear, Kara’s smile turned crooked. “I was okay. I’m sorry I kept it from you, though.”

 

            “You didn’t keep it from me. We weren’t really at liberty to tell each other things, and it hasn’t really come up. Priorities and all that.”

 

            She smiled, and Kara cupped her cheek. Turning into her touch, Lena kissed her palm, and then her eyes darted to the archway at the sound of the front door opening. Withdrawing her touch, Kara twisted her torso, and they both watched Kelly come into sight, smiling warmly at them as she unfastened the buttons of her robe with one hand, an overnight bag in the other.

 

            “Hey. We thought we’d come a bit early so you can get settled in,” she explained.

 

            “Thanks,” Kara murmured with a fleeting smile, running a hand over her face, which was already a bit clammy.

 

            The thump of Alex’s boots kicked off into the jumbled mess of shoes in the corner beside the door greeted them, and then she stepped up beside her wife, hands buried in the pockets of her jeans. “Alright?”

 

            Climbing to her feet, Kara nodded, an apprehensive look on her face as she ran her palms over her thighs. “Thanks for this.”

 

            Nodding, Alex shrugged dismissively and then took the bag from Kelly’s hand. “I’ll pop this upstairs. Lena, which bed do you sleep in?”

            

            “Oh, no, you can take both,” Lena insisted, a flicker of surprise running across her face, as if it was obvious that she wouldn’t need a bed. “I don’t sleep on full moons.”

 

            “I actually get more sleep than she does,” Kara informed them with a laugh that died in her mouth.

 

            “I’ll take the sofa,” Lena said, patting the seat cushion beside her.

 

            Accepting her decision with a nod, Alex lingered a moment, still clutching the overnight bag, and looked at her sister. “I’ve left you some blankets on the kitchen table. I wasn’t sure which room you’d want to be in, but the floor will be cold so-”

 

            “Room?” Kara interrupted, her face crumpling. “I’m not going to transform inside your house. I’ll break something.”

 

            “It can be fixed,” Kelly reassured her with a wave of her hand.

 

            “I- no, I can’t do that. This will be the first time in … a while since I’ve taken Wolfsbane, and … I don’t know, I-” She faltered, turning to look down at Lena. Her blue eyes were guilty and pleading as she nervously toyed with her fingers and lowered her voice until it was a soft murmur. “I was hoping you’d stay.”

 

            Pushing herself to her feet, Lena looked relieved as she reached out to press her hand to Kara’s back. “Of course I’ll come and stay with you.”

 

            “I know it won’t make a difference, I just- I want you close,” she quietly admitted. Then she looked back at Alex and spoke a bit louder, her voice firmer. “I’ll stay in the garden shed.”

 

            “The shed?” Alex sceptically echoed.

 

            “If that’s okay.”

 

            “Yeah, I mean, that’s fine, it’s just- well, there’s not much space, and it’s full of crap. And it’ll be bloody freezing.”

 

            “That’s okay,” Kara weakly smiled. “I’ll just curl up and sleep.”

 

            “Alright, well … the blankets. Don’t forget.”

 

            “Thank you.”

 

            Glancing down at her watch, looking a little anxious, Lena’s mouth thinned at the corners, and she looked as pale as Kara, although not as ashen. “We should probably get a move on then.”

 

            “Spare room’s made up,” Kelly stopped Lena as she ushered Kara out of the living room. “And help yourself to anything you like.”

 

            “Thanks.”

 

            “Mum! I’m off,” Kara called out, her voice taking on a rough edge.

 

            She heard the sound of footsteps upstairs and then a door being opened, and a second later, Eliza became visible at the top of the stairs. Hurriedly descending, she hugged Kara and kissed her cheek, wishing her luck and telling her to stay safe, while Kara withstood her mother’s usual fussing over the full moon. Giving her a quick smile, Kara said goodnight to everyone and towed Lena out the front door, before Apparating them to Alex and Kelly’s cottage. 

 

            Instead of going inside, they rounded the cottage and crossed the damp grass, aiming for the small wooden shed set in the back corner of the hedged-in garden. Kara paused outside it and peered through the dusty windows before she gestured to the door to open on rusting hinges, revealing the rather grim interior. It was a garden shed, after all, with a tall rack of shelves on the left holding terracotta pots and garden tools, while a few bags of dragon manure were heaped in the back corner beside a plastic bin of grass clippings and a metal rake.

 

            “Cosy,” Kara deadpanned.

 

            Clicking her tongue, Lena grimaced. “Are you sure you won’t come inside? I’ll ward the doors for you.”

 

            Shaking her head, Kara drew in a deep breath to steady herself. “No, I don’t fancy my sister’s house being blown apart if something goes wrong.”

 

            Lena knocked on the wooden exterior of the shed and gave Kara a droll smile when their eyes met.
