Still, she didn’t argue with her that it would all be fine, only tried to find a way to make the most of Kara’s situation, and her apparent anxiousness over her first transformation with Wolfsbane in nine months. 

 

            “Well, I’ll get the blankets. We can make you a small bed there, and maybe do something about the manure,” Lena suggested, delicately wrinkling her nose at the smell.

 

            She disappeared through the back door of the cottage and returned a few minutes later with an armful of blankets and quilts, while Kara was carefully leaning the bags of manure against the exterior of the shed. Making a nest of blankets on the floor, Lena eyed her handiwork with a sceptical look on her face, but didn’t try to convince Kara otherwise. Undoing the clasp of her necklace, Kara nestled the chain and pendant in her palm and then tipped it into Lena’s hand, before undoing her watch, removing her glasses and handing over her wand. Squinting slightly as everything blurred, Kara toed the heels of her shoes and stripped off her socks before shedding the rest of her clothes, each item neatly folded and piled into Lena’s waiting arms. When she was finished, Kara couldn’t see the brightness in Lena’s eyes, as if she was fighting back tears, but she could hear the thickness in her voice when she spoke.

 

            “You’ll be okay,” Lena promised. “I’ll be right inside, okay?”

 

            “I’ll see you at dawn,” Kara replied, leaning in to kiss her, her fingertips gently caressing Lena’s cheek.

 

            “I love you,” Lena whispered against her lips.

 

            “I love you, too.”

 

            Kara stepped over the threshold of the garden shed, packed earth giving way to the padding of a quilt, and gave Lena a fleeting smile. Looking pained to do it, Lena started to ease the door shut, her voice quiet in the late evening, before the door was closed and latched. “Goodnight.”

 

            The sky outside was a deep blue, a chill starting to seep in, and Kara heard the muffled sound of Lena warding the door and spelling the lock and hinges tighter. Then, against the encroaching darkness, she saw her fiancée’s hand pressed against the latticed pane of the dusty window set beside the closed wooden door. A smile curved the corners of Kara’s mouth, and she reached out to press her palm against the same spot, holding it there a moment before she backed away.

 

            She couldn’t go far in the cramped confines of the garden shed, but she found that comforting. It reminded her of those first few times in Lena’s office at the Dublin flat, and the security of being penned in was a relief after months of running wild without her mind intact. At least she’d be in control this time, would be able to curl up where she stood and rest. Even as she thought it, she could feel her skin prickling with sweat, her lower back, under her arms, the soles of her feet all damp with it as her body anticipated what came next. Moonrise wasn’t far off.

 

            Staring out the window, watching the shade of blue deepen until it was navy, Kara slowly breathed in and out as her pulse picked up, until it was so fast and loud that she could hear it thudding in her ears. Everything took on a tinny quality then, a high-pitched whine in her ears as pain stole over her, the hairs on her sweaty body standing on end as she let out a strangled gasp, hunching over as blonde hair spilt around her ashen face. 

 

            Gripping the shelf tightly, Kara ground her teeth together behind clamped lips, eyes squeezed shut as she felt the hot agony of the transformation scrape over her body, her bones starting to stretch and splinter into unnatural shapes. Dropping to her knees, Kara let out a ragged sound of pain, petering off into a whimpering sob, and she swallowed the overpowering urge to vomit as she drew in frantic gasps of air. Feeling her bones snap, her vision dimming around the edges as she momentarily blacked out, Kara fell to the pile of blankets and writhed on the ground from the blinding agony of the transformation, hair sprouting over her as her arm and leg joints bent and formed backwards, her nose and chin lengthened, and her teeth turned sharp inside her mouth.

 

            It felt endless, and she was aware of it all in the moment, thrashing about as she tried to muffle her screams in case Lena could hear them inside the cottage. Until her hands grew claws and she was shredding the blankets, and her thrashing toppled the shelving unit, terracotta pots and small garden tools falling onto her, the pain of their bruising impact not even enough to register in comparison to the suffering that eclipsed all else. Eventually, she lay spent, a panting werewolf where a human witch had been before, and Kara had the thought that it was almost worse to be aware of the pain in the moment. But, as she curled up to sleep the night away, she knew that it was far worse to not be in control of herself, to know she might hurt someone, even by accident.

 

            Her sleep wasn’t peaceful, and she twitched and occasionally yapped like a pet dog, tail thumping against the blankets as her muzzle peeled back over sharp teeth, as nightmares plagued her even then. Except, she didn’t have Lena beside her for comfort and reassurance, and when she awoke at one point with a snarling growl working up her throat, it caused a moment of panic, before she settled down again, thinking of Lena and wishing she were there.

 

            With the dawn, it all reversed. Kara roused from sleep with a gasp of pain as she writhed, a whimpering howl escaping her as bones re-broke and hair gave way to pale skin. By the time it was over, she was sweating in the pile of blankets as her chest quickly rose and fell, and the cold morning air seeped in, making her shiver slightly as the sweat cooled on her skin, making her colder. It was only a few minutes before the door was jerked open, though, and Kara forced her eyes open at the intrusion, even though she so desperately wanted to sleep.

 

            But then Lena was there, pausing a moment as she looked at the mess with surprise. She had to right the shelves first before she could even enter, the top of the entire unit propped up against the opposite wall, and then she knelt at Kara’s feet, picking up pieces of pots that had shattered against each other and setting them aside, before she surveyed the damage. It wasn’t too bad, just a dried bloody nose where a pot had struck her in the face, some bruising from knocking over the shelves, a few cuts and scrapes where she’d writhed against the broken shards of pottery, and Kara thought she must’ve bitten her tongue with her sharp teeth as well, because she could taste blood at the back of her throat.

 

            “Good morning,” Kara whispered, her mouth easing into a weak, tired smile.

 

            Lena ran her fingers through Kara’s hair as she looked over her, a delicate smile on her worried face as she gave her a minute to come around properly. She looked cold, the chilly night followed by a grey morning as pale light started to fall through the open doorway, and Kara realised that she was cold too, without her fur to keep her warm. Lena was already trying to pull a blanket out from under her to bundle her up in, and Kara made a low sound of appreciation at the back of her throat.

 

            “How do you feel?”

 

            “Better now.”

 

            “Take a minute, and then we’ll get you inside and warmed up.”

 

            “Singing daffodils,” Kara murmured. 

 

            “What?” Lena asked, her face furrowing with immediate concern as she hurriedly yanked her wand out of her pocket, lighting the tip as she held her finger above Kara’s face. “Look here. Can you follow the light?”

 

            Kara shut her eyes, wincing as she feebly moved her hand to mask the brightness. “They should be our wedding flowers. They’re the first flowers you ever gave me.”

 

            “Oh. Okay,” Lena breathlessly replied, her shoulders slumping with relief, before extinguishing the light and then smoothing the side of Kara’s face. “We’ll have … ten thousand singing daffodils. As many as you want.”

 

            Kara’s pale lips split into a smile, and her eyelids parted as she looked up at Lena. They stayed there on the floor of the garden shed for a few minutes, until Kara was willing to let Lena help her to her feet, leaning heavily on her as she stepped out of the shed, onto grass damp with morning dew. The sky was overcast, no smoke from the cottage chimney and no birds in the garden, probably scared off by the smell of a werewolf nearby, and she suppressed a shiver as she tried to cinch the blanket Lena had dragged up with her tighter around her shoulders.

 

            Inside her sister’s house, Kara heavily sank onto a dining chair, her body aching and bruised as she slumped against the table. Lena had left her pile of clothes on the table and reached for them, pulling socks over Kara’s feet, dragging sweatpants up her legs and helping her into the long-sleeved top, before she cupped Kara’s cool hands in her own, rubbing warmth back into them as she crouched before her chair. Giving her a weak smile, Kara’s eyelids shuttered.

 

            “I’m okay,” she mumbled, her chin itchy with dried blood as she reached up to rub it. “Let’s go home.”

 

            “You sit for a minute. I’ll tidy up, and then I’ll take you home.”

 

            Nodding, Kara folded her arms on the table and laid her head on top, eyes closed as she tried to dismiss the faint nausea in her empty stomach. She never ate before a full moon, having learnt over the years that it was very likely that she’d vomit, so she’d be better off not eating dinner, at the very least, but it made her weaker the next morning, hunger gnawing at her stomach. Drawing in slow, deep breaths as she waited, Kara felt the minutes drag by before Lena stepped back inside and locked the back door.

 

            Dusting off her hands as Kara’s head of tousled curls raised, Lena gave her a small smile. “All done.”

 

            Pushing herself to her feet, Kara stifled a groan and rolled her shoulders, and Lena gathered up the rest of her things. She carried Kara’s boots for her, and put away a book she’d been reading through the night, before straightening up the sofa cushions and taking Kara’s hand as she led her over the threshold, locked the front door, and Apparated them to Cornwall.

 

            The weather change was immediately palpable, the sky a pale blue, the sun shining, and the mild sea breeze almost warm compared to the chill of the Highlands, and Kara paused on the doorstep of her mother’s house, tipping her face up to the sun. Stepping over the threshold, Kara heard the sound of chatter in the kitchen and called out to them.

 

            “Mum, we’re home.”

 

            Eliza’s head poked out of the kitchen, and her eyebrows rose at the sight of Kara’s bloody face. “What happened here?” she asked, maternal worry kicking in immediately.

 

            “Knocked a shelf over. Broke a few pots,” Kara shrugged. “Bloody stupid, that’s all.”

            

            Clicking her tongue, Eliza’s mouth thinned. “I’ll get some bruise salve or-”

 

            “Don’t fuss. Lena will have it sorted in a heartbeat.”

 

            “You can count on that, Eliza,” Lena promised, deathly serious as she prodded Kara upstairs. “In the bath with you; clean up before I put the bruise salve on, or you’ll just wash it all off later.”

 

            “Yes, Healer Luthor,” Kara murmured, giving her a sideways glance of amusement.

 

            Lena’s lips twitched, and she shadowed Kara upstairs. In the bathroom, Kara turned the water on and waited until the shower was so hot that it nearly scalded her before stepping under its stream. Her skin turned a livid red, but she stood there and endured it as she scrubbed herself clean. She didn’t linger too long, though, and when she got out, she wrung as much water out of her hair as she could and then wrapped herself in a towel. Pausing to brush her teeth, Kara was grateful for the steam that hid her reflection in the mirror, and slipped out of the bathroom as it started to recede at the edges.

 

            Freshly showered, she dressed in a worn Falmouth Falcons t-shirt that she was sure was Alex’s from their late Hogwarts days, and a pair of thin flannel bottoms, feeling clean and cosy. Lena was sitting on the made bed they were now sharing, and patted the spot beside her. Obeying, Kara patiently endured her fussing, humming in acknowledgement when Lena told her that her nose wasn’t broken, had merely been bleeding from the impact of a pot, and then let her smear some bruise salve over the various points of impact, before she went in with a stinging disinfectant and some Dittany for the odd scrapes and cuts. 

 

            In a sullen mood by the time she was done, Kara just wanted to sleep, but she also felt too restless for that, and insisted on going downstairs to eat breakfast, the hole in her stomach nagging at her. Lena obliged, and she assembled sausage sandwiches from the ones left for them in the pan, while Kara sat beside her sister at the table. Kelly was finishing the last bite of her own breakfast, and Kara stifled a yawn behind her hand as she watched her eat.

 

            “You can use it next month, too,” Alex was saying, raising the dregs of her black coffee to her lips. “And the one after that. Well, all of them until you’re back home, that is.”

 

            “That could be a long time,” Kara darkly murmured. “I’ll probably tear the place apart by that point.”

 

            “It was nothing I couldn’t fix with a wave of my wand,” Lena dismissively cut in, setting a plate down in front of Kara.

 

            Mumbling her thanks, Kara felt her appetite evade her, even though she knew she was hungry. It took a few sips of tea and a few nibbles before it kicked back in, and she watched the tension bleed out of Lena, who watched her surreptitiously - although it wasn’t really, because Kara was aware of it, of how much she worried about her - and took a bigger bite. Finishing her breakfast, washing it down with tea, Kara levitated their dishes to the sink and made for the back door. She just wanted to bask in the sun for a bit, crossing the lawn and sinking to it as she closed her eyes and tipped her head back.

 

            The soft pad of footsteps followed behind her, and Lena took a seat next to her, neither of them speaking for a moment. Kara could feel Lena watching her, though, and opened her eyes a minute later, giving her a small smile as she shifted, drawing her knees to her chest and hugging them to herself. Chin propped on top, she stared back at Lena until her fiancée leaned in and kissed the tip of her nose. Smile growing a fraction, Kara closed her eyes again.

 

            “You should sleep,” Lena told her.

 

            “You should sleep. You’ve been up all night.”

 

            “I’m used to it. I don’t think I’ve gotten so much sleep since I was at school. If I’m kept away from work for too long, I’m going to become lazy.”

 

            “That’s the last thing anyone could ever accuse you of.”

 

            Humming, Lena’s eyes narrowed against the sunshine, and Kara’s face softened as she took in the changes in her expression. After a moment, Lena blinked and straightened where she sat, arching an eyebrow. “So, singing daffodils?”

 

            “If you’re happy with that.”

 

            “I’m happy if you’re happy.”

 

            Kara rolled her eyes at that and gave Lena an exasperated look. “Well, what do you want at our wedding?”

 

            Humming for a moment, Lena’s gaze drifted down to the grass, and her expression brightened as she plucked a fistful of blades and cupped them in both hands. Blowing as she opened her hands, a dozen white butterflies fluttered away, making Kara laugh. It was a genuine laugh, one that bubbled up easily and made her screw her face up, eyes creased at the corners as she uncurled from her position and fell back on her elbows. Her laughter made Lena laugh, and Kara’s smile widened at the dimples in her fiancé’s cheeks from the effort of it.

 

            “Butterflies, of course,” Lena said. “Paper ones would be more fitting - and a few cranes - but live ones are more appropriate for a wedding.”

 

            “Of course,” Kara murmured, lifting a finger and letting a butterfly land on it. She brought it closer to her face and smiled softly as she studied it, and then let it flutter off to a nearby Alihosty tree. “How could we forget butterflies?”

 

            “And what else?” Lena asked. “Ready to pick a date?”

 

            “Hm. A nice nap in the sun, first, I think.”

 

            Lena laughed as Kara sank into the grass, pulling the legs of her flannel bottoms up to catch the sun. On her knees, Lena moved towards her and loomed overhead, dark hair falling about her face, tickling Kara’s scarred cheek, before she ducked down and kissed her. “You’re terrible at wedding planning.”

 

            “I’m indecisive!” Kara argued. “And my brain’s not working today.”

 

            “Mm, well, we need to pick a date.”

 

            “We will,” Kara promised. “Now, go on, you’re going to burn if you stay out here.”

 

            Kissing her again, Lena straightened up on her knees. “So will you. Don’t stay out here too long.”

 

            “I won’t.”

 

            Appeased, Lena pushed herself to her feet and walked over to the back door, which was open to let in the mild breeze, airing out the cottage as spring crept towards summer. She stepped inside and found Eliza packaging herbs at the table, a neat pile of brown paper parcels already set to one side. She looked up as Lena walked inside, and Lena offered some lemon squash, making five glasses and levitating them to their respective recipients. Eliza thanked her, and Lena sank onto the chair across from her, reaching for an order slip and reading over the requests, before she took over weighing the herbs and parcelling them into small envelopes to be wrapped in brown paper and twine for mailing.

 

            “She laughs easier,” Eliza noted after a few minutes of silent work.

 

            “What my brother did … it’s difficult to move past, but she will. She’s strong.”

 

            “It’s not because of him. She stopped laughing so much when you left. I think she lost a piece of herself, then.”

 

            A lump caught in Lena’s throat, and she tried to wash it down with some squash and softly coughed before replying. “I think I lost more than a piece of myself then, too,” Lena quietly admitted. “I’m just starting to rediscover who I was before.”

 

            “You are who you’ve always been. None of this has changed who you are.”

 

            A pained smile flitted across Lena’s face. “I don’t know if that’s a good thing or not. I saw some … horrible things. And I didn’t stop it. If that didn’t change me, maybe I was never as good as I thought I was.”

 

            “The fact that you care proves that it’s not true. Do you think your brother cares about the things he does? Does it keep him up at night? You’re not a bad person, Lena; you’re just someone who has had bad things happen to her, and that’s a very different thing.”

 

            Eyes stinging, Lena chewed on the inside of her lip as she fiddled with a dried piece of Devil’s Snare. She was too tired for that sort of conversation, and she sat there for a moment longer, her throat tight around a lump, before she softly cleared it.

 

            “I think I might go to bed now,” she whispered, setting down the Devil’s Snare and pushing her chair back.

 

            Eliza nodded and took a sip of her squash before resuming her work alone. Stepping out of the kitchen, Lena slowed at the sight of Alex and Kelly consumed by a game of Wizard’s Chess and then continued upstairs. Pulling back the covers, she crawled into bed, and her mind went round and round in circles until she fell asleep somewhere in the midst of it, only stirring when the edge of the blanket was pulled out, and the mattress jostled slightly as Kara slid into bed beside her.

 

            Lena woke first, despite being the one who hadn’t slept - she always bore the sleepless nights of the full moon better than Kara did, even when she spent all night curled up in her wolf form - and she carefully slipped out of bed. Taking the time to shower and quietly change into clean clothes without waking Kara, Lena made her way downstairs, where Kelly was listening to the radio, while Eliza read a book. Alex was nowhere to be seen.

 

            Saying hello to them both, Lena moved through the kitchen and outside, levitating an empty basket with her and fetching the washing from the line. Back inside, she made her way to the living room and started to fold everything into neat piles for each person in the household. Eliza attempted to get up to help her, but Lena waved her back down and let herself fall into the peaceful routine of folding shirts, pants and rolling socks into pairs. She took hers and Kara’s upstairs when she was down, quietly setting them in their respective drawers, before going downstairs to make some coffee. She was adding sugar to Kelly’s coffee when the front door opened and Alex stepped inside, the silhouette of someone else behind her. Lena leaned backwards, making herself visible to them, and watched as Nia trailed the Auror inside, animatedly chatting as she shed her denim jacket, folding it over the bannister of the stairs.

 

            “Coffee?” Lena called out.

 

            “Go on then,” Alex replied, taking off her coat.

 

            “Nia?”

 

            “Milk and two sugars, please.”

 

            Fetching two more mugs, Lena spooned more coffee granules into them and poured over the just-boiled kettle of water, before adding a splash of milk and stirring a sugar in for Nia. They filed into the kitchen before Lena could bring them their cups, and Alex carried her mother’s through to the living room for her, before coming back to the kitchen.

 

            The four of them sat around the table, and Nia gave Lena a friendly smile. “I thought I’d come and see how Kara’s doing. And you. We haven’t seen you both around much since.”

 

            “I’m, ah, not sure I’m welcome, yet,” Lena said with a tight smile.

 

            “They’ll get over it,” Alex confidently assured her.

 

            Giving her a teasing glance, Lena’s cheeks shallowly dimpled. “Well, if you can, there’s hope for all.”

 

            “Well, I always liked you, I was just made not to,” Alex rolled her eyes, a faint flush creeping into her cheeks.

 

            “Except at Hogwarts,” Kara mumbled as she appeared in the doorway, rubbing her eyes. “You didn’t like her then, either.”

 

            Dropping her hands from her eyes, revealing how bruised they looked from her exhaustion, Kara smiled at her sister’s exasperated eyeroll. Her hair was mussed from sleep, and she shuffled inside, stooping to kiss Lena’s cheek and then crossed over to the stove, making a quick cup of coffee for herself and then dropping onto the empty chair at the head of the table.

 

            “How’re you feeling?” Kelly quietly asked.

 

            Shrugging indifferently, Kara’s eyes landed on the tin of biscuits sitting in the middle of the dining table, and she leaned forward to pull it closer. She popped the lid off and pulled out a shortbread that Lena had helped Eliza make a few days before. Leaving the lid off, Kara nudged the tin back towards the middle of the table and took a bite.

 

            “How’s things?” Kara asked Nia.

 

            “About the same. You know how it is with the Order. I swear there’s more gossip that goes through the place than you’d find in the Prophet.”

 

            “Mm, I’m glad I’m staying away from that for a bit.”

 

            “Are you not coming back?” Nia asked, her expression falling.

 

            Kara shifted in her seat and glanced at Lena. There was an edge of guilt to her glance, but it was unnecessary. Lena leaned forward and took a biscuit, and Nia followed her suit. “Of course we are,” Lena scoffed. “What would be the point in being members if we didn’t do our bit?”

 

            “You’ve done your bit already,” Alex darkly murmured.

 

            “There’s always more to do, I wager.”

 

            Arching an eyebrow, Alex took a sip of coffee. “Shouldn’t you be focusing on wedding planning?”

 

            “Have you set a date yet?” Nia asked, biting into a biscuit as she raised her eyebrows at them.

 

            Exchanging a glance, Kara’s hand moving to Lena’s knee beneath the table, they both gave her sheepish looks, shrugging helplessly. “We’ve been planning, and we want to do it soon - soonish - but we haven’t settled on anything yet.”

 

            Perking up, Nia smiled. “The thirtieth of June! That must be it.”

 

            Looking bewildered, Kara’s brow creased. “What?”

 

            “I’ve been having this feeling. You know how I get feelings sometimes?” Nia babbled, while the four women exchanged glances. They both personally knew that Nia’s feelings held some weight to them and weren’t to be dismissed lightly. “It’s this date.”

 

            “Go on,” Lena prompted her with sceptical amusement.

 

            She had nothing against divination and knew that Nia’s gut instincts weren’t fraudulent, and that the Department of Mysteries had once held thousands of prophecies, so it was a genuine form of magic, but she’d never put much faith in it herself. Lena had a healthy dose of respect for divination, and any sort of prophecy or ability to use the inner eye, but it had never been an area she’d spent much time studying, and her mother had derided the subject altogether.

 

            “It keeps coming up. I keep dreaming about something important happening on the thirtieth of June, but I couldn’t think of anything it could mean. It’s not anyone’s birthday, it’s not mine and Querl’s anniversary. It’s your wedding day! It has to be.”

 

            “I hope this doesn’t come out the wrong way,” Lena said with a small laugh, “but is our wedding such an important event for you to be dreaming about it?”

 

            Alex quietly snorted with laughter, and Nia spluttered, looking almost offended. “Well, yeah. You’re my friends. Why wouldn’t it be?”

 

            “Okay,” Lena easily agreed.

            

            “So … thirtieth of June?” Kara asked, arching an eyebrow as she waited for Lena’s response.

 

            Hesitating, mentally checking when the full moon was, and satisfied that ten days prior to their wedding would be sufficient time for Kara to recover, Lena nodded. Giving her a reassuring smile, she reached out to cup the back of Kara’s neck, smoothing her thumb over the notches of her spine as she tenderly gazed at her. “It’s as good a day as any.”

Chapter 66

            Eliza’s back garden was a riot of yellow as every square inch of free space was occupied by singing daffodils. The sound of them was a constant drone over the last few weeks, almost maddening but amusing as well, and they’d had to cast Muffliato on the back windows and doors to keep the noise from seeping inside, but it was a cheery sight whenever one of them stepped outside to water the growing wedding flowers. 

 

            The weeks had flown by since they’d decided on their wedding date, and invitations had been sent out. Lena visited Andrea once to inform her of the engagement at the same time, trying to gloss over her long period of absence and then dodging her friend’s questions before she made a hasty exit. Kelly’s mother had kindly agreed to let them host it at her home when Kara had wistfully sighed about how nice Alex and Kelly’s wedding had been, and how they couldn’t risk choosing anywhere public but didn’t have anywhere private and with a big enough garden to host. They’d flipped through Witch Weekly editions and mailed in orders for dress robes, receiving them in the post and standing on a footstool in the kitchen as Eliza pinned them to size and altered them. It all came together quickly, and without the planning that either of them would have liked in an ideal world, Lena willing to empty her Gringotts vault to give Kara a day that ensured she knew how much she loved her, but they were more insistent that they get married than worrying about any of the details.

 

            And then it was the night before, and both women were wedged in beside each other on the sofa in Alex’s living room with Alex, Kelly, Sam, Nia and Andrea as they’d insisted upon a small hen’s night, even if it wasn’t safe enough to pile into a booth at The Leaky Cauldron and down a few pints. As it was, they’d amassed enough wine, beer and spirits to do a good job of it themselves, the coffee table littered with empty bottles and half-drunk glasses, an ashtray piled with cigarette butts as Alex, Andrea and Nia seemed to chain-smoke them as they all laughed and told stories, mercilessly teasing the engaged couple.

 

            “No, no, tell it properly,” Andrea insisted, seemingly over her initial frostiness towards Lena and her closely guarded secrets.

 

            “That is how it happened,” Lena insisted.

 

            Taking a drag of her cigarette, icy blue smoke curling out of her mouth as she shook her head, Andrea flicked ash into the overflowing ashtray. “No, you were a stubborn cow, and a smart arse. You tried to outlast the candle by practically blistering your palm, and then you called Veronica a cunt.”

 

            “Well, she is,” Lena shrugged, taking a sip of wine.

 

            Kara let out a snort of laughter, having heard this story before, and she rolled her eyes and gave Lena an exasperated look before patting her knee. Alex chuckled and raised her eyebrows sceptically. “That’s how you found out?”

 

            “Oh, well, I’d suspected months before that. They were screaming bloody murder at each other at Russell’s aunt’s house when we went away for the weekend.”

 

            “A weekend I’d prefer not to dwell on,” Lena sheepishly winced.

 

            Cupping her chin, Kara pressed a firm kiss to her cheek and laughed, her voice low and gravelly. “You were never going to marry him. Not if I had anything to say about it.”

 

            “If I remember correctly, you did have something to say about it. You were very vocal about how stupid I was being.”

 

            “One of the few times I was right, and you were wrong.”

 

            A pillow smacked them both in their close together faces, and they jerked apart, scowling and complaining as Alex rolled her eyes. “Give it a rest. We’re going to have to put up with enough of it tomorrow. Come on, stop whispering together and finish the story.”

 

            “You already know the story,” Kara tutted with annoyance, wiping a bit of spilt beer on the thigh of her jeans and then taking a swig from the bottle she held. “Lena was freshly engaged. I kissed Lena. Lena wasn’t very happy about that. And then a few months later, she showed up at mum’s and the rest is history. Well … not quite.”

 

            “Mm, bit of a mess of things,” Kelly hummed, her eyes flitting to Andrea.

 

            “I’m going to get another bottle of wine,” Lena declared to dispel any further conversation about the period where they’d split up, just in case Andrea tried to ask any questions she couldn’t convincingly lie about just then. “Beer? Alex?”

 

            “I’ll give you a hand,” Kara offered, clapping her hands on her thighs and pushing herself to her feet, reaching out to grab Lena’s waist to steady herself as she picked her way around the coffee table.

 

            They walked out of the candlelit living room and blinked at the darkness of the hallway as they walked through to the kitchen. Eyes adjusting after a few seconds, they fumbled over to the wine rack and fridge, Kara opening the latter and letting a soft light illuminate the kitchen as she fetched a few brown bottles, while Lena plucked a bottle of elderflower and paused before laughing and picking up a bottle of Berry Ocky Rot. Showing Kara what she’d found, Lena grinned, and Kara groaned.

 

            “Are you planning on making it to the altar tomorrow?”

 

            “Don’t worry, I brewed some Hangover Cures at Sam’s. I’ll be waiting for you tomorrow with time to spare.”

 

            “Not if I beat you there,” Kara murmured, a smile in her voice as she set the beers down on the countertop and reached out to pull Lena in close.

 

            Wrapping her arms around her fiancée’s neck, Lena smiled into Kara’s shoulder as she felt her arms tighten around her waist. They were silent for a moment, swaying slightly in each other’s embrace, before Lena turned her head slightly, her face pressed into the side of Kara’s neck as she murmured into it. “Are you sure you want to risk bad luck by staying with me tonight?”

 

            Her soon-to-be wife’s hand smoothed down her hair before her embrace tightened around Lena. Her voice was a vulnerable whisper in the dimness of the kitchen, the world shrinking to the two of them as laughter drifted from the living room. “I don’t think I can bring myself to sleep apart from you.”

 

            “Good,” Lena whispered, snuggling in closer, holding onto her tighter. “Neither can I.”

 

            “Hey! Whatever you’re doing out there, cut it out,” Nia’s voice drifted out to them, and they both chuckled, slowly pulling apart.

 

            Kissing Lena quickly, Kara picked up her bottles of beer, and they both traipsed back into the living room, brandishing their offerings. There were mixed reactions to the Berry Ocky Rot, guaranteed to give them a hangover at 17% alcohol, but they all braved a small jot in their glasses, knocking it back and feeling it scorch its way down to their stomachs. To console them all, Lena fished little vials of her hangover cure out of her pockets and tossed them to each witch, keeping her own tucked inside her pocket as she poured herself a glass of elderflower wine, glancing at her watch as she settled back down on the sofa.

 

            “Is that the time? It’s already past midnight.”

 

            “Hey,” Kara murmured, a slow, smug smile spreading across her face as she stared at Lena through heavy-lidded eyes, “we’re getting married today.”

 

            Lena laughed, leaning in to steal a kiss as she grinned, a warmth spreading through her chest. It was short-lived, though, still grinning as she pulled away, squeezing Kara’s knee and then groaning as Alex insisted on another round of shots to celebrate their wedding day arriving, unstoppering the bottle of Berry Ocky Rot as they were assaulted with the astringent smell of the sweet liquor. She was making a mess of it on the cluttered coffee table when a silver streak of light shot through the room and paused, coalescing into a corporeal Patronus in the shape of a wolf.

 

            “What are you doing?” Nia snorted as she raised her eyebrows at Kara.

 

            “Me?” Kara spluttered. “That’s not mine.”

 

            “Isn’t yours a wolf?”

 

            Alex frowned as she peered at the Patronus, before she went white, shooting to her feet. “That’s a werewolf. Fuck. Fuck, fuck, fuck.”

 

            “What is it?” Kelly asked, staggering up, concern etched on her face as she snagged the bottle from Alex’s hand and tried to calm her.

 

            “Tonks.”

 

            Kelly blanched, “oh, shit.”

 

            “What?” Kara dumbly asked, completely out of the loop as she watched her sister and sister-in-law fumble for the potions Lena had given them.

 

            Lena was already slipping hers out of her pocket, cottoning on a bit faster than her fiancée as she uncapped the vial and knocked back the contents. She felt the sharpness of clarity seep through her bloodstream as the potion worked its magic, her mind clearing, her vision enhancing, and the nausea that threatened to bloom in her stomach quelled, although the cause of it wasn’t the alcohol. They’d been having such a good night, but the mood had immediately dropped, a tense edge of panic blanketing them as the old gramophone continued to play from the corner of the room.

 

            They were all on their feet, and Andrea was glancing about, watching Alex and Kelly traipse to the door and shove their feet into shoes, Nia still in the middle of knocking back her potion to follow after them, leaving Lena to deal with her friends. Kara had managed to piece it together by then, stumbling after her sister.

 

            “Alex, where?” she called after her, voice fraught with dread, but her sister was already gone. Whirling around, Kara stared at Nia. “Nia?”

 

            “Hogwarts,” Nia divulged, wand in hand as she brushed past her and made for the hallway.

 

            “What’s going on?” Sam asked as Lena’s gaze met hers. “Something’s happening at Hogwarts?”

 

            “You both need to go home. Don’t talk about this with anyone, do you hear me?” Lena said, grabbing a fistful of both of her friends' shirts and towing them to the door.

 

            “What the bloody hell is going on?” Andrea demanded, pulling herself free.

 

            “I can’t tell you. I don’t have time right now,” Lena impatiently replied.

 

            Sam was surprisingly stubborn then, where she normally would’ve trusted Lena without another word, but she blocked the doorway and remained firmly rooted inside the cottage as she gave Lena a fearful look. “You need to tell me. You need to tell me right now-”

 

            “You need to go home,” Lena cut her off, gripping her shoulders and managing to keep her composure as she met her friend’s hazel eyes with a stern look. “Trust me.”

 

            “Ruby is there,” Sam argued, her voice breaking with panic at her daughter’s name.

 

            “I’ll get her,” Lena calmly promised. “I promise. I won’t leave without her. But I need you to go home and stay there, okay?”

 

            Hesitating, Sam reluctantly nodded, and Lena felt some of the tension bleed out of her. Glancing at Andrea, she nodded and swallowed past the tightness in her throat. “I’ll explain later.”

 

            Returning her nod without a word, although there was a good amount of mistrust in Andrea’s blue eyes, she brushed past Sam and snagged her shirt, Disapparating the two of them, as if unsure that Sam would have left. Lena was grateful for that; they might be inclined to stay put if they were together, although she knew that neither woman really held any sway over the other.

 

            Alone with Kara, Lena turned, opening her mouth to ask a question she thought she already knew the answer to, but before she could get a word out, Kara confirmed it for her, taking Lena’s hand, dragging her outside and turning on her heel as the world stretched and warped and took them further east into the Highlands. They came out at the gates of Hogwarts, the night cold at the higher altitude, and it was pitch black out as they hurried down the few feet left of the path leading up from Hogsmeade and paused at the wrought iron gate as a beam of light fell across them, and Kara hastily threw up Shield Charm, her heart pounding in her chest.

 

            No hex was forthcoming, and she got a good look at the witch behind the wandlight then, letting out a relieved breath. “Emmeline. I was with Alex-”

 

            “She came this way,” Emmeline confirmed, unlocking the gate from the inside and stepping aside. “I need to hold my post, but they’ve gotten inside the castle somehow. I don’t know what-”

 

            Kara was already taking off at a run, nodding in acknowledgement of the witch’s words without letting her finish as gravel crunched underfoot, unable to be stealthy in her haste. A second later, a raven swooped past with a soft caw, and her gaze flitted up before she redoubled her effort, unwilling to let Lena go inside alone. They hadn’t had time to talk about it; they didn’t even know what they were running into, but they both knew keeping each other out of it was tantamount to pointless. At the very least, they would face it together.

 

            Sprinting across the castle grounds, a part of her worried that Lena would try to take matters into her own hands and get the deed done before Kara could get involved. Kara was sweating and had a stitch in her side by the time she reached the firmly shut front doors of the Bell Tower. Lena was already there, back in her human form as she bristled with frustration, raking a hand through her hair as she looked up at the tall, wooden doors banded with iron.

 

            “They’re locked,” Lena bitterly explained as Kara’s loud footsteps approached. “Can’t open it from the outside. None of the spells are working. I can fly up-”

 

            “I know a way,” Kara gasped, barely pausing as she skidded to a stop at Lena’s side, grabbed her hand, and towed her to the left of the Bell Tower.

 

            They didn’t speak, their footsteps pounding in tandem across the grassy stretch off the paths of the castle grounds. Kara was faster than Lena, who had never been athletic, and she had a few inches on her, too, so Lena had to drop her hand or risk tripping herself up at the relentless pace Kara set. She didn’t get too far ahead of her, though, and Lena ran on her heels, the shadow of her fiancée barely visible against the darkness of the night. It didn’t take long for Lena to realise Kara was making straight for the Herbology Greenhouses, and she didn’t bother wasting breath on questions, just kept going as quickly as possible, losing minutes to this detour, but desperately needing to get inside the castle, one way or another.

 

            Leading Lena around the greenhouses, Kara followed the edge of the Forbidden Forest until she came to a pause, sinking to a crouch and hastily brushing leaves and debris off a hidden trapdoor. Heaving the doors open, Kara dropped into the passage and hurried onwards, Lena following behind her. It was dank and cold, the way she remembered it, and she lit her wand and forged deeper, the old tunnel sloping downwards as she fought to keep her balance, but kept a brisk pace.

 

            “This comes out not far from the Hospital Wing,” Kara breathlessly explained. “I used to use it on full moons.”

 

            Lena didn’t respond as she absorbed the piece of information; she just stayed close on Kara’s heels as they went deeper underground. It felt like forever as they traversed half of the castle grounds, whilst having no clue what was happening above them. They had no information to go on, other than it was Order business, and something was afoot. Other Order members had to be there already if Tonks and Emmeline had been there, aware that something was going to happen that night, but what it was, they would have to find out once they made it inside the castle walls. 

 

            Eventually, they started to go up, the sloping passage turning into steps that wound up through the South Wing of Hogwarts. Kara’s pulse was racing as she led the way, lit wand held aloft to illuminate the spiralling staircase, hoping it was enough to keep Lena’s fear of the dark at bay, before she came to a stop at the end. The passage came out around the corner from the fourth-floor corridor, and she paused before exiting, turning to Lena, wandlight making funny shadows on her face as she gave her a fearful look, her eyes a fraction wider, her face pinched and pale. “What if he’s here?”

 

            Lena hesitated and licked her lips before her expression tightened and her shoulders squared. “I won’t let fear ruin my life.”

 

            Nodding, Kara swallowed the painful lump in her throat, hesitating as she licked her lips and then spoke. “Stay safe, please. No matter what happens, you stay alive. For me.”

 

            “I promise,” Lena whispered, reaching out to fleetingly press her fingertips to Kara’s face and then leaning in to steal the briefest of kisses.

 

            “I love you, Lena.”

 

            Their foreheads were lightly touching, and she gently bumped her nose against Kara’s, her voice barely a whisper in the confines of the tunnel as she softly replied. “I know. I love you, too.”

 

            Swallowing thickly, Kara squeezed her hand and then turned, tapping her wand against the brick wall and watching them ripple to reveal the back of a suit of armour. Politely clearing her throat, Kara piped up with a quiet, “excuse me.”

 

            Moving aside with a clatter, the suit of armour let them out of the passage, and they paused for a moment, looking both ways. The school was quiet, unnervingly so, given the circumstances, and Kara glanced at Lena. “Which way?”

 

            Pausing, considering their options, Lena’s mouth thinned at the corners. “The Grand Staircase. We’ll find our way from there.”

 

            Nodding, Kara took off, confidently leading them through corridors that Lena hadn’t walked in many years, battling the nostalgia of their school days as she passed by the closed doors of familiar classrooms and narrow archways at the top of staircases, recessed nooks where windows overlooked the grounds or courtyards below with a wide sill to sit and observe in between classes. They bypassed the entrance to the Hospital Wing and continued down the hallway leading to the Faculty Tower, where Kara’s old rooms had been when she’d taught there. She blew past them, adrenaline coursing through her now that they were inside, seeking out danger with the burning need to help, with Lena by her side this time. They’d never done this before, had never been openly on the same side, and she felt anxious in a way she never had before, trying to stamp down the fear that threatened to overwhelm her, that almost made her ask her fiancée to go back, to hide until it was over.

 

            Mouth clamped shut, swallowing her fear, Kara ran as quickly as she could until they reached the Grand Staircase, where she doused the light of her wand and plunged them into the gloom of Hogwarts at night. They paused, listening for a moment, before she heard a distant noise far below. Her eyes met Lena’s, and Lena nodded. “Down.”

 

            Without further deliberation, they hurried onwards, taking the steps two at a time as the huge column of the Grand Staircase ran round and around, taking them down through the castle’s sprawling floors. The noises didn’t get much louder, not until they reached the ground floor, stepping off the staircase and pausing on the threshold of the Reception Hall. It was silent for a mere minute before all hell broke loose.

 

            They seemingly came out of nowhere, the sudden noise of footsteps and shouts filling the gloom of the dimly lit hall, echoing off the stone floors and high ceilings, leaving both women confused about the direction. Then Kara caught a glimpse of a spell skittering off a wall and blasting apart a suit of armour around the curve of the staircase, coming from the Quad Courtyard, and she took off before Lena could tell her to stop. All she could do was follow after her, wand slippery in her clammy palm as she didn’t let Kara out of her sight.

 

            Then they were in the thick of it, a riot of red, green and silver streaking through the night as people filled the Quad Courtyard. It quickly became apparent that several of them were being pursued, and Lena identified them first, stepping past Kara and firing off a jinx before her fiancée could react. “Flipendo.”

 

            She watched as Amycus Carrow was struck in the chest and knocked backwards, earning her the attention of the other Death Eaters rushing straight towards them. Throwing up a Shield Charm, Lena dragged Kara back inside, taking two spells to the shield before it buckled, giving Kara the opportunity to strike a black-robed man with a Full Body-Bind Curse. He keeled over as Lena caught a glimpse of his face - Benjamin Lockwood. Even in the moment, she couldn’t help but feel a flicker of satisfaction at that, knowing what he’d helped do to Kara.

 

            Side by side, the two of them duelled the Death Eaters, Lena recognising more faces than she cared to admit, and they were slowly driven backwards, yielding a step with each spell, until they were fully back inside the Grand Staircase tower. Others were still spilling into the Quad Courtyard, Order members and Death Eaters alike, and as the fight progressed inside, Lena grabbed Kara’s sleeve, cast an Impediment Jinx towards the advancing group to slow them down, and dragged Kara back through to the Reception Hall.

 

            It bought them precious moments, and Kara jerked Lena down as a spell shot towards them and smashed apart the Gryffindor hourglass set against the opposite walls. Glass and rubies rained down to the flagstone floor, and the women turned around, falling back into their duelling stances as they yelled spells at their opponents. Lena was dimly aware of seeing Snape sweep through, but didn’t acknowledge him. He had his part to play, as she’d played hers, and she let him go untouched, wondering what Dumbledore had asked of him this night. More bodies trickled in, the fighting getting so messy that she could barely tell the Order members apart from the Death Eaters, so many of her own allies unknown to her at Dumbledore’s insistence. She targeted those she knew, instead, and there were enough of them at that. 

 

            There were students there, too, just a few of them, standing their ground against the Death Eaters. Lena watched a boy go down and blasted back the wizard who’d hit him, but couldn’t do much more than that to help him then. There was blood on the floor by that point, and she slipped on a patch, going down to one knee and narrowly avoiding a large chunk of stone that was blasted from the wall as Rowle set about virtually destroying the place. Coughing at the dust and then catching sight of Otis Graves, Lena pushed herself to her feet and shot a Stunning Spell at the wizard’s back, watching him collapse unconscious and get trampled on as the Death Eaters fled.

 

            Hidden by the chaos as the fighting drifted from the Reception Hall, down the marble staircase, and into the Entrance Hall, bodies and blood everywhere, half the ceiling having fallen in, and she’d lost sight of Kara somewhere in the haze of dust that lingered, but that didn’t stop her from recognising her brother. He swept through the Entrance Hall with an arrogant air of nonchalance, blasting aside a young witch, a streak of red cast from his wand a moment later as he targeted someone else, causing the hairs on Lena’s body to stand on end as she recognised it for the Cruciatus Curse.

 

            She took off after him, her hatred towards him eclipsing anything else, including sense. She’d thought she’d be frightened to see him again, after what he’d done last time and what he would do to her now, but she felt only rage. It surprised her; he’d caused her more pain than anyone else she’d ever known, and yet that pain had paled in comparison to the agony of seeing what he’d done to Kara, knowing what she’d endured at his hands and at his command. Dodging past Mercy Graves, who was locked in a duel with a pink-haired witch, staggering over a patch of rubble, Lena chased after her brother, unwilling to let this chance for her revenge slip through her fingers, Dumbledore’s orders be damned.

 

            “Lex!” Lena’s sharp shout cut through the laughter and shouts of the Death Eaters as they rushed through the Viaduct Courtyard, causing as much damage as they could in their departure.

 

            Her brother paused, turning to stare at her. His face was hard and cruel in the dark, but she could read his disdain easily, and the surprise he fought hard to mask. “Sister. Come to grovel your way back to my side?”

 

            She didn’t spare him a response as she slowly descended the steps to the courtyard, just cast a Stinging Hex and watched him deflect it. Advancing as she cast spell after spell at him, her jaw clenched, fury pounding in her head as her vision darkened at the edges, Lena stalked towards him as they duelled. He didn’t give her the satisfaction of retreating even an inch, and the gap between them shrank until they were a dozen feet apart, duelling in silent, graceful danger in the middle of the courtyard. He had the upper hand in how far he was willing to go, his cruelty boundless, but she was fuelled by her rage. For what he’d done to Kara, and for what he’d done to her for years - as a child and an adult. 

 

            Yet, neither of them could truly claim the upper hand as they continued to duel, blocking and deflecting each other’s spells and firing off their own, to no avail. Lex laughed as a few minutes passed by, other Death Eaters long gone already, fleeing through the Hogwarts grounds, a few of the remaining still duelling with other Order members around them, and a few more still exiting the Entrance Hall, trying to assist as they rushed past, before they were roughly rebuked by her brother. Not before Lena had been cut up a bit and knocked flat on her stomach from a spell in the back, but Lex had bit the heads off those who’d interfered.

 

            “Leave it! She’s mine to deal with,” he snapped at a brutish-looking man, who’d started to raise his wand at Lena.

 

            With a huff of laughter, Lena’s eyes flashed with anger. Her palms were clammy, her whole body covered in sweat as they duelled, but she just tightened her grasp on her wand and refused to back down. “Deal with?” she sneered. “You failed miserably at that last time we spoke.”

 

            “I underestimated you,” he curtly replied, his lip curling into a sneer. “I don’t intend to do it again, and you’re a one-trick Hippogriff, so you’ll hardly pull one over on me again. And I am the better dueller.”

 

            Scoffing, Lena sent a Stunning Spell rocketing towards him, and threw herself aside with an outraged look of shock on her face as a streak of green was served back at her. His audacity never ceased to surprise her, but she wouldn’t retaliate similarly; that was a line Lena would never cross. That’s what set them apart at the end of the day. Lex knew that, and he laughed, shaking his head as he deflected her next curse, burying one hand in his suit pocket as he took a lazy stance.

 

            “You’ll never beat me, you know. You’re too weak.”

 

            “That’s where you’re wrong,” Lena rasped, a Shield Charm wavering in front of her as she advanced, reducing the distance between them. “I beat you before, you just didn’t know it.”

 

            He sneered at her, letting out a bark of laughter. “Oh?”

 

            As she’d advanced, her brother had held his ground, and she was a few feet away from him now, that Shield Charm still between them. Giving him a contemptuous look, Lena’s expression was almost smug as she raised her chin and haughtily arched an eyebrow, her voice wavering slightly with her bravado. “Who do you think turned you over to the Aurors?”

 

            Whatever he’d been anticipating, it wasn’t that, and she watched his mask drop, unabashed shock rippling across his face, before his expression contorted and he tried to grab her. But her Shield Charm held, and he could do little but pound his fist against the barrier, a snarl on his face as his dark eyes hardened. He was too close to jinx her, not enough room between himself and the barrier to fire off an Unforgivable Curse, and Lena’s mouth twisted into a shrewd smile.

 

            “No response?” Lena said through bared teeth, putting all of her will into the Shield Charm, knowing it was the only thing between her and her brother’s hands around her throat. 

 

            He stared at her for a moment, a blankness crossing his face, and that unnerved her more than anything. Wand held at his side, he blinked, and his face hardened, a muscle twitching in his jaw, before he blasted the ground at their feet, causing Lena’s attention to lapse as she was thrown backwards from the impact of it. Sprawling on her back, taking the brunt of the spell, she was slower to respond than her brother, and Lex was already picking himself up, his wand trained on her, and Lena was dragged across the courtyard cobblestones until she was at her feet. Considering he’d already cast the Killing Curse at her once that night, she stared at the tip of his wand and anticipated it again, unable to get her wand up in time to stop him.

 

            “You cunt,” he quietly snarled as he loomed over her. “Crucio.”

 

            The pain was blinding, and Lena’s whole body went rigid, her eyes squeezed shut as her face rippled with her silent suffering. Her tendons were taut, and she writhed for a moment, a whimper swallowed as her mouth clamped tightly shut around any sound of pain. But it was nothing new. It was familiar, an echo of past pain, and Lena endured it as she’d endured it then. He wouldn’t break her with it, but she was helpless to stop him.

 

            Until the spell broke off, the seemingly endless pain cutting off far too soon, if her memory served her right. Blinking back dizzying black spots, Lena watched her brother stagger backwards, his hand going to his left shoulder, and a hand gripped the back of her shirt, hauling her to her knees as she panted and retched, a ragged sound of panic escaping her as she tried to get her bearings back. Wand in her hand, she shakily raised her arm to point it at her brother, but whoever had her was casting spell after spell at him, and he was forced to retreat. It took Lena a moment to realise it wasn’t because she had backup, but because there were no more Death Eaters left to fight, catching sight of Mercy Graves fleeing through the courtyard, giving Lex no other option than to go, or find himself facing whatever remained of the Order, teachers and students alone. It was obvious to her then that whatever objective the Death Eaters had had that night, it didn’t involve staying to fight.

 

            Watching her brother go, backing away with his own Shield Charm in place, cursing as he shook out his left arm and let spell after spell skitter off the barrier, Lena was hauled the rest of the way to her feet. Blinking, still in a daze, she was roughly turned, and Kelly’s face came into focus, ashen with worry as she patted Lena’s cheek. “Hey, hey, focus. You’re okay now. You’re okay.”

 

            “Thank you,” Lena mumbled through numb lips, shaking her head slightly, the muffled ringing in her ears starting to fade as she blinked and drew in a deep breath.

 

            Looking around, she took stock of the damage. Cobblestones were blasted to bits or lay unevenly, a few arches of the viaduct walkways enclosing the courtyard were broken, and people were retreating back inside, while others spilt out. Lena knew the mess was inside, along with the majority of the injured, and her eyes scanned those nearby, searching faces as she watched a handful of Order members grab students and comrades and lift them up, while teachers corralled any students unharmed back into the castle.

 

            Making herself move, Lena stumbled over her feet for a moment, her body still in shock from the blinding pain, but she regained her senses as urgency took over. Hurrying up the steps and into the Entrance Hall, Lena pushed past people, stumbling over apologies as she saw the same sort of triaging take place inside, unconscious bodies moved aside, injured people helped up, while those uninjured were already moving debris to the edges of the room. Her eyes darted about, panic growing in her chest, until she caught sight of a blonde witch weaving between people on the marble staircase. Feeling as if she might faint from the relief that swept through her, Lena let out a small cry as she rushed towards her.

 

            Kara barrelled into her, wrapping her in a tight hug, and Lena’s hands flitted about her body, forcing Kara back so she could assess her. “Are you hurt?” Lena asked, her voice breaking as she tried to see beneath the dust coating Kara’s clothes.

 

            “I’m fine, I’m fine,” Kara brokenly assured her, her smile wavering.

 

            There were a few scrapes on her cheek, a little blood at her hairline, and she winced as she shifted her weight, but otherwise she was fine. Lena felt as if she might cry, wrapping her in a hug as Kara asked her the same in return.

 

            “I’m okay,” Lena breathlessly murmured into the side of her neck, the tension bleeding out of her.

 

            “Have you seen Alex?” Kelly asked, her voice wavering as she interrupted them.

 

            Pulling away, Lena looked at her and scrambled as she thought of the last time she’d seen Alex. Truthfully, she hadn’t seen her at all. Not since her sister-in-law had walked out of the cottage before them. Cursing under her breath, Lena’s eyes ran around the room, but her panic was short-lived as she caught sight of Alex towing Tonks towards the staircase, her eyes darting around as she sought out Kelly.

 

            “There,” Lena pointed out, and Kelly took off without another word, falling upon her wife with relief and helping share the burden of the other Auror.

 

            Kara and Lena stood there for a moment, surveying the scene, and Lena cleared her throat, raking her hand through sweat-dampened hair, her eyes gritty from exhaustion as the adrenaline waned now that the fighting was over. There were many injured, and she recalled the amount of blood she’d seen as the fighting had spread through the halls. “I should help.”

 

            Snagging her arm before she could rush off, Kara gave her a haunted look, speechless for a moment before she got the words out. “Dumbledore’s dead.”

 

            Disbelief knifed through Lena, and the air rushed out of her lungs as she jerked back, a multitude of emotions crossing her face, before understanding settled in. That had been their objective tonight, that had been the purpose of this infiltration, yet it didn’t seem possible. Dumbledore had seen to the castle’s defence, more Order members there than she could count, as if he’d anticipated this very thing. For a moment, she thought Kara must’ve been mistaken.

 

            “No,” she replied, frowning. “No, surely-”

 

            “There’s a Dark Mark above the Astronomy Tower,” Kara rasped, nudging up her dusty glasses to wipe at her eyes. “J’onn said it’s true.”

 

            Lips parted in surprise, Lena shook her head slightly, not quite believing her. And yet, the castle had been breached, and her old Headmaster had been nowhere to be seen. Silent for a moment as she struggled to comprehend that, Lena cleared her throat and nodded. “Right. Well …”

 

            Grimacing, Kara leaned in and gave her a quick kiss, exhausted but brimming with restlessness. “You go. I’ll find you at the Hospital Wing. I’m going to lend a hand here.”

 

            Nodding, Lena ran a hand over her face and then leapt into action, catching sight of Querl leaning against the wall, his face green as he couldn’t control his powers. He was gripping his leg, the thigh of his jeans stained with blood, and Lena rushed over to him, breathlessly tripping over her words as she asked him what happened and reassured him that he’d be okay, not even giving him a chance to answer before she was kneeling and parting the ripped denim to take in the deep gash. It had missed his femoral artery but was bleeding a lot, and she climbed to her feet, pointing her wand at his leg and bandaging it, before she slung his arm around her shoulder and started towing him towards the marble staircase.

 

            She half-carried him all the way to the Hospital Wing, staggering a little under the dead weight of the slight man as he leaned heavily on her, until he paused and muttered a small, “oh no.” 

 

            Sagging, Querl fell unconscious, and Lena had to levitate him the rest of the way, which was an easier task than bearing his weight herself. Guiding his limp form through the corridors, she burst into the Hospital Wing and floated him over to a bed without preamble, ensuring he was securely laid out on the mattress before she turned and moved towards the supply cupboard, which had been unlocked by a swamped Madam Pomfrey. Lena didn’t ask for permission, just grabbed what she needed and carried her armful of supplies over to the bed.

 

            Vanishing the bandages, she further ripped Querl’s jeans and poured a Wound-Cleaning Potion into the deep gash, watching him come to with a shout of pain as it smoked, before she pointed her wand at him and stunned him back into unconsciousness. Lena was working on a limited timeframe, without the resources of St Mungo’s, and she didn’t have time to consider the ethics of treating patients, too focused on helping as many wounded as she could. Querl’s injury was an easy fix: Essence of Dittany and some lengthy spellwork knitting the muscle of his thigh back together, a rationed dose of a Blood-Replenishing Potion slipping past his lips and fresh bandages doing the trick. He could rest there until he came back around, but Lena was confident he would be just fine.

 

            Moving on to the next person she laid eyes on, she jerked a dislocated arm back into its shoulder joint and sent the man on his way, before her attention fell on a student whose face and neck had been ravaged. The girl was softly crying, another girl and a boy at her bedside, looking dazed and nauseated, evidently witnessing enough of the fighting to have traumatised them. Approaching, Lena softened her brusqueness, touching the girl’s chin so she could get a better look at her injuries.

 

            “Did either of you see what happened?”

 

            The boy shook his head slightly, blinking dumbly at her as his mouth opened and closed. It was the young witch who spoke, holding her friend’s hand in a white-knuckled grip as she stared vacantly at the gashes. “A man. He- he was big. He had … fangs. I don’t know. He was like a- a monster. He bit her, like he was trying to- to eat-”

 

            The girl cut off, shaking her head, and Lena looked up, pausing to stare at her for a moment. Dread turned in her stomach, and she knew exactly who the witch was describing. Fortunately, it wasn’t a full moon, but that didn’t stop Lena’s mouth from thinning as she carefully pulled aside the collar of the girl’s pyjamas to see the bite wound on her shoulder. Clearing her throat, Lena swallowed thickly.

 

            “I’ll be back in a moment.”

 

            Hurrying over to the cupboard, Lena found powdered silver and a small bowl, hurrying back over to the bed, where she’d left the Essence of Dittany she’d carried with her from Querl’s healing. Mixing the powdered silver with some of it in the small bowl, Lena used the pipette from the bottle of Dittany and carefully squeezed droplets of the mixture into the long scratch marks and the bite wound. It would scar, even though it wasn’t a full moon, but silvery scars were nothing to contracting Lycanthropy. The girl could be consoled by that.

 

            “She’ll be okay,” Lena quietly comforted her friends once she’d finished. “She just needs to sleep, okay?”

 

            “Wha-” a voice squawked, before recognition replaced indignation as Lena turned and paused.

 

            “Madam Pomfrey.”

 

            “Lena Luthor. Merlin, I’m glad to see you. Still working at St Mungo’s? Fantastic, there’s a fellow over there who’s been crushed under a pile of stone. I think his ribcage might be caved in.”

 

            Swearing under her breath, Lena followed the general direction the matron gestured in and set off quickly, weaving around people as the Hospital Wing filled up. There were groups milling about beds as Order members and students who’d been out of bed, roused by the noise, congregated there with the injured they brought in. Some were merely there for information, gossiping as they tried to uncover what had happened. Pushing through a knot gathered around a bed, Lena paused as she found herself staring at James. A second glance around the group revealed more familiar faces - Lucy, Winn, and Mike.

 

            Without waiting for the awkwardness to dispel, Lena moved over to James’ side and heard the wheezing breaths he drew in, blood at the corners of his mouth as his chest shallowly rose and fell. It was oddly shaped as well, and she thought Madam Pomfrey was right, reaching out to unclasp his robe and then tearing open his shirt to reveal the dented right side of his chest.

 

            “Winn,” Lena said, glancing over her shoulder and watching Kara’s friend blink, startling slightly as she spoke to him. “I need you to go to the supply cupboard and get me a bottle of Skele-Gro. A Wiggenweld Potion as well, if you can find any.”

 

            Turning her attention back to James, Lena levelled her wand at his chest, before she met his gaze and hesitated. “Don’t move. I’m going to vanish your broken bones and give you some Skele-Gro to regrow them. I’ve done it before; it’ll itch like mad, but you’ll be fine.”

 

            “Okay,” he weakly nodded.

 

            Nodding back at him, Lena’s expression turned stern as she started to mutter beneath her breath, concentrating hard, until a sweat broke out on her brow. Her throat felt dry and her hand wavered slightly, but she kept it up until all the little pieces of broken bones in James’ chest cavity were gone. Winn was back well before she needed the Skele-Gro, and when it was time, she measured out a dose and made James drink it all before following it with the Wiggenweld Potion Winn had found.

 

            “I don’t think your ribs punctured anything, but you’ll need to be observed for internal bleeding,” Lena informed James. “You’ll need to stay here until the rest of your ribcage regrows as well. Probably until this evening.”

 

            He was already looking slightly better, and he swallowed thickly. “Thank you.”

 

            Nodding, Lena swiped her bottle of Essence of Dittany from the nightstand and turned, locking eyes with Lucy. “Get him an Invigoration Draught in about an hour. Just to be sure he doesn’t bring up the Skele-Gro. And get yourselves some Murtlap Essence; it’ll help with the scrapes.”

 

            She gestured to their battered faces, and they nodded, mumbling their thanks. Moving on to the next person, Lena worked tirelessly through the early hours of the morning, exhaustion weighing heavily on her, the lingering shakiness of the Cruciatus Curse making her pause occasionally, eyes screwed shut as she drew in deep breaths, before forging onwards. The worst of the injuries were taken care of, with Madam Pomfrey delegating to her on them as they were brought in, recovered from the sprawling halls and corridors spanning half of the castle, and she was relieved to find that no one had died. No one except Dumbledore.

 

            Eventually, the crowd in the Hospital Wing started to disperse; those with minor injuries or recovering well were sent out, making room for more critical patients, and Lena briefly caught sight of Kara with Kelly, speaking to James as they joined the group around his bed, before they were ushered out as well. Their eyes briefly met, and Kara gave her a wan smile, dark circles beneath her eyes, before she jerked her chin to the door and walked outside, waiting for Lena to finish.

 

 

            Kara curled up on the ledge of a window just outside the Hospital Wing, arms wrapped tightly around her knees as she blinked back the stinging exhaustion in her eyes. The sun was just creeping up, and she remembered in a daze that she was supposed to be getting married later that day. It all felt surreal, most of all the fact that Dumbledore was dead. Kara held a lot of resentment towards the old man, but he’d always seemed immortal, unbeatable, the one person who frightened even Voldemort. Running a hand over her face, she let out a weary sigh and opened her eyes at the sound of someone approaching.

 

            Alex sank onto the wide windowsill and mirrored Kara’s position, a grim set to her mouth as she propped her chin on her knees, hugging her legs to her chest as she stared at her sister. Meeting her eyes, Kara swallowed thickly. “You’re alright?”

 

            “Mhm. Nothing but scrapes and bruises,” Alex murmured. “How’s Lena?”

 

            “She’s okay. No point trying to get her to stop until the last person’s taken care of.”

 

            Pausing, Alex licked her lips. “I- did she tell you?”

 

            “Tell me what?”

 

            “Kelly found her. She was duelling with her brother. He-” Alex cut off, anger bright in her eyes as a muscle jumped in her jaw. “He was using the Cruciatus Curse on her. Kelly stepped in and fought him off.”

 

            Kara’s stomach dropped, and it took her a moment to speak, her throat tight as her pulse raced. She felt as if she wasn’t getting enough air, her chest rising and falling quickly as blinding anger filled her. “I- no, I-”

 

            “She’ll be alright,” Alex softly comforted her. “Just … make sure she’s taken care of, too.”

 

            Letting go of her legs, Kara buried her face in her hands. She’d lost sight of Lena somewhere in the fighting in the Reception Hall, and it had all gone downhill from there. Everywhere she’d looked, there had been people, with chunks of the wall tripping her up, and streaks of blood as the fighting got ugly, and she didn’t know at what point she’d last seen Lena, but Kara had been hard-pressed to fight off the Death Eaters near her to even think about searching for her then. It hadn’t been until it had ended, a sudden calmness blanketing them all as they’d retreated back inside, that she’d been able to search the faces, trembling all over as she feared the worst, until she caught sight of Lena entering the castle with Kelly. She’d thought her knees might buckle beneath her at the sight of her, pale but okay. Except that she hadn’t been, and there was nothing Kara could do to take away that pain.

 

            “I have to ask,” Alex tentatively forged onwards. “Dumbledore-”

 

            “J’onn said it was Snape.”

 

            “I heard. I- that’s not what I want to know. I know you’re mad at me, and we haven’t really had time to talk about it all, um … but you never liked him much. It’s funny, because I remember you being desperate to join the Order in the first war, and you thought he was as brilliant as the rest of us, and … I can’t remember when that changed, but … it was her, wasn’t it? So, I have to ask, what did he do to her?”

 

            Lifting her head from her hands, Kara tried to find her voice as her mouth opened and closed, and she hoarsely cleared her throat, looking down at her lap as she shifted into a cross-legged position. “It’s not my place to tell you everything,” Kara quietly explained, “um, but … he used her as a spy in the first war, made her make friends with her Housemates so she could gather gossip from their parents and siblings - she did the same with her brother - and feed it back to him. He didn’t always do anything with that information. People died because of that, but … he said it was for the greater good, that You Know Who couldn’t know there was a spy. One of the times, she warned me about it before it happened, um, and I accused her of being a Death Eater. That’s why we fell out. I didn’t find out until much later that it- it wasn’t the truth at all, that he’d- I could never look at him the same. He preyed on someone vulnerable and lonely, and manipulated her into doing his bidding, and she had to pay the price for it. Um … it’s why I didn’t want to get involved again. It was never about me, about being frightened, I just- I wanted to keep her safe. She wouldn’t sit by, though, not after her brother escaped, so … she let it happen all over again. I lost all respect for him, but I never imagined he would …”

 

            Roughly exhaling as she raked a hand through her hair, Alex’s expression was grave. “Yeah. I don’t know what happens next. This is just- I don’t know.”

 

            “Things are about to get a whole lot worse, aren’t they?” Kara quietly asked.

 

            Giving her sister a grim look, Alex firmly nodded. Rubbing the bridge of her nose, Kara’s mouth twisted ruefully, and she dropped her hand, turning her head at the flicker of movement out of the corner of her eye. Lena was approaching, wiping her freshly washed hands on the dusty hem of her shirt, her eyes red with fatigue, and her shoulders slumped. Uncurling from her position, Kara hurriedly stood, reaching out for her hand, her expression softening as she gave Lena a tender, searching look.

 

            “Hey.”

 

            “I’m all done,” Lena rasped, clearing her throat, looking down at the floor.

 

            “I should get going,” Alex murmured, climbing to her feet. “I’ll see you both at mum’s.”

 

            They nodded and muttered goodbyes, and Kara looked at Lena. “Shall we get Ruby and go?”

 

            Hesitating, Lena shook her head, gently tugging Kara’s hand. “Not yet. I- there’s someplace I want to go first.”

 

            Kara let her lead her away from the Hospital Wing, walking through corridors and hallways, making for a different wing of the castle as they went down a few staircases and crossed the mess of the Quad Courtyard. She’d already figured out where Lena was leading them, what place could be so important for them to visit while they were there together, and she didn’t speak, not even to confirm what she’d guessed, as they moved through the castle as dawn crept into morning and they made their way up through the Astronomy Tower, until they reached the portrait of Hesper Starkey.

 

            Lena cleared her throat as she took in the untouched portrait with the witch peeking around the edge of the frame, and spoke the password. “Lunartickle.”

 

            The frame swung open, and they both stepped into the hidden room, cluttered with the same equipment as when they’d been at school. Both of them felt nostalgia slam into them, a sense of deja vu in the act of returning as well, and they held hands tightly as they skirted past orrery devices and telescopes, until the crowded room opened up to a clear space before an arched window and a wide windowsill. They stared at the space for so long, the silence heavy, and they both thought about how young they’d been when they’d first met there, all those years ago. Lena had been sitting at that very windowsill, red-eyed from crying, interrupted by a barefoot Kara, who was recovering from the full moon all alone. How different they were now from the girls they’d been.

 

            “So much of my dignity still haunts the walls of this room,” Lena eventually broke the silence, a halting laugh dying in her mouth as her eyes ran over the stones and beams. “I never thought I’d be inside it with you again, after everything that happened in here.”

 

            Kara stood behind her left shoulder, staring at the window.
