The window faced east, which meant the room was dim enough without the morning sunlight slanting in to let her see her faint reflection in the glass. She’d stood there once, years ago, wanting to kiss the woman she was set to marry that afternoon, but had been too afraid to do it when she’d caught sight of her scarred reflection. Now, Kara stared at her scarred reflection and was afraid again. Stepping past Lena, she crossed over to the windowsill, where countless hours had been spent during her school years, and sat on the edge of it, her knee jogging up and down as she raked a hand through her hair, ran her palm over her dirty face, blood and grit coming away, wiped on the thigh of her dirty jeans.

 

            “Kelly told Alex what happened,” Kara rasped as she looked up, her voice strangled with pain as her shoulders slumped.

 

            Lena blanched, bristling slightly as she tried to feign haughty indignation. It was ruined by the spasm of shame that crossed her face, the way her shoulders hunched slightly, and she ducked her head, letting out a choked sound of pain. “Oh.”

 

            “It’s alright,” Kara murmured, her voice wavering as she spoke, trying to coax Lena’s defences down. “You’re okay now.”

 

            Nodding, Lena’s lips were firmly pressed together, and her throat bobbed as she swallowed painfully, her eyes smarting. Sniffing, she reached up and wiped her eyes, and Kara pushed herself to her feet, cautious and agonised to keep her distance as she let Lena process it. Her own anger was stamped down, unacknowledged then as she focused on the more pressing matter of her fiancée’s wellbeing.

 

            “Come here,” Kara whispered, more of a plea than a command.

 

            And she knew Lena must’ve been more rattled than she was letting on, rocked by the pain of a curse she hadn’t felt in decades, because she went willingly, her hands by her sides as she pressed her face into Kara’s neck and let her hold her. Arms wrapping tightly around her, Kara let out a soft breath, something caving in her chest as she stroked Lena’s hair and kissed her temple.

 

            “I thought he was going to kill me,” Lena mumbled into her neck, her voice small and shaking.

 

            “I’m sorry I wasn’t there,” Kara hoarsely apologised, hating herself for not fighting harder to find Lena amongst the chaos, for not keeping a closer eye on her in the first place.

 

            Lena was silent for a moment before she confessed, “I chased him. I called him back. It was … stupid. I just saw red. I wanted to … hurt him for hurting you.”

 

            Stomach jolting, Kara winced with guilt, holding Lena a little tighter as she softly hushed her. “It’s done now. And we’re both going to be okay.”

 

            Pulling back, Lena’s eyes were wet, her face a scowl as her chin wobbled slightly, but that was all the weakness she was willing to show, and Kara knew how much restraint it had to be taking to not show more than that. If Lena was showing that much, her pain had to be immeasurable, and it cut Kara a little to not be able to comfort her properly, because Lena would never let herself be truly vulnerable again if she had anything to say about it. Not since she’d fallen apart when leaving Kara, and not when she’d gotten her back, all pretences out the window both times. It wasn’t to be repeated a third time then.

 

            Swallowing thickly, guilt flickered in Lena’s glassy green eyes as her face contorted with pained resignation. “We can’t get married today, can we?”

 

            Hesitating, Kara’s expression was bitter as she reached out to caress Lena’s cheek, an ache in her chest as she grimaced. “No.”

 

            Nodding, Lena sniffed, pressing her hand against Kara’s chest, feeling the strong beat of her heart. They’d had it all planned; they had a guest list a mile long, the singing daffodils were in Eliza’s garden, ready for the afternoon. And half of Kara’s friends were in the Hospital Wing, and Lena couldn’t make her hands stop shaking as she remembered the phantom pain of her brother’s handiwork. This wasn’t how their wedding day was going to go.

 

            Licking her lips, Kara drew in a shaky breath, eyes cast downwards as she spoke quickly. “Maybe it’s for the best.”

 

            Lena looked as if she’d been slapped, jerking away, a look of wounded disbelief flashing across her face. Then she grew angry, her voice shaking with it as she stepped back in, pointing a finger at Kara’s chest. “Don’t you dare. I won’t let you do this to me, I-”

 

            Kara caught Lena’s hand in her own, raising it to her lips and pressing a kiss to her fingers as a strangled laugh bubbled up. “Just listen. I love you, Lena. More than anything in this world. I’d do anything to be your wife, but … maybe this is how I keep you safe.”

 

            “What are you talking about?” Lena asked, her face crumpled with confusion.

 

            “I don’t know how this war looks without Dumbledore, but I know- things are only going to get worse now. I don’t know if we can win this. And if the worst happens, there’s no place for me in that world. Being what I am. But there’s a place for you. If the worst happens, you can go back, and you can survive it. Just promise me you won’t go home to-”

 

            “You stupid woman,” Lena berated her, snatching her hand back as her eyes filled with tears and she let out a breathless sob. Her cheeks reddened as she curled her hands into fists, her temper flaring up at Kara’s audacity. “You think there’s a place for me in a world without you? I would rather kill myself than go crawling back to kiss the ground before his feet. I would stick a- a knife through my heart before I begged for my brother's forgiveness, which is impossible now, because he knows what I did, that I turned him in.”

 

            “Oh,” Kara faintly murmured. “That’s why he-?”

 

            “Yes,” Lena fiercely hissed, “because I hate him, and I wanted him to know that before I killed him. That there is no world where I would stand for anything he stands for. Or any of them. I will not grovel for mercy like a coward if the worst happens; I will die beside you. And we might not be getting married today, but I will marry you, whether you like it or not. Do you hear me, Kara Danvers?”

 

            “I hear you,” Kara meekly replied, a faint smile in her voice.

 

            Still fuming, almost glaring at her for even attempting to do the noble thing, Lena leaned in and gave Kara a quick peck before she wiped her damp cheeks and gestured impatiently. “Then let’s go. And don’t you ever even suggest that again.”

Chapter 67

            Unlocking the front door of Sam’s flat with a wave of her hand, Lena stepped back and ushered Ruby inside first, before lugging the girl’s trunk in after her. At the sound of the door opening, a chair hastily scraped across the floorboards, and Lena was still shutting the door as Sam came rushing out of the kitchen and bore down on her daughter with a ragged sound of relief. The cat in Ruby’s arms twisted free as it was squashed between mother and daughter, and Lena watched it pad off and noticed Andrea poking her head out of the kitchen.

 

            “Oh, you’re okay,” Sam softly exclaimed as she held her daughter close, eyes squeezed shut for a moment, before she pulled back, smoothing Ruby’s hair out of her face as she got a good look at her. “Merlin, I’ve been worried sick.”

 

            “I’m fine,” Ruby assured her, sounding confused. Lena hadn’t told her much when she’d fetched her from the Hufflepuff dormitory before the girl had even woken up that morning. “What’s going on?”

 

            Sam’s mouth opened and closed, and her eyes flitted up to meet Lena’s. Giving her the slightest shake of her head, her mouth a grim line, Lena hovered in the hallway with Ruby’s trunk. Forcing a smile to her face, Sam patted her daughter’s arm and let out a breathless laugh.

 

            “Nothing, I’ll, uh, tell you later. How about you take your trunk to your room and unpack, okay?”

 

            Starting to object, Ruby was silenced by her mother’s quiet plea, turning to fetch her trunk from Lena, rolling her eyes as she met her eye. The corner of Lena’s mouth twitched slightly with amusement, and she handed over the trunk, patting Ruby’s shoulder, and watched her lug it to her room. Moving further into the flat, Lena stepped into the kitchen after Sam, the witch easing the door closed as she shut the three adults inside.

 

            Andrea was boiling the kettle and gave Lena a once-over. “You look awful.”

 

            A near-hysterical laugh escaped Lena, and she ran a hand over her face, her eyes dry and sore, the stress of the night catching up with her. Sinking heavily onto the chair Sam pulled out for her, Lena slumped in her seat and glanced between them both. They’d evidently had no sleep last night, enduring the hours of waiting for her return together. It would’ve been easier if they hadn’t, and Lena drew in a quick breath, cutting to the chase.

 

            “Dumbledore’s dead.”

 

            “Shut up,” Andrea exclaimed, knocking over the clean mug she’d fetched for Lena as her head whipped around to face her, eyes wide with shock.

 

            Lena hummed at the back of her throat, rubbing her eyes as she felt frustration well up within. She couldn’t make sense of it. He had been a constant for so many years, invincible in the eyes of most wizarding folk, particularly the Order. He’d been ancient since the day she’d first laid eyes on him, but even then, Dumbledore had always felt immortal. It hadn’t processed in her mind that someone so significant could have been killed in such a way.

 

            “What happened?” Sam softly asked.

 

            “Um …” Lena halted, raking her hair back, blinking owlishly. 

 

            A cup of black coffee was set down before her, and Lena thanked Andrea, who gripped the back of an empty chair, impatiently awaiting the explanation she’d been promised. She was silent for a moment, feeling the impatience of the other women, but she faltered then, caught between honesty and damage control. Sam knew enough, although Lena had stopped her from being anything more than an ally to the Order - she sent members to Sam to be patched up after skirmishes, and her flat was a safe house if needed, but that was it - but Andrea knew absolutely nothing, so completely shut out of Lena’s life for the last year and a half that even news of her engagement had come as a surprise.

 

            Looking up at Andrea, Lena gave her a weary look of resignation. “Can we talk later? I-”

 

            “We can talk now,” Andrea cut her off, a sharpness to her pale blue eyes as she stared back at her expectantly.

 

            Roughly exhaling, Lena dug the heels of her palms into her eyes, shoulders hunched slightly. “Look, I just need- I need five minutes to just … sort things out, without having to deal with telling you everything from start to finish as well. Can you just give me that? Five minutes? Please.”

 

            Her curtness was met with silence, and Andrea was still for a moment before she cleared her throat, gripping the back of the chair tightly and then letting go. “I’m going home.”

 

            Lena kept her eyes closed, although her hands were laid flat on the table top, and she softly breathed out, a stab of guilt in her chest. “Wait up for me. I’ll come and see you in a bit-”

 

            “Don’t bother.”

 

            “Wait,” Lena said, reaching out to snag her arm, staring up at her with a defeated expression on her face. “Please. I will explain, I just- it’s more complicated than that. I’ll come over once I’m done here, and … I’ll tell you everything.”

 

            Mouth pressed into a flat line, Andrea folded her arms over her shoulder and shifted from foot to foot for a second, before she sighed. “Fine.”

 

            Nodding, Lena watched her leave, and she took a sip of her hot coffee, hoping that might fortify her a little, before she met Sam’s gaze. Her friend was not so pushy as Andrea, but she could see the anticipation in her eyes and knew she wouldn’t be able to get away with glossing over what had transpired in the early hours that morning. With another sip of coffee, Lena grimaced and shook her head slightly.

 

            “What a mess,” she sighed, softly groaning as she rubbed her face. “I haven’t told Ruby anything; she was still asleep when I got her. Had to get Kara to help me into the Hufflepuff Common Room.”

 

            “Thank you for that.”

 

            Nodding, Lena fell silent, tapping a finger on the side of her mug. Shifting in her seat, she cleared her throat and squarely met Sam’s searching stare. “It was a shitshow when we got there. The castle doors were locked; I have no clue how they got inside in the first place.”

 

            “Death Eaters?” Sam quietly asked, a solemn look on her face at Lena’s nod.

 

            “I don’t know if Dumbledore was already dead then. He had the good sense to have Order members patrolling the hallways and grounds, though. Kara and I- it was just the two of us. The others beat us there. We caught up with the Death Eaters trying to run, got stuck in the middle of all the fighting, of course. You should’ve seen it - blood everywhere. One of them, Rowle - you might’ve seen him in the paper - was practically trying to bring down the place. It didn’t even last that long, really. I’m sorry to keep you waiting, but there were a good few injured during it, and Madam Pomfrey needed the help. They had Greyback with them, and he had a right show of ripping into as many people as he could.”

 

            Sam had her hand over her mouth as she listened with a growing look of dismay on her face. Falling silent after her brief explanation, Lena took another sip of coffee and cleared her throat. “It’s almost the holidays anyway, so I can’t imagine it matters now, but you shouldn’t send Ruby back to school next year.”

 

            Groaning, Sam ran a hand over her face, tipping her head back. “I don’t want to, but I don’t know what this means for her future. She’s supposed to be doing her OWLs next year.”

 

            “Better her miss out on her OWLs and have a future,” Lena darkly warned her.

 

            Sam looked surprised at her sombre warning, but hummed in agreement, taking a sip of her own coffee as she fell silent. Clearing her throat, Lena straightened in her chair, hands wrapped tightly around her mug as she pursed her lips. “Um … you might want to consider packing in work as well. Things are only going to get worse from now on.”

 

            “I can’t do that yet,” Sam sighed.

 

            “You should think about it. Seriously think about it.”

 

            “I just don’t think there’s any need yet. I’m not a target.”

 

            “My brother knows who you are, that we were friends.”

 

            “What’s that got to do with me? If your mum asks, I’ll just say I haven’t seen you. I have been saying that; she’s not the only one who asked. Half of the hospital - well, what’s left of it - asked where you were when you stopped showing up.”

 

            Mouth a grim line of dismay, Lena rubbed the bridge of her nose and didn’t meet her friend’s eyes. “He knows I turned him in.”

 

            Freezing, Sam stared at her, unblinking for a moment with fear in her hazel eyes. “And how does he know that?”

 

            “I told him.”

 

            “Why would you tell him that?” Sam asked, aghast. “Are you trying to get yourself killed?”

 

            Shrugging slightly, looking annoyed, Lena folded her arm over her chest and bit the corner of her thumb nail. “I saw him. I went after him; of course I did, I couldn’t help myself. Not after what he … did to her.” She paused, her jaw tightening with anger, and her voice was rougher as she continued. “I just- I thought I had him, for a second, and I thought … that would make his guard slip. Well, it did. But it went … awry. He ran after that, but, um … well, I don’t want to risk him trying to get to me through anyone I care about. That includes you.”

 

            “So, now I’m supposed to pack up my life and go into hiding because you had to try to take him down by yourself? I thought you weren’t going to do that. You told me you weren’t doing that, that you were just- just focusing on yourself, on getting better. After what he did to you last time.”

 

            A little surprised by her friend’s anger, Lena blinked as her mouth opened and closed. Speechless for a moment, she cleared her throat and frowned. “Well, none of this was expected, of course. Kara and I haven’t even been involved since … everything that happened. Neither of us was supposed to be involved in this, but, well, getting her to stay out of it is like expecting a poisonous toadstool to change its spots,” Lena scoffed.

 

            “You’re supposed to be getting married today,” Sam shot back, spreading her hands as she gave Lena a pointed look. “I take it that’s not happening?”

 

            “Well, no,” Lena curtly replied. “It doesn’t seem appropriate, given what’s happened.”

 

            “And now my daughter is caught up in it-”

 

            “I brought her home for you.”

 

            “Yes, to the home you’re telling me I could be targeted at because of our friendship. And your advice is to keep her here. She was supposed to be safe at Hogwarts; there was always supposed to be that comfort, having Dumbledore there.”

 

            “This is all out of my control,” Lena tried to reason. “What do you want me to do?”

 

            “I don’t know,” Sam softly exclaimed, the heels of her palms pressed to her temples, looking stressed and tired. “I should’ve been kept out of this. You shouldn’t have told me anything in the first place.”

 

            Mouth turning down slightly at the corners, Lena gave her a brooding glance. “That wouldn’t have kept you safe.”

 

            “I know. I’m not saying any of this is your fault, I just- I don’t need this stress. I’m all Ruby has. She doesn’t have a dad, or grandparents, or any aunties and uncles and-”

 

            “She has me. You know if anything happened to you, I’d look after her for you.”

 

            Letting out a laugh that was slightly hysterical, Sam smiled as she shook her head. “I know you believe that, but how does Kara feel about that? Not to mention the chances of you making it out of this if I don’t. You told him you got him locked up in Azkaban. Why the fuck would you do that, Lena? In his eyes, you’re as good as dead, and I really hope you’re smart enough to stay home and out of the way until this is all … I don’t know if it’ll ever be over. Is there even a chance of winning now? Without Dumbledore?”

 

            Chewing on the inside of her lip, Lena was silent, and a long minute stretched between them, fraught with tension. Draining the rest of her coffee, Lena slowly pushed the chair back and pushed herself to her feet, her throat scratchy as she gently cleared it.

 

            “I hope you’re wrong about all of that, and I’ll do everything in my power to make sure you are. It’s not over yet … and there’s still a chance. I’m sorry for dragging you into this. It was never my intention to endanger you or your daughter, but I’ll do my best to keep you safe as well. You have the ring; you know I’ll come, no matter what.”

 

            Shoulders slumping, Sam climbed to her feet and paused before crossing over to Lena and wrapping her in a tight hug. She didn’t notice the slight wince as fresh bruises were made aware to Lena. “I’m worried for you.”

 

            Returning the hug, Lena gave her a limp pat on the back, guilt clawing at her, and extracted herself. “I’ll be fine. He won’t lull me into a trap. Not again.”

 

            Sam’s expression was unconvinced, but she didn’t say anything, just walked Lena to the fireplace. She hadn’t taken it off the network yet, and Lena cautioned her about it as she took a pinch of Floo powder and dashed it into the grate, before she stepped in and spoke Andrea’s address and let the fireplace drag her through to her friend’s living room.

 

            Andrea was sitting in an armchair, cheek propped up on her fist as she dozed, waiting for Lena to come. Feeling a stab of regret, Lena crossed over to her and gently shook her awake. Coming to with a quiet start, Andrea slowly blinked, her face crumpled with confusion, before she looked up at Lena and startled again, clarity sharpening her stare as she raked dark hair back.

 

            “What happened?” she demanded, her voice thick with sleep.

 

            Rubbing her forehead, Lena stammered wordlessly for a moment. She realised she couldn’t give her too much information, that she’d be running the risk of dragging Andrea into trouble as well, endangering another person she cared about. And Lena had few enough of them already.

 

            “There was … a situation at the school. It wasn’t really anything to do with me; it was Alex-”

 

            “Oh, come off it,” Andrea scoffed, pushing herself to her feet. “You knew exactly what was going on. You saw that Patronus, and you put the pieces together immediately. Don’t play daft with me now.”

 

            “I-“ Lena faltered. Her mouth twisted derisively as she paced away, her heart pattering in her chest. “Look, things are getting very ugly. I don’t want you to get involved, and-“

 

            “Involved in what?”

 

            Lena turned and gestured helplessly, avoiding Andrea’s questioning gaze. “Just … everything. It’s not safe, and you’re already walking a thin line with what you’ve been publishing-“

 

            Scoffing, Andrea scowled. “It’s a newspaper; I can publish what I like.”

 

            “What the Ministry likes,” Lena corrected her.

 

            “What, and you don’t trust the Ministry?”

 

            With a huff of laughter, Lena rubbed the bridge of her nose. “The list of people I trust could be counted on my fingers.”

 

            “And I don’t make the cut?”

 

            “It’s not that, it’s just- it’s not something I should talk about so openly. It’s-“

 

            “Secret? You-“ Andrea huffed before she stiffened, shooting Lena an accusing glance. “You’re not serious?”

 

            “What?” Lena feigned ignorance.

 

            “Oh, come off it.” Lena met her frustration with a wall of silence, and Andrea angrily tossed her hair, bristling. “I’m not stupid. Yes, okay, I am only allowed to run stories the Ministry allows, but that doesn’t mean I’m unaware of things they don’t want the public to know about.”

 

            “I never said you were stupid.”

 

            “But you’re treating me like it.”

 

            “How?”

 

            “You’re a terrible liar.”

 

            “Darling, is everything- oh, Lena,” Russell sleepily mumbled as he shuffled into the room in his dressing gown, rubbing his eyes. “What the bloody hell happened to you?”

 

            “Nothing,” Lena murmured. “Late night.”

 

            He looked utterly bewildered at the sight of her, covered in dust and dirt, blood beneath her fingernails and a multitude of scrapes and bruises that weren’t all visible on her face. Andrea cleared her throat and turned, giving him a sweet smile. “Will you make us some tea, darling? Maybe a bit of brandy in them.”

 

            Russell nodded, stifling a yawn as he went to do as she’d asked. Andrea turned back around, facing Lena, and sat back in the armchair she’d fallen asleep in. Leaning back, she crossed her legs and folded her arms over her chest in a stubborn manner that Lena was all too familiar with. Lena let out an exasperated sigh as she picked up where they’d left off. 

 

            “No, I’m not.”

 

            “What?”

 

            “I’m not a terrible liar.”

 

            “Oh,” Andrea chuckled. “Right, so, you’re going to look me in the eye and tell me the Order of the Phoenix doesn’t exist?”

 

            “No, I’m not going to tell you that, and I’d be surprised if you didn’t know about it; it's been public knowledge since the last war.”

 

            Making a sound of anger at the back of her throat, Andrea pointed at her as she tried to keep her voice down. “You know what I mean.”

 

            “What?” Lena bluffed.

 

            “You’re a part of it, aren’t you? All of you are; yes, the warning was for Alex, but you wouldn’t have known what it meant if you weren’t involved.”

 

            Lena didn’t respond, standing there with her arms folded over her chest. She glanced past Andrea and watched as Russell came in with two cups of tea, stopping at the arm of the armchair and handing Andrea hers, before he levitated the other cup over to Lena. Muttering her thanks, she held it between her cold palms, staring down at the dark amber as she breathed in the whiff of brandy in the steam.

 

            “Will you give us a moment?” Andrea asked him, touching his arm, smiling slightly as he dropped a kiss on her brow and slipped back out.

 

            Taking a sip of her tea, she gave Lena a piercing stare over the rim of her cup. Trying to avoid it, Lena took a sip of her own tea, scalding as it filled her mouth. Forcing herself to swallow, she looked down at the carpet. “There are some things that aren’t mine to tell.”

 

            With a snide huff of laughter, Andrea gave her a crooked smile. “That’s a ridiculous excuse. Do you not trust me?”

            

            “It’s not about trust.”

 

            “Because from where I’m sitting, only one of us has a known Death Eater in their family.” Lena winced at that, her expression hardening. “Unless you have something you’d like to share with me? You never did take your shirt off around me, not when we were shagging, or when we lived together.”

 

            Giving her a cutting glance, insulted by the accusation, Lena’s mouth twisted with annoyance. “Don’t you dare. You know I’ve never thought that way. You don’t need to see my arm to know I’d never have his mark put on me. But maybe that should be convincing enough for you; I don’t think the Order would let someone with a known Death Eater brother join their cause.”

 

            That only incensed Andrea further, too sharp for Lena’s haughty deflections. “Oh, but I bet that’s exactly who they want, isn’t it? It all makes sense now,” Andrea bitterly laughed. “You went running straight back to your mum the second Lex was out of Azkaban. I thought you’d lost your mind, but you’re too clever for that; you were spying.”

 

            With a scornful sound, Lena’s mouth twisted, “I wasn’t spying on her.”

 

            “You weren’t spying on her, or you weren’t a spy?” Andrea latched onto her response, apprehensive as she gave Lena an appraising once-over.

 

            Raking a hand through her hair, Lena cleared her throat, shifting from foot to foot. “If you’re going to jump to conclusions, then I’m not going to stay and explain anything further.”

 

            She stepped towards the open doorway, not bluffing at all, and very much eager to make her escape. Truthfully, she hoped Andrea wouldn’t back down, just to hasten her departure without giving away too much. Lena hadn’t given her friend enough credit for her ability to ferret out details and undivulged information from between the lines; she should’ve held her position at The Daily Prophet in higher esteem.

 

            “You know, you’ve been a shit friend for the last year,” Andrea stopped her in her tracks, Lena’s spine stiffening. It was true, of course, and she didn’t deny it. Didn’t make a move. “I tried to be understanding, after you finished with Kara, but you avoided me at every opportunity. Before you came to tell me you were getting married to her, I can’t even remember the last time we spoke. And the truth is, you never really forgave me for sacking her, anyway. But I thought you’d at least have the decency to not lie to my face.”

 

            Turning slowly, Lena raised her eyebrow in a patronising manner, gesturing off-handedly. “What have I lied about?”

 

            She took another sip of her tea, trying to remain aloof, but she hated how she was acting, driving a wedge between herself and Andrea out of self-preservation. Not that there was a lot to preserve anyway; Lena had been a bad friend, out of necessity, and she knew that being honest now would only make her a bad friend in a different light. She had too many secrets, held close to her chest for years. And that wasn’t even touching on the secrets from her childhood.

 

            “You might not have been around enough to know, but Veronica was very vocal about her loyalties. Did you know I haven’t spoken to her since last June, after she had a wobbly about what was being printed in the Prophet? No, you wouldn’t, would you? She didn’t like that I was sympathising with Dumbledore, with Harry Potter. She had a lot to say about you, as well, though. And your brother.”

 

            Lena was still, her throat dry as she bit the inside of her lip, staring at Andrea. She didn’t speak, didn’t know what to say, didn’t want to implicate herself further. Instead, she let her friend keep going.

 

            “See, I didn’t believe her at first, but she insisted that you were glued to his side, which is funny, because you always used to say how you and your brother didn’t get on. And now he’s a fugitive, and you’ve just been sitting by, letting him do whatever he wants, while you live in your mum’s house again, which is just- I wouldn’t have believed that in a million years. And on top of it all, you ignored me while you were spending all this time with Veronica, of all people. You never liked her much either. So, whatever the truth of the matter is, or whatever reason you have for it, you’re a liar. You’re either lying to Kara, or you were lying to your family. Either way, you’ve definitely been lying to me.”

 

            Biting back her anger, Lena’s mouth tightened, and she shook her head slightly, a bitter look on her face. She deliberated over it for a moment, rubbing the bridge of her nose as she stared down at the floor.

 

            “Which one is it?”

 

            “My family,” Lena curtly replied.

 

            Nodding, Andrea pressed her lips into a flat line, processing it. Humming dubiously, she leaned forward and set her empty cup on the coffee table before sitting back and staring at Lena. “So, you were spying on Lex?”

 

            “This is ridiculous,” Lena breathlessly scoffed, eyebrows rising as she smiled, tipping her head back and looking up at the high ceiling.

 

            “Yes, it is a bit,” Andrea agreed, nettled. “Because I’ve been your friend for years, and it feels like you never even really cared to return the sentiment.”

 

            Waving a hand in her direction, Lena swallowed her guilt. “Well, there you have it, then.”

 

            “No. I deserve better than that. I want you to tell me the truth.”

 

            Finally looking at her, Lena’s green eyes were hard with irritation. “Tell you what? That I was spying? Fine, I was. And it cost me everything to do it, so remember that while you sit there feeling sorry for yourself because your friend didn’t respond to your letters. I was … stuck in that house … with him. And if you knew how … terrible that was for me, you wouldn’t be asking me these things.”

 

            “Well, my knowing would involve you actually having to speak to me,” Andrea tersely replied.

 

            “I could never have told you any of this,” Lena scornfully replied. “You might not have a Death Eater in the family, but you surrounded yourself with enough people to make me doubt.”

 

            On her feet, Andrea scoffed, pink-cheeked. “To make you doubt? What have I done in all the years we’ve been friends to give you any reason to doubt me?”

 

            “I’m not talking about now.”

 

            Blinking, Andrea looked taken aback, her mouth opening and closing as she paused. A look of confusion clouded her expression, and she let out a puzzled laugh, cocking her head to the side. “What-”

 

            “This isn’t the first time Dumbledore asked me to spy,” Lena softly confessed. “Um … you’re right; someone with a Death Eater in the family was exactly the sort of person he wanted to recruit for the Order. Even better if I had Slytherin friends to pass gossip to me. Everyone had someone - parents, siblings, cousins, friends. Oddly enough, you probably were the only person who didn’t, but … you were my in. By complete accident.”

 

            Andrea looked pale, hurt in her eyes as she drew in a hitching breath. “Fuck you.”

 

            “I’m sorry,” Lena shrugged, a vacant look in her eyes. “I did what I had to.”

 

            “Well, I hope it was worth it.”

 

            Blinking herself back to the moment, Lena took in the bright sheen of betrayal in Andrea’s eyes and wilted slightly. “It was. Um … people survived because of the things I found out. My brother- I was the one who turned him in. Not many people know that, uh, well, he knows now, too, so … but it was worth it for those reasons. I lost a lot, too, though. Kara didn’t speak to me for years because of the company I kept, and what she thought that meant. You were my only real friend after that.”

 

            “Oh,” Andrea quietly laughed, pained amusement flashing across her face. “Right, well, I guess I was good for filling a hole.”

 

            “Are you even listening to me?” Lena sharply demanded. “My brother knows I’m the reason he got carted off to Azkaban. Next time I run into him, I’ll likely be dead. I’m sorry that you feel used, but that’s not the truth at all. The others? Sure. I admit it. I couldn’t bear to be around them most of the time, but I endured it for the sake of the Order. But you really think after the war ended, I moved in with you to keep the pretence going?”

 

            Shaking her head, Andrea’s voice was soft as she gave Lena a dubious look. “I don’t know what to think.”

 

            Nodding, Lena drained her cup of tea and stepped forward, stooping to set it down on the coffee table. Clearing her throat as she wiped her palms on the thighs of her jeans, she grimaced. “Right, well, there’s not really anything else for me to say. You’re angry, that’s fine, I don’t expect you to feel otherwise, but I’d appreciate it if you could keep this to yourself. For obvious reasons.”

 

            Almost in a daze, still in disbelief at the truth that had been unveiled, Andrea nodded distractedly, and while she knew her friend was angry and deeply hurt, Lena knew that she meant it. Her trust wasn’t misplaced; she’d just never wanted to risk anyone else getting hurt. Still, her throat was tight as she forged onwards, unable to apologise further, unable to explain things properly, either, and she clenched her hands into fists and cleared her throat.

 

            “Uh … the wedding’s off, so … I’ll let you know when we reschedule, if you still want to come.”

 

            Andrea just stared at her, a choked laugh working its way up her throat as Lena moved towards the doorway. Cheeks stinging, throat closed around a lump, Lena didn’t look at her, but she could feel Andrea’s eyes tracking her across the room. Pausing in the doorway, Lena gripped the frame and stared at the stone floor of the hallway as she quietly spoke.

 

            “You should take yourself off the Floo network,” she gave her friend the same warning she’d given Sam.

 

            Without another word, Lena walked down the hallway and stepped out of the house. They hadn’t set up a Secret Keeper for the place, and she grimaced at their lax precautions, Andrea under the assumption that being a Pureblood witch uninvolved in the war would keep them safe. There wasn’t much Lena could do beyond warn her against doing anything further to paint a target on themselves. Lena just wished she’d give up The Daily Prophet instead of further stoking the conflict.

 

            With nothing else to do, she Apparated to Cornwall, letting herself into the cottage as she glanced down at her watch. It was only just seven o’clock, the early sunrise of the Scottish summers making it feel like the day was already so late. Already, the fighting seemed a distant memory, but she could feel her exhaustion right down to her bones as she stepped over the threshold and eased the door shut.

 

            She had a direct line of sight down the hallway and into the kitchen, and she watched Kara lean back in a chair to check who it was, hurrying to her feet at the sight of Lena. Slowly kicking off her shoes, Lena gave her fiancée a tired smile as Kara quickly approached, brimming with anxiety and relieved to have her back home. They ordinarily hated to be parted further than the length of the house, but especially then, after a night like that.

 

            “What a palaver,” Lena sighed, rubbing a hand over her face as she leaned back against the closed door. Giving Kara a morose look, her mouth turned down at the corners. “Are you cross with me as well?”

 

            Taking Lena’s hand in hers with a faint smile on her lips, Kara kissed her fingers. “No, I’m not cross.”

 

            Swallowing thickly as she nodded, a slight loosening in her shoulders, the corners of Lena’s mouth curved ever so slightly as she felt her worry diminish. Kara pressed a soft kiss to her chapped lips, and Lena melted into it, a balm to her frustration, to that hollowness inside her, wrung out by the night and the toll taken on her - physically and mentally. It always felt disconcerting after being subjected to the Cruciatus Curse, because there was nothing to show for the suffering, no lingering mark or injury, but it was evident in how utterly empty she felt, unable to describe how she felt, and nothing to do to help ease it.

 

            “You should lie down,” Kara murmured.

 

            “Let me have a bath first,” Lena demurred. “And some sugar; I feel …”

 

            Humming, Kara tenderly stroked the backs of her fingers over Lena’s cheek, disappointment in her eyes as she wryly smiled. “Well, there’s cake. It would be a shame for it to go to waste.”

 

            With a huff of laughter, Lena grimaced, reaching up to take Kara’s hand in hers. She toyed with her fingers, fiddling with the ring finger, bare of a ring for the foreseeable future, and felt dismayed. They both knew it wasn’t the right thing to do, though, that they could hardly tie the knot with the blood of injured children still beneath Lena’s fingernails. Not to mention the fact that they both looked awful, exhaustion written on their faces in the bags beneath their eyes, the weary slump of their shoulders. Their wedding day was supposed to be happy, not overshadowed by a long night of horrors.

 

            “It’ll be alright,” Kara whispered, kissing Lena’s cheek, squeezing Lena’s hand that held hers.

 

            Gently tugging her towards the stairs, Kara led her up, and Lena plodded up each step, fighting the urge to sink to them and never move again. It wasn’t the fact that she hadn’t slept that night - she did that often enough for work, even if she usually had a potion to take the edge off - but the despair that shrouded her, feeling defeated, even though she was alive. They’d lost a pivotal part of their fight against Voldemort, and while it had been out of her power to save Dumbledore, it didn’t comfort her to know that the Order was even more doomed than they’d originally thought.

 

            Inside the bathroom, Lena robotically shed her clothes, her eyes sore from dust and sleeplessness as she blinked at the bathtub, slowly filling with water, which Kara charmed to heat faster as the old pipes groaned. Lena didn’t wait for it to fill before climbing in, wincing as her aches and pains made themselves known. She had a nasty bruise on her left elbow, the joint stiff and swollen, and while the denim hadn’t worn away, she’d scraped her shin on something, unaware of it at the time as adrenaline spurred her onwards through the fighting. With a soft sigh, Lena rinsed her skin with hot water and a flannel and tried to brush out the knots in her hair with her fingers before she gave up. She didn’t have the energy to wash her hair then, barely had the energy to wash herself, letting Kara take the flannel from her hand and gently wipe dust and blood from her face. Lena gave up, settling back against the rim of the bathtub as she closed her eyes and let herself be bathed.

 

            Kara touched her cheek when she was done, and Lena quietly startled, heart lurching in her chest as the water sloshed. Looking at her with a pained expression, Kara didn’t say anything, just stood and fetched a clean towel, unfolding it as Lena pulled the plug out and stood. Wrapped in the towel, Lena wiped her face dry and looked at her fiancée through her lashes. Kara gently cupped Lena’s chin and gave her a sad smile before she opened the bathroom door.

 

            Following her onto the landing and into the bedroom, Lena shut the door and dressed in the soft pyjamas Kara fetched for her. She chose her own clothes, and Lena gratefully enveloped herself in the feeling of them, something comforting and wholly Kara in the act of donning them. It was a small thing, but she felt better for it, layering a jumper over the baggy t-shirt and tugging the hem of pilled flannel bottoms over long fuzzy socks. She wanted to crawl into bed and sleep the rest of the day away, good for nothing now that she wasn’t getting married, and Lena paused to stare at the dress robes hanging from the back of the bedroom door so they didn’t wrinkle in the cupboard. Standing in the narrow gap between the door and the foot of Kara’s bed, Lena ran her fingers over the sage green satin and grimaced.

 

            Coming up behind her, Kara wrapped her arms around Lena’s waist and kissed the back of her head. “We’ll pick a new date for you to wear it. A good day.”

 

            “How will we know which days are going to be good now?”

 

            “If I’m marrying you, it’ll be a good day.”

 

            Smiling wanly, Lena dropped her hand from the fabric and opened the door. Walking downstairs, she stepped into the kitchen and was greeted by the rest of Kara’s family. Kelly pushed her chair back, reaching out to hug her, giving her back a comforting pat. “How are you feeling? He got you good.”

 

            “Mm,” Lena hummed with disdain, pulling back and rubbing her eyes. “I’m lucky you were there. Thank you.”

 

            “Here,” Eliza murmured, stepping in.

 

            She put an arm around Lena’s shoulder as she ushered her to a chair, evidently up to date on what had transpired. She had a small teacup with something astringent in it, and Lena didn’t bother mentioning she’d just had a cup of tea with some brandy in it. It was port, Lena realised after a sip, and she knocked the rest back, the liquor fortifying as it went down easily. Her hand trembled a little as she set the cup back down, and a cup of tea took its place. Kara had stirred two sugars into it, the way she took hers, and Lena found it sickly, but welcomed the sweetness of the sugar as she swallowed a big mouthful.

 

            “Cake, anyone?” Kara asked, brandishing a knife over the small, two-tier wedding cake that Kelly and Eliza had spent the weekend making.

 

            They looked surprised at her intentions, but after a second, Kelly nodded. “Go on then, I’ll have a slice.”

 

            Five servings of the fruit cake and marzipan were laid on plates, and the five of them sat around the table, drinking their tea or coffee in between mouthfuls of cake. No one said much, either brooding or contemplating the future, and Lena finished her slice and drained her tea down to the dregs, feeling a little steadier now. Pushing her chair back from the table, she climbed to her feet with her plate and cup in hand, and kissed Kara’s cheek before she set her dirty dishes in the sink and went upstairs to bed.

 

            The room was warm, then, the day already proving to be a hot one, the sky a clear blue as she peered through the bedroom window overlooking the Muggle street below and Falmouth beyond. Shedding the jumper and the socks, feeling a little clammy, Lena lay down on top of the blankets and stared up at the ceiling. She ended up having to shed the flannel bottoms as well and got up to crack the window to let in the mild breeze, but sleep still evaded her.

 

            Kara wasn’t long to follow, and she stretched out on the opposite bed, too warm to cuddle up next to Lena in such a narrow bed. Neither of them spoke, but the sound of Kara’s quiet breaths just a few feet away was soothing enough for Lena to fall asleep first, turned on her side as she faced Kara. Still, her sleep was restless, and despite how late she’d stayed up, Lena woke at noon, sitting up in bed and staring at Kara for a minute as she plucked at the front of the t-shirt. She felt clammy and was eager for some fresh air, fetching a pair of shorts and wearing the t-shirt downstairs. Lena couldn’t remember the last time she’d worn a t-shirt around someone other than Kara, and even then, she didn’t do it often, didn’t even own her own t-shirt, but it was too hot that day and she was too tired to concern herself with hiding a scar that everyone knew was there anyway. 

 

            Padding downstairs, she didn’t find anyone in the living room or kitchen and fetched herself a glass of water, leaning back against the sink as she glanced out the window. Her attention was caught by Alex, pacing back and forth on the grass, out of her leather duster for once, shirtsleeves rolled up as she smoked. Draining her water, Lena set the empty glass down and eased open the back door, stepping out into the clear, sunny day.

 

            She squinted at the brightness, scowling as she raised an arm to shade her face, and shut the back door. Alex turned at the sound of the door opening and lowered the cigarette from her lips, icy blue smoke coming out of her mouth as she exhaled. 

 

            “It’s bloody boiling; would’ve been lovely weather for a wedding,” Alex said.

 

            Lena hummed, leaning back against the cool stone of the cottage wall, seeking what little shade she could in the slight overhang of the back door. She covered her left forearm with her right hand, looking around the garden, bare of the singing daffodils, which had already been delivered to Kelly’s mother’s house the day before, ready to be set up for the ceremony.

 

            “Where is everyone?” Lena asked, trying to distract herself from the fact that she wasn’t getting married that day.

 

            “Um … my mum went to help Kelly … tidy up.”

 

            Nodding, Lena’s mouth thinned at the corners, and she pressed her thumb firmly into the scarred words on her arm. Alex’s attention drifted to her arm, and Lena could see her thinking about it, Alex’s thoughts so easily readable on her face.

 

            “Too hot for long sleeves,” Lena murmured, choosing not to dance around it.

 

            “I remember you coming here for dinner one time. It was roasting, and you were still wearing long sleeves. Made me want to pass out, just looking at you,” Alex said with an awkward laugh.

 

            “Mm.”

 

            Lena didn’t say anything else, and Alex just smoked the rest of her cigarette and then hid the butt inside the half-smoked pack tucked in the pocket of her trousers. Then she crossed over to Lena’s side, leaning against the cool wall, partially in the shade, and glanced sideways at her. Lena just stared straight ahead, eyeing the neat garden beds and plant pots as she listened to the sound of a lawnmower drifting from one of the Muggle gardens.

 

            “How are you, Lena?” Alex quietly asked.

 

            “Fine.”

 

            It was clear from the way Alex had asked that she already had an opinion on how Lena should be feeling. It made Lena shift uncomfortably beneath her appraising gaze. The corners of her mouth twitched with annoyance, and she glanced at Alex, finding nothing but concern in her eyes. Blinking in surprise, Lena quickly looked away, clearing her throat but saying nothing.

 

            “You know,” Alex started, pulling out her cigarettes and plucking another one from the pack, turning it over in her hands as she forged onwards, “I’ve never had the Cruciatus Curse used on me before. But I’ve seen what it does to people. It was a popular spell in the first war; I remember my first week as an Auror, a Senior Auror got hit with it on a sting operation. He was a hard man, but it left him shaken. I’d never seen someone so … rattled before. Scared the shit out of me, to be honest.”

 

            “Hm.”

 

            “It’s described as an endless pain,” Alex paused, putting the cigarette between her lips and pushing off the wall, before she turned, facing Lena. Lighting the cigarette, she gave her a long stare, letting out a plume of orange smoke as she continued. “So intense that it makes people wish for death.”

 

            “Mm. Understandable.”

 

            “But you … you get hit with it, and you just … walk it off like it’s nothing.”

 

            Shrugging indifferently, Lena dug her thumbnail into her arm, avoiding Alex’s gaze. “It didn’t last long enough to hurt that much. Thanks to Kelly.”

 

            “The duration of it doesn’t matter; it’s the intention behind it. Doesn’t work well if you don’t mean it, right? You have to want to cause pain. I think your brother meant it.”

 

            “Probably,” Lena laughed, the sound flat.

 

            Alex paused, biting her lip as she tried to tactfully broach her suspicions. “You said your family did worse things to you than the quill. I think your brother’s done this to you before.”

 

            Mouth twisting with annoyance, Lena skimmed a bare foot over a paving stone of the small patio, silent for a moment as she swallowed the indignation that rose within. “Yes,” she curtly replied.

 

            Lying served her no purpose, so she was honest. It didn’t matter anyway, not when Kelly had had to step in and stop him using the spell on her. Now they all knew, and she felt ashamed that she’d let him slip past her guard and do it, so it didn’t make much difference to let herself be openly ashamed about never raising a finger to stop him in the past. Lena didn’t want anyone’s pity, but she had no use for secrets anymore.

 

            Closing her eyes, rubbing her forehead as orange smoke trailed off in wisps from between her fingers, Alex swallowed thickly. “And he did it to Kara, too, didn’t he?”

 

            That was harder for Lena to confirm, her throat so tight around her response that she let out a small sound of pain as the breath hitched in her throat, coming out as a small sob. It was all the answer Alex needed, and she quietly seethed for a moment, gritted teeth bared as she paced a few steps, her anger silently radiating from her, before she turned to Lena and nodded resolutely.

 

            “I’m going to kill him,” she promised. “One day, I’m going to kill him for you. I’ll make it right, even if it’s the last thing I do-”

 

            “You need to stop this,” Lena told her with a pained smile. “You don’t need to- to atone for anything. What’s done is done; you don’t need to earn my forgiveness or trust back. Just … stay alive. Can you do that for me? Because I don’t have many people to love, and I’d rather be mad at a living person than forgive a dead one. In fact, I’d be even angrier at you if you died for me while trying to take down my brother.”

 

            Alex let out a surprised bark of laughter and grinned at Lena. “Well, I wasn’t planning on dying. But I will make sure he doesn’t lay a finger on you again. I can promise you that much.”

Chapter 68

            July flew by, the hot summer slowly waning as news of deaths trickled in every day. It wasn’t just contained within the Wizarding World, but to the Muggles now, as well, and Kara felt dread knotting her stomach further with each passing day. She knew that part of that feeling was her concerns for Lena’s safety, and she so desperately wanted to stay outside of it all, as they had last time, but she knew they couldn’t. The Order had need of them, and they’d spent their time adjusting back to life, but now they couldn’t bring themselves to sit by anymore.

 

            Lena was perhaps more valuable to the cause than Kara, summoned late at night or roused from sleep in the early hours of the morning to heal injured members coming back from raids or stakeouts. The headquarters had been moved to the Burrow since Dumbledore had passed, no one wanting to test the security of Grimmauld Place after Snape’s betrayal, and Kara went with her on occasion, sitting on a sagging sofa as Molly Weasley plied her with tea while they watched Lena knit muscle and skin back together or wrench bones back into place. A few times, they’d helped with a stakeout, going together, Lena in her Animagus form, while Kara hid beneath the Invisibility Cloak that had made its way back into Lena’s possession. They tailed notable Ministry officials, suspected Death Eater sympathisers, reporting back what they’d seen and then going home to their beds, safely tucked away in Kara’s childhood bedroom. She feared the day their reconnaissance would lead to fighting, knowing that if there was even a sign of Lex being there, Lena’s life would be in even more danger.

 

            So far, they’d prevailed, and Kara shut herself away in the garden shed at Alex’s house on the full moon, sleeping the night away and waking the following morning to the news that Vasquez had been killed that night. Her sister told her, red-eyed at their mother’s kitchen table, tired from a sleepless night, as she hoarsely recounted the Dark Mark left over the Muggle Prime Minister’s residence, the witch standing guard over him overnight. It was another shock of reality, another reminder that their friends, their family, were in danger, and Kara’s gaze was fearful as her eyes flitted over to Lena, leaning against the kitchen counter, looking just as scared, her face pale and drawn with exhaustion and the toll this was all taking on her.

 

            They had little cause for celebration, the days growing shorter and grimmer as autumn approached, so they took advantage of what happiness they could. It found them both at the Burrow on the first day of August, wearing dress robes as they sat towards the back amidst a crowd of witches and wizards - a great deal of them with red hair - as they attended the wedding of Bill Weasley and Fleur Delacour. Kara had spent a decent amount of time with Bill Weasley, enough to warrant a wedding invite as an active Order member, and Lena had helped seal up the wounds of his face after Fenrir Greyback had clawed it that night at Hogwarts, and she sat beside Kara, although she didn’t know the wizard beyond that.

 

            Sitting there, Kara couldn’t help but feel a pang of jealousy. She envied the couple standing before them all, the officiant presiding over the ceremony as it went off without a hitch. Kara wanted that for herself, should’ve already had that if things had gone to plan, but it rarely did where she and Lena were concerned. Things always had to be as difficult as possible for them. Still, there was nothing stopping them from setting a new date, except the despairing state of things, which they didn’t want to overshadow a day that was supposed to be so full of joy. Watching the ceremony proceed in front of her, Kara was starting to think they just had to pick a day and make the most of it. 

 

            It didn’t matter that a few days ago, Mad-Eye Moody had been killed bringing Harry Potter to the Burrow; their wedding had still gone ahead, despite the pall cast over the pre-celebrations. Kara had almost volunteered to help with that mission, a very good flier, essential for an aerial battle, but she knew that Lena wasn’t, had barely flown a broomstick at all, and there had been enough volunteers anyway; even Alex hadn’t been involved in it, taking over Kingsley Shacklebolt’s guard of the Prime Minister while he assisted with the mission. Lena had been roused from her bed later that night, though, helping treat a severed ear of one of the Weasley twins - Kara couldn’t tell them apart - and had enquired about her brother’s presence there. He’d been there, of course, and survived it, naturally. Kara wished she’d gone, just to blast him off his broomstick and let him fall to his death.

 

            Lena’s hand on her knee, squeezing slightly, brought her back to the moment, blinking as she glanced at her fiancée. She’d been brooding, a stern look on her face as she stared unseeingly ahead, and she gave Lena a thin smile, covering her hand with her own. The newlywed couple were kissing then, though, and everyone was clapping, standing to shower them with sparks as they walked back down the aisle. 

 

            There were congratulations after that, and the marquee rearranged itself into round dining tables and space for a dancefloor. There were speeches, and they ate and drank and watched them cut the cake, sitting at a table with Alex and all of their friends. It was a good night, dusk blanketing the orchard, and Kara was enjoying herself, enjoying the way her friends had made their peace with Lena, accepting the truth without further suspicion after what had happened that night at Hogwarts. James was whole and healthy, and he’d been genuinely grateful to Lena when he’d thanked her earlier that evening. Not that she’d needed to prove herself, but the goodwill her healing had earned her had eased a few of the strained relationships around the table, and even Mike was less of a prick than usual.

 

            When the string quartet started playing lively tunes, Kelly whisked her brother off to the dancefloor, Alex somewhere outside the marquee as she smoked with J’onn, Tonks and Nia, and Querl went to fetch another round of drinks, although Kara was still finishing off her fourth glass of wine and Lena still had half a glass of a red, her dark lipstick smudge on the rim of it. Feeling a warm glow in her chest, a pleasant sensation after so much worrying, Kara let her fingers glide down the length of Lena’s arm, the smooth silk of the fitted burgundy dress robes soft beneath her fingertips. Reaching for her glass of wine, Kara knocked the rest of it back and then climbed to her feet, stooping to speak softly to her, her voice a low hum over the music as her lips brushed Lena’s ear.

 

            “Dance with me.”

 

            “You know I don’t dance.”

 

            “You made an exception at the last wedding we attended.”

 

            With an eyeroll, Lena took another sip of wine as she considered it, before setting her glass down and putting her hand in Kara’s. “Go on then.”

 

            Grinning, Kara pulled her to her feet and towed her between the round tables, to the fringes of the dancefloor, where they wouldn’t be in full view of the entire marquee. So much of their relationship had existed on the fringes of things, and it was familiar to them, comforting to be allowed to exist in their own world. Hand on Lena’s waist, Kara leaned in and kissed her chastely, before she fell in with the rhythm of the music, Lena’s hand in hers, standing close together as they danced. 

 

            Other guests danced too, along with the happy couple, occupying the middle of the dancefloor as people kept toasting them and applauding, birds swooping overhead and showers of sparks raining down. It was bittersweet for Kara as she caught sight of them, dressed in their finery, glowing with happiness. Lena didn’t say anything, reading the envy on Kara’s face without having to turn and see what had brought it on; she’d read it on her face earlier, too, during the ceremony.

 

            “This should’ve been us,” Kara said through gritted teeth, resentment building in her chest as they slowly turned.

 

            She couldn’t help it, attending someone else’s wedding, surrounded by people celebrating another couple’s happiness. And she and Lena had suffered so much, endured so many hardships together, and none of it had warranted even just one day for them to be happy, to bind themselves to each other fully. Kara had never been one to complain about the fairness of life, having learnt that lesson at a very young age, but she felt the unfairness then.

 

            “It will be,” Lena murmured, pressing a kiss to her cheek as her hand tightened on Kara’s shoulder.

 

            “I know, I’m just-” Pressing her closer, Kara buried her face in Lena’s hair, feeling frustrated.

 

            With a soft exhale, Lena pulled back, giving her a searching look. “If I asked you to marry me, would you?”

 

            Kara reached up and lifted Lena’s left hand off her shoulder, turning it so the small diamonds surrounding the moonstone caught the floating candlelight, winking as they both looked at it. “Considering I’ve already asked you, surely you know the answer,” Kara replied, voice flush with amusement.

 

            “I mean, do we need … this?” She let go of Kara’s shoulder to gesture to the marquee.

 

            “I want you to have it. I want you to have a day filled with so much love and happiness that you never forget how you felt on that day.”

 

            “I just want you. And your name,” Lena awkwardly laughed.

 

            Kara paused, bringing them to a halt on the edge of the dancefloor as she gave Lena a surprised look. “Oh.”

 

            Lena gave her a wry smile. “Lena Danvers has a nice ring to it, don’t you think?”

 

            “Healer Lena Danvers,” Kara corrected her.

 

            “Right, of course. Much better than Healer Lena Luthor.”

 

            Picking up on the beat of the music again, Kara swayed them back into motion. “You’re not your family’s name.”

 

            “Well, we both know that’s not true. Not just for me; half the people here are automatically respected because of their family’s name. I’d like to know what it’s like to not have to live with the stain of other people’s actions on me, for them to not have these … preconceived notions about me.”

 

            “I love your name,” Kara whispered, both hands on Lena’s waist now, as Lena’s arms came around her neck.

 

            “You wouldn’t love it if I changed it to yours?”

 

            With a small laugh, slightly breathless with amusement, Kara held her closer. “It wasn’t mine. It’s not the last name I had when I was little. It’s the last name that gave me a family who accepted me for who I was, though, when my mom didn’t. I think … I understand what it’s like, to a degree. Mine wasn’t about the name, but about the family that came with it, which you can understand better than anyone. And I know that the family I have now has room for one more.”

 

            A slow smile spread across Lena’s face, a little vulnerable but pleased, and Kara stopped to kiss her, her hands sliding across Lena’s back, until she was holding her in a tight embrace. Kissing her back, Lena cupped the back of Kara’s neck and was slightly breathless when she pulled back, a light flush in her cheeks.

 

            “So … was that a yes to getting married without a big ceremony or …?”

 

            With a chuckle, Kara brushed the tip of her nose against Lena’s. “I’ll-”

 

            They were interrupted then, everyone on the dancefloor freezing at the sight of a silver Patronus arriving in the form of a cat. It started to speak, and Kara couldn’t hear it at first, straying a little closer as the string quartet cut off with a jarring jumble of notes, silence radiating from the dancefloor as other wedding guests started to realise what was happening, drawing in closer to hear for themselves.

 

            “The Ministry has fallen. Scrimgeour is dead. They are coming.”

 

            The silver cat vanished then, and a scream cut through the silence, jolting Kara back to herself as she sharply turned her head to Lena. Panic spread quickly, and while she was still processing the information, Kara watched as black-robed figures started Apparating into the crowd of wedding guests. The protective barrier warding the Burrow had failed, and Kara felt her stomach lurch. Without a word, she grabbed Lena’s hand and Disapparated.

 

            In her haste, she’d only set them down a few miles away from the Burrow, her mind focused on safety instead of home, and she staggered through the grass at the top of Stoatshead Hill. The glow of lights in the nearby Muggle village was visible to the north-east, but otherwise it was dark and windy, the sky speckled with stars as Kara let go of Lena’s hand, her fiancée’s expression stunned from the sudden change in her surroundings.

 

            “What-” Lena spluttered, taken aback as she looked at Kara. “What are you doing?”

 

            “There were Death Eaters-”

 

            “We have to go back,” Lena cut her off, taking a step forward as if she were going to march the whole way back to the Burrow.

 

            Kara was seized with panic, cutting Lena off and wrapping her arms tightly around her. Struggling, Lena let out a few indignant sounds of disbelief, and Kara held her tightly around the waist, jaw clenched as she tried to reason with her.

 

            “No, no, we can’t-”

 

            “They need help.”

 

            “I can’t let you,” Kara insisted, fighting to keep her arms around Lena. “What if he’s there?”

 

            “Let me go,” Lena hoarsely commanded her as she stiffened in her embrace, and Kara’s grasp immediately went slack, letting go of her as she stepped back.

 

            Rounding on her, Lena’s face was pale with outraged disbelief, and hard, too, an edge of anger to her stare as Kara meekly met her eyes. They stared at each other for a second, a strange tension between them that hadn’t been felt for years, and Kara opened and closed her mouth, ducking her head as she rubbed her brow, cursing herself for her insatiable need to keep Lena safe. It wasn’t normal, the lengths she would go to, even to the detriment of their relationship, but she couldn’t willingly let her put herself in harm’s way.

 

            “I’m sorry,” she apologised, her voice small and agonised.

 

            She looked up and saw the decision in Lena’s eyes a moment before she spoke. “So am I.”

 

            Lips parting, eyes widening, Kara watched her start to turn on her heel and lunged forward, grabbing her arm right as Lena tried to Apparate back to the Burrow. Except Kara fought against it, determined to keep Lena out of her brother’s way, so afraid of him killing her that she would’ve rathered her fiancée hate her for the rest of time and be alive than risk her life for a second. But Lena had gotten the jump on her, and Kara was towed along, despite her best efforts to stop them from Apparating away from the hill, and in the act, she Splinched herself.

 

            Lena’s focus hadn’t been quite so accurate, and she brought them down too far away from the fighting to throw them straight into it, but close enough to hear the shouts and screams. Staggering as she found solid ground under her feet, Kara stumbled, a ragged scream escaping her, too, as she felt agony tear through her body. They were near the edge of the corn field adjacent to the orchard behind the Burrow, the stalks taller than they were, hiding them from sight, and Kara staggered, her vision dimming at the edges as she reached for something solid to brace herself against and pitched into the corn. Hands caught her, straightening her back up, and Kara choked on a breathless gasp and let out a frayed sound as she felt a wet warmth seeping into her pink dress robes.

 

            Ashen-faced and sweating, feeling as if she might vomit, or perhaps even faint, Kara swayed unsteadily on her feet as she was turned around, blinking at Lena with a stunned look on her face. Lena was pale, eyes wide with shock, and her eyes ran over Kara’s body, a small whimper escaping her as she stared at the large bloodstain spreading across her abdomen. Clumsily reaching, Kara pressed her palm to the wetness, so much pain in her stomach that even that light pressure made everything go black for a moment, white-hot pain shooting through her, and she gritted her teeth as she let out another ragged bellow.

 

            “I’m sorry, I’m sorry,” Lena breathlessly repeated as she lowered Kara to the ground between the rows of corn, stretching her out on her back as Kara’s face rippled with agony. “I’m sorry, let me look. Please let me- I’m sorry, I-”

 

            Kara’s chest heaved, her breath short and frantic and loud, each one a panicked pant. She was aware of Lena ripping the seams of the dress robe to expose where she’d been Splinched, hands badly shaking as she tore satin and lace. The Healer paused at the sight of what was beneath the robe, swallowing thickly, and Kara stared at her in a daze, mouth opening and closing, but unable to make a sound. She couldn’t even ask how bad it was, choking on a whimper as the night breeze assaulted the open wounds.

 

            It wasn’t just one, it was a series of open gashes, deep gashes, spreading from her right hip, across the stomach and ribcage. It was similar to how her abdomen had looked that one time Lena had treated Kara after a full moon, when she’d practically ripped herself apart while miscarrying. Muscles parted, leaving gaping chunks, and where it carved open her ribs, yellow bone was visible, so much blood welling up that Lena didn’t even know where to begin as she pressed her hands to the large wound, choking on a sob.

 

            “Oh.”

 

            Wincing at the pressure, the tendons in Kara’s neck went taut as she arched off the ground, a loud scream escaping her as she writhed. She collapsed back against the dirt and retched, panting as she tried to catch her breath, and then pushed herself up to her elbows, twisting as she vomited all over the roots of the growing corn. She caught sight of her stomach then and let out a strangled sound of horror, the blood draining from her face as she sagged back again.

 

            “I’m sorry,” Lena quietly sobbed, pushing Kara’s shoulder, trying to urge her onto her back again. “I’m sorry, I didn’t mean to, I- it’ll be okay, just … lie still. I need you to lie still, okay? Please, just-”

 

            Kara made a guttural sound of agreement at the back of her throat, mouth clamped shut as she breathed through her nose, gripping fistfuls of dirt. At the pressure of Lena’s hands on her stomach again, Kara couldn’t stop the broken shout that worked its way up her throat, but Lena didn’t stop this time, her wand in her bloody hand as she tried to speak the spells, but was too shaken to work through anything complex. 

 

            As she worked, the corn field started to rustle, and Lena froze at the sound of movement pushing through the rows. Kara was still drawing in ragged breaths, in between hitching cries of pain, and Lena felt panic knife through her, hearing the movement draw closer, and more rustling following. She had to settle for bandages, a relatively easy spell that wrapped Kara tightly, but quickly started to spot with red as she bled freely, and at the yelp of pain Kara let out as the bandages cinched around her, Lena threw herself on top of her, bloody hand clamping down over Kara’s mouth as she shushed her, her voice a shaky whisper, barely audible over the approaching sounds.

 

            “Shh. It’s okay. Don’t talk.”

 

            Tears traced down Kara’s temples, sliding into her hair, and her cry was muffled by Lena’s hand. It was dark, and she couldn’t see anything, pain muffling her senses, but she could hear Lena’s quiet sobs, breathless and hitching as she pinned Kara to the ground, softly hushing her as she trembled. Her whole body was taut, wand clutched in a blood-slick hand as she braced for an attack, sure that someone would’ve heard the screams, but as the rustling grew louder, it was further north of where they were, and pounding footsteps raced past them, plunging deeper into the corn field. Lena surmised that it was a wedding guest trying to escape, but didn’t move, aware of other footsteps giving chase.

 

            Hidden by the tall stalks and the darkness, Kara was pinned there for agonising minutes as footsteps raced past on either side, the crack of non-verbal spells splitting the hush, followed by the loud shout of voices as an altercation happened to the south of where they were. Kara jolted at that, the sudden loudness of voices startling her, and her ragged cry of pain was stifled by Lena’s hand pressed firmly over her lips. When the footsteps continued to rush deeper into the corn field, the fighting moving past them, Lena’s taut body went slack, and she eased herself off Kara, who drew in a ragged breath, sobbing as she tasted bile at the back of her throat.

 

            “It’s okay,” Lena tearfully whispered, “I’m going to get you help, okay? This is- this is going … to hurt. But it’ll all be okay after that. I need you … to trust me.”

 

            Her voice deepened, breaking as she babbled, and she rose to her feet unsteadily before pointing her wand at Kara and levitating her to a standing position. At the sensation of her body moving, Kara let out a loud shout, eyes screwed shut as her mind furred at the edges, and there was the frantic sound of swishing corn as footsteps pounded back towards them, the blinding red of a spell rocketing through the stalks right as Lena’s arms came around Kara, turning them as she Disapparated before it could strike.

 

            They were on the landing of a residential building, a closed door in front of Kara as she clung to consciousness, sagging against Lena, who was trying her hardest to keep it together, covered in her fiancée’s blood, cheeks wet with tears and chest tight with panic. She didn’t even knock, just nonverbally spelled the door open with so much urgency that the door rebounded off the hallway wall as she dragged Kara inside.

 

            “Sam!” Lena hoarsely yelled. 

 

            There was a clatter in the living room at the sound of the door banging open, and Sam was already approaching the mouth of the doorway when Lena called out, her wand held aloft as she stepped out. At the sight of them, her arm lowered, and she rushed forward, her tense expression going slack with surprise before she gave Lena a stern look.

 

            “What happened?”

 

            “Splinching,” Lena brokenly explained.

 

            “Splinching?” Sam echoed, aghast at the state Kara was in, and the idea that Lena wouldn’t have been able to heal it herself in a heartbeat.

 

            She had Kara’s other arm draped over her shoulder, and they had to turn sideways to lead her down the hallway and into the living room. Deposited on the sofa, Kara let out a listless groan, her face spasming as she sagged into the cushions. Sam quickly moved over to the door and shut it so Ruby wouldn’t walk in and see, and hurried over to Lena’s side, sinking to a crouch beside her. Lena was sitting on her haunches, green eyes haunted in her agonised face, and Sam cleared her throat.

 

            “Kara, can you hear me?”

 

            At the hum of assent, Sam nodded, and Kara’s lashes fluttered as she stared at her through half-lidded eyes. “I-”

 

            “It’s alright, don’t talk,” Sam cut her off.

 

            Cutting off with a rasping sound of amusement, Kara closed her eyes, feeling tired and cold. Sam was speaking then, but the words were all muffled, and there was a tinny sound in Kara’s ears as her head lolled. She was aware of cold fingers tightly clutching her hand, then, and she smiled thinly, weakly returning the squeeze.

 

            “Lena,” she lethargically slurred.

 

            Lena softly shushed her, fingers stroking the back of Kara’s hand, and Sam was back then, nudging Lena aside so she could press a vial to Kara’s lips, forcing her to drink. She gave her two potions, and Kara choked them both down before letting the Healer pull apart the ruins of her dress robes and vanish the bandages around her midriff. Sam hissed at the sight of what was underneath them, fresh blood continuing to well up, and she looked at Lena, giving her a grave look.

 

            “Hold her firmly.”

 

            Nodding, Lena pushed herself to her knees and pressed down on Kara’s shoulders, pinning her in place. Lashes fluttering as she opened her eyes, Kara made a sound of consternation at the back of her throat, reaching up to touch her trembling fingertips to Lena’s cheek. They came away wet, and she frowned, oblivious to Sam uncorking a Wound-Cleaning Potion behind Lena.

 

            “S’alright,” Kara mumbled.

 

            She tensed then, her face crumpling with pain as Sam poured the Wound-Cleaning Potion into the open gashes. It took everything in Kara to bite back a scream, the Blood-Replenishing Potion and Restorative Draught doing much to revitalise her, which only made her more aware of the pain of healing. Lena held her down, though, and Kara squeezed her eyes shut, stiff as a broomstick as she lay stretched out on the sofa, the sting of the potion subsiding, only to be replaced by a Wiggenweld Potion, the gashes too deep for Essence of Dittany to do the trick this time. Muttering spells beneath her breath as she slowly dripped the potion into the wounds, Sam slowly stitched Kara back together, until nothing but tender new skin and her old scars marred her stomach.

 

            Chest quickly rising and falling, Kara took a few minutes to breathe, her body slick with sweat and blood, and she closed her eyes, the drum of her heartbeat loud in her ears. Lena held her hand tightly, her forehead pressed to Kara’s shoulder as she knelt there, hunched over, and Kara seemed to shake herself out of it then, easing herself into a sitting position as she winced faintly at the tenderness. Sam had cleaned away the bloody bandages and the potion vials, and Kara shifted so she could swing her legs around, sitting fully upright, bare feet - she’d lost her heels at some point - on the rug, as she pulled her torn dress robes tighter around herself. Lena knelt on the rug, head ducked down, and Kara reached out to cup her shoulders, trying to get her to get up off the floor.

 

            “Off the floor,” she whispered, trying to coax her, to no avail.

 

            Lena didn’t respond, didn’t move an inch, and Kara suppressed a sigh, guilt needling her as she kept her hands on Lena’s shoulders. Trying a different tactic, she swallowed thickly, her voice softening to a plea. “Will you sit next to me, please?”

 

            Climbing to her feet, her movements jerky, Lena turned and sat beside her, so close that they were pressed together. Still, she wouldn’t look up, and Kara grimaced, putting an arm around her back and resting her chin on Lena’s shoulder. She was quiet for a moment, swimming in her regret, and she pressed a delicate kiss to Lena’s shoulder before she spoke, her voice barely above a whisper.

 

            “I’m sorry.”
