            Flinching, Lena jerked away from her, green eyes sharp with anger and disgust as she finally looked at Kara. “Don’t.”

 

            “I was just trying to keep you safe,” Kara continued. “I shouldn’t have taken you away like that, I just- I panicked, and I-”

 

            “Stop, stop, stop,” Lena cut her off, burying her face in her hands. “Don’t apologise to me.”

 

            “I will,” Kara firmly insisted. “I didn’t give you a choice, I-”

 

            “I hurt you.”

 

            “I think I hurt myself, actually. I was trying so hard to stop you from Disapparating that I Splinched myself,” Kara laughed, the sound rueful and sheepish.

 

            Lena didn’t say anything, but Kara could see a muscle twitching it her jaw as she kept her face in her hands. Reaching out, her hand falling to Lena’s back, Kara soothingly rubbed it, feeling a wince of guilt twinge in her chest. “Hey, look at me.”

 

            Dropping her hands, Lena’s head sharply turned towards Kara, and tears wet her cheeks, even though her eyes were hard with anger. Panic jolted through Kara, and her stomach plummeted at the sight of Lena’s tears. They were a rare occurrence, and never for something so small as a Splinching, but it left Kara alarmed as she reached for her, tenderly wiping away her tears, her voice anguished as she quietly spoke.

 

            “It’s alright. I’m sorry. I-“

 

            Lena jerked her head away from Kara’s fingers, her shoulders taut as she balled her hands into fists in her lap, and then she wilted, collapsing into Kara’s lap. Face buried in the cool skin of her thigh, clutching at ripped silk, Lena let out a choked sound of relief. Stroking her dark hair, Kara’s guilt deepened.

 

            “I’m sorry.”

 

            She couldn’t say more than that, and Lena didn’t have a chance to berate her as Sam returned with two glasses and three mugs. Kara patted Lena’s shoulder reassuringly and gave her a minute to collect herself as Sam set the collection of cups down on the coffee table and took a seat in the adjacent armchair. She picked up her cup of tea and a glass, extending the glass to Kara.

 

            Leaning forward, Kara took it from her, mumbling her thanks, and caught a whiff of Firewhisky. Sipping it slowly, she felt heat spread through her chest and closed her eyes. The sound of a clock filled the tense silence as she sipped until her glass was empty and then wandlessly levitated it back to the coffee table. Lena kept her face safely tucked in Kara’s lap the entire time.

 

            “What happened?”

 

            “Um …” Kara started rubbing the bridge of her nose as she frowned. “We were at a wedding. An acquaintance from our … extended friend group.” Sam just gave her an exasperated look, and Kara smiled weakly. “It was interrupted with a warning; the Ministry’s fallen, I don’t know if you’ve heard yet?”

 

            “What?”

 

            “Yeah, they’ve killed Scrimgeour.”

 

            “Fucking hell,” Sam sighed, shaking her head. “I was listening to Witching Hour and they didn’t mention it.”

 

            “It must still be breaking. Um, well, Death Eaters showed up. I … took us away. Lena wanted to go back … but I didn’t, um … got myself Splinched trying to stop her from Apparating.”

 

            “Ah. I wondered why it was so … extensive. That’ll do it.”

 

            Kara hollowly chuckled and hummed in agreement. “Stupid of me, really.”

 

            Lena’s head reared up then, and she stiffly reached for her own glass of Firewhisky, draining it in one gulp and setting the glass back down. Then she climbed to her feet, her voice rough as she quietly spoke. “We should go.”

 

            “No, you’re not fit to Apparate anywhere,” Sam objected, “and you’re not on the Floo network. You can take my bed for the night.”

 

            “Everyone will be worried.”

 

            “So send word.”

 

            Looking annoyed but resigned to her fate, Lena raked a hand through her hair. “Fine. Do you have any parchment?”

 

            Sam laughed, arching an eyebrow. “Were you planning on them finding out before dawn, or?”

 

            “I’ll send a Patronus,” Kara cut in, her eyes flitting to Lena’s, watching her fiancée’s shoulders loosen slightly. 

 

            Lena had still never managed that piece of magic, not even a streak of silver, despite the many happy years with Kara in between the wars. It was a secret she’d managed to keep hidden at work for all this time, letting Interns and Residents notify families while she pretended to be too busy to do menial tasks like that. Even Sam didn’t know, and Kara spared her the embarrassment of having to admit that to her friend, on top of an already shit night she was having. Sam nodded, climbing to her feet and leaving the room, and Kara cleared her throat, thinking of Alex as she cast her Patronus, the wolf bounding away, far-flung to where her sister was as it relayed Kara’s message that they were safe, that they’d gotten away and were spending the night at Sam’s flat.

 

            While she sent word, Lena reclaimed her seat at Kara’s side and sipped her tea, her hand still holding a tremor as she sat rigidly with a wooden look on her face. Finishing her short missive, Kara set her wand down and reached for her tea as well, draining half of it quickly, the sweetness of sugar perking her up as the potions in her bloodstream continued to mend her, and she was down to the dregs by the time Sam returned, easing the door open and sticking her head in.

 

            “I’ve put some clean clothes and towels in the bathroom for you. Thought you might want to get cleaned up before bed.”

 

            “Thank you,” Kara gratefully murmured, swallowing the last bits of tea, sugar crystals dissolving on her tongue, and climbing to her feet.

 

            She followed Sam to the bathroom, pausing in the doorway and glancing back as Lena remained seated. Suppressing a sigh, Kara made herself keep moving, thanking Sam again as she was shown to the bathroom, the tatters of her dress clenched closed as she slipped past her and shut the door. Shedding her clothes, ruined beyond repair, Kara turned the shower on and waited for the water to heat before stepping beneath the stream and feeling her muscles loosen. It felt nice against her aching limbs, and she carefully cleaned away the blood on her stomach, her chest, even running down her thigh, where the deep gash on her hip had trickled down with gravity, and she watched the water run pink down the drain.

 

            She was still beneath the water, soap suds sluicing down her skin as she worked the dirt from beneath her nails, when the bathroom door opened and closed. Peeking through the shower curtain, she watched Lena shed her bloodstained dress robes, the discolouration almost hidden by the deep burgundy of the silk, and stepped back to let her get in with her. Kara didn’t speak, just moved Lena so she was beneath the stream of water, and picked up her hand, rubbing soap into the grooves of her palm as she rinsed her blood off her skin. Lena ended up taking the soap from her and washing herself, and Kara climbed out, giving her a few minutes to herself, pausing at the sound of a choked breath, but allowing her the privacy of a curtain between them.

 

            Drying herself off with the towel, she tried her best to work the bloodstains out of her underwear and then put on the set of flannel pyjamas Sam had left for her. Sitting on the closed lid of the toilet, Kara cleaned her glasses on the corner of the towel and waited for Lena to emerge. She was quicker than Kara had been, and livid red lines crisscrossed her body as she climbed out of the shower, quick to grab the towel and cover herself up, but not quite quick enough. With a deep ache suffusing her, Kara got to her feet and walked over to her, gently peeling the towel away from her skin, and lightly kissed the marks raking Lena’s shoulders. Lena made a pitiful sound of objection, twisting out of her grasp, and hastily dried off, changing into the other pair of pyjamas and cuffing the sleeves and pants to fit her better. She hung the towel over the rail with Kara’s and unlocked the door, walking out without a word. Pulling the light string, Kara trailed her out and shut the door, finding Sam in the kitchen, setting their cups in the sink. She glanced up at the appearance of Lena, giving her a small smile.

 

            “Are you hungry? Did you want something to-”

 

            “I’d like to go to bed,” Lena quietly cut her off, and Sam nodded.

 

            “Alright, well, help yourself to anything if you get up during the night. You know where the bathroom is. Um … I’m not at work until tomorrow night, so I’ll see you in the morning.”

 

            They both said goodnight, and Kara followed Lena through the flat, anxiously wringing her hands as she felt a moment of anticipatory dread for the moment they were left alone together without anything to occupy their attention. She stepped into Sam’s bedroom after Lena and quietly shut the door, taking in the double bed with the thick gingham quilt and abundance of pillows, the cosy orange glow of a bedside lamp turned on for them, and the signs of Sam’s life - perfume bottles, candles and books scattered across the nightstand, worn clothes left on top of the chest of drawers with her work bag and a pile of paperwork peeking out - and wishing they were somewhere else, somewhere they could talk without the awkwardness of being in someone else’s house. 

 

            Rounding the bed, Lena shifted a few of the decorative pillows to the floor and climbed beneath the quilt, her back to Kara as she moved a pillow into place and faced the wall. Doing the same on her side, Kara’s throat felt tight, and she turned off the lamp before she sank against the pillows. Staring unseeingly at the dark ceiling for a moment, she turned on her side and slid across the mattress, having to bridge a bigger gap than was reasonable in a double bed, until she was pressed up against Lena’s back. Slowly wrapping an arm around her waist, Kara kissed the shoulder of Lena’s pyjamas and leaned her forehead against her upper arm.

 

            “I’m sorry.”

 

            “Don’t,” Lena whispered.

 

            “I am,” Kara insisted. “I just- I don’t want you to be angry with me.”

 

            “Just stop,” Lena flatly cut her off, bolting upright in bed and throwing the blankets off as she climbed out.

 

            Falling silent for a moment, sitting up with her, Kara’s mouth closed, and then she felt a flash of irritation and opened it again. With a sharp gesture of her hand, she wandlessly turned the lamp back on, casting that warm glow over the bedroom again as she sat beneath the blankets, scowling with a stubborn jut to her chin. “No, I won’t. A month ago, you were having a go at me for trying to back out of this with as much selflessness as I could manage, and you said no. You wouldn’t let me do that. But now you want to shut me out? Because I got hurt? I’ve been Splinched before.”

 

            “You got hurt because you were trying to keep me safe.”

 

            “Yes,” Kara quietly exclaimed. “Yes, and I’d do it all over again to keep you safe. I don’t care. Okay, I’m sorry for taking away your choice in the matter, but I’m not sorry for keeping you alive. For making sure you stay that way. And the truth is … I’d let them all die in an attack if it meant you lived, and that’s just- that’s a horrible thing to admit to.”

 

            Her voice wobbled then, tears in her eyes as she stared at Lena with agony wrenching her face. Licking her lips, Kara shook her head slightly and let out a strained laugh as she wrung the edge of the quilt in her hands.

 

            “But it’s true. And I’m not ashamed to feel that way, because I can’t- there might be no world for you without me in it, but there’s not one for me without you, either. And I am … scared. I’ve been scared every day since your brother caught me. Because he will hurt you, kill- it’s all I dream about, it’s what keeps me up at night, and I just- now he won’t waste time tormenting you, and there won’t be time for me to save you, because he’ll just … so I can’t let you get anywhere near him, now. Because I’m- I’m so frightened that you won’t walk away from it.”

 

            Dashing the heel of her palm across her wet eyes, Kara drew in a shuddering breath, sniffing as she pressed her lips into a flat line. Her chin dimpled from the effort it took to swallow her fear, the urge to fall apart, so tired and defeated as she stared at Lena, who looked ashen with surprise. None of it was surprising, though. It still took her a long minute to reply, gesturing off-handedly as her mouth opened and closed, until she could make her voice work. It was scratchy and low, and Kara just wanted to wrap her in her arms.

 

            “I know that you’re scared. I’m scared, too. I’m not ashamed to admit it. I just- I can’t prioritise myself over other people’s safety. I can’t let that fear rule my life. Not when I can help.”

 

            “That’s because other people have never prioritised you,” Kara tried to reason, getting out of bed, two long strides bringing her before Lena as she reached up to cup her face in her hands.

 

            “I’ve never been worth prioritising; not to anyone but you. My use has always been in helping other people. Whether that was through spying or healing, it didn’t matter, but-“

 

            “You’re not alive to be useful. To me or anyone else. And I know you've been hurt in ways that I can’t even imagine, but I- that doesn’t mean you exist to- to martyr yourself for the cause, to sacrifice everything for other people. Not even for me. You tried that once, and you promised me you wouldn’t do it again-“

 

            “But you would do the same. Wouldn’t you? If it was between one of us dying - hell, even if it was just to save my life - you would step in front of me and take my place.”

 

            Dropping her hands from Lena’s face, Kara softly sighed as the corners of her mouth turned down slightly. “Yes.”

 

            “And that is what I can’t stand. That is what just … pisses me off,” Lena roughly replied, pointing a finger at Kara as she punctuated her words with accusatory jabs. “You expect more of me than you’re willing to give. If I weren’t with you tonight, you wouldn’t have run.”

 

            “Because no one there wants me dead. Not me specifically. Oh, I’m sure they’ll happily kill me, if given the chance, but I don’t have a big target on my back because I couldn’t help but- why did you have to tell him you turned him in?”

 

            “Because I thought that I-” Lena cut off, her mouth snapping shut as she quietly seethed, shaking her head. It took her a few seconds to swallow her resentment before she could continue, giving Kara a sullen smile, barely a twist of her lips as she let out a huff of laughter. “I thought that I was going to kill him. How arrogant of me, I know. And I think you were right, when you said it wasn’t just your family’s name, but the family that came with it, because … I am … so scared that what’s inside of me … is the same thing that’s inside of him, and that we’re all just … rotten all the way through from being part of that family. Um … and I don’t know what I’ll do if I see him, because I don’t know if I want to know that I have the capacity for that in me, but I know that- I can’t forget that he hurt you. I could forgive - no, forget - what he did to me, but … not you. And I don’t know what the limit on my revenge will be. I want him dead. I want him dead so badly, but I don’t know what it’ll mean for me if it’s at my hand. What that will do to me to become like them.”

 

            Kara’s face was slack with shock to hear that admission, and she made a small sound of confusion as she processed the words, before her shoulders caved, her expression wretched. “You are nothing like them. Nothing at all. You are good, you are gentle, and kind, and caring - everything your brother isn’t. Nothing could ever change that, and you know that’s true, because your mum tried so hard to change you. And you’re still here, as yourself, despite it all, and I know that you would never do anything that could change that.”

 

            “That’s because you don’t know what I saw, what I stood by and just … let happen,” Lena said, gesturing aimlessly as her voice wobbled, eyes bright. “A good person doesn’t do that. And I can live with the fact that I was doing it for the greater good, and I will try my hardest to make amends and help save as many people as I can, but you don’t know what I could or couldn’t do. Because that limit hasn’t been tested yet. And I was so sure that it was going to be at Hogwarts, and the only reason it wasn’t was that I couldn’t get past his defences. And I don’t know what will happen next time I see him, um … and I don’t want to put you through that-”

 

            “You were asking me to marry you without a ceremony, barely an hour ago,” Kara said, incredulous as she kept her voice down.

 

            “Because I want to marry you!” Lena exclaimed, her voice loud in the room, before she lowered it, wincing at the thought of waking Ruby or being overheard by Sam. “I want to marry you before …” She didn’t want to finish the thought, a strained smile on her lips as she looked at Kara with aching green eyes. “I want you to be looked after. I want to make sure my mother can’t-”

 

            “You think I give a shit about an inheritance?” Kara cut her off with a scathing scoff. “She can take it all, she can fucking have it. I don’t want to be a widow!”

 

            A pitiful sob passed her lips before she could stop it, and Kara clutched at the front of her pyjamas as she felt her cheeks flame, hot tears spilling onto them as she voiced her fear. Drawing in a hitching breath, dashing away her tears, Kara sniffed, staring at the carpet as she continued, Lena stunned into silence.

 

            “And you are … so sure that you’re going to die. And what about me? What about me when you go chasing your death? You want to get married more than you want a ceremony, but all I can think about is … if you- if you-” She couldn’t say it again, giving her head a quick shake as a pained look of amusement flashed across her face. “I will be left all alone, and I won’t even have that day to remember you by. Just … one day. I just want the memories of that … one happy day with you, with our family, our friends, celebrating. Because I am fucking terrified that I’m going to lose you. And your lack of self-preservation is a liability, because I can’t trust you to put yourself first, and that- I can’t walk into a fight with you again, knowing that your brother might be there, and you’ll be so- so clouded by the thought of revenge that you won’t know when to run.”

 

            “I’m not planning on dying,” Lena curtly replied.

 

            “That’s not the problem. The problem is, I don’t think you’ll draw the line. And I don’t want to let you out of my sight, because I don’t know what happens next. And I just- I wish we had never gotten involved. I hate that you walked back into this fight, that you put Dumbledore’s wishes first, the second your brother broke out of Azkaban, because we lost … so much time. And things haven’t been right since then. Not even since I got you back. And it’s selfish, I know that, but I never pretended that I wasn’t a selfish person. Um … and I just- I don’t think things will be right again. Because we don’t know how much time we have left, or what comes next, and I-”

 

            Taking a step towards her, tears in her eyes as well, although she retained her composure better than Kara did, Lena haltingly reached for Kara and drew her into a hug. Holding onto her tightly, Kara buried her face in Lena’s shoulder and let out a choked breath, feeling weak as she clung to her, desperate, even. Rubbing Kara’s back, Lena quietly hushed her, but there was a shakiness to her voice that belied the pain in her chest as well.

 

            “I’ll draw the line,” Lena whispered, talking quickly, until she was practically babbling, her warm breath ghosting over the side of Kara’s throat. “I’ll draw the line, I’ll- I’ll get myself out. Just like I promised you last time. I did it, didn’t I? I came back to you, and I’ll … I’ll do it again, I just- I can’t uninvolve myself. I’m already involved, and so are you, and I refuse to be a coward about it. No matter if my brother is waiting for me. But I can promise you, I have no intention of leaving you alone. I will fight harder than I’ve ever fought for anything to stay alive for you. I promise you that. I will- I will make an Unbreakable Vow if it reassures you. I just- I can’t live with the fear of him being out there somewhere for the rest of my life. I have to do this for myself, too. You’re right, and I hate that we both got dragged back into it, that it all played out like this, and I’m as much to blame for it as you are, but … it won’t be right again unless we win. It’s clear that there’s no place for us in the world if he wins, and that means fighting. That means you trusting me.”

 

            “I do trust you,” Kara murmured, her voice so miserable. “Just not with your own safety.”

 

            “You have to. You have to trust me with that, too, or you’ll be a liability in a fight as well. And we can’t afford to be distracted if we’re going to make it through this alive.”

 

            “I just want to keep you safe,” Kara whispered as she pulled back, her fingertips brushing over Lena’s cheeks as she looked at her with gutwrenching longing. “I don’t want you to fight.”

 

            “I know. But you won’t stop me again,” Lena told her, and it wasn’t an order, but a warning.

Chapter 69

            Lena slept like shit that night, tossing and turning as she kept going back to particular words exchanged, a pit in her stomach as she kept picturing Kara’s rent open body, how hot her blood had been on her hands, the broken look on her face as she’d tearfully confessed her fears in the lamplight of Sam’s bedroom. It would’ve been easier if she’d blamed Lena for the Splinching, but she didn’t, and there was no absolution for Lena to be found within herself, so she restlessly whiled away the night, waiting for dawn so she could give up the pretence of rest and get up. 

 

            She could’ve gotten up anyway, but she didn’t want to leave Kara’s side, the two of them up well past midnight, propped up against the pillows once she’d insisted that Kara rest properly after the Splinching. Lena occasionally thumbed tears off her cheeks, while Kara sniffled at her side, the two of them trying to pretend like they weren’t crying, weren’t hurt by this imbalance between them when it was already so hard to pretend like everything was normal, was fine, and weren’t terrified at the prospect of their fears coming true. She was miserable all night, red-eyed and exhausted, and irritated by her inability to stamp down her bottled emotions. Lena had been so good at it for years, decades, even, and now it was like a dam had been unleashed and a flimsy wall erected in its stead, bursting at every opportunity.

 

            At five, she got out of bed, tucking Kara in and kissing her wayward curls before she slipped out of the bedroom and sat at the kitchen table in the dark until she heard a door quietly creak open. Waving a hand towards the overhead kitchen light, Lena lit it as footsteps approached, and Sam came in, rubbing her eyes and mumbling a good morning. Lena quietly greeted her, too lost in her thoughts to be too chatty, and she accepted the strong cup of coffee Sam set before her with thanks. Dragging out a chair, Sam sat across from her and curled up on the seat, knees to her chest as she cradled her mug in her hands.

 

            “You alright?”

 

            “Fantastic,” Lena sarcastically sighed, rubbing her forehead as a headache throbbed at her temples.

 

            Sam took a sip of her steaming coffee, staring at Lena over the rim of her mug. “Sounded like things got a bit heated last night.”

 

            “Sorry, I hope we didn’t wake Ruby. Or disturb you.”

 

            With a dismissive laugh, Sam shook her head. “Merlin, you’re a funny cow sometimes.”

 

            Lena blinked, her focus sharpening as her eyebrows rose in surprise. “What?”

 

            “You show up on my doorstep with Kara bleeding all over the bloody floor, don’t say a single, solitary word the whole time while I patch her up, and spend the night in my bed after shouting the house down for nigh on half an hour, and all I get is a sorry? You could at least have the decency to gossip a little and tell me what had your wand in a knot.”

 

            Giving her a withering look, Lena couldn’t help but smile slightly. “Well, you didn’t have to give up your bed. How’s your back?”

 

            Sam hummed, flipping her off as she took another sip of coffee. “Not quite the same having to share a bed with a fifteen-year-old as it was when she was five. Now, out with it.”

 

            “It’s just … this whole … situation.”

 

            “Oh. The situation. Well, that’s cleared everything up,” Sam rolled her eyes.

 

            Feeling the heaviness in her chest alleviate slightly at her friend’s attempts to poke fun at something that felt so dire to Lena last night that she hadn’t slept a wink, she let out a reluctant laugh. Running her hands over her face, she picked up her coffee and took a sip.

 

            “I got mad at her for Apparating us away, and then she got hurt, so I was mad at myself. But it’s more than that, it’s- neither of us is guaranteed to survive this. I think … I was a bit rash in my decision to tell my brother what I did, and now I’ve painted an even bigger target on my back. And now Kara’s more scared than she was before, because in her mind, I’m a dead witch walking, but I- I want to help. I want to keep her out of it, too, but that’s just as impossible. It’s just- we both wish the other wasn’t involved, but neither of us is willing to stay out of it - if it’s even possible to stay out of it anymore. It’s just- it’s a lot of worry. Arguing about it hasn’t gotten us anywhere, staying out of it didn’t either, so … well, we just have to hope we do pull through, at the end of the day.”

 

            “Right. Well, I’m on Kara’s side, I’m afraid, love. You’re too reckless with your safety for anyone to feel comfortable letting you loose in a fight. I mean … you got very lucky at Hogwarts.”

 

            “I know,” Lena sighed. “I think I got all defensive because … there’s a lot of truth to what she was saying. But I don’t want to give her more reason to worry by telling her she’s right.”

 

            “She’d probably be happy to feel vindicated,” Sam pointed out.

 

            “It’s just- it’s silly,” Lena sighed again, grimacing as she stared into her coffee. “And it’s not silly, it’s … terrifying. The thought of her being hurt … I don’t know how I’m supposed to think of anything else.”

 

            “I imagine she feels much the same.”

 

            “She does. That only makes me feel worse.”

 

            Sam gave her a grim look, “I can’t tell you not to fight. It wouldn’t change your mind. And it’s no good crying over a spilt potion; what’s done is done. Just … try to stay out of trouble for … I don’t know, is a month too ambitious for you? It might reassure her a bit. And stay away from your brother.”

 

            “The problem with that is I don’t know if he’s going to be there or not,” Lena exasperatedly replied. 

 

            “Mm, a fair point.”

 

            “I have to assume he would be. The bastard is inescapable; I don’t know how the Aurors haven’t caught him. Maybe I should just offer myself up as bait to make their job easier for them.”

 

            Sam clicked her tongue and gave Lena a stern look, but she smiled, and Lena’s cheek shallowly dimpled. “It’s shit advice, but I think you just need to … stress a bit less. I mean, things have been shit since you got back. That must be a hard adjustment. And, I mean, you’re living with her mum; how’s that going?”

 

            “Oh, well, Eliza’s fantastic. We get on great-”

 

            “I mean for you and Kara. That’s got to be … I don’t know, limiting your time spent together. Alone.”

 

            With a scoff, Lena tipped her head back, smiling wryly. “I don’t think our relatively non-existent sex life is the issue here.”

 

            “Probably not helping things, though, is it? You were apart for so long, and now you can’t even have a little privacy to feel a little closer to her. And two single beds?”

 

            “Well, we’re actually sleeping in one. That’s probably part of the problem, too. Even with the potions you gave us, I’m not sleeping well, she’s not sleeping well, and neither of us can sleep alone, so ...”

 

            “Tell you what, have a crack at that, and see how it goes. What can go wrong with a nice shag and a proper night’s sleep?”

 

            Taking a sip of her coffee, Lena opened her mouth and closed it again at the sound of footsteps approaching the doorway, twisting in her seat to watch Kara shuffle in. Her curls were unruly, her cheek embedded with the print of the pillowcase seam, and her wire-rimmed glasses pushed up as she rubbed her eyes.

 

            “Morning,” she murmured, pausing to kiss the top of Lena’s head.

 

            “Hey,” Lena whispered, her hand finding Kara’s, squeezing her fingers.

 

            “Tea? Coffee?” Sam offered, pushing her chair back to stand.

 

            “Oh, no, I’m fine, thank you,” Kara replied, pulling the chair beside Lena out and sitting.

 

            She looked tired, folding her arms over her stomach as she blinked owlishly at the kitchen window, the sky still dark beyond. Lena finished her coffee quickly and then cleared her throat, straightening in her seat.

 

            “Thank you. We should probably go home, let everyone know we’re fine.”

 

            “Mm, best not to keep them worrying,” Sam replied rather pointedly.

 

            Giving her a tight smile, Lena rose to her feet and set the mug in the sink, before she backtracked to the bedroom and fetched their dress robes. Hers was fine, aside from the blood, so she changed back into it and put Sam’s pyjamas in the heaped laundry basket in the corner of the room, and carried her heels in hand, while Kara’s dress robe was bundled in her arm. Sam waved her aside when she apologetically mentioned returning them at a later date, and she hugged them both goodbye at the door.

 

            Taking Kara’s hand with care, Lena hesitated before Apparating them home. They made it there in one piece, and Kara ushered her inside ahead of her, the cottage quiet and still, but the glow of the fireplace greeted them, letting them know that Eliza was already up. At the sound of the front door opening, she heard movement upstairs, and Eliza appeared in her dressing gown, hurrying down to wrap Kara in a tight hug, holding onto her for a prolonged moment, before she pulled away. She made no mention of the pyjamas, but her eyes landed on the wadded bloody fabric in Lena’s possession, and she fretted over her daughter for a beat longer.

 

            “We weren’t involved,” Kara wearily explained. “We got away before the fighting even started. How’s everyone else?”

 

            “No one was killed, but apparently, the Death Eaters questioned everyone left behind. They all got away before then, but your sister went back afterwards to help.”

 

            Relief shot through Lena, and she felt some of the tension between her and Kara dissipate at that news. Swallowing thickly, Lena nodded, and Kara worked herself free of her mother and made straight for the stairs. Lena made to follow after her put was stopped in her tracks as Eliza stepped in front of her.

 

            “Are you okay?” Eliza quietly asked, reaching out to touch Lena’s arm.

 

            “Fine,” Lena tersely replied, before remembering herself and softening. “Thank you, Eliza. It was … a long night. I’m sorry if we worried you.”

 

            “Alex came and told me what had happened right before midnight. She said Kara had sent word.”

 

            “Good,” Lena nodded.

 

            She hesitated and then followed her fiancée up the stairs, feeling a stab of guilt as she left Eliza standing at the bottom, worried and clueless as to what had happened. Lena was otherwise preoccupied with Kara’s well-being at the moment, though, so she didn’t stay behind to placate her mother-in-law. Reaching the landing, she turned left into the open door to what had become their bedroom and stepped inside.

 

            “Can we talk?” Lena quietly asked, easing the door shut behind herself.

 

            Kara turned to look at her, an anxious edge to her face as she nervously wrung her hands. She stood in the narrow space at the foot of the bed, where the chest of drawers was pushed up against the wall, penning Lena into the small area inside the door.

 

            “Can I go first?” she asked in a small voice.

 

            “Of course,” Lena softly murmured, leaning back against the door and the assortment of robes and dressing gowns hung on the back of it.

 

            Raking a hand through her hair, Kara blew all of the air out of her lungs, shaking her head. “Look, I know this … worry is not good for me. It’s not good for us. I’m trying … so hard to let go of it, I just- I want to keep you safe. And it’s not fair to you, for me to just … whisk you away. And I’m sorry. I’m finding it really difficult at the moment. With everything that happened before, and at Hogwarts. Um … but I think I need to accept that I can’t control everything, least of all you. But … I think you’re also dealing with some things that aren't good for you, as well.”

 

            She fell silent, and Lena felt a lump lodge in her throat as she stared back at her. Swallowing thickly when Kara didn’t continue, she cleared her throat, her voice rasping as she arched an eyebrow. “Like what?”

 

            Looking a little annoyed at Lena’s nonchalance, Kara’s mouth flattened, and she nodded slightly to herself before forging onward. “I’m afraid that … since you don’t have the quill anymore-“

 

            “Oh,” Lena quietly scoffed, her mouth twisting bitterly, “great, the fucking quill again.”

 

            “I’m just concerned that you’re trying to find new ways to punish yourself again-“

 

            “You have never let it go, have you? No matter how many years ago it was.”

 

            Reaching for her but letting her hand limply fall back to her side, Kara sighed defeatedly. “It’s not about letting it go, I just- I’m worried that this is all going to bring it all back up.”

 

            “I destroyed the quill after all of this started,” Lena sharply reminded her. 

 

            “I’m not accusing you of anything, it’s just- more … shit keeps happening,” Kara frustratedly argued. “And I can’t help but worry that you’re just … using the opportunity to rush into danger, to get a thrill. Like you think you deserve to risk your life to save others, because … if it all went wrong, you’d have made amends for the rest of it. And I can’t let go of my worry until I know that’s not true.”

 

            Lena was silent as Kara finished speaking, and her scar itched to be gouged at, but she just drew in a shaky breath and fixed Kara with an unwavering stare. “I’m not doing it to get a thrill, or to replace the quill, and I’m not doing it to make amends for anything, but you’re not wrong. I- well, I think I do deserve to risk my life for others. That’s what I agreed to do; to save people’s lives. That doesn’t just apply to healing or spying. I can promise you I’m not intentionally trying to get myself hurt. I know I can be reckless and impulsive sometimes, that my anger or hurt can get the better of me, but I can promise you that I’m not purposely trying to get hurt.” 

 

            “You promise?” Kara quietly asked.

 

            Mouth curving into a small smile, Lena nodded. “I promise. I told you, I’ll swear an Unbreakable Vow that I won’t do that, if it reassures you.”

 

            With a soft laugh, Kara’s cheek shallowly dimpled as she smiled unevenly. “No, I just needed to hear you say it. Because neither of us will sit by, I know that - it’s one of the more frustrating things about us - so we need to be able to trust each other if we’re going to fight. Otherwise, I won’t be able to focus on anything but you.”

 

            “Good,” Lena whispered, some of the lingering tension dissipating at the knowledge they were on the same page now.

 

            Giving her a grim smile, Kara nodded, and then she paused. “What did you want to say?”

 

            “Oh,” Lena murmured, her brow furrowing as she lowered her gaze. “Just that … well, I know that things have been off since I got back, and I just- I miss you. Um … it’s not your fault, or mine, it’s just so different to how things were before. I don’t think it’ll be the same until we can go back to our home, to our life. But I miss it. I miss going to The Leaky Cauldron, and just … walking around Diagon Alley, going shopping, and- and having our friends over, and going to work. I miss having sex with you; we used to have so much great sex all over the bloody house, and now we live with your mum, who is lovely but is always here. I just- miss how close we were. It took me so long to be able to talk openly about things with you, to be vulnerable and not feel weak, and it just- it feels like I’ve gone back a few steps, and I don’t quite know how to go forward again. But I am … so relieved to just be here with you, that it’s all seemed so unimportant right now, but it is important. It’s us. And maybe that’s why I was in such a rush to marry you, so I could know that things weren’t coming undone, that we could still take steps forward.”

 

            Kara listened with a searching look on her face, head cocked to the side slightly, patient and understanding as Lena started to ramble on. A small smile played on her lips, and she inched closer as Lena wound down, gesturing helplessly. Then, Kara reached out and kissed Lena roughly, pressing her against the door, and Lena’s lips parted in surprise, a surprised breath hitching in her throat as she felt Kara’s hands on her waist.

 

            “Sorry, I can’t really kick my mum out, but we can at least have sex,” Kara murmured as she broke off the kiss and started to trail them along Lena’s jaw and down her neck. “If you’re not still mad at me.”

 

            Lena let out a breathless laugh, pushing Kara backwards. “I’m always mad at you. Take your clothes off.”

 

            Hurrying to obey, Kara waved her wand towards the bedroom door, which stiffened its hinges and the doorknob, and warded the room against any noise, before she tossed her wand onto the chest of drawers and hurriedly undid the buttons of the flannelette pyjama top. Lena didn’t give her much opportunity to undress, bearing down on Kara as she kissed her with a hunger that had been building for days, weeks, and Kara returned the sentiment with fervour, her hands running all over Lena as she cupped the side of her neck, skimmed her waist, pulled her closer so they were pressed up against each other, before her fingers searched for the fastenings of the dress robes.

 

            “Just … rip it,” Lena breathlessly insisted, Kara’s lips warm on her neck. “I won’t wear it again.”

 

            Making a low sound in response, Kara pulled back slightly and grabbed the neckline in her hands, ripping silk with ease as she tore it straight down the front. Lena had to admit, it gave her a little bit of a thrill to watch Kara tear her clothes right off her, and she laughed softly as Kara pinned her up against the chest of drawers, roughly kissing her as she gripped the edge of the dresser, her arms bracketing Lena. Leaning back, pulling Kara flush with her, Lena’s breath hitched, and she relaxed into the kiss as she worked her dress robes the rest of the way off, the torn silk pooling at her feet. Kara’s mouth dipped down to her collarbone, wet, open-mouthed kisses scattered across her chest as she stooped, Lena knotting her fingers in Kara’s hair as she closed her eyes, felt her heart pound in her chest, basking in the feeling.

 

            Her eyes snapped open a moment later, when she was lifted off her feet with a small sound of surprise escaping her, and deposited onto the bed as Kara came down with her, pressing her firmly into the mattress, while keeping her weight on her elbows and knees so she didn’t squash Lena beneath her. It made it easier for Kara to kiss her way down Lena’s stomach, not going particularly slow, too impatient for that, but not fast enough for Lena’s pent-up frustration as she let out strained huffs, giving Kara a severe look when her fiancée’s head reared up to give her a goading smile, before she made a more conscientious effort to take her sweet time.

 

            Lena gave just as good as she’d gotten, switching it up on Kara after her frustration had been fully vented, kissing every scar - and there were many of them - before she even made the slightest effort to touch her properly. Kara just pressed the heels of her palms into her eyes and laughed, which sounded more like a groan, as she yielded herself to the agonising torment of a long road to any sort of release. Fighting back a smile, Lena just kissed her sweetly and continued her slow, teasing efforts, enjoying Kara’s flushed cheeks and the way she restlessly moved, seeking any sort of friction as her pulse fluttered at her throat.

 

            Afterwards, Lena lay with her head pillowed on Kara’s shoulder, the length of her pressed against Kara’s side, their sweat-slicked skin practically suctioned together as Kara idly drew shapes over the bare expanse of Lena’s back and ribs, occasionally touching on a ticklish spot that made Lena buck away and click her tongue in mock annoyance. Eyes closed as she indulged in the closeness of bare skin on bare skin, Lena let out a soft breath, nuzzling into Kara’s shoulder as she felt some of her discontentment ease.

 

            “Better?” Kara murmured, pressing a soft kiss to her brow.

 

            “Much,” Lena hummed, practically purring with satisfaction as she stretched her legs and rolled half on top of Kara.

 

            Kara was silent for a moment before she softly sighed, her fingers walking down Lena’s spine as she spoke slowly. “You were right. Things haven’t been right since, and we haven’t been able to spend much time being us. But we can’t go home yet-”

 

            “I know. Honestly, I’m grateful to be here. That’s not the problem-”

 

            “I know, I was just going to say, well, I’m thirty-five soon; I'm pretty sure my mum knows we have sex. She respects our privacy enough not to barge in. I just- I wasn’t sure if … with everything that happened, maybe that’s why you’ve … kept your distance.”

 

            Lena groaned, pressing her face into Kara’s shoulder, dark hair spilling around her as she grimaced. “You have a very different relationship with your mum than I have with my family. I was afforded very little privacy, not just as a child, but even recently. It’s a … stupid thing to have stuck in my head. I was almost too afraid to go to sleep, knowing he could come in at any moment - that he did come in and drag me out of bed - or that I’d come out of the bathroom and he’d be sitting in my room, going through my things. I’m very conscious of the fact that Eliza’s not like that, I just- it has me on edge, I think. And honestly, sex isn’t the main thing, either; it’s just- we can’t sleep apart, because I’m afraid to even be a foot away from you. I’m so … tired, and I think- it took me such a long time to move on from what happened last time, and it’s worse this time around, because I knew better, and I was involved in it directly this time, and I’m just … angry that I have to move on from it again, and it feels so much harder this time. I can’t pretend none of it happened, because I’m surrounded by people who know it happened.”

 

            “No one expects you to just move on. Least of all this quickly,” Kara quietly assured her. “But it’s … very draining. I understand that. But we’ll get through it together, and we’ll go home soon, and I just- it’s not unimportant right now. It’s the most important thing in the world to me that we’re together again, and I want it to be right. So, however we can get back to how we were, just tell me and I’ll get us back there. I promise. Even if it’s a rushed wedding.”

 

            “Well … we’ll see about that,” Lena murmured, kissing the side of her neck.

 

 

            The next seven weeks were better. Not in terms of the war, but in terms of their relationship, and it eased some of the worry, some of the tension. There was an understanding between them now, a line drawn and reassurances made, trust established, and it afforded them the ability to help the Order more. They threw themselves fully into the thick of the fighting with no holding back, which wasn’t necessarily a good thing, considering their complicated past with the Order and how they’d had to walk back their decision to stay out of it all, but it was the right thing to do. They’d both tired of sitting at home, supposedly recovering from what they’d been subjected to, while growing increasingly agitated at being sidelined, but with Dumbledore dead, and the news growing darker by the day, they were needed more than ever.

 

            There were late-night skirmishes, duelling with Death Eaters in narrow alleyways in a dozen cities across the UK, chasing them through relentless rain as they hurled curses back and forth, and early mornings stalking suspects through the public streets of Knockturn Alley and the adjoining districts, attempting to get the jump on Death Eaters and their planned attacks. They were there when The Daily Prophet was attacked towards the middle of August, Lena stunning Mercy Graves in the face and dragging Andrea out with her after the fighting was over. Her friend had been shaken and pale, but had the sense to abandon her business, letting the Death Eaters take over, much like they’d taken over the Ministry. Everything published after that was propaganda for the Dark Lord, and Lena seethed every time she got her hands on a copy, no longer willing to fork over the pittance for a daily newspaper delivery.

 

            By the start of September, Sam had quit work as well, heeding Lena’s advice and not letting Ruby board the Hogwarts Express on the first of the month. The ring on Lena’s finger had turned red two days after that, and she’d immediately Apparated to Sam’s flat with Kara’s hand in her own, wands out on the landing as they heard the sounds of a scuffle within, the door blasted off its hinges. Death Eaters had come to see why Ruby wasn’t at school, and Sam was standing her ground alone against the pair when Lena had stormed in, a curse already forming on the tip of her tongue before the duo even realised reinforcements had arrived. They managed to get Sam and Ruby out of there, but had to leave the unconscious bodies of the Death Eaters inside Sam’s flat, Apparating to Cornwall and spending the night on the living room sofas as they gave up the single beds to mother and daughter, while Eliza was only mildly surprised at her new houseguests.

 

            They only stayed two nights before Alex put them up in her cottage, relaying the news that, apparently, any students who hadn’t been on the Hogwarts Express were being tracked down all over the Isles, and insisted on their not returning to Sam’s flat. As the weeks went by, more Order members went to ground, everything so disorganised without Dumbledore there to involve them in his plans, and there really wasn’t much they could achieve without their established network of contacts, which grew slimmer with each passing day as more people were killed off or fled the country. Still, they showed up to foil as many plans as possible, using attacks plotted against the Muggles, and had nothing to show for it afterwards, no way of arresting any Death Eaters and carting them off to Azkaban, not when the Ministry had been overtaken, and the Dementors allied with them. That was a particular sore point for Lena, who knew that if she was fortunate enough to capture her brother, there was no place for him to go, except six feet under. The possibility of killing him seemed harder than his arrest, though.

 

            By the time September was almost over, they were exhausted. So many sleepless nights and long days left them in bed at all hours, coming and going without warning most of the time, and trying to catch up on rest when they could. Eliza grew quieter and more worried with each passing day, trying her best not to mention it, but oftentimes asleep on the sofa when they came in, as if she’d been waiting up for them, reassuring herself that they got home okay. Lena knew that pained Kara, but no amount of pleading for her to sleep upstairs in her bed persuaded her otherwise, and the schedule they kept ate away at all three of them. On top of that were the frequent visits from Alex and Kelly, in and out as much as Kara and Lena were, mostly to reassure Eliza that they were okay as well, other times to quietly exchange new tidbits of information with Kara and Lena as they huddled in close around the kitchen table, the news growing bleaker and more dire with each occurrence. 

 

            The development of Potterwatch became their new saving grace, passing information over the secure radio network, tuning into the channel at all hours of the day, listening for anything important. One of those things was the list of the dead, which seemed longer each time they listened to it. Kara’s hair seemed more grey than blonde these days, the stress of everything, on top of her Lycanthropy, leaving its mark in her curls, and Lena couldn’t help the growing sense of panic inside her. She should’ve been spending all of her time researching a cure, not ferreting out evil and achieving nothing from it. All she could do was work on a new batch of the Wolfsbane Potion in Eliza’s kitchen, with Sam’s flat out of the question now, and ensure Kara took all seven doses, before locking her in Alex’s garden shed, sending everyone inside that house back to Eliza’s for the night, as she waited out the full moon alone. Sam offered to wait with her, no stranger to dealing with werewolves during her healing residency, but Lena was glad for the peace, a reprieve from the constant, nagging worry that pervaded every moment of her life. 

 

            Despite things with Kara getting better, the constant deluge of bad news was so demoralising that she could scarcely enjoy the ways they were reconnecting. Even sex, which was no longer a rare occurrence, didn’t hold the comfort she’d hoped it would, both of them so tired most of the time that it seemed to sap whatever energy they had left. But they talked a lot, especially when it was dark out, and the bedroom was lamplit to keep the night at bay, their fears quietly spoken to each other as they lay together in the one bed, still unable to sleep apart. It was the only solace Lena felt sometimes, and she often said more than she meant to; that deep vulnerability within her was able to come out as she spilt her guts, her voice wobbling at times, especially at the near misses. And there were several of them over those weeks, watching Kara dodge a streak of green that had Lena letting out a panicked yelp, earning a nasty gash across her ribs, which Sam had healed afterwards. Kara had dislocated her collarbone lurching out of the way of a chunk of a wall collapsing and tripping over a pothole, landing funny in the process, and Lena had taken a nasty punch to the face when a duel with a Death Eater had taken a physical turn and swelled her left eye shut, the bruise black by the time she staggered into Eliza’s cottage with a weary slump to her shoulders and a few choice words for the man who’d gotten the jump on her. But they were alive, and they considered themselves lucky for it. Not everyone else could say the same.

 

            The twentieth of September was another late night. Alex Apparated to the cottage at eleven o’clock, knocking on the closed bedroom door before she opened it a crack, as both witches jolted awake in the narrow bed. Rubbing her eyes, Kara sat up and squinted at her sister, and Lena blearily blinked as she pushed herself up onto her elbows.

 

            “What’s wrong?” Kara hoarsely asked.

 

            “An attack in central Birmingham,” Alex breathlessly explained, already moving, her feet thundering downstairs.

 

            Kara shot out of bed, fumbling for her glasses, and Lena was on her heels, wand in hand as she made for the bedroom door. Kara nodded and rushed out of the room, the sound of their feet on the stairs loud in the stillness of the house. A cold sea breeze swept in through the open front door, Alex already gone, and Eliza on her feet in the open archway of the living room, tying her dressing gown shut against the chill and tucking her hair behind her ears. Kara reached the bottom of the stairs and jammed her feet into the first shoes she found, tall wellies going on over her pyjama bottoms, and dragged a cloak from the hook.

 

            “Be careful,” Eliza warned them both as Lena neared the bottom, her hand on Kara’s back as she squeezed past.

 

            Nodding, reaching out to squeeze her mother-in-law’s arm, Lena shoved her feet into slippers and grabbed a coat for herself. It was Eliza’s gardening coat, waxed canvas comfortably worn in, and Lena was still getting her hand in the second sleeve when Kara grabbed her arm, towing her over the threshold and Apparating them to Birmingham.

 

            Lena had never been to Birmingham before, but she was sure it wasn’t usually that foggy. It was thick and brought a damp, muffled atmosphere to the middle of the city. She could barely see in front of her, getting her other arm through the sleeve as she turned in a slow circle, wand in her hand, and felt the hairs on her arms and the back of her neck stand on end. Stifled shouts surrounded her, and she could hear echoing footsteps, caught a dim streak of light through the smoke, a spell fired off by someone, even though she couldn’t see who. She couldn’t even see Kara, who’d been by her side only moments before, but was lost somewhere in the fog.

 

            And then that hair-raising feeling intensified, a bone-chilling coldness sweeping over Lena, and she felt her stomach lurch with realisation, dread suffusing her as she felt a lump in her throat. Whipping around, lit wand raised, she stumbled back as something dark and cloaked swooped at her, and a wave of despair crashed into her, so intense that Lena let out a small gasp. The Dementor brought a wave of sadness with it, so strong that Lena felt weak in the knees as she raised her wand a fraction, teeth gritted against the awful pit inside her, and spat out a spell.

 

            “Expecto Patronum!”

 

            Nothing happened. She wasn’t surprised; she’d never conjured a Patronus before, not even a wisp of one. Still, Lena had never faced a Dementor before, and she felt her skin prickle with a cold sweat, her heart hammering in her chest as fear took over. She’d seen drawings of course, in textbooks, seen photos in The Daily Prophet, and the after-effects of a Dementor attack when patients had been rushed to St. Mungo’s, but the reality of it was so much worse. Staring into the creature’s hooded face, Lena’s mouth went dry, and she heard a roaring sound in her ears and went rigid as it started to feed on her. 

 

            Immediately, she was overcome with a barrage of her worst memories, a ragged sound escaping her as the Dementor swooped past. It glided over her head, and the sensation ended, her knees buckling, and she collapsed to all fours on the pavement, chest heaving as she let out a frayed sound of panic. It was back before she could collect herself, that rattling sound of its breath as it seemed to inhale - if it was capable of breathing - sucking at her face as she went rigid, her head seeming drawn to it, as helpless as she was. Another onslaught of memories overwhelmed her, and Lena let out a choked sound of pain, reliving all the horrifying moments of her childhood that she’d thought she’d buried. There were ones she’d even forgotten about, lost amidst the years of pain, and she let out a broken sob as the Dementor swept past again.

 

            She didn’t give it a chance to come back a third time, didn’t try to stay and hold her ground with another attempt at the Patronus Charm, just staggered to her feet and ran. Lena wasn’t particularly fast, but she was desperate, losing the slippers as they flopped off her feet, and she glanced over her shoulder, through the thick fog, as if she’d be able to see the Dementor chasing after her, running out into the road and unaware of the headlights that cut through the fog moments before the car clipped her left side, sending her reeling into the other lane, letting out a yelp of surprise as she narrowly avoided a car coming the other way and tripped up the curb. 

 

            Frantically breathing, Lena turned in a circle, limping, clueless as to where she was, or who was out there, feeling a pain in her hip where the car had caught her as she’d darted past, and she wiped strands of hair out of her sweaty face and turned slowly. Her chin wobbled, and she felt unbalanced, not expecting the Dementors and too rattled as a result of them, and she drew in a shuddering breath before she took off running again as a creeping sadness oozed towards her. Feeling nauseous, unable to stop shivering as her body was wracked with weakness, Lena ran and ran until each breath hurt, and she could hear the shouts of spells all around her.

 

            Going so fast, and so blinded by the thick white blanket of fog, Lena didn’t see the body on the ground until she tripped over it and went flying. Sprawling several feet away, skinning palms and smacking her chin on the pavement, her mouth filled with the taste of blood, and she let out a whimpering groan, her hands and knees hurting, and took a good minute to get her body to cooperate so she could get to her feet. It wasn’t going well, not at all, and as she staggered up, she ran straight into a dark-cloaked figure looming out of the fog.

 

            Rebounding, Lena’s wand arm came up as she cast a Shield Charm, just in time to deflect the Disarming Charm shot at her. It took her a moment in the darkness and the swirling fog to make out the figure in the black robes, but she stiffened with anger when she recognised the witch. Veronica Sinclair likewise paused as she recognised Lena, a smirk twisting her lips as she raised her chin. “Well, well. Lena.”

 

            “You fucking bitch,” Lena spat at her, her Shield Charm wavering as she was wracked by another shiver, her arm feeling leaden from the weakness of the Dementor attack.

 

            Veronica laughed, a sharp smile crossing her face. “Oh, come now, you can’t be mad that I’ve proven my loyalty. It’s more than you can say; betraying the Dark Lord for your mongrel-”

 

            Dropping the Shield Charm, Lena silently slashed her wand, a streak of purple fire emitting from the tip of it as it billowed towards Veronica. It caught the witch by surprise, but she was quick enough to defend herself, her amusement vanishing as her expression hardened. They exchanged a flurry of spells, neither of them yielding ground as they deflected the shots and countered them with jinxes and hexes, blasting the ground and shop windows as they fought on the side of the street, and despite the fatigue from the Dementor, Lena held her own. If she wasn’t weakened, she probably would’ve gotten past Veronica’s defences already, but she hadn’t managed to disarm her yet. 

 

            And then the coldness intensified, signalling the proximity of another Dementor, and Lena futilely tried to conjure a Patronus again, but was helpless to stop it from feeding on her as it swooped in, sucking at her face. It didn’t matter what happy memories she tried to conjure to evoke even a hint of a silver streak; nothing happened. Instead, her body went taut, wand arm dropping to her side as her chin lifted, face tilted towards the creature, and she let out a ragged gasp, feeling the onslaught of misery once more. It was heartbreaking, the assault of so much wretchedness on her mind, and she staggered limply as it drifted past, feeling faint as the intensity of the desolation dimmed. 

 

            Only to be struck in the face, feeling her nose break as she let out a surprised yelp, tripping over backwards and going down as blood spilt down her chin, and her wand went rolling from her clammy hand. Pushing herself up to her knees, Lena licked her lips, tasting blood, and looked up at the sight of Veronica advancing on her, twirling her wand in her fingers as she smirked.

 

            “Everyone’s always prattling on about how clever you are, but look at you; you can’t even cast a Patronus to save yourself,” she laughed, before her voice turned mocking. “What’s the matter? Is everything not so perfect with your beloved mutt?”

 

            With another laugh, Veronica sank to a crouch a few feet away from her, head cocked to the side as she gave Lena an appraising once-over. Stiff as she knelt on the damp pavement, Lena drew in shallow breaths, her whole body trembling, and gave her old Housemate a venomous look. She wouldn’t give her the satisfaction of her fear.

 

            “You’re a sorry sight, compared to how you used to be, before you betrayed your own kind. I’m surprised you’d even show your face in public; he’s on the hunt for you, didn’t you hear? Not Lex, although he’s furious that you humiliated him, carting him off to Azkaban like that. No, the Dark Lord. He doesn’t take kindly to spies,” Veronica contemptuously spat, her amusement curdling to disgust. “And to think he gave you the opportunity to be loyal to him, to wear his mark, and you turned him down for your precious little werewolf. She made you weak, Lena. Well, my loyalty will be rewarded when I bring you to him. I’d be proud to wear his mark.”

 

            Biding her time, her strength, knowing that she couldn’t do much without her wand in hand, Lena sagged on her knees, pretending to be more exhausted than she was. She was rattled, of course, and she couldn’t stop her hands from shaking, but there was rage inside her, too, and that was all the motivation she needed. Jaw clenched as she listened to Veronica deride her, Lena waited until she snapped.

 

            Catching Veronica off guard, Lena threw herself at her, and while she wasn’t particularly big or strong, she was determined, and she had the edge of surprise. Her hands went around Veronica’s throat as she lunged for the witch, and her weight drove them down to the pavement, her body pinning Veronica down, and they struggled for a moment, her left hand going to Veronica’s right wrist so she couldn’t point her wand at Lena, and her right hand tightening, choking off any words. Pressing her knee firmly into the witch’s stomach, Lena hunched over her, fingers digging into the sides of her neck, and she held her pinned to the cold ground as she hissed in her ear.

 

            “That’s where you’re wrong; she made me strong. And you should be grateful to her, because it’s that strength she’s given me that will let you walk away from this unharmed. Because if it were up to me, I don’t think I’d have the strength to show you any mercy for what you did. But for her, I can do it. Just this once.”

 

            Lena’s fingers tightened, and Veronica let out a feeble plea as she scrabbled at the back of Lena’s hand, desperate for her to let go. Face stony and her voice so cold, so harsh that she barely recognised it for her own, Lena gave Veronica a hard shake. “But if you ever touch her again, I won’t be so lenient. Do you understand me? Good.”

 

            She snatched the wand from her hand before she staggered to her feet, letting go of Veronica’s throat and standing over her as she watched her gasp for air, writhing on the pavement as she stared up at Lena with shock. Clutching the wand in both hands, Lena snapped it cleanly in half and dropped both pieces onto the witch’s chest before she spat on her.

 

            “And that’s how much I think of your Dark Lord.”

 

            Backing away, sweating but cold, trembling but tense, Lena stooped to snatch up her wand before she turned and ran away, limping as she disappeared into the fog. She was filled with a desperate urge to find Kara, then, her lip quivering as she blindly ran onwards, ducking as a streak of red came out of the mist, stunning a wizard that came barrelling after it a moment later and didn’t see her, before she heard the muffled sound of a spell being yelled and recognised the voice. Relief cut through her, and she set off towards the sound of it, but the fog was too disorienting, and she didn’t know where it had come from exactly, the shouts echoing around her.

 

            The Dementors found her again, then, and Lena’s cry of pain was loud and sudden as she sagged, kept on her feet by the creature sucking at her face. Collapsing to the street as it cut off, she clutched the sides of her head as she drew in frantic breaths, trying to regain her composure, filled with a sense of urgency to find Kara. If she could find Kara, it would be okay. The pain in her chest would go away if she could just find her. But Lena couldn’t move, couldn’t speak, as another Dementor swooped in almost as soon as the first one had stopped feeding. And there were more of them, drawn to her hopeful thoughts of Kara, until Lena was laid out on her back, unable to get to her feet and run as they slowly drained her, taking it in turns as she choked on her sobs, tears in her eyes as she relived so much trauma that it was like it was happening all over again.

 

            And then a silver wolf bounded towards the group of Dementors, driving them away, and Lena turned her head to the side, tear-stained face searching, until she saw Kara appear out of the wall of white, dropping to her knees and dragging Lena into her lap. Her relief was palpable, a choked sob escaping her as her shoulders slumped, and Lena smiled weakly up at Kara, reaching up to touch her shaking fingers to her cheek. 

 

            “Oh, you’re okay,” Kara shakily exclaimed, the white look of shock on her face letting Lena know she’d feared the worst, feared that they’d Kissed her already.

 

            “I’m okay,” Lena whispered, forcing herself to sit up.

 

            She couldn’t deny that it had taken a lot out of her, that each feeding weakened her more and more, but she couldn’t stay there. They had to keep moving, keep fighting. The Patronus winked out of existence as Kara helped her the rest of the way to her feet, and their combined relief was like a beacon in the fog, a magnet for the Dementors, drawing them back in as soon as the buffer the Patronus had given them vanished. But the Dementor that swooped in went for Kara this time, her hope and relief so intense that it eclipsed Lena’s emotions.

 

            Lena sagged at Kara’s side as her fiancée’s hold on her went slack, and she stumbled away, a small cry of panic falling from her lips as she tried to regain her balance. Whirling around, watching as another Dementor pounced, that awful rattling filling her ears as her breath plumed before her, the cold so harsh that it was like winter had sprung early, Lena levelled her wand at the Dementor and gritted her teeth, all of her determination and every scrap of happiness within her going into the spell.

 

            “Expecto Patronum!”

 

            And still, nothing happened. Letting out a pitiful sob, hearing the gasping pain of Kara’s breath, Lena didn’t hesitate as she darted forward and threw herself in between the Dementors and her love. Arms spread wide, she raised her chin. “Here!”

 

            Diverting their attention, she did all that she could do, knowing that Kara would need to drive them off again, that Kara would need to pull herself together and cast another Patronus. All Lena could do was buy herself enough time to do it by allowing the Dementors to feed on her instead. Except Kara collapsed to the ground behind her, on all fours as she panted, the full moon only four nights before, leaving her more exhausted than usual as she recovered from the toll it had taken on her body. Lena felt a stab of panic then as the Dementor feeding on her broke off, and she realised that Kara was of no help to them. They could only be fed on so many times before it would be too much, before their souls were at risk, and the thought of that made her stomach jolt with fear.

 

            “Kara, get up,” she ground out, her body already taut as she anticipated the next bout of feeding, a strangled noise at the back of her throat as the creature sucked at her face and then passed on. Lena swallowed a sob as she slumped, her hands going to her knees as she choked out a breathless plea. “Please, get up.”

 

            And Kara listened, spitting a sound of agony through gritted teeth as she pushed herself up. Another Dementor glided towards Lena, and she endured the torment of it as Kara raised her wand and tried to conjure another Patronus, a wisp of silver shooting from the tip and then guttering. It managed to get the Dementor to let go of Lena, backing away slightly, but there was no silver wolf charging towards them, rebuffing their attack, and Kara’s face fell, a look of horror dawning on it as she realised how doomed they were.

 

            She lunged forward to grab Lena’s hand, dragging her away, but the Dementors gathered, a horde of them honing in on the radiating emotions of the witches, and Lena held Kara’s hand tightly as they continued to back away, while dread settled heavily in their stomachs. It was relentless after that, a near-constant attack as the Dementors encircled them, feeding off them as they were trapped inside the circle of utter misery. They were back-to-back, Lena’s hand slipping free from Kara’s, and all she could see was a wall of dark-robed figures hovering everywhere she looked, the fog so thick that it blotted out anything else, and Lena’s breath was frantic and painful as she staggered about weakly, still on her feet somehow.

 

            Kara went down first, on her knees behind Lena, unable to muster the energy to withstand their insatiable feeding any longer, and when Lena almost tripped over her, whirling around to see her slumped on the ground, it felt as if her heart had been ripped from her chest. And then a burning anger filled her, her vision furring at the edges as she was enraged by the thought of Kara being overwhelmed by these creatures, that they could make her feel anything negative at all. And that anger served to fill Lena with renewed determination to get them out of there, because she loved her, and she would not let them take Kara’s soul. Not when they were getting married. That thought spurred her into action, because Lena would not let go of that thought, the only good thing in her future she had to look forward to. No one could take that away from her, least of all these creatures.

 

            “Expecto Patronum!” she hoarsely yelled, unwavering as she stood protectively over Kara, refusing to go down without a fight.

 

            She wouldn’t let them have her. She was hers, and hers alone, and Lena was going to marry her. And as she felt that certainty swell in her chest, the determination to have that happy moment for herself, to have a wife she loved, and who loved her, something small and silver flew from the tip of her wand. And for the first time, Lena cast a Patronus, shock and then awe etched on her face as she watched the raven dive at the Dementors, swooping around in a circle as it drove them away, and then further still, a wide circle of silvery light radiating from where she stood. 

 

            It felt endless, the silver light so bright that it was almost blinding, the circle of it growing bigger and bigger, while the Dementors peeled back, the fog retreating with them. When the spell finally failed, Lena almost collapsed, her knees wobbling as she sank to the floor, just behind Kara’s left shoulder. Wand clattering to the ground, she let out a small whimper, too stunned to speak, and grasped a fistful of Kara’s cloak, clawing herself closer to her, until her arms enveloped her in a hug, her face buried in her shoulder. Kara choked on a quiet sob and reached behind her, her fingers fumbling over Lena’s head, touching her hair, reassured by her presence.

 

            Lena was oblivious to it all then, unsure whether she blacked out or just lost track of time, her body curled protectively over Kara, until she was suddenly aware of the sounds of the city, of Muggle sirens and shouts, and her fiancée shivering in her arms. It was Alex who found them, her footsteps loud on the asphalt as she ran across the road, the bright lights of the city centre making them easy to spot with the fog vanishing altogether, and Lena startled as her hand clapped down on her shoulder. Blinking up at her, still somewhat dazed, and so tired that she couldn’t move, she took in the blood dried to one half of Alex’s face and stared dumbly at her, dimly aware that she was speaking to her.

 

            “Lena,” Alex’s voice sharply pierced the fog around her mind, a rough shake bringing some clarity back to her as she blinked again. “Is she okay?”

 

            Mouth opening and closing, Lena couldn’t get her voice to work, had to try again, clearing her throat and shifting, moving Kara with her. Kara, who was unconscious, slumped in her curled-up position as Lena had held onto her. Panicked now, Lena gave her a shake and then scrabbled for her dropped wand, shakily pointing it at Kara.

 

            “Rennervate.”

 

            She came to with a ragged breath, her eyes flying open, and Lena let out a frayed sound of relief, burying her face in Kara’s hair as she hugged her tightly to her chest. Face crumpling with relief, she kissed her face and heard the small sound of Kara’s questioning plea.

 

            “I’m okay,” Lena whispered, her voice scratchy and hollow.

 

            Alex was crouching at their side then, her hand still on Lena’s shoulder as her worried gaze moved between the two of them. “What happened? You’re okay?”

 

            “Dementors,” Kara shakily explained, sitting up slightly, a haggard look on her face.

 

            “Bastards,” Alex spat. “They got me, too, before I realised they were here.”

 

            Lena made a near-hysterical sound of amusement at the back of her throat, her green eyes wide and haunted as she stared vacantly ahead. “I couldn’t fight them off. They just … kept coming.”

 

            “Wha- the Patronus, the raven, wasn’t that yours? It looked the same as your Animagus.”

 

            Turning her head to look at her, Lena laughed. It was hitching and confused, catching in her throat as she cocked her head to the side. “I’ve never been able to do one. It wouldn’t work. I thought we were done for, but … I couldn’t let them have her.”

 

            She frowned, her expression one of pure bafflement as she stared at Alex. And then she let out another laugh, before it turned into a hitching sob. Alex stared back at her with a stricken look of alarm, and Lena turned her attention back to Kara, giving her a wavering smile as she stroked her blonde hair.

 

            “They couldn’t have you,” she whispered, her voice thick and scornful at the mere idea of it. “I wouldn’t let them.”

 

            Kara made a bewildered sound of surprise as her face crumpled. “You saved me.”

 

            “I had to.”

 

            “The Patronus … it was yours?”

 

            “I had to do it,” Lena repeated, continuing to stroke Kara’s hair as she sat there with a look of utter disbelief on her face. “I had no other choice.”

 

            “You did well, Lena,” Alex gently broke in then, squeezing her shoulder. “Really well. Why don’t you let me help you up? We should get you home to rest. Dementors are nasty business.”

 

            “Chocolate,” Lena absently replied. “She needs chocolate. The Dementors, they fed off her. They just … kept feeding.”

 

            “Yes, chocolate,” Alex agreed. “Let’s get Kara some chocolate. Help her up, and I’ll take her to get some.”

 

            Diverting Lena’s attention to Kara’s care worked immediately, with Lena stiffly climbing to her feet, reaching down to help Kara up as she gently coaxed her. Kara wasn’t quite as dazed as Lena, though, and the perturbed expression on her face was for her fiancée’s well-being, shooting her sister a panicked look and keeping silent as Alex shook her head in warning, the pointed look in her eyes urging Kara to play along.

 

            Gripping both of them, Alex Apparated them to her cottage without a word, not letting go of them until they’d been dragged over the threshold of the front door and through to the kitchen. She let go of Kara and dragged a dining chair out, steering Lena down onto it, and then vanished from the room. Mouth opening and closing, Lena stared at Kara and swallowed a whimper as she rose to her feet again, reaching out to cup Kara’s face in her scraped palms, tears in her eyes.

 

            “You’re here.”

 

            “I’m here,” Kara agreed, her voice gravelly and uneven.

 

            The tears in her blue eyes were from the pain of the night, and she didn’t have to ask why Lena might’ve sought reassurance that she was there. She’d seen it too, reliving all of the worst moments of her life, but she hadn’t been fed on quite so many times as Lena, who’d already been severely weakened before Kara had found her and failed to keep the Dementors at bay for good. Lena moved slowly, trance-like as she stepped in closer and wrapped her arms around Kara, her face pressed into the side of her neck as she let out a frayed sound of pain, of pure relief.

 

            “It’s alright,” Kara quietly insisted, stroking Lena’s hair, rubbing her back, listening to the sounds of footsteps descending the stairs.

 

            Alex reappeared with Sam in tow, and the Healer immediately leapt into action, having been briefed on the situation, pouring milk into a saucepan and finding a block of Honeydukes chocolate in the pantry, breaking off a few pieces and breaking apart the witches to insist they eat it. Alex had some too, also a little pale and shaken, and then the rest went into the pot of milk, along with a few heaped tablespoons of sugar. Nibbling on the corner of her chocolate, Lena felt the sweetness fill her mouth and sank back onto the dining chair, blinking owlishly as she felt herself slowly come out of her muddled mind.
