            “Are you hurt anywhere?” Sam asked as she left the hot chocolate to simmer on the stovetop, crouching in front of Lena as she gave her a searching look.

 

            “I got hit by a car,” Lena whispered.

 

            Kara almost knocked over her chair as she lurched to her feet in a panic, and Lena blinked, her eyes straying to her, before she smiled slightly. “It clipped me.”

 

            “Can I see?” Sam gently coaxed her.

 

            Nodding, Lena put the rest of the chocolate in her mouth, chewing quickly, feeling the sugar dissolve on her tongue, and climbed to her feet. She shed Eliza’s waxed coat and pulled up the hem of her pyjama top, watching the three witches wince at what was beneath it. Peering down at her left hip, Lena took in the nasty bruising and tugged down the waistband on her pants, cringing at the dark, mottled skin disappearing further down her side. Alex took over the hot chocolate, and Sam made Lena stand still with her top up and pants down as she fetched a bruise salve and applied a thick layer of it over the skin, after a few probing prods with her wand revealed nothing was broken. Her hip joint was swollen, though, and she was advised to stay off her feet for the next day to let the Anti-Inflammatory Potion she gave her work its magic.

 

            Her broken nose was fixed as well, a wince of pain all the reaction Lena gave, and other than the scrapes of her palms, the bruised knees and elbows, and cut up soles of her feet, Lena was physically okay. She didn’t have to explain beyond that; everyone knew what Dementors did, and everyone had the decency not to ask what had been dredged up. Kara could guess well enough, but she would never have brought it up in front of other people. Lena was grateful for that, coming back to herself more and more with each passing minute, especially when she was ushered back down onto her seat with a steaming mug of hot chocolate to knock back, the warmth of it seeping through her as that desolate cloud of depression in her mind was banished.

 

            She did as she was told while watching Sam tend to Kara, her expression hawkish as she took stock of her injuries, of the swollen ankle and cracked sternum, and Sam was in the middle of applying a Burn-Healing Salve to Alex’s right shoulder, the flames having eaten right through her clothes, when Kelly arrived back home. She was limping and drenched, but it wasn’t anything Sam couldn’t fix in a few minutes, a certain hush over the kitchen as they were all left to think about the gravity of the night. When they’d all finished being treated, the conversation came, slow at first as they lingered in a stupor, but falling into a sense of normalcy as the hot chocolates went down easily, chased by a jot of Firewhisky each to fill in the gaps.

 

            “I could see fuck all from the moment I got there,” Alex exasperatedly rasped, raking her hand through her hair over and over again.

 

            “It was bedlam,” Kelly said, “there was nothing we could do. Querl’s still there helping J’onn rework the memories of any Muggles who saw what happened.”

 

            “I’m just glad there weren’t any giants this time,” Alex sighed. “The Dementors were bad enough, on top of the Death Eaters.”

 

            “Mm,” Lena rasped, rubbing the bridge of her nose. “Veronica Sinclair got me good.”

 

            “Veronica?” Kara bristled, her shoulders stiffening as her expression tightened.

 

            Giving her a weak smile, Lena reached out to touch the back of her hand. “Don’t worry, I snapped her wand. I don’t think she’ll be in a hurry to cause trouble for us again.”

 

            Kara blinked in surprise, but the tension bled out of her. She picked up Lena’s hand and pressed a kiss to her grazed palm, before squeezing her fingers and then picking up her Firewhisky and taking a sip.

 

            “How’d everyone else fare?” Kara asked. “Any casualties?”

 

            “Two Muggles,” Kelly sighed. “They left a bloody Dark Mark over the city, too. Not ideal.”

 

            “Was my brother there?” Lena quietly asked.

 

            Alex and Kelly exchanged a glance that immediately had Lena’s hackles rising, alarm stealing over her. With a sigh, Kelly grimaced. “Tonks saw him kill one of the Muggles. He left before the Dementors arrived.”

 

            Nodding as she absorbed the information, Lena swallowed thickly, quietly seething. Her hatred was even more prevalent right then, with everything he’d done to her at the forefront of her mind. She touched the middle of her forehead, as if she could make the bad thoughts disappear. “Cowardly prick.”

 

            “Not sure I’d want to stick around for that lot, either, though,” Alex sourly muttered. “Nasty work. I won’t be sad to see the end of them once this is all over.”

 

            “Blimey, that was a strong Patronus, though,” Kelly said, rubbing her bruised knuckles. “They were everywhere one minute, and flying away like mad the next. Whose was it? Never seen it before.”

 

            Lena didn’t speak, and there was a pause as Kara and Alex waited for her to claim it. It didn’t feel like a moment of pride to Lena, though; it was embarrassing to divulge that she’d never managed it before, that she didn’t have memories powerful enough to muster the happiness to cast it. Softly clearing her throat, Kara replied for her.

 

            “Lena’s.”

 

            “Le- yours?” Kelly asked with surprise. “Ah, that’s what it was; a raven.”

 

            “Your Patronus is a raven?” Sam asked, eyebrows raised.

 

            “Mhm,” Lena hummed, the corners of her mouth twitching with a smile.

 

            “Hm. I don’t remember knowing that.”

 

            “That’s because I’ve never been able to cast one before,” Lena admitted.

 

            “You- oh. Well. I thought- well, with work-“

 

            “Yep. Not very hard to delegate that to the Interns, though,” Lena wryly replied, rubbing her grazed chin as she shifted uncomfortably.

 

            “Must’ve been a powerful memory,” Kelly quietly spoke, and Lena gave her a wry smile, humming.

 

            It was already late when they’d been roused from their bed, and it was even later when they’d arrived at Alex and Kelly’s, but they stayed a while yet. It wasn’t until the pall the Dementors had cast had been forgotten about, or at least pushed aside as they dwelled in the gratitude of being alive and relatively unharmed, that they finally went home. There were offers for Sam to share with Ruby and give them her bed for the night, but they were insistent that they get home, and Kara’s explanation that Eliza would be waiting for them put their persuading to an end.

 

            Hand-in-hand, they Disapparated from the doorstep, and Kara wandlessly opened the door to the cottage, leading Lena inside. Eliza was asleep on the sofa, the banked embers of the fire casting a dim orange glow over the room, and Lena watched her stir as they quietly let themselves in. She didn’t have any shoes to kick off, but she took her mother-in-law’s coat off and carefully hung it up as Kara quietly conversed with her mother. It was just past two o’clock, and Lena felt dead on her feet.

 

            “Yeah, we’re okay. No one got hurt that badly; it was just- it was a tough one. Um … I think we’re just going to go to bed,” Kara softly explained to Eliza, who was sitting upright, the dim light making the fine lines of her face deeper, her worry making her seem older.

 

            Kissing her mother’s cheek, Kara hung up her cloak and plodded upstairs after Lena. Inside the bedroom, Lena glanced around the lamplit room, with the rumpled bedding and the clutter of their cramped life, and felt a rush of peace sweep through her. Her eyes stung, and she was rooted to the spot for a moment before Kara’s palm pressed between her shoulder blades, and she walked between the beds, sinking to the edge of Alex’s mattress. Kara dropped a kiss to the top of her head and then sank to her knees in front of Lena, looking up at her with worry in her searching eyes.

 

            “Are you okay?” she asked, her voice strained with anxiety.

 

            Nodding, Lena’s chin dimpled briefly as a tremor ran through her. Running a hand over her face, she swallowed thickly. “I’ll be fine.”

 

            Hand resting on the thigh of Lena’s pants, Kara squeezed gently. “I’ll get you a Dreamless Sleep Potion.”

 

            Before she could move to stand, Lena covered her hand with her own, making a small sound of objection. “I don’t want to sleep right now.”

 

            “Okay,” Kara whispered. “What can I do?”

 

            Lena’s chin wobbled again, and she shrugged helplessly, her brow furrowing as she stared down at her lap with a faraway look in her eyes. Her expression was troubled, as expected, but she wasn’t quite sure what she was feeling. She felt like she could cry, but she was managing to keep it together quite well, so far, although her fear had gotten the better of her at the time.

 

            “Nothing,” she whispered, “just- sit with me for a bit.”

 

            Nodding, Kara rose to sit across from her, leaning forward so she could take Lena’s hands in her own. Her hands were warm, in contrast to Lena’s cold ones, and she tucked them safely between her palms, rubbing some feeling back into them. It was a tense few minutes, and they could hear Eliza coming up the stairs, confident that they wouldn’t be leaving again that night and seeking a proper night’s sleep in her own bed, and it wasn’t until after the door shut that Lena spoke, her voice rasping and uneven.

 

            “I thought- I was so scared I couldn’t save you.”

 

            “I know. I was scared of the same. I’m sorry I failed you; my Patronus, I-” Kara cut off, shaking her head with dismay as she shamefully hung it.

 

            “I’ve never felt … so awful,” Lena confessed. “Not that much all at once. Um … and I couldn’t stop them. They just … kept coming. And it hurt so much, so much … sadness. I felt so- so weak.”

 

            Kara hummed in agreement, thumbs smoothing over the backs of Lena’s hands. “Even around a full moon, I’ve never felt so horrible. It was like … bearing the full moon on the worst day of my life.”

 

            Lena hesitated, licking her lips, and her eyes flitted up to Kara’s face before she dared to ask. “What did you see?”

 

            She could hear Kara swallow the painful lump in her throat, and her voice wavered when she replied. “Um … there were a few things. The night I was turned, being bitten, and watching my dad die. And the transformations - the worst ones, anyway - and your brother, but … there were other ones, um, when- when you left, when I lost you, and … that night you came back, with Alex. Mostly full moons, though; there were too many of them to count.”

 

            Kara looked up, meeting her eyes as she told her, and when she fell silent, Lena could see the anxious question in Kara’s eyes, but she refused to ask it. Lena loved her a little more for that, but she couldn’t ask her to be so vulnerably honest without returning the act. Drawing in a shallow breath, she cleared her throat.

 

            “Mine were mostly my brother. And my mum - both mums. Um … there was that day at the lake, where I almost drowned. And the quill. Lots of memories of those days. And … the cellar. Um … there were a lot of those days, too. It’s funny; I think I’d forgotten how bad it was, how much it hurt. But the worst of it-” she cut off, her throat closing up as tears pricked her eyes. “The worst day of my life was leaving you. And there was so much pain that came from that, that I just- I kept thinking about how we’re supposed to be getting married. It’s all I could think about. Isn’t that silly? I relived my brother’s torture over and over again, and the shame that came from what happened and what I did, and they just. Kept. Coming. And I thought I was going to lose you, but I couldn’t lose you. Because we’re getting married. I didn’t have a memory happy enough to conjure a Patronus … but that thought, the certainty that I would marry you, was the only thought I had.”

 

            “That’s how you did it?”

 

            “Yeah,” Lena said with a shaky laugh, a crooked smile flitting across her face. “I knew that I couldn’t give up without that moment. It’s- it’s all I’ve been looking forward to. It’s the only good thing, the only happy thing that could ever make up for all the pain I was feeling then. That thought … I think it could get me through anything.”

 

            They were silent for a moment, Lena sniffing as she watched Kara fiddle with her fingers, the warmth of them so nice as she suppressed a shiver at the memory of how cold the Dementors had been. Kara stared down at their hands as well, and she chewed on the inside of her lip as she took a moment to pluck up the nerve to speak, to suggest the idea that was growing in her mind.

 

            “Let’s get married today,” Kara whispered, reaching up to tuck Lena’s hair behind her ear.

 

            Lena blinked in surprise, taken aback by her suggestion. “Today?”

 

            “It’s technically the twenty-first of September already. This is the day we met.”

 

            “It’s your birthday tomorrow.”

 

            Kara smiled faintly, leaning in and kissing the tip of Lena’s nose. “I know, but … I really can’t bear to wait until I’m another year older to call you my wife.”

 

            Lena hummed, a weak twitching of the corners of her mouth, and she gently bumped her nose against Kara’s. “You make a compelling argument.”

            

            “It’s a special day, too. It’s not … random. It’s a reason to celebrate. Especially after tonight.”

 

            “I don’t think we can pull together a big party that quickly. I mean, we have no flowers, or a cake - well, there’s your birthday cake, but that’s for tomorrow - and it’ll be a nightmare trying to get word to everyone together at the last minute.”

 

            Letting Lena rattle off a list of requirements for a moment, Kara leaned in again and silenced her with a kiss, before pulling back and squeezing Lena’s hands, scant inches between their faces. “We don’t need a big party.”

 

            “But you-”

 

            “I know what I said,” Kara interrupted, “but … I was talking out of fear, and I was wrong anyway. We don’t need a big ceremony with everyone watching to make it a happy day; it’ll be a happy day because we’ll be marrying each other. The thought of it alone saved us tonight with your Patronus; what other proof do we need that it’ll be the happiest moment of our lives? I don’t want to wait any longer. And it’s not for an inheritance, or because I think you’re going to get yourself killed, I just- I want to marry you. I’ve wanted to marry you for such a long time, and I- I love you. I want to be your wife, I want you to have my last name, whatever you want, just … marry me today.”

 

            Pulling back, Lena gave her an appraising look, searching her face for any doubt and finding none. “Today?”

 

            “Right now.”

 

            “And you’re sure?”

 

            “I’ve never been more certain in my life.”

 

            They were sitting on a bed each, their knees almost knocking in the narrow space between them, and Lena smiled slightly as she tightly held Kara’s hands, an odd expression on her face. “We were sitting just like this when I showed up here all those years ago and asked you if there was still a chance for us. And again, when I asked you to propose to me. Two beginnings to two different chapters of our relationship. Seems fitting to start the next one the same way, don’t you think?”

 

            Expression softening, blue eyes shining with warmth, Kara squeezed Lena’s hands. “It’s perfect. We can do it, just you and me, and we’ll have a proper wedding later with our family and friends.”

 

            Her expression was suddenly serious as she held onto Lena’s hands, giving her a searching look. At Lena’s firm nod, she nodded too, and she let go of Lena’s hands, reaching for her wand on the desk. Lena slipped her wand from her pocket, and she smiled, a small, secret smile, just like things had always been between them, and held her left hand out for Kara’s left hand, their wands held aloft in their right.

 

            “You go first,” Kara quietly insisted.

 

            Softly clearing her throat, Lena angled her wand, pointing it at their joined hands, and moved the tip in a small infinity symbol as she spoke quietly but clearly, a shimmering gold strand wrapping around their entwined hands.

 

            “With this oath, I bind my heart to yours, my soul to yours, my life to yours. I promise to love, honour, and cherish you, in times of joy and sorrow, in laughter and tears. In the joining of hands and the words of this oath, I freely bind my life to yours, for as long as we both shall live.”

 

            The strand of gold lingered as she finished speaking the marriage oath, and she lowered her wand, keeping a tight grasp on Kara’s hand, and watched Kara draw in a deep breath before she spoke. Her voice was low but steady, her blue eyes so piercing as she met Lena’s green eyes, a sheen of tears there, and Kara slowly moved her wand in an infinity symbol as a second strand of gold wrapped around their hands.

 

            “With this oath, I bind my heart to yours, my soul to yours, my life to yours. I promise to love, honour, and cherish you, in times of joy and sorrow, in laughter and tears. In the joining of hands and the words of this oath, I freely bind my life to yours, for as long as we both shall live.”

 

            Kara lowered her wand, and they both stared at the gold strands, crisscrossing their hands and seeming to sink right into their skin, an afterimage visible for a moment longer before it vanished completely. They looked up, their eyes meeting, and they both laughed at the same time, almost shy as they hesitated, their left hands still joined, before Kara slid off the bed, tall on her knees as she reached up to cup Lena’s cheek in her right hand and leaned in to kiss her. Her lips were soft against Lena’s, and Lena’s lips parted as she reached up to thread her fingers through Kara’s curls, crushing their mouths together with more urgency as she tried to push all of her love into it, coming away a bit breathless when the kiss ended a moment later.

 

            “My wife,” Kara whispered, her voice equal parts disbelief and pride as she tenderly smiled up at Lena.

 

            And just like their friendship started twenty-three years ago as a secret between the two of them, alone in a room, so did their marriage as they sat on the edge of the beds and gazed at each other with as much curiosity as the first time they’d met, as if hardly daring to believe what they’d done. Tracing her fingertips over the silver scar across the bridge of Kara’s nose as tears swam in her eyes, Lena softly smiled and felt hot tears on her cheeks, too. And for the first time in her life, they were tears of happiness, and Lena knew that for the rest of her life, she’d be able to conjure a Patronus from the memory of that moment.

Chapter 70

            They didn’t tell a soul that they’d wed in secret, and it brought a little bit of a thrill to their relationship as they enjoyed skirting around it, exchanging smug glances behind the backs of their family, Lena kissing the bare ring finger of her wife, while Kara whispered ‘Healer Danvers’ to her when they were alone. It was a cherished secret and closely guarded for no reason other than them wanting to enjoy this one thing together when everything else was so awful. They knew that Kara’s family would’ve been ecstatic, and understanding of them prioritising marriage over a wedding, but they decided to keep it to themselves for the time being, never quite able to find the right moment with the five of them together, without other people around, without the shadow of bad news as death lists got longer, or another attack was reported. They didn’t mind the secrecy, though, and they were good at sneaking around; it had been the basis of their relationship for such a long time that it felt familiar.

 

            They were married a month before they even knew it, and a week after the October full moon, Lena turned thirty-four. She woke early, the sky still dark outside as the weather turned, grey and frigid, with a cold snap blowing in overnight. In the lamplit bedroom, she stayed beneath the covers with her wife until she felt restless enough to sneak out of bed without rousing Kara. Pulling on socks and twisting her hair up, her wand stuck through the knot to hold it in place, Lena crept downstairs, the house still and dark. Eliza was still in bed, and a glance at her watch showed it was just after six.

 

            Lighting a fire in the empty grate in the living room, Lena slipped on a pair of wellies near the front door and went to check on the garden. She’d spent hours over the last few weeks helping Eliza ready the more delicate plants for the coming winter, November fast approaching and lashing rain leaving patches of the garden waterlogged, and they’d planted trays of seeds as well, winter varieties that had already sprouted, to be planted soon. They were safely housed in the garden shed, where it was warmer, and they were sheltered from the worst of the rain and frost as they formed strong roots. Lena let herself into the gloomy shed, breathing in the smell of compost, dragon manure and damp. 

 

            Enjoying the peace of a little time to herself, contemplating thirty-four years of her life as she checked over trays of seedlings, checking they were damp enough, topping up the soil in a few trays as she reburied sprouting stems, dragonhide gloves blackened with rich earth as she carefully tended to the plants. She took her time, the sky lightening outside, although it remained grey and overcast, and Kara found her there almost an hour later, the latch on the shed rattling as she lifted it and ducked to step inside, a dark silhouette against the dawn outside. Lena smiled and continued to shift a few trays on the shelves, rotating them so she could check on the seedlings in the back cells, and Kara eased the door shut before she stepped up behind her and leaned forward to kiss her cold cheek.

 

            “Happy birthday, Healer Danvers,” Kara practically purred into the side of Lena’s neck, the novelty of it not yet worn off, her arms wrapped tightly around her wife’s waist.

 

            Mouth curving with a smile, Lena leaned back into her. “Good morning, Mrs Danvers. Thank you.”

 

            Kara hummed, kissing the sensitive spot behind Lena’s ear. “What are you doing out here so early?”

 

            “Just checking in on the seedlings,” Lena murmured, sliding a tray of little green shoots further back on the shelves. “Making sure they survived the frost last night. I think your mum must’ve heated the shed to keep them warm.”

 

            Humming again, Kara’s hand slipped beneath the hem of Lena’s jumper and slid upwards over her stomach, to the bottom of her ribcage, fingers warm and roaming. “Do you need to be warmed up, too?”

 

            With a soft snort, Lena’s cheeks dimpled with a smile as she shifted another tray of seedlings forward to check on them. “Are you trying to seduce me in the garden shed?”

 

            “Well, I was hoping you wouldn’t need persuading, but I’m up to the task,” Kara murmured, her fingers dipping beneath the waistband of Lena’s pyjama bottoms.

 

            Letting out a huff of laughter, Lena pressed back against her, her pulse quickening as she smiled, eyelashes fluttering closed, and reached up, cupping the back of Kara’s neck. Turning her head to the side, she clumsily kissed the underside of her wife’s jaw as Kara’s hands went wandering, and she gripped the edge of the shelf tightly in her other hand as she let out a stuttering laugh, feeling a warm flush spread through her. Kara’s mouth was hot and hungry when she kissed Lena, spurred on by the feeling of Lena’s hand moving from the back of her neck to her hair, gripping a fistful tightly as if making sure Kara didn’t pull away.

 

            Making a small sound into Kara’s mouth, Lena broke off the kiss and leaned back against her, head tipping back as she let out a soft breath. It gave Kara access to the column of her throat, which was faintly flushed as Kara touched her, working her up, until it was almost too much to bear, too overstimulating. With a breathless laugh, Lena let go of the shelf and caught Kara’s wrist, stopping her attentive teasing and turning in the circle of her arms so she could crush her lips against Kara’s in a bruising kiss. It was rough and needy, her teeth scraping over Kara’s lip, and Kara reciprocated, pulling her flush against her and then lifting Lena. Turning, she deposited her on the small workbench pressed against the opposite wall of the narrow garden shed, and Lena leaned back into her palms and lifted herself slightly as she let Kara pull her pants down.

 

            Head tipped back, Lena closed her eyes and quietly gasped as Kara kissed her way down Lena’s throat, pushing aside the shoulder of her jumper to kiss her collarbone, and then pushed her jumper up, ducking her head down so she could kiss her stomach, her kisses trailing further down, until she sank to her knees, nipping at Lena’s thighs. With Kara’s mouth on her, Lena wound her fingers in her blonde curls and clutched tightly, a small moan passing her lips as she was offered some immediate relief from the teasing of their foreplay. 

 

            And then she let out a yelp as white-hot pain shot through her, practically launching herself off the workbench and catching herself on the opposite shelves as Kara was knocked back onto the packed dirt floor, wide-eyed with surprise. With a wordless sound of confusion, Kara pushed herself up into a sitting position, her eyebrows rising to her hairline as she looked up at Lena.

 

            “Ow. What the-”

 

            “What’s wrong?”

 

            Twisting, a scowl on her flushed face, Lena craned her neck to look down. “I don’t know, it just- it fucking hurt, like I’ve been stung or something.”

 

            Kara was on her knees, turning Lena as she pushed the hem of her sweater up and frowned, peering at the mark that was situated right in the centre of her right arse cheek. Face crumpling with bewilderment, Kara leaned in a little closer to be sure, the gloominess of the garden shed offering very little light through the small windows, and made a sound of confusion.

 

            “It looks like a bite mark,” she said with appalled wonder.

 

            Lena whirled around, her eyes going wide as she looked down at Kara, who looked straight back up at her, and then Lena’s eyes landed on the shelving unit beside the workbench, running over the array of plants. Blanching, pulling up her pants, any further notions of sex forgotten about, she braced herself against the unit and stooped to peer at the Venomous Tentacula seedling situated at the edge, a little fanged head amidst a pile of vines as it swayed slightly.

 

            “Oh, fuck,” Lena winced, jerking back as the head snapped at her face, backing up against the shelves and then giving Kara a stricken look. “I need you to ask your mum if she has an Antidote to Uncommon Poisons right now.”

 

            “Wha-”

 

            Already pushing Kara towards the closed door of the garden shed, Lena jerked the door open and ushered her out, their footsteps crunching over icy grass as they hurried to the back door of the cottage. “Fucking Venomous Tentacula. I didn’t see it there.”

 

            Alarm shot through Kara, and she turned, her face white, stopping in her tracks before she even made it inside the cottage. “Venomous Tentacula? They’re deadly-”

 

            “They can be,” Lena brusquely corrected. “It’s fine, I just need a potion, and-”

 

            “Right, the potion,” Kara quietly said to herself, jerking open the back door and rushing through the kitchen, already calling out for Eliza by the time she reached the bottom of the stairs. “Mum!”

 

            Lena hovered in the kitchen, her bum on fire as she softly cursed beneath her breath, restlessly shifting her weight as she contemplated the bad luck of ushering in her thirty-fourth birthday with a bit of mild poisoning. Footsteps hurried downstairs, voices overlapping, and Eliza made a beeline for a cupboard with a white look of shock on her face, rummaging through the contents as she rambled.

 

            “Well, this is a lovely start to the day. Although I’m surprised you were bitten, sweetheart, you’re normally so careful with the plants. I’m sure you know not to turn your back on a Venomous Tentacula - especially not one that’s just finished teething. Not to worry, I keep a few antidotes around. Can’t be too careful growing poisonous plants. Ah, here we go.”

 

            Getting to her feet, a small stoppered jar filled with orange liquid in hand, Eliza gave her a sympathetic look and handed it over. A little pink around the ears at her stupidity, Lena weakly thanked her and took the jar, breaking the wax seal as she uncorked it and knocked the contents back. It had a bitter, earthy taste to it, and she grimaced, clearing her throat as she set the jar down.

 

            “You’re lucky it was only an adolescent; their venom’s not as potent as an adult,” Eliza clicked her tongue, grimacing. “Now, let me take a look at the bite.”

 

            Lena swallowed a strangled laugh and gave her mother-in-law a feeble smile. “Oh. That’s alright, I’ll put some Dittany on it, and it’ll be fine.”

 

            “Yes, but their baby fangs are a bit brittle when they first come in. They’re like thorns; they might’ve broken off in the bite. It can cause a nasty infection if they’re not plucked out.”

 

            Reminded of her rotations on the Bite Ward in the early days of her Residency, Lena masked a wince at the thought of it getting infected, but she was mortified at the mere idea of her mother-in-law picking thorny teeth out of her arse. Clearing her throat, Lena weakly smiled, red creeping up her neck as she stubbornly objected.

 

            “It’s fine. Really.”

 

            “Just let me take a quick look to be sure,” Eliza tried to reason with an exasperated sigh, one hand on her hip and the other beckoning impatiently, as if expecting Lena to show her a bite on her palm. Lena wasn’t forthcoming, and Eliza gave her an expectant look as the three of them stood around the kitchen table.

 

            “It bit her bum,” Kara sheepishly divulged, her cheeks turning pink, while Lena’s face further reddened as her embarrassment intensified. Shooting Kara a baleful glance of betrayal, Lena folded her arms over her chest, shoulders hunched as she rubbed her flushed cheek.

 

            Absorbing that piece of information with an air of nonchalance that surprised even Kara, Eliza just pursed her lips and slowly nodded, looking from her daughter to her daughter-in-law and reading everything in their sheepish expressions. “Right. Well … I don’t think I need to know what you were doing in my shed to end up in that position,” she breezily said, turning to the cupboard she’d fetched the potion from and pulling out with an at-home healing kit, set on the table and picked through until she found a pain of tweezers, “but that doesn’t change the fact that the bite needs to be treated, and I’m sorry to say that Kara’s not much use with healing.”

 

            Wanting the ground to swallow her whole, Lena cleared her throat, “I’ll do it myself.”

 

            Kara cleared her throat, giving her an apologetic smile. “I don’t think you’ll be able to, the angle’s not very-”

 

            “Thank you,” Lena curtly cut her off. “Um … let me just call Sam?”

 

            “A great idea,” Eliza brusquely agreed, dropping the tweezers back into the tin of healing supplies.

 

            She set about making them some coffee, giving Lena’s shoulder a reassuring pat and wishing her a happy birthday, before retreating to the living room. Lena had changed her ring to amber while the kettle boiled, not in any great rush after taking the antidote, so she let Kara lead her into the living room, the three of them lingering in a certain awkwardness as they waited. She couldn’t sit properly, a dull throb radiating from the bite, which made her shift into an awkward position so no pressure was put on the right cheek, and she cupped her mug of coffee in her cool palms as the minutes passed by, the silence filled by the clack of Eliza’s knitting needles as she worked on their Christmas presents.

 

            The sound of the door bursting open greeted them not five minutes later, despite the lack of urgency in the colour, and it was Alex who raced in first, wand aloft, to find the three of them sitting there, everything seemingly normal, despite the silence. She frowned as she lowered her wand, a little harried but confused, as Kelly and Sam appeared behind her, likewise tensed for a fight. Lena bit back a groan and felt a new flush creep up her neck.

 

            “What- are you joking me?” Alex asked, her voice full of relief. “I thought- you had me worried sick. Sam said you sent her an emergency signal.”

 

            “I turned it amber,” Lena grumbled, even more embarrassed by the arrival of the rest of her family as well. “Amber’s not urgent.”

 

            “Well, how was I supposed to know that?” Sam asked with a sheepish look on her face. “You said to change its colour, and you’d come. I assumed it worked the same for you.”

 

            “So, no Death Eaters?” Alex asked, running a hand through her hair.

 

            “No, um … well, it’s only Sam that we wanted,” Kara apologetically told her sister, who was shuffling past the coffee table to collapse onto the sofa beside their mother.

 

            “Why are you sitting like that?” Alex asked as she looked at Lena, arching an eyebrow at her.

 

            “One of my Venomous Tentaculas bit her,” Eliza blithely explained, purling a row of stitches.

 

            “What, on your arse?” Alex snorted.

 

            Lena scowled as her blush deepened, and she leaned forward to put her coffee mug down, wincing as she climbed to her feet, somewhat flustered. She looked at Sam and opened her mouth, but Kelly beat her to it, laughing as her face crumpled with bewildered amusement.

 

            “How’d you manage that?”

 

            Eliza quietly chuckled, shaking her head as she counted stitches and then continued with her pattern. Clearing her throat, Lena gestured vaguely and stepped over Kara’s legs. “I was just … helping in the garden shed. Sam?”

 

            She hurried out of the room, dragging her friend by the arm and through to the kitchen. The kitchen door was never shut, but Lena took the opportunity to firmly close it then, her cheeks heated as she pressed her hands against the wood, and then turned, clearing her throat. Sam was leaning against the edge of the table, her arms folded over her chest as she studied her with amusement.

 

            “So … the garden shed, huh? With your pants down?”

 

            “Yep,” Lena curtly replied.

 

            With a snort of laughter and a grin on her face, enjoying herself immensely, all things considered, Sam pushed off the table. “Let me guess, Kara happened to be there, too.”

 

            Huffing, Lena crossed over to the tin and picked up the tweezers, the tips of her ears burning, and held them out as she hotly replied. “Obviously. I think it’s clear to everyone we were having sex, and I can see you’re enjoying my humiliation, so laugh all you want, but can you make sure I don’t have any fangs in my arse first?”

 

            Sam crossed over to her and took the tweezers, arching an eyebrow. “From your lack of urgency, I take it you’ve already taken something for the venom?”

 

            With a glower, gripping the back of a chair, Lena’s mouth turned down at the corners. “Yes, Eliza keeps some stocked.”

 

            “Thank Merlin. Alright, pants down. Do you need something for the pain?”

 

            Brooding, Lena worked her pyjama pants down slightly and scoffed. “No. Do you have anything for embarrassment?”

 

            Laughing, Sam washed her hands at the sink and stepped up behind Lena. “Mind bracing yourself on the edge of the table? Ta.”

 

            Sinking to a crouch as Lena hunched over, hands firmly planted on the wood, Sam pulled Lena’s pants down further to study the bite, humming as she took in the inflamed wound, squinting in the dim light of the dreary day. “The lighting’s a bit shit in here,” she muttered, “hang on.”

 

            Lighting her wand, she held it close and then reached out to pull the skin around the bite taut, Lena baulking at the touch as she let out a squawk of protest, straightening and glancing behind her to give Sam a cutting look. Rolling her eyes, Sam just pulled the bite mark taut again, muttering under her breath. “You’re not this much of a prude at work; is there something special about your arse?”

 

            “Well, everyone wants to have a good look at it today,” Lena sarcastically replied, “so yeah, maybe so. Are there any fangs in there, or?”

 

            “If you’d bloody … keep still,” Sam grumbled, “I’d be able to see, wouldn’t I?”

 

            Huffing again, Lena tipped her head back, eyes closed, and tried to pretend like her best friend wasn’t poking around in her arse cheek at half past seven in the morning on her birthday. It stung, and she let out a soft hiss, wincing as Sam slowly worked broken fangs out of the bite mark, before her friend finished. She’d pulled out four in total and dribbled a bit of Essence of Dittany into the little holes left by the plant’s teeth, the wound smoking as it sealed up, and Sam taped a bit of gauze over the pink marks left behind, her voice flush with amusement as she told Lena it would be tender for the rest of the day.

 

            “Happy birthday,” Sam said once she was finished, dragging her pants up for her and slapping the other side of her bum as she got to her feet.

 

            Scoffing as she rolled her eyes, arms folded over her chest, Lena watched Sam move to the sink to wash her hands again. “Thank you.”

 

            “So, you’re not going to sulk for the rest of the day, are you? Alex said we were coming over for tea. Fish and chips, yeah? I’ll be cross if I have to get an eyeful of your arse and don’t get any birthday cake as a thank you out of it.”

 

            Lena laughed, burying her face in her hands. “Oh, fucking hell. I don’t want to go back out there.”

 

            Sam laughed as well, drying her hands on a tea towel and shaking her head. “Shall I fetch Kara?”

 

            Face still buried in her hands, Lena let out a sound of frustration, and Sam took that as a yes, crossing over to the door and opening it. She only had to take three steps to the open archway of the living room, and Lena could hear the amusement in her voice as she quietly conversed with Kara before her wife anxiously came to check on her. Stepping into the kitchen, Kara cocked her head to the side as she looked at her, and Lena raked her hand through her hair as she raised her head and gave her an exasperated look.

 

            Crossing over to her, Kara cradled her waist and gave her a searching look, amusement in the crease of her eyes. “You alright?”

 

            “She took out four of the little buggers,” Lena pouted, and Kara smiled and kissed the tip of her nose.

 

            “Good thing you had it looked at.”

 

            With a groan, Lena rested her forehead on Kara’s shoulder. “I’m just grateful your mum didn’t have to do it; I already don’t know how I’m going to look her in the eye again. I’m already mortified, as it is.”

 

            “Well, it’s not like she caught us in the act. That would be a bit embarrassing.”

 

            “No, she just has the knowledge burned into her brain that we were shagging on her workbench.”

 

            “I don’t think she knows that specifically,” Kara tried to comfort her, amusement in the corners of her eyes and mouth as they creased slightly. “At least you’ll always remember your thirty-fourth birthday.”

 

            “So will everyone else. I’ll never live this down,” Lena groaned, dissolving into laughter. “They’re going to laugh at me.”

 

            The whole situation was so laughable that they didn’t even consider how strange that was for Lena, to be fixated on something so harmless, because that was the worst thing they could’ve done to her. For all the pain and torment Lena’s family had inflicted upon her over the years, it wasn’t even a consideration that any of the women sitting in the living room would hurt her in the same way. And while she lamented over the embarrassment of the whole situation, it was with a certain fondness for her new family and how they made light of anything they could. Those moments were in short order at present, and she knew they would eagerly latch onto the hilarity of this one. And truthfully, she didn’t mind that much, because there was no maliciousness to it. It was simply silly. 

 

            “I don’t like being made fun of,” Lena complained. “And the worst part is we didn’t even get to finish.”

 

            “I’m sure I can help with that later,” Kara murmured, drawing back a bit as she cupped Lena’s arms, smiling slightly. “But you can’t hide in the kitchen for the rest of the day.”

 

            “I could try.”

 

            Chuckling, Kara kissed her. “Don’t worry, I’ve already dealt with most of their teasing.”

 

            “You weren’t bitten on the arse,” Lena sourly countered.

 

            “Not the birthday present I was hoping to give you. But there are others,” Kara coaxed her, giving her a persuading smile. 

 

            Suppressing a sigh, Lena rolled her eyes, the colour beginning to fade from her cheeks, and she moved over to the kettle. “Fine. Let me make some tea first. Do you want to check if they’re staying a bit?”

 

            Kara kissed her temple, stroking her hair, before she went to ask, returning with the three empty mugs from their coffee and rinsing them out. She added three more to the row and helped Lena make tea to everyone’s liking, before she levitated them through to the living room, handing off Kelly and Sam’s and settling the other four onto the coffee table. Lena hovered on the threshold of the living room, ignoring the muffled snickers of the other women as they found her embarrassment amusing, and awkwardly cleared her throat.

 

            “I’m really sorry, Eliza,” Lena apologised, a little flustered as she rubbed the back of her neck. “I hope the plant wasn’t harmed.”

 

            Setting her knitting aside, Eliza climbed to her feet, and her expression was almost impassive as she tried to hide her amusement from her bashful daughter-in-law, but she couldn’t quite hide it. Giving Lena a pat on the shoulder, she softly sighed, shaking her head. “I’m sure it did more harm to you, honey. But I’ll thank you to keep any more funny business out of my shed.”

 

            Cringing, Lena meekly hummed in agreement and sank to the sofa, folding her arms over her chest as she stared at the coffee table. “Well …”

 

            “Well, well,” Alex guffawed as soon as her mum was out of earshot, going to check on her plants anyway. “Lena Luthor, how scandalous.”

 

            Giving her a withering look, Lena sighed and then scowled when Alex threw a cushion at her. “For your arse.”

 

            Rolling her eyes, cheeks pink and mouth pressed into a flat line of grim amusement, Lena wedged the pillow beneath her. Sinking to her side, Kara gave her sister a pointed look as she wrapped an arm around Lena’s back.

 

            “Will you leave her alone?” Kara curtly asked, giving her a brittle stare that chastened Alex somewhat as she was reminded of her tenuous relationship with her sister at present.

 

            “Lena knows I’m only poking fun.”

 

            “It’s fine,” Lena murmured, leaning into Kara.

 

            “It’s her birthday, in case you’ve forgotten,” Kara reminded her sister, her thumb stroking Lena’s waist as she glanced at her wife.

 

            “Oh, right. Happy birthday,” Alex chuckled. “Sorry, your present’s at home; we were in a bit of a rush to get here, but if I’d known it wasn’t serious, I would’ve taken a minute to bring it along.”

 

            Lena rubbed her warm cheek and leaned forward for her mug before she sank down low on the sofa and tried to hide her face in the tea. There was a beat of silence, everyone raising their mugs to their lips, the fire merrily crackling along, Bastet loafing beside Lena’s thigh, before Kelly cleared her throat, unable to resist poking a little more fun at her sister-in-law.

 

            “So, just out of curiosity’s sake, why the garden shed?” Kelly asked, amused but bewildered as she sipped her tea.

 

            Mouth flattening as she exhaled sharply through her nose in place of a withering sigh, Lena fixed her eyes on the ceiling and gestured helplessly, trying to fight the warmth in her face. “It’s a small cottage. There are only so many places to sneak off to.”

 

            “Why are you sneaking? You’re witches; ward the room, you drip.”

 

            “Yes, I know. I was actually gardening, I’ll have you know. Until someone came to wish me a happy birthday,” Lena tartly replied.

 

            “A nice happy birthday, I thought,” Kara darkly muttered, her turn to flush as the silvery scars on her face starkly contrasted the pink in her cheeks. “I didn’t know she was keeping one of those in there. You might’ve warned me.”

 

            “Warned you? I’m the one who got bit on the arse,” Lena spluttered. “And I was otherwise preoccupied, so it slipped my mind.”

 

            “Well, that’s not a mistake you’ll make again in a hurry,” Sam dryly replied, leaning against the archway and raising her mug to her lips.

 

            With a quiet huff, Lena drained the rest of her tea and leaned forward to set her empty mug down before climbing to her feet. “You can all piss off; I’m going to work on my Wolfsbane Potion, but by all means, continue to laugh at me while I’m gone.”

 

            She didn’t go far, repurposing the cupboard under the stairs for the use of brewing the monthly potion. There were a lot of other things in there as well - boxes of photo albums, a battered leather trunk, broomsticks and camping supplies - so Lena couldn’t even fit inside and close the door, so she was still privy to the conversation in the living room as she stooped her head and pored over the potion, going through the motions of brewing by muscle memory now, having brewed it so many times over the years. Kelly came to make more tea, scooting past her to enter the kitchen, and then leaned against the solid side of the stairs as she chatted away with Lena for a while, leaving a mug of tea for her on the floor of the hallway, out of reach of her just in case, and Lena was just finishing up when everyone left. 

 

            Washing her hands in the kitchen, leaving the Wolfsbane Potion to simmer until tomorrow morning, she called goodbye to everyone, knowing she’d say them later that afternoon, and then fetched her tea, reheating it with a tap of her wand, and stepped outside, leaving the kitchen door open for Kara to follow after her. Eliza was in the shed, her silhouette visible through the small window in the side of it, and Lena leaned back against the cold stone of the cottage as Kara stepped up beside her.

 

            “Happy birthday,” she whispered, leaning in to kiss Lena’s cheek.

 

            Turning, Lena smiled at her, shuffling to the right ever so slightly so she could press up against Kara as they breathed in the cold, salt-laced air of Cornwall. The sky was starting to clear up a little, patches of blue amongst the clouds, and the garden was still clinging to its greenery, and things didn’t seem so dire at that moment as they were. They wouldn’t have believed that there was a war going on, and that they were both at risk because of their involvement, and it was a nice reprieve from it all for Lena as she sipped her tea, steam curling from the surface of it in the biting air, and ruminated on being thirty-four.

 

            “You shouldn’t let Alex get under your skin,” she murmured after a minute of silence.

 

            Kara muffled a groan, tipping her head back against the wall as her shoulders slumped. “You said you don’t like being laughed at.”

 

            Lena chuckled, her mouth curving at the corners. “I know, I just- I know I’m an uptight person. It makes it easy to tease me. If I didn’t bite so easily, it probably wouldn’t be so fun for them, but unfortunately, I can’t help myself. Anyway, I can’t blame them; I’d find it funny, too, if it wasn’t my arse.”

 

            “It’s a little bit funny,” Kara quietly admitted, fighting a smile.

 

            “It is, but I’m also very, very annoyed we were so rudely interrupted,” Lena replied with a crooked smile.

 

            “Will presents make up for it?”

 

            Humming, Lena feigned a sullen look and then smiled. “Go on, then. I know you’re dying to watch me open them.”

 

            “I am,” Kara agreed, smiling as she hurried inside and left Lena to follow after her.

 

            Kara’s feet pounded on the stairs as she ran up them to gather the hidden presents from their bedroom, and Lena sank onto the sofa, sipping the dregs of her tea while she waited for her to return. Coming back down with an armful of wrapped gifts, Kara set them down beside Lena on the sofa with a pleased look on her face. Perched on the edge of the coffee table, Kara gestured to the pile.

 

            “Obviously, with loads of the shops being closed, it was hard to buy anything, and I wasn’t about to go walking around Diagon Alley to do some shopping with the state of everything, so if there’s something you want, we can go and get it when all of this is over. Whenever that will be. I know it’s not much, but I hope you like them.”

 

            Leaning forward, Lena took Kara’s face in her hands and kissed her firmly. “I already love them. Thank you.”

 

            Placated, Kara seemed to relax, and Lena started to open the presents, a few obvious book-shaped ones revealing new titles that had been published in her absence of normal life, a new robe in a nice shade of green, and the customary bag of Fizzing Whizzbees that Kara bought her for every occasion, a little call back to the first gift she’d even given Lena for Christmas the year they’d met. Lena was very vocal in her appreciation for them, and as she was reading the blurb on the new books, Eliza came inside and went to fetch Lena the presents she’d bought for her, too, one of them being the same diary she’d bought for Kara every year. Lena didn’t think it was such a bad idea to start writing down her thoughts; so many things had been dredged up that she’d thought she’d forgotten about, and it was almost overwhelming to be left alone with her thoughts these days.

 

            She thanked them both and took her presents upstairs, putting them away and then going to take a shower. Putting a little more Essence of Dittany on the red mark that lingered, Lena dressed and then started reading one of her new books in the living room, Eliza continuing her knitting, while Kara puzzled through a bit of chess by herself, making the moves for both colours while they listened to the radio for background noise. It was nothing out of the ordinary, but still bleak to listen to, but they all knew it was better to be informed than to avoid it for the sake of not feeling defeated.

 

            They had sandwiches for lunch and then went for a walk, the streets glistening wet from the light showers that had intermittently broken the mildness of the late October day. The sun was shining weakly now, and Lena wore a pair of wellies and her new robe, while Kara bundled up with a thick wool coat that had been Lena’s way back when, but somewhere throughout the years had become a shared coat between them. Rounding the quiet street of cottages, they ended up traipsing through the overgrown field behind their house, dampening their hems with rain and dew, and breathed in the green freshness of their surroundings, with the faint tang of the sea on the blustery wind. They talked, unhurried and unusually contemplative, walking hand-in-hand, squinting slightly against the sun as it peeked out, brightening the day, and the whole time, they had their free hands in their pockets, gripping their wands. Even then, in a small town in Cornwall, they couldn’t let go of the fear and tension that pervaded every part of their life, that they might be caught, that someone knew where they were, even if they weren’t able to find Eliza’s cottage with Alex as Secret Keeper. Lena often wondered if her mother had gone through archived hospital records from Kara’s file, digging out the addresses listed for Lex to try and find them. If so, they hadn’t noticed anything unusual in the street, and they came and went frequently enough to have noticed if they’d been caught. 

 

            Still, they cherished the rare occasion to walk freely on the outskirts of the town, Kara reminiscing about her early days there, fresh from America, resentful at having her life uprooted and crammed into a tiny cottage with her new family. She spoke of it with sheepish amusement, expressing how ungrateful she’d been at the time, how she couldn’t have known how the future would play out. Now, she was nothing but grateful for Eliza, to have a mother and sister who loved her, and to have met her future wife at school. It felt strange to consider how different both of their lives might’ve turned out if Kara had never been bitten by a werewolf. Voicing that, Lena was unsurprised to hear Kara admit that she wouldn’t change a thing if she had the power to do so, that it all worked out for the better, no matter how difficult each full moon was. Hearing that only resolved Lena to work harder at a cure, to find something to stop the transformations altogether, to make it so that Kara didn’t have to bear the pain of it anymore.

 

            Staying out for hours, finding a spot in a patch of trees where they could sit on an old log and listen to the sound of the birds and breathe in the fresh air, too restless from being cooped up, they eventually walked back home, skirting past the cottage and walking into the town. Kara had Muggle money exchanged at Gringott’s, and they paid for their order and lingered inside the fish and chip shop, the smell of vinegar and fryer oil filling the shop, earning strange glances from the Muggles who came in. They were vigilant, wands grasped in their pockets, but the people who came in to collect vinegar-soaked parcels were ordinarily unassuming, chatting to the staff with familiarity, but it was still a relief to leave, and Lena still dragged them into the alley behind the row of shops to Apparate them home as the afternoon darkened. She didn’t want to risk walking home in the fading light, limiting their vision.

 

            On the doorstep of Eliza’s house, they let themselves in, Kara taking the stacked, soggy bundles of food straight through to the kitchen, while Lena hung up her robe and took a seat on the bottom steps of the staircase to work the wellies off. The door opened as she was working on the second one, and she looked up as Alex stepped inside first, pausing as a gleeful look crossed her face.

 

            “Oh, hello. How’s your arse? Still tender?” she chuckled, taking off her coat, while Lena rolled her eyes, freeing her foot and setting the shoe down.

 

            She climbed to her feet, and Alex gestured with a wrapped gift before pressing it into her hands. “Kara was sure you didn’t have that one, without being able to check your shelves at home. Anyway, thought it might be useful for your research.”

 

            Brows furrowing, Lena unwrapped the paper as everyone else shuffled in and stared down at the unassuming brown leather cover of a book titled Taliesin’s Tome of Tricky Transformations. She didn’t have it, and she realised Alex meant for it to help her with her Lycanthropy cure. Grinning, Lena thumbed through it quickly before she was disturbed by another present landing on top of it. Looking up, she blinked and smiled at Sam, giving her friend a quick one-armed hug as she thanked her, and then gestured her down the hallway, giving Ruby a smile and her shoulder a quick squeeze before she corralled her after her mother.

 

            Setting her new book safely aside in the crowded kitchen, Lena stood off to one side and opened the gift from Sam, pulling out a pair of leather goggles. She smiled and arched an eyebrow at her friend, who returned her smile and shrugged. “Alex put the idea in my head; I thought you might need a new pair of brewing goggles for when you start experimenting again. Just in case they get … volatile."

 

            With a snort, Lena shook her head. “Thanks. I’m not planning on blowing up the place, though.”

 

            “Well, I’m glad,” Kara murmured, stepping up beside her with a glass of elderflower wine and pressing a kiss to her cheek. “Anything that protects your pretty green eyes is a good gift, in my opinion.”

 

            “Anything that helps me find you a cure is a great gift, in my opinion,” Lena replied, before turning her attention back to her friend, balling up the wrapping paper. “Thanks, Sam.”

 

            Nodding, Sam moved to the table and took a seat, and Lena was wedged in beside Kelly and Ruby, while Kara helped ferry the slices of buttered bread that Alex was churning out to the table. The wrapped parcels of food were opened and covered the entire table, everyone holding up their glasses for a second to help spread the newspaper out neatly, and Lena stole a chip as she watched the quiet chaos of too many people filling the little kitchen for the sake of her birthday. 

 

            They chatted animatedly, swapping gossip and news as usual, none of them having anything else to talk about, out of work and school - except for Eliza, who continued to dutifully send out what her garden provided with the use of Morrigan to deliver the goods - so it largely revolved around Potterwatch or what news Alex was still reading in the newspaper to stay informed of Voldemort’s schemes. After they’d finished eating, the damp newspaper was balled up and removed, a sponge cake was pulled from the fridge and dotted with lit candles, set down before Lena as she grew bashful as they loudly sang to her. Her embarrassment almost rivalled that of the first thing that morning, but she felt so glad to be there with them that her throat started feeling tight somewhere towards the end of the off-pitch song.

 

            Eating her slice of cake with another glass of wine, she was reminded of how her birthday was last year, and how miserable she’d been without Kara, and how stunned she still was to be able to call her her wife. And no one else had a clue, and Lena marvelled at that as she gazed adoringly at Kara, watching her gesture wildly as she animatedly talked with Sam. She almost wanted to tell everyone right then, a perfect way to end her birthday by basking in the happiness her wife brought, but she kept it to herself, a warmth in her chest at the knowledge that it was a secret thing, just for them. For a little while longer, at least. She was quite content to eat her birthday cake and stare at her, knowing how lucky she was to be back at her side.

 

            After everyone left, Lena went upstairs to put on some pyjamas and felt exhausted from the day. She’d been up early, unable to sleep, and it was starting to make her eyes burn, the two glasses of wine she’d had helping to speed up the leaden feeling in her body. Heading back downstairs, Lena quietly asked if anyone else would like some tea before she boiled the kettle. Saying goodnight to her mother-in-law, she went upstairs to read in bed for a bit, putting a dent in one of the books Kara had bought her by the time her wife slipped into the bedroom, a little bit after nine o’clock.

 

            Holding her place in her book, Lena looked up through her lashes as she watched Kara change into her pyjamas, and then set her closed book beside the empty mug on the desk and shifted across the bed to make some room for her. Not that there was much space at all, the bed so narrow that the only way they managed to sleep with any sort of comfort was on their sides, back to chest and the wall suffocatingly close. Lena kept forgetting to suggest they rearrange the room, moving the desk from between the single beds and pushing them together to make a double, and each time she remembered, she didn’t want to suggest it anymore, with Kara pressed up against, reminding her that she never wanted to be any further from her than that. 

 

            “How was your birthday, my love?” Kara quietly asked, removing her glasses and sitting on the edge of the bed.

 

            She sat facing Lena, instead of stretching out beside her, and Lena laid a hand on her knee as her expression softened. “Really good, thank you.”

 

            “Even with you being bitten?”

 

            “Actually, yes. It was nice to worry about something silly, like my pride, for a change,” Lena murmured, her mouth curving with a wry smile.

 

            Kara softly laughed and then kissed her gently. “One day, the silly things will be all you have to worry about.”

 

            “Do you really believe that?”

 

            “Of course I do. And your pride isn’t silly.”

 

            “I think it is in this situation. It’s not a birthday I’ll forget in a hurry; what terrible luck to start off thirty-four. But, then again, I feel very, very lucky, too, because at least I got to spend it with you this year.”

 

            A shadow of regret passed Kara’s face, and she tenderly brushed Lena’s hair out of her face. “How was it last year?”

 

            “I worked the whole day. Stayed on for emergencies, too, so I didn’t have to go home. I think … it was the worst birthday I’ve ever had, which is funny, because nothing horrible happened to me, I just- I’d gotten used to my birthday being a day to celebrate with a family and friends who loved me. To have that taken away from me was more painful than I’d imagined.” Lena cut off and then let out a small laugh, her green eyes darting to Kara’s face. “And then the next trip to the cottage, I found the butterfly you’d left me, and the feeling passed. I was still loved by you, even if we weren’t together, and that made it more bearable.”

 

            “You were loved by me every second that you were gone,” Kara whispered. “And you were missed just as much. I thought about you the whole day. I thought about you every day.”

 

            “I thought about you every day as well. It was the only thing that kept me going.”

 

            “I love you, Lena,” Kara whispered, leaning in to kiss her slowly.

 

            “Mm, I love you, too. Even if you are a pain in the arse sometimes - quite literally.”

 

            “Let me see,” Kara said as she fought back a smile, and Lena rolled onto her stomach and let her shimmy her pyjama pants down and peel off the taped gauze.

 

            It was little more than a pink circle now, and Kara stifled a laugh as Lena propped herself up on her forearms and glanced over her shoulder to take a look, scowling. “You’re to blame for this, too, you know.”

 

            “Shall I kiss it better?” Kara offered, mirth in her eyes as she arched an eyebrow.

 

            “Oh, you’ll have to do far more than a kiss to make it better, Kara Danvers.”

 

            Pressing a delicate kiss to the tender spot, Kara smiled, and her voice was laced with laughter as she dutifully obliged. “Of course, Healer Danvers.”

Chapter 71

Chapter Notes

soz things are a bit busy atm but i have a backlog of like 10 chapters to upload so i'll try to be quicker with the updates

            Late November was bitterly cold, and Kara was stretched out on the sofa, her right leg elevated on a pillow at her wife’s orders, as she rested the healed break. It was from earlier that morning, a skirmish that had ended up with her tibia snapped in half and a face full of mud as she chased Death Eaters through a patch of woodland outside of York, the foggy morning obscuring the den of some creature that she’d accidentally stepped into. 

 

            She’d had to take herself out of the fight then, freeing her broken leg and limping off to take cover in a patch of thorny brambles as she waited it out. The pre-dawn darkness slowly lightened as the sun rose, and it wasn’t until she heard her name being called that she roused herself, stiff and cold in her hiding spot, unable to put any weight on her right leg as she hopped out between two oaks, answering her wife’s call.

 

            Lena had found her and patched her up easily enough, seeing her safely home with strict orders to keep her leg elevated, before she’d left for the Burrow to help heal anyone else who needed it. Left to her own devices, the stretch of days blending together as she lingered in the uncertainty of unemployment and the tense waiting for news of another fight to throw herself into, Kara read a book on the sofa and tried to pretend that she didn’t see her mum checking in on her every five minutes, face etched with worry, even though it was just a simple broken leg.

 

            She’d already had two strong cups of tea and a bacon and egg sandwich, and Lena still wasn’t home, and her valiant efforts to lose herself in the dense text of her book were unsuccessful. Instead, Kara just stared at the page and anxiously thought of her wife, who she knew would be fine, was probably up to her elbows in blood, if the fighting she’d experienced had been anything to go by. Still, it would be impossible to rest until Lena was safely back home, with news of everything that had unfolded. Kara hated that part, the exchanging of their experience, the things they’d witnessed, coming so close to harm. She knew it was similarly difficult for Lena, especially when she was the one who had to patch up Kara’s injuries, but they’d pulled through relatively unscathed every time. It felt like playing with fire, to keep throwing themselves back into it, knowing that at some point their luck would’ve stretched too far.

 

            The door opened then, and Kara bolted upright, book flung aside as she looked towards the open archway of the living room. She’d purposely chosen the sofa on the opposite side of the room from the windows and had lain so she was facing the archway, so she could see the front door. When Lena stepped inside, shivering and brooding, Kara leapt to her feet.

 

            “Ah-ah, sit back down,” Lena sternly ordered her.

 

            “Let me kiss you first,” Kara argued, limping past the coffee table.

 

            With a sigh, shedding a cloak and a thick wool coat, Lena met her halfway, giving her a quick kiss, her lips chapped from the cold. Kara rubbed some warmth back into her hands as she anxiously stared at her.

 

            “Was anyone badly hurt?”

 

            “Not badly,” Lena sighed, guiding her back over to the sofa and making her elevate her leg again. “Mostly broken bones. Mike lost a finger. Everyone pulled through, though, which is the main thing.”

 

            “Thank Merlin,” Kara muttered, raking a hand through her hair. “You’re alright?”

 

            Giving her a tired smile, Lena laid her hand over Kara’s. “Fine. And you?”

 

            “Ah, broken bones aren’t anything out of the ordinary for me, are they?” Kara wryly replied. 

 

            While her bones didn’t actually break during her transformations, the magical nature of the curse changing her splintered bones into those of a werewolf and then reversing it without anything to show for it - aside from any self-inflicted wounds- made the pain of it similar. Less, even. A broken leg hurt a hell of a lot less than agonising minutes spent having every bit of you changed into something else.

 

            “You really fell into a hole?” Lena asked, a flicker of amusement crossing her face.

 

            “Yeah,” Kara said with a hoarse laugh, cheeks turning pink. “It was a fox den, or a badger’s, I don’t know. Bloody stupid.”

            

            They both laughed for a bit, and it felt good, alleviating some of the tension and worry that weighed heavily on them. Stroking the back of Kara’s hand, Lena watched her for a moment as they both fell silent. It was Kara who broke it, clearing her throat and moving her other hand to pat the back of Lena’s.

 

            “Go on, get into some pyjamas and come and sit by the fire. You’re freezing.”

 

            “Yes, Mrs Danvers,” Lena softly replied, leaning in to kiss her before climbing to her feet.

 

            “And go and tell my mum you’re home. You know how she gets; she’s out the back.”

 

            Nodding, Lena made a detour to the kitchen, pausing to set the kettle on to boil, and then opened the back door. Kara could hear the muffled sound of conversation, and Lena backtracked down the hallway, rubbing her hands together as she glanced at Kara, her cheeks bitten red by the cold, and gave her a crooked smile before she took the stairs two at a time.

 

            Kara leaned back against the pillows, her eyes closed as she listened to the light patter of her heart. It was still struggling to slow: the adrenaline of the morning, her anxiety at being parted from Lena, and then her wife’s safe return making it hard for her to relax, to know she was safe. Breathing slowly and deeply, she opened her eyes again at the unhurried footsteps coming back downstairs.

 

            Lena had a pair of pyjamas on, with one of her knitted jumpers from Eliza, and thick socks on her feet to fend off the cold. The cold sea air outside permeated the walls of the cottage at that time of year, and she made straight for her wife, dragging the blanket off the back of the sofa and draping it over her, before snagging Kara’s empty mug from the coffee table.

 

            The sounds of Lena pottering around in the kitchen reached Kara’s ears, and she smiled faintly at the ordinariness of it. Reappearing with three steaming mugs, Lena set them down and moved over to Kara’s legs, lifting them and the pillow and sitting cross-legged, before she set them back down in her lap. Eliza came in then, shivering slightly in her gardening coat and dragonhide gloves, wellies glistening with water and her cheeks red from the cold. She gratefully nursed her mug of coffee, and none of them spoke as Kara turned on the radio and they listened to Potterwatch and the sound of the crackling fire.

 

            When the segment ended, Lena made Kara have another potion, just to help with the lingering ache in her healed break, and Kara dozed on the sofa until lunchtime. She hadn’t showered when she’d gotten home, and the dirt of the forest was still etched into the lines of her palms and beneath her fingernails, the sweat of chasing Death Eaters through the forest dried on her skin. She suggested a bath to Lena, even though the tub made for a cramped bath, and they squeezed into it, submerged in the heat of the water as it stung the small scrapes and cuts peppering their skin.

 

            Feeling refreshed afterwards, they had lunch in the warm kitchen and then decided to visit Alex and Kelly for more information. It wasn’t safe for Alex to operate as an Auror any longer, but that didn’t mean that she wasn’t in the thick of Order business, with enough connections to be aware of anything happening in the Wizarding community and beyond. Drinking tea in the living room, Alex wearily recounted information that had been passed on from Kingsley, or Tonks, or J’onn, everyone having a little piece of a story that sometimes cobbled together something important. This time, the information fit together to reveal the Muggleborn witch that had been killed in York, the Dark Mark Kara had seen at the beginning of the mad chase through the woodland, an explanation for the death she’d already known about.

 

            In low spirits, they didn’t stay too long. Sam seemed to take it worse than any of them, shocked each time one of them recounted the awful things they’d witnessed. She was in the thick of it now, except for the fighting; she had Ruby to think about, and Kara knew Lena was relieved that at least one person she cared about was sitting on the fringes of it all. Still, it was an asset to the Order to have another Healer on hand for the nights when there were so many injured that Lena couldn’t treat them all simultaneously, and to have someone else to help Lena brew potions. Kara knew that Lena’s vault at Gringott’s held more money than she knew what to do with, and she knew the amount her wife forked out on potion ingredients wouldn’t even make a dent. Still, the vials pocketed by any Order members visiting the cottage, or the ones left at the Burrow, were so in demand as the fighting grew more frequent and more dangerous that Lena and Sam combined couldn’t keep up.

 

            Kara was silent, sitting by herself as Lena and Sam discussed which potions were their top priority, roping in Alex, who more often than not helped to distribute the potions for them. Kelly looked ready to fall asleep, sitting at one end of the sofa with her chin propped up on her fist, heavy-lidded with her mug clenched in her other hand. There was still that thread of tension that fraught their every waking moment now, though, and Kara couldn’t relax, despite the relative peace of the early afternoon. She ended up fetching the empty mugs and walking to the kitchen to try and shake off her restlessness, but there was a lingering agitation that left her walking laps up and down the hallway, kicking off her shoes on her second lap, her socks going on the third, so her bare soles could feel grounded against the frigid cold of the stone floor underfoot.

 

            “What are you doing?” Lena brusquely asked, without looking up from the list of parchment the three women pored over, heads ducked close together, nattering on about brewing times and ingredient scarcity.

 

            “Thinking,” Kara muttered, frustrated.

 

            On the next pass, Lena handed the quill to Sam and looked up. “You should be resting your leg.”

 

            “It’s fine. It’s been fine since the moment you healed it,” Kara wearily replied, clicking her tongue with annoyance.

 

            “Are you the Healer or am I?”

 

            Rolling her eyes, Kara paused halfway back down the hallway, staring at the closed back door as she tipped her head back. “Fine, Healer D- Luthor,” she tripped herself up, turning on her heel and limping slightly as she walked back to the living room and slipped back onto the sofa. “I defer to your expertise.”

 

            “A wise decision,” Lena dryly replied, the spark in her eyes letting Kara know she’d caught her trip. “I won’t be much longer.”

 

            “Are you hungry?” Alex asked, glancing over at her sister.

 

            Giving her the briefest glance, Kara restlessly shifted, arms folded over her chest. “I’m fine.”

 

            “Kelly made some toffee. It’s in the kitchen.”

 

            Not particularly hungry, and not wanting to listen to her sister, Kara remained seated for a few minutes, idly drumming her fingers on the thighs of her jeans, but she was too fidgety to stay still, so she used the toffee as an excuse to pace some more. Walking into the kitchen, she helped herself to some, walking absentmindedly in circles as she chewed thoughtfully, and paused at the sight of Alex coming into the kitchen. She was still harbouring resentment for her sister, and while it might’ve been a bit petty, she tried her hardest to avoid being alone with her, using the presence of others as a buffer, so she quickly washed her hands and brushed past her, trying to ignore the wounded look on Alex’s face as she set the kettle on to boil.

 

            “Ready to go?” Kara asked, hands in her pockets as she hovered on the threshold of the living room. She stretched her right leg and grimaced slightly. “I think I need to elevate this.”

 

            And she wasn’t lying; she’d brushed off Lena’s concerns, but the phantom aching was bothering her a little, making her limp ever so slightly, and she was eager to lie down and put her feet up. Of course, she could’ve done that there, in her sister’s home, but Kara wasn’t really in the mood for the air of awkwardness that persisted between her and Alex. She wasn’t doing anything to ease that awkwardness - in fact, she was doing everything she could to prolong it, making her sister suffer in a way that was uncharacteristically vengeful for her. But then Kara had always been protective of Lena, and sometimes it shone a light on the parts of her that were not so meek and soft.

 

            “I’ll put the order in,” Lena offered, rolling up the length of parchment. “Should take a couple of days for the delivery, but if you start with the Blood-Replenishing Potion, we should have enough powdered unicorn horn to get by until the restock comes in. Might be a bit tricky getting stewed Mandrakes at this time of year, though; the seedlings will probably be hibernating for the winter.”

 

            “My mum might have some dried Mandrakes from this year’s mature batch,” Alex suggested, brushing past her sister.

 

            “Mm, probably. The potion doesn’t require it to be fresh, but it's more potent when it is. But anything’s better than nothing, I suppose.”

 

            “Anything to stop people dying from blood loss,” Sam agreed with a grimace. “Wound Cleaning should be our priority after that. It won’t do to patch everyone up if there’s a nasty infection beneath the skin.”

 

            Sighing, Alex planted her hands on her hips, a harried look on her face. “Just having them alive would be nice. I’m sure you two can sort out the rest if push comes to shove.”

 

            “Of course we can,” Lena brusquely replied, climbing to her feet. “This sort of healing is an intern-calibre skillset; easy but bloody annoying. And messy. I can’t remember the last time I spent so much time patching up lacerations; it’s normally idiots charming their lungs out of their bodies or something stupid like that.”

 

            “Well, at least we’re not dealing with any Enlarging Charms,” Sam chuckled, “then it would really feel like residency days.”

 

            “Enlarging Charms?” Kelly asked, still awake, despite looking like she wished she were in bed.

 

            “You know how men are,” Lena rolled her eyes, not needing to elaborate. “I don’t miss dealing with that on a regular basis.”

 

            “Oh, gross,” Alex wrinkled her nose. “There’s an idea, though. How do you think the Death Eaters will manage if I enlarge them until they explode?”
